zh: 贾拉勒丁·马苏德沙阿是因朱王朝在法尔斯的开创者谢拉夫丁·马哈茂德沙阿之子。1335年父亲被伊儿汗阿尔帕处死之后，他投奔札剌亦儿部的哈桑·布祖格；后来阿尔帕被叛军俘获，交到马苏德沙阿手中处死。他曾任札剌亦儿人拥立的傀儡伊儿汗穆罕默德汗的维齐尔，随后在设拉子与兄弟凯霍斯鲁争夺统治权，直到后者于1338/39年去世。他被楚邦王朝逐出后与亚吉·巴斯提结盟，却于1342年被后者杀害。

en: Abu Ishaq Inju (1321–1357), born Jamal al-Din, was the last Injuid ruler and the youngest son of Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah. After the collapse of Ilkhanid authority he seized Shiraz from the Chobanid Yagi Basti in March 1343 and for about twelve years ruled Fars, Isfahan and Luristan from Shiraz, issuing his own coinage in Isfahan in 1349–1350. His repeated wars against the Muzaffarids ended when Mubariz al-Din Muhammad took Shiraz in 1356 and captured him in Isfahan in 1357; Abu Ishaq was sent back to Shiraz and executed.
zh: 阿布·伊沙克·因朱（1321—1357），原名贾马勒丁，是因朱王朝末代统治者，谢拉夫丁·马哈茂德沙阿的幼子。伊儿汗政权崩溃后，他于1343年3月从楚邦王朝的亚吉·巴斯提手中夺取设拉子，以设拉子为中心统治法尔斯、伊斯法罕和洛雷斯坦约十二年，并于1349—1350年在伊斯法罕以自己的名义铸币。他连年与穆扎法尔王朝交战，1356年穆巴里克丁·穆罕默德攻占设拉子，1357年又在伊斯法罕俘获他；阿布·伊沙克被押回设拉子处死。

en: Sharaf al-Din Mahmud Shah was the founder of the Injuid dynasty of Fars. Around 1304 the Ilkhan Öljeitü sent him to Shiraz to administer the royal estates known as inju, and by 1325 he held nearly absolute power across Fars and was formally named its governor. His power alarmed Ilkhan Abu Sa'id, who dismissed him and, after a failed revolt, imprisoned him at Tabriz. After Abu Sa'id's death in 1335, Arpa Khan took the throne and had Sharaf al-Din executed. His sons then fought each other over Shiraz.
zh: 沙拉夫·丁·马哈茂德·沙阿是法尔斯因朱王朝的开创者。约1304年，伊儿汗完者都派他前往设拉子，管理名为“因朱”的汗室私产；到1325年，他已在法尔斯几乎独揽大权，并被正式任命为当地长官。他的坐大令伊儿汗不赛因不安，遂将他罢免；他起兵反抗失败后被囚于大不里士。1335年不赛因死后阿儿巴汗继位，下令处死沙拉夫·丁。他的儿子们随后为争夺设拉子彼此攻杀。

en: Kan Ekʼ, or Ajaw Kan Ekʼ, was a name or title used by the Itza Maya kings at their island capital of Nojpetén in Lake Petén Itzá.
zh: 坎·埃克，又称阿豪·坎·埃克，是伊察玛雅国王在佩滕伊察湖中的岛国都城诺赫佩滕使用的名字或王号。

en: Jakob Fugger the Elder (1398–1469) was an Augsburg merchant, master weaver and town councillor who founded a branch of the Fugger trading family. His father Hans had moved to Augsburg in 1367 and built a fortune in weaving and textiles. After Hans died in 1408, Jakob's mother Elisabeth continued the business, assisted by her sons Andreas and Jakob, both trained as goldsmiths. The family prospered in the first decades of the 15th century. In 1441 Jakob married Barbara Bäsinger, daughter of the mint master Franz Bäsinger; they had eleven children. He separated from the family business in 1454 and by 1461 ranked among Augsburg's twelve richest citizens. His son Jakob the Rich later expanded the firm across Europe.
zh: 老雅各布·富格尔（1398—1469）是奥格斯堡商人、织工师傅和市议员，创立了富格尔商人家族的一个支系。他的父亲汉斯于1367年迁到奥格斯堡，靠织造和纺织品贸易积累财富。汉斯于1408年去世后，雅各布的母亲伊丽莎白继续经营生意，儿子安德烈亚斯和雅各布从旁协助，两人都曾学习金匠手艺。15世纪初几十年间，家族日渐兴旺。1441年，雅各布迎娶铸币官弗兰茨·贝辛格之女芭芭拉，两人育有十一个孩子。1454年他从家族生意中分出，独立经营，到1461年已跻身奥格斯堡十二位最富有的市民之列。他的儿子“富翁”雅各布后来将商号扩展到欧洲各地。

en: Jacobus Arminius (1560–1609), born Jakob Hermanszoon at Oudewater, was a Dutch Reformed minister and theologian. His father died when he was young, and his mother was killed in the Spanish massacre at Oudewater in 1575. The mathematician Rudolph Snellius helped him study at Leiden, where he became a professor of theology in 1603. Tasked with defending Calvinist predestination against Coornhert's criticisms, he came instead to teach a grace sufficient for all who believed. His disputes with Franciscus Gomarus split the Dutch Reformed Church. He died at Leiden in 1609, before his followers issued the 1610 Remonstrance and the Synod of Dort of 1618–1619 condemned their doctrines.
zh: 雅各布斯·阿民念（1560—1609），原名雅各布·赫尔曼松，生于奥德瓦特，是荷兰归正会的牧师与神学家。他幼年丧父，母亲在1575年西班牙军队对奥德瓦特的屠杀中遇害。数学家鲁道夫·斯内利乌斯帮助他进入莱顿大学求学，他于1603年成为该校神学教授。他受命为加尔文派预定论辩护、驳斥科恩赫特的批评，却转而主张上帝的恩典足以使一切信者得救。他与弗朗西斯库斯·戈马鲁斯的论争使荷兰归正会分裂。他于1609年在莱顿去世，此后追随者于1610年提出《抗辩书》，1618至1619年的多德会议则将他们的教义定罪。

en: Jacques Cartier (1491–1557) was a Breton mariner from Saint-Malo whom Francis I commissioned to seek a western passage to Asia. On his first voyage in 1534 he explored the Gulf of Saint Lawrence and claimed the Gaspé shore for France. In 1535 he sailed up the Saint Lawrence River to the Iroquoian towns of Stadacona and Hochelaga, later Quebec and Montreal, and adopted the word kanata as the name Canada. His third voyage in 1541 established a short-lived settlement near Quebec; Jean-François de Roberval arrived separately in 1542. Cartier spent his later years at Saint-Malo and his nearby estate, sometimes serving as a Portuguese interpreter. He died at Saint-Malo in 1557, his claims the basis of New France.
zh: 雅克·卡蒂埃（1491—1557）是出身圣马洛的布列塔尼航海家，受法王弗朗索瓦一世委托寻找通往亚洲的西方航路。1534年首次航行时，他考察了圣劳伦斯湾，并在加斯佩海岸为法国立下领土标记。1535年，他沿圣劳伦斯河上溯，抵达后来魁北克和蒙特利尔所在的易洛魁人城镇斯塔达科纳和霍切拉加，并把当地词语“卡纳塔”用作“加拿大”一名。1541年第三次航行时，他在魁北克附近建立了一处短命的定居点；让-弗朗索瓦·德·罗贝瓦尔于1542年另行抵达。卡蒂埃晚年住在圣马洛及附近的庄园，有时担任葡萄牙语翻译。1557年他在圣马洛去世，其地理发现成为新法兰西的立基。

en: Jacques Cœur (c. 1395–1456), a merchant born at Bourges, opened regular French trade with the Levant after buying goods at Damascus in 1432, running his operations from Montpellier. He brought wool, silk and carpets among other goods into France by way of Narbonne. Summoned to Paris by Charles VII in 1436, he became master of the mint, steward of royal expenditure in 1438, and was ennobled in 1441; his loans funded the reconquest of Normandy. In 1451 he was arrested on a fabricated charge of poisoning Agnès Sorel, and in 1453 sentenced to confiscation and exile. Escaping in 1455, he found refuge with the pope in Rome and died on Chios in 1456 while leading a papal fleet to relieve Rhodes.
zh: 雅克·柯尔（约1395—1456）是布尔日商人之子。1432年他在大马士革采购东方货物，以蒙彼利埃为基地，开通法国与黎凡特之间的常规贸易。他经纳博讷将羊毛、丝绸和地毯等货物运入法国。1436年查理七世召他入巴黎任铸币总管，1438年掌管王室开支，1441年受封贵族，他的借款资助了诺曼底收复战。1451年，他被诬陷毒死国王情妇阿涅丝·索蕾而遭逮捕，1453年被判没收财产并流放。1455年他越狱出逃，在罗马受到教皇庇护；1456年奉教皇之命率舰队驰援罗得岛，途中在希俄斯岛病逝。

en: Jacques Necker (1732–1804) was a Genevan banker who served as finance minister to Louis XVI. He moved to Paris in 1748 as a bank clerk, became a partner and later a director of the French East India Company. After making his fortune in Paris, he attacked Turgot's free-trade grain policies in 1775 and was appointed director of the royal treasury in 1776. From 1777 he financed France's part in the American War of Independence by loans. In 1781 he published the Compte rendu, the first public account of the royal budget, and was dismissed months later. Recalled in 1788, his dismissal on 11 July 1789 helped provoke the storming of the Bastille. Recalled again, he faced opposition to tax reform and resigned in 1790; he died in 1804.
zh: 雅克·内克尔（1732—1804）是日内瓦银行家，后任法王路易十六的财政总监。1748年他到巴黎做银行职员，后来成为合伙人，又出任法国东印度公司董事。他在巴黎发迹，1775年撰文抨击杜尔哥的谷物自由贸易政策，1776年被任命为皇家金库主管，1777年起主持法国财政，以举债支持法国参与美国独立战争。1781年他公布《财政报告书》，首次公开王室账目，数月后即被解职。1788年他被召回；1789年7月11日再度被免，成为攻占巴士底狱的导火索之一。他再次获召，税制改革却遭到反对，于1790年辞职，1804年去世。

en: Al-Hariri (c. 1054–1122) was an Arab poet and Arabic-language scholar of the Bedouin Banu Harram tribe, who spent most of his life in Basra under Seljuk rule. After studying jurisprudence he worked as an official writer, dividing his time between business affairs in Basra and literary circles in Baghdad. His fame rests on the Maqamat al-Hariri, fifty anecdotes in rhymed prose that blend verse and storytelling and rank among the most admired works of Arabic literature. He also wrote a long poem on grammar and died in Basra in 1122.
zh: 哈里里（约1054—1122）是贝都因巴努·哈兰部落出身的阿拉伯诗人和阿拉伯语学者，大半生在塞尔柱人统治下的巴士拉度过。他修习伊斯兰教法后担任官方文书，往返于巴士拉的产业与巴格达的文学圈之间。他以《玛卡梅集》闻名，五十篇故事以押韵散文写成、韵散结合，是阿拉伯文学史上最受推崇的作品之一。他还著有一部讨论语法的长诗，于1122年在巴士拉去世。

en: Anbarchi was a Mongol prince of the Ilkhanate, a son of Möngke Temür and grandson of Hulagu. After Gaykhatu's accession in 1291 he was appointed viceroy of the eastern provinces, based at Ray, and led reinforcements to Ghazan in Khorasan against the rebel emir Nawruz, until famine forced his army back to Azerbaijan. In 1292 the faction of the emir Taghachar spread word that Gaykhatu had been killed in Anatolia and urged Anbarchi to claim the throne; distrusting the news, he arrested the envoys instead. He was later accused of revolt and died on 24 September 1294 at Nakhchivan.
zh: 安巴尔赤是伊儿汗国的蒙古宗王，蒙哥帖木儿之子、旭烈兀之孙。1291年海合都即位后，他被任命为东部诸省总督，驻于雷伊，并曾率军前往呼罗珊援助合赞、征讨叛将捏吾鲁兹，后因饥荒被迫退回阿塞拜疆。1292年，异密塔加查尔一系散布海合都在安纳托利亚战死的消息，怂恿他起兵夺位；他不信传言，反而把来使下狱。后来他被控谋叛，于1294年9月24日死于纳希切万。

en: Dilshad Khatun (died 1351) was a Chobanid princess, daughter of the amir Demasq Kaja and granddaughter of Chupan. After her father's execution in 1327 she found refuge at the court of Il-Khan Abu Sa'id, who married her in 1333 after divorcing her aunt Baghdad Khatun. Following Abu Sa'id's death she became the chief wife of the Jalayirid ruler Hasan Buzurg and mother of his successor Shaikh Awais, along with two other sons. She died on 27 December 1351 and was buried at Najaf; contemporaries suspected Hasan Buzurg had her poisoned for sympathizing with the rival Chobanid Malek Ashraf.
zh: 德尔沙德·哈屯（？—1351）是楚邦系蒙古公主，异密德马什克·火者之女、出班的孙女。1327年父亲被杀后，她在伊儿汗不赛因的宫廷中得到庇护；1333年不赛因与她的姑母报达·哈屯离婚，改娶她为妻。不赛因死后，她改嫁札剌亦儿王朝君主大哈散，生下继承人谢赫·乌韦斯等三子。1351年12月27日她去世，葬于纳杰夫；当时人怀疑大哈散因她同情楚邦王公马立克·阿什拉夫而将她毒杀。

en: Esen Temür was a Mongol Ilkhanid prince, son of Prince Anbarchi and grandson of Hulagu's son Möngke Temür, whose name appears in genealogies.
zh: 也先·帖木儿是旭烈兀家族的伊儿汗国蒙古宗王，为宗王安巴赤之子、蒙哥·帖木儿之孙，其名见于谱系记载。

en: Hasan Buzurg (c. 1305–1356) founded Jalayirid rule in Iraq and Persia. A Jalayir amir, after the Ilkhanate collapsed in 1335 he became its supreme commander and kingmaker: in 1336 he set up the child Muhammad Khan at Tabriz after defeating 'Ali Padshah at Qara Darra. Defeated by the Chobanid Hasan Kucek at Ala Tagh in 1338 and on the Jaghatu in 1340, he withdrew to Baghdad and built an independent state there, ruling as ulus beg without taking the khan's title. He died in July 1356 and was buried at Najaf, succeeded by his son Shaikh Awais.
zh: 大哈散（约1305—1356），又称谢赫·哈散，是札剌亦儿王朝在伊拉克和波斯统治的奠基者。他出身札剌亦儿部，在伊儿汗廷为异密；1335年伊儿汗国瓦解后，他成为军队最高统帅和拥王者，1336年在卡拉达拉击败阿里·帕迪沙，将年幼的麻合马扶上大不里士的汗位。1338年在阿拉塔格、1340年在贾加图相继被楚邦系的小哈散击败后，他退守巴格达，建立独立政权，只称兀鲁思异密而不称汗。1356年7月他去世，葬于纳杰夫，其子谢赫·乌畏思继位。

en: Möngke Temür (23 October 1256 – 26 April 1282) was the youngest son of the Ilkhan Hulagu by an Oirat wife. In 1266 Abaqa placed him on the Caucasus frontier against the Golden Horde. Betrothed at five to Abish Khatun, ruler of Shiraz, he married her in 1272 and helped govern Fars. In 1281 he led an army, with Armenian and Georgian allies, against the Mamluk sultan Qalawun in Syria, was wounded, defeated, and fled to Mosul. Abaqa's chosen heir, he died suddenly in April 1282, days after his brother. His son Anbarchi was accused of revolt and died in 1294.
zh: 蒙哥帖木儿（1256年10月23日—1282年4月26日）是伊儿汗旭烈兀与一位斡亦剌部妻子所生的幼子。1266年，兄长阿八哈命他镇守高加索边境，防御金帐汗国。他五岁时与设拉子女统治者阿必失哈敦订婚，1272年成婚，并参与治理法尔斯。1281年，他率领大军，会同亚美尼亚和格鲁吉亚盟军，在叙利亚迎战马穆鲁克苏丹嘉拉温，负伤战败，退往摩苏尔。他本是阿八哈选定的继承人，却于1282年4月在阿八哈死后数日猝逝。其子安巴尔赤被控谋叛，1294年死去。

en: Muhammad Khan (died 1338), born Hussein, was a child claimant to the Ilkhanid throne. In 1336 the Jalayirid amir Hasan Buzurg raised him to power under the regnal name Muhammad Khan, opposing the rival khan Musa. In July 1336 their army defeated 'Ali Padshah and Musa at the Battle of Qara Darra, and Hasan Buzurg installed him in Tabriz. He reigned only as a Jalayirid puppet: on 16 July 1338 the Chobanids under Hasan Kucek defeated them at Ala Tagh near Van, and Muhammad Khan was captured and executed.
zh: 麻合马（？—1338），原名忽辛，是伊儿汗位的年幼竞争者。1336年，札剌亦儿异密大哈散将他扶上汗位，取汗号麻合马，与敌对可汗木撒相抗；同年7月，他们的军队在卡拉达拉之战击败阿里·帕迪沙与木撒，大哈散随即将他安置在大不里士。他不过是札剌亦儿人的傀儡：1338年7月16日，小哈散率领的楚邦军队在凡湖附近的阿拉塔格将其击败，麻合马被俘并处死。

en: Jan Długosz (1415–1480) was a Polish canon, diplomat and chronicler, regarded as Poland's first historian. Educated at the Kraków Academy from 1428, he served Bishop Zbigniew Oleśnicki as secretary and chancellor, and was ordained a priest in 1436. In 1450 he persuaded John Hunyadi and Jan Jiskra of Brandýs to sign a truce after six days of talks. He undertook missions for Casimir IV, including peace negotiations in the Thirteen Years' War and the education of the king's sons from 1467. He is best known for his Latin Annals of the Famous Kingdom of Poland in twelve books, covering 965–1480, and his Banderia Prutenorum of 1448 on Grunwald. Nominated Archbishop of Lwów, he died in 1480 just before the pope confirmed his elevation.
zh: 扬·德乌戈什（1415—1480）是波兰教士、外交官与编年史家，被视为波兰第一位历史学家。他1428年起在克拉科夫学院求学，后任克拉科夫主教兹比格涅夫·奥莱希尼茨基的秘书兼掌玺官，1436年晋铎。1450年，他经过六天谈判，说服亚诺什·匈雅提与布兰迪斯的扬·伊斯克拉签订停战协定。他为卡齐米日四世执行多项外交使命，包括十三年战争中的和谈，1467年起负责教导王子。他以拉丁文十二卷《著名波兰王国编年史》闻名，记事上起965年、下至1480年；另著有1448年记述格伦瓦德之战的《普鲁士旗帜图谱》。他被提名为利沃夫大主教，1480年在教皇批准前不久去世。

en: Jan Długosz (1415–1480) was a Polish priest, diplomat and chronicler, regarded as Poland's first historian. He studied at Kraków Academy from 1428 to 1431 without taking a degree. Ordained in 1436, he became a canon of Kraków and chancellor to Bishop Zbigniew Oleśnicki. Casimir IV Jagiellon used him in negotiations with the Teutonic Knights during the Thirteen Years' War of 1454–1466 and, from 1467, as tutor to his sons. His Banderia Prutenorum of 1448 recorded the 1410 Battle of Grunwald, and his Annals of the Famous Kingdom of Poland surveyed the nation's history from earliest times to 1480. He was nominated Archbishop of Lwów shortly before dying in Kraków in 1480.
zh: 扬·德乌戈什（1415—1480）是波兰神父、外交家和编年史家，被视为波兰第一位历史学家。1428—1431年，他在克拉科夫学院求学，但没有获得学位。1436年晋铎后，他成为克拉科夫法政牧师，并任克拉科夫主教兹比格涅夫·奥莱希尼茨基的秘书长。卡齐米日四世·雅盖隆契克派他参与十三年战争（1454—1466）期间对条顿骑士团的谈判，1467年起又命他教导王子。他1448年写成的《普鲁士军旗》记录了1410年的格伦瓦德之战，代表作《波兰史》则记载了波兰自起源至1480年的历史。他在临终前获提名为利沃夫大主教，同年于克拉科夫去世。

en: Jan Kochanowski (1530–1584), born at Sycyna near Radom, was the foremost poet of the Polish Renaissance. He wrote in Polish and Latin, adapting and popularizing forms of Polish verse. Educated at Kraków, Königsberg and Padua, he travelled in Italy and France and met Pierre de Ronsard before returning to Poland in 1559. From about 1564 he served as royal secretary to Sigismund II Augustus and attended the 1569 Sejm of Lublin that sealed the Union of Lublin. After retiring to his Czarnolas estate he wrote The Dismissal of the Greek Envoys (1578), the first Polish tragedy, and the Laments (1580) mourning his daughter Urszula. His Epigrams appeared in 1584, the year he died at Lublin.
zh: 扬·科哈诺夫斯基（1530—1584），生于拉多姆附近的瑟齐纳，是波兰文艺复兴时期最杰出的诗人。他以波兰语和拉丁语写作，改造并推广了波兰语诗歌形式。他曾在克拉科夫、柯尼斯堡和帕多瓦求学，游历意大利与法国，见过诗人皮埃尔·德·龙萨，1559年回到波兰。约1564年起，他担任国王齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特的王室秘书，出席了1569年确立卢布林联合的卢布林议会。退居恰尔诺拉斯庄园后，他写下波兰第一部悲剧《希腊使节的辞别》（1578）和悼念亡女乌尔苏拉的《挽歌》（1580）。他的《警句集》于1584年出版，同年他卒于卢布林。

en: Jan Žižka of Trocnov (c. 1360–11 October 1424) was the Czech knight who led the Taborite Hussites against the crusades, undefeated. Born into the lower nobility of Bohemia, he served at the royal court; a later history records that he was chamberlain to Queen Sofia. A follower of Jan Hus who had fought at Grunwald in 1410, he led the Hussite army to victory at Sudoměř and on Vítkov Hill in 1420 and against Sigismund's host at Kutná Hora in 1421. He drilled townsmen and peasants to fight behind armoured wagon forts mounting cannon, using terrain and gunfire against cavalry charges. Wounded at Rabí in 1421, he lost his remaining eye but kept command until his death before Přibyslav on 11 October 1424.
zh: 特罗茨诺夫的扬·杰式卡（约1360—1424年10月11日）是率领塔博尔派胡斯军抗击十字军、一生未尝败绩的捷克骑士。他出身波希米亚下层贵族，曾在王室宫廷任职；据后来的史书记载，他还担任过索菲娅王后的侍从官。他追随扬·胡斯，曾参加1410年格伦瓦德之战；1420年率胡斯军在苏多梅日和维特科夫山获胜，1421年又在库特纳霍拉大破西吉斯蒙德的大军。他操练市民与农民，依托装有火炮的装甲“战车工事”作战，凭地形与火力克制骑兵冲锋。1421年他在围攻拉比城堡时负伤，仅存的一目也告失明，却仍坚持指挥，直到1424年10月11日在围攻普日比斯拉夫期间病逝军中。

en: Aisu Tsunenobu was a head of the Aisu warrior clan of Kii Province in the Kamakura period. As jitō, steward of the Nambu, Mitsu and Akitsu manors, he built Kinugasa Castle on Mount Kinugasa. His castle overlooked the Nakahechi route of the Kumano road and Tanabe Bay to the south, and Akitsuno to the north. After the Hōji War in 1247 he resigned his stewardship and, in his later years, moved his residence from Nambu Hall to the castle, which became the seat of the Kii Aisu clan. The Aisu were a seafaring clan based in the Kumano region.
zh: 爱洲经信是镰仓时代纪伊国豪族爱洲氏的首领，曾任国内南部庄、三栖庄、秋津庄的地头，在衣笠山修筑衣笠城。他的城堡向南俯瞰熊野街道中边路与田边湾，向北俯瞰秋津野。1247年宝治合战之后他辞去职务，晚年把居馆从南部馆迁到衣笠城，该城此后成为纪伊爱洲氏的居城。爱洲氏是以熊野为据点、从事海运的武士豪族。

en: Akamatsu no Hisanori was the second head of the Akamatsu warrior house of Harima Province, succeeding his father Ienori. In 1233 he fought at Sayo and slew Sugawara no Mitsasuke, a local warrior who became the subject of many legends.
zh: 赤松久范是播磨国赤松武家的第二代当主，继其父家范之后统领家族。1233年，他在佐用与当地武士菅原满佐交战并将其讨杀，满佐后来成为诸多传说的主角。

en: Akamatsu no Ienori was an early Kamakura-period warrior and, per the genealogical work Sonpi Bunmyaku, Norikage’s heir and the first of his line to take the name Akamatsu, after his father became steward of Akamatsu estate in Harima.
zh: 赤松家范是镰仓时代初期的武士。据谱系书《尊卑分脉》记载，他是则景的嗣子，在父亲出任播磨国赤松村地头之后，成为家族中首个以赤松为姓的人。

en: Akamatsu Mitsunori (1320–1381), also called Shichijō Mitsunori after his Kyoto residence, was a Nanbokuchō-era commander and shugo of Settsu Province. The eldest son of Akamatsu Norisuke and grandson of Norimura, he inherited the Settsu shugo post in 1351 after his father's sudden death, while the clan headship and Harima passed to his uncle Sokuyū. In 1352 he helped the Northern Court retake Kyoto from the Southern Court and fought at the siege of Otokoyama. He lost the Settsu post to Sasaki Dōyō in 1360, regained it in 1363, and was replaced again in 1374. He died in 1381.
zh: 赤松光范（1320—1381）是南北朝时代的武将、摄津国守护，因住在京都七条的宅邸，又称七条光范。他是赤松范资的嫡男、赤松则村（圆心）之孙。1351年父亲急逝后，他承袭摄津守护之职，家督与播磨国则归叔父赤松则祐。1352年，他协助北朝从南朝手中夺回京都，并参加男山包围战（八幡之战）。1360年，摄津守护之职被佐佐木道誉取代；1363年再任，1374年又被替换。他于1381年去世，享年62岁。

en: Akamatsu Norimura (1277–1350), also known by his dharma name Enshin, was the fourth head of the Akamatsu clan and shugo of Harima Province. In January 1333 he answered Prince Morinaga's call and rose against the Hōjō, helping Ashikaga Takauji storm the Rokuhara headquarters in Kyoto. The Kenmu regime soon confiscated his governorship, so in 1335 he backed Takauji's revolt. In 1336 he held Shirohata Castle for fifty days against Nitta Yoshisada's army, enabling Takauji's victory at the Minato River. He died suddenly in Kyoto in 1350.
zh: 赤松则村（1277—1350），法名圆心，是赤松氏第四代当主、播磨国守护。1333年1月，他响应护良亲王的令旨举兵反抗北条氏，协助足利尊氏攻陷京都的六波罗探题。建武新政开始后不久，他的播磨守护职被没收，遂于1335年追随尊氏反叛。1336年，他据守白旗城抵御新田义贞的大军五十日，为尊氏在凑川取胜争取了时间。1350年，他在京都突然去世。

en: Akamatsu Norisuke (died 1351) was the legitimate heir of Akamatsu Norimura and fifth head of the Akamatsu clan. In 1333 he fought beside his father in the attack on the Kamakura shogunate's Rokuhara headquarters in Kyoto. When the Kenmu regime withheld the clan's rewards, he followed his father into Ashikaga Takauji's service against the imperial court, and Takauji appointed him shugo of Settsu Province. In 1350 he succeeded as clan head and took Harima as well. He fought at Uchidehama during the Kannō Disturbance and died suddenly at his Kyoto residence in 1351.
zh: 赤松范资（？—1351）是赤松则村的嫡男、赤松氏第五代当主。1333年，他随父参加攻打京都六波罗探题的战役。建武新政对赤松氏恩赏冷淡，他便随父转投足利尊氏，与朝廷军作战，之后被尊氏任命为摄津国守护。1350年父亲去世，他继任家督并领有播磨。观应扰乱中他参加打出滨之战，1351年在京都的宅邸突然去世。

en: Akamatsu Norisuke, also called Sokuyū (1314–1371), was a Nanbokuchō-era commander, sixth head of the Akamatsu clan and son of Akamatsu Norimura. Once a monk on Mount Hiei, he served Prince Morinaga and in 1333 carried the prince's anti-shogunate order to his father. He held Kanjōyama Castle against Nitta Yoshisada in 1336. In 1351 he succeeded his elder brother as clan head and shugo of Harima, adding Bizen in 1355. In 1361, after rebels seized Kyoto, he sheltered the young Ashikaga Yoshimitsu at Shirahata Castle. Appointed to the Zenritsugata in 1370, he died in Kyoto the next year.
zh: 赤松则祐（1314—1371）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，赤松氏第六代当主，赤松则村之子。他年轻时在比叡山延历寺出家，跟随护良亲王转战；1333年作为亲王使者，把倒幕令旨送交其父，赤松氏遂在播磨举兵。1336年，他据守感状山城，力抗新田义贞的大军。1351年兄长范资急逝后，他继任家督与播磨国守护，1355年又兼任备前国守护。1361年京都被叛军占领时，他把年幼的足利义满安置在白旗城避难。1370年就任禅律方，次年在京都去世。

en: Akamatsu Sadanori (1306–c. 1374) was a commander and shugo daimyō of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, the second son of Akamatsu Norimura. In 1333 he joined his father's campaign against the Kamakura shogunate, defeating a Hōjō force at Funasaka Pass in Bizen and helping defend Mount Maya in Settsu. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji at the battle of Hakone-Takenoshita in 1335 and later organized the Akahata ikki for the Northern Court. In 1349 he built Himeyama Castle, the nucleus of later Himeji Castle. He held Mimasaka Province as shugo from 1356 until the bakufu replaced him in 1364.
zh: 赤松贞范（1306—约1374）是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，赤松则村（圆心）的次子。1333年，他随父参加倒幕之战，在备前国舟坂峠击败伊东宣祐，又在摄津国摩耶山击退幕府军。1335年，他追随足利尊氏参加箱根·竹之下之战，南北朝时期归附北朝，组织赤旗一揆，为室町幕府的确立效力。1349年春，他修筑姬山城，即日后姬路城的前身。1356年起出任美作国守护，1364年被幕府替换。

en: Akamatsu no Shigenori was the third head of the Akamatsu warrior house of Harima Province and the father of Akamatsu no Norimura, better known as Enshin, who led the clan in the Genko War of 1333.
zh: 赤松茂则是播磨国赤松武家的第三代当主，是赤松则村之父。则村法名圆心，在1333年的元弘之乱中统率赤松一族作战。

en: Akamatsu Tomonori was a Nanbokuchō-era commander, a son of Akamatsu Norisuke and grandson of Norimura, though the Taiheiki names his uncle Sokuyū as his father. He fought consistently for Ashikaga Takauji through the Kannō Disturbance. In the second month of 1351 he joined Sokuyū under Kō no Moronao to attack Ishidō Yorifusa at Kōmyōji in Harima. In 1355 he served Ashikaga Yoshiakira at the battle of Jinnan in Settsu, where he charged enemy general Yamana Morouji and scattered his troops, himself suffering severe wounds.
zh: 赤松朝范是南北朝时代的武将，赤松范资之子、赤松则村之孙，不过《太平记》把叔父则祐记作他的父亲。观应之扰乱期间，他始终追随足利尊氏。1351年二月，他随则祐听命于高师直，攻打播磨光明寺的石堂赖房。1355年，他随足利义诠参加摄津神南合战，直扑敌将山名师氏、冲散敌军，自己也身负重伤。

en: Akamatsu Ujinori (1330–1386) was a Nanbokuchō-era commander, the fourth son of Akamatsu Norimura. A warrior famed for his strength, he quarreled with his three elder brothers and, unlike them, sided with the Southern Court in the Kannō Disturbance. In 1353 he helped defeat Ashikaga Yoshiakira, and in 1355 he joined Yamana Tokiuji in briefly retaking Kyoto. In 1360 he joined Prince Akamatsu's rebellion, then surrendered to Sokuyū. He rose again in 1369 and 1386; after the last revolt, Hosokawa Yorimoto's forces trapped him and he killed himself at Kiyomizu-dera with over a hundred followers.
zh: 赤松氏范（1330—1386）是南北朝时代的武将，赤松则村的四男。他以力大闻名，与三位兄长不和，观应之扰乱中与兄长们不同，投向南朝。1353年，他参与击败足利义诠；1355年与山名时氏一度夺回京都。1360年他附和赤松宫谋反，随后归降则祐；1369年和1386年两度再度起兵，最后遭细川赖元的军队围困，与百余名追随者在清水寺自尽。

en: Akana Tsunetsura, also called Saba Tsunetsura, was a local lord of Izumo Province. The second son of Saba Sanetsura, he became jitō of Akana Manor in Iishi District and built Akana Castle in 1377; his descendants took the clan name Akana from the manor.
zh: 赤穴常连，一称佐波常连，是出云国的国人领主。他是佐波实连的次男，出任饭石郡赤穴庄地头，1377年修筑赤穴城，其后人以庄园地名为号，改称赤穴氏。

en: Aki Chikauji was a warrior of the Aki clan in Tosa Province. Tradition records that in 1309 he fortified a site in Aki District in eastern Tosa, building Aki Castle, which thereafter served as the clan's stronghold.
zh: 安艺亲氏是土佐国安艺氏的武将。相传1309年，他在土佐国东部的安艺郡筑城，即安艺城，此后该城便成为安艺氏的据点。

en: Aki no Sanenobu is known only from the Aki clan genealogy of Tosa Province, which makes him the last head of the Tosa Soga line and the first to bear the name Aki. His sons founded the Aki main house and the Hatakeyama branch.
zh: 安芸实信仅见于土佐国安芸郡《安芸市史》所收的安芸氏系图。系图将他列为土佐苏我氏谱系的末代当主，也是首位以安芸为苗字者。诸子分别开创安芸本家与分家畑山氏，安芸氏由此分为两支。

en: Aki no Tomonobu was a son of Aki no Sanenobu who succeeded his father as head of the Aki house of Aki District, Tosa Province, and was followed by his son Tomochika.
zh: 安芸知信是安芸实信之子，继承了土佐国安芸郡的安芸本家，之后由其子安芸知亲继任当主。

en: Akizuki Taneaki was the eighth head of the Akizuki clan of Chikuzen Province. The son of the seventh head, Akizuki Tanetaka, he succeeded his father as clan head and was the father of the ninth head, Akizuki Tanemichi.
zh: 秋月种显是筑前国秋月氏的第八代当主，为第七代当主秋月种高之子。他继任父亲的家督，其子即第九代当主秋月种道。

en: Akizuki Taneie was the third head of the Akizuki clan of Chikuzen Province. He was the son of the second head, Akizuki Taneyuki, whom he succeeded, and was himself succeeded by his son Akizuki Taneyori.
zh: 秋月种家是筑前国秋月氏的第三代当主，为第二代当主秋月种幸之子。他在父亲之后继任家督，死后由其子秋月种赖继承。

en: Akizuki Tanemichi was a warrior of the Nanboku-cho period and the ninth head of the Akizuki clan, lords of Akizuki in Chikuzen Province. In 1336 he fought on the loyalist Southern Court side under the Kikuchi at the Battle of Tatarahama against Ashikaga Takauji's army. The Akizuki were routed and lost more than twenty of their clansmen. Tanemichi broke away and fled as far as Dazaifu, where pursuing troops surrounded him and killed him in the third month of 1336.
zh: 秋月种道是日本南北朝时代的武将，筑前国秋月氏第九代当主。1336年，他在多多良滨之战中隶属于菊池氏麾下的南朝宫方，迎战足利尊氏的军队。秋月军大败，二十余名同族战死。种道脱离战线，一路逃到大宰府，仍被追兵包围，最终于1336年农历三月战死。

en: Akizuki Tanekatsu, born Harada Tanekatsu, was a warrior of Chikuzen Province in northern Kyushu and the founder of the Akizuki clan. He lived at the castle of Harada Tanenao, described as his elder brother, though another account makes him Tanenao's son. His Harada family served the Taira, and he fought for the Taira cause when the Taira court fled to Kyushu in 1183. The Akizuki family genealogy records that he went into hiding after the Taira destruction at Dannoura in 1185 and Tanenao's capture. Around 1203 the Kamakura shogunate granted him the Akizuki manor; he settled there, took the name Akizuki and built Mount Kosho castle, founding the line of Akizuki lords.
zh: 秋月种雄原名原田种雄，是九州北部筑前国的武士，秋月氏的始祖。他曾住在原田种直的居城；种直被称为他的兄长，也有一说认为种雄是种直之子。他出身的原田氏为平家家人，1183年平氏奉安德天皇逃往北九州时，他随族人继续为平家作战。据《秋月家谱》记载，1185年平家在坛之浦覆灭、种直被捕后，他一度藏身匿迹。1203年前后，他获镰仓幕府封给秋月庄，入居秋月一地，改称秋月氏，并修筑古处山城，开创了秋月氏世代统治该地的家系。

en: Akizuki Tanesada was the sixth head of the Akizuki clan of Chikuzen Province. He was the son of the fifth head, Akizuki Tanesuke, whom he succeeded, and was in turn succeeded by his son Akizuki Tanetaka.
zh: 秋月种贞是筑前国秋月氏的第六代当主，为第五代当主秋月种资之子。他在父亲之后继任家督，死后由其子秋月种高继承。

en: Akizuki Tanesuke was the fifth head of the Akizuki clan of Chikuzen Province. The son of the fourth head, Akizuki Taneyori, he succeeded his father as clan head and was succeeded by his own son, Akizuki Tanesada.
zh: 秋月种资是筑前国秋月氏的第五代当主，为第四代当主秋月种赖之子。他继任父亲的家督，死后由其子秋月种贞继承。

en: Akizuki Tanetada was a head of the Akizuki clan of Asakura District, Chikuzen Province in northern Kyūshū, and the son of Akizuki Tanemichi, under whom the clan fought for the Southern Court at the Battle of Tatarahama in 1336.
zh: 秋月种忠是九州北部筑前国朝仓郡武家秋月氏的当主，为秋月种道之子；种道在世时，秋月氏于1336年的多多良滨之战中追随南朝一方，与足利尊氏作战。

en: Akizuki Tanetaka was the seventh head of the Akizuki clan, lords of Akizuki in Chikuzen Province. He succeeded his father, the sixth head Akizuki Tanesada, and was himself succeeded by his son Akizuki Taneaki.
zh: 秋月种高是筑前国秋月氏的第七代当主，其家世代领有筑前秋月一地。他继任父亲第六代当主秋月种贞的家督，死后由其子秋月种显继承。

en: Akizuki Taneyori was the fourth head of the Akizuki clan, the warrior family based at Mount Kosho castle in Chikuzen Province. He succeeded his father, the third head Akizuki Taneie, and was in turn succeeded by his son Akizuki Tanesuke.
zh: 秋月种赖是筑前国秋月氏的第四代当主，该家族以筑前的古处山城为据点。他继任父亲第三代当主秋月种家的家督，死后由其子秋月种资继承。

en: Akizuki Taneyuki was the second head of the Akizuki clan, the warrior family founded at Akizuki in Chikuzen Province by his father, Akizuki Tanekatsu. He succeeded his father as clan head and was in turn succeeded by his son Akizuki Taneie.
zh: 秋月种幸是筑前国秋月氏的第二代当主。秋月氏由他的父亲秋月种雄在筑前秋月一地开创，种幸在种雄之后继任家督，死后由其子秋月种家继承。

en: Anayama Yoshitake, first named Norinobu, was a son of the Kai governor Takeda Nobutake and is counted as the founder of the Anayama clan. Genealogies make him Nobutake's third son. He settled at Anayama in Koma District of Kai Province and took the place name as his family name. The Taiheiki records that in the tenth month of 1359 he accompanied the Zen monk Hatakeyama Dōsei up to Kyoto, together with his elder brother Takeda Nobunari. Having no son of his own, he was succeeded by his grandnephew Anayama Mitsuharu, born Takeda Nobumoto.
zh: 穴山义武，初名范信，是甲斐守护武田信武之子，诸系图称其为信武三男，被尊为穴山氏之祖。他以甲斐国巨摩郡穴山为据点，改称穴山姓。《太平记》记载，1359年十月他随禅门畠山道誓上洛，同行者还有其兄武田信成。他没有亲生子嗣，由侄孙穴山满春（初名武田信元）作为养子继承穴山氏。

en: Andō Iesue (fl. 1330–1338) was a Mutsu Province commander of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, Andō Morosue's younger brother and a traditional son of Andō Munesue. In 1333 he and his brother fought for the imperial court at the siege of Daikōji Castle. They later switched to the Northern Court, and in 1336 Shiba Ienaga appointed Iesue Tsugaru battle magistrate, and Iesue attacked the pro-Southern Nanbu clan. Kitabatake Akiie's letters accuse him of seizing Tsugaru and Sotogahama under conflicting claims of authority. After 1338 he vanishes from the records, replaced by his brother.
zh: 安藤家季（活跃于1330—1338年）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代陆奥国的武将，安藤师季之弟，相传同为安藤宗季之子。1333年，他与兄长一同作为朝廷方参加大光寺城之战。后来兄弟改投北朝，1336年斯波家长任命家季为津轻合战奉行，家季进攻南朝方的南部氏。北畠显家的御教书指责他借两头授权之名强占津轻与外滨。1338年以后，家季不见于史料，由其兄接替。

en: Andō Morosue (fl. 1325–1341), first named Takasue, was a commander of Mutsu Province in the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, said to be Andō Munesue's son. Deeds of 1325 and 1330 record him inheriting Hanawa District lands and western Tsugaru. He fought for the court at Daikōji Castle in 1333, and Kitabatake Akiie confirmed his lands in 1334 and 1335. In 1338 he replaced his brother Iesue as Tsugaru battle magistrate. He took a character from Kō no Moronao to form the name Morosue, and in 1341 briefly rejoined the Southern Court, playing both courts to protect his domain.
zh: 安藤师季（活跃于1325—1341年）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代陆奥国的武将，初名高季，相传为安藤宗季之子。1325年和1330年的让状记载，他相继继承了鼻和郡与津轻西滨的领地。1333年，他作为朝廷一方参加大光寺城之战，1334至1335年其领地得到北畠显家承认。1338年，他取代弟弟家季出任津轻合战奉行。他取执事高师直的偏讳改名师季，1341年又一度倒向南朝，在两朝之间周旋以保全领地。

en: Ando Munesue was a late Kamakura warrior based in Hanawa district of Mutsu Province in Tsugaru. Most scholars identify him with Ando Suehisa, who from before 1318 fought his kinsman Ando Suenaga over the Ezo deputy post, sparking the Ando clan war. In 1322 the dispute came before the Hojo Tokuso, and in 1325 Munesue was named Ezo deputy and took the name Munesue. Bakufu troops captured Suenaga in 1326 and a settlement followed in 1328. Surviving deeds record grants to his son Inuhoshi in 1325 and to Takasue in 1330; Inuhoshi is thought by many to have been Morosue's childhood name.
zh: 安东宗季是镰仓时代末期的武将，据点在陆奥国鼻和郡的津轻地方。通说认为他与安东季久为同一人：自1318年以前，季久便与亲族安东季长争夺虾夷代官一职，引发安东氏之乱。1322年纠纷上交北条得宗裁决，1325年宗季被任命为虾夷代官并改用此名。1326年幕府军擒获季长，1328年双方达成和议。留存的让状记载，他于1325年让地给儿子犬法师，1330年让地给高季；一种有力的观点认为犬法师是师季的幼名。

en: Andō Norisue was a Nanbokuchō-era sea lord of Mutsu and Ezo, traditionally a son of Andō Morosue. The Mera Documents place him among the generations of Shimokuni lords, between Morosue and Morisue, with the clan based at Tosa-minato in Tsugaru.
zh: 安藤法季是南北朝时代活动于陆奥、虾夷地的海上豪族，相传为安藤师季之子。《米良文书》所记‘奥州下国殿’的代代当主中，他位列师季与盛季之间，其家族以津轻十三湊为据点。

en: Anenokōji Ietsuna (died 1390) was a fourteenth-century court noble and head of the Anenokōji family, the son of Anenokōji Takamoto. An account names him among those captured alongside his nephew Tadatsuna in fighting against Northern Court forces in Etchū in 1371, though the identity of the governor of Hida involved in that fighting is uncertain. Ietsuna is the first member of his family recorded as governor of Hida Province, named in a court diary under the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month, 1378.
zh: 姊小路家纲（卒于1390年）是14世纪的公卿、姊小路家当主，姊小路高基之子。一种记载称，1371年他与侄子尹纲在越中国同北朝军作战时一同被俘，但参与此战的飞驒国司是否为家纲仍有争议。他是史料中最早可考的飞驒国司姊小路氏，见于1378年8月27日的《后深心院关白记》。

en: Anenokōji Tadatsuna was a Southern Court noble and warrior of the Nanbokuchō era, the son of the lesser captain Anenokōji Yoritoki, titled master of the Left Capital Office. He settled at Furukawa in Yoshiki District, Hida Province, and took the family name Furukawa. In 1371 he was captured fighting Northern Court troops at Kurose in Etchū Province together with his uncle Ietsuna. In 1411 he raised arms at Furukawa Castle over disputed Yamashina family lands, resisting a bakufu army composed of the Kyōgoku, Shiba and Ogasawara clans; on the third day of the ninth month he was killed by Kyōgoku Takakazu in the later-named Hida Revolt.
zh: 姊小路尹纲是南北朝时代的南朝公卿、武将，左少将姊小路赖时之子，官至左京大夫。他定居飞驒国吉城郡古川乡，称古川氏。1371年，他在越中国新川郡黑濑日宫与北朝军交战，与伯父家纲一同被俘。1411年，因围绕山科家领地的争端，他在古川城举兵，抵抗室町幕府派出的京极、斯波、小笠原诸氏讨伐军，同年9月3日被京极高数攻杀，史称飞驒之乱。

en: Anenokōji Takamoto (1297–1358) was a court noble from the late Kamakura era into the Nanbokuchō wars, the son of the courtier Fujiwara no Yorimoto. He reached Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade in 1309 and served as chamberlain until resigning in 1315, after which no office is recorded for him for twenty years. When Emperor Go-Daigo founded the Southern Court at Yoshino in 1336, Takamoto joined it as a lieutenant of the Left Imperial Guards, became master of the Palace Office in 1342, and reached Junior Third Rank in 1347. He died in the third month of 1358.
zh: 姊小路高基（1297—1358）是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的公卿，为朝臣藤原赖基之子。他于1309年叙从五位上，曾任侍从，1315年辞官，此后二十年间没有任官记录。1336年后醍醐天皇在吉野开设南朝朝廷，高基出仕南朝，任左近卫少将，1342年任宫内卿，1347年升至从三位。他于1358年3月去世。

en: Ankan (466–536), the 27th emperor of Japan in the traditional order, was the eldest son of Emperor Keitai by Menokohime of the Owari clan. Born Prince Magari no Ōe, he ascended the throne in 531 after his father's death. During a reign of fewer than five years he worked to enlarge the Yamato court's economic power, ordering the establishment across the provinces of royal granaries called miyake, together with attached service households known as nashiro. He died in 536, and the throne passed to his younger brother, Emperor Senka.
zh: 安闲天皇（466—536）是日本传统世系中的第27代天皇，为继体天皇与尾张氏之女目子媛所生的长子，本名勾大兄。531年父亲去世后即位。在位不足五年，他着力扩充大和朝廷的经济实力，在各国广设屯仓，并配属称名代的服役民户。536年去世，皇位由其弟宣化天皇继承。

en: Ano no Kiminaka was a member of the Ano house in the Kamakura period, a son of Ano Sanenao and father of Ano Kinkado, whose daughter Renshi became the favoured consort of Emperor Go-Daigo.
zh: 阿野公仲是镰仓时代阿野家的人物，为阿野实直之子、阿野公廉之父；公廉之女廉子后来成为后醍醐天皇的宠姬。

en: Ano no Kinkado was a Kamakura-period court noble of the Ano house who rose to lieutenant of the Right Inner Palace Guards. His daughter Renshi became the favoured consort of Emperor Go-Daigo and mother of Emperor Go-Murakami, while his son Sanekado reached junior third rank.
zh: 阿野公廉是镰仓时代阿野家的公卿，官至右近卫中将。其女廉子成为后醍醐天皇的宠姬、后村上天皇的生母，其子实廉则叙从三位。

en: Ano no Kinsuke (c. 1160–before 1226), also called Fujiwara no Kinsuke, was an early Kamakura court noble and founder of the Ano house. The son of Fujiwara no Narichika, he was adopted by Fujiwara no Sanekuni of the Kanin line. In 1185, at Minamoto no Yoritomo's request, he moved from chamberlain to provisional head of the Right Stables Office as a pro-shogunate noble. Slander cost him his court access in 1192, and he later went to Kamakura. He married a daughter of Yoritomo's half-brother Ano Zenjō; their son Sanenao took the Ano name.
zh: 阿野公佐（约1160—1226年前），又名藤原公佐，是镰仓时代前期的公卿、阿野家的家祖。他本是藤原成亲之子，被闲院流的藤原实国收为养子。1185年，在源赖朝的要求下，他作为亲幕府的公卿，由侍从转任右马权头。1192年，他因遭人谗言被停止升殿，后来还曾前往镰仓。他娶源赖朝异母弟阿野全成之女为妻，二人之子实直以阿野为姓。

en: Ano Renshi (1301–1359) was a court lady and favoured consort of Emperor Go-Daigo. A daughter of the court noble Ano no Kinkado, she entered court service in 1319 and bore Go-Daigo Princes Tsuneyoshi (1325), Nariyoshi and Noriyoshi, the future Emperor Go-Murakami (1328). Promoted to junior third rank in 1331, she followed the emperor into exile on Oki after the Genkō War and later went with him to Yoshino. As Go-Murakami's mother she became Southern Court empress dowager, received the ingō Shintaikemon-in in 1351, took Buddhist vows in 1357 and died at Kanshin-ji in Kawachi in 1359.
zh: 阿野廉子（1301—1359）是后醍醐天皇的女官与宠姬。她出身公家，为阿野公廉之女，1319年入仕后宫，后来成为后醍醐的侧室，生下恒良亲王（1325年）、成良亲王和后来成为后村上天皇的义良亲王（1328年）。1331年她叙从三位，元弘之乱后随驾流放隐岐，后又随赴吉野。作为后村上的生母，她成为南朝皇太后，1351年受院号“新待贤门院”，1357年落发出家，1359年在河内观心寺崩逝。

en: Ano Sanenao (1209–1251) was an early Kamakura court noble of the Ano house, the son of Ano Kinsuke. In the twelfth month of 1221, aged thirteen, he was made a chamberlain on the recommendation of Sanjō no Shushi, former consort of Emperor Go-Shirakawa. He rose through the palace guards to lieutenant of the Right Inner Palace Guards, served as assistant governor of Owari, Dewa, Bitchū and Hitachi, and reached junior third rank in 1249. Reappointed chamberlain in 1251, he died on the tenth day of the ninth month that year; his son Kiminaka continued the family line.
zh: 阿野实直（1209—1251）是镰仓时代前期公卿、阿野公佐之子。1221年十二月，年仅十三岁的他经后白河院的女御三条琮子推举叙爵，担任侍从。此后他在近卫府累迁至右近卫中将，并历任尾张、出羽、备中、常陆四国介，1249年叙从三位，跻身公卿。1251年他再任侍从，同年九月初十去世，其子公仲延续了家族血脉。

en: Antoku (1178–1185), son of Emperor Takakura and Taira no Tokuko, was Taira no Kiyomori's grandson. Named crown prince at about a month old, he was enthroned in 1180 at two, with Kiyomori ruling in his name. When the Minamoto seized Kyoto in 1183, the Taira fled west with the boy and the imperial regalia, and their foes enthroned Go-Toba as a rival emperor. At the naval Battle of Dan-no-ura in April 1185 the Taira were destroyed; his grandmother Taira no Tokiko clasped the six-year-old emperor and drowned with him in the Shimonoseki Straits, and the sacred sword was lost.
zh: 安德天皇（1178—1185）是高仓天皇与平清盛之女平德子之子，即清盛的外孙，出生约一个月即被立为太子，1180年两岁时登基，由清盛以他的名义执政。1183年源氏攻占京都，平家带着幼帝与三神器西逃，敌方另立后鸟羽天皇与之并立。1185年4月坛之浦海战中平家覆灭，祖母平时子抱着六岁的安德天皇一同跳入下关海峡溺亡，神剑也随之沉入海中。

en: Arima Iesumi is named in the Hizen-Arima clan genealogy as its third head, after Tomosumi and before Tsurasumi, in the Kamakura period, when the clan held power in southern Takaki District of Hizen Province.
zh: 有马家澄在肥前有马氏谱系中列为第三代当主，位列朝澄之后、连澄之前，时当镰仓时代，有马氏据有肥前国高来郡南部。

en: Arima Mitsuzumi was a head of the Hizen-Arima clan in Takaki District, Hizen Province, during the Northern and Southern Courts period. He succeeded his father Arima Sumiyo and was followed by his son Arima Ujizumi.
zh: 有马满澄是南北朝时期肥前国高来郡肥前有马氏的当主，继承父亲有马澄世，之后由其子有马氏澄继任家督。

en: Arima Sadazumi was the fifth head of the Hizen-Arima clan, a warrior family based at Arima Manor in Takaki District, Hizen Province on Kyūshū. He succeeded his father Tsurasumi and was followed by his son Sumiyo.
zh: 有马贞澄是肥前有马氏第五代当主；该族是以九州肥前国高来郡有马庄为根据地的武士家族。他继承父亲连澄的家督之位，死后由其子澄世继任。

en: Arima Sumiyo was a head of the Hizen-Arima clan, a warrior family holding lands in Takaki District of Hizen Province in Kyushu. In the Northern and Southern Courts wars the clan followed the Kikuchi and the Shoni. In 1353 Sumiyo invited the Soto Zen master Daichi Sokei, who had studied in Yuan China and enjoyed the Kikuchi's patronage, to Kazusa in southern Hizen; there Daichi founded Suigetsusan Entsu-ji, the temple where he died in 1367. Sumiyo was succeeded as clan head by his son Arima Mitsuzumi.
zh: 有马澄世是九州肥前国高来郡在乡武士家族肥前有马氏的当主；南北朝战乱中，有马氏从属于菊池氏和少贰氏。1353年，澄世将曾入元求法、受菊池氏归依的曹洞宗禅师大智祖继迎至肥前南部的加津佐，大智在此创建水月山圆通寺，并于1367年在该寺圆寂。澄世之后，家督由其子有马满澄继承。

en: Arima Tomosumi is listed in the Hizen-Arima clan genealogy as its second head, after Tsunezumi, who took the Arima name after receiving the jitō office of the Arima manor in Hizen around 1213 to 1219.
zh: 有马朝澄在肥前有马氏谱系中列为第二代当主，位列有马经澄之后；经澄于1213—1219年受任肥前国有马庄地头，始称有马氏。

en: Arima Tsunezumi, also called Fujiwara no Tsunezumi, was an early Kamakura-period warrior and the recorded founder of the Hizen-Arima clan. During the Kenpo era of 1213 to 1219 he was granted the jitō office of the Arima manor in Takaki District, Hizen Province, and took the surname Arima, at first written Ajima. During the same era he built Hinoe Castle on the Shimabara Peninsula. Clan tradition called him a descendant of the Heian pirate leader Fujiwara no Sumitomo, though scholars instead trace the family to Taira stewards of nearby Fujitsu manor.
zh: 有马经澄，又称藤原经澄，是镰仓时代前期的武士，肥前有马氏谱系上的初代当主。建保年间（1213—1219年），他获任肥前国高来郡有马庄的地头，从此以有马为姓，最初写作“有间”；同一时期，他在岛原半岛修筑日野江城。家传称他是平安时代海贼首领藤原纯友的后裔，但研究者多认为有马氏实际出自邻近藤津庄庄司平清澄、直澄一脉。

en: Arima Tsurasumi is named in the Hizen-Arima clan genealogy as its fourth head, after Iesumi and before Sadazumi, in the Kamakura period, when the clan held its estates in southern Takaki District of Hizen Province.
zh: 有马连澄在肥前有马氏谱系中列为第四代当主，位列家澄之后、贞澄之前，时当镰仓时代，有马氏在肥前国高来郡南部保有领地。

en: Asakura Hirokage (1254–1352) was a warrior of the Nanboku-chō period and the first head of the Echizen Asakura clan, born in Asakuradani in Tajima Province. After the Kamakura shogunate fell, he took service under Ashikaga Takauji and followed Shiba Takatsune into Echizen. He fought at the Battle of Fujishima against Nitta Yoshisada and was rewarded with Kuromaru Castle, where he took the name Kuromaru Uemon Nyūdō. In 1342 he founded Kōshō-ji temple. He died in 1352, aged about ninety-eight, and was succeeded by his son Takakage.
zh: 朝仓广景（1254—1352）是日本南北朝时代的武将，越前朝仓氏初代当主，生于但马国朝仓谷。镰仓幕府灭亡后，他投奔足利尊氏，随斯波高经进入越前。他在藤岛之战中参加讨伐新田义贞，因战功受赐黑丸城，遂号黑丸右卫门入道。1342年，他建立弘祥寺。1352年，他以约九十八岁高龄去世，家督由其子高景继承。

en: Asakura Takakage (1314–1372) was the second head of the Echizen Asakura clan, serving the Ashikaga shoguns as a retainer of the Shiba. In 1355 he helped defeat a thirty-thousand-strong Southern Court army at the battle before Tō-ji's southern gate in Kyoto, and in 1357 he was made steward of the Asuwa estate. During the Jōji Disturbance of 1366 he joined the bakufu forces against his own lord Shiba Takatsune at Somayama Castle, receiving steward rights over seven Echizen estates and laying the clan's territorial foundation. He died in 1372 and was succeeded by his son Ujikage.
zh: 朝仓高景（1314—1372）是越前朝仓氏第二代当主，以斯波氏被官的身份侍奉足利氏。1355年，他在京都东寺南门外的合战中参与击溃三万南朝大军；1357年被任命为足羽庄的预所。1366年贞治之变中，他加入幕府军，在杣山城攻打自己的主君斯波高经，因此获封越前七处庄园的地头职，奠定了朝仓氏的领地基础。他于1372年去世，家督由其子氏景继承。

en: Asayama Kagetsura, also called Asayama Jirozaemon-no-jo, was a warrior of the Asayama clan of Izumo Province who served Ashikaga Takauji at the time of the Kenmu Restoration. In 1335 he was appointed shugo of Bingo Province, a post he held until 1338, when Niki Yoshinaga succeeded him. The Edo-period chronicle Bingo Kojoki records that he built the fort on Koyajima in 1335, the earliest fortification on the later Kannabe Castle site. He held the titles of saemon-no-jo and Izumo gon-no-kami, and Takauji granted him estates for his service in Aki Province. His son Yoshikage later served the Ashikaga shoguns.
zh: 朝山景连，通称朝山二郎左卫门尉，是出云国朝山氏的武将，在建武新政时期出仕足利尊氏。1335年他被任命为备后守护，在任至1338年，由仁木义长接任。据《备后古城记》记载，他于1335年在古城山筑城，被视为后来神边城最早的城郭。他官任左卫门尉、出云权守，因在安艺国的军功受足利尊氏恩赏领地。其子朝山义景后来也出仕足利氏。

en: Asayama Koremoto, also called Katsube no Sukune Koremoto, was an official of Asayama district in Izumo Province in the late 12th century and a member of the provincial administration.
zh: 朝山惟元又称胜部宿祢惟元，是12世纪末出云国朝山乡的乡司，也是出云国在厅官人。

en: Asayama Koretsuna was an official of Asayama district in Izumo Province and the elder brother of Mototsuna. His daughter married Nogi Mitsutsuna, a son of Sasaki Takatsuna who became steward of Nogi in the early Kamakura period. Their son Takasada inherited Kizu Mishima from his mother. After the Jōkyū War of 1221, most of Koretsuna's family lost their standing, while his brother Mototsuna became head of the Katsube no Sukune lineage.
zh: 朝山惟纲是出云国朝山乡的乡司，也是元纲之兄。他的女儿嫁给野木光纲；光纲是佐佐木高纲之子，镰仓时代初期成为乃木保地头。他们的儿子高定从母亲继承了木津御岛。1221年承久之乱后，惟纲一系大多没落，其弟元纲则成为胜部宿祢一族的惣领。

en: Ōtomo Masamochi, later known as Asayama, went to Izumo as a member of the Kebiishi office during the Tenchō era (824–834) and became a local power.
zh: 大伴政持后来称朝山氏，天长年间（824—834）作为检非违使厅的成员下向出云，成为当地的势力。

en: Shrine tradition names Asayama Yoshimura as steward of Asayama in Izumo Province, entrusted by Minamoto no Yoritomo with worship at Asayama Hachiman Shrine.
zh: 据朝山八幡宫由绪记载，朝山嘉邑是出云国朝山乡的地头，受源赖朝委托兼管该神社的祭祀。

en: Ashikaga Ietoki (1260–1284) was the sixth head of the Ashikaga house and a Kamakura gokenin. Succeeding young, he first appears granting land to a retainer in 1266 and in 1269 set rules for the clan temple Banna-ji. By 1276 he held junior fifth rank as Shikibu dayū, and in 1282 became Iyo no kami, the first warrior to hold it since Minamoto no Yoshitsune. After losing a land suit against a Kōya-san monk in 1279 he grew critical of the shogunate. He took his own life at Kamakura in the sixth month of 1284, succeeded by his son Sadauji.
zh: 足利家时（约1260—1284）是镰仓幕府御家人、足利宗家第六代当主。他幼年继承父亲赖氏，1266年首次见于向被官颁发下文的记载，1269年为氏寺鑁阿寺制定寺规。1276年时已以从五位下任式部大夫，1282年补任伊予守，是自源义经以来第一位出任该职的武家。1279年，他在与高野山金刚三昧院僧人争夺领地的诉讼中败诉，对幕府渐生不满。1284年六月，他在镰仓自尽，由儿子贞氏继嗣。

en: Ashikaga Sadauji (1273–1331) was the seventh head of the Ashikaga house and a late Kamakura gokenin. Succeeding his father Ietoki at about ten, he was guided by the Kō stewards and received his name from the regent Hōjō Sadatoki. As Sanuki no kami he restored the family temples Jōmyō-ji and Banna-ji. He took vows around 1301 and later may have yielded the headship to his eldest son Takayoshi in 1314 or 1315. Takayoshi died in 1317, whereupon Sadauji resumed rule. He died in 1331; his son Takauji inherited and overthrew the Hōjō in 1333.
zh: 足利贞氏（1273—1331）是镰仓时代后期御家人、足利宗家第七代当主。他约十岁继承父亲家时，由执事高氏一族辅佐，元服时得执权北条贞时赐偏讳“贞”字。他官居赞岐守，复兴了足利氏的菩提寺净妙寺和鑁阿寺。他约于1301年出家，后来可能在1314至1315年间把家督让给长子高义。高义于1317年早逝，贞氏再度主持家政。1331年他去世，儿子尊氏继承家督，并于1333年推翻北条氏、灭亡镰仓幕府。

en: Ashikaga Tadafuyu (1327–c. 1400) was an illegitimate son of Shogun Ashikaga Takauji. Unacknowledged by his father and raised as a novice at the Tōshōji in Kamakura, he was adopted around 1345 by Takauji's brother Tadayoshi. He won his first campaign against Southern Court forces in Kii in 1348 and became Nagato tandai by 1349. During the Kannō Disturbance he turned against Takauji, fought in Kyushu and the Chūgoku region, and was briefly named Kyushu tandai in 1351. His faction collapsed after Takauji's death in 1358; his last known letter dates to 1366, and later genealogies place his death in 1400.
zh: 足利直冬（1327—约1400）是日本南北朝时代武将，室町幕府初代将军足利尊氏的私生子。他自幼不被父亲承认，在镰仓东胜寺做小沙弥，约1345年被尊氏之弟直义收为养子。1348年他在纪伊讨伐南朝势力的初阵中立下战功，1349年前后出任统领西国的长门探题。观应之乱中，他与尊氏反目，在九州和中国地方举兵抗衡，1351年一度被任命为九州探题。尊氏1358年死后，其党羽瓦解；存世的最后一封文书作于1366年，后世系图记载他于1400年去世。

en: Ashikaga Tadayoshi (1306–1352), younger brother of the shōgun Takauji, ran the government of the Ashikaga regime while Takauji commanded its armies, the pair being called the two shōguns. After the Hōjō fell he governed Kamakura as deputy to Prince Nariyoshi; when the Nakasendai rebellion overran the city in 1335, he killed the imprisoned Prince Moriyoshi and fled. He shaped much of the 1336 Kenmu Shikimoku, and as a disciple of the Zen master Musō Soseki he expanded the Five Mountains temples. In 1349 his feud with the steward Kō no Moronao broke into the Kannō disturbance, and he was forced to take Buddhist vows. He joined the Southern Court in 1350 and beat Takauji at Uchidehama in 1351, taking Kyoto and then entering Kamakura; Moronao and his brother were killed, yet Takauji then made peace with the south and turned on him. Defeated at Satta Pass, Tadayoshi was held in a Kamakura monastery and died suddenly on 26 February 1352; the Taiheiki says he was poisoned.
zh: 足利直义（1306—1352）是征夷大将军足利尊氏之弟。尊氏掌管军队，直义主持足利政权的政务，时人称兄弟二人为“两将军”。北条氏覆灭后，他奉成良亲王前往镰仓，以副手身份治理当地；1335年中先代之乱攻陷镰仓时，他杀害了被幽禁的护良亲王，随后出逃。1336年的《建武式目》多出自他的主张。他师从禅师梦窗疏石，扩建了五山禅寺体系。1349年，他与执事高师直的积怨爆发为观应扰乱，被迫出家。1350年他投奔南朝，1351年在打出滨击败尊氏，攻占京都，随后进入镰仓，高师直兄弟随后被杀；尊氏却转而与南朝讲和，出兵讨伐他。直义在萨埵山兵败，被幽禁于镰仓的寺院，1352年2月26日突然去世，《太平记》称他是被毒杀的。

en: Ashikaga Takauji (1305–1358) founded the Ashikaga shogunate and split Japan between two imperial courts. In 1333 the Hōjō-run Kamakura shogunate sent him against Emperor Go-Daigo's rising, holding his wife and young son hostage; at Shinomura he declared against the Hōjō instead, and on 7 May his allies took the shogunate's Rokuhara headquarters in Kyoto. The Kenmu Restoration soon lost the samurai's support. After putting down the Nakasendai rebellion in 1335, Takauji rewarded his followers without the court's permission and was declared a rebel. Driven from Kyoto to Kyūshū, he won at Tatarahama, then beat Nitta Yoshisada and Kusunoki Masashige at the Minatogawa in 1336. He enthroned Emperor Kōmyō and issued the Kenmu Shikimoku, while Go-Daigo fled to Yoshino and set up a Southern Court. Made shōgun in 1338, he built Tenryū-ji for the dead Go-Daigo, and ruled with his brother Tadayoshi until the Kannō disturbance set them against each other. He died in 1358, with the south too weak to overthrow the north, and his son Yoshiakira succeeded him.
zh: 足利尊氏（1305—1358）创立室町幕府，也使日本分裂为南北两个朝廷。1333年，北条氏掌权的镰仓幕府派他去镇压后醍醐天皇的举兵，并把他的妻子和幼子扣在镰仓为质；他在丹波篠村改而举兵反对北条氏，5月7日，盟友攻陷幕府设在京都的六波罗探题。建武新政很快失去了武士阶层的支持。1335年平定中先代之乱后，尊氏未经朝廷许可便向追随者论功行赏，被宣布为朝敌。他从京都败退九州，在多多良滨获胜，又于1336年在凑川击败新田义贞和楠木正成。他拥立光明天皇，颁布《建武式目》，后醍醐天皇则逃往吉野另立南朝。1338年他就任征夷大将军，并为已故的后醍醐天皇兴建天龙寺。他起初与弟弟足利直义共同执政，后来两人反目，爆发观应扰乱。1358年他去世时，南朝已无力推翻北朝，由其子足利义诠继任。

en: Ashikaga Takayoshi (1297–1317) was a gokenin of the late Kamakura shogunate and the eldest son of Ashikaga Sadauji by his principal wife, a daughter of Hōjō Akitoki. At his coming of age he took a character from the regent Hōjō Takatoki; his name used the Minamoto character yoshi instead of the customary uji. He held the title Sama-no-suke and in 1315, already acting as head, confirmed a monk's office at Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine. He died in 1317, aged twenty-one, leaving little other record; his younger brother Takauji later won the shogunate.
zh: 足利高义（1297—1317）是镰仓时代末期武将、镰仓幕府御家人，足利贞氏的长子，母亲是正室、北条显时之女释迦堂殿，即足利尊氏、直义的异母兄。元服时他获执权北条高时赐偏讳，取名高义；名字不用足利氏通字“氏”而用清和源氏通字“义”。他官居左马助，1315年已以当主身份向鹤冈八幡宫僧人发出供僧职安堵状。1317年去世，年仅21岁，事迹留存不多；其弟尊氏后来开创了室町幕府。

en: A genealogy cited by the Kai Kokushi records that a niece of the shogun Ashikaga Takauji married the Kai warrior Takeda Nobutake, governor of Aki Province and a trusted commander of Takauji.
zh: 《甲斐国志》所引家谱记载，幕府将军足利尊氏的一位侄女嫁给甲斐源氏武将武田信武；信武曾任安艺国守护，是足利尊氏信赖的部将。

en: Ashikaga Yasuuji (1216–1270) was the fourth head of the Ashikaga house and a Kamakura gokenin. The legitimate son of Ashikaga Yoshiuji by a daughter of the regent Hōjō Yasutoki, he was named for Yasutoki at his coming of age. Appointed Tango no kami in 1236, he served the shōgun Fujiwara no Yoritsune. In 1251 he took vows without the shogunate's leave; the regency seized his Hanabusa manor in Shimōsa and he retired to Ashikaga. His Tokusō-born son Yoriuji became heir after the elder son Ieuji was set aside and founded the Shiba line. He built Chikōji in 1265.
zh: 足利泰氏（1216—1270）是镰仓幕府御家人、足利宗家第四代当主，为足利义氏的嫡男，母亲是执权北条泰时之女，元服时由泰时赐名。1236年任丹后守，出仕幕府将军藤原赖经。1251年，他未经幕府许可擅自出家，被没收下总国埴生庄的领地，退回足利本领隐居。得宗家出身的正室所生之子赖氏被立为继承人，长子家氏遭废嫡，成为斯波氏之祖。1265年他建立智光寺。

en: Ashikaga Yoriuji (1240–1262) was the fifth head of the Ashikaga house and a gokenin of the mid-Kamakura shogunate. A son of Ashikaga Yasuuji by a daughter of Hōjō Tokiuji of the Tokusō line, he was made heir over his elder brothers and held the two provinces of Kazusa and Mikawa. First named Toshiuji, he placed the cap at the 1256 coming of age of the regent's son Hōjō Tokisuke, and was renamed Yoriuji with a character from Hōjō Tokiyori. His last court title was Jibu gon-no-daifu. He died in 1262, aged twenty-three, and his young son Ietoki succeeded him.
zh: 足利赖氏（1240—1262）是镰仓时代中期武将、镰仓幕府御家人，足利宗家第五代当主。他是足利泰氏与北条得宗家北条时氏之女所生之子，虽有兄长，仍被立为嫡子，统领上总、三河两国。初名利氏，1256年为执权北条时赖之子北条时辅元服加冠，得时赖赐偏讳“赖”字，改名赖氏，最终官居治部权大辅。1262年去世，年仅23岁，由年幼的儿子家时继承家督。

en: Ashikaga Yoshiakira (1330–1367), son of Takauji, was the second shōgun of the Ashikaga shogunate. As a child named Senjuō he was left behind in Kamakura as a Hōjō hostage in 1333, and when his father turned on the Hōjō, warriors who stormed the city rallied under his name. Recalled to Kyoto during the Kannō disturbance to replace his uncle Tadayoshi in the government, he fled in 1352 when Southern Court troops seized the capital and captured the Northern Court's imperial family. He retook the city and enthroned Emperor Go-Kōgon without the imperial regalia. He succeeded his father as shōgun in 1358. In 1361 his own steward Hosokawa Kiyouji went over to the south and helped it hold Kyoto briefly; by 1363 the Yamana and Ōuchi had come to pay their respects to his government. In 1367 he entrusted his young son Yoshimitsu to Hosokawa Yoriyuki and died, and was buried beside the grave of the Southern Court warrior Kusunoki Masatsura.
zh: 足利义诠（1330—1367）是足利尊氏之子，室町幕府第二代征夷大将军。他幼名千寿王，1333年被北条氏扣作人质留在镰仓；父亲倒戈反对北条氏后，攻袭镰仓的武士以他的名义集结。观应扰乱期间，他被召回京都，接替叔父足利直义主持政务；1352年南朝军队攻占京都、俘虏北朝的皇室成员，他出逃近江，随后夺回京都，在没有三神器的情况下拥立后光严天皇。1358年他继任将军。1361年，他的执事细川清氏投奔南朝，协助南朝短暂占据京都；到1363年，山名氏和大内氏前来参谒幕府。1367年他把幼子足利义满托付给细川赖之后去世，葬在南朝武将楠木正行墓旁。

en: Ashikaga Yoshikane (1154–1199) was the second head of the Ashikaga clan and a close vassal of Minamoto no Yoritomo, founder of the Kamakura shogunate. When Yoritomo rose in Izu in 1180, Yoshikane joined him in Kamakura, and in 1181 he married a younger sister of Hōjō Masako, becoming Yoritomo's brother-in-law. He fought in the campaigns against the Taira and the northern Fujiwara, and in 1190 led the suppression of a revolt in Dewa. He took Buddhist vows at Tōdai-ji in 1195 and died at the family's Kabasaki temple in 1199.
zh: 足利义兼（1154—1199）是足利宗家第二代当主，也是镰仓幕府开创者源赖朝的亲信御家人。1180年源赖朝在伊豆举兵，义兼在镰仓加入其麾下；1181年他娶北条政子之妹为妻，与赖朝结为义兄弟。他参加了追讨平氏和奥州藤原氏的战事，并于1190年率军平定出羽的叛乱。1195年他在东大寺出家，1199年在足利庄的桦崎寺去世。

en: Ashikaga Yoshiuji (1189–1255) was the third head of the Ashikaga house and a gokenin of the early Kamakura shogunate. A son of Ashikaga Yoshikane by Hōjō Tokiko, daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa, he inherited the family leadership through his mother's Hōjō blood. He supported the Hōjō regents in the Wada conflict of 1213 and the Jōkyū War of 1221, after which he became shugo of Mikawa Province, commanding the road between eastern and western Japan. He held the titles Mutsu no kami and Musashi no kami, took Buddhist vows in 1241, founded Hōrakuji in 1249, and died in 1255.
zh: 足利义氏（1189—1255）是镰仓时代前期武将、镰仓幕府御家人，足利宗家第三代当主。他是足利义兼与北条时政之女时子之子，因母亲出自北条氏而继承家督，一生与北条氏关系密切。他在1213年的和田合战和1221年的承久之乱中辅佐北条义时、泰时父子，乱后获任三河国守护，扼守日本东西往来的要冲；历任陆奥守、武藏守。1241年出家，1249年创建法乐寺，1255年去世。

en: Minamoto no Yoshiyasu, better known as Ashikaga no Yoshiyasu (c. 1125–1157), was a late Heian warrior and founder of the Ashikaga clan. The second son of Minamoto no Yoshikuni, he inherited the Ashikaga manor in Shimotsuke Province and took its name. He served Retired Emperor Toba as a northern guard and became a kebiishi officer and governor of Mutsu. In the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 he led over a hundred horsemen on the side of Emperor Go-Shirakawa, alongside Taira no Kiyomori and Minamoto no Yoshitomo. He died in 1157, little more than thirty years old.
zh: 源义康，通称足利义康（约1125—1157），是平安时代末期武将、足利氏的始祖。他是源义国的次子，继承下野国足利庄后以足利为姓。他出仕退位的鸟羽上皇，担任北面武士，后任检非违使和陆奥守。1156年保元之乱中，他率百余骑加入后白河天皇一方，与平清盛、源义朝并肩作战。他于1157年去世，年仅三十出头。

en: Ashina Morikazu (c. 1285 – 4 September 1335), also known as Ashina Hōgan, was the sixth head of the Ashina clan of Aizu, succeeding his father Morimune. In 1333 he marched on Kyoto with the Kamakura bakufu's army sent to subdue Emperor Go-Daigo, but was defeated. In the seventh month of 1335 he answered Hōjō Tokiyuki's call in the Nakasendai Rebellion and made for Kamakura with Miura Tokitsugu and others. The next month Ashikaga Takauji's counterattack caught him at the Battle of Katasegawa in Sagami, where he was killed. The seventh head, Ashina Naomori, succeeded him.
zh: 芦名盛员（约1285—1335年9月4日），通称芦名判官，是会津芦名氏第六代当主，继父亲第五代当主盛宗之后接任。1333年，他作为镰仓幕府军的一员上洛，追讨后醍醐天皇，却遭败北。1335年7月北条时行发动中先代之乱，他与三浦时继等人响应起兵，赶往镰仓。同年8月，足利尊氏反攻，他在相模国片濑川之战中战死。家督由第七代当主芦名直盛继承。

en: Ashina Morimune, also called Jirō Saemonnojō, was the fifth head of the Ashina clan of Aizu in the late Kamakura period and was succeeded by his son Morikazu.
zh: 芦名盛宗，通称次郎左卫门尉，是镰仓末期会津芦名氏第五代当主，其子盛员继任家督。

en: Ashina Naomori was the seventh head of the Ashina clan in the Nanboku-chō period. In 1335 he succeeded after his father Morimune and his brothers died fighting in the Nakasendai Rebellion. He clashed with local lords such as Shingū Akitsuna and expanded his power from the Jōwa years. In 1352 he abandoned Ashikaga Takauji for the Nitta side at Kotesashigahara, then was driven back into Aizu. A 1373 land guarantee shows him pressing on the Sahara clan's holdings, and tradition credits him with founding the Higashi-Kurokawa residence in 1384, the precursor of Kurokawa Castle.
zh: 芦名直盛是日本南北朝时代芦名氏第七代当主。1335年，父亲盛宗与兄弟在中先代之乱中战死，他继承家督。此后他与新宫明继等当地势力交锋，自贞和年间起扩张势力。1352年小手指原之战时，他背离足利尊氏，倒向新田一方，随后败逃回会津。1373年，他就大荒居村领有权发出安堵状，显示其势力已压迫佐原氏的领地。相传他于1384年修筑黑川城的前身东黑川馆，芦名氏正是在他这一代扎根会津。

en: Ashina Yasumori was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Ashina family, the Aizu offshoot of the Miura clan's Sahara line. A son of Sahara Mitsumori, though one tradition calls him an adopted son-in-law, he was the younger brother of Ashina Tsunemitsu, who became shugo of Hōki in 1272. After Tsunemitsu lost the post and wandered the provinces, Yasumori overran his private estates and called him a beggar; the Kamakura bakufu found him guilty of insult and land grabbing and restored the lands to his brother. Yet the Ashina lords of Aizu who later rose to power descended from Yasumori's line.
zh: 芦名泰盛是镰仓时代武将，属三浦氏佐原流在会津分出的芦名氏。他是佐原光盛之子（一说为婿养子）、芦名经光之弟；经光于1272年出任伯耆守护。经光被解职、流浪各国期间，泰盛侵占其私领，还骂他是讨饭的；镰仓幕府判定泰盛恶口与侵占领地有罪，把领地还给经光。然而后来在会津兴起的芦名氏，恰恰出自泰盛这一支。

en: Aso Korekage was daiguji of Aso Shrine in Higo in the mid-Kamakura period. His descendants formed the Era, Uji and Sakanashi branches. After his grandson Koretane was disowned for an offence, the headship passed from his eldest son Koresuke to his third son Korekuni.
zh: 阿苏惟景是镰仓时代中期肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司。他的子孙分出惠良、宇治、坂梨三家庶流；孙子惠良惟种获罪被勘当后，家督由嫡男惟资转至三男惟国。

en: Aso Korekuni was the third son of Aso Korekage, head of the Aso shrine family in Higo Province. He took the family name Uji, and his son Koretoki became daiguji, chief priest of Aso Shrine, in 1319.
zh: 阿苏惟国是肥后国阿苏神社大宫司家当主阿苏惟景的第三子，分称宇治姓；其子阿苏惟时于1319年就任阿苏大宫司。

en: Uji Korenobu was the earliest historically attested head of the Aso family, the daiguji shrine house of Aso Shrine in Higo Province. By the first half of the twelfth century his line had formed a warrior band that ruled the country around Aso. He is named in the Uji Korenobu ge, a formal report dated the twelfth month of 1142, and he is the first figure in the Aso genealogy collected in the Zoku Gunsho Ruijū whose existence can be verified; the family still used the surname Uji in his lifetime. His successor was Uji Sukenaga.
zh: 宇治惟宣是肥后国阿苏神社大宫司家阿苏氏中，第一个能被史料证实的当主。12世纪上半叶，其族人已组成支配阿苏一带的武士团。康治元年（1142年）12月的文书《宇治惟宣解》中可见其名；在《续群书类从》所收的阿苏氏系图里，他也是第一个能证实确有其人的人物，当时这一家仍以宇治为姓。继其之后的当主是宇治资永。

en: Aso Koresuke, eldest son of daiguji Korekage, headed Aso Shrine in Higo and died young. His line used the surname Era; his son Era Koretane had been disowned for an offence, so the headship passed to his younger brother Korekuni.
zh: 阿苏惟资是大宫司惟景的嫡男，曾任阿苏神社大宫司，早逝。他这一支以惠良为姓；其子惠良惟种获罪被勘当，家督遂由弟弟惟国继承。

en: Aso Koretoki was daiguji, chief priest and lord of Aso Shrine in Higo Province, appointed to the office by 1319. In 1333 he answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call against the shogunate, joining the assault on the Rokuhara tandai in Kyoto and the fighting against Ashikaga Takauji, then retired in favour of his son Korenao. After Korenao killed himself following defeat at Tatara Beach in 1336, Koretoki resumed the headship. Between 1349 and 1351 he switched between the Northern and Southern courts four times. In 1351 he adopted Koremura as heir, and he died in 1353.
zh: 阿苏惟时是肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司，至迟于1319年就任此职。1333年，他响应后醍醐天皇的讨幕纶旨，参加攻打京都六波罗探题，并与足利尊氏作战，随后让位于长子惟直，退居幕后。1336年惟直在多々良滨战败后自尽，惟时只得重管家督。1349至1351年间，他在北朝与南朝之间四次反复改换阵营。1351年，他收惟村为养子继承人，最终于1353年去世。

en: Aso Koretsugu succeeded his father Koreyasu as daiguji, head priest of Aso Shrine in Higo Province. In 1196 Hōjō Tokimasa, custodian of the Aso estates, issued a warrant appointing Koretsugu, then still called Uji Koretsugu, to the daiguji office, and in 1200 his father transferred the Nangō valley lands to him. Tradition places in his time the move of the clan seat south beyond the caldera toward Yabe, and in 1222 he is said to have relocated the Tendai temple Aitōji and fortified its site.
zh: 阿苏惟次继父亲惟泰之后出任肥后国阿苏神社大宫司。1196年，掌管阿苏社领的北条时政发出下文，补任当时仍称宇治惟次的他担任大宫司；1200年，父亲把南乡谷的所领让给他。相传他这一代把本据向南翻过外轮山迁到矢部一带；贞应元年（1222年），他迁移天台宗寺院爱藤寺，在寺迹修筑城郭，相传即为爱藤寺城的起源。

en: Aso Koreyasu was daiguji, head priest of Aso Shrine in Higo Province, and the first of his line to call himself Aso instead of Uji. In 1180 he was made daiguji of the Aso and Kengun shrines as a Genji estate steward. He settled the Nangō valley, opened Kōsa and in 1184 sponsored a branch Aso shrine at Nagoya. Having taken the Taira side in Kyushu during the Genpei War, he was removed by the Kamakura shogunate, which placed it under Hōjō Tokimasa. In 1196 Tokimasa named his son Koretsugu daiguji, and in 1200 Koreyasu handed over his holdings.
zh: 阿苏惟泰是肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司，也是家族中第一个放弃宇治旧姓、改称阿苏的当主。1180年，他以源氏庄官身份被补任为阿苏、健军两座神社的大宫司；此后进入南乡谷，开垦甲佐一带，并于1184年在名越谷劝请阿苏神社分祀。治承·寿永之乱中，他在九州追随平家，镰仓幕府建立后将他解任，阿苏神社交由北条时政管理。1196年，时政任命惟泰之子惟次为大宫司；1200年，惟泰把家族所领让给惟次。

en: Aso Koreyoshi was daiguji, head priest of Aso Shrine in Higo Province, in the early Kamakura period, succeeding his father Koretsugu and followed in the office by Koretada.
zh: 阿苏惟义是镰仓时代前期肥后国阿苏神社的大宫司，接替父亲惟次就任，其后由惟忠继任。

en: Aso Korezumi (c.1309–1364) was a late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō warrior and the Southern Court daiguji of Aso Shrine. Of the disgraced Era branch, he was long called Era Korezumi. In 1333 he defected to Emperor Go-Daigo before Chihaya Castle, and in 1336 fought Ashikaga Takauji at Tatara Beach. He backed Prince Kanenaga in 1337 and in 1340 killed Northern Court claimant Sakanashi Magomarumaru at Nango Castle. Taking Dazaifu with the Kikuchi in 1361 won him recognition as daiguji, though a Northern Court rival split the clan. In 1364 he yielded office to his son Koremura, dying shortly after.
zh: 阿苏惟澄（约1309—1364）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，南朝方的阿苏神社大宫司。他出身获罪的庶流惠良氏，长期自称惠良惟澄。1333年，他在随军攻打千早城途中接到护良亲王令旨，倒向后醍醐天皇的官军；1336年参加多々良滨之战，对抗足利尊氏。1337年，他在九州拥立怀良亲王；1340年攻落肥后南乡城，讨杀北朝方的坂梨孙熊丸。1361年，他协助菊池氏攻占大宰府，被征西府承认为大宫司，但北朝另立竞争者，阿苏家再度分裂。1364年，他把大宫司之职让给儿子惟村，不久后去世。

en: Uji Sukenaga was an early head of the Aso family, the daiguji shrine house of Aso Shrine in Higo Province. In the Aso genealogy he follows Uji Korenobu and precedes Koreyasu, in the age when the family still used the surname Uji.
zh: 宇治资永是肥后国阿苏神社大宫司家阿苏氏的早期当主，在阿苏氏系图的大宫司序列中列于宇治惟宣之后、阿苏惟泰之前，其时尚以宇治为姓。

en: Chikatsuna was a son of Asonuma Hirotsuna and a younger brother of Tomotsuna, the second head. He inherited Tōno manor in Hei District, Mutsu Province, and was said to have gone there himself, though he probably ruled through deputies at first. From 1213 to 1219 he built Yokota Castle on Mount Gomadō as his seat of government. For his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221 he was made jitō of Yano-Arayama manor in Aki Province, where he is credited with building Tokonoyama Castle and founding the Aki branch of the clan.
zh: 亲纲是阿曾沼广纲之子、二代当主朝纲之弟，继承了陆奥国闭伊郡的远野保；相传他曾亲自下向远野，但一般认为初期实际靠代官统治。1213—1219年间，他在护摩堂山修筑横田城，作为统治中心。1221年承久之乱时他立下军功，被补任为安艺国世能荒山庄的地头；相传他还在鸟笼山筑城，阿曾沼氏的安艺一支由此发端。

en: Asonuma Hirotsuna, also called Shirō, was a Shimotsuke warrior of the Fujiwara-descended Ashikaga clan, the fourth son of Ashikaga Aritsuna. He took the name Asonuma from his holding of Asonuma in Aso District. When the head Ashikaga house joined the Taira in the Genpei War, Hirotsuna instead served Minamoto no Yoritomo and became a Kamakura gokenin, fighting under Oyama Tomomasa with his father and his brother Sano Mototsuna against Shida Yoshihiro and Ashikaga Toshitsuna. In 1189 he campaigned in Ōshū and was appointed jitō of Tōno manor in Hei District, Mutsu.
zh: 阿曾沼广纲，通称四郎，是下野国藤姓足利氏的武将，为足利有纲第四子，因领有安苏郡阿曾沼之地而称阿曾沼氏。源平合战时，宗家足利氏站在平家一方，广纲却追随源赖朝，成为镰仓幕府的御家人。他又与父亲有纲、兄长佐野基纲一同加入小山朝政麾下，击败志田义广以及宗家的足利俊纲。1189年，他参加奥州之战，获补任为陆奥国闭伊郡远野保的地头。

en: Kimisato was the fifth head of the Tōno Asonuma and a son of Kintsuna. His brother Mitsusato's descendants formed the Aki branch, while Kimisato kept the clan's lands around Tōno in Mutsu Province. His son Ujitsuna succeeded him as sixth head.
zh: 公乡是远野阿曾沼氏第五代当主、公纲之子。其弟光乡的后裔形成安艺分支，公乡则保有陆奥国远野一带的本领，后由其子氏纲继任第六代当主。

en: Kintsuna was the fourth Asonuma head and a son of Chikatsuna. His son Kimisato continued the main line at Tōno in Mutsu, while the Aki Asonuma traced their descent to his son Mitsusato.
zh: 公纲是阿曾沼氏第四代当主、亲纲之子。其子公乡继承陆奥国远野的嫡流，安艺阿曾沼氏则出自他另一子光乡的后裔。

en: Mitsutsuna, third head of the Asonuma, was a son of Chikatsuna adopted by the heirless Tomotsuna to succeed him. His second son Moritsuna is said to have founded the Masuzawa branch of the Tōno region.
zh: 光纲是阿曾沼氏第三代当主、亲纲之子，被无嗣的伯父朝纲收为养子继承家业。其次子守纲相传是远野地方鱒泽氏的始祖。

en: Tomotsuna was a son of Asonuma Hirotsuna and, by tradition, inherited the family's original lands in Shimotsuke Province. He had no son of his own and made Mitsutsuna, the son of his younger brother Chikatsuna, his heir. He probably held Asonuma Castle.
zh: 朝纲是阿曾沼广纲之子，相传继承了家族在下野国的本领。他没有儿子，立弟弟亲纲之子光纲为继承人，据点大约在阿曾沼城。

en: Asonuma Tomotsuna was lord of the Tōno Asonuma, a warrior house of Fujiwara-descended Ashikaga stock, seated at Yokota Castle in Hei district, Mutsu province. In 1334, the first year of Kenmu, his title to the Tōno estate was confirmed by Kitabatake Akiie, the Southern Court's governor of Mutsu. In the Kenmu or Shōhei era, his second son Jirō went to Ōtsuchi to keep order on the eastern coast of Hei district and built Ōtsuchi Castle as his seat, becoming the founder of the Ōtsuchi house.
zh: 阿曾沼朝纲是远野阿曾沼氏的当主，该族为出自藤原氏的足利一族旁支，据点在陆奥国闭伊郡的横田城。建武元年（1334年），臣属南朝的陆奥国司北畠显家安堵了他对远野保的所有权。建武年间或正平年间，他的次子大槌次郎前往大槌，维持闭伊郡东部沿海地区的治安，并修筑大槌城作为居城，成为大槌氏的始祖。

en: Ujitsuna was the sixth head of the Tōno Asonuma in Mutsu and son of the fifth head, Kimisato. He was the father of the seventh head, Tomotsuna, in whose time Kitabatake Akiie, governor of Mutsu, confirmed the clan's possession of Tōno manor in 1334.
zh: 氏纲是陆奥国远野阿曾沼氏第六代当主、第五代当主公乡之子。其子为第七代当主朝纲；1334年，陆奥国司北畠显家安堵了阿曾沼氏对远野保的所有权。

en: Imperial Prince Atsumi (893–967), known as the Rokujō Prince, was the eighth son of Emperor Uda and a full younger brother of Emperor Daigo. Invested as an imperial prince in 895, he reached the first imperial rank and headed the Shikibu ministry. A gifted musician, he played flute and strings at court ceremonies and led one side of the Teiji-in poetry contest of 913. He resigned his offices in 945, took Buddhist vows as Kakushin at Ninna-ji in 950, and died there in 967 aged seventy-five. His son Minamoto no Masanobu was the ancestor of the Uda Genji line.
zh: 敦实亲王（893—967），称六条宫，是宇多天皇的第八子，醍醐天皇的同母弟。他于895年获亲王宣下，官至一品、式部卿。敦实富有音乐才华，常在宫廷典礼上吹奏笛子、演奏弦乐，并在913年的亭子院歌合中担任右方带头人。他于945年上表辞官，950年在仁和寺剃度出家，法名觉真，967年在寺中去世，终年七十五岁。其子源雅信是宇多源氏一脉的祖先。

en: Bidatsu (538–585), the 30th emperor of Japan, was the second son of Emperor Kinmei by Princess Ishi-hime, daughter of Emperor Senka. Named crown prince in 569, he ascended in 572. His court was dominated by the rivalry between Soga no Umako, who patronised Buddhism, and Mononobe no Moriya, who defended the native kami. Bidatsu leaned toward the traditional cults, and when plague swept the country in 585 he banned Buddhism; he died of it the same year. The Nihon Shoki records that his court established relations with Baekje and Silla. His widow, the half-sister Suiko, later reigned as empress.
zh: 敏达天皇（538—585）是日本第30代天皇，钦明天皇与宣化天皇之女石姬皇女所生的次子。569年被立为太子，572年即位。他在位时，朝廷由苏我马子与物部守屋的对立主导：前者扶持新来的佛教，后者维护传统神祇信仰。敏达本人倾向本土神道教，585年瘟疫蔓延时下令禁佛，同年自己也染疫身亡。据《日本书纪》记载，他的朝廷与百济、新罗建立了关系。他的皇后、异母妹推古在他死后成为女帝。

en: Chiba Kazutane (c. 1310–1336) was the eldest son of Sadatane, eleventh head of the Chiba clan of Shimōsa, and is counted as the clan's twelfth head, though he died before formally succeeding. In the Nanboku-chō war, his father fought their cousin Tanesada for the Chiba headship. Kazutane served the Southern Court under Nitta Yoshisada against Ashikaga Takauji. On the sixteenth day of the first month of 1336, at Shiga village in Tamba province, he was killed in battle by Hosokawa Jōzen of the Ashikaga army. His younger brother Ujitane eventually succeeded their father as Chiba head.
zh: 千叶一胤（约1310—1336）是下总国千叶氏第十一代当主贞胤的嫡男，被列为第十二代当主，但在正式继承家督前战死。南北朝动乱中，父亲贞胤与堂兄胤贞争夺千叶氏家督，一胤则加入南朝方新田义贞的军队，对抗足利尊氏。1336年正月十六日，他在丹波国志贺乡被足利军的细川定禅讨杀。后来由其弟氏胤继承父亲，成为千叶氏当主。

en: Chiba Munetane (1265–1294) was the ninth head of the Chiba clan of Shimōsa and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate, succeeding his father Yoritane in 1275. Ordered to Kyushu on the ikoku keigoban coastal guard after the Mongol invasions, he was stationed in Ogi district, Hizen, where his eldest son Tanesada was born in 1288. While Munetane was absent in Kyushu, his younger brother Tanemune, minding the home estate of Chiba-no-shō, made himself its effective master. Munetane died in 1294; his heirs fought Tanemune's line for the headship, and his second son Taneyasu founded the Kyushu Chiba.
zh: 千叶宗胤（1265—1294）是下总国千叶氏第九代当主、镰仓幕府御家人，1275年继承父亲赖胤。元寇之后，他奉命出任异国警固番役，驻扎在九州肥前国小城郡，1288年其嫡男胤贞即生于当地。宗胤滞留九州期间，留守本领千叶庄的弟弟胤宗成为庄园的实际领主。1294年宗胤去世，其后人为家督之位与胤宗一系相争，次子胤泰则开创了九州千叶氏。

en: A daughter of Chiba Munetane, ninth head of the Chiba clan of Shimōsa, she married Utsunomiya Kintsuna, ninth head of the Utsunomiya clan, and became the mother of Utsunomiya Ujitsuna, born in 1326, who became the tenth Utsunomiya head.
zh: 她是下总千叶氏第九代当主千叶宗胤之女，嫁给宇都宫氏第九代当主宇都宫公纲，生下1326年出生、后来成为第十代当主的宇都宫氏纲。

en: Chiba Naritane (1155–1218) was the fifth head of the Chiba clan and held the title Chiba no suke, succeeding his father Chiba Tanemasa. In the ninth month of 1180, on the orders of his grandfather Chiba Tsunetane, he joined Tō no Taneyori in a raid on the pro-Taira deputy of Shimōsa at the provincial headquarters, killing him. When the Taira-appointed governor Fujiwara no Chikamasa hurried back to assault the Chiba manor, Naritane met him at Yugihama on the fourteenth and took him prisoner. His son Chiba Tanetsuna succeeded him as clan head.
zh: 千叶成胤（1155—1218）是千叶氏第五代当主，官称千叶介，继其父千叶胤正之后继任。1180年9月，他奉祖父千叶常胤之命，与东胤赖一同突袭下总国府，讨杀亲平家的下总目代。被平氏政权任命为下总守的藤原亲政闻讯回师急攻千叶庄，成胤于14日在结城浜迎战，将其擒获，即结城浜之战。其子千叶胤纲后来继任千叶氏当主。

en: Chiba Sadatane, eleventh head of the Chiba clan, was the son of the tenth head Tanemune and took his name from the Hōjō regent Sadatoki. In 1312 he succeeded as shugo of Iga and Shimōsa. In 1333 he abandoned the Hōjō to join Nitta Yoshisada's attack on Kamakura, and from 1335 he fought his cousin Tanesada for the headship. His heir Kazutane fell in January 1336; that October Sadatane surrendered at Kome Pass in Echizen, then defected to the Northern Court. He fought at Shijōnawate in 1348 and died in Kyoto on 1 January 1351, aged sixty-one.
zh: 千叶贞胤是千叶氏第十一代当主，第十代当主千叶胤宗之子，名字中的“贞”字得自北条执权贞时。1312年他继承家督，接任伊贺、下总两国的守护职。1333年他背弃北条氏，投奔攻打镰仓的新田义贞；1335年起又与堂兄胤贞争夺家督，1336年1月嫡男一胤战死。同年10月他在越前国木芽峠投降，随后转投北朝方。1348年他在四条畷作战，1351年1月1日以61岁卒于京都。

en: Chiba Tanemasa (1141–1203), fourth head of the Chiba clan, was the eldest son of Chiba Tsunetane, commonly called Shinsuke. In 1180 he and his father answered Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising; in April 1181 he was named among the eleven warriors guarding Yoritomo's own quarters. He fought in the Ōshū campaign of 1189 and helped crush the rebel Ōkawa Kanetō the following year. In 1190 he was one of seven attendant warriors at the court ceremony naming Yoritomo captain of the Right Imperial Guards. He died in 1203, traditionally aged sixty-three, and was succeeded by his son Naritane.
zh: 千叶胤正（1141—1203）是千叶氏第四代当主，千叶常胤的长子，通称新介。1180年源赖朝举兵，他与父亲一同投奔赖朝从军；1181年4月，他被选为警卫赖朝寝所的十一名武士之一。1189年他参加奥州合战立下武功，次年又参与镇压奥州藤原氏残党大河兼任的叛乱。1190年赖朝上洛、拜贺右近卫大将时，他是参加参院供奉的七名布衣侍之一。1203年去世，通说享年63岁，家督由儿子成胤继承。

en: Chiba Tanemune (1268–1312) was the tenth head of the Chiba clan of Shimōsa and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate, the second son of the eighth head, Yoritane. After Yoritane died in 1275, his elder brother Munetane was posted to Hizen in Kyushu on the ikoku keigoban coastal guard, leaving Tanemune to administer the clan's estate of Chiba-no-shō. When Munetane died in 1294, his heir Tanesada was young and far away in Kyushu, so Tanemune made himself lord of the estate and became the tenth Chiba head. He died in 1312 and was succeeded by his son Sadatane.
zh: 千叶胤宗（1268—1312）是下总国千叶氏第十代当主、镰仓幕府御家人，第八代当主赖胤的次男。1275年父亲赖胤死后，兄长宗胤奉派前往九州肥前国担任异国警固番役，由他掌管本领千叶庄。1294年宗胤去世，其继承人胤贞年幼且远在九州，胤宗遂成为千叶庄之主，出任千叶氏第十代当主。1312年他去世，由其子贞胤继任。

en: Chiba Tanetsuna (1198–1228), sixth head of the Chiba clan and a Kamakura gokenin, succeeded his father Naritane in 1218. In the seventh month of 1219 he escorted the new shōgun Fujiwara no Yoritsune down to Kamakura. During the Jōkyū War of 1221 he marched west up the Tōkaidō with Hōjō Yasutoki against the retired emperor's forces and won distinction; afterwards he took custody of the courtier Bōmon Tadanobu, who had backed the court side, and escorted him partway before he was released. He died in the fifth month of 1228, aged thirty-one.
zh: 千叶胤纲（1198—1228）是镰仓时代前期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，千叶氏第六代当主，千叶成胤之子。1218年继承父位，1219年7月供奉四代将军藤原赖经下向镰仓。1221年承久之乱中，他随北条泰时沿东海道西上，讨伐后鸟羽上皇一方，立下战功；战后他接收了追随朝廷的公卿坊门忠信，将其押解至途中，忠信随后获释。1228年5月去世，享年31岁。

en: Chiba Taneyasu was a warrior of the Nanboku-chō period and the second son of Chiba Munetane, ninth head of the Chiba clan. While Munetane governed Hizen Province, his younger brother Tanemune seized the family's Chiba manor in Shimōsa, and Tanemune's son Sadatane took the headship. In 1335 Taneyasu's elder brother Tanesada attacked Sadatane's estate, but died of disease in Mikawa in November 1336, just after Sadatane surrendered. Taneyasu, established in Ogi district of Hizen, then founded the Kyushu, or Hizen, branch of the Chiba.
zh: 千叶胤泰是日本南北朝时代的武将，为千叶氏第九代当主千叶宗胤的次子。其父宗胤前往肥前国期间，叔父胤宗占据了千叶氏在下总国的本领，胤宗之子贞胤继任家督。1335年，胤泰之兄胤贞攻打贞胤的千叶庄；1336年贞胤投降，胤贞却于同年11月在归国途中病死于三河。定居肥前国小城郡的胤泰由此开创九州千叶氏，又称肥前千叶氏，成为这支分家的始祖。

en: Chiba Tokitane (1218–1241) was the seventh head of the Chiba clan, succeeding as Chiba no suke in 1228; later genealogies make him Tanetsuna's son, not his brother. He received a character for his name from the regent Hōjō Yasutoki. In 1235 his retainers forced their way into the Kyoto house of Taira no Tsunetaka, and in 1236 Tokitane received an imperial edict to rebuild Katori Shrine, the chief shrine of Shimōsa. Ordered by Yasutoki to finish it, he was kept from joining Shōgun Yoritsune's Kyoto trip in 1238. He died in 1241 aged twenty-four while work on the shrine was still underway, and his son Yoritane succeeded him.
zh: 千叶时胤（1218—1241）是镰仓时代前期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，千叶氏第七代当主。旧说据《千叶大系图》以他为千叶成胤第三子，近年则普遍认为他是千叶胤纲的长子；其名中的“时”字得自执权北条泰时的偏讳。1228年胤纲去世，他继任千叶介。1235年，其家臣在京都闯入公卿平经高的宅邸滋事；1236年他奉宣旨营建下总国一宫香取神宫。1238年因工事未完，泰时不许他随将军藤原赖经上洛。1241年香取神宫营建期间他去世，年仅24岁，子赖胤继任。

en: Chiba Tsuneshige (1083–1180) was a late-Heian samurai of Shimōsa Province and the second head of the Chiba clan, son of Taira no Tsunekane. In 1124 his uncle Tsuneharu ceded him the district of Sōma, and he inherited the Chiba district on his father's death in 1126, uniting the two. In 1126 he is said to have moved his seat from Ōjii in Kazusa to Chiba and built Chiba Castle, fixing the clan's base there. He donated the Chiba manor to Cloistered Emperor Toba and the Sōma Mikuriya to Ise Shrine in 1130, and in 1135 passed leadership to his young son Tsunetane.
zh: 千叶常重（1083—1180）是平安时代后期下总国的武将，千叶氏第二代当主，平常兼之子。1124年，叔父常晴将相马郡让给他；1126年父亲去世，他又继承千叶郡，兼领两郡。相传他在同年把据点从上总国大椎迁至千叶，修筑千叶城，奠定了千叶氏的根基。他将千叶庄进献给鸟羽法皇，又于1130年将相马御厨寄进伊势神宫，1135年把家督让给年轻的嫡子常胤。

en: Chiba Tsunetane (1118–1201), third head of the Chiba clan, raised his house to Kamakura vassal standing. Son of Chiba Tsuneshige, he fought under Minamoto no Yoshitomo in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156. In 1180 he answered Yoritomo's call to arms, ordered his son and grandson to kill the Taira-aligned deputy of Shimōsa, and joined Yoritomo with three hundred riders. After Kazusa Hirotsune was killed in 1183 he took headship of the Bōsō Taira. He fought at Ichinotani in 1184 and commanded the Tōkaidō army in the 1189 Ōshū campaign. He died in 1201 aged eighty-four; later Chiba heads took the character tane from his name.
zh: 千叶常胤（1118—1201）是千叶氏第三代当主，将一族从地方豪族提升为镰仓幕府的御家人。他是千叶常重之子，1156年在源义朝麾下参加保元之乱。1180年源赖朝举兵，他起兵响应，命儿子和孙子攻杀亲平氏的下总目代，率三百骑投奔赖朝。1183年上总广常被诛后，他取得房总平氏惣领的地位。1184年他参加一之谷之战，1189年在奥州合战中任东海道方面大将。1201年去世，享年84岁；此后千叶当主的名字多继承“胤”字。

en: Chiba Yoritane (1239–1275) was the eighth head of the Chiba clan of Shimōsa and a gokenin vassal of the Kamakura shogunate. In 1241, aged three, he succeeded his father Tokitane, while the kinsman Chiba Hidetane held real power until his faction was destroyed in the Hōji conflict of 1247. In 1249 he earned merit erecting halls for the rebuilding of Katori Jingū. Called to the Kyushu coastal guard during the Mongol invasions, he was wounded fighting the Yuan army and died in 1275 aged thirty-seven, leaving the clan to his son Munetane.
zh: 千叶赖胤（1239—1275）是下总国千叶氏第八代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1241年父亲时胤去世，年仅三岁的他继承家督，实权由族人千叶秀胤掌握，直至1247年宝治合战中秀胤一派被幕府诛灭。1249年，他在香取神宫迁宫时承担正神殿等营造而立功。元寇来袭时他奉命出任异国警固番役，在九州与元军作战负伤，1275年去世，终年37岁，家督由其子宗胤继承。

en: Prince Chinu (late sixth to early seventh century) was an Asuka-period imperial prince, son of Prince Oshisaka no Hikohito no Ōe. By Princess Kibitsu-hime he fathered Empress Kōgyoku and Emperor Kōtoku, but he appears only in genealogies and no deeds of his are recorded.
zh: 茅渟王（6世纪后期—7世纪初）是日本飞鸟时代的皇族，押坂彦人大兄皇子之子。他与吉备姬王生有皇极天皇和孝德天皇，本人仅见于谱系记载，事迹不详。

en: Chōsokabe Kanemitsu was the seventh head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō castle in Tosa in the Kamakura period. In his time it spun off the Hiroi, Nakajima, Noda and Oguro branch houses. He was the son of Mitsuyuki and father of Shigetoshi.
zh: 长宗我部兼光是镰仓时代土佐长宗我部氏第七代当主、冈丰城主，在他这一代派生出广井、中岛、野田、大黑诸庶家。他是满幸之子，生子重俊。

en: Chōsokabe Kaneyoshi was the twelfth head of the Chōsokabe clan and castellan of Okō Castle in Tosa Province, succeeding his father Nobuyoshi, who served Ashikaga Takauji on the Northern Court side. With the Hiroi clan he fought under the Hosokawa, shugo of Tosa, at Higashi-Sakamoto on Mount Hachiman in Nagaoka district, northeast of Okō; for this service father and son were rewarded with the stewardship of the Ōnokida and Yoshiwara estates. Around 1345 he became temple magistrate of Kyūkō-an on Mount Godai and rebuilt the temple, an office his descendants inherited.
zh: 长宗我部兼能是长宗我部氏第十二代当主、土佐国冈丰城城主，继出仕北朝足利尊氏的父亲信能之后统领家族。他与广井氏一同归属时任土佐守护的细川氏，在冈丰城东北、长冈郡八幡山的东坂本作战；凭此战功，他与父亲信能获赐大埇乡和吉原的地头职。约1345年，他出任五台山吸江庵的寺奉行，主持该庵的改建，此后这一职务由历代当主世袭。

en: Chōsokabe Mitsuyuki was the sixth head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō castle in Tosa during the Kamakura period. His son Kanemitsu became the seventh head of the clan.
zh: 长宗我部满幸是镰仓时代土佐长宗我部氏第六代当主、冈丰城主，其子兼光成为第七代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Nobuyoshi was the eleventh head of the Chōsokabe, a warrior clan of Tosa Province in Shikoku, succeeding his father Shigemune. In May 1333, after the fall of the Kamakura shogunate, Ashikaga Takauji ordered him and Kōsokabe Hideyori to suppress a rising of local landowners at Kera-no-shō in Tosa. From his generation the clan organized the local myōshū landholders and consolidated its base as a regional lord.
zh: 长宗我部信能是四国岛土佐国豪族长宗我部氏的第十一代当主，继其父重宗之后统领家族。1333年5月镰仓幕府灭亡后，足利尊氏命他与香宗我部秀赖一同镇压土佐介良庄在地豪族发动的叛乱。自信能一代起，长宗我部氏将当地名主组织起来，巩固了家族作为在地领主的根基。

en: Shigemune Chōsokabe (dates unknown) was the tenth head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō Castle in Tosa Province. Also called Shigeie, he was the son of the ninth head Shigetaka and father of Nobuyoshi, the eleventh head.
zh: 长宗我部重宗（生卒年不详）是长宗我部氏第十代当主、土佐国冈丰城城主，又名重家。他是第九代当主长宗我部重高之子，其子信能继任为第十一代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Shigetaka was the ninth head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō castle in Tosa. He was the son of Shigetoshi, the eighth head, and was succeeded in turn by his own son Shigemune.
zh: 长宗我部重高是土佐长宗我部氏第九代当主、冈丰城主，为第八代当主重俊之子，后由其子重宗继为当主。

en: Chōsokabe Shigetoshi was the eighth head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō castle in Tosa during the Kamakura period. He was the son of Kanemitsu, the seventh head, and his son Shigetaka succeeded him as the ninth.
zh: 长宗我部重俊是镰仓时代土佐长宗我部氏第八代当主、冈丰城主，为第七代当主兼光之子，其子重高继任为第九代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Shigeuji was the fourth head of the Chōsokabe clan in Tosa during the Kamakura period. He was the son of Tadatoshi, and his own son Ujiyuki succeeded him as the fifth head.
zh: 长宗我部重氏是镰仓时代土佐长宗我部氏第四代当主，为忠俊之子，其子氏幸继任为第五代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Tadatoshi was the third head of the Chōsokabe clan in Tosa during the Kamakura period. He succeeded his father Toshimune, and his son Shigeuji became the fourth head.
zh: 长宗我部忠俊是镰仓时代土佐长宗我部氏第三代当主，继其父俊宗之后统领一门，其子重氏后为第四代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Toshimune was the second head of the Chōsokabe clan in Tosa in the early Kamakura period. A son of the founder Yoshitoshi, his sons included Tadatoshi and Kureda Tadayuki, ancestor of the Kureda branch family.
