zh: 长宗我部俊宗是镰仓时代初期土佐长宗我部氏第二代当主，为始祖能俊之子。其子有忠俊和久礼田忠幸，后者分出久礼田氏。

en: Chōsokabe Ujiyuki was the fifth head of the Chōsokabe clan and lord of Okō castle in Tosa's Nagaoka district. He was the son of Shigeuji, the fourth head, and fathered Mitsuyuki, who succeeded him as the sixth head.
zh: 长宗我部氏幸是土佐长宗我部氏第五代当主、长冈郡冈丰城主，为第四代当主重氏之子，其子满幸继任为第六代当主。

en: Chōsokabe Yoshitoshi was the founder of the Chōsokabe clan of Tosa. At first called Hata no Yoshitoshi, he was said to descend from the Hata clan that held Sarashina district in Shinano. Chronicles relate that he fought for Retired Emperor Sutoku in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 and fled to Tosa after the defeat, settling in Sogabe in Nagaoka district. Tradition makes him the builder of Okō castle and the first to bear the name Sogabe, later written Chōsokabe to distinguish his line from the Kōsokabe of Kami district. His son was Toshimune.
zh: 长宗我部能俊是土佐长宗我部氏的始祖，初名秦能俊，相传为领有信浓国更级郡的秦氏后裔。据《更科郡记》记载，1156年保元之乱时，他站在崇德上皇一方作战，战败后逃入土佐，定居长冈郡宗我部乡。相传他在宗我部村的冈丰山筑城，首称宗我部；为与香美郡的香宗我部氏相区别，这一支后来改称长宗我部。其子为俊宗。

en: Chūjō Hidenaga was a commander of the Chūjō house of Musashi, a family of the Yokoyama party. In 1335, as lord of Koromo Castle in Mikawa Province, he invited the Zen monk Taiyō Gichū and founded Chōkō-ji as his family temple; with its eighteen subtemples it was then the largest monastery in the region. Under the new Muromachi shogunate he was appointed shugo, military governor, of Owari Province, holding the post from 1336 to 1338.
zh: 中条秀长是武藏中条氏（横山党一族）的武将。1335年，他以三河国举母城（又称衣城）城主的身份请来禅师太阳义冲，创建长兴寺作为菩提寺；寺内当时有十八座塔头，是当地最大的寺院。室町幕府建立后，他被任命为尾张国守护，在任时间为1336年至1338年。

en: Chūjō Iehira was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Chūjō house of Musashi province. He was shugo, or military governor, of Owari in 1240, an office long held by members of his house.
zh: 中条家平是镰仓时代武藏国中条氏的武将。1240年他已任尾张守护，这一职务长期由中条氏一门担任。

en: Chūjō Ienaga (1165 – 26 September 1236) was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yokoyama league in Musashi province, the eldest son of Chūjō Kanetsuna, known as the hōkyō Seijin. Adopted by Hatta Tomoie, he took the surname Chūjō and claimed descent from the Michikane line of the northern Fujiwara. He fought under Minamoto no Noriyori at Ichinotani in 1184, in the Ōshū campaign of 1189–1190 and in the 1205 expedition against Hatakeyama Shigetada. In 1225 he joined the first Council of State, helping frame the Goseibai Shikimoku.
zh: 中条家长（1165—1236年9月26日）是镰仓时代武藏国横山党的武将，法桥成寻中条兼纲的长子。他被八田知家收为养子，改姓中条，自称藤原北家道兼流后裔。1184年他随源范赖参加一之谷之战，又从军1189至1190年的奥州合战，以及1205年讨伐畠山重忠的战役。1225年他成为幕府初代评定众之一，参与制定《御成败式目》。

en: Chūjō Kagenaga was a warrior of the Chūjō house of Musashi Province, one of the Yokoyama party bands that had served the Kamakura shogunate. In 1290 he is recorded as shugo, or military governor, of Owari Province. In 1333 he followed Ashikaga Takauji in the campaigns that overthrew the Kamakura shogunate, winning distinction in arms. He held Koromo Castle in Mikawa Province; after his eldest son Tokinaga moved to a grant in Ōshū in 1334, his second son Nagahide succeeded him as castellan in 1354.
zh: 中条景长是武藏国中条氏的武将，该族属于效力镰仓幕府的武藏七党之一横山党。1290年，他被任为尾张国守护。1333年，他追随足利尊氏，在推翻镰仓幕府的战役中立下武功。他领有三河国举母城；长子时长于1334年受封奥州并迁居当地后，次子长秀于1354年继任城主。

en: Chūjō Nagahide (d. 1384) was a Nanbokuchō-period warrior, the second son of Chūjō Kagenaga, who fought for Ashikaga Takauji against the Kamakura shogunate. In 1354 he succeeded his father as lord of Koromo Castle in Mikawa Province. He trained under Nenami Jion, founder of the Nen-ryū sword school, and was counted among the master's fourteen leading disciples before founding his own Chūjō-ryū. He served the Muromachi shogunate as shugo of Iga, a rewards-board officer, temple-construction magistrate and councillor, and taught swordsmanship to Ashikaga Yoshimitsu. A disciple of the poet Ton'a, his verses appear in several imperial anthologies.
zh: 中条长秀（？—1384年）是日本南北朝时代武将，为追随足利尊氏攻灭镰仓幕府的中条景长之次子。1354年，他继承父亲成为三河国举母城主。他师从念流开山之祖念阿弥慈恩，位列“念流十四哲”，后综合家传武艺开创中条流平法。他在室町幕府历任伊贺守护、恩赏方众、寺社造营奉行和评定众，并担任足利义满的剑术指南役。他又是和歌僧人顿阿的高足，作品被收入多部敕撰和歌集。

en: Chūjō Narihiro, recorded as Chūjō Yoshikatsu with the clerical title hōkyō Seijin and also called Chūjō Kanetsuna, was a Musashi warrior of the Yokoyama league, based at Ono in Saitama district. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose against the Taira in 1180, Narihiro answered his call and distinguished himself at the Battle of Ishibashiyama. With his eldest son Ienaga, he fought against Fujiwara no Yasuhira in 1189 and helped suppress Ōkawa Kanetō's revolt the following year. He also supervised construction of shogunate buildings and temples. His sons Ienaga and Yoshitoki founded the main Chūjō line and the Waga warrior house of Mutsu province respectively.
zh: 中条成寻，史料中记作中条义胜，僧位法桥、法名成寻，又名中条兼纲，是武藏国埼玉郡小野地方的横山党武士。1180年源赖朝举兵讨伐平氏时，成寻响应起兵，在石桥山之战中立下战功。1189年他与长子家长一同讨伐藤原泰衡，翌年又参与平定大河兼任之乱。他还担任幕府建筑和寺院的普请奉行。他的儿子家长与义季，分别成为中条氏嫡流和陆奥国和贺氏武家的祖先。

en: Chūjō Tokinaga was the eldest son of the warrior Chūjō Kagenaga and elder brother of Nagahide. In 1334, the first year of Kenmu, he received an estate in Ōshū and moved north, after which Nagahide inherited their father's Koromo Castle in Mikawa in 1354.
zh: 中条时长是武将中条景长的长子、长秀之兄。1334年（建武元年），他受封奥州的领地并迁居北方，因此后来由长秀在1354年继承父亲的三河国举母城。

en: Chūjō Yorihira was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Chūjō house of Musashi province. He was shugo, or military governor, of Owari in 1252, following his kinsman Chūjō Iehira in an office his house held for generations.
zh: 中条赖平是镰仓时代武藏国中条氏的武将。1252年他已任尾张守护，此前担任该职的有同族中条家平，守护一职由中条氏一门世代担任。

en: Chūjō Yoshitoki, also named Narisue and known in religion as Sainen, was a Kamakura gokenin, the second son of Chūjō Yoshikatsu, called the hōkyō Seijin. He was adopted by Wada Yoshimori, chief of the shogunate's Board of Retainers, and took the Kanmu Taira surname. For his military service he was granted Katta district in Mutsu province and styled himself Katta Saburō Saemon-no-jō. During the Jōkyū era of 1219–1222 his son Yoshiyuki entered Waga district as half-district jitō, and Yoshiyuki's line adopted the Waga clan name.
zh: 中条义季，又名成季，法名西念，是镰仓御家人、中条义胜（法桥成寻）的次子。他被镰仓幕府侍所别当和田义盛收为养子，改姓桓武平氏；后因军功受封陆奥国刈田郡，自称刈田三郎左卫门尉。承久年间（1219—1222年），其子义行以半郡地头的身份进入和贺郡，义行一支此后改称和贺氏，即陆奥和贺氏之祖。

en: Emperor Chūkyō (1218–1234) was the 85th emperor of Japan, though his reign lasted barely two months in 1221. At the age of two he succeeded his father Emperor Juntoku, who abdicated to join Retired Emperor Go-Toba's rising against the Kamakura shogunate. When the Jōkyū Incident ended in defeat, the shogunate dethroned the infant in favour of Emperor Go-Horikawa. Long known as the Kujō Dethroned Emperor or the Half-Emperor, he was recognised as an emperor and given the posthumous name Chūkyō in 1870, long after his death.
zh: 仲恭天皇（1218—1234）是日本第85代天皇，1221年在位仅约两个月。其父顺德天皇为参与后鸟羽上皇讨伐镰仓幕府的起兵而退位，年仅两岁的怀成亲王随即继位。承久之乱失败后，幕府废黜幼帝，另立后堀河天皇。他长期被称为九条废帝、半帝，直到去世多年后的1870年才被承认为天皇，获追号仲恭天皇。

en: Emperor Daigo (884–930), personal name Atsuhito, was the 60th emperor of Japan, reigning from 897 to 930. The eldest son of Emperor Uda, he was unusual among Heian sovereigns in ruling for decades without a Fujiwara regent. In 901 his minister Sugawara no Michizane was exiled to Dazaifu and the relevant records were burned; in 906 Ki no Tsurayuki presented the Kokin Wakashū anthology. When lightning struck the palace in 930 and killed several courtiers, it was read as Michizane's vengeance. Daigo abdicated that autumn, took Buddhist vows, and died days later at forty-six, buried at Daigo-ji.
zh: 醍醐天皇（884—930），名敦仁，是日本第60代天皇，897年至930年在位。他是宇多天皇的长子，在平安时代的天皇中颇为罕见——数十年间不设藤原氏摄政，亲理朝政。901年，大臣菅原道真被流放至大宰府，相关记录遭焚毁；906年纪贯之呈上《古今和歌集》。930年雷电击中皇宫，多名朝臣毙命，时人视为道真怨灵作祟。醍醐于当年秋天退位、出家，数日后去世，终年四十六岁，葬于醍醐寺。

en: Daihōji Akiuji was a Kamakura-period head of the Ōizumi warrior family in the Shōnai region of Dewa Province, and the first head listed under the Daihōji name; his three predecessors used Mutō. He succeeded his father Mutō Ujikage.
zh: 大宝寺秋氏是镰仓时代出羽国庄内地区大泉武家的一位家督，也是该族历代家督名录中首位使用大宝寺苗字的人，此前三位家督均称武藤氏。他继父亲武藤氏影之后接任家督。

en: Daihōji Chikauji was the seventh head of the Daihōji clan of Dewa Province. The clan genealogy names him a son of the sixth head, Morouji, and father of the eighth head, Mochiuji. The early clan heads were based at Daihōji Castle in Shōnai's Tagawa district.
zh: 大宝寺亲氏是出羽国大宝寺氏第七代当主。据大宝寺氏系图，他是第六代当主师氏之子、第八代当主持氏之父。大宝寺氏早期当主以庄内田川郡的大宝寺城为据点。

en: Mutō Moriuji was the second head of the warrior family holding Ōizumi manor in the Shōnai region of Dewa Province, the line that later took the name Daihōji. He succeeded his father Mutō Ujihira, the founder of the line, during the Kamakura period.
zh: 武藤盛氏是领有出羽国庄内地区大泉庄的武家的第二代家督，该家族后来以大宝寺为苗字。他在镰仓时代继其父、该家系始祖武藤氏平之后接任家督。

en: Daihōji Morouji was the sixth head of the Daihōji clan of Dewa Province, listed in the clan genealogy as a son of Nagamori. He succeeded Nagamori to the headship, and his own son Chikauji became the seventh head of the house.
zh: 大宝寺师氏是出羽国大宝寺氏第六代当主，系谱列为长盛之子。他继长盛之后继任当主，其子亲氏后来成为第七代当主。

en: Daihōji Nagamori, also called Mutō Nagamori, was the fifth head of the Daihōji clan of Dewa Province, son of the fourth head Akiuji. His family descended from Mutō Yorihira, a bureaucrat of the early Kamakura shogunate. In 1189 Yorihira's son Sukeyori had been appointed steward of Ōizumi estate in Dewa, a post inherited by his brother Ujihira. During the Northern and Southern Courts period, Nagamori is said to have built a castle at Daihōji on the estate and taken its name. Morouji succeeded him as head of the clan.
zh: 大宝寺长盛，一称武藤长盛，是出羽国大宝寺氏第五代当主，第四代当主大宝寺秋氏之子。他的家族出自镰仓幕府初期的官僚武藤赖平。1189年，赖平之子资赖获任出羽国大泉庄地头，其弟氏平继承了这一职位。相传南北朝时期，长盛在大泉庄的大宝寺筑城，并以大宝寺为氏。此后师氏继任家族当主。

en: Mutō Ujihira was an early Kamakura-period warrior of Fujiwara descent, a son of Mutō Yorihira and the founding head of the family that later became the Daihōji of Dewa Province. As jitō, or estate steward, of Ōizumi manor in the Shōnai region, he took the family name Ōizumi. In 1209 the monk-soldiers of Mount Haguro brought suit against him for encroaching on the mountain temple's estates. His successors later settled at Daihōji Castle, the center of the manor, and renamed the clan Daihōji. By the late Kamakura period, members of the Hōjō family held the stewardship of Ōizumi.
zh: 武藤氏平是镰仓时代初期的武将，出自藤原氏，为武藤赖平之子，也是出羽国后来成为大宝寺氏的一族的初代家督。他担任庄内地区大泉庄的地头，因而自称大泉氏。1209年，羽黑山的僧徒控告他侵占羽黑山寺的寺领。他的后继者后来居于庄园中心的大宝寺城，将苗字改为大宝寺氏。到镰仓时代末期，大泉庄的地头职已由北条氏一门担任。

en: Mutō Ujikage was the third head of the warrior family holding Ōizumi manor in the Shōnai region of Dewa Province, the Kamakura-period line that later renamed itself Daihōji after Daihōji Castle. He succeeded his father Mutō Moriuji as head of the family.
zh: 武藤氏影是领有出羽国庄内地区大泉庄的武家的第三代家督；这一家系在镰仓时代后来因居于大宝寺城而改称大宝寺氏。他继父亲武藤盛氏之后接任家督。

en: Daijo Mitsumoto was the eldest son and heir of Daijo Suemoto, the Hitachi Daijo, but he died before his father. Suemoto therefore made Mitsumoto's young son Tsunemoto family head under his own guardianship. Mitsumoto's sons later fought over the headship for more than twenty years.
zh: 大掾光干是常陆大掾孝干的嫡子与继承人，但先于父亲去世。孝干改立光干年幼的长子经干为家督，自任后见。光干的儿子们后来为争夺家督诉讼了二十余年。

en: Daijo Mochimoto was, in the Daijo genealogy, the third son of Mitsumoto of the Hitachi Daijo house. The genealogy records that, with his maternal grandfather Kudo Rikaku's backing, he expelled his brother Tsunemoto and took the family headship; another account attributes the expulsion to Tokimoto.
zh: 大掾持干在大掾氏系图中是常陆大掾家光干的第三子。系图记载，他在外祖父工藤理觉的支持下驱逐兄弟经干，夺取了家督；另有一说将驱逐经干之事归于时干。

en: Morimoto Daijō appears in the genealogy of the Daijō warrior clan of Hitachi Province as the eldest son of Tokimoto Daijō and the elder brother of Takamoto, the clan's lord of Mito Castle. No deeds of his survive.
zh: 大掾盛幹见于常陆国武家大掾氏的系谱，是大掾時幹的长子、大掾氏水户城主高幹之兄，本人事迹无存。

en: Daijo Suemoto was head of the Daijo house of Hitachi Province, succeeding his father Tomomoto as Hitachi Daijo; in his later years he took Buddhist vows and called himself Myokan. His chosen heir, his son Mitsumoto, died young, so Suemoto had Mitsumoto's eldest son Tsunemoto named family head and acted as the boy's guardian. The Heishi fu records that Suemoto died on 27 April 1289 at the age of sixty-eight. His death at once opened a succession crisis, as the Hojo houseman Kudo Mitsuteru intervened to install his own grandson and drive Tsunemoto out.
zh: 大掾孝干是常陆国大掾氏当主，继父亲朝干之后担任常陆大掾，晚年出家，法号妙观。他选定的继承人光干早逝，孝干便让光干的长子经干继任家督，自己担任后见。《常陆志料》所引《平氏谱》记载，孝干于1289年4月27日去世，享年68岁。他一死，家督之争随即爆发：御内人工藤高光出面干预，把自己的外孙扶上当主之位，驱逐了经干。

en: Daijo Sukemoto (died c. 1227), also called Baba Sukemoto, was a warrior and gokenin of Hitachi Province at the turn of the thirteenth century, regarded as the founder of the Daijo house. The Azuma Kagami first names him in 1190, in the vanguard when Minamoto no Yoritomo entered Kyoto. In 1193, after Taki Yoshimoto fell from power, Yoritomo granted him Yoshimoto's lands and appointed him Hitachi Daijo, a senior post in the provincial government. In 1214 he became jito of Hitachi-Fuchu by the provincial capital, and his heirs inherited the Daijo office, from which the family took its name.
zh: 大掾资干（？—约1227），又称马场资干，是12世纪末至13世纪初常陆国的武将、御家人，被视为大掾氏之祖。《吾妻镜》首次提到他，是1190年源赖朝上洛时他位列前锋。1193年多气义干失势后，赖朝把义干的领地授予资干，并任命他为常陆大掾。1214年，他又出任国府所在地常陆府中的地头；其子孙世代继承大掾一职，家族遂以大掾为姓。

en: Daijō Takamoto, head of the Daijō house of Hitachi and lord of Mito Castle, was a warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars, known in religion as Jōei. In 1330 he is credited with founding Seiryō-ji in Hitachi. In 1335 he joined Hōjō Tokiyuki's Nakasendai Rebellion and fought against Ashikaga Takauji at the Sagami River. He then sided with the Southern Court with the Oda family, submitted to the Northern Court in 1337, and fought in the Kannō Disturbance. Afterward he attended Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Motouji and restored his house's power, dying between 1382 and 1386.
zh: 大掾高干是常陆国大掾氏当主、水户城主，南北朝时代武将，法号净永。相传1330年他在常陆建立清凉寺。1335年，他加入北条时行发动的中先代之乱，在相模川迎战足利尊氏；随后与小田氏一同投靠南朝，1337年又归降北朝，并卷入观应之扰乱。此后他出仕镰仓公方足利基氏，恢复了大掾氏的势力，于1382年至1386年间去世。

en: Daijo Tokimoto was a son of Daijo Mitsumoto and became head of the Daijo house of Hitachi Province while still a child named Choju. When his grandfather Suemoto died in April 1289, his maternal grandfather, the Hojo houseman Kudo Mitsuteru, had the boy installed as family head in place of his elder brother Tsunemoto, who was driven out; after coming of age Choju took the name Tokimoto. Tsunemoto contested the succession for more than twenty years, but Tokimoto won the final judgement in the Tokuji era, 1306 to 1308. His sons Morimoto and Takamoto succeeded him in the family.
zh: 大掾时干是大掾光干之子，幼名长寿，还是孩童时就成了常陆国大掾氏当主。1289年四月祖父孝干死后，他的外祖父、御内人工藤高光把年幼的长寿扶上家督之位，取代被驱逐的兄长经干；元服后他改名时干。经干为争夺继承权诉讼了二十余年，时干最终在德治年间（1306—1308年）胜诉。他的儿子盛干和高干相继继承了大掾家。

en: Daijo Tomomoto was the eldest son of Daijo Sukemoto, founder of the Daijo house of Hitachi Province, and succeeded him as Hitachi Daijo. When Sukemoto died, Oda Tomoshige challenged Tomomoto's right to the post, but in the twelfth month of 1227 the Kamakura regent Hojo Yasutoki ruled in his favour, citing Minamoto no Yoritomo's written order that the office pass from Sukemoto to his heir. The judgement confirmed the Daijo family's hereditary hold on the Hitachi Daijo post. Tomomoto was in turn succeeded by his son Suemoto.
zh: 大掾朝干是常陆国大掾氏初代资干的嫡子，继资干之后担任常陆大掾。资干死后，小田知重对他的继承权提出异议。1227年十二月，镰仓幕府执权北条泰时依据源赖朝让大掾一职由资干传给继承人的下文作出裁决，判定朝干胜诉，由此确认了大掾氏对常陆大掾一职的世袭。后来由他的儿子孝干继任家督。

en: Daijo Tsunemoto was the eldest son of Daijo Mitsumoto and briefly the head of the Daijo house of Hitachi Province. When Mitsumoto died young, Tsunemoto's grandfather Suemoto had him named heir while still a child and acted as his guardian. After Suemoto's death in April 1289, however, the Hojo houseman Kudo Mitsuteru had Tsunemoto expelled and installed his own grandson Choju, later called Tokimoto, as family head. Tsunemoto carried his protest to the Kamakura shogunate, but after more than twenty years of litigation the case ended against him in the Tokuji era, 1306 to 1308.
zh: 大掾经干是大掾光干的长子，曾是常陆国大掾氏的年幼当主。光干早逝后，祖父孝干指定他为继承人，并亲自担任后见。1289年四月孝干死后，御内人工藤高光随即将经干驱逐，把自己的外孙长寿（元服后取名时干）扶上家督之位。经干向镰仓幕府提出申诉，兄弟间的诉讼持续了二十多年，最终在德治年间（1306—1308年）以时干胜诉告终。

en: Date Masayori (1227–1301) was a mid-Kamakura gokenin and the fourth head of the Date clan, lord of Yanagawa castle in Mutsu; he was also called Date Jirō or Awano Kurōdo, held junior fifth rank, and after taking vows was known as Gansai. A second son of Date Yoshihiro, he kept the clan residence in Kamakura and fathered his successor Munetsuna. A devout Buddhist, he imitated the Five Mountains of Kyoto and Kamakura by founding five monasteries around Date, including Kannon-ji in 1247, Tōshō-ji in 1283, and Manjōju-ji in 1286; Tōshō-ji became the Date family's first ancestral temple.
zh: 伊达政依（1227—1301）是镰仓时代中期的御家人、伊达氏第四代当主、陆奥国梁川城主，通称伊达次郎、粟野藏人，叙从五位下，出家后号愿西。他是伊达义广的次子，举家居于镰仓，其子宗纲继为当主。政依笃信佛教，仿效京都五山与镰仓五山，在伊达一带创建东昌寺、光明寺、满胜寺、观音寺、光福寺五寺，合称伊达五山（即今北山五山）：1247年建观音寺，1283年建东昌寺，1286年建满胜寺。东昌寺是伊达家最早的菩提寺。

en: Date Motomune (died 28 August 1335), called Magotarō, was the sixth head of the Date clan of Mutsu in the late Kamakura period, holding Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, as Kunai Shōyū. His son Date Yukitomo succeeded him.
zh: 伊达基宗（卒于1335年8月28日），通称孙太郎，是镰仓时代后期陆奥伊达氏第六代当主，官至从五位下宫内少辅。其子伊达行朝继为第七代当主。

en: Date Munemura (1173–1251) was the second head of the Date clan of Mutsu, the second son of Date Tomomune by a daughter of the Yūki house; his common name was Jirō and he held junior fifth rank, lower grade. The Azuma Kagami lists him as Tameshige among the four sons who fought beside their father in the 1189 Ōshū campaign, after which the family received Date district. Old Date genealogies even name Munemura, rather than Tomomune, as the clan's founder. He was the father of Date Yoshihiro.
zh: 伊达宗村（1173—1251）是陆奥伊达氏第二代当主、初代当主伊达朝宗的次子，母亲为结城氏之女；通称次郎，叙从五位下。《吾妻镜》把他记作“为重”，列为1189年随父参加奥州合战的四个儿子之一，伊达郡即此战的恩赏。伊达氏的古系图中，颇有以宗村而非朝宗为初代当主者。他是伊达义广之父。

en: Date Munetō (1324–1385) was the eighth head of the Date clan of Mutsu, active in the Nanboku-chō period, with the court rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. From about 1380 he waged a calculated campaign against the Nagai clan, mixing alliances and surprise attacks. In 1381 he defeated the Osaki, seizing the Shinobu, Katta, Igu and Shibata districts, and brought Watari under his control after beating Takeishi Yukitane. In 1385 he destroyed the Nagai and secured Yonezawa for the Date. He also rebuilt the hall of the Narushima Hachiman shrine in Yonezawa.
zh: 伊达宗远（1324—1385）是陆奥伊达氏第八代当主，南北朝时代的武将，位至从五位下。约1380年起，他软硬兼施，以一揆契约和偷袭等手段持续蚕食长井氏。1381年他与大崎氏交战，夺取信夫、刈田、伊具、柴田四郡，又击败武石行胤，将亘理郡纳入实际支配。1385年他攻灭长井氏，为伊达氏取得米泽。他还重修了米泽成岛八幡宫的拜殿。

en: Date Munetsuna (1254–1317) was a mid-Kamakura gokenin and the fifth head of the Date clan, the eldest son and heir of Date Masayori; he was commonly called Kai Kotarō. His sons included his successor Date Motomune, Munemasa, and Yukitsuna, who took the Senoue name. His younger brother Munehiro left the main line to become adopted heir of Shiraishi Nagatoshi and began the Shiraishi house.
zh: 伊达宗纲（1254—1317）是镰仓时代中期的御家人、伊达氏第五代当主，伊达政依的嫡男，通称甲斐小太郎。其子有继为当主的伊达基宗、宗昌（彦二郎），以及改称濑上氏的行纲（濑上五郎）。其弟宗弘离开宗家，出继白石长俊为养嗣子，开创白石氏。

en: Date Tameie was the fourth son of Date Tomomune, founder of the Date clan, and was commonly called Shirō. The Azuma Kagami names him among the sons who fought beside their father at the Battle of Ishinazaka in Minamoto no Yoritomo's 1189 Ōshū campaign, for which the family was rewarded with Date district in Mutsu. He is regarded as ancestor of the Suruga Date line. The Date Seshin Kafu relates that his son Date Tameshige settled in Hienuki district, entered Osegawa castle, and took the place name, beginning the Hienuki clan; other accounts differ on the clan's origins.
zh: 伊达为家是伊达氏始祖伊达朝宗的第四子，通称四郎。《吾妻镜》记载，1189年源赖朝发动奥州合战，他与兄弟们随父参加石那坂之战，伊达家因此受封陆奥国伊达郡。他被视为骏河伊达家之祖。《伊达世臣家谱》称，其子伊达为重前往稗贯郡，入小濑川城，以地名为姓氏，开创稗贯氏；关于该氏族的起源还有其他说法。

en: Date Tomomune (1129–1199) was a late Heian warrior and the first head of the Date house. Originally called Nakamura Tarō, he administered the Nakamura estate in Haga district, Shimotsuke Province, and served at court as Tōtōmi no kami and Hitachi no suke. In 1180 he joined the rising of his maternal cousin Minamoto no Yoritomo. In the 1189 Ōshū campaign his four sons stormed the Ishinazaka fortress and captured enemy general Satō Motoharu; rewarded with Date district in Mutsu, Tomomune took the name Date. He was succeeded by his second son, Munemura.
zh: 伊达朝宗（1129—1199）是平安时代后期至镰仓初期的御家人，伊达宗家初代当主。他原称中村太郎，管理下野国芳贺郡的中村庄园，并历任远江守、常陆介等官职。1180年源赖朝举兵时，因赖朝是他姑表兄弟，他驰赴其麾下。1189年奥州合战中，他的四个儿子充当前锋，攻破信夫郡石那坂城砦，生擒敌将佐藤基治；他以此功受领陆奥国伊达郡，遂改称伊达姓。死后由次子伊达宗村继承。

en: Date Yoshihiro (1185–1256) was an early Kamakura gokenin and the third head of the Date clan, the second son of Date Munemura. He was called Awano Jirō, took the monk name Kakubutsu, and held junior fifth rank as kurōdo no tayū. In his generation the clan seat moved from Takakogaoka to the Kurino mansion in Kōri, Date district; the character in his name is thought to have been granted by shogunal regent Hōjō Yoshitoki. In the 1221 Jōkyū War he sent a retainer to fight under Yoshitoki's son Yasutoki at Uji. Sources give his death as 1251 or 1256.
zh: 伊达义广（1185—1256）是镰仓时代前期的御家人、伊达氏第三代当主，伊达宗村的次子。他通称粟野次郎，出家后法名觉佛，叙从五位下，任藏人大夫。他这一代把居城从伊达郡桑折乡的高子冈迁至同乡的栗野大馆；其名中的“义”字被认为得自镰仓幕府二代执权北条义时。1221年承久之乱中，他派遣家臣随义时之子北条泰时在宇治作战。关于其卒年，《伊佐早文书》作1251年，《伊达系图》作1256年。

en: Date Yukitomo (1291–1348), later called Yukimune, was the seventh head of the Date clan of Mutsu and a Southern Court commander in the Nanboku-chō wars. In 1331 he joined the Hōjō army sent against the Genkō rising, but after the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333 he served under Kitabatake Akiie on the Mutsu provincial council. He campaigned west with Akiie in 1335 and again in 1337, and after Akiie's death held Isa Castle in Hitachi against Kō no Morofuyu before escaping home. He died in 1348; his verses appear in the Fūga Wakashū as Fujiwara no Tomomura.
zh: 伊达行朝（1291—1348），晚年改名行宗，是陆奥伊达氏第七代当主，南北朝时代效力南朝。1331年元弘之变时，他加入北条高时派往畿内的讨伐军；1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，出仕北畠显家，任陆奥式评定众，参与奥羽政务。1335年和1337年他两度随显家西征，显家死后据守常陆国伊佐城抵御高师冬，最终突围返回本领。他于1348年去世，曾以藤原朝村之名在《风雅和歌集》中留有和歌。

en: Sanehira Dohi (died 1191) was a Sagami warlord of the Kanmu Taira lineage, ancestor of the Dohi and, by tradition, the Kobayakawa clans. From Dohi-gō he led the Nakamura war-band, and in 1180 was among the first to join Minamoto no Yoritomo's revolt; after the defeat at Ishibashiyama he fled with Yoritomo and helped him escape to Awa. He fought at the Fuji River, Uji and Ichinotani, leading over seven thousand cavalry on the western wing. He became military governor of the three Kibi provinces and then of Nagato and Suō, and served in the 1189 Ōshū campaign.
zh: 土肥实平（？—1191）是相模国豪族，出自桓武平氏良文流，为土肥氏之祖，相传也是小早川氏的祖先。他以土肥乡为据点统领“中村党”武士团，1180年源赖朝举兵时率先率众投奔；石桥山战败后他随赖朝逃亡，并助其渡海撤往安房国。此后他参加富士川、宇治川和一之谷诸役，在一之谷率七千余骑从西翼进攻。他先后出任吉备三国（备前、备中、备后）及长门、周防的总追捕使，并参加了1189年的奥州合战。

en: Dohi Tōhira (died 1237) was a Kamakura shogunate retainer and heir of Dohi Sanehira. From his family's estate at Dohi-gō in Sagami he built a hall at Kobayakawa village, from which his descendants took their name. In 1180 he and his father joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's uprising and fought at the defeat of Ishibashiyama; when Yoritomo fled to Awa, Tōhira carried word of his safety to Hōjō Masako. After the Genpei War he was made steward of Nuta manor in Aki Province. During the Wada conflict of 1213 he stayed neutral, though his son was executed for joining the rebels.
zh: 土肥远平（？—1237）是镰仓幕府御家人、土肥实平的继承人。他领有相模国土肥乡，在小早川村筑馆，子孙后来即以小早川为姓。1180年他随父亲参加源赖朝举兵，在石桥山之战中战败；赖朝逃往安房国时，他充当使者向北条政子报告赖朝平安无恙。源平合战后，他被任命为安艺国沼田庄的地头。1213年和田合战之际，他保持中立，而他的儿子因加入叛军被处死。

en: Doi Michikage was a son of Doi Michinari of the Doi clan in Iyo Province, a cadet branch of the Kōno family with lands at Minami-Doi in Ishii, Kume district, and one of the younger brothers of the Kenmu-era warrior Doi Michimasu.
zh: 土居通景是伊予国土居氏的土居通成之子、镰仓末期至南北朝时期武将土居通增的弟弟之一。土居氏为河野氏旁支，在久米郡石井乡南土居拥有领地。

en: Doi Michimasu, called Hikokurō, was an Iyo warrior of the Kōno branch clan and eldest son of Doi Michinari. In 1321 the Kamakura shogunate gave him charge of Iyo's maritime defense. In the intercalary second month of 1333 he was among the first to rise for Emperor Go-Daigo, storming Fuchū Castle and routing Hōjō Tokinao at Ishiihama. Under the Kenmu government he served as Bitchū no Kami, and in 1336 fought for the Southern Court with Nitta Yoshisada at Teshimagawara and Minatogawa. On 14 November 1336 he fell with his kinsmen in Shiba Takatsune's snowbound ambush at Arachi in Echizen.
zh: 土居通增，通称彦九郎，是伊予国武士、河野氏支流土居氏的土居通成长子。1321年，镰仓幕府委任他负责伊予的海上警备。1333年闰二月，他与得能通纲等人最早起兵响应后醍醐天皇倒幕，攻克伊予守护宇都宫贞宗的府中城，又在石井浜击退长门探题北条时直。建武政权下他官至备中守；1336年随新田义贞为南朝作战，参加丰岛河原与凑川诸役。1336年11月14日，他在越前荒乳遭斯波高经趁雪伏击，与一族一同战死。

en: Doi Michimoto was a son of Doi Michinari of the Doi clan in Iyo Province, a cadet branch of the Kōno family with lands at Minami-Doi in Ishii, Kume district, and one of the younger brothers of the Kenmu-era warrior Doi Michimasu.
zh: 土居通元是伊予国土居氏的土居通成之子、镰仓末期至南北朝时期武将土居通增的弟弟之一。土居氏为河野氏旁支，在久米郡石井乡南土居拥有领地。

en: Doi Michimura belonged to the Doi family of Iyo; a family genealogy records him as a son of Doi Michiyo.
zh: 土居通村出身伊予土居氏，家谱记载他是土居通世之子。

en: Doi Michinari was a Kamakura-period warrior of Iyo Province, from the Doi branch of the Kōno clan seated at Minami-Doi in Kume district. A son of Kōno Michitsugu, he was the father of the Southern Court loyalist Doi Michimasu.
zh: 土居通成是镰仓时代伊予国的武士，出自河野氏的土居支流，盘踞久米郡石井乡南土居。他是河野通继之子，南朝忠臣土居通增之父。

en: Doi Michiyo was a son of Doi Michinari of the Doi clan in Iyo Province, a cadet branch of the Kōno family with lands at Minami-Doi in Ishii, Kume district, and a younger brother of the Kenmu-era warrior Doi Michimasu.
zh: 土居通世是伊予国土居氏的土居通成之子、镰仓末期至南北朝时期武将土居通增之弟。土居氏为河野氏旁支，在久米郡石井乡南土居拥有领地。

en: Emperor En'yū (959–991), personal name Morihira, was the 64th emperor of Japan, reigning from 969 to 984. The fifth son of Emperor Murakami and Reizei's younger brother, he was named heir in 967 with Fujiwara backing, and the Anna Incident of 969 ruined Minamoto no Takaakira, clearing his path to the throne. He favoured his uncle Fujiwara no Kanemichi in the clan's struggle over the kampaku post. Palace fires between 976 and 982 wrecked the Sacred Mirror. En'yū abdicated in 984, took Buddhist vows as Kongō Hō in 985, and died in 991; his only son became Emperor Ichijō.
zh: 圆融天皇（959—991），名守平，是日本第64代天皇，969年至984年在位。他是村上天皇的第五子，冷泉天皇的同母弟，967年在藤原氏支持下被立为皇嗣；969年的安和之变使源高明失势，为他扫清了即位之路。在位期间，他在藤原氏围绕关白之位的争斗中偏袒舅父藤原兼通。976年至982年间皇宫屡次失火，神镜被烧毁。圆融于984年退位，985年出家，法名金刚法，991年去世；他的独子后来成为一条天皇。

en: En'ya Sadakiyo (died 1 May 1326) was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and shugo of Izumo Province, the son of En'ya Yoriyasu. Also called Sasaki Sadakiyo or Magojirō, he came of age between 1284 and 1311 under the ninth shikken Hōjō Sadatoki, receiving the character sada in his name. He inherited the Izumo shugo office from his father, held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and served as Saemon-no-jō, kebiishi and Ōmi-no-kami. In the fifth month of 1325 he barred shugo officials from entering Gakuen-ji. He died on 1 May 1326, and the headship passed to his legitimate son Takasada.
zh: 盐冶贞清（？—1326年5月1日）是日本镰仓时代末期武将、出云国守护，盐冶赖泰之子，又称佐佐木贞清，通称孙二郎。1284年至1311年间，他在第九代执权北条贞时主持下元服，从其偏讳中拜领‘贞’字。他继承父亲的出云守护职务，叙从五位下，历任左卫门尉、检非违使、近江守。1325年5月，他下令停止守护使进入鳄渊寺。1326年5月1日去世，家督之位由嫡子高贞继承。

en: Enya Sadayasu was a son of the Izumo shugo Enya Sadakiyo, who died in 1326, and a brother of Enya Takasada, the last head of the clan's main line.
zh: 盐冶贞泰是出云守护盐冶贞清之子，父亲于1326年去世；他的兄弟盐冶高贞是盐冶氏嫡流最后一任当主。

en: Enya Takasada was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts period, head of the Enya clan, a Sasaki branch that had long held the post of shugo of Izumo Province. When Emperor Go-Daigo escaped exile on Oki during the Genko War of 1333, Takasada ignored the shogunate's call to seize him and joined the emperor at Mount Senjo, afterwards becoming shugo of both Izumo and Oki. He later sided with Ashikaga Takauji, but in 1341 he suddenly fled Kyoto after being accused of treason and killed himself at Kageyama in Harima.
zh: 盐冶高贞是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，为盐冶氏当主；盐冶氏出自名门佐佐木氏，世代担任出云国守护。1333年元弘之乱中，后醍醐天皇从流放地隐岐逃出，高贞不理会幕府追捕天皇的要求，驰赴船上山投奔天皇，建武政权成立后兼任出云、隐岐两国守护。他后来转投足利尊氏，1341年被指谋反，突然逃出京都，最终在播磨国影山自尽。

en: Enya Tokitsuna is known only from genealogies, as a younger brother of Enya Takasada, shugo of Izumo, who perished in 1341. They make him ancestor of Enya Mitsumichi, who revived the clan as Muromachi bakufu hokoshu in the early fifteenth century.
zh: 盐冶时纲仅见于后世家谱：他是出云守护盐冶高贞之弟，高贞于1341年自尽。家谱以他为盐冶满通的先祖，满通于15世纪初以室町幕府奉公众身份复兴盐冶氏。

en: En'ya Yoriyasu was a Kamakura shogunate gokenin and shugo of Izumo Province, founder of the Izumo En'ya clan. A son of Sasaki Yasukiyo, he came of age between 1246 and 1263 under the shikken Hōjō Tokiyori, receiving from him the character yori in his name. Around 1278 he succeeded his father as shugo of Izumo, built Ōsako Castle in Enya village in Kando District and took the place name En'ya, beginning the clan. In 1283 he funded the three-storey pagoda at Gakuen-ji, and in 1288 granted rice land to Kitsuki Taisha. The Izumo shugo office passed through the line of his son Sadakiyo throughout the Kamakura period.
zh: 盐冶赖泰是日本镰仓幕府御家人、出云国守护，出云盐冶氏的始祖。他是佐佐木泰清之子，1246年至1263年间在执权北条时赖主持下元服，并从其偏讳中领受‘赖’字。约1278年，他继承父亲的出云守护一职，在神门郡盐冶乡修筑大回城，以地名称盐冶左卫门尉，盐冶氏由此发端。1283年，他遵亡父遗志出资协助鳄渊寺营造三重塔；1288年又将盐冶乡内田地一町捐给杵筑大社。其子贞清一系此后在镰仓时代世袭出云守护之职。

en: Fujiwara no Akinori (1097–1152) was a court noble of the late Heian period, the son of Fujiwara no Morizane of the Northern House's Kajūji line, who rose to lesser councillor at senior fourth rank. In 1120 he was named provisional governor of Kai Province. As his sister married Fujiwara no Tadazane and bore the minister Fujiwara no Yorinaga, Akinori served Yorinaga as a household administrator. He died suddenly in 1152 aged 54, still attending his duties the day before.
zh: 藤原显宪（1097—1152）是平安时代后期公卿，为藤原北家劝修寺流治部卿藤原盛实之子，官至正四位下少纳言。1120年他被任命为甲斐权守。其姊妹嫁给藤原忠实并生下藤原赖长，显宪因此以舅父身份担任左大臣赖长的家司。1152年他以54岁之龄突然去世，据《本朝世纪》记载，去世前一天他仍在执行公务。

en: Fujiwara no Akisue (1055–1123) was a nobleman and waka poet of the late Heian period, the second son of Fujiwara no Takatsune, governor of Mino Province. As his mother was Emperor Shirakawa's wet nurse, Akisue was the emperor's foster brother and trusted aide, serving as governor of Sanuki, Tamba and Owari. He grew wealthy as governor of Harima and Dazai Daini, and in 1104 reached Junior Third Rank, the first of his lineage at court in two centuries. Known as the Rokujō Shuri no Daibu, he founded the Rokujō Fujiwara school of poetry.
zh: 藤原显季（1055—1123）是平安时代后期的贵族与和歌歌人，为美浓守藤原隆经的次子。其母是白河天皇的乳母，显季因此作为天皇的乳兄弟深受信任，历任赞岐、丹波、尾张等国国司。他任播磨守、大宰大贰期间积蓄了丰厚财力，1104年升从三位，是其家族两百年来首位公卿。他号六条修理大夫，是和歌流派六条藤家之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Akitaka, known as Tōdayū, was a son of the court noble Fujiwara no Ienari and the progenitor of the Sanuki Fujiwara houses, including the Hanyū and Kōzai clans. His son Suketaka first took the Hanyū name.
zh: 藤原章隆，通称藤太夫，是公卿藤原家成之子、讃岐藤原氏诸家（羽床氏、香西氏等）的始祖。其子资高最先以羽床为苗字。

en: Heyako no Aritsuna (?–1186), also called Ashikaga no Aritsuna, was a warrior of the Fujiwara-line Ashikaga clan of Shimotsuke Province, descended from Fujiwara no Hidesato and ancestor of the Sano and Asonuma families. As steward of the Tōdai-ji estate of Heyako-ho he built Fuma Castle. In 1180 he joined the Taira attack on Minamoto no Yorimasa at Uji, but at the Battle of Nogimiya he sided with the Minamoto alongside his sons Mototsuna and Hirotsuna. In June 1186 he fought Ashikaga Yoshikane at Akamiyama, was shot in the left eye, and killed himself while fleeing.
zh: 户矢子有纲（？—1186），又称足利有纲，是下野国藤姓足利氏的武将，出自藤原秀乡一脉，为佐野氏与阿曾沼氏之祖。他担任东大寺领地户矢子保的保司，修筑不摩城。1180年宇治之战时，他随平氏攻打源赖政；后来的野木宫之战中，又与儿子基纲、广纲加入源氏一方。1186年6月，他在赤见山与足利义兼交战，被箭射中左眼，败走后自尽。

en: Fujiwara no Asayori (died c. 965) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Kanjūji branch of the northern Fujiwara, fourth son of the udaijin Fujiwara no Sadakata. He spent his career at court, serving as head of the Left Stables, senior assistant president of the Censors, lesser councillor, minor captain of both the right and left inner palace guards, major controller of the left and commander of the left middle palace guards, ending at junior fourth rank upper as head of the Audit Commissioners. Unlike his brothers Asatada and Asahira he never rose to kugyō, but his descendants prospered as the Kanjūji line.
zh: 藤原朝赖（?—约965）是日本平安时代中期的贵族，出身藤原北家劝修寺流，为右大臣藤原定方的第四子。他历任左马头、弹正大弼、少纳言、右近卫少将、左近卫少将、左大弁、左兵卫督，最终官至从四位上勘解由长官。与同母兄弟朝忠、朝成不同，他终未能晋升公卿，但子孙作为劝修寺流繁衍兴旺。

en: Fujiwara no Chikamasa was an eleventh-century Fujiwara courtier who, tradition records, was exiled to Kutsuna Island in Iyo after falling into disgrace. In 1084 he settled there and became lord of the Kutsuna and Hashira island groups in the Seto Inland Sea, launching reclamation works across the islands. In 1086 he founded Choryo-ji temple at Oura. His son Fujiwara no Chikatomo continued the work, opening the six Kutsuna islands between 1087 and 1094 and the outer five Hashira islands by about 1096. The seafaring Kutsuna clan claimed Chikamasa as its ancestor.
zh: 藤原亲贤是11世纪的藤原氏贵族。相传他因获罪被流放至伊予的忽那岛，于1084年入岛，成为濑户内海忽那诸岛与柱岛群岛的领主，着手开垦各岛。1086年，他在大浦创建长领寺。其子藤原亲朝继续经营，1087—1094年间开垦包括忽那岛在内的六岛，约1096年完成柱岛外五岛的开发。后来称雄濑户内海的忽那七岛水军一族——忽那氏，即奉亲贤为始祖。

en: Fujiwara no Chikatomo was the second head of the Kutsuna clan, a sea power based on the Kutsuna Islands off Iyo Province. The Kutsuna development chronicle records that during 1087 to 1094 he opened six islands, including Kutsuna Island itself.
zh: 藤原亲朝是以伊予国海外忽那诸岛为据点的海上势力忽那氏的二代目。《忽那开发记》记载，1087至1094年间，他着手开垦了包括忽那岛在内的六座岛屿。

en: Fujiwara no Chikatsuna was a late Heian and early Kamakura courtier of the Koichijo Fujiwara line, recorded in the Anekoji genealogy as a son of the poet Fujiwara no Morotsuna and the father of Fujiwara no Ietoki.
zh: 藤原亲纲是平安末期至镰仓初期小一条流藤原氏贵族，姊小路家系图将他记为歌人藤原师纲之子、藤原家时之父。

en: Fujiwara no Chitsune (died 1012), also written Chizune or Tomotsune, was a military noble of the Northern Fujiwara's Uonama line and a son of Fujiwara no Hidesato. In 968 the province of Shinano reported him to the court for rebellion. After his elder brother Chiharu was exiled in the Anna Incident of 969, Chitsune became the principal heir of Hidesato's line and was named general of the chinjufu in 970. In 979 Shimotsuke reported him fighting one Minamoto no Hi. He later served as captain of the left palace guards and governor of Mino, holding the Sago estate in Oyama.
zh: 藤原千常（？—1012），一作知常，是藤原北家鱼名流的军事贵族，为藤原秀乡之子。968年，信浓国向朝廷奏告他谋反。969年安和之变后其兄千晴被流放，千常遂成为秀乡流的嫡子，并于970年出任镇守府将军。979年，下野国奏报他与源肥交战。他后来还任左卫门尉、美浓守，以小山庄寒河御厨为本领，1012年去世。

en: Fujiwara no Fuhito (659–720), second son of Fujiwara no Kamatari, laid the foundations of the clan's power. He helped enthrone Emperor Monmu in 697 and led the compilation of the Taiho Code of 701. In 698 he secured for his descendants alone the right to bear the Fujiwara name, and married his daughter Miyako to Monmu and another daughter Komyoshi to Emperor Shomu, who became Japan's first non-imperial empress. His four sons founded the clan's four branches. He moved the family temple to Nara as Kofuku-ji and died in 720 while compiling the Yoro Code.
zh: 藤原不比等（659—720）是藤原镰足的次子，奠定了藤原氏权势的根基。他参与拥立文武天皇（697年），主导编纂701年的《大宝律令》。698年，他为自己的子孙争取到独用藤原姓的特权，又把女儿宫子嫁给文武天皇、女儿光明子嫁给圣武天皇——光明子后来成为日本第一位非皇族出身的皇后。他的四个儿子开创了藤原四家。他还把氏寺迁至奈良，改称兴福寺，720年在编纂《养老律令》期间病逝。

en: Fujiwara no Fujinari (776–822) was an early Heian noble of the Northern Fujiwara, the fifth son of Sadaijin Fujiwara no Uona. Appointed Harima suke in 811, he was tasked in 813 with the civilizing of Emishi captives resettled in the province. He spent Emperor Saga's reign mainly as a provincial governor, rising to senior fifth rank, lower grade, in 815 and junior fourth rank, lower grade, in 817, and ending as Ise no kami. He died in 822 aged 47, and is counted as ancestor of the warrior line of Fujiwara no Hidesato.
zh: 藤原藤成（776—822）是平安初期贵族，出自藤原北家，为左大臣藤原鱼名第五子，被视为秀乡流藤原氏之祖。811年任播磨介，813年兼任专官，负责教化移配到当地的夷俘并回应其诉求。嵯峨朝时他主要担任地方官，历任播磨守、伊势守，815年叙正五位下，817年叙从四位下。822年去世，终年47岁，最终官位为伊势守从四位下。

en: Fujiwara no Fujitsugu (773–817) was an early Heian court noble of the Northern Fujiwara, a grandson of Sadaijin Fujiwara no Uona and second son of Fujiwara no Washitori. Appointed Hitachi no jō in 793, he received junior fifth rank in 799 and rose rapidly under Emperor Heizei in 806. In 809 he became Tōgū daibu, Crown Prince Takaoka's household chief, and during the 810 Kusuko Incident sided with Emperor Saga. In 812 he became Sangi and concurrently served as Dazai daini in Kyūshū. He died in 817 aged 45, his final rank junior fourth rank, upper grade.
zh: 藤原藤嗣（773—817）是平安初期公卿，出自藤原北家，为左大臣藤原鱼名之孙、中务大辅藤原鹫取次子。793年任常陆掾，799年叙从五位下，806年平城天皇即位后一年内连升四级。809年叙从四位上，任皇太子高岳亲王的春宫大夫。810年药子之变中他依附嵯峨天皇，兼任右近卫中将。812年任参议兼大宰大贰，位列公卿。817年去世，终年45岁，最终官位为参议从四位上。

en: Fujiwara no Fuminaga was a mid-Heian military aristocrat of the Hidesato line, the son of Chinjufu Shōgun Fujiwara no Chitsune and grandson of the warrior Fujiwara no Hidesato. After serving as a palace attendant and police commissioner of Shimotsuke Province, he was appointed Chinjufu Shōgun, general of the northern defense headquarters, at an extraordinary court ceremony in 988, after presenting gifts to Empress Senshi for Regent Kaneie's sixtieth year; he then held junior fifth rank, lower grade. In 1001 he sent a horse to the courtier Fujiwara no Yukinari. He died on the third day of the second month, 1025.
zh: 藤原文脩是平安时代中期的军事贵族，属藤原秀乡流，为镇守府将军藤原千常之子、武将藤原秀乡之孙。他历任内舍人、下野国押领使，988年为摄政藤原兼家六十贺寿向皇太后诠子进献任料，遂在临时除目中被补任为镇守府将军，时为从五位下。1001年，他曾赠马一匹给公卿藤原行成。1025年二月三日，文脩去世。

en: Fujiwara no Fumiyuki (dates unknown) was a mid-Heian noble of the Hidesato line of the Fujiwara Hokke, the son of Chinjufu General Fujiwara no Fuminaga. He held junior fifth rank and served as a guard officer and kebiishi police commissioner, and later as governor of Shimotsuke. Michinaga's diary records that in the sixth month of 1006 he fled the kebiishi after fighting with Fujiwara no Shosuke and sought out Michinaga, and his charges were reported six days later.
zh: 藤原文行（生没年不详）是平安时代中期贵族，出自藤原北家秀乡流，为镇守府将军藤原文修之子。他叙从五位下，历任左卫门尉、检非违使、下野守。据《御堂关白记》记载，1006年6月他因与藤原正辅争斗而遭检非违使追捕，便前去投奔藤原道长，同月其罪名被奏报朝廷。

en: Fujiwara no Fusasaki (681–737), second son of Fujiwara no Fuhito, founded the Fujiwara Northern House. In 703, soon after the Taiho Code, he became an inspector of the Tōkaidō, and in 709 he inspected the Tōkai and Tōsandō circuits during campaigns against the Emishi. Made councillor in 717 ahead of his elder brother Muchimaro, he was named inner minister at the deathbed of Empress Genmei in 721, to assist Empress Genshō. He died in the smallpox epidemic of 737 and was posthumously granted senior first rank and the office of grand minister.
zh: 藤原房前（681—737）是藤原不比等的次子，藤原北家之祖。703年《大宝律令》施行后不久，他出任东海道巡察使；709年在征讨虾夷期间巡察东海、东山两道。717年，他先于兄长武智麻吕出任参议。721年元明上皇临终时，他被任为内臣，受命辅佐元正天皇。737年他死于天花流行，死后获追赠正一位太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Fusatsugu was an early Heian court noble, the son of Fujiwara no Sueshige, governor of Mimasaka. He took junior fifth rank in 811 and served in the Ministry of Central Affairs and as vice-governor of Sagami before reaching junior fifth upper rank and becoming governor of Kii, in which office he died. His daughter Sawako, a consort of Emperor Ninmyo, bore Prince Tokiyasu, who ascended as Emperor Koko in 884. Fusatsugu was thereupon posthumously raised to senior first rank and, in 885, to grand minister.
zh: 藤原总继是平安时代初期的贵族，为美作守藤原末茂之子，也是光孝天皇的外祖父。811年叙从五位下，历任中务少辅、相模介，后升从五位上、任纪伊守，最终卒于纪伊守任上。他的女儿泽子是仁明天皇的女御，所生时康亲王于884年即位，是为光孝天皇；总继因此被追赠正一位，885年又追赠太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Fuyutsugu (775–826) was an early Heian statesman, general and poet of the Northern Fujiwara, second son of Udaijin Fujiwara no Uchimaro. A close aide to Emperor Saga from his crown-prince days, he was named with Kose no Notari as the first heads of the Kurōdo-dokoro secretariat, established by Saga in 810 to counter the retired Emperor Heizei and Fujiwara no Kusuko. He joined the council as Sangi in 811, became Chūnagon in 816, Dainagon in 819 and Udaijin in 821, and was Sadaijin when he died in 826. His daughter was the mother of Emperor Montoku, who posthumously raised him to Daijō-daijin in 850.
zh: 藤原冬嗣（775—826）是平安初期的公卿、武将与歌人，出自藤原北家，为右大臣藤原内麻吕次子。他自嵯峨天皇为皇太子时即为亲信，810年嵯峨天皇为对抗平城上皇与藤原药子而设藏人所，他与巨势野足同任首任藏人头。811年任参议，位列公卿，此后历任816年中纳言、819年大纳言、821年右大臣，去世时官居左大臣。其女为文德天皇之母，850年文德天皇追赠他为太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Hidesato (c. 891–958), also known as Tawara Tōda, was a warrior lord of the northern Fujiwara based in Shimotsuke Province. When Taira no Masakado seized eight Kantō provinces in 939, Hidesato joined Taira no Sadamori and Fujiwara no Tamenori against him; in the second month of 940 they stormed Masakado's base in Shimōsa and killed him, ending the revolt. Hidesato was rewarded with the posts of chinjufu shōgun and governor of Shimotsuke and Musashi. He became ancestor of numerous warrior houses, including the Ōshū Fujiwara, and legend makes him slayer of a giant centipede in Ōmi.
zh: 藤原秀乡（约891—958），通称俵藤太，是以下野国为根据地的藤原北家武将。939年平将门起兵夺取关东八国，秀乡与平贞盛、藤原为宪联手讨伐，于940年二月攻入将门的据点下总国猿岛郡，将其斩杀，平定叛乱。他因功出任镇守府将军，并叙任下野、武藏两国国司。秀乡是奥州藤原氏等众多武家的始祖，民间还流传着他在近江国三上山斩杀大蜈蚣的传说。

en: Fujiwara no Ienari (1107–1154) was a late Heian court noble, third son of Councillor Fujiwara no Ieyasu of the Northern House's Uona line, who became middle counsellor at senior second rank. Under Emperor Toba's cloistered rule he was the retired emperor's chief favourite and, with his cousin Bifukumon-in, led the court while amassing many estates. In 1134 he built the Shōkōmyō-in chapel at the Toba palace. In 1151 followers of Fujiwara no Yorinaga sacked his mansion, enraging Toba and setting the scene for the Hōgen Disturbance. He died in 1154; his descendants founded the Shijō and Yamashina houses.
zh: 藤原家成（1107—1154）是平安时代末期公卿，为藤原北家鱼名流参议藤原家保的三子，官至正二位中纳言。在鸟羽上皇实行院政时期，他是上皇的第一宠臣，与堂姊妹美福门院一同深涉国政中枢，并在各国广建庄园，积聚财富。1134年，他在鸟羽殿营造胜光明院。1151年，藤原赖长的随从借口仆从相争袭击并捣毁他的宅邸，此事激怒鸟羽法皇，成为赖长失脚乃至保元之乱爆发的伏笔。1154年他去世，子孙繁衍为羽林家四条家与山科家。

en: Fujiwara no Ietoki was a Kamakura-period courtier of the Koichijo Fujiwara line. The Anekoji genealogy names him as a son of Fujiwara no Chikatsuna and the father of Morohira, Sadatoki and Nobutoki.
zh: 藤原家时是镰仓时代小一条流藤原氏贵族，姊小路家系图将他记为藤原亲纲之子，师平、贞时、信时三兄弟之父。

en: Ashikaga no Ietsuna was a late Heian warrior and third head of the Fujiwara-surnamed Ashikaga house of Shimotsuke, adopted heir of its founder Nariyuki. A famed strongman, he entered a court sumo contest in 1111 while still under age. Falsely accused of treason by Onodera Yoshihiro, he was exiled to Anraku-ji in Dazaifu. From 1142 to 1161 he fought Minamoto no Yoshikuni over the Yanada estate. His son Toshitsuna died after Shida Yoshihiro's rising of 1183; Ietsuna is last recorded in 1184, holding a memorial for him.
zh: 足利家纲是平安时代末期武将，下野国藤姓足利氏第三代当主，被始祖成行收为养子，以魁梧神力闻名，是相扑好手。1111年，他尚未元服便参加了宫中相扑节。他遭小野寺义宽诬陷谋反，被流放至大宰府安乐寺。约1142年至1161年，他为梁田御厨的地头职与源义国相争约二十年。1183年嫡子俊纲因志田义广举兵失败而死，家纲至1184年仍在为子追善，卒年不详。

en: Fujiwara no Ieyasu (1080–1136) was a late Heian court noble, the second son of the palace minister Fujiwara no Akisue of the Northern House's Uona line. He held a string of provincial governorships and won exceptional favour under the cloistered rule of Emperor Shirakawa, rising to councillor at junior third rank in 1134; his branch overtook the senior line as head of the Zenshōji house. He spent the wealth from his governorships on temples such as Shōkongō-in. After Shirakawa's death he fell from power under Emperor Toba, while his son Ienari rose.
zh: 藤原家保（1080—1136）是平安时代后期公卿，为藤原北家鱼名流修理大夫藤原显季的次子。他历任各国国司，在白河法皇院政时期深得宠信，1134年升至从三位参议，其一支凌驾于长兄长实的系统，取得善胜寺流嫡流的地位。他以任国司积累的财力出资修建证金刚院等多处堂塔。白河法皇去世后，他在鸟羽上皇的院政下失势，而三子家成代之兴起。

en: Fujiwara no Kamatari (614–669), born Nakatomi no Kamatari, was the founder of the Fujiwara clan. Born into the Nakatomi family of ritualists, he refused appointment as a ritual official and plotted against the Soga regime; in 645 he joined Prince Naka no Oe in a coup that killed Soga no Iruka and drove his father Emishi to suicide, launching the Taika Reform. As the new government's Inner Minister he helped build a Chinese-style centralized state. Shortly before his death in 669, Emperor Tenji granted him the surname Fujiwara and the highest rank Taishokan. His son Fuhito carried on the new house.
zh: 藤原镰足（614—669），本名中臣镰足，是藤原氏的始祖。他出身世掌祭祀的中臣氏，拒任祭官后谋划推翻苏我氏政权；645年，他与中大兄皇子发动政变，诛杀苏我入鹿，迫使其父苏我虾夷自尽，由此开启大化改新。他作为新政权的内臣，协助建立仿唐的中央集权国家。669年临终前，天智天皇赐姓藤原，并授予最高冠位大织冠。其子不比等继承了这一新家族。

en: Fujiwara no Kanefusa (1001–1069) was a Northern Fujiwara court noble, eldest son of the chūnagon Fujiwara no Kanetaka. Appointed Right Guards captain in 1015, he became notorious for violence at court: at a 1018 palace banquet he insulted the head chamberlain Fujiwara no Sadayori, kicked over his food and pelted his room with stones, and in 1023 had attendants beat an official in the palace, and the regent Yorimichi expelled him. He then held the provincial posts of Tango, Bitchū, Harima and Sanuki without further promotion. He died in 1069, aged sixty-nine; his son Sōen founded the Utsunomiya line.
zh: 藤原兼房（1001—1069）是平安时代中期至后期的贵族，藤原北家中纳言藤原兼隆的长子。1015年任右近卫少将，以在宫中行凶闹事闻名：1018年的一次内宴上，他辱骂藏人头藤原定赖、踢散其食物并向其居室投石；1023年又指使随从在宫中殴打官员，被关白藤原赖通逐出内裏。此后他历任丹后守、备中守、播磨守、赞岐守等地方官，再未得到升迁，终未能位列公卿。1069年去世，享年69岁；其子宗圆是宇都宫氏之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Kaneie (c. 929–990) was a son of Fujiwara no Morosuke and father of the regents Michitaka, Michikane and Michinaga. Long out of favour during the ascendancy of his rival brother Kanemichi, he was named minister of the right in 978. In the Kanna Disturbance of 986 he and his son Michikane pressured Emperor Kazan into taking the tonsure at Gangyō-ji, placing Kaneie's seven-year-old grandson on the throne as Emperor Ichijō. Kaneie then ruled as sesshō regent and became grand minister in 989. He took Buddhist vows shortly before his death in 990.
zh: 藤原兼家（约929—990）是藤原师辅之子，也是摄政道隆、道兼、道长的父亲。他在与兄长兼通的争斗中长期不得志，978年任右大臣。986年宽和之变中，他与儿子道兼逼迫花山天皇在元庆寺出家退位，拥立七岁的外孙即位为一条天皇，随后以摄政身份总揽朝政，989年升任太政大臣。990年他病重出家，不久去世。

en: Fujiwara no Kanemitsu (dates unknown) was an eleventh-century military noble of the Hidesato Fujiwara line, a son of Chinjufu General Fujiwara no Fuminaga and father of Fujiwara no Yoriyuki and Fujiwara no Munemichi. He is recorded as a commander of the chinjufu defense headquarters.
zh: 藤原兼光（生没年不详）是11世纪秀乡流藤原氏军事贵族，系图记为镇守府将军藤原文修之子、藤原赖行与藤原宗道之父，本人也曾任镇守府将军。

en: Fujiwara no Kanenori was a twelfth-century noble, said to be a son of the courtier Fujiwara no Yukinari. He migrated from Ōmi Province to Miyoshi district in Bingo Province; his son Kanemune took the title Miyoshi Dayū and founded the Bingo Miyoshi warrior clan.
zh: 藤原兼范是12世纪的贵族，相传为公卿藤原行成之子。他从近江国迁居备后国三吉乡，其子兼宗自称三吉大夫，开创了备后三吉氏。

en: Fujiwara no Kanetaka (985–1053) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Fujiwara Hokke, the second son and heir of Regent Fujiwara no Michikane, who died weeks after taking office in 995. Unlike his cousins Korechika and Takaie, he attached himself to his uncle Michinaga, becoming the youngest councillor in 1008 at twenty-four. He rose to provisional middle counsellor in 1019, middle counsellor in 1023 and senior second rank in 1024, though gossip blamed him for Crown Prince Atsuaki's resignation in 1017. He resigned in 1035, took vows in 1046, and died in 1053.
zh: 藤原兼隆（985—1053）是平安时代中期公卿，出自藤原北家，为关白右大臣藤原道兼次男，长兄夭折后作为嫡子抚养。995年父亲就任关白不到两周便急死，他没有像堂兄伊周、隆家那样反抗，而是依附叔父藤原道长，1008年以24岁成为最年轻的参议。他于1019年升权中纳言，1023年任中纳言，1024年叙正二位；1017年敦明亲王辞去皇太子，风传是受他欺骗。1035年他辞去中纳言，1046年出家，1053年10月去世，享年69岁。

en: Fujiwara no Kaneyuki was an eleventh-century warrior of the Fujiwara Hidesato line, recorded as a son of Fujiwara no Yoriyuki. His line settled in Kozuke province in his day, and his son Nariyuki took the name Ashikaga in Shimotsuke, beginning the Fujiwara Ashikaga clan.
zh: 藤原兼行是11世纪藤原秀乡流的武士，家谱记为藤原赖行之子。相传在他这一代家族定居上野国，其子成行以下野国足利郡为据点改称足利氏，即藤姓足利氏之始。

en: Fujiwara no Kinmichi was a court noble of the late Heian period, from the Ononomiya line of the Northern Fujiwara. The Sonpi Bunmyaku genealogies name him as a son of the councillor Fujiwara no Kinsada, who died in 1099.
zh: 藤原公通是平安时代后期的贵族，出自藤原北家小野宫流。《尊卑分脉》系图将他列为1099年去世的参议藤原公定之子。

en: Fujiwara no Kinmitsu was an eleventh-century warrior of the Hidesato branch of the Fujiwara, a fifth-generation grandson of Fujiwara no Hidesato and a son of Fujiwara no Fumiyuki, Shimotsuke no kami. He served the court of Emperor Go-Reizei with distinction. In the eleventh month of 1057, the year after the Akurigawa incident opened the Earlier Nine Years' War in the north, he followed Minamoto no Yoriyoshi against Abe no Yoritoki in Mutsu and was killed in the fighting. His son Tsunenori became the ancestor of the Hatano warrior house.
zh: 藤原公光是平安时代的武士，藤原秀乡的五代孙，下野守藤原文行之子。他在后冷泉天皇朝立有军功。1057年（天喜五年）十一月，即阿久利川事件的次年，他随源赖义前往陆奥，与安倍赖时交战，最终战死，是前九年合战的一部分。其子藤原经范成为波多野氏的初代祖先。

en: Fujiwara no Kinnari (999–1043) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Northern House's Kan'in line, eldest son of Middle Counsellor Fujiwara no Sanenari and maternal grandfather of Emperor Shirakawa. Adopted in childhood by his grandfather, Grand Minister Fujiwara no Kinsue, he came of age in 1011, headed the imperial secretariat from 1020, and became a councillor in 1026. In 1043 he was promoted to provisional middle counsellor at junior second rank, dying months later aged forty-five. His daughter Shigeko, adopted by Fujiwara no Yoshinobu, married Emperor Go-Sanjō and bore Shirakawa, beginning the Kan'in line's rise as imperial in-laws.
zh: 藤原公成（999—1043）是平安时代中期的公卿，藤原北家闲院流中纳言藤原实成的长子，也是白河天皇的外祖父。他幼年被祖父、太政大臣藤原公季收为养子并深受溺爱，1011年元服，1020年起出任藏人头约六年，1026年任参议。1043年，他升任从二位权中纳言，但数月后便去世，享年45岁。其女茂子为藤原能信的养女，嫁给后三条天皇，生下白河天皇，开启了闲院流作为外戚的荣华。

en: Fujiwara no Kinsada (1049–1099), known as the Takamatsu Chancellor, was a court noble of the Ononomiya branch of the Fujiwara Hokke and the eldest son of Provisional Middle Counsellor Fujiwara no Tsuneie. He received his first rank in 1060 and served as chamberlain. In 1072, after Emperor Shirakawa acceded and his brother Sanehito became crown prince, Kinsada became the prince's provisional assistant. Following the death of retired Emperor Go-Sanjō in 1073, his appointments stalled for a time. He became head chamberlain in 1083 and provisional left middle controller in 1084, then joined the kugyo as councillor in 1086. Promoted only slowly thereafter, he reached junior third rank in 1092 and senior third rank in 1097, and died in 1099 aged fifty-one.
zh: 藤原公定（1049—1099）是平安时代后期公卿，出自藤原北家小野宫流，为权中纳言藤原经家的长子，号高松宰相。他于1060年叙从五位下，曾任侍从。1072年白河天皇即位，其弟实仁亲王立为皇太子，公定出任春宫权亮。1073年后三条上皇去世后，他的叙任一度停滞。他于1083年任藏人头，1084年任权左中辨，1086年任参议，跻身公卿。此后他晋升迟滞，1092年才叙从三位，1097年升正三位，1099年去世，享年51岁。

en: Fujiwara no Kinsue (c. 956–1029) was the eleventh son, by some accounts the twelfth, of the udaijin Fujiwara no Morosuke; his mother was Princess Yasuiko, a daughter of Emperor Daigo. After his mother died soon after his birth, his sister Empress Anshi raised him at court, where Emperor Murakami treated him much like a prince. Named Sangi in 983, he became naidaijin in 997 after Fujiwara no Korechika fell from power. He supported Fujiwara no Michinaga's government during his long tenure, became udaijin in 1017, and in 1021 was promoted to daijō daijin under Emperor Go-Ichijō. He died in office in 1029, was posthumously granted senior first rank and the Chinese-style posthumous name Jingi-kō, and is known as the Kan'in Minister, ancestor of the Kan'in Fujiwara line.
zh: 藤原公季（约956—1029）是右大臣藤原师辅的第十一子（一说第十二子），母亲为醍醐天皇之女康子内亲王。母亲在他出生后不久去世，他由姐姐中宫安子在宫中抚养，村上天皇待他如同皇子。他于983年任参议，997年在藤原伊周失势后接任内大臣，长期任职期间支持藤原道长的政权；1017年任右大臣，1021年在后一条天皇朝升任太政大臣。1029年他在任内去世，追赠正一位，汉风谥号为仁义公，号闲院大臣，是藤原氏闲院流之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Kintō (966–1041), known as the Shijō Dainagon, was a Heian courtier, poet and calligrapher, the son of the regent Fujiwara no Yoritada. Admired by contemporaries including Murasaki Shikibu and Sei Shōnagon, he laid the groundwork for the imperial anthology Shūi Wakashū with a draft collection made in 996–999, compiled the celebrated Wakan rōeishū of Chinese and Japanese verse, and around 1009–1011 established the canon of the Thirty-Six Poetry Immortals. With Fujiwara no Tadanobu, Minamoto no Toshikata and Fujiwara no Yukinari he is counted one of the Four Nagon. His son was the poet Sadayori.
zh: 藤原公任（966—1041）是平安时代的公卿、歌人与书法家，关白藤原赖忠之子，世称四条大纳言。他深受紫式部、清少纳言等同时代人推崇，996—999年编成《拾遗抄》，为敕撰《拾遗和歌集》奠定基础；又编纂荟萃中日诗歌的《和汉朗咏集》，并于1009—1011年前后确立三十六歌仙的谱系。他与藤原齐信、源俊贤、藤原行成并称“四纳言”，其子为歌人藤原定赖。

en: Fujiwara no Kinzane (1053–1107) was a court noble and poet of the Kan'in branch of the Fujiwara Hokke, eldest son of Major Counsellor Fujiwara no Sanesue, known as the Sanjo Major Counsellor. He became fifth-rank chamberlain on the accession of his cousin Emperor Shirakawa in 1072, head chamberlain and councillor in 1080, and provisional major counsellor in 1100. As maternal uncle of Emperor Toba he was made the crown prince's steward in 1103, and when Toba acceded in 1107 he claimed the regency but was rejected, dying four months later. His daughter Shoshi later bore Emperors Sutoku and Go-Shirakawa.
zh: 藤原公实（1053—1107）是平安时代后期公卿、歌人，出自藤原北家闲院流，为大纳言藤原实季的长子，人称三条大纳言。1072年从兄白河天皇即位后，他任五位藏人，1080年任藏人头、参议，1100年升权大纳言。作为鸟羽天皇的外伯父，他于1103年兼任春宫大夫；1107年鸟羽天皇即位时他主张由自己出任摄政，却遭驳斥，四个月后去世。其女璋子后来为鸟羽天皇生下崇德、后白河两天皇。

en: Fujiwara no Kiyofusa, also called Kanshuji Kiyofusa, was a court noble of the Kanshuji line of the Fujiwara Hokke, son of Fujiwara no Morinori. After his father and uncle were exiled in the Hogen Disturbance of 1156, the family fell, but Kiyofusa served Emperor Go-Toba and restored its standing. When the Jokyu Disturbance of 1221 brought Go-Toba's exile to Oki, Kiyofusa took the tonsure and followed him there. In 1240 he was appointed governor of Dewa. His second son Shigefusa, lord of the Uesugi manor in Tamba, became the founder of the Uesugi clan.
zh: 藤原清房（又称劝修寺清房）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代前期的公卿，出自藤原北家劝修寺流，为藤原盛宪之子。1156年保元之乱后，父亲与叔父都被流放，家道中落；清房近侍后鸟羽天皇，致力复兴家门。1221年承久之乱后，后鸟羽上皇被流放隐岐，他出家相随。1240年他出任出羽守。其次子重房领有丹波国上杉庄，即上杉氏之祖上杉重房。

en: Fujiwara no Kiyonatsu was an early Heian noble of the Southern Fujiwara house, recorded in genealogies as a son of Takasuke, governor of Mutsu, and father of the warrior-noble Fujiwara no Korechika.
zh: 藤原清夏是平安时代前期贵族，属藤原南家乙麻吕流。谱系记载他是陆奥守藤原高扶之子、武将藤原维几之父。

en: Fujiwara no Korechiyo (dates unknown) was a Heian-period noble of the southern Fujiwara house, the son of Fujiwara no Kiyoka and deputy governor of Hitachi Province. In 939 he clashed with the local magnate Fujiwara no Haruaki, who had withheld taxes and seized provincial goods, and demanded that Taira no Masakado surrender the fugitive. Masakado refused, stormed the Hitachi headquarters with about a thousand men, routed Korechiyo's three-thousand-strong provincial force and captured him along with the provincial seal. His son Fujiwara no Tamenori later helped destroy Masakado in 940.
zh: 藤原维几（生卒年不详）是日本平安时代贵族，出身藤原南家，为藤原清夏之子，官至常陆介、从五位。939年，他与拒缴租税、夺取官物的当地豪族藤原玄明对立，要求平将门交出逃入门下的玄明；将门不允，率约千人进攻常陆国府，击溃维几的三千国衙军队，将其俘获并夺取印玺。其子藤原为宪后来投奔藤原秀乡，于940年参与攻灭将门。

en: Fujiwara no Korekimi (727–789), first named Kuromaro, was the eldest son of Fujiwara no Otomaro of the Fujiwara Southern House. After his father's death in 760 he served as governor of Harima and Yamashiro and rose swiftly under Empress Shōtoku, changing his name to Korekimi. Made councillor in 774, he headed the household of Crown Prince Yamabe, who as Emperor Kanmu raised him to middle councillor in 781, great councillor in 782 and right minister in 783. He died in 789 aged sixty-three, concurrently commander of the imperial guards, and was posthumously granted junior first rank.
zh: 藤原是公（727—789），初名黑麻吕，是藤原南家藤原乙麻吕的长子。760年父亲死后，他历任播磨守、山背守，在称德天皇朝升迁迅速，并改名是公。774年他出任参议，还担任皇太子山部亲王的春宫大夫；山部亲王即位为桓武天皇后，于781年升他为中纳言，782年升大纳言，783年拜右大臣。789年他去世，享年63岁，死时兼中卫大将，即日追赠从一位。

en: Fujiwara no Koretada (924–972) was the eldest son of Fujiwara no Morosuke and maternal uncle of Emperors Reizei and En'yū, whose mother was his sister Anshi. In 951 Emperor Murakami made him a compiler of the imperial waka anthology, and his poetry later entered the Hyakunin Isshu. He rose to minister of the right in 970 and, after the death of his uncle Saneyori, became sesshō regent; in 971 he was named grand minister. He supervised En'yū's enthronement early in 972 but fell ill and died that November, aged forty-nine.
zh: 藤原伊尹（924—972）是藤原师辅的长子，其妹安子为村上天皇中宫，故他是冷泉、圆融两天皇的外伯父。951年，村上天皇命他参与敕撰和歌编纂，其和歌后来收录于《百人一首》。他于970年任右大臣，伯父实赖去世后接任摄政，971年又任太政大臣。972年初他主持圆融天皇即位仪式，同年11月病逝，享年49岁。

en: Fujiwara no Managa was a Nara-period official of the Northern Fujiwara, son of Dainagon Fujiwara no Matate and elder brother of Udaijin Fujiwara no Uchimaro. His highest rank was senior sixth rank, upper grade, and he never reached the fifth rank.
zh: 藤原真永是奈良时代官人，出自藤原北家，为大纳言藤原真楯之子、右大臣藤原内麻吕之兄。他最高官位仅止正六位上，终身未能叙至五位。

en: Fujiwara no Masanori (c. 997–1064) was a mid-Heian military commander in Kyushu, remembered as the father of Kikuchi no Noritaka, ancestor of the Kikuchi clan of Higo. Genealogies claim he was a son of Fujiwara no Takaie, the Dazaifu viceroy celebrated for repelling the Toi invasion of 1019, though modern scholars regard this descent as a claim adopted by the Kikuchi to ennoble their line. He served as junior assistant at Dazaifu, held the governorships of Tsushima in 1013 and Hizen in 1015, and was once pursued on suspicion of murdering Fujiwara no Sadatō.
zh: 藤原政则（约997—1064）是平安时代中期在九州活动的武将，被视为肥后菊池氏始祖菊池则隆之父。各类家谱称他是藤原隆家之子——隆家曾任大宰权帅，因击退1019年的刀伊入寇而闻名；但现代学者认为，菊池氏自称出自隆家一系属于冒称。政则曾任大宰少贰，1013年任对马守、1015年任肥前守，还曾因涉嫌杀害藤原定任而遭到追捕。

en: Fujiwara no Matate (715–766), first named Yatsuka, was a court noble of the Fujiwara Northern House, third son of Fujiwara no Fusasaki. A gifted poet favoured by Emperor Shōmu, he rose fast and became councillor in 748. He supported Fujiwara no Nakamaro's Chinese-style reforms and in 758 received the Tang-style name Matate, becoming middle councillor in 762. In Nakamaro's rebellion of 764 he sided with retired Empress Kōken and commanded the imperial guards. Made great councillor in 766, he died soon after aged fifty-two and was posthumously made grand minister. His son Uchimaro continued the Northern House line.
zh: 藤原真楯（715—766），初名八束，是奈良时代的公卿，出自藤原北家，为藤原房前的第三子。他富有诗才，受圣武天皇器重，升迁迅速，748年出任参议。他支持藤原仲麻吕的唐风改革，758年获赐唐式名字“真楯”，762年任中纳言。764年仲麻吕之乱时，他站在孝谦上皇一边，统率近卫兵。766年他升任大纳言，不久去世，享年52岁，死后追赠太政大臣。其子内麻吕延续了北家一脉。

en: Fujiwara no Michiie (c. 1027–1038) was a noble of the mid-Heian period, of the Mikohidari line of the Northern Fujiwara. He was the eldest son of Major Counselor Fujiwara no Nagaie, sixth son of the regent Michinaga, and his mother was Yoshiko, daughter of Minamoto no Takamasa. Raised in the Sanjō mansion called the Mikohidari residence, he reached only junior fifth rank, lower grade. He died on 14 May 1038, shortly after coming of age, and his grieving mother took Buddhist vows.
zh: 藤原道家（约1027—1038）是日本平安时代中期的贵族，属藤原北家御子左流，为大纳言藤原长家的长子，长家则是摄政藤原道长的第六子。母亲是源高雅之女源懿子。他在三条的御子左第长大，位阶仅至从五位下。1038年5月14日，他元服后不久即早逝，母亲悲痛出家。

en: Fujiwara no Michikane (961–995) was the third son of Fujiwara no Kaneie and a mid-Heian courtier. In 986 he played the key part in unseating Emperor Kazan: when the grief-stricken emperor, mourning his consort Yoshiko, was persuaded to renounce the world, Michikane escorted him secretly from the palace to the Gangyō-ji monastery to take the tonsure, then left without keeping his own vow to become a monk, clearing the way for his nephew Emperor Ichijō. Promoted udaijin in 994, he succeeded his brother Michitaka as kampaku in 995 but died only seven days later, remembered as the Seven-Day Kampaku.
zh: 藤原道兼（961—995）是藤原兼家的第三子，平安时代中期的公卿。986年，花山天皇因宠爱的女御藤原忯子去世而悲痛厌世，道兼劝其出家，并立誓相随，趁夜将天皇秘密带出皇宫，送往山科的元庆寺落发；天皇出家后他却借故离去，一去不返，为外甥一条天皇即位扫清了道路。994年他升任右大臣，995年继兄长道隆之后出任关白，仅七天便病死，世称“七日关白”。

en: Fujiwara no Michinaga (966–1028) was the Heian statesman under whom Fujiwara power reached its height. After his brothers Michitaka and Michikane died in 995, he defeated his nephew Korechika in the struggle for power, rising from minister of the right to minister of the left by 996. Though never kampaku, he ruled as the Mido Kampaku, marrying four daughters to Emperors Ichijō, Sanjō and Go-Ichijō and the future Go-Suzaku, and serving as sesshō from 1016. He yielded the regency to his son Yorimichi, took vows in 1019 and died in 1028, leaving the diary Midō Kanpakuki.
zh: 藤原道长（966—1028）是把藤原氏权势推向顶峰的平安时代公卿。995年两位兄长道隆、道兼相继死后，他在与侄子伊周的权力斗争中胜出，995—996年间由右大臣升任左大臣。他始终未任关白，却以“御堂关白”之名主宰朝政，把四个女儿分别嫁给一条、三条、后一条天皇以及后来的后朱雀天皇，并于1016年出任摄政。后来他把摄政之位让给儿子赖通，1019年出家，1028年去世，留有日记《御堂关白记》。

en: Fujiwara no Michitaka (953–995) was the eldest son of the regent Fujiwara no Kaneie and a leading courtier of the mid-Heian period. When Kaneie died in 990, Michitaka succeeded him, serving first as kampaku and then as sesshō to his nephew Emperor Ichijō. That same year he made his daughter Teishi the emperor's chūgū, creating the unprecedented simultaneous presence of four empresses. Known as the Naka-no-Kampaku, he later fell ill and tried to hand the regency to his son Korechika, but failed; he died in 995 after barely five years in power.
zh: 藤原道隆（953—995）是摄政藤原兼家的长子，平安时代中期的公卿。990年兼家去世后，他以外伯父身份先后担任一条天皇的关白与摄政；同年将长女定子立为一条天皇的中宫，出现史无前例的四后并立。他世称“中关白”，晚年患病，欲把关白之位让给儿子伊周却未能实现，主政仅约五年便病没。

en: Fujiwara no Michito (974–1039) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Northern House, son of Major Counselor Fujiwara no Naritoki. Ennobled in 986, he served from 996 Crown Prince Okisada, whose consort was his sister Seishi. When Okisada ascended as Emperor Sanjo in 1011, Michito became head chamberlain and then councilor, reaching junior third rank in 1012. His career was checked by Fujiwara no Michinaga, who blocked his promotions and in 1017 pressured Seishi’s son, Crown Prince Atsuakira, into resigning. Michito reached senior third rank in 1023 and provisional middle counselor in 1035, dying in 1039 aged sixty-six.
zh: 藤原通任（974—1039）是平安时代中期的公卿，出自藤原北家小一条流，为大纳言藤原济时之子。986年叙爵，996年起侍奉皇太子居贞亲王，其姐娍子是太子之妃。1011年居贞即位为三条天皇，通任随即出任藏人头、参议，1012年升至从三位。他的仕途受到藤原道长阻挠：道长压下他的晋升，并于1017年逼迫娍子所生的皇太子敦明亲王辞退储位。通任1023年升正三位，1035年任权中纳言，1039年去世，享年66岁。

en: Fujiwara no Morinori was a late-Heian court noble of the Fujiwara Northern House's Kanjūji line and the eldest son of Shōnagon Fujiwara no Akinori. His aunt was Fujiwara no Yorinaga's mother, and as a maternal cousin he served Yorinaga as a close attendant. He also waited on Retired Emperor Sutoku, and in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 joined the Sutoku side with his brothers. After the defeat he fled with Yorinaga, took the tonsure and was captured; tortured on a sorcery charge, he was exiled to Sado Province on 3 August 1156. His grandson Shigefusa founded the Uesugi clan.
zh: 藤原盛宪是平安时代后期的公卿，出自藤原北家劝修寺流，为少纳言藤原显宪的长子。他的姑母是藤原赖长的生母，因此作为母方表亲近侍赖长，同时也是崇德上皇的殿上人。1156年保元之乱时，他与兄弟们加入上皇一方；战败后随赖长逃亡，出家后仍被捕获，并因涉嫌诅咒而遭受拷问，于8月3日流放佐渡国。其孙重房后来以上杉为苗字，是上杉氏的始祖。

en: Fujiwara no Morizane (died between 1107 and 1119) was a court noble of the late Heian period from the Kanjūji line of the Northern Fujiwara, the son of Fujiwara no Norisuke, minister of the palace household. He served the regent house as a household officer, holding the posts of minor councillor and steward of the empress's household and serving as governor of Tosa Province in 1106; his highest rank was Senior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade, as minister of civil administration. His daughter became Fujiwara no Tadazane's concubine and bore Fujiwara no Yorinaga.
zh: 藤原盛实（卒于1107—1119年间）是平安时代后期的贵族，出自藤原北家劝修寺流，为宫内卿藤原宪辅之子。他作为家司侍奉摄关家，历任少纳言、中宫亮，1106年任土佐守，最终官至正四位下治部卿。其女成为藤原忠实的侧室，生下藤原赖长。

en: Fujiwara no Morohira was a Kamakura-period courtier of the Koichijo Fujiwara line, recorded in the Anekoji genealogy as a son of Fujiwara no Ietoki and the father of Fujiwara no Yorimoto.
zh: 藤原师平是镰仓时代小一条流藤原氏贵族，姊小路家系图将他记为藤原家时之子、藤原赖基之父。

en: Fujiwara no Moromichi (1062–1099) was a late Heian regent, the eldest son of the kampaku Fujiwara no Morozane. In 1094 he succeeded his father as kampaku and, with Emperor Horikawa, pursued vigorous government independent of the retired Emperor Shirakawa, reining in the cloister court's appointees; contemporaries praised the realm as orderly under his rule. In 1095 he forcefully rejected Enryaku-ji monks' demands and had their armed protest driven off. He died suddenly in 1099, aged 37, and the regent house never recovered its former power against Shirakawa.
zh: 藤原师通（1062—1099）是平安时代后期的公卿，关白藤原师实的嫡男。1094年他继任关白，与堀河天皇联手推行积极政务，摆脱白河上皇的掣肘，约束院近臣的任官，时人称赞当时天下肃然。1095年延历寺日吉社发起强诉，他断然拒绝其要求，派兵驱散僧兵。1099年师通暴卒，年仅37岁，摄关家从此在白河上皇面前一蹶不振。

en: Fujiwara no Moronari (1009–1081) was a court noble of the Koichijo branch of the Fujiwara Hokke, the eldest son of Provisional Middle Counsellor Fujiwara no Michito. He received his first rank in 1021 and rose through guard and provincial posts, serving as governor of Bitchu in 1045, Tango in 1056 and Omi in 1062. In 1063 he was appointed senior assistant minister of Dazaifu and promoted to junior third rank, joining the kugyo. He became senior second rank in 1073 and councillor in 1075, retired in 1080, and took monastic vows and died the next year aged seventy-three.
zh: 藤原师成（1009—1081）是平安时代中期至后期的公卿，出自藤原北家小一条流，为权中纳言藤原通任的长子。他于1021年叙爵，历任近卫府武官与地方受领，1045年任备中守，1056年任丹后守，1062年任近江守。1063年他就任大宰大贰并叙从三位，跻身公卿，1073年升正二位，1075年任参议。1080年辞官，次年出家并去世，享年73岁。

en: Fujiwara no Moroshige (born c. 1050) was an eleventh-century courtier of the Fujiwara Hidesato line, son of Fujiwara no Naomichi and provisional governor of Kii. Genealogies name him as the father of Fujiwara no Munenaga, who is recorded living at Yuasa in Kii around 1099.
zh: 藤原师重（约1050年生）是11世纪藤原秀乡流的贵族，藤原直道之子，曾任纪伊权守。家谱记他为藤原宗永之父；约1099年前后，宗永作为纪伊汤浅的居民见载。

en: Fujiwara no Morosue was an eleventh-century courtier of the Koichijo Fujiwara line, recorded in the Anekoji genealogy as a son of the councillor Fujiwara no Moronari and the father of Fujiwara no Tadatoki.
zh: 藤原师季是11世纪小一条流藤原氏贵族，姊小路家系图将他记为参议藤原师成之子、藤原尹时之父。

en: Fujiwara no Morosuke (909–960), known as Kujō-dono, was the second son of the regent Fujiwara no Tadahira and a learned mid-Heian statesman. He married three daughters of Emperor Daigo in succession, beginning with Princess Kinshi around 930. Promoted to udaijin in 947, he overshadowed his elder brother Saneyori as the driving force of Emperor Murakami's Tenryaku government, aided by his daughter Anshi, the empress who bore the future emperors Reizei and En'yū. He died in 960 aged fifty-three, never regent himself; under his sons Koretada and Kaneie his Kujō line became the Fujiwara regent house.
zh: 藤原师辅（909—960），人称九条殿，是摄政藤原忠平的次子，博学多才、精通朝仪的平安时代公卿。约930年起，他先后娶醍醐天皇的三位皇女为妻，首娶勤子内亲王。947年他升任右大臣，在村上天皇的天历之治中比兄长实赖更握实权；其女安子为天皇中宫，生下后来的冷泉、圆融两位天皇。他于960年病逝，享年53岁，生前并未出任摄关；在儿子伊尹、兼家等人手中，他的九条流成为藤原氏嫡流摄关家。

en: Fujiwara no Morotada (920–969) was the fifth son of the regent Fujiwara no Tadahira and founder of the Koichijō lineage of the clan. He came of age in 932 and rose steadily at court, joining the senior councillors in 946 and becoming provisional middle counsellor in 948. His daughter Yoshiko entered Emperor Murakami's harem and was named an imperial consort in 958. After the Anna Incident of 969, in which he and his brother Saneyori engineered the downfall of Minamoto no Takaakira, Morotada took Takaakira's post as minister of the left, but died of illness only months later.
zh: 藤原师尹（920—969）是摄政太政大臣藤原忠平的第五子，为藤氏小一条流之祖。他于932年元服，在朝中稳步晋升，946年成为公卿，948年任权中纳言。其女芳子入村上天皇后宫，958年受封女御。969年安和之变中，他与兄长实赖合力扳倒左大臣源高明，随后接任左大臣，仅数月后便病逝。

en: Fujiwara no Morotsuna (died 25 September 1172) was a late Heian noble and poet of the Koichijo Fujiwara line, the eldest son of Fujiwara no Tadatoki. As a close aide of Retired Emperor Shirakawa he held the posts of palace minister, chief of the imperial table and general of the chinjufu. In 1142, while governor of Mutsu, he took a firm stand against Fujiwara no Motohira of the Oshu Fujiwara, who controlled the province, winning fame for upholding court authority. He ended at senior fourth rank, lower grade. His descendants became the Anekoji house, hereditary governors of Hida.
zh: 藤原师纲（？—1172）是平安时代末期的贵族与歌人，出自小一条流藤原氏，为刑部少辅藤原尹时的长子。他身为白河上皇的院近臣，历任宫内卿、大膳大夫、镇守府将军。1142年任陆奥守期间，他对实际控制该国的奥州藤原氏当主藤原基衡采取强硬姿态，因伸张朝廷权威而声名远扬，最终官至正四位下。其子孙后来成为世代担任飞驒国司的姊小路家，一直延续到战国时代。

en: Fujiwara no Morozane (1042–1101), sixth son of the kampaku Fujiwara no Yorimichi, became heir to the regent's house after the sudden death of his elder brother Michifusa. He outmaneuvered his uncle Norimichi and cousin Nobunaga over the regency, became kampaku after Norimichi's death, and then served as sessho for Emperor Horikawa, the son of his adopted daughter Kenshi, restoring the power of the Mido line. A noted poet, he placed sixteen poems in imperial anthologies, held a great poetry contest at Koyo-in in 1094, and left the diary Kyogoku Kampakuki.
zh: 藤原师实（1042—1101）是关白藤原赖通的六子，在嫡兄通房急死后被立为摄关家继承人。他与叔父教通、堂兄信长围绕摄关之位相争，教通死后就任关白。他把养女贤子送入白河天皇后宫，贤子生下堀河天皇，师实又出任天皇的摄政，重振了道长以来御堂流的权势。他擅长和歌，有16首作品入传敕撰和歌集，1094年在高阳院举办盛大歌合，另著有日记《京极关白记》。

en: Fujiwara no Mototsune (836–891) was the dominant statesman of the early Heian court. Third son of Fujiwara no Nagara, he was adopted by his uncle, the regent Fujiwara no Yoshifusa, and inherited his power. He became minister of the right in 872 and regent in 876, and in 879 helped complete the Veritable Records of Emperor Montoku. After Emperor Yozei's abdication in 884 he exercised powers later associated with the kampaku under Emperor Koko; the term appeared in an imperial edict under Emperor Uda in 887. He died in 891.
zh: 藤原基经（836—891）是平安时代前期权倾朝野的公卿。他是藤原长良的三男，被叔父、摄政藤原良房收为养子并继承其权柄，872年任右大臣，876年任摄政，879年参与修成《日本文德天皇实录》。884年阳成天皇退位后，他在光孝天皇朝实际上行使后来关白的职权；“关白”一词于887年宇多天皇的诏书中出现。891年，他去世。

en: Fujiwara no Muchimaro (680–737), eldest son of Fujiwara no Fuhito, founded the Fujiwara Southern House. After early service at court and as governor of Omi, he became middle councillor after his father's death in 720. In 729 he led the interrogation that destroyed Prince Nagaya and was made great councillor. In 730 he brought his brothers into the council, establishing the rule of the four Fujiwara brothers, and became right minister in 734. He died in the smallpox epidemic of 737, receiving senior first rank and the office of left minister on his deathbed.
zh: 藤原武智麻吕（680—737）是藤原不比等的长子，藤原南家之祖。他早年在朝廷任职，曾任近江守，720年父亲去世后出任中纳言。729年，他主导审问、扳倒长屋王，随后升任大纳言。730年，他把弟弟们引入议政官，确立藤原四兄弟政权，734年升任右大臣。737年他死于天花流行，临终时被授予正一位和左大臣之职。

en: Fujiwara no Munemichi was a Heian-period noble of the Hidesato line of the Northern Fujiwara, recorded in genealogies as the son of Kanemitsu and father of Naomichi, ancestors of the Yuasa clan of Kii Province.
zh: 藤原宗道是日本平安时代贵族，属藤原北家秀乡流。谱系载其为藤原兼光之子、藤原直道之父，是纪伊国汤浅氏的先祖。

en: Fujiwara no Munenaga was a noble of the late Heian period, from the Hidesato line of the Northern Fujiwara and a son of Fujiwara no Moroshige, provisional governor of Kii Province. Commonly called Yuasa Sakon Daibu, he appears around 1099 in the origin chronicle of Kokawadera as Fujiwara no Munenaga, a resident of Yuasa in Kii. His eldest son Yuasa no Muneshige had his holdings, including Yuasa estate, confirmed after the establishment of the Kamakura shogunate and became its vassal. Munenaga's daughter married Suzuki Shigekuni, also of Kii.
zh: 藤原宗永是平安时代末期的贵族，出自藤原北家秀乡流，为纪伊权守藤原师重之子，通称汤浅左近大夫。《粉河寺缘起》记载，1099年前后纪伊有一位“汤浅之住人藤原宗永”。其长子汤浅宗重在镰仓幕府成立后获得汤浅庄等所领的安堵，成为幕府御家人。宗永之女嫁给同在纪伊的铃木重邦。

en: Sudō no Munesuke, titled Nasu Mushadokoro, was the sixth head of the Sudō warrior house of Nasu District in Shimotsuke Province. The son of Sudō no Sukefusa, he led the clan when it abandoned Kanda Castle, its stronghold for four generations, and moved to Inazumi Castle. His son Suketaka was the first of the line to take the surname Nasu and fathered Nasu no Yoichi, the archer famed at the Battle of Yashima in 1185.
zh: 须藤宗资，称那须武者所，是下野国那须郡须藤武士家族的第六代当主。他是须藤资房之子，在他这一代，家族放弃了历经四代的本据神田城，移往稻积城。其子资隆是这一家族中最先改用“那须”苗字的人，并生下了在1185年屋岛之战中闻名的弓箭手那须与一。

en: Fujiwara no Murao (died 932) was a noble of the Northern Fujiwara house, son of Toyosawa and father of the celebrated warrior Hidesato, known as Tawara no Tōta. He succeeded his father as senior secretary of Shimotsuke Province, was promoted to junior fifth rank lower in 887 and junior fourth rank lower in 911, and also served as governor of Kawachi and Shimotsuke. His daughter married Taira no Kunika and bore Taira no Sadamori. The office he inherited passed down among his descendants, including the Ōta and Oyama warrior clans. He died in 932.
zh: 藤原村雄（？—932）是平安时代前期至中期的贵族，属藤原北家，为藤原丰泽之子、名将藤原秀乡（俵藤太）之父。他承袭父职任下野大掾，887年叙从五位下，911年升至从四位下，还曾任河内守、下野守。其女嫁与平国香，生下平贞盛。他承袭的职务在后裔中延续，包括太田氏、小山氏等武家。他于932年去世。

en: Fujiwara no Nagaie (1005–1064) was a mid-Heian noble and waka poet, the youngest son of the regent Fujiwara no Michinaga. Born to Minamoto no Meishi and adopted by Michinaga's wife Rinshi, he advanced rapidly, joining the council in 1022 and reaching provisional senior counselor, his highest post, in 1028; his elder brothers blocked further rise. In 1060 he burned his carriage when his young nephew Morozane was promoted past him. He took vows during illness in the tenth month of 1064 and died weeks later. He founded the Mikohidari house of poets, the line of Shunzei and Teika.
zh: 藤原长家（1005—1064）是平安时代中期的公卿、歌人，摄政藤原道长最小的儿子，生母为源明子，后为道长的嫡妻源伦子收养。他晋升顺利，1022年位列公卿，1028年官至权大纳言，这也是他的最高官职，此后因兄长们长年在世而再难升迁。1060年，年轻的外甥师实官位升到自己之上，他愤而烧毁座车。1064年十月，他在病中出家，几周后便去世。他是御子左家歌人之家的始祖，俊成、定家皆出自这一流。

en: Fujiwara no Nagara (802–856) was an early Heian statesman of the Northern House of the Fujiwara and eldest son of Minister of the Left Fujiwara no Fuyutsugu. Trusted by Emperor Ninmyo from his crown-prince years, he headed the palace secretariat and a guard division before becoming councillor in 844, ten years behind his brother Yoshifusa. He reached provisional middle counselor in 854 and junior second rank in 856, dying soon after. His daughter Takaiko bore Emperor Yozei and his third son Mototsune, adopted by Yoshifusa, fathered the five regent houses; Nagara was posthumously made grand minister in 879.
zh: 藤原长良（802—856）是平安时代前期的公卿，属藤原北家，为左大臣藤原冬嗣的长子。他在仁明天皇为皇太子时便深得信任，曾任藏人所长官与卫府督，844年才拜参议，比弟弟良房晚了十年；854年升权中纳言，856年叙从二位，同年去世，终年五十五岁。他的女儿高子生下阳成天皇，三男基经出继良房，其后人分出五摄家；879年长良被追赠太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Nakamasa was an early to mid-Heian noble, the seventh son of Councillor Fujiwara no Yamakage of the Northern Fujiwara house. Under Emperor Daigo (r. 897–930) he served as a junior captain of the right palace guards, and under Emperor Suzaku (r. 930–946) as mayor of the eastern capital and senior assistant in the Board of Censors, ending at junior fourth rank upper; he also governed Settsu Province as a zuryō. Though never a minister, his daughter married the regent Fujiwara no Kaneie, making him maternal grandfather of Fujiwara no Michinaga and Higashi-Sanjōin, mother of Emperor Ichijō.
zh: 藤原中正是平安时代前期至中期的贵族，属藤原北家鱼名流（山荫流），为中纳言藤原山荫的第七子。他在醍醐朝（897—930年在位）任右近卫少将，朱雀朝（930—946年在位）历任左京大夫、弹正大弼，最终位至从四位上，还曾以受领身份担任摄津守。他虽未位极人臣，女儿时姬却嫁给关白藤原兼家，因此成为藤原道长与一条天皇生母东三条院藤原诠子的外祖父。

en: Fujiwara no Naomichi was an early Heian noble of the Northern House Uona line, son of Kii governor Fujiwara no Fusatsugu and a maternal uncle of Emperor Koko. In 843, as a captain of the Left Military Guards, he was sent to search the Heian-kyo and Naniwa mansions of Funya no Miyatamaro, suspected of treason, for weapons. He took junior fifth rank in 849 and thereafter held mainly provincial posts, including vice-governor of Sagami and governor of Mino, with capital interludes as director of the mint in 859 and lesser councilor and chamberlain in 861. He became governor of Bizen in 863.
zh: 藤原直道是平安时代前期的贵族，属藤原北家鱼名流，为纪伊守藤原总继之子，光孝天皇的外叔父。843年，文室宫田麻吕被控谋反而遭拘禁，时任左兵卫大尉的直道与左中弁良岑木莲等人奉命搜查宫田麻吕在平安京与难波的宅邸，搜寻谋反所用的武具。他849年叙从五位下，其后历任相模介、美浓守等地方官，又于859年任铸钱长官、861年任少纳言兼侍从，863年出任备前守。

en: Fujiwara no Naomichi was a Heian-period noble of the Hidesato line of the Northern Fujiwara. Genealogies name him as the son of Fujiwara no Munemichi and father of Fujiwara no Moroshige, ancestors of the Yuasa clan of Kii Province.
zh: 藤原直道是日本平安时代贵族，属藤原北家秀乡流。谱系载其为藤原宗道之子、藤原师重之父，是纪伊国汤浅氏的先祖。

en: Fujiwara no Naozumi is known only through the genealogies claimed by the Ōmura and Arima warrior houses of Hizen Province, which called him a grandson of the rebel Fujiwara no Sumitomo. Their tradition holds that in 994 he moved from Ōzu in Iyo Province to Ōmura in Sonogi District of Hizen and took that place name as his family name. Later scholarship identifies him instead with Taira no Naozumi, son of the Fujitsu manor steward Taira no Kiyozumi, said to have invented Sumitomo ancestry to erase his forebears' disgrace.
zh: 藤原直澄仅见于肥前国大村氏、有马氏两家武家自称的家谱：他们奉他为海贼藤原纯友之孙。相传他于994年从伊予国大洲迁往肥前国彼杵郡大村，并以地名为家名，大村氏由此而始。后世考证则认为，他其实是肥前藤津庄庄司平清澄之子平直澄，为洗刷先世污名才冒称纯友后裔。

en: Fujiwara no Naritoki (941–995) was a mid-Heian court noble, second son of Minister of the Left Fujiwara no Morotada. Ennobled in 958, he became head chamberlain in 967 and a councilor in 970. In 977 the dying regent Fujiwara no Kanemichi gave him the Right Imperial Guards captaincy, just stripped from his rival Kaneie. A close supporter of Regent Michitaka, Naritoki reached senior second rank as major counselor in 991. He died in the 995 smallpox epidemic, aged fifty-five, and was posthumously appointed minister of the right in 1012, when his daughter Seishi became Empress of Emperor Sanjō.
zh: 藤原济时（941—995）是平安时代中期的公卿，为左大臣藤原师尹次子。958年叙爵，967年任藏人头，970年任参议。977年，病危的关白藤原兼通将右近卫大将一职授予他，此职刚从兼通的政敌兼家手中被褫夺。济时是关白道隆的亲信，于991年官至正二位大纳言。995年天花大流行，他染病去世，享年55岁。1012年其女娍子成为三条天皇皇后，他被追赠右大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Nariyuki, or Ashikaga no Nariyuki, was a late Heian warrior in Shimotsuke Province. Genealogies describe him as the son of Fujiwara no Kaneyuki, who settled in Kōzuke, and the founder of the Fujiwara Ashikaga clan; his son Shigetoshi began the Ōgo branch.
zh: 藤原成行，又称足利成行，是下野国的平安时代后期武士。系图称他是定居上野国的藤原兼行之子，为藤姓足利氏的始祖；其子重俊开创了大胡氏支流。

en: Fujiwara no Norisuke (died 1079) was a noble of the mid-to-late Heian period, of the Kajuji line of the Northern Fujiwara, the son of Mino governor Fujiwara no Yoriaki. After serving in the Chamberlains' Office, he received junior fifth rank in 1039 and began a long career as a provincial governor, first in Kaga. He served as governor of Bitchū, Bingo, Ōmi and Bizen across the reigns of three emperors over more than twenty years, reaching senior fourth rank in 1068. He became a monk around 1077 and was known as the Bizen Novice, dying in 1079.
zh: 藤原宪辅（？—1079）是日本平安时代中期至后期的贵族，属藤原北家劝修寺流，为美浓守藤原赖明之子。他初任藏人式部丞，1039年经巡爵叙从五位下，随后转为受领，初任加贺守。此后历任备中守、备后守、近江守、备前守，在后冷泉、后三条、白河三朝连任受领二十余年，1068年叙正四位下。约1077年他出家，人称“备前入道”，1079年去世。

en: Fujiwara no Otokawa was an early Heian noble of the Southern Fujiwara, son of Dainagon Fujiwara no Otomo. In 813 he was granted junior fifth rank, lower grade, and appointed Ise suke, later serving as Echizen suke and Iga no kami.
zh: 藤原弟河（一作弟川）是平安初期贵族，出自藤原南家，为大纳言藤原雄友之子。813年叙从五位下，任伊势介，其后历任越前介、伊贺守。

en: Fujiwara no Otomaro was a Nara-period court noble of the Fujiwara Southern House, a son of Fujiwara no Muchimaro. After his father and uncles died in the smallpox epidemic of 737, he served in the war ministry. In 750 an oracle of the Usa Hachiman shrine brought him a sudden promotion to junior third rank and governor-general of Dazaifu. Removed in 752 and demoted to governor of Mimasaka in 757, possibly after a rift with his brother Nakamaro, he returned as war minister in 759 and died in 760, shortly after Empress Komyo. His son was Fujiwara no Korekimi.
zh: 藤原乙麻吕是奈良时代的公卿，出自藤原南家，为藤原武智麻吕之子。737年父亲与叔父们死于天花后，他在兵部任职。750年，因宇佐八幡宫的神谕，他被骤然提拔为从三位大宰帅。752年去职，757年被贬为美作守，可能因与兄长仲麻吕失和；759年他回朝任武部卿，760年在光明皇太后驾崩后不久去世。其子为藤原是公。

en: Fujiwara no Otomo (753–811) was a court noble of the Southern Fujiwara, second son of Udaijin Fujiwara no Korekimi. Starting as Mimasaka no kami in 783, he rose quickly, joining the council as Sangi in 790, becoming Chūnagon in 798 and reaching senior third rank in 804. In 806 he was made Dainagon, briefly heading the Great Council before Fujiwara no Uchimaro was promoted above him. In the wake of the 807 Prince Iyo incident he was exiled to Iyo Province. Pardoned in 810 during the Kusuko disturbance, he died in 811 aged 59 and was posthumously named Dainagon.
