zh: 藤原雄友（753—811）是奈良至平安初期的公卿，出自藤原南家，为右大臣藤原是公次子。783年任美作守，此后迅速升迁，790年任参议，位列公卿，798年任中纳言，804年升至正三位。806年任大纳言，一度位居太政官首班，不久藤原内麻吕被擢为右大臣，位居其上。807年伊予亲王之变后，他受牵连流放伊予国。810年药子之变期间获赦复位，811年去世，终年59岁，追赠大纳言。

en: Fujiwara no Otosada was an early Heian-period noble of the Northern Fujiwara, son of Fujiwara no Managa and grandson of Dainagon Fujiwara no Matate. His mother was a daughter of Saeki no Hisayoshimaru.
zh: 藤原弟贞是平安时代初期贵族，出自藤原北家，为藤原真永之子、大纳言藤原真楯之孙，其母为佐伯久良丸之女。

en: Fujiwara no Sadakata (873–932) was a noble and poet of the Northern Fujiwara house, second son of the naidaijin Takafuji and maternal uncle of Emperor Daigo. Named a palace page in 892, he rose through the guards, becoming a councillor in 909 and, leaping over six seniors, middle counsellor in 913. He became dainagon in 920 and minister of the right in 924, serving alongside Fujiwara no Tadahira, and reached junior second rank in 926. He died in 932 and was posthumously granted junior first rank, known as the Sanjō minister of the right.
zh: 藤原定方（873—932）是平安时代前期至中期的贵族、歌人，属藤原北家，为内大臣藤原高藤的次子、醍醐天皇的外叔父。他于892年任内舍人，之后历任近卫府武官，909年任参议，913年越过六名上位者升任从三位中纳言，920年任大纳言，924年升任右大臣，与藤原忠平并为左右大臣，926年叙从二位。他于932年去世，享年60岁，追赠从一位，因宅邸在三条而号三条右大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Sadatō was a noble of the mid-to-late Heian period, of the Yamakage line of the Northern Fujiwara, whose father was Fujiwara no Tamemori, governor of Echizen. After serving as a menial officer in the Chamberlains' Office, he was admitted to the audience of Crown Prince Atsunaga, the future Emperor Go-Suzaku, in 1020. In 1040, while Sadatō was governor of Iga, Sugano no Atsuyori, governor of Chikuzen, requested an exchange of posts; Sadatō may have become governor of Chikuzen. He ended his career at Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade, as governor of Yamato, taking Buddhist vows in 1081 while still in office.
zh: 藤原定任是日本平安时代中期至后期的贵族，属藤原北家山荫流，为越前守藤原为盛之子。他自藏人所杂色出仕，1020年获准升殿春宫敦良亲王，即后来的后朱雀天皇。1040年定任任伊贺守时，筑前守菅野敦赖请求交换官职，定任可能转任筑前守。其最终官位为从四位上大和守，1081年在大和守任内出家。

en: Fujiwara no Sadayori (995–1045) was a mid-Heian noble and poet of the Ononomiya Fujiwara line, eldest son of the poet Fujiwara no Kinto. After coming of age in 1007 he became head chamberlain in 1017, councillor in 1020, provisional middle counsellor in 1029, and reached senior second rank in 1042. Regent Yorimichi reprimanded him in 1019, and in 1030 he was caught cheating at a palace composition contest. Remembered as one of the Late Classical Thirty-Six Poets, he appears in the Ogura Hyakunin Isshu. He took vows in 1044 and died in 1045 aged fifty-one.
zh: 藤原定赖（995—1045）是平安时代中期公卿、歌人，出自藤原北家小野宫流，为歌人藤原公任长子。1007年元服后历任近卫府武官与弁官，1017年任藏人头，1020年任参议，1029年任权中纳言，1042年叙正二位。他的仕途起伏：1019年被摄政藤原赖通谴责，1030年又在清凉殿御前作文时作弊被揭穿。他是中古三十六歌仙之一，小仓百人一首以“权中纳言定赖”收录他。1044年他因病出家，1045年去世，享年51岁。

en: Fujiwara no Sanenari (975–1045) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Kan'in line of the Fujiwara Hokke, eldest son of Grand Minister Fujiwara no Kinsue. He became head chamberlain in 1004 and councillor in 1008, served in Empress Shoshi's household, became provisional middle counsellor in 1015, and took middle counsellor in 1023 and senior second rank in 1024. From 1033 he also headed the Dazaifu, but in 1038 he was dismissed after a retainer robbed Anraku-ji at Dazaifu. Restored to rank in 1040, he took vows and died in 1045 aged seventy-one.
zh: 藤原实成（975—1045）是平安时代中期公卿，出自藤原北家闲院流，为太政大臣藤原公季长子。他于1004年任藏人头，1008年任参议，又曾任中宫藤原彰子的中宫权亮，1015年升权中纳言，1023年任中纳言，1024年叙正二位。1033年起他兼任大宰权帅，1038年因郎从盗窃大宰府安乐寺财物受牵连，被解除中纳言与大宰权帅并除名，1040年恢复正二位本位，1045年出家后去世，享年71岁。

en: Fujiwara no Sanesue (1035–1092) was a court noble of the Kan'in branch of the Fujiwara Hokke, the second son of Provisional Middle Counsellor Fujiwara no Kinnari. His advancement was slow until his sister Shigeko married Crown Prince Takahito, who as Emperor Go-Sanjō made him head chamberlain in 1069 and councillor in 1072. As maternal uncle of Emperor Shirakawa he leapt over five senior councillors to become provisional middle counsellor in 1074, and reached major counsellor at senior second rank in 1083. He died in 1092. After his daughter Ishi bore Emperor Toba, he was posthumously named grand minister at senior first rank and became known as the Go-Kan'in posthumous grand minister.
zh: 藤原实季（1035—1092）是平安时代后期公卿，出自藤原北家闲院流，为权中纳言藤原公成的次子。他早年晋升缓慢，后因妹妹茂子成为皇太子尊仁亲王之妃而得到亲信；尊仁亲王即位为后三条天皇后，他于1069年任藏人头，1072年任参议。作为白河天皇的外伯父，他于1074年越过五位上级参议任权中纳言，1083年升正二位大纳言。他于1092年去世，后因女儿苡子生下鸟羽天皇，被追赠正一位太政大臣，人称后闲院赠太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Saneyori (900–970), known as Onomiya-dono, was the eldest son of the regent Fujiwara no Tadahira and a leading Heian statesman. He became udaijin in 944 and sadaijin in 947, and in 949 shared the duties of daijō-daijin with his brother Morosuke during their father's final illness. As head of the Fujiwara he upheld Emperor Murakami's Tenryaku-era government, and in 967 was named kampaku for Emperor Reizei, becoming sesshō, or regent, in 969. He died in 970 aged seventy; his Ononomiya line never kept the regency, which passed to Morosuke's descendants.
zh: 藤原实赖（900—970），人称小野宫殿，是摄政藤原忠平的长子，平安时代公卿。他944年任右大臣，947年升任左大臣；949年父亲忠平病重期间，与弟弟师辅共同承担太政大臣的政务。作为藤氏长者，他辅佐村上天皇的天历之治，967年冷泉天皇即位时出任关白，969年改任摄政。他于970年去世，享年70岁；其小野宫流未能久保摄关之位，后来摄政关白转入师辅的九条流子孙之手。

en: Fujiwara no Sueshige was a Nara-period noble of the Northern Fujiwara, third son of Sadaijin Fujiwara no Uona. In 777, when Emperor Kōnin visited his father's offices, he was raised three ranks to junior fifth rank, lower grade, later holding military posts and provincial offices such as Mino suke and Higo no kami. After Uona fell in 782, Sueshige was demoted to Tosa suke. Recalled in 783, he was briefly made Iyo no kami in 784 but again exiled to Hyūga. Pardoned once more, he became junior fifth rank, upper grade, and Mimasaka no kami in 790.
zh: 藤原末茂是奈良时代贵族，出自藤原北家，为左大臣藤原鱼名第三子。777年光仁天皇行幸其父官署时，他由从六位上连升三级，叙从五位下，其后历任武官和美浓介、肥后守等地方官。782年父亲鱼名失势，末茂受牵连被贬为土佐介；783年获准返京，784年一度出任伊予守，不久再贬日向介。再度获赦后，他于790年叙从五位上、任美作守。

en: Sudō no Sukefusa was a twelfth-century warrior of Nasu in Shimotsuke, placed by Nasu genealogies between his father Sukekiyo and son Munesuke in a line that later took the Nasu name and claimed descent from the Northern House of the Fujiwara.
zh: 须藤资房是12世纪下野国那须郡的武士，那须氏谱系把他列在父亲须藤资清与儿子须藤宗资之间；这一支后来改称那须氏，自称出自藤原北家。

en: Fujiwara no Sukeie was a warrior of the late Heian period, said to descend from the Fujiwara Hokke as a grandson of the poet Fujiwara no Nagaie, sixth son of Michinaga. He is credited with destroying a bandit called Iwatakemaru who had hidden on Mount Yamizo in Shirakawa district, Mutsu, after praying for victory at Miwa Shrine. For this exploit he received Nasu district in Shimotsuke province and settled there, calling himself Sudo Gon no Kami Sadanobu. Around 1125 he built Kanda Castle as his seat, and his descendants settled the land as the Nasu clan.
zh: 藤原资家是平安时代后期的武将，相传为藤原北家藤原道长的后裔、道长六子歌人藤原长家之孙。他征伐盘踞在陆奥国白河郡八沟山的贼人岩狱丸时，曾向三和神社祈愿获胜；讨贼之后，他因功受封下野国那须郡并前往定居，自称须藤权守贞信。约1125年，他修筑神田城作为居城，其后代世代土居于此，成为那须氏之祖。

en: Sudō no Sukekiyo was a warrior of the Nasu district in Shimotsuke Province in the late Heian period. The Nasu genealogies place him between his father Sukemitsu and his son Sukefusa. His house, then called Sudō, claimed Fujiwara descent and later took the name Nasu.
zh: 须藤资清是平安时代后期下野国那须郡的武士，那须氏谱系把他列在父亲须藤资满与儿子须藤资房之间。其家族当时称须藤氏，自称出自藤原北家，后来才改称那须氏。

en: Fujiwara no Sukemichi, also called Sudō no Sukemichi, was a late Heian warrior. Nasu clan genealogies list him as the son of Fujiwara no Sukeie, called Sudō Sadanobu, who settled in Nasu district of Shimotsuke Province, and the father of Sudō no Sukemitsu.
zh: 藤原资通，又称须藤资通，是平安时代后期的武将。那须氏系图将他列为定居下野国那须郡的藤原资家（号须藤权守贞信）之子，须藤资满之父。

en: Sudō no Sukemitsu was a warrior of the Nasu clan in Shimotsuke Province, the son of Sudō no Sukemichi and father of Sudō no Sukekiyo. In the Heiji Disturbance of 1160 he and his son followed Minamoto no Yoshitomo and were killed in the defeat.
zh: 须藤资满是下野国那须氏的武士，须藤资通之子、须藤资清之父。1160年平治之乱时，他与儿子资清一同追随源义朝，兵败战死。

en: Fujiwara no Sukemitsu, also called Nii Sukemitsu, was a fourth son of Fujiwara no Suketaka, the second head of the Sanuki Fujiwara in Sanuki Province, and founded the Nii warrior house. He fought in the Genpei War, distinguishing himself at the Battle of Mizushima in Bitchū in 1183 and joining Minamoto no Yoshitsune's force at the Battle of Yashima in 1185. For his service he received a letter of commendation from Minamoto no Yoritomo and was confirmed in his holdings in Aya District. His son Sukemura later took the name Kōzai after the Jōkyū War of 1221.
zh: 藤原资光，又称新居资光，是讃岐藤原氏第二代当主藤原资高的第四子，创立了新居氏。源平合战中，他于1183年在备中国水岛之战立下战功，1185年屋岛之战时加入源义经的阵营，因战功获源赖朝颁发感状，其在阿野郡（绫郡）的领地得到安堵。他的儿子资村在1221年承久之乱后改姓香西。

en: Fujiwara no Suketada (died 973) was a mid-Heian noble and waka poet of the Uonome Fujiwara, son of the Dewa governor Fujiwara no Tsurashige. He began as a sixth-rank imperial secretary in 945, served the retired Emperor Suzaku after 946, and later governed Settsu and Inaba. In 965 he was appointed senior assistant minister of Dazaifu in Kyushu, serving there until recalled in 970; he ended his career at junior fourth rank upper as head of the Audit Commissioners. One of his poems is included in the Shūi Wakashū, and his court notes, the Suketada shiki, survive in part.
zh: 藤原佐忠（?—973）是日本平安时代中期的贵族、和歌歌人，出身藤原北家鱼名流，为出羽守藤原连茂之子。他945年以六位藏人兼木工助出仕，946年朱雀天皇退位后继续侍奉朱雀院，又历任式部丞、肥后权守及摄津、因幡等国国司。965年他出任大宰大贰，赴九州任职，970年奉召还朝，最终官至从四位上勘解由长官。他有一首和歌收入《拾遗和歌集》，所著《佐忠私记》的一部分保存在前田家本《西宫记》的奥书中。

en: Fujiwara no Suketaka, second head of the Sanuki Fujiwara line and son of its founder Akitaka, took his estate's place name in the late Heian period to found the Hanyū clan in Sanuki Province. His sons also established the Ōno and Nii houses.
zh: 藤原资高是讃岐藤原氏第二代当主、始祖章隆之子。平安时代末期，他以领地的地名为苗字，在讃岐国创立羽床氏；诸子还分出大野氏与新居氏。

en: Fujiwara no Sumitomo (died 941) was a Heian-period noble of the northern Fujiwara house, a son of the Dazaifu official Fujiwara no Yoshinori. Posted as an assistant governor of Iyo Province, he was sent to suppress the pirates of the Seto Inland Sea, but became their leader instead. In 939 he rose in Iyo in concert with Taira no Masakado's eastern revolt, raiding provincial offices across the San'yō region and capturing Dazaifu in 941. Defeated at Hakata Bay by Ono no Yoshifuru and Minamoto no Tsunemoto, he was captured in Iyo and executed by Tachibana no Tōyasu.
zh: 藤原纯友（?—941）是日本平安时代的贵族，出自藤原北家，为太宰府官员藤原良范之子。他出任伊予国掾，起初奉命镇压濑户内海的海贼，后来却成为海贼首领。939年，他在伊予举兵，与关东平将门的叛乱遥相呼应，史称承平天庆之乱；叛军劫掠山阳道各国国衙，并于941年攻陷太宰府。朝廷派小野好古、源经基率军追讨，纯友在博多湾战败，逃回伊予后被捕，由橘远保处死。

en: Fujiwara no Tadahira (880–949) was a Heian-period court noble, the fourth son of Fujiwara no Mototsune. After his elder brother Tokihira died young in 909, he took charge of the government as head of the Fujiwara clan, becoming udaijin in 914 and sadaijin in 924. In 927 he completed the Engishiki, the compiled rites and regulations of the Engi era. When the infant Emperor Suzaku came to the throne in 930, Tadahira was appointed sesshō, or regent; he became daijō-daijin in 936 and kampaku in 941, and remained the leading court minister until his death.
zh: 藤原忠平（880—949）是日本平安时代公卿，藤原基经的第四子。909年兄长藤原时平早逝后，他以藤氏长者身份主持朝政，914年任右大臣，924年升任左大臣。927年，他主持完成《延喜式》，即延喜年间礼仪与法规的汇编。930年年幼的朱雀天皇即位，忠平被任命为摄政；936年任太政大臣，941年改任关白，终其一生都居于朝廷执政之位。

en: Fujiwara no Tadatoki was a late Heian courtier of the Koichijo Fujiwara line who held the post of junior assistant minister of justice. He was the father of the noble and poet Fujiwara no Morotsuna.
zh: 藤原尹时是平安时代后期小一条流藤原氏贵族，官至刑部少辅，为贵族歌人藤原师纲之父。

en: Fujiwara no Tadazane (1078–1162) was a regent of the late Heian period, the eldest son of the kampaku Fujiwara no Moromichi. On his father's sudden death in 1099 he inherited the regent house and became kampaku in 1105, but a quarrel with the retired Emperor Shirakawa cost him office in 1120, and he spent ten years confined at Uji. Restored after Shirakawa's death, he later favoured his son Yorinaga and in 1150 disowned the kampaku Tadamichi. On the losing side with the retired Emperor Sutoku and Yorinaga in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156, he was placed under confinement until his death.
zh: 藤原忠实（1078—1162）是平安时代后期的公卿，关白藤原师通的嫡男。1099年父亲暴卒后，他成为藤原摄关家的家督，1105年任关白；但1120年与白河上皇发生冲突而被停职，在宇治度过了十年幽禁岁月。白河上皇死后他重返政界，后来偏爱儿子赖长，于1150年与关白忠通断绝父子关系。1156年保元之乱中，他站在崇德上皇与赖长一方，战败后被幽禁，直至去世。

en: Fujiwara no Takafuji (838–900) was a court noble of the Northern Fujiwara house, grandson of the minister Fuyutsugu and second son of the low-ranking Yoshikado. His advancement was slow until his daughter Taneko married Emperor Uda and her son was named crown prince in 893. He reached junior third rank in 894, joined the senior nobility as a councillor in 895, and became dainagon in 899. In 900, as the dying maternal grandfather of Emperor Daigo, he was appointed to the revived office of naidaijin; he died two months later and was posthumously named grand minister of state.
zh: 藤原高藤（838—900）是平安时代前期公卿，属藤原北家，为左大臣藤原冬嗣之孙、内舍人藤原良门的次子。他早年升迁迟缓，直到女儿胤子嫁给宇多天皇、胤子所生的敦仁亲王于893年被立为太子后才平步青云，894年叙从三位，895年任参议，899年升任大纳言。900年，作为醍醐天皇的外祖父，他在病危时被任命为停废百余年的内大臣，两个月后去世，追赠正一位太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Takafusa (795–852) was an early Heian court noble of the Northern House of the Fujiwara, third son of Councillor Fujiwara no Fujitsugu. After serving in capital offices he took junior fifth rank in 827 and went to Mino as vice-governor, where firm yet flexible rule and his exposure of plots left the province free of bandits. He later governed Bingo, Higo and Echizen, but advanced only to junior fifth upper rank in 841 and senior fifth rank in 850. He died in 852 as governor of Echizen, aged fifty-eight.
zh: 藤原高房（795—852）是平安时代初期的贵族，属藤原北家鱼名流，为参议藤原藤嗣第三子。他先在京都官署任职，827年叙从五位下，出任美浓介，在任宽猛相济，屡发阴谋奸恶，国中盗贼绝迹。此后历任备后、肥后、越前等国国守，但升迁迟缓，直到841年才升叙从五位上，距上次受爵已过十四年，850年又升正五位下。852年他在越前守任上去世，终年五十八岁。

en: Fujiwara no Takaie (979–1044) was a mid-Heian noble of the Fujiwara Hokke, fourth son of Regent Fujiwara no Michitaka and brother of Empress Teishi. After his father died in 995 power passed to his uncle Michinaga, and in 996 Takaie and his brother Korechika were exiled for shooting arrows at Retired Emperor Kazan's party. Pardoned in 998, he regained middle counsellor in 1009. Seeking treatment for an eye disease, he obtained appointment as Dazai viceroy in 1014; in 1019 he commanded the defense of Hakata against the Jurchen Toi pirates, repelling them and receiving 259 captives returned by Goryeo. He died in 1044.
zh: 藤原隆家（979—1044）是平安时代中期公卿，出自藤原北家，为摄政藤原道隆第四子、皇后定子之弟。995年父亲去世后，政权落入叔父藤原道长之手；996年，他与兄长藤原伊周因向花山法皇一行射箭等罪名被流放，998年遇赦回京，1009年任中纳言。1014年他因眼疾赴任大宰权帅，1019年刀伊（女真）海盗袭扰对马、壹岐并进攻博多，他担任总指挥将其击退，并接收高丽送还的259名被俘日本人。1044年他去世。

en: Fujiwara no Takanaga was a late-Heian court noble and the third son of Minister of the Left Fujiwara no Yorinaga. He rose quickly through the Palace Guards, becoming a chamberlain in 1151, provisional middle captain of the Left in 1152, and rising to senior fourth rank in 1153. When his father was killed on Retired Emperor Sutoku's side in the 1156 Hōgen Disturbance, Takanaga was stripped of office and, on 3 August 1156, exiled to Izu Province. He never returned to the capital and died in exile; tradition holds that his grandson settled in Ōsumi and founded the Hishikari clan.
zh: 藤原隆长是平安时代末期的公卿，为左大臣藤原赖长的第三子，官至正四位下、左近卫权中将。他在近卫府升迁顺利：1151年任侍从，1152年任左近卫权中将，1153年升至正四位下。1156年保元之乱中，父亲随崇德上皇败死，隆长被解官，于同年8月3日流放伊豆国，终未返京，死于配所。相传其孙定居大隅国，成为菱刈氏之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Takasuke was an early Heian court noble of the Southern House of the Fujiwara, son of Fujiwara no Otokawa, governor of Iga. He received junior fifth rank lower grade in 833 and rose to junior fifth rank upper grade in 837, and he served as governor of Mutsu and provisional assistant commander of the Right Gate Guards. His great-grandson Fujiwara no Tamenori took the name Kudo Taifu and founded the Kudo warrior house, from which the Ito, Kikkawa, Nikaido and Sagara clans later branched.
zh: 藤原高扶是平安时代初期的贵族，属藤原南家，为伊贺守藤原弟河之子。833年叙从五位下，837年升叙从五位上，又曾任陆奥守与右卫门权佐。他的曾孙藤原为宪号工藤大夫，开创工藤氏，其后人又分出伊东、吉川、二阶堂、相良等氏族。

en: Fujiwara no Takatsune was a mid-Heian court noble and poet of the Uona branch of the Northern Fujiwara, the son of the Uchūben Fujiwara no Yoritō. He served as Tōgū no daishin, secretary to the crown prince Takahito, who became Emperor Go-Sanjō, and afterward held a string of provincial governorships, including Kai, Settsu and Mino. In 1072 he rose to senior fourth rank, lower grade. As an imperial anthology poet he contributed three poems to the Goshūi Wakashū and seven poems in all to the imperial anthologies. His son was the poet Fujiwara no Akisue.
zh: 藤原隆经是平安时代中期的贵族、歌人，属藤原北家鱼名流，为右中弁藤原赖任之子。他曾任皇太子尊仁亲王（即后来的后三条天皇）的春宫大进，之后历任甲斐守、摄津守、美浓守等国司，1072年（延久四年）升至正四位下。作为敕撰歌人，他有三首和歌收入《后拾遗和歌集》，此后各敕撰和歌集共收录其作七首。其子为歌人藤原显季。

en: Fujiwara no Tamemori (died c. 1029) was a mid-Heian noble of the Yamakage line of the Northern Fujiwara, son of the councillor Fujiwara no Yasuchika. In 1005 he presented two horses to Fujiwara no Michinaga. A former sixth-rank chamberlain, he reached junior fifth rank by 1011 and had governed Kaga Province before 1013. He spent many years without office until, in 1028, he was made governor of Echizen, where he lost his certificate of appointment. The court diary Shōyūki records him as dead by the leap second month of 1029. His son was Fujiwara no Sadatō.
zh: 藤原为盛（？—约1029）是平安时代中期的贵族，属藤原北家山荫流，参议藤原安亲之子。1005年，他曾向藤原道长进献两匹马。他由六位藏人出仕，1011年以前经巡爵叙从五位下，1013年之前曾任加贺守。此后他长期担任散位，直到1028年被任为越前守，却遗失了任符；《小右记》记载，到1029年闰二月时这位越前守已经去世。其子为藤原定任。

en: Fujiwara no Tamesuke (c. 920–986) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Kanjūji Fujiwara, eldest son of Fujiwara no Asayori and grandson of the udaijin Sadakata. He became a sixth-rank imperial secretary in 945, then served for years as governor of Buzen, Inaba, Owari, Tamba and Yamashiro, rising through his record of administration. Appointed sangi in 975, he joined the senior nobility and reached senior third rank in 984. In the first month of 986 he became provisional middle councillor and deputy viceroy of Dazaifu, but died only months later, aged sixty-seven; he was known as the Kanroji Chūnagon.
zh: 藤原为辅（约920—986）是日本平安时代中期公卿，出身藤原北家劝修寺流，为左兵卫督藤原朝赖的长子、右大臣藤原定方之孙。945年他以六位藏人出仕，此后历任丰前、因幡、尾张、丹波、山城等国国司，以治绩稳步升迁。975年他任参议，跻身公卿，984年升至正三位。986年正月，他出任权中纳言兼大宰权帅，同年八月二十七日去世，享年67岁，人称甘露寺中纳言。

en: Fujiwara no Tokiakira was a mid-Heian noble of the Northern Fujiwara's Uonama line, the son of Fujiwara no Suketada, governor of Settsu. Under Emperor En'yū he served as a sixth-rank royal secretary and assistant in the Ministry of Justice, then held provincial posts as deputy governor of Kōzuke and governor of Izumi. Around 991 he entered the household of Empress Fujiwara no Senshi, mother of Emperor Ichijō, as steward of the Higashi-Sanjō-in, while also holding a guards post. He later governed Yamato and Yamashiro, reached senior fifth rank lower, and died around 998.
zh: 藤原时明是平安时代中期的贵族，出自藤原北家鱼名流，为摄津守藤原佐忠之子。他在圆融朝任六位藏人兼刑部少丞，后历任上野介、和泉守等地方官。约991年，他出仕一条天皇生母藤原诠子，任东三条院别当，并兼任右卫门权佐。此后他又历任大和守、山城守，位至正五位下，约于998年去世。

en: Fujiwara no Tokinaga was an early Heian noble of the Northern House Uona line, son of Echizen governor Fujiwara no Takafusa. In 877, as vice-governor of Mino, he helped conduct the Yuki rites at Emperor Yozei's enthronement festival, and he later became junior assistant minister of military affairs. In 879 he officiated at the purification of the Saiō, Imperial Princess Shishi. Promoted to senior fifth rank in 886, he was named governor of Higo but failed to set out for his post; summoned to explain, he was demoted one rank later that year. He also served as vice-governor of Hitachi at an unknown date.
zh: 藤原时长是平安时代前期的贵族，属藤原北家鱼名流，为越前守藤原高房之子。877年阳成天皇举行大尝祭，他以美浓介身份担当悠纪行事；后历任从五位上、兵部少辅，879年在斋宫识子内亲王行禊时担任后次第司长官。886年正月叙正五位下，旋即被任命为肥后守，却到期不曾赴任，二月被召问缘由，五月遭降位一阶。他还曾任常陆介，时间不详。

en: Fujiwara no Tokitaka (born 947) was a noble of the Northern Fujiwara's Kajuji line, the second son of provisional middle counsellor Fujiwara no Tamesuke. After service as secretary and guard officer he took junior fifth rank in 974, and in 998 became fifth-rank secretary on the recommendation of Fujiwara no Yukinari while also holding a police commissioner post. As governor of Settsu he quarrelled with Sumiyoshi Shrine, whose clergy chased him through the capital in 1004. Passed over for the senior council despite long service as a major controller, he took the Harima governorship in 1012.
zh: 藤原说孝（947年生）是藤原北家劝修寺流贵族，权中纳言藤原为辅的次子。他历任藏人、卫门尉，974年叙从五位下，之后在弁官一职上稳步升迁：998年经藤原行成推举任五位藏人，并兼任检非违使佐。他兼任摄津守时与住吉神社发生争端，1004年曾被上京陈诉的神社神人在宫门追堵。他任大弁长达八年却始终未能升任参议，1012年自请出任播磨守，转任地方。

en: Fujiwara no Tomosuke was an early eleventh-century governor of Tōtōmi Province. The Ii clan legend makes him the adoptive father of a foundling, Ii Tomoyasu, who succeeded to the family in 1032 and founded the Ii clan.
zh: 藤原共资是11世纪初的远江国国司。相传井伊氏始祖井伊共保本为弃儿，被他收为养子；共保于1032年继承家业，开创井伊氏。

en: Fujiwara no Tootsune (835–888) was an early Heian noble of the Northern House, second son of Provisional Middle Counselor Fujiwara no Nagara and a maternal uncle of Emperor Yozei. After guarding the palace gates he took junior fifth rank in 866 and served his aunt Grand Empress Dowager Junshi. From 876 he held key posts under his nephew Emperor Yozei, as controller and guard captain, and in 882 became head of the imperial secretariat. He was made major controller of the right in 886 without joining the senior nobility, dying in 888 at junior fourth rank, aged fifty-four.
zh: 藤原远经（835—888）是平安时代前期的贵族，属藤原北家，为权中纳言藤原长良次男，阳成天皇的外伯父。他初任卫门武官，866年叙从五位下，不久出仕姑母太皇太后藤原顺子。876年外甥阳成天皇即位后，他历任右少弁、近卫少将等文武要职，882年任藏人头兼权左中弁。886年兼任右大弁，却始终未能升进公卿，888年去世，终年五十四岁，最终官位为从四位上右大弁。

en: Fujiwara no Toshihito (born c. 850) was an early Heian noble and warrior of the Northern Fujiwara house, son of the minister Tokinaga. After serving in the palace guards, he held successive Bandō posts: assistant governor of Kōzuke in 911 and Kazusa in 912, and later governor of Musashi. In 915 he crushed several thousand bandits who had seized tribute in Shimotsuke and was made general of the Chinjufu garrison, reaching junior fourth rank lower. His second son Nobumochi founded the Saitō clan, and Toshihito became a hero of medieval warrior tales, including the imo-gruel story in the Konjaku Monogatarishū.
zh: 藤原利仁（约850年生）是平安时代前期贵族、武将，属藤原北家鱼名流，为民部卿藤原时长之子。他历任左近将监等职，911年任上野介，912年转任上总介，后又担任武藏守等坂东国司。915年，他在下野国高藏山镇压数千名夺取贡调的群盗，因此出任镇守府将军，最终位至从四位下。其次子叙用是斋藤氏之祖；利仁本人也成为中世传说中的名武士，《今昔物语集》载有他的芋粥故事。

en: Fujiwara no Toshiyo is named in the Ii clan's genealogies as a son of the Heian court official Fujiwara no Yoshikado and an ancestor of the Ii warrior house of Tōtōmi, but he does not appear in earlier genealogies such as the Sonpi Bunmyaku.
zh: 藤原利世见于井伊氏家谱，被记为平安时代前期官人藤原良门之子、远江国井伊武士家的先祖，但《尊卑分脉》等更早的系谱中并无此人。

en: Fujiwara no Toyosawa was a noble of the early and middle Heian period, recorded in genealogies such as the Sonpi Bunmyaku as a son of Fujiwara no Fujinari, governor of Ise, and ancestor of the Hidesato branch of the Fujiwara. Appointed junior secretary of Shimotsuke, he served there as a suppression commissioner, an office his descendants including the Ota and Oyama houses inherited for generations. He rose to junior fifth rank in 840 and junior fourth rank in 858, and died in 887; his final recorded office was governor of Mutsu.
zh: 藤原丰泽是平安时代前期的贵族，《尊卑分脉》等谱系称他为藤原北家伊势守藤原藤成之子，是秀乡流藤原氏的祖先。他任下野少掾并担任押领使，负责平定地方盗乱，这一职务由太田氏、小山氏等子孙世代承袭。他于840年叙从五位下，858年升至从四位上，887年去世，最终官位为陆奥守。

en: Fujiwara no Tsuneie (1018–1068) was a noble of the mid-Heian period, of the Ononomiya line of the Northern Fujiwara, and the son of provisional middle counselor Fujiwara no Sadayori. After receiving junior fifth rank in 1031, he climbed the ladder of the Controllers' Office, becoming head of the Chamberlains' Office in 1048 and major controller of the right in 1050, promoted over his senior Taira no Sadachika. He joined the high nobility with junior third rank in 1056, became councillor in 1061, reached senior third rank in 1063, and was appointed provisional middle counselor in 1065. He died in 1068 aged fifty-one.
zh: 藤原经家（1018—1068）是日本平安时代中期的公卿，属藤原北家小野宫流，为权中纳言藤原定赖之子。1031年叙从五位下，此后在弁官局历任右少弁、右中弁等职，1048年任藏人头，1050年越过资深的平定亲升任右大弁。1056年叙从三位，跻身公卿；1061年任参议，1063年进正三位，1065年升任权中纳言。1068年去世，享年51岁。

en: Fujiwara no Tsurashige was a noble of the early to mid-Heian period, from the Uona branch of the Northern Fujiwara house and a son of Fujiwara no Naomichi, governor of Bizen. He served as governor of Dewa in the far north and governor of Tajima, and held junior fifth rank lower. His descendant, the noble and poet Fujiwara no Akisue, born in 1055, founded the family's Zenshōji line.
zh: 藤原连茂是平安时代初期至中期的贵族，属藤原北家鱼名流，为备前守藤原直道之子。他曾出任北方的出羽守和但马守，位阶为从五位下。其后裔、贵族与歌人藤原显季（1055年生）开创了藤原氏的善胜寺流。

en: Fujiwara no Uchimaro (756–812) was a Northern Fujiwara noble, third son of Dainagon Fujiwara no Matate, and served Emperors Kanmu, Heizei and Saga. He became Sangi in 794 soon after the move to Heian-kyō, Chūnagon in 798, and in 799 oversaw construction of the new capital. In 806 he was made Udaijin, head of the council, reaching junior second rank in 809. In the 810 Kusuko Incident he backed Emperor Saga alongside Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. He died in 812 aged 57 and was posthumously promoted to Daijō-daijin. His many sons, above all Fuyutsugu, laid the foundation of Northern Fujiwara power.
zh: 藤原内麻吕（756—812）是奈良至平安初期公卿，出自藤原北家，为大纳言藤原真楯第三子，历仕桓武、平城、嵯峨三朝。794年迁都平安京后不久任参议，798年任中纳言，799年负责营建新京。806年任右大臣，成为太政官首班，809年叙从二位。810年药子之变中，他与坂上田村麻吕协同支持嵯峨天皇，稳固了朝廷。812年去世，终年57岁，死后追赠太政大臣。其子众多，尤以冬嗣为重，奠定了藤原北家日后繁盛的基础。

en: Fujiwara no Uona (721–783) was a court noble of the Fujiwara Northern House, the fifth son of Fujiwara no Fusasaki. He sided with retired Empress Kōken in Nakamaro's rebellion of 764, became councillor in 768, and in 770 helped enthrone Emperor Kōnin and remove the monk Dōkyō. Rising to great councillor and then inner minister, he became left minister and head of the Dajōkan under Emperor Kanmu in 781. In 782 he was suddenly dismissed and assigned to Dazaifu, while his sons were also demoted. Recalled in 783, he died soon after aged sixty-three and was posthumously restored as left minister.
zh: 藤原鱼名（721—783）是奈良时代的公卿，出自藤原北家，为藤原房前的第五子。764年仲麻吕之乱时他站在孝谦上皇一边，768年任参议，770年参与拥立光仁天皇、排除僧人道镜。他历任大纳言、内大臣，781年在桓武天皇朝任左大臣，成为太政官首班。782年他突然被罢官，贬任大宰帅，诸子也遭贬；783年获召还，不久去世，享年63岁，死后恢复左大臣官位。

en: Fujiwara no Washitori (born c. 750) was a late-Nara noble of the Fujiwara Northern House, a son of the left minister Fujiwara no Uona. Beginning in 771 he served in Ise Province, rising from deputy to governor by 774 and to junior fifth rank, upper grade, in 775. Called to the capital, he directed palace construction and in 778 became senior assistant minister of central affairs, concurrently governor of Kōzuke in 779. His daughter Kouso became a consort of Emperor Kanmu and mother of Prince Manda, and his son Fujiwara no Fujitsugu rose to councillor.
zh: 藤原鹫取（约750年生）是奈良时代后期的贵族，出自藤原北家，为左大臣藤原鱼名之子。771年起他在伊势国任职，774年已由次官升任伊势守，775年叙从五位上。他后来调回京城，主持宫室营造，778年任中务大辅，779年兼任上野守。其女小屎成为桓武天皇的夫人，生下万多亲王；其子藤原藤嗣后来官至参议。

en: Fujiwara no Yamakage (824–888) was an early Heian court noble, third son of Echizen governor Fujiwara no Takafusa. He entered the crown prince's service in 858 and, as a trusted aide of Emperor Seiwa, combined guard and secretariat posts with provincial offices in Bingo, Iyo and Mino. His promotion stalled for a decade, then quickened after Fujiwara no Yoshifusa's death in 872: he became head of the secretariat in 875, a councillor in 879, and under Emperor Koko rose in 886 to middle counselor of junior third rank, concurrently minister of popular affairs. He died in 888, aged sixty-five.
zh: 藤原山荫（824—888）是平安时代前期的公卿，为越前守藤原高房第三子。858年入东宫侍奉皇太子惟仁亲王，清和天皇即位后作为天皇侧近，历任藏人、近卫武官，同时兼任备后权介、伊予介、美浓守等地方官。他的升迁曾停滞近十年，872年藤原良房死后突然加速，875年任藏人头，879年拜参议，又于光孝朝886年升至从三位中纳言，兼行民部卿。888年去世，终年六十五岁。

en: Fujiwara no Yasuchika (922–996) was a noble of the Yamakage branch of the Northern Fujiwara, the third son of Fujiwara no Nakamasa, governor of Settsu, and a great-uncle of Emperor Ichijō. After long service as a royal secretary and as governor of Settsu, Yamato, Sagami and Ise, he was promoted after the Kanna Disturbance of 986, when his younger sister's grandson ascended the throne and his brother-in-law Fujiwara no Kaneie became regent. Named senior councillor in 987, he reached senior third rank in 991 and died in 996 at the age of seventy-five.
zh: 藤原安亲（922—996）是藤原北家山荫流公卿，摄津守藤原中正的第三子，也是一条天皇的大叔父。他长期担任藏人及摄津、大和、相模、伊势等地国司，986年宽和之变后，因外甥孙即位、妹夫藤原兼家出任摄政而获得提拔。他于987年任参议，位列公卿，991年升至正三位，996年去世，享年75岁。

en: Fujiwara no Yoriaki (died 1027) was a mid-Heian noble of the Kanjuji line of the Fujiwara Hokke, son of Harima governor Fujiwara no Tokitaka. A minor court official under Emperor Ichijo, he was abducted during a quarrel with the retinue of Fujiwara no Shigetada in 1000, and in 1004 won his junior fifth rank only after petitioning Grand Minister Kinsue, who had blocked it. In 1006 he presented two thousand volumes of texts to Fujiwara no Michinaga. He later served Grand Empress Shoshi as a senior secretary, became Mino governor in 1025, and died in office in 1027.
zh: 藤原赖明（生年不详，卒于1027年）是平安时代中期贵族，出自藤原北家劝修寺流，为播磨守藤原说孝之子。他在一条朝担任低级官职，1000年与藤原重尹随从争执时遭到绑架；1004年内大臣藤原公季拒绝为他叙位，他上书陈情后才叙从五位下。1006年他向左大臣藤原道长献上文书两千卷，后任太皇太后藤原彰子的太皇太后宫大进，1025年任美浓守，1027年在任上去世。

en: Fujiwara no Yorimichi (992–1074), eldest son of Fujiwara no Michinaga, dominated mid-Heian court politics. He became regent for Emperor Go-Ichijo in 1017 at twenty-six, the youngest sessho ever, and as regent or kampaku led the government for some fifty years under three emperors, becoming grand minister in 1061. His regency faced the Toi raid of 1019 and the Earlier Nine Years' War. He made his Uji villa into Byodo-in and its Phoenix Hall, completed in 1053. After Emperor Go-Sanjo, with no Fujiwara mother, took the throne in 1068, he retired, took vows in 1072, and died in 1074.
zh: 藤原赖通（992—1074）是平安时代中期至后期的公卿、歌人，为摄政太政大臣藤原道长的长子。他于1017年以26岁接替父亲担任后一条天皇的摄政，是史上最年轻的摄政，此后以摄政、关白身份在三位天皇治下主政约五十年，1061年任太政大臣。任内经历1019年刀伊入寇与前九年之役；他将宇治别墅改建为平等院，凤凰堂于1053年落成。1068年母亲并非藤原氏出身的后三条天皇即位，他退居宇治，1072年出家，1074年去世，享年83岁。

en: Fujiwara no Yorimoto was a late Kamakura court noble of the Koichijo Fujiwara line who rose to junior third rank and was the father of Anekoji Takamoto.
zh: 藤原赖基是镰仓后期小一条流藤原氏公卿，官至从三位，是姊小路高基之父。

en: Fujiwara no Yorinaga (1120–1156), favourite son of the regent Fujiwara no Tadazane, was the most formidable court noble of his day. A brilliant Confucian scholar, he became Minister of the Left in 1150 and was dubbed the Aku Safu, the Wicked Minister of the Left, for his rigid defence of the Fujiwara regency against the cloistered-court faction. After Emperor Konoe died in 1155 he lost the succession struggle, and in July 1156 he joined Retired Emperor Sutoku in the Hōgen Disturbance. Wounded when Sutoku's stronghold was stormed, he died on 1 August 1156.
zh: 藤原赖长（1120—1156）是摄政藤原忠实的爱子，也是当时最有权势的公卿。他精通儒学，1150年出任左大臣，因强硬维护摄关政治、对抗院政势力，被政敌称为“恶左府”。1155年近卫天皇去世后，他在皇位之争中失势；1156年7月，他追随崇德上皇发起保元之乱，据守的据点被攻破时中箭负伤，于8月1日死去。

en: Fujiwara no Yoritada (924–989) was the second son of the regent Fujiwara no Saneyori and head of the Ononomiya lineage. After long service in the imperial guards and Council of State, he became minister of the right in 971 and minister of the left in 977. Later that year the dying kampaku Kanemichi made Yoritada his successor. His daughter Junshi was named empress in 982 but bore no prince, weakening his position against Fujiwara no Kaneie. When Kaneie made the young Ichijō emperor in the Kanna Disturbance of 986, Yoritada resigned as kampaku and died in 989.
zh: 藤原赖忠（924—989）是摄政藤原实赖的次子，为小野宫流的当主。他历任近卫府与太政官官职，971年任右大臣，977年任左大臣；同年临终的关白兼通将关白之位传给他。其女遵子于982年立为中宫，却未诞下皇子，使他在与藤原兼家的较量中处于下风。986年宽和之变中兼家拥立年幼的一条天皇，赖忠遂辞去关白，989年去世。

en: Fujiwara no Yoritō (died 1030) was a mid-Heian noble, the son of Fujiwara no Tokiakira. After beginning as a literature student he served as fifth-rank chamberlain and imperial diarist, then as a police magistrate and an officer of the empress's household under Empress Kenshi, reaching junior fifth rank, upper grade, in 1013. Around 1017 he was made governor of Tamba. In 1019 its peasants protested his abuses at the Yōmeimon gate, and he sent mounted soldiers to pursue them, drawing a reprimand from Fujiwara no Michinaga and his son Yorimichi. He governed Mino from 1021 to 1025 and was named middle controller of the right in 1029. He died in the seventh month of 1030.
zh: 藤原赖任（？—1030）是平安时代中期的贵族，藤原时明之子。他初为文章生，后任五位藏人、内记，又任检非违使右卫门权佐，并以中宫权大进身份侍奉中宫藤原妍子，1013年叙从五位上。约1017年他出任丹波守，1019年丹波百姓到阳明门申诉他的苛政，他却派骑兵追捕，因此受到藤原道长、赖通父子斥责。1021—1025年他任美浓守，1029年由散位直任右中弁，1030年七月去世。

en: Fujiwara no Yoriyuki was an eleventh-century warrior of the Hidesato line of the Northern Fujiwara, son of defense commander Fujiwara no Kanemitsu. Medieval genealogies name his sons Kaneyuki and Yukitaka as ancestors of the Shimotsuke warrior houses of Yūki and Oyama.
zh: 藤原赖行是11世纪的武将，属藤原北家秀乡流，为镇守府将军藤原兼光之子。中世系图载其子兼行、行隆（太田行隆）为下野国结城氏、小山氏等武家的先祖。

en: Genealogical tradition names Fujiwara no Yoshiharu as a son of Fujiwara no Tomoyoshi, father of Yoshimune and head of the imperial archives office.
zh: 据系谱记载，藤原良春是藤原共良之子、良宗之父，曾任藏人头。

en: Fujiwara no Yoshikado was an early Heian courtier of the Northern Fujiwara, the sixth son of Sadaijin Fujiwara no Fuyutsugu. Unlike his brothers he never rose above senior sixth rank, serving as an Udoneri, a palace attendant, and he died young soon after his sons Toshimoto and Takafuji were born. The Konjaku Monogatari recounts that Takafuji was left fatherless as a child; Takafuji only received junior fifth rank in 868. Undistinguished in life, Yoshikado was ancestor of the Kajuji lineage, and Murasaki Shikibu descended from his son Toshimoto.
zh: 藤原良门是平安时代前期官人，出自藤原北家，为左大臣藤原冬嗣第六子。他是诸兄弟中唯一未能升至五位者，官位仅止正六位上内舍人，在生下利基、高藤二子后不久即早逝；《今昔物语集》记载高藤幼年丧父，高藤也迟至868年才叙从五位下。良门本人仕途平平，其后代却形成劝修寺流等藤原北家名门，紫式部即出自其子利基一支。

en: Fujiwara no Yoshinobu (995–1065) was a mid-Heian court noble and poet, the fourth son of Regent Fujiwara no Michinaga. He became provisional middle counsellor in 1017 and provisional major counsellor at senior second rank in 1021. In 1037 he became guardian of Prince Takahito, future Emperor Go-Sanjō, and in 1045 secured the dying Emperor Go-Suzaku's testament naming Takahito heir. For twenty years he was the prince's lone court supporter and married his adopted daughter Moshi to him. He died in 1065, aged seventy-one, before Takahito's accession, and in 1073 was posthumously made grand minister of senior first rank.
zh: 藤原能信（995—1065）是平安时代中期的公卿、歌人，摄政藤原道长的第四子。他升迁神速，1017年未经参议即任权中纳言，1021年升正二位权大纳言。1037年，他成为尊仁亲王（日后的后三条天皇）的监护人，1045年又从病危的后朱雀天皇处取得立尊仁为皇太弟的遗诏。此后二十年间，身为春宫大夫的能信是尊仁在朝中唯一的依靠，并将养女茂子嫁给他。1065年能信去世，享年71岁，未能见到尊仁即位；1073年被追赠正一位太政大臣。

en: Fujiwara no Yoshinori was an early Heian noble of the Northern Fujiwara house, son of the senior court official Fujiwara no Tōtsune. He served Empress Dowager Takako as a junior secretary in her household and received junior fifth rank lower in 882. After a posting as assistant governor of Suō, he returned to the capital in 885 as an imperial chamberlain, later serving as junior assistant at the Dazaifu and governor of Chikuzen in Kyushu. He is remembered as the father of Fujiwara no Sumitomo, who led the Seto Inland Sea pirate revolt of 939.
zh: 藤原良范是平安时代前期贵族，属藤原北家，为右大弁藤原远经之子。他在阳成朝以皇太后宫少进身份侍奉皇太后藤原高子，于882年叙从五位下；其后转任周防介，885年回京任侍从，后来再任大宰少贰、筑前守，赴九州任职。他最为人知的是作为藤原纯友之父——纯友于939年发动了濑户内海的海贼叛乱。

en: Fujiwara no Yoshitaka (954–974) was a mid-Heian noble and waka poet, the third son of the regent Fujiwara no Koretada. He served as captain of the right inner palace guards and was counted among the Late Classical Thirty-Six Poetry Immortals; one of his poems appears in the Ogura Hyakunin Isshu, and his private collection is the Yoshitaka-shū. When Koretada died in 972 he considered taking Buddhist vows, but stayed for his newborn son, the future calligrapher Fujiwara no Yukinari. In 974 he died of smallpox on the same day as his elder brother Kyoken, aged about twenty.
zh: 藤原义孝（954—974）是平安时代中期的公卿与歌人，摄政太政大臣藤原伊尹的第三子，官至右近卫少将，名列中古三十六歌仙；其和歌一首入选《小仓百人一首》，家集为《义孝集》。972年父亲伊尹去世时他曾想出家，却因不舍当年出生的儿子、后来的书法大家藤原行成而留在俗世。974年，他染上当时流行的天花，与兄长举贤同日去世，年仅约二十岁。

en: Fujiwara no Yukinari (972–1028) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Fujiwara Hokke, the eldest son of Minor Captain Fujiwara no Yoshitaka. Orphaned in childhood, in 995 he was made head chamberlain to Emperor Ichijo on the recommendation of Minamoto no Toshikata, and he later rose to provisional major counsellor at senior second rank, counted among the Four Counsellors of the Kanko era. With Ono no Michikaze and Fujiwara no Sukemasa he was one of the Sanseki, the three greatest Heian calligraphers; his style was called Gonseki, and he founded the Sesonji school of calligraphy.
zh: 藤原行成（972—1028）是平安时代中期公卿，出自藤原北家，为右少将藤原义孝长子，幼年丧父。995年，他经源俊贤推举任一条天皇藏人头，后官至正二位权大纳言，为“宽弘四纳言”之一。他与小野道风、藤原佐理并称“三迹”，书风被称为“权迹”，并开创书法世尊寺流，为世尊寺家之祖。

en: Emperor Fushimi (1265–1317), the 92nd emperor of Japan, was a son of Emperor Go-Fukakusa and head of the Jimyōin-tō line. Through his father's lobbying he became crown prince ahead of the Daikakuji-tō, and in 1287 succeeded his cousin Emperor Go-Uda, taking direct charge after Go-Fukakusa withdrew in 1290. Naming his own son heir in 1289 deepened the rival line's hostility, and he survived an assassination attempt in 1290 before abdicating in 1298 to rule as cloistered emperor. In 1308 the shogunate backed his fourth son's enthronement as Emperor Hanazono. He took Buddhist vows in 1313 and died in 1317.
zh: 伏见天皇（1265—1317）是日本第92代天皇，后深草天皇之子，持明院统的首领。经父亲奔走，他压过大觉寺统一脉被立为皇太子，1287年接替堂弟后宇多天皇即位，并于1290年后深草上皇停止院政后亲理政务。1289年他立自己的儿子为嗣，加深了大觉寺统的敌意，1290年又躲过一次刺杀，1298年退位实行院政。1308年，在幕府支持下，他的第四子即位为花园天皇。1313年他出家，1317年去世。

en: Empress Genmei (660–721), Japan's fourth reigning empress, was a daughter of Emperor Tenji, consort of Crown Prince Kusakabe and mother of Emperor Monmu. When Monmu died in 707 she took the throne in trust for her young grandson Shōmu. Copper deposits were reported in Musashi in 707; the discovery gave the Wadō era its name in 708, when a copper sample was presented at court and a mint established. In 710 she founded the new capital Heijō-kyō, now Nara, opening the Nara period. Under her the Kojiki was completed in 712 and the provincial Fudoki gazetteers begun in 713. She abdicated in 715 for her daughter Empress Genshō and died in 721.
zh: 元明天皇（660—721）是日本第四位女帝，天智天皇之女、草壁皇太子之妃、文武天皇之母。707年文武天皇去世，她为年幼的孙子首皇子（后来的圣武天皇）代管皇位而即位。707年武藏国报告发现铜矿；708年朝廷因此改元“和铜”，铜样被呈献宫廷，铸币所也随之设立。710年她营建新都平城京（今奈良），开创奈良时代。在她治下，《古事记》于712年成书，713年又下令编纂各地《风土记》。715年她让位于女儿元正天皇，721年去世。

en: Empress Genshō (680–748), the 44th monarch of Japan, reigned from 715 to 724. A daughter of Crown Prince Kusakabe and Empress Genmei, she took the throne when her mother abdicated, the only empress regnant in Japanese history to succeed another reigning empress, and ruled as a placeholder for her young nephew Prince Obito. During her reign the Nihon Shoki chronicle was completed in 720, and the Three-Generations Land Act was issued in 723 to encourage the opening of new fields. In 724 she abdicated in Obito's favor; he ruled as Emperor Shōmu. Genshō never married and died in 748.
zh: 元正天皇（680—748）是日本第44代天皇，715年至724年在位。她是草壁皇子与元明天皇之女，因母亲禅让而即位，是日本历史上唯一一位由女天皇传位给女天皇的君主，代年幼的侄子首亲王执掌皇位。在位期间，《日本书纪》于720年修成，723年颁布三世一身法，鼓励开垦新田。724年，她让位于首亲王，即圣武天皇。元正终身未婚，于748年去世。

en: Emperor Go-Daigo (1288–1339), personal name Takaharu, was the second son of Emperor Go-Uda of the Daikakuji line and ascended the throne in 1318. Direct rule under Emperor Daigo in the Engi era was his ideal, and he even chose his posthumous name in life to share it. He plotted against the Kamakura shogunate, which had directed his appointment as crown prince; after the Genkō Incident of 1331 he was exiled to the Oki Islands, but escaped in 1333 and, with Ashikaga Takauji and Nitta Yoshisada, overthrew the Hōjō regents and launched the Kenmu Restoration. Disputes over land and rewards and the exclusion of samurai from government bred discontent. When Takauji turned against him in 1336, Go-Daigo surrendered the regalia, but in January 1337 slipped out of Kyoto, declaring those regalia counterfeit, and set up the Southern Court at Yoshino, facing Takauji's Northern Court. He died there in 1339.
zh: 后醍醐天皇（1288—1339）名尊治，是大觉寺统后宇多天皇的第二子，1318年即位。他以醍醐天皇延喜年间的亲政为理想，甚至生前就自定谥号与之相同。他曾由镰仓幕府主导立为皇太子，却密谋推翻幕府；1331年元弘之变败露后被流放至隐岐岛，1333年逃脱，在足利尊氏与新田义贞的协助下推翻北条氏执权政治，随即推行建武新政。土地和封赏纠纷以及武士被排除在政权之外，使人们心生不满。1336年足利尊氏反叛，后醍醐天皇交出了神器，1337年1月却潜出京都，称交出的神器是赝品，在吉野建立南朝朝廷，与尊氏拥立的北朝对峙，1339年在吉野去世。

en: Emperor Go-Fukakusa (1243–1304), the 89th emperor of Japan, ascended in 1246 at two years old when his father Emperor Go-Saga abdicated and kept power as cloistered emperor. In 1259 Go-Saga forced him to step down in favour of his younger brother Emperor Kameyama. His line recovered when shogunate negotiations made his son Hirohito crown prince; in 1287 Hirohito became Emperor Fushimi and Go-Fukakusa ruled as cloistered emperor until taking Buddhist vows in 1290. His descendants formed the Jimyōin-tō line, and another son, Hisaaki, became the eighth Kamakura shōgun.
zh: 后深草天皇（1243—1304）是日本第89代天皇。1246年父亲后嵯峨天皇退位，年仅两岁的久仁亲王登基，由后嵯峨上皇实行院政。1259年，后嵯峨上皇迫使他让位给弟弟龟山天皇。后来经与幕府交涉，他的儿子熙仁被立为皇太子，1287年即位为伏见天皇，他也重开院政，直到1290年出家。他的后裔形成持明院统，另一子久明亲王则出任第八代镰仓将军。

en: Emperor Go-Fushimi (1288–1336), the 93rd emperor of Japan, was the eldest son of Emperor Fushimi and a Jimyōin-tō prince. Named crown prince in 1289, he ascended in 1298 when his father abdicated, but in 1301 the rival Daikakuji-tō drove him from the throne for Emperor Go-Nijō. He acted as cloistered emperor for his younger brother Emperor Hanazono from 1313 to 1318, when the shogunate sponsored a short-lived plan to alternate the throne between the two lines. He petitioned Kamo Shrine for his son's elevation; in 1331 Kazuhito became Emperor Kōgon, first of the Ashikaga-backed Northern Court emperors.
zh: 后伏见天皇（1288—1336）是日本第93代天皇，伏见天皇长子，持明院统亲王。1289年被立为皇太子，1298年因父亲退位而登基，1301年被对立的大觉寺统逼迫退位，让位于后二条天皇。1313至1318年，他为弟弟花园天皇主持院政，其间幕府促成了两统轮流继位的短命约定。他曾向贺茂神社祈愿儿子继位；1331年，量仁即位为光严天皇，是足利氏支持的初代北朝天皇。

en: Emperor Go-Horikawa (1212–1234), the 86th emperor of Japan, was placed on the Chrysanthemum Throne in 1221 after the Jōkyū Incident, when the Kamakura shogunate crushed Retired Emperor Go-Toba's bid for power and barred his line from the succession. A grandson of Emperor Takakura aged only ten, he replaced the deposed Emperor Chūkyō while his father Imperial Prince Morisada directed the court as cloistered emperor Go-Takakura-in. In 1232 he abdicated for his infant son Emperor Shijō and ruled as retired emperor until his death two years later.
zh: 后堀河天皇（1212—1234）是日本第86代天皇。1221年承久之乱爆发，后鸟羽上皇倒幕失败，镰仓幕府将其一脉排除出皇位继承；身为高仓天皇之孙、年仅十岁的茂仁亲王取代被废的仲恭天皇登基，其父守贞亲王以后高仓院的身份主持院政。1232年，他让位给襁褓中的儿子四条天皇，以上皇身份理政，两年后去世。

en: Emperor Go-Ichijō (1008–1036), personal name Atsuhira, was the 68th emperor of Japan. The second son of Emperor Ichijō, his mother was Fujiwara no Shōshi, daughter of Fujiwara no Michinaga; he was only eight in 1016 when Emperor Sanjō abdicated in his favour. Real power rested first with Michinaga and then with his son Yorimichi, who ruled as sesshō regent. He married Michinaga's daughter Ishi and had two daughters, later consorts of Emperors Go-Reizei and Go-Sanjō, but no son. On his death in 1036 at age 27 the throne passed to his younger brother, who became Emperor Go-Suzaku.
zh: 后一条天皇（1008—1036），名敦成，日本第68代天皇。他是一条天皇的次子，母亲是藤原道长之女藤原彰子，1016年三条天皇退位时年仅8岁便登基。在位期间，实权先后由任摄政的藤原道长、赖通父子掌握。他娶道长之女威子为中宫，仅生有两位内亲王，后来分别成为后冷泉、后三条天皇的中宫，终无皇子。1036年他以27岁去世，皇位由弟弟敦良亲王继承，即后朱雀天皇。

en: Emperor Go-Murakami (1328–1368), personal name Noriyoshi, was a son of Emperor Go-Daigo and the second sovereign of the Southern Court. Named crown prince in 1338, he succeeded his father at Yoshino in 1339 and spent his reign moving between temporary palaces as the Nanboku-chō war dragged on. In 1348 he fled Yoshino before Kō no Moronao's attack; in 1352 Southern Court forces briefly seized Kyōto and carried off three retired Northern emperors, only to lose the capital within weeks. A second brief occupation in 1361 also failed, and he died at Sumiyoshi in 1368 with his cause weakening.
zh: 后村上天皇（1328—1368）名义良，是后醍醐天皇之子、南朝第二代天皇。他于1338年被立为皇太子，1339年在吉野继承父位，在位期间因南北朝战乱辗转于多处临时行宫。1348年高师直进攻吉野，他被迫出逃；1352年南朝军队一度攻入京都，裹挟三位北朝上皇退走，但不出二十天便再失京都。1361年南朝再次短暂占领京都，仍告失败。1368年他在住吉去世，南朝势力已日趋衰微。

en: Emperor Go-Nijō (1285–1308), the 94th emperor of Japan, was the eldest son of Emperor Go-Uda, head of the Daikakuji-tō line. In 1298 he was made crown prince to the Jimyōin-tō Emperor Go-Fushimi, and in 1301, after the Kamakura shogunate pressed the court to rotate the throne, Go-Fushimi abdicated and Go-Nijō succeeded with Go-Uda ruling as cloistered emperor, an elevation his grandfather Emperor Kameyama had secured by lobbying Kamakura. Amid the continuing rivalry between the two imperial lines, he died of illness in 1308 at Nijō-Takakura Palace after a seven-year reign.
zh: 后二条天皇（1285—1308）是日本第94代天皇，后宇多天皇的长子，属大觉寺统。1298年，他被立为持明院统后伏见天皇的皇太子；1301年，镰仓幕府要求朝廷两统交替，后伏见天皇退位，邦治亲王继位，由后宇多上皇实行院政，祖父龟山上皇曾为此向幕府大力奔走。在两统围绕皇位持续对立之际，他于1308年在二条高仓宫病逝，在位七年。

en: Emperor Go-Reizei (1025–1068), personal name Chikahito, was the 70th emperor of Japan, the eldest son of Emperor Go-Suzaku and Fujiwara no Yoshiko. He succeeded on his father's abdication in 1045 and reigned 23 years, with Fujiwara no Yorimichi and later Norimichi holding the kampaku regency. In 1051 the Abe clan rose in the north, beginning the Zenkunen War; the court sent Minamoto no Yoriyoshi to Mutsu as chinjufu shōgun, and the Abe were crushed by 1062. Go-Reizei left no children at his death in 1068, so the throne went to his half-brother, Emperor Go-Sanjō.
zh: 后冷泉天皇（1025—1068），名亲仁，日本第70代天皇，后朱雀天皇与藤原道长之女嬉子所生的长子。1045年父亲退位后他随即登基，在位23年，藤原赖通、教通兄弟先后任关白。1051年安倍氏在陆奥起兵，引发前九年之役；朝廷派源赖义出任镇守府将军前往征讨，至1062年平定安倍氏。他无子嗣，1068年去世后，皇位由异母弟尊仁亲王继承，即后三条天皇。

en: Emperor Go-Saga (1220–1272), the 88th emperor of Japan, reigned from 1242 to 1246. A son of Emperor Tsuchimikado, he was placed on the throne after the ten-year-old Emperor Shijō died suddenly, the Kamakura shogunate rejecting a candidate from Retired Emperor Juntoku's line. In 1246 he abdicated to his son Emperor Go-Fukakusa and ruled as cloistered emperor, forcing Go-Fukakusa aside in 1259 in favour of his younger son Emperor Kameyama. Rivalry between the two brothers' descendants produced the Jimyōin-tō and Daikakuji-tō lines and later the Northern and Southern Courts.
zh: 后嵯峨天皇（1220—1272）是日本第88代天皇，1242至1246年在位。他是土御门天皇之子，十岁的四条天皇暴死后被拥立为帝，镰仓幕府拒绝了顺德上皇一脉的人选。1246年他让位给儿子后深草天皇，以上皇身份实行院政，又于1259年迫使后深草天皇退位，改立幼子龟山天皇。两兄弟的后裔彼此争夺皇位，形成持明院统与大觉寺统两大皇统，最终酿成后来的南北朝分裂。

en: Emperor Go-Sanjō (1034–1073), personal name Takahito, was the 71st emperor of Japan. A younger son of Emperor Go-Suzaku by the imperial princess Teishi, he was the first emperor in 170 years whose mother was not a Fujiwara, and the kampaku Fujiwara no Yorimichi cold-shouldered him as crown prince. Succeeding his half-brother Go-Reizei in 1068, he ruled in person, issuing the Enkyū Shōen Regulation Decree of 1069 and auditing private estates to curb Fujiwara wealth. He abdicated in 1073 in favour of his son Shirakawa, took Buddhist vows, and died at 40 before his cloistered rule could begin.
zh: 后三条天皇（1034—1073），名尊仁，日本第71代天皇。他是后朱雀天皇与祯子内亲王之子，是170年来首位母亲不姓藤原的天皇，在东宫时遭到关白藤原赖通冷落。1068年异母兄后冷泉天皇去世后即位，他亲理万机，1069年颁布延久庄园整理令，核查庄园，遏制藤原氏的势力。1073年他让位于皇子白河天皇，出家为僧，同年病逝，年仅40岁，规划中的院政未能展开。

en: Go-Shirakawa (1127–1192), a son of Emperor Toba, took the throne in 1155 after Emperor Konoe's sudden death, bypassing retired Emperor Sutoku's heir. In 1156 he won the Hōgen Rebellion with Taira no Kiyomori and Minamoto no Yoshitomo, then abdicated in 1158 and ruled as cloistered emperor through five reigns. After the Taira beat the Minamoto in the 1160 Heiji Disturbance, Kiyomori dominated the court and confined him after the failed Shishigatani plot. In the Genpei War he backed Minamoto no Yoritomo; the Taira were destroyed at Dan-no-ura in 1185.
zh: 后白河天皇（1127—1192）是鸟羽天皇之子，1155年近卫天皇骤逝后继位，越过了崇德上皇继承人的顺位。1156年，他借助平清盛与源义朝的武力赢得保元之乱，1158年让位于儿子二条天皇，以上皇身份经五帝之世执掌院政。1160年平治之乱后源氏战败，平清盛把持朝廷，并在鹿谷阴谋败露后将他囚禁。源平合战中他支持源赖朝，平家于1185年在坛之浦覆灭。

en: Emperor Go-Suzaku (1009–1045), personal name Atsunaga, was the 69th emperor of Japan and a younger son of Emperor Ichijō and Fujiwara no Shōshi. Named crown prince in 1017 after Prince Atsuakira stepped aside, he succeeded his brother Go-Ichijō in 1036 and ruled for nine years while Fujiwara no Yorimichi dominated the court as regent. His eldest son, born of Michinaga's daughter Yoshiko, succeeded him as Emperor Go-Reizei; another son, born of the imperial princess Teishi, later became Emperor Go-Sanjō. He abdicated in February 1045, took Buddhist vows, and died two days later at 37.
zh: 后朱雀天皇（1009—1045），名敦良，日本第69代天皇，一条天皇与藤原彰子之子、后一条天皇之弟。1017年敦明亲王辞去东宫之位后，他被立为皇太子，1036年继承兄长的皇位，在位九年，朝政由藤原赖通以摄政、关白身份把持。他与藤原道长之女嬉子所生的长子继位为后冷泉天皇，与祯子内亲王所生之子后来成为后三条天皇。1045年2月他退位出家，两天后便去世，年仅37岁。

en: Go-Toba (1180–1239), a son of Emperor Takakura, was enthroned at three in 1183 after the Taira fled Kyoto with Emperor Antoku and the imperial regalia, the first accession without the sacred treasures. He abdicated in 1198 and ruled as cloistered emperor through the reigns of his sons Tsuchimikado and Juntoku. A gifted poet, he commissioned and edited the Shin Kokinshū anthology and patronized the swordsmiths who opened Japan's golden age of blades. In 1221 he rose against the Kamakura shogunate in the Jōkyū War, was defeated, and died in exile on the Oki Islands in 1239.
zh: 后鸟羽天皇（1180—1239）是高仓天皇之子，1183年平家带着安德天皇和三神器逃离京都后，年仅三岁的他即位，成为首位没有神器传承的天皇。1198年他让位给儿子土御门天皇，以上皇身份经土御门、顺德两朝实行院政。他擅长和歌，主持编纂《新古今和歌集》，并扶持刀匠，开启日本刀剑的黄金时代。1221年他举兵讨伐镰仓幕府，史称承久之乱，兵败后被流放隐岐群岛，1239年在流放地去世。

en: Emperor Go-Uda (1267–1324), the 91st emperor of Japan, was a son of Emperor Kameyama and head of the Daikakuji-tō line. Named crown prince under Retired Emperor Go-Saga's settlement, he succeeded in 1274 while Kameyama ruled as cloistered emperor, and his reign saw the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281 repelled by the Hōjō-led shogunate. In 1287 the rival Jimyōin-tō and the Kamakura shogunate forced him to abdicate for Emperor Fushimi. He later ran the court as cloistered emperor for his son Emperor Go-Nijō from 1301 to 1308 and again for his second son Emperor Go-Daigo from 1318 until 1321.
zh: 后宇多天皇（1267—1324）是日本第91代天皇，龟山天皇之子，大觉寺统的首领。他依照后嵯峨上皇的安排被立为皇太子，1274年继位，由龟山上皇实行院政；在位期间，蒙古于1274和1281年两度来袭，均被北条氏主导的幕府击退。1287年，对立的持明院统联合镰仓幕府迫使他让位给伏见天皇。后来他先后在儿子后二条天皇（1301—1308）和次子后醍醐天皇（1318年起）在位时实行院政，直至1321年后醍醐天皇亲政。

en: The Sonpi Bunmyaku genealogy names Gotō Kimihiro as a son of Kimisato, adopted by Gotō Noriaki, and the father of Sanenobu.
zh: 据《尊卑分脉》系图，后藤公广是公乡之子，过继给后藤则明为养子，育有一子实信。

en: Gotō Kiminori belonged to the Fujiwara no Toshihito line; the genealogical collection Sonpi Bunmyaku records Noritsune as his adopted son.
zh: 后藤公则出自藤原利仁流，谱系书《尊卑分脉》记载则经为他的养子。

en: Gotō Motohide appears in a genealogy of the Gotō family of Ise as the son of Mototaka and father of Motoaki.
zh: 伊势后藤氏的系谱记载，后藤基秀是基隆之子、基秋之父。

en: Gotō no Motokiyo was a Kyoto warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods. The genealogical collection Sonpi Bunmyaku makes him a son of Satō no Nakakiyo, brother of the poet-monk Saigyō, adopted by Gotō no Sanemoto. He served Minamoto no Yoritomo, fought at the Battle of Yashima in 1185, and became shugo of Sanuki Province and later of Harima. As a western-face guard and police commissioner for the retired Emperor Go-Toba, he joined the court in the Jōkyū War of 1221; after the defeat he was beheaded on the shogunate's orders by his son Mototsuna.
zh: 后藤基清是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的京都武将、御家人，曾任赞岐国、播磨国守护。谱系书《尊卑分脉》记载，他本为歌僧西行之兄佐藤仲清之子，被后藤实基收为养子。他出仕源赖朝，参加1185年的屋岛之战，此后出仕后鸟羽上皇，担任西面武士和检非违使。1221年承久之乱中他加入上皇一方，兵败后被幕府下令处刑，奉命将他斩首的正是其子后藤基纲。

en: Gotō Mototaka, identified as a son of Gotō Mototsuna, was listed among the guards on duty in 1252.
zh: 后藤基隆被认作后藤基纲之子，1252年的格子番名单中列有其名。

en: Gotō no Mototsuna (1181–1256) was a Kamakura-period gokenin and court poet, son of Gotō no Motokiyo. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he served the Kamakura shogunate as an army commissioner and, on its orders, beheaded his father, who had fought for the retired emperor. In 1225 he joined the newly created Council of State, later holding the reward and land commissioner posts. Dismissed in the 1246 palace purge, he returned as a Hikitsuke-shū judge in 1252. His verses appear in imperial anthologies including the Shin Chokusen Wakashū, and some traditions name him as author of the Jikkinshō.
zh: 后藤基纲（1181—1256）是镰仓时代前期的御家人与歌人，后藤基清之子。1221年承久之乱时，他在幕府军中担任军奉行，奉幕府之命处死了追随后鸟羽上皇的父亲。1225年，他就任新设的评定众，后历任恩泽奉行、地奉行。1246年他因宫骚动被解职，1252年以引付众身份复职。他的和歌被收入《新敕撰和歌集》等敕撰和歌集，也有说法认为他是《十训抄》的作者。

en: Fujiwara no Noritsune was an eleventh-century Fujiwara warrior of the Toshihito branch, active in Kawachi Province. A retainer of Minamoto no Yorinobu, he was adopted as heir to Fujiwara no Kiminori, resident lord of the Sakato ranch.
zh: 藤原则经是11世纪河内国的武士，出自藤原氏利仁流，本为源赖信的郎党，后成为坂门御牧住人藤原公则的养子与继承人。

en: Gotō Sanenobu appears in a genealogy of the Gotō family as the son of Kimihiro and father of Sanetō.
zh: 后藤氏系谱记载，后藤实信是公广之子、实远之父。

en: Fujiwara no Sanetō was a northern-face guard in Kyoto of the Fujiwara Hidesato line. The genealogical collection Sonpi Bunmyaku names him as father of Gotō no Sanemoto, whose adopted heir was Gotō no Motokiyo, making Sanetō Motokiyo's adoptive grandfather.
zh: 藤原实远是京都的北面武士，出自藤原秀乡流。谱系书《尊卑分脉》记载，他是后藤实基之父；实基收后藤基清为养子，因此实远是基清的养祖父。

en: Hanazono (1297–1348), personal name Tomihito, was the 95th emperor of Japan, reigning from 1308 to 1318. A son of Emperor Fushimi of the Jimyōin line, he succeeded his cousin Emperor Go-Nijō under the cloistered rule of his father and brother. The Bumpō Agreement arranged rotation between the two rival imperial lines, and in 1318 he abdicated to Go-Daigo of the Daikakuji line. He raised his nephew Emperor Kōgon, took Zen vows in 1335 and turned his palace into Myōshin-ji temple. A waka poet of the Kyōgoku school, he left the diary Hanazono-in Minki.
zh: 花园天皇（1297—1348），名富仁，是日本第95代天皇，1308年至1318年在位。他是持明院统伏见天皇之子，在再从兄后二条天皇死后继位，在位期间由父亲与兄长以上皇身份实行院政。文保协议安排两大皇统轮流继承皇位，1318年他让位给大觉寺统的后醍醐天皇。他抚养了侄子光严天皇，1335年出家为禅僧，将自己的宫殿改为妙心寺。他是京极派的和歌名手，留有日记《花园院宸记》。

en: Hata Mochi was a warrior of the Matsura confederation in Hizen Province and the second son of Matsura Hisashi, whose genealogies traced the family to the Heian warrior Watanabe no Tsuna. In 1102 he moved to the Hata district of Matsura, took the surname Hata, and built Kishidake Castle as his stronghold. He thereby founded the Hata clan, which became the leading family among the Upper Matsura bands and held Kishidake for some four hundred years, down to the Sengoku period.
zh: 波多持是肥前国松浦党的武士，松浦党始祖松浦久的次子；据其家谱记载，家族出自平安时代武士渡边纲一脉。1102年，他移居松浦郡波多乡，改姓波多，并修筑岸岳城作为据点，由此开创波多氏。波多氏后来成为松浦党上松浦一支最大的豪族，据守岸岳城约四百年，一直延续到战国时代。

en: Hatakeyama Iekuni was a military commander of the late Kamakura period and a member of the Hatakeyama branch of the Ashikaga clan. A son of Hatakeyama Sadakuni, he held the court rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade and served as Jibu-taifu. His sons included Kunikiyo and Yoshifuka, while a daughter became the wife of Ashikaga Motouji. He later took Buddhist orders under the name Sairen and died in 1335; his descendants grew into the house that supplied kanrei deputies to the Muromachi shogunate.
zh: 畠山家国是镰仓时代末期的武将，出身足利氏支流畠山氏，为畠山贞国之子。他叙从五位下，官至治部大辅。其子有畠山国清、畠山义深等人，女儿清溪尼嫁给足利基氏为妻。家国后来出家，法号西莲，于1335年去世；他的子孙后来成为世代出任室町幕府管领的家族。

en: Hatakeyama Kunikiyo (d. 1362 or 1364), clerical name Dōsei, was a son of Hatakeyama Iekuni and a leading general of the early Ashikaga bakufu. After fighting at Tatarahama in 1336 he was made shugo of Izumi, later holding Kii and Kawachi. In 1353 he became the first Kantō kanrei, adviser to the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Motouji, and in 1358 arranged the murder of Nitta Yoshioki. Ousted in 1361, he rebelled in Izu, surrendered at Shuzenji Castle, and died soon after; he is regarded as the founder of the Kawachi Hatakeyama line.
zh: 畠山国清（1362或1364年卒），法名道誓，是畠山家国之子、室町幕府初期的重要武将。1336年在多多良滨之战立功，被任命为和泉守护，后来历任纪伊、河内守护。1353年他成为首任关东管领，辅佐镰仓公方足利基氏，1358年策划谋杀新田义兴。1361年他被罢免，在伊豆举兵反叛，最终在修禅寺城投降，不久死去，被视为河内畠山氏的实际始祖。

en: Hatakeyama Kuniuji was a Nanboku-chō warrior and the heir of Hatakeyama Takakuni. Appointed Ōshū kanrei in 1345, he joined his father at the Taga provincial seat in Mutsu to subdue Southern Court forces. He later clashed with his fellow kanrei Kira Sadaie, an ally of Ashikaga Tadayoshi, siding with Takauji in the Kannō Disturbance. In the second month of 1351 Sadaie's troops besieged Iwakiri Castle, and Kuniuji and his father took their own lives. His son Kuniakira stayed in the region and became ancestor of the Nihonmatsu clan.
zh: 畠山国氏是南北朝时代的武将、畠山高国的嫡子。1345年他被任命为奥州管领，与父亲一同前往陆奥国的多贺国府，负责镇压南朝势力。后来他与同为奥州管领、依附足利直义的吉良贞家对立，在观应之扰乱中站在足利尊氏一方。1351年二月，贞家的军队围攻岩切城，国氏与父亲一同自尽。其子国诠留在当地，成为二本松氏之祖。

en: Hatakeyama Munekuni, first named Munetsugu, was a Nanboku-chō warrior of the Mino branch of the Ashikaga-related Hatakeyama clan. A son of Hatakeyama Muneyoshi, he was an elder brother of the Hyūga shugo Hatakeyama Tadaaki and the father of Hatakeyama Tadamune, an aide to Ashikaga Tadayoshi.
zh: 畠山宗国（初名宗继）是南北朝时代的武士，出身足利一门畠山氏的美浓畠山氏，为畠山宗义之子、日向守护畠山直显之兄，也是足利直义亲信畠山直宗之父。

en: Hatakeyama Muneyoshi was a late Kamakura-period warrior of the Mino Hatakeyama, a branch of the Ashikaga-related Hatakeyama clan. He was the father of the Hyūga shugo Hatakeyama Tadaaki and of Hatakeyama Munekuni, whose son Tadamune became an aide to Ashikaga Tadayoshi.
zh: 畠山宗义是镰仓时代后期武将，出身足利一门畠山氏的美浓畠山氏，为日向守护畠山直显与畠山宗国之父，其孙畠山直宗为足利直义的亲信。

en: Hatakeyama Sadakuni, a Kamakura-period gokenin called Hatakeyama Jirō, was the son of Tokikuni, younger brother of Takakuni and father of Iekuni; he held Junior Fifth Rank and the offices of Shikibu-dayū and Minbu-no-jō.
zh: 畠山贞国是镰仓时代的御家人，通称畠山次郎，为时国之子、高国之弟、家国之父，叙从五位下，历任式部大夫、民部丞。

en: Hatakeyama Tadaaki (d. after 1358), first named Yoshiaki, was a warrior of the Ashikaga-related Hatakeyama clan, a son of Hatakeyama Muneyoshi. After Ashikaga Takauji's victory at Tatarahama, Tadaaki was sent to Hyūga to subdue Southern Court forces in southern Kyushu, bringing local lords including Kimotsuki Kaneshiba to submission by 1339. In 1345 he was appointed shugo of Hyūga. During the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi and Tadafuyu against the bakufu, but defeat at Shibushi Castle in 1357 by the Shimazu and by Kikuchi Takemitsu shattered his power; he fled to Bungo in 1358 and disappears from the records.
zh: 畠山直显（1358年后在世）初名义显，是足利一门畠山氏的武将、畠山宗义之子。足利尊氏在多多良滨之战获胜后，他被派往日向国，负责平定南九州的南朝势力，到1339年使肝付兼重等当地豪族归服。1345年，他被室町幕府任命为日向守护。观应之扰乱中，他追随足利直义与足利直冬、背离幕府；1357年在志布志城先后败于岛津氏和菊池武光，势力崩溃，1358年逃往丰后国，此后不见记载。

en: Hatakeyama Tadamune, also called Ōkura Shōsuke, was a warrior of the Mino branch of the Ashikaga-related Hatakeyama clan, son of Hatakeyama Munekuni and nephew of Hyūga shugo Hatakeyama Tadaaki. He became a close aide to Ashikaga Tadayoshi, receiving the character tada of his name from him. In 1349 he and Uesugi Shigeyoshi secured the dismissal of Tadayoshi's rival Kō no Moronao, then plotted his murder; the plan leaked, Tadamune was exiled to Echizen, and in the twelfth month of that year Moronao's agents forced him and his family and followers to kill themselves, the opening bloodshed of the Kannō Disturbance.
zh: 畠山直宗，通称大藏少辅，出身于足利一门畠山氏的美浓畠山氏，是畠山宗国之子、日向守护畠山直显之侄。他成为足利直义的亲信，名字中的“直”字即得自直义的偏讳。1349年，他与上杉重能成功使直义的政敌高师直被免去执事之职，随后又策划暗杀师直；计划泄露后，直宗被流放越前国，同年十二月，师直的密使逼使他与家人、随从一同自尽，成为观应之扰乱的开端。

en: Hatakeyama Takakuni (1305–1351) was a Northern and Southern Courts era warrior and shugo lord, son of Hatakeyama Tokikuni and head of the main Hatakeyama line. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji at Kyoto in 1336 and became shugo of Ise, but lost the post in 1338 after failing to stop Kitabatake Akiie's march through the province. In 1345 he went to Mutsu as guardian to his son Kuniuji, the new Oshu kanrei, and ruled from Taga. In the Kanno Disturbance he took Takauji's side; besieged at Iwakiri Castle by Kira Sadaie, he killed himself in 1351, aged forty-seven.
zh: 畠山高国（1305—1351）是日本南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，畠山时国之子，畠山氏嫡流当主。1336年他在京都为足利尊氏作战，随后就任伊势守护；1338年因未能阻止北畠显家南下通过伊势，被罢免守护职。1345年，他作为新任奥州管领、其子国氏的后见人同赴陆奥，以多贺国府为据点经营奥州。观应之扰乱中他站在尊氏一方，遭吉良贞家围攻岩切城，于1351年自尽，享年四十七岁。

en: Hatakeyama Tokikuni was a Kamakura-period warrior, possibly the renamed Kuniuji, eldest son of Hatakeyama Yasukuni, and jitō of the Nakakita manor and Tsuruyama district in Mino. In the Kenchō era of 1249 to 1256 Yasukuni and Kuniuji served the bakufu as ordinary gokenin, attending the shogun and meeting construction levies in the Kantō; Kuniuji did not enter the Kamakura regime's inner circle, though the house in Tokikuni's time ranked with the heads of Hōjō branch families. His eldest son Takakuni founded the Ōshū Hatakeyama line and his second son Sadakuni the Kawachi Hatakeyama, later one of the three Kanrei houses.
zh: 畠山时国是镰仓时代武将，一说即畠山泰国长男国氏改名后的名字，曾任美浓国仲北庄和鹤山乡的地头。建长年间（1249—1256年），泰国与国氏一同出仕幕府，活动仅限普通御家人役：担任将军的供奉、近习、随兵，承担在关东的营造夫役；国氏未进入幕府中枢，但时国时期的家格被视为与北条庶流一门的当主相当。长男高国一支后来成为奥州畠山氏，次男贞国一支成为河内畠山氏，后者在室町时代位列三管领之一。

en: Hatakeyama Yasukuni was an early Kamakura gokenin of the Ashikaga-related Hatakeyama clan, the third son of Ashikaga Yoshizumi. His mother was a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa and widow of Hatakeyama Shigetada, through whom he inherited the Hatakeyama legacy; he was the first of the line to bear the Hatakeyama name, while his half-brothers founded the Iwamatsu and Tanaka families. His name character came from his cousin Hōjō Yasutoki. He held lands in Mino, served the bakufu with his son Kuniuji in the Kenchō era (1249–1256), and was succeeded by Kuniuji, who may have been the Tokikuni named in genealogies; Yoshio's branch became the Mino, later Hyūga, Hatakeyama.
zh: 畠山泰国是镰仓时代前期武将、镰仓幕府御家人，出身足利一门畠山氏，为足利义纯第三子。其母是北条时政之女、畠山重忠的遗孀，他由此继承畠山氏名迹，也是这一脉中实际最早使用畠山苗字的人，异母兄则分别成为岩松氏、田中氏之祖。名字中的“泰”字得自表兄北条泰时的偏讳。他领有美浓国的领地，建长年间（1249—1256年）仍与子国氏一同出仕幕府，后由国氏继承家督；国氏或即系图中的时国。其子义生一支成为美浓畠山氏，后来发展为日向畠山氏。

en: Hatakeyama Yoshifuka (1331–1379) was the sixth head of the Hatakeyama clan and a younger brother of the Kantō kanrei Hatakeyama Kunikiyo. He fought for the Northern Court in the Kantō region and in 1359 faced Southern Court troops under Shijō Takatoshi at Ryūmonzan. Joining his brother's revolt in 1361, he surrendered with him, but was pardoned in 1366 and made shugo of Echizen, overthrowing Shiba Takatsune in the Jōji Incident. He later held the shugo posts of Noto, Etchū, Kawachi, Izumi and Kii, and died in 1379.
zh: 畠山义深（1331—1379）是畠山氏第六代当主、关东管领畠山国清之弟。他在关东为北朝作战，1359年在龙门山迎战南朝方四条隆俊的军队。1361年他参与兄长国清举兵，随兄投降；1366年获幕府赦免，被任命为越前守护，在贞治之变中击败斯波高经，此后历任能登、越中、河内、和泉、纪伊等国守护，1379年去世。

en: Hatakeyama Yoshikata belonged to the Mino branch of the Hatakeyama family, appearing in a genealogy as the son of Yoshio and father of Muneyoshi.
zh: 畠山义方出身美浓畠山氏，在系图中列为义生之子、宗义之父。

en: Hatakeyama Yoshio was a Kamakura-period warrior, a son of Hatakeyama Yasukuni and younger brother of Tokikuni. He inherited the family's Mino lands and founded the Mino Hatakeyama branch, which later moved to Hyūga; the Hyūga shugo Hatakeyama Tadaaki was his descendant.
zh: 畠山义生是镰仓时代武将，畠山泰国之子、时国之弟，继承了家族在美浓国的领地，开创美浓畠山氏；该支后来移往日向国，日向守护畠山直显即其裔孙。

en: Hatakeyama Yoshizumi (1174–1210), born Ashikaga Yoshizumi, was the eldest son of Ashikaga Yoshikane, raised at Nitta manor in Kōzuke by his great-uncle Nitta Yoshishige. In 1205, after the Hōjō destroyed the Musashi warrior Hatakeyama Shigetada, Hōjō Yoshitoki married Yoshizumi to Shigetada's widow, a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa, and had him succeed to the Hatakeyama name. He is counted the ancestor of the Minamoto-line Hatakeyama clan of the Ashikaga kindred, and Hatakeyama Yasukuni was his son. He died in the tenth month of 1210, aged thirty-seven.
zh: 畠山义纯（1174—1210），原名足利义纯，是足利义兼的长子，由大伯父新田义重在新田庄养大。1205年北条氏攻灭武藏武士畠山重忠后，北条义时将重忠的遗孀、北条时政之女嫁给他，令其继承畠山的名号，由此被视为足利一门中源姓畠山氏之祖，畠山泰国即其子。1210年十月去世，终年37岁。

en: Hatano no Hidetō was the third head of the Sagami Hatano, a grandson of its founder Saeki no Tsunenori and father of Hatano no Tōyoshi. He served in the secretariat of Retired Emperor Toba and held the post of secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
zh: 波多野秀远是相模波多野氏第三代当主，家祖佐伯经范之孙、波多野远义之父。他出仕鸟羽院，任藏人所众，官至刑部丞。

en: Hirosawa no Sanekata, born of the Hatano clan of Sagami, was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and ancestor of the Hirosawa house. In 1155 he fought under Minamoto no Yoshihira at the Battle of Ōkura, and the next year received lands at Hirosawa in Musashi Province, from which he took his name. He served Minamoto no Yoritomo in the Genpei War, winning merit at Fujito in 1184, joined the 1189 Ōshū campaign, accompanied Yoritomo to Kyoto in 1190 with his son Sanetaka, and in 1192 was granted twelve estates in Bingo Province.
zh: 广泽实方出身相模波多野氏，是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武士、广泽氏之祖。1155年，他随源义朝之子义平参加大藏合战并立下战功，翌年受赐武藏国新座郡广泽之地，遂以广泽为姓。治承·寿永之乱中他追随源赖朝，1184年在藤户之战立功，1189年从军奥州合战；1190年携子实高随赖朝上洛，1192年获赐备后国三谿郡十二乡。

en: Hirosawa Sanemura was a Kamakura-period warrior in Bingo province and grandson of Hirosawa Sanekata. His sons Sanetsuna and Sanenari divided his lands; Sanenari took the Wachi manor and founded the Wachi clan, while Sanetsuna's line became the Eda clan.
zh: 广泽实村是镰仓时代备后国的武士，为广泽实方之孙。他的儿子实纲与实成分割其领地：实成领有和知庄，以和智为氏，是和智氏之祖；实纲的子孙则称江田氏。

en: Hirosawa Sanetaka was a warrior of the Hatano clan of Sagami, son of Hirosawa Sanekata. In 1185 he served as an escort at the dedication of Kamakura's Shōchōju-in temple, and in 1190 he accompanied Minamoto no Yoritomo to Kyoto. In 1211 he went down to the family's lands in Bingo province to crush a bandit rising. During the Wada War of 1213, Wada Yoshimori requisitioned a hundred arrowheads from him in the shōgun's name; after the revolt Sanetaka was slandered as a Wada ally until his Hatano kinsmen cleared him in Kamakura.
zh: 广泽实高是相模国波多野一族的武士，广泽实方之子。1185年，他担任随兵参加镰仓胜长寿院的落成供养；1190年陪同源赖朝上洛。1211年，他前往家族所领的备后国，镇压当地起事的贼徒。1213年和田合战时，和田义盛假借将军之命向他催征一百支征矢尻；乱后实高遭谗言勾结和田氏，最终波多野一门在镰仓为他辩护，洗清嫌疑。

en: Hatano no Tōyoshi was a late-Heian warrior of Sagami Province and the fourth head of the Hatano clan, ruling Hatano manor in Yurugi District, an estate of the Fujiwara regents' house. He combined local lordship with court service: he belonged to the secretariat of Emperor Sutoku and in 1124 attended the first purification of the Ise princess Shushi, later becoming provisional governor of Chikugo. His sons, led by his second son Yoshimichi, who inherited Hatano manor, followed Minamoto no Yoshitomo and Yoritomo, and the Kawamura and Ōtomo houses traced their descent to him.
zh: 波多野远义是平安时代后期相模国的武士、波多野氏第四代当主，以余绫郡幡多乡一带的波多野庄为本领——该庄园是藤原摄关家的领地，波多野氏一边在地经营，一边出仕朝廷。远义是崇德天皇的藏人所众，1124年参与伊势斋宫守子女王的初次禊仪，后任筑后权守。他的儿子们以继承波多野庄的次子义通为首，多追随源义朝与源赖朝；河村氏、大友氏都出自他的后裔。

en: Hatano no Tsunehide was, in the Hatano clan genealogy, the second head of the Sagami Hatano, the son of the founder Saeki no Tsunenori and the father of Hatano no Hidetō.
zh: 据波多野氏家谱，波多野经秀是相模波多野氏的第二代当主，为家祖佐伯经范之子、波多野秀远之父。

en: Saeki no Tsunenori, also known as Hatano no Tsunenori, was a mid-Heian warrior of Sagami Province and the recorded founder of the Hatano clan. Genealogies including the Sonpi Bunmyaku name him a son of the Sagami governor Fujiwara no Kinmitsu, descended from Fujiwara no Hidesato, and rank him junior fifth lower without office. He held Hatano manor in Yurugi District, from which his house took its name, served Minamoto no Yoriyoshi of the Kawachi Minamoto, and fought in the Earlier Nine Years' War of 1051–1062.
zh: 佐伯经范，又称波多野经范，是平安时代中期相模国的武士，被谱为波多野氏的家祖。据《尊卑分脉》等家谱记载，他是相模守藤原公光之子，出自藤原秀乡一脉，叙从五位下散位。他领有相模余绫郡的波多野庄，一族即以波多野为苗字；经范仕于河内源氏的源赖义，参加了1051—1062年的前九年之役。

en: Hatano no Yoshimichi (1108–1169) was a late-Heian commander and fifth head of the Sagami Hatano, based at Hatano manor in Sagami Province. Son of the provisional Chikugo governor Tōyoshi, he served Minamoto no Yoshitomo from the latter's youth in the east, and his sister became Yoshitomo's concubine and mother of his second son Tomonaga. He fought for Yoshitomo in the 1156 Hōgen Disturbance, but fell out with him and left Kyoto in 1158, possibly over the succession. He joined Yoshitomo again in the 1159 Heiji Disturbance. He died in 1169; his son Yoshitsune opposed Yoritomo's 1180 uprising and took his own life.
zh: 波多野义通（1108—1169）是平安时代末期的武将、相模波多野氏第五代当主，本据为相模国波多野庄。他是筑后权守远义之子，自在东国的源义朝少年时便近身侍奉；其妹成为义朝侧室，生下次男朝长。1156年保元之乱中他随义朝从军，1158年与义朝不和、离开京都，原因可能是继嗣之争。1159年平治之乱中他再度追随义朝。1169年去世。其子义常与1180年举兵的源赖朝敌对，最终自尽。

en: Hatano no Yoshitsune, also Matsuda Yoshitsune, was a late-Heian warrior and sixth head of the Sagami Hatano, son of Hatano no Yoshimichi. After the Heiji Disturbance of 1159 he served in Kyoto as a Right Stables officer, becoming a leading Sagami magnate, even joining Minamoto no Yoritomo on a hunt in 1176. But when Yoritomo rose against the Taira in 1180, Yoshitsune refused the call. Yoritomo sent Shimokōbe Yukihira against him, and before the troops reached Matsuda manor Yoshitsune killed himself in the tenth month of 1180. His heir Aritsune was pardoned in 1188 and founded the Matsuda house.
zh: 波多野义常，亦称松田义常，是平安时代末期的武士、相模波多野氏第六代当主，波多野义通之子。1159年平治之乱后，他在京都出仕，任右马允，成为相模国有力武士，1176年还曾随行源赖朝狩猎。但1180年赖朝举兵讨伐平氏时，义常拒绝参阵。赖朝派下河边行平等前来诛伐，军队尚未抵达松田乡，义常便在1180年十月先行自害。其嫡子有常于1188年获赦，成为镰仓幕府御家人，是松田氏之祖。

en: Oda Haruhisa (1300–1353), eighth head of the Oda family of Hitachi, a branch of the Hatta clan, was the son of the seventh head, Sadamune. First named Takatomo, he distinguished himself in 1327 fighting in his father's place to help crush the Ando rebellion in Mutsu. After the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333 he served Emperor Go-Daigo and took the name Haruhisa from the emperor's name. In 1336 he joined the Southern Court, fighting the Satake clan of the Northern Court at Urizura Castle and sheltering Kitabatake Chikafusa at Oda Castle, until he submitted to Ashikaga rule in 1341. He died in 1353 and his son Takatomo succeeded him.
zh: 小田治久（1300—1353）是常陆小田氏第八代当主。小田氏出自八田氏，他是第七代当主小田贞宗之子，初名高知。1327年，他代父出征，在陆奥平定安藤氏之乱立功。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他出仕后醍醐天皇，受天皇名讳“尊治”中的一字，改名治久。1336年他加入南朝，在瓜连城与北朝的佐竹氏作战，并将北畠亲房迎入小田城，直至1341年归降足利方。1353年去世，由其子孝朝继嗣。

en: Oda Munetomo was a Kamakura-period head of the Oda family of Hitachi, a branch of the Hatta clan. His name character came from the Hōjō regent Tokimune, and he was shugo of Hitachi from 1301. He fathered Oda Sadamune.
zh: 小田宗知是镰仓时代常陆国武将小田氏（八田氏分支）的当主，名字得自北条执权时宗的偏讳，1301年起担任常陆国守护，为小田贞宗之父。

en: Oda Sadamune (1283–1335), also called Sadatomo, was the seventh head of the Oda warrior family of Hitachi, a branch of the Hatta clan. A character in his name was granted by the Hōjō regent Sadatoki. In 1327, when the Kamakura bakufu ordered the Andō rebellion in Mutsu crushed, he sent his heir Haruhisa to lead the family's men, and the young man won distinction in the campaign. After the bakufu fell in 1333, Haruhisa entered Emperor Go-Daigo's service. Sadamune died in 1335, the second year of the Kenmu Restoration.
zh: 小田贞宗（1283—1335），又名贞知，是常陆国武将小田氏（八田氏分支）的第七代当主，名字中的一字得自北条执权贞时的偏讳。1327年镰仓幕府下令平定陆奥国安藤氏之乱时，他派嫡子治久代己出征，治久在平叛中立功。1333年幕府灭亡后，治久出仕后醍醐天皇。贞宗于建武2年（1335年）去世。

en: Oda Tokitomo was a Kamakura-period head of the Oda family of Hitachi, the main line of the Hatta clan, succeeding his father Yasutomo. A character in his name came from the Hōjō regent Tsunetoki or Tokiyori, and he is the first head called Oda named in the Azuma Kagami. After the Hōji conflict of 1247 destroyed the Miura clan, his family's Miura ties cost it the Hitachi shugo post and part of its lands; he was still a minor in 1252. He was succeeded by his son Munetomo.
zh: 小田时知是镰仓时代常陆国武将小田氏的当主。小田氏为八田氏嫡流，他承袭父亲泰知的地位，名字中的一字得自北条执权经时或时赖的偏讳，也是《吾妻镜》中最早以“小田”之名出现的当主。1247年宝治合战三浦氏败亡后，小田氏因与三浦氏的姻亲关系被没收常陆守护职和部分领地；1252年时他仍是少年。其子宗知继嗣。

en: Hatta Tomoie (1142–c. 1225) was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, son of Utsunomiya Munetsuna, who held Hatta in Niihari district of Hitachi. He fought in the Hōgen War of 1156 and, after joining Minamoto no Yoritomo in 1180, helped crush Shida Yoshihiro at Nogi in 1183 and commanded the Tōkaidō army in the Ōshū campaign of 1189. As shugo of Hitachi he brought down the rival Daijō faction in 1193, and in 1199 joined the Council of Thirteen advising Shōgun Yoriie. He founded the Oda clan and built Oda Castle.
zh: 八田知家（1142—约1225）是平安末期至镰仓前期的武士，宇都宫宗纲之子，以常陆国新治郡八田为据点。他曾参加1156年的保元之乱，1180年起追随源赖朝，1183年在野木宫之战中与小山氏合力击溃志田义广，1189年奥州合战时担任东海道军大将军。任常陆国守护期间，他于1193年以谋略扳倒敌对的大掾氏，1199年又成为辅佐年幼将军源赖家的十三人合议制成员。他是小田氏的始祖，主持修筑了小田城。

en: Oda Tomoshige, also called Hatta Tomoshige, was a Kamakura warrior, son of Hatta Tomoie, from whom he inherited the post of shugo of Hitachi. In 1181 Minamoto no Yoritomo named him one of eleven archery masters guarding his bedchamber, and he fought beside his father in the Ōshū campaign of 1189. In 1213 he warned Ōe no Hiromoto that Wada Yoshimori was gathering troops, opening the Wada battle, and in 1221 he marched in the Jōkyū War. In 1228 the bakufu rebuked his scheme to seize the hereditary Daijō office in Hitachi.
zh: 小田知重（生卒年不详，一称八田知重）是镰仓幕府御家人，八田知家之子，后来继承了常陆国守护之职。1181年，源赖朝把他选为担任寝所警卫的十一名弓术达人之一；1189年他随父亲参加奥州合战。1213年，他察觉和田义盛聚集兵马，随即报告大江广元，揭开和田合战的序幕；1221年又在承久之乱中随军出征。1228年，他图谋夺取常陆大掾的世袭职位，被幕府斥为非分之想。

en: Oda Yasutomo was a mid-Kamakura warrior, the legitimate son of Oda Tomoshige and grandson of Hatta Tomoie, and the third of his line to serve as shugo of Hitachi. He died in 1245 at thirty-five, leaving a young heir, Tokitomo. The office passed to Yasutomo's cousin Shishido Iechika, possibly because Tokitomo was young or because his mother belonged to the Miura clan, which fell in the Hōji conflict of 1247. Another account, at odds with the date of Yasutomo's death, says that he fought for the Miura in that conflict and lost his office and some lands.
zh: 小田泰知是镰仓时代中期的武士，小田知重的嫡男、八田知家之孙，继父亲之后担任常陆国守护，是家族中第三代出任此职者。他于1245年去世，年三十五岁，留下年幼的嫡子时知。守护之职改由泰知的堂弟宍户家周（一作国家）继任，原因可能是时知年幼，或是其生母出自1247年宝治合战中覆灭的三浦氏。另有一说称泰知在该战中加入三浦方，因而失去守护职和部分领地，与他的卒年相矛盾。

en: Hei no Chikamitsu was a warrior of the Hei clan of Mutsu province and a son of Hei no Mitsuyori. When the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333 and Emperor Go-Daigo opened the Kenmu Restoration, he took service with Kitabatake Akiie, the governor of Mutsu, who confirmed the family's holdings in Hei district. The clan then marched south in Akiie's Oshu army on the Southern Court side, routing Ashikaga Takauji's forces at Aonogahara in 1338 before defeat at the battle of Ishizu in 1338.
zh: 闭伊亲光是陆奥国闭伊氏的武士，闭伊光赖之子。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡、后醍醐天皇开启建武新政后，他追随陆奥国司北畠显家，闭伊郡的家族所领得到安堵。此后闭伊一族作为南朝一方加入显家的奥州军南下，1338年在青野原击败足利尊氏的军队，同年却在石津之战中战败。

en: Hei no Ieasa, titled Dewa no kami, appears in the Edo-period genealogy of the Hei, later Hanawa, clan of Hei district in Mutsu as the son of the clan founder Hei no Yorimoto and the father of Hei no Tameyori.
zh: 闭伊家朝，家谱称出羽守，见于陆奥国闭伊郡闭伊氏（后为花轮氏）江户时代所修家谱，是闭伊氏始祖闭伊赖基之子、闭伊为赖之父。

en: Hei no Mitsutomo appears in the genealogy of the Hei Hanawa family as the father of Mitsuyori, in the line descended from Tameyori in Hei district, Mutsu.
zh: 闭伊光朝见于闭伊花轮氏家谱，是光赖之父，属于陆奥国闭伊郡为赖的后裔。

en: Hei no Mitsuyori was a Kamakura-period gokenin of the Hei clan, a warrior family based in Hei district in Mutsu province. Between the Shōō and Gen'ō eras (1288–1319), he and his kinsman Hei no Kazutsura disputed the lands left by Hei no Mitsukazu, and the regent Hōjō Takatoki judged the case himself at Kamakura. Mitsuyori kept the estates along the Hei River, including Takusari, Oyamada and Akimae, while Kazutsura received Kuwasaki and Kasama. His son was Chikamitsu.
zh: 闭伊光赖是镰仓时代陆奥国闭伊郡武家闭伊氏的御家人。正应至元应年间（1288—1319），他与同族闭伊员连围绕先代闭伊光员留下的领地发生继承纠纷，官司打到镰仓，由执权北条高时亲自裁决：光赖获得老木、闭伊川、田锁、小山田、闭伊崎、赤前等地，员连则分得锹崎与笠间。其子为闭伊亲光。

en: Hei no Tameyori appears in the Edo-period genealogy of the Hei, later Hanawa, clan of Hei district in Mutsu as the son of Hei no Ieasa and the father of Hei no Mitsutomo.
zh: 闭伊为赖见于陆奥国闭伊郡闭伊氏（后为花轮氏）江户时代所修家谱，为闭伊家朝之子、闭伊光朝之父。

en: Hei no Yorimoto was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, remembered as founder of the Hei clan of Hei district in Mutsu. Late Edo genealogies claim he was the third son of Minamoto no Tametomo, who escaped exile in Izu with his mother and reached the Sanriku coast. He is said to have met Minamoto no Yoritomo during the 1189 Oshu campaign, taken the name Sasaki Juro Yukimitsu, received Hei and Kesen districts after the Northern Fujiwara fell, and then called himself Hei no Yorimoto. No contemporary source supports his claimed Genji birth.
zh: 闭伊赖基是平安时代末期至镰仓时代前期的武将，被尊为陆奥国闭伊郡闭伊氏的始祖。江户时代后期编纂的诸家谱称，他是源为朝的三子，随母亲逃出配流之地伊豆，漂流至三陆海岸。相传他在1189年奥州合战时谒见源赖朝，改名佐佐木十郎行光，奥州藤原氏灭亡后受命统治闭伊、气仙两郡，随后取领地之名改称闭伊赖基。其源氏出身并无同时代史料佐证，后世多认为属于冒称。

en: Emperor Heizei (774–824) was the 51st emperor of Japan, reigning from 806 to 809. The eldest son of Emperor Kanmu, he was named crown prince in 785 and succeeded his father in 806. During his brief reign he reorganized the imperial bodyguards, appointing Sakanoue no Tamuramaro senior commander of the right. In 809, seriously ill, he abdicated in favor of his younger brother Emperor Saga and retired to Nara. In 810 his consort Fujiwara no Kusuko and her brother Nakanari raised a failed revolt in his name, the Kusuko Incident; Heizei then took Buddhist vows and died in 824.
zh: 平城天皇（774—824）是日本第51代天皇，806年至809年在位。他是桓武天皇长子，785年被立为皇太子，806年继位。在位时间不长，曾改组近卫府，任命坂上田村麻吕为右近卫大将。809年他因病重，让位于同母弟嵯峨天皇，退居奈良。810年，其宠妃藤原药子与药子之兄仲成借他的名义起兵失败，史称药子之变；事败后平城出家为僧，于824年去世。

en: The Hienuki clan genealogy counts Mitsuie Hienuki as the second head of the clan that ruled Hienuki district in Mutsu province, the son of the founder Tameshige and the father of Shigeyasu.
zh: 稗贯光家是陆奥国稗贯郡豪族稗贯氏的第二代当主，始祖稗贯为重之子、稗贯重泰之父。

en: Shigeyasu Hienuki was the third head of the Hienuki clan, which ruled Hienuki district in Mutsu province. The clan genealogy names him as the son of Mitsuie Hienuki and the father of his successor, Tamemasa Hienuki.
zh: 稗贯重泰是陆奥国稗贯郡豪族稗贯氏的第三代当主，稗贯光家之子、后继当主稗贯为正之父。

en: Tameshige Hienuki was the traditional founder of the Hienuki clan. The Date clan genealogy names him as a son of Date Tameie. In 1197 he went to Hienuki district in Mutsu province, entered Osegawa Castle, and took the district name as his family name. Tradition holds that he served Minamoto no Yoritomo and was granted the lands along the Kitakami River after the Ōshū campaign. His son Mitsuie succeeded him.
zh: 稗贯为重是传说中的稗贯氏始祖，据《伊达世臣家谱》记载，他是伊达为家之子。1197年，他前往陆奥国稗贯郡，入据小濑川城，以郡名为姓氏。相传他出仕源赖朝，在奥州之战后受封北上川流域的稗贯郡，其子稗贯光家继为当主。

en: Hiraga no Kanemune belonged to the Aki Hiraga clan; during the Nanboku-cho period his third son, Norikane, left the main house and founded the Higashimura branch family at Takaya in Aki Province.
zh: 平贺兼宗属于安艺平贺氏；南北朝时代，他的三男范兼从本家分出，在安艺国高屋保另立东村氏。

en: Hiraga no Koreyasu, also called Matsuba no Koreyasu, was the son of Sukemune, founder of the Aki Hiraga clan. In his generation the family settled on its estate in Hiraka district of Dewa Province and took the place name as its family name, styling itself Hiraka, later written Hiraga. On the eleventh day of the seventh month, he came of age at the Kamakura mansion of Hojo Yasutoki, the shogunal regent, who gave him the character yasu from his own name.
zh: 平贺惟泰又名松叶惟泰，是安艺平贺氏始祖平贺资宗之子。在他这一代，一族定居于出羽国平鹿郡的领地，以平鹿地名为姓，后来写作平贺氏。七月十一日，他在镰仓的执权北条泰时府邸举行元服礼，由北条泰时赐予其名字中的“泰”字。

en: Hiraga Naomune was a warrior of the Hiraga clan and its sōryō, the designated head of the main family line. Around 1274, the clan member Korenaga went from Dewa to Takaya in Aki Province in response to the Mongol invasion; Naomune's illegitimate elder brother Tomokane later held Takaya and served Ashikaga Takauji when the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333. The brothers then fought over the succession; Naomune won, took up residence at Takaya and ruled the district himself. Under him Takaya became the Hiraga clan's permanent base, while its ancestral lands in Hiraka district of Dewa were gradually lost.
zh: 平贺直宗是平贺氏的武士，也是宗家的总领，即家督继承人。约1274年，族人惟长因元军入侵自出羽下向安艺国高屋保；后来直宗的庶长兄共兼领有该地，并在1333年镰仓幕府灭亡时追随足利尊氏。此后兄弟二人为家督继承相争，直宗获胜，亲自下向高屋保实施统治。在他治下，高屋保成为平贺氏的永久本据，而出羽平鹿郡的祖领则逐渐丧失。

en: Hiraga no Sukemune, first called Matsuba no Sukemune, was the founder of the Aki Hiraga clan. A warrior of the late Heian period, he backed Minamoto no Yoritomo in the Genpei War of 1180 to 1185 and won repeated distinction in the fighting.
