He was rewarded with estates in four provinces: Hiraka district in Dewa, Takaya in Aki, Sakurao in Kazusa, and Aburaden in Etchu. His descendants later settled at Hiraka and took its name, calling themselves Hiraga. The clan claimed descent from the great minister Fujiwara no Yoshifusa.
zh: 平贺资宗原名松叶资宗，是安艺平贺氏的始祖。平安时代末期，他起兵追随源赖朝，在1180—1185年的治承·寿永之乱（源平合战）中屡立战功，因此获赐四处领地：出羽国平鹿郡、安艺国高屋保、上总国樱尾乡与越中国油田条。其后人后来迁居平鹿郡，以地名为家名，改称平贺氏。该族自称是太政大臣藤原良房的后裔，出自藤原北家。

en: Hiraga Tomokane was a warrior of the Hiraga clan of Aki Province. Around 1274, the clan member Korenaga went from Dewa to Takaya in response to the Mongol invasion and built Misonou Castle there. After the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333, Tomokane, who held Takaya, fought under Ashikaga Takauji. As the clan's illegitimate eldest son he contested the headship with his younger brother Naomune, the sōryō, but lost the struggle; Naomune went to Takaya and governed it himself, and it became the clan's permanent base while the old lands in Hiraka district of Dewa slipped away.
zh: 平贺共兼是安艺国平贺氏的武士。1274年前后，族人惟长因元军入侵自出羽下向高屋保，在那里修筑御薗宇城。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，领有高屋保的共兼追随足利尊氏转战。他是家中的庶长子，与担任平贺氏总领的弟弟直宗争夺家督，却在这场抗争中失败。直宗随后下向高屋保亲自统治，平贺氏的本据就此固定在安艺高屋保，出羽平鹿郡的旧领则逐渐丧失。

en: Hirosawa Yoshizane (c. 1165–c. 1240), also written Yata Yoshizane, was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, the son of Ashikaga Yoshikiyo, who fell at the Battle of Mizushima in 1183. He was known as Hirosawa Hangandai after Hirosawa village in Kamo district where he lived. When Ashikaga Yoshiuji was made military governor of Mikawa after the Jōkyū War of 1221, Yoshizane's sons Sanekuni, Yoshisue and Yoshimune settled in that province. Sanekuni's descendants became the Niki clan, and Yoshisue's the Hosokawa clan; Yoshimune made Togasaki his base.
zh: 广泽义实（约1165—约1240），又作矢田义实，是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，为足利义清之子——义清于1183年在水岛之战中战死。他因住在加茂郡广泽村而通称广泽判官代。1221年承久之乱后，足利义氏被任命为三河守护，义实之子实国、义季、义宗随之进入三河。实国的后裔形成仁木氏，义季的后裔形成细川氏；义宗则以户贺崎为据点。

en: The Hishikari family history records that Hishikari Shigenobu led the Kyushu clan after Takaharu and before Atsushige.
zh: 据菱刈氏家史记载，菱刈重信在隆春之后、笃重之前统领九州的菱刈氏。

en: Fujiwara no Shigetae, later known as Hishikari Shigetae, was by family tradition a grandson of the courtier Fujiwara no Takanaga, who was exiled to Izu after the Hōgen War of 1156. Minamoto no Yoritomo confirmed his holding of the two Hishikari estates of Tara and Goishi in Ōsumi province, where he settled and became the ancestor of the Hishikari clan. Tradition also makes him the founder in 1194 of the Kōriyama Hachiman shrine, whose deity he invited by oracle from Usa Hachiman.
zh: 藤原重妙（后称菱刈重妙），相传为平安末期公卿藤原隆长之孙；隆长在1156年保元之乱后被流放伊豆。源赖朝把大隅国菱刈的太良、牛屎两处庄园封领确认给他，他于是下向大隅定居，成为菱刈氏的氏祖。又传他在1194年奉神谕，从宇佐八幡宫劝请分灵，开创了郡山八幡神社。

en: The Hishikari family history records Hishikari Shigezane as the legitimate son and successor of Hishikari Shigetae, founder of the clan in Kyushu.
zh: 据菱刈氏家史记载，菱刈重实是菱刈重妙的嫡子与继承人；重妙在九州创立了菱刈氏。

en: The Hishikari family history records that Hishikari Takaharu succeeded Shigezane as head of the Kyushu clan and died fighting outlaws.
zh: 据菱刈氏家史记载，菱刈隆春在重实之后继承了九州菱刈氏的家督，后在与凶徒的战斗中阵亡。

en: Hongō Suketada was a Nanboku-chō-period warrior and first head of the Hongō branch of the Satsuma Shimazu. He was the sixth son of the fourth Shimazu head, Shimazu Tadamune; of the seven brothers, the eldest inherited the main house and the other six each founded a cadet house. From 1336 he campaigned for his eldest brother Sadahisa, commanding a wing at the siege of Kaseda castle in Ōsumi. In 1351 he served the Northern Court in Chikuzen under Isshiki Noriuji, and in 1352 he received part of Hongō in Hyūga by a grant from Ashikaga Takauji or his son Yoshiakira. Tradition says he entered Satsumasako that winter and took the Hongō name, though the date of his entry is uncertain. He died in 1359 or 1365.
zh: 北乡资忠是日本南北朝时代萨摩、日向的武将，萨摩守护岛津氏有力支族北乡氏的初代当主。他是岛津宗家第四代当主岛津忠宗的第六子；七兄弟中长兄继承宗家，其余六人各自开创分家。1336年起，他随长兄贞久转战，在攻打大隅加濑田城时担任搦手大将。1351年，他随一色范氏在筑前为北朝作战；1352年，他凭足利尊氏或其子义诠的文书获授日向北乡的部分土地。相传他于同年冬进入萨摩迫，以乡名为氏，称北乡氏，但确切入部时间不详。他于1359年或1365年去世。

en: Honkōin (born c. 1306) was the wife of Ashikaga Tadayoshi, who directed the early Muromachi shogunate alongside his brother Takauji, and she held the junior third rank. A daughter of Shibukawa Sadayori, her secular name is unrecorded. In 1347, at about forty, she bore Tadayoshi his son Nyoimaru. During the Kannō Disturbance of 1350–1352 she lost both husband and son. She inherited Tadayoshi's Akatsuka estate in Musashi Province, took the tonsure, and spent her later years praying for their souls; one account places her death around 1363, and she was dead by 1383.
zh: 本光院（约1306年生）是室町幕府草创期与兄长尊氏共同主持幕政的足利直义之妻，位至从三位。她是涩川贞赖之女，本名不见记载，以法名行世。1347年，年约四十的她为直义生下儿子如意丸。1350—1352年的观应之乱中，她接连失去丈夫与儿子。此后她继承直义的遗领武藏国赤冢乡，落发为尼，为亡夫亡子祈求冥福；一说她1363年前后去世，至1383年时则确已不在人世。

en: Honma Arinao was a head of the Sado Honma clan, the warrior family that ruled Sado Island as shugodai from Sawata Castle; the clan's genealogy names him as the son and successor of Honma Yasunori.
zh: 本间有直是佐渡本间氏的家督，本间氏以杂太城为据点，以守护代身份统治佐渡岛；本间氏家系载他是本间泰宣之子并继其父为家督。

en: Honma Munetada was a head of the Sado Honma clan. A clan genealogy records that he lived at Sawata and erected a sacred image of Kumano Gongen at Hatano in 1308.
zh: 本间宗忠是佐渡本间氏的家督。据本间氏家谱记载，他居住在杂太，并于1308年在畑野村建立熊野权现神像。

en: Honma Tadaie was an early Kamakura-period warrior and the eldest son of Honma Yoshitada, holder of Echi in Aikō District, Sagami. His name appears in 1219 among the palanquin attendants when the young Fujiwara no Yoritsune traveled to Kamakura. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he served in Hōjō Tokifusa's army, fought at Seta and Uji, and helped capture the Mino Genji leader Kōji Yoritsune at Kibune. Remaining in Kyoto with the Rokuhara deputies, he led troops against disorderly monks at Onjō-ji in 1227 and at Kōya-san in 1228, and became shugodai of Ise Province.
zh: 本间忠家是镰仓时代前期的武士，本间义忠的嫡子，据有相模国爱甲郡依智乡。1219年，幼主藤原赖经前往镰仓时，忠家的名字出现在舆役名单中。1221年承久之乱时，他加入北条时房的军队，在势多与宇治作战，并在贵船协助擒获美浓源氏首领神地赖经。他随后随六波罗探题留驻京都，1227年和1228年先后率军对付园城寺与高野山滋事的僧众，并出任伊势国守护代。

en: Honma Tadatsuna was a head of the Sado Honma clan; its genealogy places him between his father Honma Yoshihisa and his son Honma Munetada.
zh: 本间忠纲是佐渡本间氏的家督，本间氏家系把他列在父亲本间能久与儿子本间宗忠之间。

en: Honma Yasunori was a head of the Sado Honma clan, which ruled Sado Island from Sawata Castle as shugodai under the Kamakura shogunate; the clan genealogy places him between his father Yorinao and his son Arinao.
zh: 本间泰宣是佐渡本间氏的家督，本间氏以杂太城为据点，在镰仓幕府下以守护代身份统治佐渡岛；据本间氏家系，他上承父亲赖直，下传儿子有直。

en: Honma Yasusada was the fourth head of the Sado Honma clan, which from 1185 ruled Sado Province as shugodai from Sawata Castle. He succeeded Munetada and was followed by Yorinao.
zh: 本间泰定是佐渡本间氏第四代当主。该家族自1185年初代当主本间能久受任守护代以来，以杂太城为据点统治佐渡国。泰定继承宗忠，之后由赖直继任。

en: Honma Yorinao was the fifth head of the Sado Honma clan, the Kamakura-period warrior family that ruled Sado Province as shugodai from Sawata Castle. He succeeded Yasusada and was followed by Yasunori.
zh: 本间赖直是佐渡本间氏第五代当主。该家族在镰仓时代以杂太城为据点，出任佐渡国守护代。赖直继承泰定，之后由泰宣继任。

en: Honma Yoshihisa was the first head of the Sado Honma clan and entered the island as shugodai for the Osaragi shugo of Sado, establishing the clan at Sawata Castle.
zh: 本间能久是佐渡本间氏的初代家督，他作为佐渡守护大佛氏的守护代进入佐渡岛，以杂太城为本间氏的据点。

en: Honma Yoshitada was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, remembered as the ancestor of the Honma clan. A son of Ebina Suisada of the Yokoyama party, one of the seven warrior bands of Musashi, he held lands at Echi in Aikō District, Sagami. He appears to have initially belonged to the Taira side, and in 1185 was among the Kyoto gokenin censured for accepting office without Yoritomo's approval. Reconciled, he served in Minamoto no Yoritomo's main army during the Ōshū campaign of 1189 and escorted Yoritomo to Kyoto in 1190 and 1195.
zh: 本间义忠是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武士，被奉为本间氏的始祖。他是武藏七党之一横山党武士海老名季贞之子，以相模国爱甲郡依智乡为据点。他起初似乎属于平氏一方；1185年，他因未经源赖朝推举便在京都任官而受到申斥。与赖朝和解后，他在1189年的奥州合战中加入赖朝的本队，并于1190年和1195年作为随兵扈从赖朝上洛。

en: Emperor Horikawa (1079–1107), personal name Taruhito, was the 73rd emperor of Japan. The son of Emperor Shirakawa and Fujiwara no Kenshi, he was only seven when his father abdicated in January 1087 and placed him on the throne. Fujiwara no Morozane served as regent while Shirakawa directed affairs through his new cloistered rule, so Horikawa's own reign was largely ceremonial; he devoted himself instead to scholarship, poetry, and music. His son by Fujiwara no Ishi, Prince Munehito, was raised by Shirakawa and succeeded him as Emperor Toba. Horikawa died in 1107 at 28.
zh: 堀河天皇（1079—1107），名善仁，日本第73代天皇，白河天皇与藤原贤子之子。1087年1月父亲退位、把他扶上皇位时，他年仅7岁。藤原师实出任摄政，白河上皇则通过首创的院政总揽政务，堀河天皇在位期间因而多居象征性地位，他本人潜心于学问、和歌与音乐。他与藤原苡子所生的皇子宗仁由白河上皇抚养，后来继位为鸟羽天皇。堀河天皇于1107年病逝，年仅28岁。

en: Hosokawa Akiharu (1330–c. 1367) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era and the founder of the Hosokawa Awa shugo house, also called the Sanshu family. A son of Hosokawa Yoriharu, he was known as Kuro in childhood and took the name Akiharu through a character granted by the second shogun, Ashikaga Yoshiakira. He followed his elder brother Yoriyuki into Awa Province, and tradition credits him with building Shozui Castle in 1363 and reviving the Zen temple Myosho-ji. He died young around 1367, and his son Yoshiyuki succeeded him.
zh: 细川诠春（1330—约1367）是日本南北朝时代的武士，为细川阿波守护家（赞州家）之祖。他是细川赖春之子，幼名九郎，后受第二代将军足利义诠偏讳，取名诠春。他随兄长赖之进入阿波国，相传于1363年修筑胜瑞城，并再兴禅寺妙照寺。他约于1367年早逝，由其子义之继嗣。

en: Hosokawa Akiuji (died 1352), second head of the Hosokawa Oshu branch, was a Northern Court general, the son of Hosokawa Yorisada of Mikawa Province. From the Genko War he served Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1336 crossed to Shikoku to win its warriors for Takauji. He became shugo of Sanuki, Kawachi, Tosa and Izumi and headed the Board of Retainers, but in 1347 was routed by Kusunoki Masatsura and lost his offices. In the Kanno Disturbance he first backed Ashikaga Tadayoshi, then returned to Takauji. In 1352 he led Northern troops against a Southern Court drive on Kyoto, dying that July.
zh: 细川显氏（？—1352）是细川奥州家第二代当主、北朝武将，为出身三河国的细川赖贞之子。自元弘之乱起他便追随足利尊氏，1336年渡海前往四国，争取岛上的武士归附足利方。他先后受任赞岐、河内、土佐、和泉四国守护，并担任侍所头人，但1347年被楠木正行击败而遭解职。观应之扰乱中他先从足利直义，后复归尊氏。1352年，他率北朝军抵御南朝对京都的进攻，同年7月去世。

en: Hosokawa Jozen (born c. 1320) was a son of Hosokawa Yorisada of Mikawa and younger brother of Akiuji. Originally a betto administrator at the Tsurugaoka Wakamiya shrine, he served Ashikaga Takauji with his brother and won distinction in the Nakasendai War of 1335. Sent to rally the warriors of Shikoku and western Honshu, in January 1336 he struck at Kyoto in concert with Takauji's own advance, and that May fought at the Minato River. He kept campaigning against Southern Court forces around the capital until the autumn of 1339, when records of him cease.
zh: 细川定禅（约1320年生）是三河细川赖贞之子、显氏之弟。他原为鹤冈若宫的别当，后与兄长显氏、堂兄和氏一同出仕足利尊氏，在1335年的中先代之乱中立功。他受命纠合四国、中国地方的国人武装，1336年1月趁尊氏攻入京都时同时进击，同年5月又参加凑川之战。此后他继续在畿内与南朝势力作战，屡立战功；1339年8月以后史料不再见其名。

en: Hosokawa Kazuuji (1296–1342), fourth head of the Hosokawa clan, was a Mikawa-born warrior in the service of Ashikaga Takauji. After the Genkō War he joined Takauji's overthrow of the Kamakura shogunate and was made governor of Awa under the Kenmu Restoration. In 1335 he helped crush the Nakasendai rebellion and then fought for Takauji against the imperial court; in 1336 he and his cousin Akiuji secured Shikoku for the Ashikaga. After the shogunate's founding he headed the Boards of Inquiry and Retainers, then retired to Akizuki in Awa, where he invited Musō Soseki to found Fudaiji and died in 1342.
zh: 细川和氏（1296—1342）是细川氏第四代当主、出身三河国的武将，效力于足利尊氏。元弘之乱后，他参加尊氏推翻镰仓幕府的行动，建武新政时受任阿波守。1335年他参与镇压中先代之乱，随后随尊氏与朝廷官军作战；1336年与堂兄弟细川显氏一同争取四国诸大名与国人归附足利方。幕府开创后，他历任引付头人、侍所头人，后隐居阿波秋月，延请梦窗疎石开创补陀寺，1342年去世。

en: Hosokawa Kimiyori was a gokenin of the late Kamakura period and the third head of the Hosokawa clan, eldest son of Hosokawa Toshiuji. Commonly called Hachirōtarō, he kept his seat at Hosokawa-gō in Mikawa Province and later took Buddhist orders under the name Raibutsu, also styled Keitokuin. His sons Kazuuji, Yoriharu and Morouji became ancestors of the clan's principal branch houses.
zh: 细川公赖是镰仓时代后期的御家人、细川氏第三代当主，为细川俊氏的长子，通称八郎太郎。他以三河国细川乡为本据，后来出家，法名赖佛，又号景德院。他的儿子和氏、赖春、师氏后来分别成为细川氏主要支流的祖先。

en: Hosokawa Kiyouji (c. 1325–1362), fifth head of the Hosokawa and son of Kazuuji, fought for Takauji in the Kanno Disturbance and became shugo of Ise, Iga and Wakasa. In 1353 he shielded Emperor Go-Kogon during a Southern Court raid on Kyoto, carrying him on his back over the mountains to Omi. In 1358 Yoshiakira made him steward, forerunner of the kanrei, but rivals drove him out in 1361 and he defected to the Southern Court. In 1362 his younger cousin Yoriyuki cornered him in Sanuki; the Taiheiki relates that Yoriyuki's feint split his army and Kiyouji died fighting alone.
zh: 细川清氏（约1325—1362）是细川氏第五代当主、和氏的嫡子，观应之扰乱中率四国军队为足利尊氏作战，后受任伊势、伊贺、若狭三国守护。1353年南朝军进攻京都时他护卫后光严天皇，曾背负天皇翻越山岭撤至近江。1358年，足利义诠任命他为执事，即管领的前身；但他于1361年被政敌逐出幕府，投奔南朝。1362年，堂弟赖之在赞岐将他逼入绝境，《太平记》称赖之以诱敌之计分散其兵力，清氏随后单骑战死。

en: Hosokawa Kokai (born c. 1323), whose personal name is unrecorded, was a monk-general of the Hosokawa, a son of Yorisada and younger brother of Akiuji, holding the clerical title Sanmi Ajari. Formerly betto of Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine, he followed Ashikaga Takauji against the Southern Court. In the third month of 1337 he fought Kutsuna Yoshinori on Kutsuna Island in Iyo, then joined Hatakeyama Kunikiyo in Kii, subduing its northern districts by late 1338. He served as shugo of Tosa from 1339 to the end of 1340, when the sources lose sight of him.
zh: 细川皇海（约1323年生），讳不传，皇海为其法名，是细川赖贞之子、显氏之弟，身为僧官，号三位阿阇梨。他曾任鹤冈八幡宫别当，南北朝动乱开始后与兄长显氏、定禅一同追随足利尊氏与南朝作战。1337年3月，他在伊予国忽那岛与忽那义范交战，随后转战纪伊，与畠山国清协力，到1338年末基本平定纪伊北部。1339年至1340年底他担任土佐守护，此后便从史料中消失。

en: Hosokawa Morouji (1305–1348), first head of the Hosokawa Awaji line, was a son of Hosokawa Kimiyori of Mikawa and brother of Kazuuji and Yoriharu. In the Genko War he followed Ashikaga Takauji against the Kamakura shogunate, then served under Tadayoshi in Kamakura and fought the Nakasendai War of 1335. As the Muromachi bakufu's shugo of Awaji, he crushed the Southern Court Uhara clan at Tachikawase. In 1347 he reduced Shodo Island, forcing the Southern Court defector Aoura Nobutsune to submit. He died in June 1348, and his descendants held Awaji as their shugo province.
zh: 细川师氏（1305—1348）是细川淡路守护家初代当主，为三河细川公赖之子、和氏与赖春的弟弟。元弘之乱中他追随足利尊氏攻灭镰仓幕府，建武年间随尊氏之弟直义前往镰仓，并参加1335年的中先代之乱。室町幕府建立后，他受任淡路守护，在立河濑之战讨灭南朝方的宇原氏。1347年，他攻取小豆岛，迫使倒向南朝的饱浦信胤屈服。1348年6月他去世，子孙世袭淡路守护职。

en: Hosokawa Naotoshi (1319–1337), commonly called the Tachihaki Senjo, was a son of Hosokawa Yorisada of Mikawa and a younger brother of Akiuji. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji in the Nanboku-cho wars: in August 1336 he helped cover the siege of Amidagamine Castle by routing Southern Court troops near Yodo and Takeda. In the third month of 1337, he and Akiuji led their men against Southern commander Otsuka Koremasa before Katsuiji Temple in Kawachi Province, and fell in the fighting, aged about nineteen.
zh: 细川直俊（1319—1337），通称细川带刀先生，是三河细川赖贞之子、显氏的弟弟。南北朝战乱中他追随足利尊氏：1336年8月，为配合阿弥陀峰城的攻城战，他在淀、竹田一带击破南朝军。1337年3月，他与兄长显氏率军在河内国葛井寺前大路迎战南朝将领大冢惟正所部，力战而死，享年19岁。

en: Hosokawa Nariuji was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era, the youngest son of Hosokawa Kazuuji, adopted as heir by Hosokawa Akiuji, head of the Hosokawa Oshu branch. When Akiuji died in 1352 he took the post of shugo of Izumi Province, was replaced the next year, and was reappointed in 1356. In 1359, after his adoptive elder brother Shigeuji died suddenly, he succeeded as head of the Oshu house. In 1368 he served at Ashikaga Yoshimitsu's coming-of-age ceremony.
zh: 细川业氏是日本南北朝时代的武将，为细川和氏的幼子，出养细川奥州家当主细川显氏。1352年显氏死后，他就任和泉国守护，次年被畠山国清取代，1356年再度出任。1359年义兄细川繁氏急逝，他遂继承奥州家家督。1368年他在足利义满的元服式上供职。

en: Hosokawa Shigeuji (c. 1325–1359), third head of the Hosokawa Oshu branch, was a Northern Court commander and the son of Hosokawa Akiuji. He fought beside his father for Ashikaga Takauji, and when Akiuji died after the 1352 Otokoyama campaign in Izumi he succeeded him as shugo of Sanuki and Tosa. From 1355 he fought Southern Court forces in Tosa and received the Settsu shugo post. The Taiheiki records that in 1359, while in Sanuki, he seized the Sutoku cloistered emperor's estates to fund a great expedition and died suddenly that summer; the chronicle blames his death on a curse.
zh: 细川繁氏（约1325—1359）是细川奥州家第三代当主、北朝武将，为细川显氏之子。他随父亲为足利尊氏作战，1352年父亲在和泉男山之战后去世，他继承家督，出任赞岐、土佐守护。1355年起他在土佐与南朝势力作战，以功受任摄津守护。《太平记》记载，1359年他在赞岐为筹划大规模远征而侵夺崇德上皇的院领以充军资，当年夏天暴病而亡，史书将其死归于崇德院的咒诅。

en: Hosokawa no Toshiuji was a gokenin of the Kamakura period (1185-1333) and the second head of the Hosokawa clan. The son of Yoshitoshi, who died young, he and his brothers were adopted by their grandfather Yoshisue, and Toshiuji became his successor; his common name was Hachiro. He took Buddhist vows under the name Raisai. He seems to have kept his base at Hosokawa-go in Mikawa, now Hosokawa-cho, Okazaki. His tomb stands at Rinsho-ji in Toyota with those of Yoshisue and his son Kimiyori, the third head.
zh: 细川俊氏是镰仓时代（1185—1333）的御家人，细川氏第二代当主。父亲义俊早逝，他与兄弟们被祖父义季收为养子，由俊氏继承家业，通称八郎。他出家后法号赖西，似乎一直以三河国细川乡（今爱知县冈崎市细川町一带）为据点。其墓与祖父义季、其子第三代当主公赖之墓一同存于爱知县丰田市幸町的邻松寺。

en: Hosokawa Ujiharu (c. 1325–1387), second head of the Hosokawa Awaji line, succeeded his father Morouji as shugo of Awaji in 1348. In 1361, when his kinsman Kiyouji was condemned and defected to the Southern Court, Ujiharu followed him, helping seize Kyoto at the year's end. Driven out with him, he crossed to Sanuki in 1362; when Kiyouji was killed there by their cousin Yoriyuki, Ujiharu soon surrendered and was restored as Awaji shugo. He served the Muromachi regime thereafter, fighting Southern Court forces in Kawachi in 1373, and died in 1387, succeeded by his son Mitsuharu.
zh: 细川氏春（约1325—1387）是细川淡路守护家第二代当主，1348年继承父亲师氏的淡路守护职。1361年，同族清氏被足利义诠下令追讨而投奔南朝，氏春随之归降，并在年末参与攻占京都。他与清氏一同被逐出后，于1362年渡海至赞岐图谋再举；清氏在赞岐被堂弟赖之攻杀后，氏春不久便归降幕府，重新受任淡路守护。此后他作为幕府武将，1373年在河内与南朝势力作战立功，1387年去世，由子满春继任。

en: Hosokawa Yoriari (1332–1391), son of Hosokawa Yoriharu, was a Northern and Southern Courts era warrior and the first head of the Hosokawa Izumi-kami shugo house. In the Kanno Disturbance he fought alongside his father in Kyoto for Ashikaga Takauji, and after his father's death in 1352 he led Sanuki troops at the Battle of Otokoyama beside his brother Yoriyuki. After Yoriyuki became kanrei, Yoriari governed Awa as his deputy and fought the Kono clan of Iyo. When Yoriyuki fell in the 1379 Koryaku coup, Yoriari stood by him in arms. He yielded the headship to his son Yorinaga in 1387 and died in 1391.
zh: 细川赖有（1332—1391）是日本南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，细川赖春之子，为细川和泉上守护家初代当主。观应之扰乱中，他随父在京都为足利尊氏作战；1352年父亲战死后，他率赞岐兵力参加男山合战，与兄长赖之协同。赖之任管领后，他作为守护代经营阿波，与伊予的河野氏交战。1379年康历政变中赖之失势，赖有集结被官，与下国的赖之共同抗敌。1387年他把家督让给嫡子赖长，1391年去世，享年六十岁。

en: Hosokawa Yoriharu (c. 1304–1352) was a Northern Court general, son of Hosokawa Kimiyori of Mikawa and ancestor of the Hosokawa kanrei line. In 1333 he and his brother Kazuuji joined Ashikaga Takauji's rising and guarded the child Senju-o, the future shogun Yoshiakira. Sent to subdue Shikoku, he fought at the Minato River in 1336 and took Kanegasaki Castle in Echizen in 1338. He became shugo of Awa, Bingo, Iyo and Hyuga, and helped destroy Kusunoki Masatsura at Shijo Nawate in 1348. In the Kanno Disturbance he abandoned Tadayoshi for Takauji. He fell defending Yoshiakira near Shichijo Omiya in 1352.
zh: 细川赖春（约1304—1352）是北朝武将，为三河细川公赖之子，也是后来世袭管领的细川京兆家之祖。1333年，他与兄长和氏一同参加足利尊氏起兵，护卫年幼的千寿王，即后来的将军义诠。他受命平定四国，1336年参加凑川之战，1338年攻取越前金崎城。他历任阿波、备后、伊予、日向四国守护，1348年在四条畷之战攻灭楠木正行。观应之扰乱中他背离足利直义归附尊氏。1352年，他在七条大宫附近护卫义诠时战死。

en: Hosokawa Yorisada was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and founder of the Hosokawa Oshu house, the genealogical source of the later Higo Hosokawa. Born at Hosokawa-gō in Mikawa Province, he was by tradition adopted in childhood by his great-grandfather Hosokawa Yoshisue. During the Nakasendai War of July 1335 his son Akiuji's forces were routed. The bedridden Yorisada refused to be a burden: the Taiheiki says he disembowelled himself facing the enemy, while the Baishōron and the Sonpi Bunmyaku place his self-inflicted death at Kawamurayama in Sagami.
zh: 细川赖贞是镰仓时代后期的武士，为细川奥州家之祖，也是延续至后世的肥后细川氏在血统上的祖先。他出身三河国细川乡，相传幼年时被曾祖父细川义季收为养子。1335年7月中先代之乱时，儿子显氏一方兵败退走，卧病的赖贞不愿成为累赘：《太平记》记载他直面敌人切腹而死，《梅松论》与《尊卑分脉》则记载他在相模国河村山自尽。

en: Hosokawa Yoriyuki (1329–1392) was the leading statesman of the early Ashikaga shogunate. The son of Yoriharu, he campaigned in Shikoku and in 1362 destroyed his defected cousin Kiyouji at Sanuki's Shiramine Castle, becoming shugo of Awa, Sanuki and Tosa. In 1367 the dying Yoshiakira named him kanrei to the young Yoshimitsu. He issued sumptuary laws and the 1368 half-tax law protecting court and temple estates, won over Kusunoki Masanori, and set the kanrei office to rotate among the Hosokawa, Shiba and Hatakeyama. Ousted in the 1379 Koryaku coup and pardoned in 1389, he died in Kyoto in 1392.
zh: 细川赖之（1329—1392）是室町幕府初期最重要的政治家，为细川赖春之子。他在四国征战，1362年在赞岐白峰城攻灭叛投南朝的堂兄清氏，身兼阿波、赞岐、土佐三国守护。1367年，临终的足利义诠任命他为管领，辅佐年幼的义满。他颁布俭约令和1368年的半济令（应安大法），保护公家与寺社领地，策反楠木正仪归附幕府，并确立管领由细川、斯波、畠山三家轮任的制度。1379年他在康历政变中被逐，1389年获赦，1392年在京都去世。

en: Hosokawa no Yoshisue was a Kamakura-period gokenin and founder of the Hosokawa clan. The second son of Hirosawa no Yoshizane of the Ashikaga line, he moved from Hirosawa in Yamada district of Kozuke Province to the Hosokawa manor in Nukata district of Mikawa Province and styled himself Hosokawa Jiro. His elder brother Sanekuni founded the Niki clan and his younger brother Yoshimune the Togasaki clan. His grandson Toshiuji, son of his own son Yoshitoshi, became his heir. His tomb lies at Rensho-in Jokyu-ji, said to have been built by his descendant Hosokawa Yoriyuki in 1392.
zh: 细川义季是镰仓时代的御家人，细川氏之祖。他是足利一族广泽义实的次子，从上野国山田郡广泽迁居三河国额田郡细川庄，自称细川二郎；其兄实国开创仁木氏，弟义宗开创户贺崎氏。义季之孙、义俊之子俊氏继承了他。他的墓在莲性院常久寺，传为后裔细川赖之于1392年所建。

en: Hosokawa no Yoshitoshi was a warrior of the Kamakura period (1185-1333) and a son of Yoshisue, founder of the Hosokawa clan of Mikawa Province. Because Yoshisue adopted Yoshitoshi's own sons, including the future heir Toshiuji, historians infer that Yoshitoshi died young, before his father. The Hosokawa were then only minor gokenin in Mikawa. The Enshu and Toichi Hosokawa branches, later shugodai of Tosa Province, descended from his son Muneyoshi.
zh: 细川义俊是镰仓时代（1185—1333）的武士，也是三河国细川氏始祖义季之子。由于义季把义俊的儿子们（包括继承人俊氏）收为养子，史家推断义俊先于父亲早逝。当时细川氏不过是三河国的弱小御家人。后来担任土佐国守护代的细川远州家与十市细川家，均出自义俊之子宗义一脉。

en: Hōjō Hisatoki (1272–1307), also called Akahashi Hisatoki, was a late-Kamakura Hōjō clansman of the Akahashi branch and a son of Hōjō Yoshimune. In 1280 Shikken Tokimune made him shugo of five provinces: Kawachi, Shinano, Hyūga, Kii and Settsu. From 1293 to 1297 he was northern Rokuhara tandai, the shogunate's deputy in Kyoto. Returning to Kamakura, he joined the hyōjōshū council and led the hikitsuke judicial board. He took vows in 1307 and died that year aged 36. His son Moritoki became the last Hōjō shikken, and his daughter Tōshi married Ashikaga Takauji.
zh: 北条久时（1272—1307），又称赤桥久时，是镰仓时代后期北条氏赤桥流的族人、北条义宗之子。1280年，执权北条时宗任命他为河内、信浓、日向、纪伊、摄津五国守护。1293年至1297年，他担任六波罗探题北方，即幕府驻京都的代表。回到镰仓后，他列身评定众，并担任引付头人，参与幕政中枢。1307年他出家，同年去世，年仅36岁。其子守时是末代北条执权，女儿登子嫁给足利尊氏。

en: Hōjō Moritoki (1295–1333), also called Akahashi Moritoki, was the sixteenth and last shikken of the Kamakura shogunate, a son of Hōjō Hisatoki of the Akahashi branch. He took office in 1326 after the Karyaku disturbance, when no other Hōjō clansman would serve, though power lay with the retired tokusō Takatoki and the Nagasaki family. In 1333 his brother-in-law Ashikaga Takauji rebelled and destroyed the Rokuhara tandai. Moritoki then led the vanguard against Nitta Yoshisada's army at the Kobusagoe pass and, overwhelmed, killed himself at Suzaki on 30 June 1333, aged 39. His son Masutoki died with him.
zh: 北条守时（1295—1333），又称赤桥守时，是镰仓幕府第十六代、也是最后一代执权，赤桥流北条久时之子。1326年嘉历骚动之后，北条一族无人愿任执权，他遂出任此职，但实权掌握在出家的得宗北条高时与长崎氏手中。1333年，他的妹夫足利尊氏叛变，攻陷六波罗探题。守时随后担任先锋，在巨福吕坂迎战新田义贞率领的倒幕军，终因寡不敌众，于1333年6月30日在洲崎自刃，时年39岁。其子益时也随他自尽。

en: Hōjō Muneyori (died 1279) was a commander of the mid-Kamakura period and a member of the Hōjō tokusō line, the fourth son of Shikken Tokiyori and a half-brother of Shikken Tokimune. In 1276, with another Mongol attack expected, the shogunate created the post of Nagato tandai to guard the western approaches, and Muneyori was sent to Nagato province as its first holder. He died there in 1279. His son Munekata became Tokimune's adopted son and was later raised to high office under Shikken Sadatoki.
zh: 北条宗赖（？—1279）是镰仓时代中期的武将、北条氏得宗家一族，第五代执权北条时赖的四男、第八代执权北条时宗的异母弟。1276年，为防备蒙古再次来犯，镰仓幕府设立长门探题以守备西部海防，宗赖被派往长门国，成为首任长门探题。他于1279年在长门去世。其子宗方成为时宗的养子，后来在执权北条贞时当政时被提拔到要职。

en: This daughter of Hōjō Muneyori, himself a son of the regent Hōjō Tokiyori, became the second wife of the Mino warlord Toki Yorisada in 1281. Her personal name is not recorded.
zh: 她是镰仓幕府执权北条时赖之子北条宗赖的女儿，于1281年嫁给美浓国武将土岐赖贞为后妻，名字不见记载。

en: Hōjō Nagatoki (1230–1264), also called Akahashi Nagatoki, was the heir of Shigetoki. He grew up in Kyoto and in 1247 succeeded his father as Rokuhara tandai, the bakufu's watchdog at court, later escorting the new shōgun, Prince Munetaka, to Kamakura. In 1256 the tonsured Tokiyori made him the sixth shikken as a caretaker for the young Tokimune, while Tokiyori kept real power. Nagatoki attended to administration until illness forced him to resign and take the tonsure in 1264; he died weeks later aged thirty-five. Twelve of his waka were included in imperial anthologies.
zh: 北条长时（1230—1264），又称赤桥长时，是北条重时的嫡子。他在京都长大，1247年接替父亲出任六波罗探题北方，充当幕府监视朝廷的耳目，后来又护送新任将军宗尊亲王东下镰仓。1256年，出家的时赖为给年幼的时宗铺路，任命他为第六代执权，作为过渡的“眼代”，实权仍操于时赖之手。长时处理政务，1264年因病辞职出家，几周后便去世，年仅三十五岁。他有十二首和歌被敕撰和歌集收录。

en: Hōjō Sadatoki (1272–1311), the ninth shikken of the Kamakura shogunate, was Tokimune's eldest son. He succeeded in 1284 aged twelve. In 1285 the Shimotsuki Disturbance destroyed his mother's Adachi clan and left Taira no Yoritsuna in control; in 1293 Sadatoki had Yoritsuna killed amid the Kamakura earthquake in the Heizenmon purge. He strengthened tokusō rule, created the Chinzei tandai in Kyushu in 1296 and issued the Einin debt-cancellation edict of 1297. He took vows in 1301 and passed the regency to Hōjō Morotoki but kept power until his death. His son was Hōjō Takatoki.
zh: 北条贞时（1272—1311）是镰仓幕府第九代执权，北条时宗的嫡男。1284年他12岁时继任执权。1285年霜月骚动中，其母出身的安达氏遭灭门，平赖纲掌握实权；1293年，贞时趁镰仓大地震之机，在平禅门之乱中诛杀赖纲。此后他强化得宗专制，1296年在九州设立镇西探题，1297年颁布永仁德政令。1301年他出家，把执权之位让给北条师时，但仍在幕后掌权直至去世。其子为北条高时。

en: Hōjō Shigetoki (1198–1261) was the third son of the shikken Yoshitoki. In 1230 he was appointed Rokuhara tandai in Kyoto, overseeing the court and western Japan for seventeen years; the letters his brother Yasutoki sent him while drafting the Goseibai Shikimoku survive. Recalled after the Miura were destroyed in 1247, he became rensho, co-shikken, to his son-in-law Tokiyori and helped stabilize Hōjō rule. He took the tonsure in 1256 and retired to Gokuraku-ji. A devout Pure Land believer, he is also known for warrior house-precepts such as the Rokuhara-dono Gokun. He died in 1261.
zh: 北条重时（1198—1261）是执权义时的第三子。1230年他出任京都六波罗探题北方，十七年间负责监视朝廷、统辖西国；其兄泰时制定《御成败式目》时写给他的书信流传至今。1247年三浦氏灭亡后，他被召回镰仓就任连署，辅佐女婿、第五代执权时赖，稳固了北条氏的统治。1256年他出家，隐居极乐寺。他笃信净土宗，还著有《六波罗殿御家训》等武家家训，1261年去世。

en: Hōjō Takatoki (1304–1333), a son of Sadatoki, was the last Hōjō tokusō and became the fourteenth shikken of the Kamakura shogunate in 1316. The Nagasaki family long dominated the government for him. In 1326 he fell ill, resigned and took vows; the Karyaku succession feud ended with Akahashi Moritoki as shikken while Takatoki stayed supreme. His regime foiled Emperor Go-Daigo's 1324 plot and exiled him to Oki in 1332, but in 1333 Go-Daigo escaped, Ashikaga Takauji defected and Nitta Yoshisada stormed Kamakura. Takatoki killed himself at Tōshō-ji with his clan, ending the Hōjō regime. His son Tokiyuki survived.
zh: 北条高时（1304—1333）是北条贞时之子、北条氏末代得宗，1316年出任镰仓幕府第十四代执权。长崎氏长期替他把持幕政。1326年他因病辞职出家，围绕继任发生的嘉历骚动最终以赤桥守时出任执权收场，而高时仍保有最高权力。其政权于1324年挫败后醍醐天皇的倒幕密谋，1332年将后醍醐天皇流放隐岐岛；但1333年后醍醐逃出隐岐，足利尊氏倒戈，新田义贞攻入镰仓。高时与一族在东胜寺自刃，北条政权灭亡。其子时行幸免于难。

en: Hōjō Tokikata was a Heian-period warrior and local magnate in Izu, of junior fifth rank lower grade and titled Izu no suke. The Sonpi Bunmyaku calls him the father of Hōjō Tokimasa, but other genealogies name Tokiie or Tokikane as the father.
zh: 北条时方是平安时代伊豆国的在地豪族，叙从五位下，任伊豆介。《尊卑分脉》等系图载其为北条时政之父，但《续群书类从》作时家、《妙本寺本》作时兼，时政之父为谁因系图而异。

en: Hōjō Tokimasa (1138–1215) was an Izu magnate who guarded the exiled Minamoto no Yoritomo and gave him his daughter Masako in marriage. He backed Yoritomo's 1180 uprising against the Taira and helped found the Kamakura shogunate. After Yoritomo's death he rose on the council of thirteen, and in 1203 became the first Hōjō shikken, crushing the Hiki family and later Hatakeyama Shigetada. In 1205 his plot to replace Shōgun Sanetomo failed; his children Masako and Yoshitoki forced him to take the tonsure and retire to Izu, where he died in 1215.
zh: 北条时政（1138—1215）是伊豆国豪族，受命看管流放伊豆的源赖朝，并将女儿政子嫁给他。1180年，他支持赖朝举兵讨伐平氏，辅佐建立镰仓幕府。赖朝死后，他借十三人合议制崭露头角，1203年就任镰仓幕府初代执权，先后诛灭比企氏与畠山重忠。1205年，他企图废掉将军实朝，事败；政子与义时迫使他出家，退回伊豆隐居，1215年死于此。

en: Hōjō Tokimune (1251–1284) was the eighth shikken, or regent, of the Kamakura shogunate, born the second son of Shikken Hōjō Tokiyori. He took office in 1268 as Mongol pressure mounted, rejecting Kublai Khan's tributary demands and executing his envoys. In 1271 he banished the monk Nichiren to Sado Island, and in 1272 he crushed the February Disturbance led by his half-brother Tokisuke. He directed the defence that repelled the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281 and built a stone wall around Hakata Bay. A patron of Zen, he founded Engaku-ji in 1282 and died in 1284 aged 34.
zh: 北条时宗（1251—1284）是镰仓幕府第八代执权，五代执权北条时赖的次男。他于1268年就任，时逢蒙古施压，他拒绝忽必烈令日本称臣朝贡的要求，并处死来使。1271年他将僧人日莲流放佐渡岛，1272年镇压异母兄北条时辅发动的二月骚动。他主持防务，在博多湾沿岸修筑石垒，击退1274年和1281年两次蒙古入侵。他崇信禅宗，于1282年创建圆觉寺，1284年去世，年仅34岁。

en: Hōjō Tokiuji (1203–1230) was the eldest son of the shikken Yasutoki. At eighteen he fought in the Jōkyū War of 1221, distinguishing himself by fording the Uji River under court-army fire in the battle that opened Kyoto to the bakufu. In 1224 he was appointed Rokuhara tandai, the shogunate's senior officer in the capital, and became shugo of Wakasa in 1228. A quarrel between his retainer and Enryaku-ji monks in 1229 led to his recall. He died of illness in Kamakura in 1230, aged twenty-eight, before his father; his sons Tsunetoki and Tokiyori both later became shikken.
zh: 北条时氏（1203—1230）是执权泰时的长子。1221年承久之乱时，年仅十八岁的他随父出征，在宇治川之战中冒着朝廷军的箭雨强渡宇治川，立下战功，为幕府军打开入京之路。1224年他就任六波罗探题北方，成为幕府驻京都的最高官员，1228年兼任若狭守护。1229年，其家臣与延历寺僧侣发生冲突，他因此被召还。1230年他在镰仓病逝，年仅二十八岁，先于父亲而亡；其子经时、时赖后来都成为执权。

en: Hōjō Tokiyori (1227–1263), fifth Hōjō shikken, was the second son of Tokiuji, raised by his grandfather Yasutoki. He succeeded his brother Tsunetoki in 1246, crushed the Nagoe plot and sent the former shōgun Yoritsune back to Kyoto, and in 1247 destroyed the Miura clan in the Hōji Battle. In 1249 he created the Hikitsuke courts for vassal lawsuits, and in 1252 replaced Shōgun Yoritsugu with Prince Munetaka, the first imperial prince to hold the office. Tonsured in 1256, he handed the shikken post to Nagatoki but kept real power until his death in 1263.
zh: 北条时赖（1227—1263）是镰仓幕府第五代执权，时氏的次男，由祖父泰时抚养长大。1246年他接替兄长经时就任执权，镇压名越光时拥兵之变（宫骚动），将前将军赖经遣送回京都；1247年在宝治合战中联合外戚安达氏诛灭三浦泰村一族。1249年他新设引付，加快御家人诉讼的审理；1252年废黜将军赖嗣，改立后嵯峨天皇之子宗尊亲王，首开亲王将军之例。1256年他因病出家，把执权之位让给长时，但仍掌握幕府实权，直至1263年去世。

en: Hōjō Tokiyuki (died 1353), second son of Hōjō Takatoki, the last Kamakura tokusō, led the Hōjō attempt to restore the fallen shogunate. He escaped Kamakura's fall in 1333 with Suwa retainers, and in 1335 the Suwa placed the boy at the head of a rising called the Nakasendai War. His army defeated Ashikaga Tadayoshi and retook Kamakura in a month, only to be driven out within twenty days by Ashikaga Takauji. Pardoned by Emperor Go-Daigo, he served the Southern Court, retook Kamakura with Kitabatake Akiie in 1337 and again in 1352, and was captured and executed at Tatsunokuchi in 1353.
zh: 北条时行（？—1353）是镰仓幕府末代得宗北条高时的次子，力图复兴灭亡的幕府。1333年镰仓失陷时，他靠诹访氏家臣救出；1335年，诹访氏奉年幼的他为首举兵，即“中先代之乱”。大军击败足利直义，仅一个月便夺回镰仓，但不出二十天又被足利尊氏逐走。后醍醐天皇赦免其朝敌之罪，他遂为南朝效力，1337年与北畠显家再度夺回镰仓，1352年又一次收复镰仓；翌年被捕，在龙口被处死。

en: Hōjō Yasutoki (1183–1242), third Hōjō shikken, was Yoshitoki's eldest son. He fought the Wada in 1213 and in 1221 commanded the bakufu army that won the Jōkyū War, forcing the Uji River and taking Kyoto. He succeeded as shikken in 1224 and set up a council government of Hyōjōshū. In 1232 he enacted the Goseibai Shikimoku, Japan's first warrior law code, fifty-one articles based on samurai custom. In 1242 he forced through the enthronement of Emperor Go-Saga, and died later that year aged sixty.
zh: 北条泰时（1183—1242）是镰仓幕府第三代执权，义时的长子。1213年他随父讨灭和田义盛；1221年承久之乱中任幕府军总大将，强渡宇治川，攻占京都。1224年他继任执权，建立以评定众为核心的合议政治。1232年，他颁布由五十一条组成的《御成败式目》，这是日本第一部依据武士习惯制定的武家法典。1242年，他排除众议拥立后嵯峨天皇，同年病逝，享年六十岁。

en: Hōjō Yoshimune (1253–1277), also called Akahashi Yoshimune, was a Hōjō clansman of the Kamakura period and the eldest son of Nagatoki, the sixth shikken. As second head of the Akahashi branch, he was appointed northern Rokuhara tandai, the shogunate's deputy in Kyoto, in 1271. On Shikken Tokimune's orders, he led the troops that hunted down and killed Tokimune's half-brother Hōjō Tokisuke during the February Disturbance of 1272. Recalled to Kamakura in 1276, he joined the hyōjōshū council in 1277 but died the same year, aged 25. His son was Hōjō Hisatoki.
zh: 北条义宗（1253—1277），又称赤桥义宗，是镰仓时代的北条氏族人、第六代执权北条长时的嫡男，赤桥流第二代当主。1271年他就任六波罗探题北方，即幕府驻京都的代表。1272年，他奉执权北条时宗之命，在二月骚动中追讨并诛杀了时宗的异母兄北条时辅。1276年他返回镰仓，1277年出任评定众，同年去世，年仅25岁。其子为北条久时。

en: Hōjō Yoshitoki (1163–1224), second Hōjō shikken, was a son of Tokimasa and younger brother of Masako. He fought in Yoritomo's 1180 uprising and the Taira wars. In 1203 he helped destroy the Hiki clan and enthrone Sanetomo; in 1205 he and Masako ousted their father, making Yoshitoki the shogunate's strongest man. After Sanetomo's assassination in 1219 he ruled outright. When Retired Emperor Go-Toba ordered his overthrow in 1221, bakufu forces took Kyoto in the Jōkyū War and exiled three retired emperors. Yoshitoki died suddenly in 1224.
zh: 北条义时（1163—1224）是镰仓幕府第二代执权，时政之子、政子之弟。他参与1180年源赖朝举兵及讨伐平氏的战事。1203年，他协助诛灭比企氏，拥立实朝为将军；1205年与政子合力放逐父亲时政，成为幕府头号实权者。1219年实朝遇刺后，他总揽幕政。1221年后鸟羽上皇颁下追讨义时的宣旨，幕府军在承久之乱中攻占京都，流放三位上皇。1224年，义时突然去世。

en: Emperor Ichijō (980–1011), personal name Kanehito, was the only son of Emperor En'yū and the sixty-sixth sovereign of Japan. After Emperor Kazan's abdication he ascended in 986 at age six, with Fujiwara no Kaneie and then Michitaka serving as regent; from 995 Michinaga held power through the office of nairan. His reign marked the apex of Fujiwara power and Heian court culture: his empresses Teishi and Michinaga's daughter Shōshi kept salons served by Sei Shōnagon and Murasaki Shikibu. A lover of letters, music and the flute, he abdicated in 1011 and died days later. His sons Atsunari and Atsunaga both became emperors.
zh: 一条天皇（980—1011）名怀仁，是圆融天皇的独子、日本第六十六代天皇。花山天皇退位后，他于986年六岁即位，先后由藤原兼家和藤原道隆担任摄政；995年起，道长以内览掌握朝政。他的治世是藤原氏权势与平安朝宫廷文化的顶峰：皇后定子与道长之女彰子各自开有文化沙龙，清少纳言与紫式部分别侍奉左右。一条天皇雅好文学、音乐与笛艺，1011年退位，数日后去世。其子敦成、敦良后来都登上了皇位。

en: Ii Kagenao was the tenth recorded head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, the son of Ii Yukinao. The clan genealogies name him between Yukinao and the next head, Ii Tadanao.
zh: 井伊景直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏第十代当主，井伊行直之子。井伊氏系谱把他列在行直与下一代当主井伊忠直之间。

en: Ii Korenao was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, counted as its fourth head in the official Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden genealogy. He was a son of Ii Tomonao and father of Ii Morinao, the fifth head.
zh: 井伊惟直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主，《宽永诸家系图传》的官方代数列为第四代。他是井伊共直之子，其子井伊盛直为第五代当主。

en: Ii Morinao was the fifth recorded head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, the son of Ii Korenao. The clan genealogies preserved in the Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden name him between Korenao and the sixth head, Ii Yoshinao.
zh: 井伊盛直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏第五代当主，井伊惟直之子。《宽永诸家系图传》所存井伊氏系谱把他列在惟直与第六代当主井伊良直之间。

en: Ii Munetsuna was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, named in the clan genealogies between his father Ii Tomomune and his son Ii Tomoaki, who succeeded him as head.
zh: 井伊宗纲是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主。井伊氏系谱把他列在父亲井伊共宗与继任当主的儿子井伊共章之间。

en: Ii Tomoaki was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, named in the clan genealogies between his father Ii Munetsuna and his son Ii Tomoie, who succeeded him as head.
zh: 井伊共章是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主。井伊氏系谱把他列在父亲井伊宗纲与继任当主的儿子井伊共家之间。

en: Ii Tomoie was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province. The official Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden genealogy counts him as the clan's second head, after the founder Tomoyasu; his son Ii Tomonao succeeded him.
zh: 井伊共家是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主。井伊家官方采用的《宽永诸家系图传》把他列为继初代共保之后的第二代当主，其子井伊共直继任。

en: Ii Tomomune was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, the son of the clan founder Ii Tomoyasu. The clan genealogies name him as the father of Ii Munetsuna, who followed him as head.
zh: 井伊共宗是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主，初代当主井伊共保之子。井伊氏系谱载其子为井伊宗纲，宗纲后继任当主。

en: Ii Tomonao was an early head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, counted as its third head in the official Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden genealogy. He was a son of Ii Tomoie and father of Ii Korenao, who succeeded him.
zh: 井伊共直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的早期当主，《宽永诸家系图传》的官方代数列为第三代。他是井伊共家之子，其子井伊惟直继任当主。

en: Ii Tomoyasu (1010–1093) was the founder and first head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province. Clan tradition relates that on New Year's Day 1010 the priest of the Iinoya Hachiman shrine found an abandoned baby boy beside a sacred well; the child proved so precocious that at the age of seven he was adopted by Fujiwara no Tomosuke, governor of Tōtōmi, whose daughter he married. In 1032 he succeeded to the estate, built his residence at Iinoya, and took the name Ii. He died in 1093 aged eighty-four and was buried at Jizō-ji, the present Ryūtan-ji.
zh: 井伊共保（1010—1093）是远江国井伊谷井伊氏的初代当主。相传1010年正月元旦，井伊谷八幡宫神主在御手洗井旁发现一名弃婴；这孩子天资聪颖，七岁时被远江国司藤原共资收为养子，并娶共资之女为妻。1032年，他继承家业，在井伊谷修筑居馆，号称井伊氏。1093年去世，终年84岁，葬于八幡山地藏寺，即今龙潭寺。

en: Ii Yanao was the seventh recorded head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, the son of Ii Yoshinao. The clan genealogies preserved in the Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden name him between Yoshinao and the eighth head, Ii Yasunao.
zh: 井伊弥直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏第七代当主，井伊良直之子。《宽永诸家系图传》所存井伊氏系谱把他列在良直与第八代当主井伊泰直之间。

en: Ii Yasunao was the eighth recorded head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province and its castellan in the early fourteenth century. Genealogies name him between Ii Yanao and his son, the ninth head Ii Yukinao.
zh: 井伊泰直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏第八代当主，14世纪前期的井伊氏城主。井伊氏系谱把他列在井伊弥直与他的儿子、第九代当主井伊行直之间。

en: Ii Yoshinao was the sixth recorded head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province, the son of Ii Morinao. The clan genealogies preserved in the Kan'ei Shoka Keizuden name him between Morinao and the seventh head, Ii Yanao.
zh: 井伊良直是远江国井伊谷井伊氏第六代当主，井伊盛直之子。《宽永诸家系图传》所存井伊氏系谱把他列在盛直与第七代当主井伊弥直之间。

en: Ii Yukinao was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period, the ninth head of the Ii clan of Iinoya in Tōtōmi Province and a son of Ii Yasunao. He took the Southern Court side and welcomed Emperor Go-Daigo's son Prince Muneyoshi into his stronghold of Mitsutake Castle. In July 1337 he fought the Northern Court commander Imagawa Norikuni at Mikatagahara and afterward repulsed an assault on Mitsutake. In 1339 and 1340 Kō no Moroyasu and Niki Yoshinaga captured his satellite castles; Mitsutake fell in January 1340 and Ōhira in August, when he surrendered.
zh: 井伊行直是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，远江国井伊谷井伊氏第九代当主，井伊泰直之子。他站在南朝一边，将后醍醐天皇之子宗良亲王迎入本城三岳城。1337年7月，他在三方原与北朝武将今川范国交战，随后击退今川军对三岳城的进攻。1339至1340年，高师泰、仁木义长等北朝军队逐一攻陷其支城，1340年1月三岳城失守，8月大平城陷落，行直遂降。

en: Ijūin Hisachika was an early head of the Ijūin clan of Satsuma, a branch of the Shimazu holding Ijūin in Hioki District. The clan genealogy places him between his father Hisakane, said to be the first to bear the Ijūin name, and his son Tadachika.
zh: 伊集院久亲是萨摩岛津氏支流伊集院氏的早期当主，领有日置郡伊集院。家谱把他列在父亲久兼与儿子忠亲之间；相传久兼是最早以伊集院为姓的人。

en: Ijūin Hisakane (dates unknown) succeeded his father Toshitada as second head of the Ijūin family of Satsuma. He was the first to use the name Ijūin, and late in the thirteenth century moved to Shiroyama in Ijūin. His son Hisachika followed him.
zh: 伊集院久兼（生卒年不详）继其父俊忠之后成为萨摩伊集院氏二代当主。他是这一支中最先使用“伊集院”名号者，13世纪末迁居伊集院的城山。其子久亲继为三代当主。

en: Ijūin Tadachika was the fourth head of the Ijūin clan of Satsuma, a branch of the Shimazu. The clan genealogy makes him the son of Hisachika and the father of Tadakuni, who in 1337 rose for the Southern Court at Ichiuji Castle.
zh: 伊集院忠亲是萨摩岛津氏支流伊集院氏的第四代当主。按家谱，他是久亲之子、忠国之父；忠国后来于1337年据一宇治城举兵，投奔南朝。

en: Ijūin Tadakuni (fl. 1337–1351), son of Tadachika, was a Satsuma warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars and fifth head of the Ijūin clan, a Shimazu branch. He at first served the Northern Court with Shimazu Sadahisa, but in 1337, after the Southern Court envoy Sanjō Yasusue reached Satsuma, he alone of the Shimazu kindred rose for the South at Ichiuji Castle. For years he warred with the main Shimazu house across Satsuma and Ōsumi, taking Matsuo Castle in Kōriyama in 1350. Later reconciling with the clan, he married his daughter to Shimazu Ujihisa and was posthumously granted Junior Third Rank in the Meiji era.
zh: 伊集院忠国（活跃于1337—1351年）是南北朝时代的萨摩武将，岛津氏支流伊集院氏的第五代当主，忠亲之子。他起初随岛津贞久从属北朝，1337年南朝先遣三条泰季抵达萨摩后，他在岛津一族中唯一据一宇治城举兵投奔南朝。此后数年，他在萨摩、大隅与宗家交战，1350年攻下郡山松尾城。后来他与宗家和解，女儿嫁给岛津氏久；明治时追赠从三位。

en: Ijūin Toshitada (dates unknown) was a Satsuma warrior of the mid-Kamakura period and first head of the Ijūin family. A son of Shimazu Tadatsune, he won the Ijūin jitō post and settled there; his son Hisakane first used the Ijūin name.
zh: 伊集院俊忠（生卒年不详）是镰仓时代中期的萨摩武士、伊集院氏初代当主。他是岛津忠经之子，得到伊集院地头职后移住当地，其子久兼最早以“伊集院”为氏。

en: Ikeda no Kagemasa appears in the Ikeda clan genealogy as the son of Ikeda no Yasutada and father of Ikeda no Noriyori.
zh: 池田景正见载于池田氏系图，是池田泰忠之子、池田教依之父。

en: Ikeda Kimisada (dates unknown) was an early head of the Settsu-Ikeda family and father of Yasusada. Tradition traced the clan to Ikeda village in Izumi, from which it opened estates in Settsu and Mino as estate stewards.
zh: 池田公贞（生卒年不详）是摄津池田氏的早期当主、泰贞之父。相传该氏出自和泉国池田村，先祖以庄官身份赴摄津、美浓两地开拓庄园。

en: Ikeda no Koremochi appears in the Settsu Ikeda genealogy as the son of Ikeda no Korezane and father of Ikeda no Koresada.
zh: 池田维望见载于摄津池田氏系图，是池田维实之子、池田维贞之父。

en: Ikeda no Koresada appears in the Settsu Ikeda genealogy as the son of Ikeda no Koremochi and father of Ikeda no Kimisada.
zh: 池田维贞见载于摄津池田氏系图，是池田维望之子、池田公贞（君贞）之父。

en: The Settsu Ikeda genealogy names Ikeda no Korezane as the second son of the Heian noble, Confucian scholar and poet Ki no Yoshimochi, who died in 919, and of a daughter of the local magnate Ikeda no Koremasa. As steward of the Ikeda manor in Settsu Province, Koremasa granted the estate to Korezane, who thereupon took the Ikeda name. He is counted the ancestor of the Ki line of the Settsu Ikeda clan.
zh: 据摄津池田氏系图，池田维实是平安时代贵族、儒者与歌人纪淑望（919年卒）的次子，母亲为摄津当地豪族池田维将之女。维将身任池田庄庄官，将这座庄园传给维实，维实遂以池田为氏，被奉为摄津池田氏纪氏流的先祖。

en: Ikeda no Noriyori was a local magnate of the Teshima district of Settsu Province who, around 1334, built Ikeda Castle at the foot of Mount Satsuki, which his descendants held for generations. The clan genealogy calls him a ninth-generation descendant of the Minamoto warrior Yasumasa. He married a daughter of Naito Mitsuyuki, who had first been the wife of Kusunoki Masatsura; when Masatsura fell in battle in 1348, she wed Noriyori, which later gave rise to a claim that her son Norimasa was fathered by Masatsura.
zh: 池田教依是摄津国丰岛郡的土著豪族，约于1334年在五月山南麓修筑池田城，此后世代为池田氏城主。池田氏系图称他是源氏武士源泰政的九世孙。他娶内藤满之之女为妻，此女先前已嫁楠木正行；1348年正行战死后她改嫁教依，后来因此产生教依之子教正实为正行之子的说法。

en: Edo-period genealogies name Ikeda Norimasa, a Settsu Ikeda warrior, as the son of Ikeda Noriyori and a daughter of Naitō Mitsuyuki. His mother remarried after her first husband Kusunoki Masatsura died in battle; tradition held that Norimasa was Masatsura's son.
zh: 《藩翰谱》等江户时代家谱记载，池田教正是摄津池田氏武将，为池田教依与内藤满之之女所生；因其母先嫁楠木正行、正行战死后方才改嫁，相传教正实为正行之子。

en: Ikeda Yasumasa, also called Minamoto no Yasumasa, was a younger brother of Minamoto no Yorimasa who was adopted into the Settsu-Ikeda family around the time of the Genpei War; his son was Yasumitsu.
zh: 池田泰政，一称源泰政，是源赖政之弟，约在源平合战时期入嗣摄津池田家，其子为泰光。

en: Ikeda Yasumitsu (dates unknown), son of Ikeda Yasumasa, was a Settsu warrior who was said to have divided the clan lands: Teshima district in Settsu passed to Tokikage and Ikeda district in Mino to Yasutsugu, ancestor of the Mino-Ikeda line.
zh: 池田泰光（生卒年不详）是摄津武将、池田泰政之子。相传他把领地分作两支：摄津丰岛郡归时景，美浓池田郡归泰继，后者即美浓池田氏之祖。

en: Ikeda no Yasunaga appears in the Settsu Ikeda genealogy as the son of Ikeda no Yasumitsu and father of Ikeda no Yasutsugu, founder of the Mino branch.
zh: 池田泰永见载于摄津池田氏系图，是池田泰光之子、美浓池田氏之祖池田泰继之父。

en: Ikeda Yasusada (dates unknown) belonged to the Settsu-Ikeda family and was listed between Ikeda Kimisada and Ikeda Yasumasa in its line.
zh: 池田泰贞（生卒年不详）出自摄津池田氏，在该家族的世系列表中列于池田公贞与池田泰政之间。

en: Ikeda no Yasutada appears in the Ikeda clan genealogy as the son of Ikeda no Yasutsugu, founder of the Mino branch, and father of Ikeda no Kagemasa.
zh: 池田泰忠见载于池田氏系图，是美浓池田氏之祖池田泰继之子、池田景正之父。

en: Ikeda no Yasutsugu was a warrior of the Settsu Ikeda clan and, in the clan genealogy, a son of Ikeda no Yasunaga and grandson of Ikeda no Yasumitsu. After the Genpei War, Yasumitsu placed him in charge of the Ikeda district of Mino Province, where Yasutsugu founded the Mino branch of the Ikeda. By the Kenmu Restoration of 1334 the district had become the direct holding of the Toki shugo, whom the Mino Ikedas then served. One tradition derives the early-modern daimyo Ikeda house from his line.
zh: 池田泰继是摄津池田氏的武士，据池田氏系图为池田泰永之子、池田泰光之孙。源平合战后，泰光让他领有美浓国池田郡，泰继由此开创美浓池田氏。到1334年建武新政时，池田郡已成为美浓守护土岐氏的直辖领，美浓池田氏此后从属土岐氏。也有说法称近世大名池田家出自他这一脉。

en: Imagawa Kuniuji (1243–1282) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the founder of the Imagawa clan. The second son of Kira Osauji and grandson of Ashikaga Yoshiuji, he inherited Imagawa Manor in Hazu District, Mikawa Province, served as its land steward, and took the name Imagawa from the estate. In his day the family ruled little more than three villages, and few records of his deeds survive. He took Buddhist vows in 1281 and died in 1282, aged about forty. His eldest son Motouji succeeded him.
zh: 今川国氏（1243—1282）是镰仓时代武将，今川氏的初代当主。他是吉良长氏的次子、足利义氏之孙，领有三河国幡豆郡今川庄并担任地头，以庄园之名首次自称今川。在他的时代，今川家不过是管辖三个村庄的小领主，其事迹存世记载很少。他于1281年出家，1282年去世，享年约40岁，由长子基氏继承家督。

en: The unnamed daughter of Imagawa Kuniuji became the wife of Isshiki Kimifuka, the Kamakura-period warrior who founded the Isshiki clan. Genealogies record her as the mother of his sons Isshiki Yoriyuki and Isshiki Noriuji.
zh: 今川国氏的女儿，名字不传，嫁给镰仓时代武士、一色氏初代当主一色公深。家谱记载她是一色赖行、一色范氏兄弟的生母。

en: Imagawa Motouji (1259–1323) was the second head of the Imagawa clan and the heir of its founder Kuniuji. He inherited Imagawa Manor in Mikawa Province and later settled at Hikuma Manor in Tōtōmi. Genealogies credit Kuniuji with receiving Hikuma from the shogun Prince Koreyasu for service in the Shimotsuki Disturbance of 1285, but Kuniuji had died before it; the recipient has therefore been identified as Motouji. The move to Tōtōmi opened the way for the clan's later rise as shugo lords of Suruga and Tōtōmi. He died in 1323 aged sixty-three, and his youngest son Norikuni succeeded him.
zh: 今川基氏（1259—1323）是今川氏第二代当主，今川家初代国氏的嫡子。他继承三河国今川庄，后来迁居远江国引间庄。谱牒记载国氏因1285年霜月骚动中的战功，获将军惟康亲王赐予引间庄；但国氏在骚动前已去世，故有说法推定受赏者是基氏。迁居远江为今川家日后成为骏河、远江两国守护大名打开了道路。他于1323年去世，享年63岁，由末子范国继承。

en: Imagawa Nakaaki (fl. 1368–1412), first named Kuniyasu and later Yoriyasu, was a son of Imagawa Norikuni adopted by his elder brother Imagawa Sadayo. In 1368 he became head of the Board of Retainers and constable of Yamashiro. From 1371 he fought under Sadayo in Kyūshū against the Southern Court, defeating Kikuchi Takemasa in Hizen in 1372, helping take Dazaifu, and killing Shōni Fuyusuke at the Mizushima incident of 1375. Appointed constable of Tōtōmi in 1388 and Owari in 1393, he took Buddhist vows in 1395. In 1412 Sadayo gave him the house code called the Imagawa-jō.
zh: 今川仲秋（活动于1368—1412年），初名国泰、后改赖泰，是今川范国之子，被次兄今川贞世收为养子。1368年他出任侍所头人兼山城守护。1371年起随贞世在九州与南朝作战，1372年在肥前击败菊池武政，并参与攻占大宰府；1375年水岛之变中，由他下手诛杀了筑前守护少贰冬资。1388年他受任远江守护，1393年任尾张守护，1395年出家。1412年，贞世将家训《今川状》传授给他。

en: Imagawa Norikuni (1295–1384) was a Nanboku-chō shugo daimyō and the first head of the Suruga Imagawa clan, the fifth son of Imagawa Motouji. After the Kamakura shogunate fell he joined Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1336 received the shugo posts of Tōtōmi and then Suruga; he was reappointed to Tōtōmi in 1352. In 1353 he retired, passing the headship to his son Noriuji, though he later served the Muromachi shogunate as head of the Board of Adjudications. A master of waka and court precedent, he also guided Ashikaga ceremonial.
zh: 今川范国（1295—1384）是南北朝时代的守护大名，骏河今川氏的初代当主，今川基氏第五子。镰仓幕府灭亡后，他追随足利尊氏转战各地，1336年先后获得远江守护与骏河守护之职，1352年重任远江守护。1353年，他把家督让给嫡子范氏后隐居，后来又应尊氏之请出任室町幕府引付头人。他精通和歌与有职故实，还曾指导足利将军家的典礼，1384年去世。

en: Imagawa Noriuji (c. 1316–1365) was the second head of the Suruga Imagawa clan and a Nanboku-chō shugo daimyō. In 1353 he inherited the family headship and the shugo posts of Suruga and Tōtōmi from his father Norikuni, but remained overshadowed by his still-active father and his gifted younger brother Sadayo. He died in the fourth month of 1365, aged fifty. His eldest son Ujiie was formally named shugo by Ashikaga Yoshiakira on October 9 that year but soon died, whereupon his second son Yasunori left holy orders to succeed him.
zh: 今川范氏（约1316—1365）是骏河今川氏第二代当主、南北朝时代的守护大名。1353年，他从父亲范国手中接管家督以及骏河、远江的守护之职，但因父亲健在、弟弟贞世更具将才，存在感一直淡薄。1365年4月他去世，享年50岁。同年10月9日，足利义诠正式任命其长男氏家为守护，氏家不久后死去，曾为僧人的次男泰范于是还俗继任。

en: Imagawa Sadayo (1326–1420), known in religion as Ryōshun, was a son of Imagawa Norikuni, constable of Suruga and Tōtōmi. A poet of the Kyōgoku and Reizei schools, he had taken Buddhist vows when the Ashikaga bakufu named him tandai of Kyūshū in 1371 to crush Prince Kaneyoshi's Southern Court revolt. He secured northern Kyūshū by 1375 and campaigned against the wokou, returning captives to Korea in 1377. Recalled in 1395 on suspicion of disloyalty and stripped of his posts in 1400, he spent his last years on religion and poetry until his death in 1420.
zh: 今川贞世（1326—1420），法号了俊，是骏河、远江两国守护今川范国之子。他身为京极派与冷泉派歌人，已出家受戒；1371年室町幕府任命他为九州探题，前往镇压怀良亲王的南朝势力，至1375年平定北九州。他还进剿倭寇，于1377年将被掳人口送还高丽。1395年他因涉嫌不忠被召回，1400年遭夺官职，晚年潜心佛法与和歌，直至1420年去世。

en: Imagawa Ujiie (born before 1334, died c. 1369) was a mid-fourteenth-century constable of Suruga, the eldest son of Imagawa Noriuji and elder brother of Imagawa Yasunori. When his father died in the fifth month of 1365, his grandfather Norikuni sought to pass the constableship to Sadayo, but Sadayo declined, and that tenth month the shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiakira confirmed Ujiie in the post; in 1366 he received full judicial powers over the province. In the tenth month of 1366 he attended Sadayo's monthly poetry gathering. He died without issue before the fifth month of 1369, when Yasunori already held the post.
zh: 今川氏家（生于1334年以前，约1369年去世）是14世纪中期的骏河守护，今川范氏长子、今川泰范之兄。1365年五月父亲范氏去世后，祖父范国本想让贞世继任守护，因贞世推辞，同年十月由二代将军足利义诠任命氏家为骏河守护，1366年又获准执掌该国检断权。1366年十月，他参加了贞世的月次和歌会。氏家没有子嗣，于1369年五月以前去世，届时泰范已经继任守护之职。

en: Imagawa Ujikane (c. 1329–c. 1398), later called Naoyo, was the third son of Imagawa Norikuni and a younger brother of Imagawa Sadayo. In 1338 he was granted old family lands in Hazu District of Mikawa Province. In 1370 he served under the kanrei Hosokawa Yoriyuki in Kawachi, was rewarded with the Yamanashi manor in Tōtōmi, and was appointed deputy constable of Echigo. He then joined Sadayo's Kyūshū campaign against the Southern Court's Kikuchi forces, returning to Kyoto in 1374. He took the name Naoyo in 1396 and died around 1398 at Kambara, ancestor of the Kambara clan.
zh: 今川氏兼（约1329—约1398），后改名直世，是今川范国第三子、今川贞世之弟。1338年，他受封三河国幡豆郡的今川家旧领。1370年，他随管领细川赖之出征河内立功，获赐远江山梨乡，并被任命为越后守护代。此后他随兄长贞世前往九州，与南朝方的菊池势力作战，1374年返回京都。1396年他改名直世，约1398年在蒲原去世，为蒲原氏之祖。

en: Imagawa Yasunori (1334–1409), third head of the Suruga Imagawa, was second son of Imagawa Noriuji and brother of Imagawa Ujiie. A novice monk at Kamakura's Kenchō-ji, he returned to secular life at his uncle Sadayo's order and inherited the family after his father died in 1365 and his brother died later. In 1378 Shōgun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu made him head of the Board of Retainers, fighting for the bakufu in the Meitoku War (1391) and Ōei War (1399). He took Buddhist vows in 1395 and from 1400 held Suruga and Tōtōmi. He died in 1409, succeeded by his son Norimasa.
zh: 今川泰范（1334—1409）是骏河今川氏第三代当主，今川范氏次子、今川氏家之弟。他本在镰仓建长寺出家为僧，父亲于1365年去世，兄长此后去世，他遂奉叔父今川贞世之命还俗，继承家督。1378年，三代将军足利义满任命他为侍所头人；他在1391年明德之乱和1399年应永之乱中均加入幕府军立功。1395年他随义满出家，1400年起领有骏河、远江两国。1409年去世，由嫡子今川范政继任。

en: Moriyasu Inawashiro was a head of the Inawashiro, a Kamakura-period warrior house based at Inawashiro in Yama District, Mutsu Province. Its genealogy records him between his father Tsuneyasu and his son Muneyasu.
zh: 猪苗代盛泰是镰仓时代的武士、猪苗代氏当主，本领在陆奥国耶麻郡猪苗代，家谱将他列在父亲经泰与儿子宗泰之间。

en: Muneyasu Inawashiro was a head of the Inawashiro, a warrior house of the Kamakura period based at Inawashiro in Yama District, Mutsu Province. The clan traced its line to the Miura through the Ashina, and its genealogy records Muneyasu as the successor of Moriyasu.
zh: 猪苗代宗泰是镰仓时代的武士、猪苗代氏当主，本领在陆奥国耶麻郡猪苗代。其家出自三浦氏、为芦名氏支流，家谱记载他继盛泰之后统领一族。

en: Tsunetsura Inawashiro was an early Kamakura-period warrior who founded the Inawashiro house of Aizu. The eldest son of Moritsura Sahara, of a warrior line claiming Kanmu Heike and Miura descent, he is said to have held Inawashiro in the Yama district after his grandfather Yoshitsura Sahara was enfeoffed with the four Aizu districts for his part in the Ōshū campaign of 1189. Local records place his fort at Yadeyama, later called Kamega-jō, in 1191; the Date family genealogy instead says that in 1248, while serving Shogun Fujiwara no Yoritsugu, he received the five-thousand-chō Asaya estate and took the name Inawashiro.
zh: 猪苗代经连是镰仓时代前期武将，会津猪苗代氏的始祖，佐原盛连的长子，家族出自桓武平氏三浦氏一脉。相传其祖父佐原义连因1189年奥州合战的军功获赐会津四郡，经连遂领有耶麻郡猪苗代之地。《会津温故拾要抄》等地方志称他于1191年在当地修筑八手山馆，即后来的龟城；《伊达世臣家谱》则记载，他在1248年三月出仕征夷大将军藤原赖嗣，获赐会津猪苗代麻谷庄五千余町，这才改称猪苗代氏。

en: Tsuneyasu Inawashiro was the second head of the Inawashiro warrior clan of Yama district in Mutsu, the son of Tsunetsura Inawashiro who founded the house, and the father of Moriyasu, who carried on the line.
zh: 猪苗代经泰是陆奥国耶麻郡猪苗代武士家族的第二代当主，猪苗代氏始祖经连之子，继承家名的盛泰是他的儿子。

en: Irie no Kagekane was a Heian-period warrior of the Irie clan of Suruga Province, a son of Kiyosada and grandfather of Kikkawa Tsuneyoshi, the first head of the line to take the name Kikkawa.
zh: 入江景兼是骏河国入江氏的平安时代武士，为清定之子、吉川经义之祖父；经义是这一家系中首称吉川氏的当主。

en: Irie no Kageyoshi was a late-Heian warrior of the Irie clan in Suruga Province, the son of Kagekane. His son Tsuneyoshi, after receiving Kikkawa Manor from Minamoto no Yoritomo in 1183, took the name Kikkawa and founded the clan.
zh: 入江景义是骏河国入江氏的平安时代末期武士，景兼之子。其子经义于1183年从源赖朝处受封吉河庄，遂以吉川为姓，成为吉川氏之祖。

en: Irie no Kiyosada was a Heian-period warrior of Suruga Province, the son of Irie no Korekiyo, founder of the Irie clan. His son Kiyozane established the Kambara branch of the family at Kambara Manor in Ihara District.
zh: 入江清定是骏河国平安时代的武士，入江氏始祖入江维清之子。其子清实另立蒲原氏一支，以庵原郡蒲原庄为据点。

en: Irie no Korekiyo was a son of Kudō no Tokinobu and the father of Irie no Kiyofusa and Irie no Kiyosada.
zh: 入江维清是工藤时信之子，入江清房与入江清定之父。

en: Isa Muneyuki was a member of the Isa family of Isa District in Hitachi Province, placed in its line of succession between Isa Tametsuna and Isa Yukikata.
zh: 伊佐宗行是常陆国伊佐郡伊佐氏的一员，家族传承顺序中位于伊佐为纲与伊佐行方之间。

en: Isa Tamemune was an early Kamakura-period warrior of Hitachi Province and the eldest son of Date Tomomune, the monk called Hitachi Nyūdō Nensai. In 1189 he and his brothers joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's Ōshū campaign against Fujiwara no Yasuhira; at the battle of Ishinazaka he stormed the enemy stronghold and took the head of Satō Motoharu with seventeen others. The feat won his family the district of Date, where his kinsmen founded the Date clan while Tamemune kept the ancestral Isa estate. In 1221 he was killed fighting for the shogunate at the Uji River in the Jōkyū War.
zh: 伊佐为宗是镰仓时代初期常陆国的御家人，伊达朝宗（出家后称常陆入道念西）的长子。1189年，他与诸弟随源赖朝参加讨伐藤原泰衡的奥州合战，在石那坂之战中攻破敌军城寨，斩下佐藤基治等18人的首级。凭此战功，其家族获封伊达郡，族人在彼地开创伊达氏，为宗则留在本领伊佐郡。1221年承久之乱中，他追随北条泰时与上皇一方作战，在宇治川战死。

en: Isa Tametsuna was a warrior of Isa District in Hitachi Province and the son of Isa Tamemune, who fell at the Uji River in 1221; the Isa line continued after Tametsuna with Muneyuki, Yukikata and Tokikata.
zh: 伊佐为纲是常陆国伊佐郡的武士，伊佐为宗之子；其父于1221年在宇治川战死，为纲之后伊佐家依次传至宗行、行方和时方。

en: Isa Tokikata was a warrior of the Isa clan of Isa District in Hitachi Province, a clan regarded as an ancestral line of the Date clan. Genealogies record him as the son of Isa Yukikata, in the succession Tsuneyuki, Yukikata, Tokikata.
zh: 伊佐时方是常陆国伊佐郡伊佐氏的武将，该族被视为伊达氏的祖家。家谱记载他是伊佐行方之子，宗行、行方、时方一脉相承。

en: Isa Yukikata was a member of the Isa family of Isa District in Hitachi Province, placed in its line of succession between Isa Muneyuki and Isa Tokikata.
zh: 伊佐行方是常陆国伊佐郡伊佐氏的一员，家族传承顺序中位于伊佐宗行与伊佐时方之间。

en: Ise Moritsugu was a warrior of the late Kamakura period, son of Ise Toshitsugu, who first took the name Ise. He was the father of Ise Sadatsugu, who served three Ashikaga shoguns and became the shogunate's Mandokoro shitsuji in 1379.
zh: 伊势盛继是镰仓时代末期的武将，伊势氏初代伊势俊继之子。他是伊势贞继的父亲；贞继先后侍奉三代足利将军，于1379年出任室町幕府政所执事。

en: Ise Moritsune was a younger brother of Ise Sadatsugu, the long-serving Mandokoro shitsuji of the Ashikaga shogunate. His descendants formed the Bitchū-Ise branch line, which supplied the shoguns with palace attendants and mōshitsugi ushers.
zh: 伊势盛经是室町幕府政所执事伊势贞继的弟弟。他的后裔形成备中伊势氏一支，世代为将军家出仕近习和申次众。

en: Ise Sadanobu was a son of Ise Sadatsugu, the long-serving Mandokoro shitsuji of the Ashikaga shogunate, and the father of Ise Sadayuki. He never held the shitsuji post himself: after Sadatsugu died in 1391, Sadanobu's son Sadayuki was appointed to succeed him.
zh: 伊势贞信是室町幕府政所执事伊势贞继之子，伊势贞行之父。他本人未曾担任执事：1391年贞继去世后，由贞信之子贞行接任政所执事。

en: Ise Sadatsugu was a warrior of the Kamakura and Muromachi periods who served the Ashikaga shoguns Takauji, Yoshiakira and Yoshimitsu. By 1361 he had taken Buddhist vows as Shōzen while remaining Yoshiakira's mōshitsugi usher, later holding the posts of mikkura bugyō and gosho bugyō. After the Kōryaku coup of 1379 he replaced Nikaidō Yukimoto as shitsuji of the shogunate's Mandokoro, holding that office until his death in 1391 and beginning the Ise family's hereditary hold on it. The Buke Nendaiki records that Yoshimitsu was born at his residence.
zh: 伊势贞继是镰仓末期至室町时代的武将，先后侍奉足利尊氏、足利义诠、足利义满三代将军。1361年之前他已出家，法号照禅，仍留在义诠身边担任申次，后来又历任御厩奉行、御所奉行。1379年康历政变后，他接替二阶堂行元出任室町幕府政所执事，一直任职到1391年去世，开启了伊势氏世袭该职的先例。《武家年代记》记载，足利义满就出生在贞继的宅邸。

en: Taira no Toshitsugu was a late-Kamakura warrior of the Ise Heishi line. After he became Ise no kami, governor of Ise Province, his family adopted the name Ise, and he is regarded as the clan's founder. The Mandokoro shitsuji Ise Sadatsugu was his grandson.
zh: 平俊继是镰仓末期武将，出身伊势平氏的一支。他出任伊势守、即伊势国长官后，一族始称伊势氏，他被奉为伊势氏之祖。室町幕府政所执事伊势贞继是他的孙子。

en: Ishidō Yorifusa (1321–1413), second son of Ishidō Yoshifusa, was the third head of that Ashikaga branch house. In 1349 he was appointed shugo of Ise and Shima. During the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi against Takauji: he raised troops at Mount Ikoma in 1350 by edict of Emperor Go-Murakami, routed Takauji's army in Harima, and fought at Satta Pass in 1351. With the Nitta brothers he repeatedly raided Kamakura and Kyoto, and in 1361 helped drive Ashikaga Yoshiakira from the capital. He surrendered around 1364, took Buddhist vows, and died in 1413 aged ninety-three.
zh: 石塔赖房（1321—1413）是足利氏支族石塔氏第三代当主、石塔义房的次子。1349年他被任命为伊势、志摩两国守护。观应之乱中他追随足利直义与尊氏为敌：1350年奉后村上天皇纶旨在生驹山举兵，在播磨击败尊氏军，1351年又战于骏河萨埵山。直义死后，他与新田义兴、义宗兄弟屡次进攻镰仓与京都，1361年曾协助把第二代将军足利义诠逐出京都。约1364年他向义诠投降，随后出家，1413年去世，享年93岁。

en: Ishidō Yorishige was a mid-Kamakura-period warrior, known as Ishidō Shirō. Genealogies variously make him a son of the fourth Ashikaga family head, Ashikaga Yasuuji, or a grandson whom Yasuuji adopted. He took the name Ishidō from an estate granted to him and became the founder of the Ishidō, a cadet branch of the Ashikaga clan. He was the father of Yoshifusa; another son, Kuniaki, is said to have become the Ji-sect preacher Kokua Shōnin.
zh: 石塔赖茂是镰仓时代中期的武将，通称石塔四郎。系图或说他是足利氏第四代当主足利泰氏之子，或说他是被泰氏收养的孙子。他以受封的土地取姓石塔，成为足利氏支族石塔氏的始祖。他是义房之父；相传另一子国明出家，成为时宗的国阿上人。

en: Ishidō Yoshifusa was a warrior of an Ashikaga branch house in the Nanboku-chō wars. In 1334 he became shugodai of Suruga and Izu under Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1336 was appointed shugo of both provinces. The following year he went to Mutsu as Ōshū commander, campaigning there until 1345 against Southern Court forces including the Date clan and Kitabatake Akinobu. In the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, fought at the Battle of Satta Pass in Suruga in 1351, and later joined Ashikaga Tadafuyu and the Nitta brothers. He vanishes from the records after Takauji took Kyoto in 1355.
zh: 石塔义房是南北朝时代足利氏支族石塔氏的武将。1334年，他担任足利尊氏治下骏河、伊豆两国的守护代，1336年就任两国守护。次年他被派往陆奥，任奥州总大将，至1345年一直在奥羽作战，压制伊达氏、北畠显信等南朝势力。观应之乱中他追随足利直义，1351年参加骏河萨埵山之战，其后投奔足利直冬，与新田义兴、新田义宗联手。1355年足利尊氏控制京都后，他便下落不明。

en: Ishidō Yoshimoto, third son of Ishidō Yoshifusa, was a Nanboku-chō warrior. In 1335 he took arms for the Ashikaga with his father, whom he accompanied to Mutsu in 1337 as Ōshū commander, remaining in Ōu until 1346 with the title Sama-no-suke. He joined Ashikaga Tadayoshi in the Kannō Disturbance and later renamed himself Ishidō Yoshinori. In 1354, after Ōshū governor Kira Sadaie died, he took Taga Castle in Mutsu from Kira Mitsuie and was named Ōshū governor by Ashikaga Tadafuyu, only to be defeated and killed, it is said, by Shiba Iekane at Mount Shiei late that year.
zh: 石塔义基是石塔义房的三子，南北朝时代武将。1335年他随父亲为足利氏举兵，1337年父亲出任奥州总大将时随行前往陆奥，至1346年一直滞留奥羽，官途名为左马助。观应之乱中他与父兄同属足利直义一方，后来改名石塔义宪。1354年奥州管领吉良贞家死后局势混乱，他从吉良满家手中夺取陆奥多贺城，被足利直冬任命为奥州管领，但相传同年末即在志荣山被斯波家兼击败战死。

en: Ishikawa Akimochi (died 1351), fifteenth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan, was the eldest son of Ishikawa Yoshimitsu. Adopted by his childless predecessor Sadamitsu, he succeeded as clan head in 1339. In the tenth month of 1351 he went up to Kyoto, where the bakufu made him Junior Fourth Rank and Daizen no daifu, and Shogun Ashikaga Yoshiakira granted him the character that formed his new name, Akimochi. He died of illness at Kamakura on the fourth day of the twelfth month that same year. His wife was a daughter of Ashina Morisada, and his son was Mitsumochi.
zh: 石川诠持（？—1351）是陆奥石川氏第十五代当主、石川义光的长子。他被无子的前代当主贞光收养，1339年继承家督。1351年10月他上洛，被任为从四位下大膳大夫，并获将军足利义诠赐偏讳“诠”字，改名诠持。同年12月4日，他在镰仓病逝。其夫人是芦名盛定之女，生子满持。

en: Minamoto no Arimitsu (1037–1086), second son of Minamoto no Yoritoo and second head of the Mutsu Ishikawa, was born at Monotsu manor in Settsu. He campaigned in Mutsu with his father under Minamoto no Yoriyoshi from 1051, and when Yoritoo fell at the Kuriyagawa stockade in 1062 took command. His merit won him Junior Fifth Rank Lower as Aki no kami and Ishikawa lands, formerly part of Shirakawa district. He first lived at Hogen Castle near Izumi and built Fujita Castle; tradition holds that he built and moved to Mitsuashi Castle. He then took the name Ishikawa and installed Iwashimizu Hachiman as the clan's tutelary deity.
zh: 源有光（1037—1086）是源赖远次子、陆奥石川氏第二代当主，出生于摄津国物津庄。1051年起，他随父亲跟从源赖义出征陆奥；1062年赖远战死厨川栅后，有光接掌军队。他以军功任从五位下安艺守，受赐原属白河郡的石川之地。他最初居住在泉乡附近的保源城，后来修筑藤田城；相传他又建成三芦城并移居于此，此后改称石川氏，又迎来石清水八幡宫的分灵作为一族氏神。

en: Ishikawa Hirosue (died 1248), second son of Ishikawa Motomitsu, was the seventh head of the Mutsu Ishikawa, chosen over a sickly elder brother. In 1183 he sent troops under Narita no Mitsuharu to join Minamoto no Yoritomo after he rose against the Taira in Izu. Bedridden when Yoritomo marched against the Ōshū Fujiwara in 1189, he sent kinsman Ōtera no Mitsuyuki as deputy to join the campaign, and Yoritomo later granted the clan shrine lands in Shida district. After visiting Kamakura in 1197 he became Daizen no daibu; his son Mitsusada succeeded him in 1248.
zh: 石川广季（？—1248）是石川基光次子、陆奥石川氏第七代当主，因兄长体弱多病而被选中继承。1183年，广季派成田光治率兵投奔此前在伊豆举兵讨伐平家的源赖朝。1189年赖朝进军讨伐奥州藤原氏时，广季卧病在床，便派同族大寺光行代他领兵从征；赖朝平定奥州后，向氏神的神社寄进志田郡的领地。1197年广季赴镰仓谒见赖朝，随后被任为大膳大夫。1248年他去世，子光贞继任。

en: Iemitsu Ishikawa (died 1330) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the twelfth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan in southern Ōshū, the eldest son of Moriyoshi Ishikawa. In the twelfth month of 1318 he visited Kamakura, met the regent Hōjō Takatoki, and was presented to Shogun Prince Morikuni, after which the Kyoto court appointed him Governor of Suruga at junior fifth rank. Returning to Kyoto with his younger brother Ietaka in the fifth month of 1325, he rose to junior fourth rank as Governor of Settsu, while Ietaka became Governor of Yamashiro at junior fifth rank. He married a daughter of Yoshinari Tatara and died in 1330.
zh: 石川家光（？—1330）是镰仓时代武将，陆奥石川氏第十二代当主，石川盛义的长子。1318年十二月，他前往镰仓会见执权北条高时，并拜谒征夷大将军守邦亲王，其后被朝廷任命为从五位下骏河守。1325年五月，他携弟弟家隆再次上洛，升任从四位下摄津守，家隆则任从五位下山城守。他娶多多良义业之女，1330年去世。

en: Taira no Iemoto, styled Ishikawa Jirō in the genealogies, was a Hitachi Taira lord of the Yoshida line. His second son Sukemoto was appointed Daijō of Hitachi in 1193 and became the ancestor of the Daijō clan.
zh: 平家干，系图称石川二郎，是常陆平氏吉田氏的领主。他的次子资干于1193年被任命为常陆大掾，成为大掾氏之祖。

en: Mitsunaga Ishikawa (died 1291) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the ninth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan in southern Ōshū, the eldest son of Mitsusada Ishikawa. After coming of age he was appointed Governor of Yamato at junior fifth rank. When the Mongol invasion of Japan was reported in 1281, he led his clansmen and retainers into the Rokuhara army guarding Kyoto, then went west to join the defense of Dazaifu under Utsunomiya Kintsuna. Rewarded for his service, he became Left Head of the Stables at junior fourth rank. He died in early 1291.
zh: 石川光长（？—1291）是镰仓时代武将，陆奥石川氏第九代当主，石川光贞的长子。元服后出任从五位下大和守。1281年元军来袭的消息传来，他率一族与部属加入六波罗军防卫京都，随后西下，随宇都宫公纲参加大宰府的防御。他因战功升任从四位下左马头，于1291年初去世。

en: Mitsusada Ishikawa (died 1269) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the eighth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan of southern Ōshū, a warrior house claiming descent from the Yamato Genji. The eldest son of Hirosue Ishikawa, he married a daughter of the regent Hōjō Yasutoki and served as Governor of Suruga at junior fifth rank. In the third month of 1263 he paid homage to Shogun Prince Munetaka at Kamakura and met Hōjō Tokiyori, then traveled up to Kyoto, where he was appointed Left Head of the Stables at junior fourth rank. He died in 1269.
zh: 石川光贞（？—1269）是镰仓时代武将，为出自大和源氏一脉的陆奥石川氏第八代当主。他是石川广季的长子，娶执权北条泰时之女为妻，任从五位下骏河守。1263年三月，他在镰仓拜谒征夷大将军宗尊亲王，并会见北条时赖，随后上洛入朝，升任从四位下左马头。1269年去世。

en: Ishikawa Mitsuyoshi (died 1121), the second son of Ishikawa Motomitsu, became the fourth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa after his elder brother Mitsutada became a monk; his son Yoshisue succeeded him.
zh: 石川光义（？—1121）是石川元光次子，因兄长光忠出家遁世而成为陆奥石川氏第四代当主，其子义季继任。

en: Moriyoshi Ishikawa (died 1318) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the eleventh head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan in southern Ōshū, the eldest son of Motomori Ishikawa. He married a daughter of the regent Hōjō Tsunetoki and served the Kyoto court as a provincial governor, rising to junior fourth rank. In the tenth month of 1314 he visited Kamakura with his second son Ietaka and kinsman Mitsusuke Ishikawa, and was presented to Shogun Prince Morikuni; in Kyoto soon afterward he was appointed Governor of Yamato. His eldest son Iemitsu succeeded him when he died in 1318.
zh: 石川盛义（？—1318）是镰仓时代武将，陆奥石川氏第十一代当主，石川元盛的长子。他娶执权北条经时之女，在朝廷历任国守，升至从四位下。1314年十月，他携次子家隆和一族的石川光助前往镰仓，拜谒征夷大将军守邦亲王；不久在京都被任命为大和守。1318年去世，长子家光继任家督。

en: Ishikawa Motomitsu (1058–1099), third son of Minamoto no Arimitsu, was the third head of the Mutsu Ishikawa, rising to Junior Fourth Rank Upper as Daizen no daibu. He briefly changed the characters of his given name before resuming Motomitsu when he succeeded his retired father and was made Jibu no taifu. In 1087 he joined Minamoto no Yoshiie's campaign against Kiyohara no Takehira in the Later Three Years' War, fought at the Kanazawa stockade in Dewa, and received Tagawa district for his merit. In 1095 he went up to Kyoto with his kinsmen to receive court rank and office.
zh: 石川元光（1058—1099）是源有光第三子、陆奥石川氏第三代当主，官至从四位上大膳大夫。他一度更改名字的写法，待父亲隐居、自己继任家督并被任为治部大辅时，才恢复元光之名。1087年，源义家出兵讨伐清原武衡，即后三年之役，元光率军参战，攻打出羽国金泽栅，因军功受赐田川郡。1095年，他率领同族上洛，接受朝廷叙位任官。

en: Ishikawa Motomitsu (died 1199), whose name was written 基光, was the sixth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa, second son of Yoshisue, distinct from the third head Motomitsu. In 1179 he went to Kyoto with kinsmen Narita no Mitsuharu and Ishikawa no Kanemasa and was appointed Junior Fifth Rank Lower, Yamato no kami. In 1181 he reburied Arimitsu's remains at Ganpō-ji and raised a three-story pagoda, and in the same year took Buddhist vows as Ryōzen. He died in the fourth month of 1199 and was succeeded by his son Hirosue.
zh: 石川基光（？—1199）是石川义季次子、陆奥石川氏第六代当主，与第三代当主石川元光名字读音相同，却并非同一人。1179年，他带同族人成田光治、石川兼雅上洛，被任为从五位下大和守。1181年，他把二代当主有光的遗骨改葬于岩峰寺，并为其修建三重塔，同年自己也出家，法号了全。他于1199年4月去世，其子广季继任。

en: Motomori Ishikawa (died 1307) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the tenth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan in southern Ōshū, the second son of Mitsunaga Ishikawa. In the eighth month of 1291 the regent Hōjō Sadatoki presented him to Shogun Prince Hisaaki at Kamakura. He then traveled up to Kyoto, entered court service, and was appointed Governor of Yamato at junior fifth rank. He married a daughter of Mitsumori Sahara and was the father of Moriyoshi, who carried on the house. He died in the seventh month of 1307.
zh: 石川元盛（？—1307）是镰仓时代武将，陆奥石川氏第十代当主，石川光长的次子。1291年八月，执权北条贞时引他在镰仓拜谒征夷大将军久明亲王。其后他上洛入朝，出任从五位下大和守。他娶佐原光盛之女为妻，继承家名的盛义是其子。1307年七月去世。

en: Ishikawa Sadamitsu (died 1341) was the fourteenth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan, based at Shirakawa. His uncle Tokimitsu held the headship during his minority. At his coming-of-age he took a character from the regent Hōjō Sadatoki's name, rising to Junior Fourth Rank and Hyōbu no taifu. In 1335 he defeated Kitabatake Akiie's officer Hirohashi Tsuneyasu at Bababara and then attacked Shirakawa Castle, and in 1336 he defeated Tsuneyasu again before the newly built Yumoto Castle. Having no son of his own, he adopted Ishikawa Yoshimitsu's sons and named the eldest, Akimochi, his heir. He died in 1341.
zh: 石川贞光（？—1341）是陆奥石川氏第十四代当主，据点在白河。他幼年时由伯父石川时光暂掌家督，元服时取执权北条贞时名字中的一字，官至从四位下兵部大辅。1335年，他在马场原击败北畠显家的部将广桥经泰，随即攻打白河城；1336年，经泰在汤本筑城进逼，又被他击败。贞光没有亲生子嗣，便收石川义光诸子为养子，立其长子诠持为继承人。他于1341年去世。

en: Tokimitsu Ishikawa (died 1335) was a late Kamakura-period warrior and the thirteenth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa clan in southern Ōshū, the fourth son of Moriyoshi Ishikawa. First named Mitsunori, he took the name Tokimitsu from a character granted by Hōjō Tokimune. When his brother Iemitsu died in 1330 leaving a young heir, Mitsuhide, he took over the house and raised him. In 1333 his son Yoshimitsu joined Nitta Yoshisada's campaign against the Kamakura shogunate in Musashi; Tokimitsu then led troops to Kyoto and was appointed Kunai no Taifu at junior fifth rank, rising in 1334 to junior fourth rank as Daizen no Daibu. He died the next year.
zh: 石川时光（？—1335）是镰仓时代后期武将，陆奥石川氏第十三代当主，石川盛义的第四子。他初名光教，因获北条时宗赐下一字而改名时光。1330年兄长、第十二代当主家光去世，嫡子光英年幼，时光遂继任家督并抚养光英。1333年，其子义光在武藏国加入新田义贞讨伐镰仓幕府的战事；时光本人则率兵上洛，出任从五位下宫内大辅，1334年升从四位下大膳大夫。他于1335年去世。

en: Minamoto no Yoritoo (1007–1062) was a mid-Heian warrior of the Yamato Genji and the third son of Yamato no kami Minamoto no Yorichika, holding Junior Fifth Rank Lower as Ise no kami. Having sat out his father's fatal clash with Kōfuku-ji monks, he escaped the exile that fell on Yorichika. In 1051 he followed Minamoto no Yoriyoshi to Mutsu against the Abe in the Earlier Nine Years' War, and fell in 1062 while storming their Kuriyagawa stockade. His son Arimitsu took over the army; Yoritoo is revered as the ancestor of the Mutsu Ishikawa.
zh: 源赖远（1007—1062）是平安时代中期的大和源氏武将、大和守源赖亲第三子，官至从五位下伊势守。父亲与兴福寺僧人交战、被流放时，他因没有参战而未受处分。1051年，他随源赖义前往陆奥国，参加平定安倍氏的前九年之役，1062年在攻打安倍氏要害厨川栅时战死。其子有光接掌军队，赖远则被尊为陆奥石川氏之祖。

en: Ishikawa Yoshimitsu was a Mutsu warrior of the Ishikawa clan's Ōshima branch. In the fifth month of 1333 he joined Nitta Yoshisada's army in Sagami and fought at Inamuragasaki, helping overthrow the Kamakura shogunate, after which the Kenmu government appointed him Junior Fifth Rank Kunaige no taifu and, in 1334, Junior Fourth Rank Daizen no daibu. In 1335 he went over to Ashikaga Takauji, followed him to Kyushu and fought at the Minatogawa River. He was killed in battle before the Jizō hall on Mount Hiei in the sixth month of 1336. His son Akimochi was adopted by Ishikawa Sadamitsu.
zh: 石川义光是陆奥国武士，出身石川氏庶流大岛氏。1333年5月，他在相模加入新田义贞的军队，参加攻灭镰仓幕府的稻村崎之战；建武新政成立后，他被任为从五位下宫内大辅，1334年升从四位下大膳大夫。1335年，他归从足利尊氏，随其下向九州，又参加凑川之战，1336年6月在比叡山地藏堂前战死。他死后，其子诠持被石川贞光收为养子。

en: Ishikawa Yoshisue (died 1177), eldest son of Ishikawa Mitsuyoshi, was the fifth head of the Mutsu Ishikawa. In 1157 he traveled to Kyoto and was appointed Junior Fourth Rank Lower, Yamato no kami, the office his father had held. His wife was a daughter of Minbu no taifu Fujiwara no Motoshige, a former governor of Mutsu. In the generations from Arimitsu to Yoshisue the clan's cadet branches, including the Dera, Yabuki and Namezu houses, were established across the Ishikawa manor. He died on August 1, 1177, and his second son Motomitsu succeeded him.
zh: 石川义季（？—1177）是石川光义长子、陆奥石川氏第五代当主。1157年他上洛，被任为从四位下大和守，接续父亲曾任的官职。其妻是民部大辅藤原基成之女，基成曾担任陆奥守。从有光到义季的几代间，大寺、矢吹、奈目津等庶流在石川庄各地分立。他于1177年8月1日去世，次子基光继任第六代当主。

en: Prince Isobe was a Nara-period imperial prince, a grandson of Prince Nagaya and son of Prince Kuwata. Probably still an infant when his grandfather and father perished in the Nagaya Incident of 729, he survived the ruin of his house. In 767 he received junior fifth rank, lower grade; in 774 he was made governor of Mikawa Province, and after promotion to upper grade in 776 he was appointed head of the Takumi artisans' bureau in 778. Through his son Prince Iwami he was an ancestor of the Takashina clan.
zh: 矶部王是日本奈良时代的皇族，长屋王之孙、桑田王之子。729年长屋王之变爆发、祖父与父亲遇害时，他推测尚在襁褓，得以幸免于难。767年叙从五位下，774年兼任参河守，776年升叙从五位上，778年带参河守职拜任内匠头。其子石见王的后代繁衍为高阶氏，他被视为高阶氏的祖先。

en: Isshiki Kimifuka (1263–1330) was a Kamakura-period warrior and founder of the Isshiki clan. The seventh son of Ashikaga Yasuuji, he first lived at Isshiki in the Kira manor of Mikawa Province, from which he took the family name. In 1319 he moved to the Tamiya manor at Satte in Shimōsa, where he is said to have built Satte Castle, later relocating to Kobunami and Kinosaki. He held the title of Sakyo no daibu before taking Buddhist vows as the Isshiki Ajari. His wife, a daughter of Imagawa Kuniuji, bore him Yoriyuki and Noriuji. He died in 1330.
zh: 一色公深（1263—1330）是镰仓时代武将、一色氏之祖，为足利泰氏第七子。他最初居住在三河国幡豆郡吉良庄的一色乡，便以一色为家族名号。1319年，他迁居下总国葛饰郡田宫庄的幸手，相传在当地修筑幸手城，此后又先后移居小文间和木野崎。他官至左京大夫，后来出家，称一色阿阇梨。其妻是今川国氏之女，生下一色赖行、一色范氏二子。他于1330年去世。

en: Isshiki Naouji, fourth head of the Isshiki clan, went to Kyushu in 1346 and later succeeded his father Noriuji as the Muromachi bakufu's second Kyushu tandai. He built Seifukuji Castle and held the shugo posts of Higo (1348), Hizen (1350), Chikuzen (1352) and Hyūga (1353). In the Kannō Disturbance he backed Takauji against Ashikaga Tadafuyu. In 1353 Kikuchi Takemitsu's Southern army crushed him at Harizurihara, and in 1355 he fled with his father to Nagato. Sent back, another defeat at Mount Asō drove him to Kyoto in 1358. His later life is unknown; his brother Norimitsu succeeded him.
zh: 一色直氏是南北朝时代武将、一色氏第四代当主，1346年前往九州，随后从父亲范氏手中接任室町幕府第二代九州探题。他修筑势福寺城，历任肥后（1348）、肥前（1350）、筑前（1352）、日向（1353）四国守护。观应之扰乱中他支持尊氏，与足利直冬一方作战。1353年，他在针摺原被菊池武光的南朝军大败，1355年随父亲逃往长门；再被派回九州后又在麻生山战败，1358年逃回京都。其后事迹不详，由其弟范光继任当主。

en: Isshiki Norimitsu (1325–1388), fifth head of the Isshiki clan, was a shugo daimyo. He fought alongside his father Noriuji and brother Naouji against the Southern Court in Kyushu, becoming shugo of Hizen in 1353, until defeat by the Kikuchi drove him back to Kyoto in 1359. He kept the trust of Shoguns Yoshiakira and Yoshimitsu, receiving Wakasa in 1366 and later Mikawa. From 1369 to 1371 he crushed the Wakasa kokujin ikki, securing Isshiki rule and the clan's place among the Four Offices. Ordained after 1367 as Shinden, he died in 1388 aged 64.
zh: 一色范光（1325—1388）是一色氏第五代当主、南北朝时代的守护大名。他随父亲范氏、兄长直氏在九州与南朝方长年作战，1353年就任肥前守护，1359年被菊池氏击败后返回京都。他始终得到将军义诠、义满的信任，1366年受任若狭守护，其后又兼任三河守护。1369至1371年间，他出兵镇压若狭国人一揆，巩固了一色氏的统治，为其跻身四职奠定基础。1367年后出家，法号信传，1388年去世，享年64岁。

en: Isshiki Noriuji (1300–1369) was the third head of the Isshiki clan and a retainer of Ashikaga Takauji. After the Ashikaga victory over Kikuchi Taketoshi at Tatarahama in 1336, he became the Muromachi bakufu's first Kyushu tandai, charged with subduing the island's great shugo houses, including the Ōtomo, Shōni, Kikuchi and Shimazu. In 1346 his eldest son Naouji joined him in the tandai office. During the Kannō Disturbance he backed Takauji, but repeated defeats by Kikuchi Takemitsu, climaxing at Harizurihara in 1353, forced him to abandon Hakata in 1355 and retire to Kyoto, where he died in 1369.
zh: 一色范氏（1300—1369）是一色氏第三代当主、足利尊氏的家臣。1336年多多良滨之战击败菊池武敏后，他出任室町幕府首任九州探题，负责压服大友氏、少贰氏、菊池氏、岛津氏等当地守护。1346年，其长子直氏也进入探题府，父子一同经营九州。观应之扰乱中他站在尊氏一方，却连遭菊池武光击败，1353年在筑前针摺原惨败，1355年又因南朝军进逼而放弃博多，退往长门，随后回京隐居，于1369年去世。

en: Isshiki Yoriyuki (died 1337) was the second head of the Isshiki clan and a retainer of Ashikaga Takauji. He followed Takauji when the latter turned against the Kenmu government and retreated to Kyushu. In 1336 he held Nangō Castle, where Southern Court forces under Era Korezumi killed his steward of the Mimura clan. In the fourth month of 1337 he advanced into Higo with his half-brother Isshiki Noriuji, the new Kyushu tandai, and fell at the Battle of Inuzukabaru against Aso Korezumi and Kikuchi Takeshige. He left a son, Yukiyoshi, but Noriuji succeeded him.
zh: 一色赖行（？—1337）是一色氏第二代当主、足利尊氏的家臣。尊氏背叛建武新政、退往九州时，赖行随军同行。1336年，他据守南乡城，代官三村氏被南朝方的惠良惟澄攻杀。1337年4月，他与新任九州探题、异母弟一色范氏一同进军肥后国，在犬冢原合战中遭阿苏惟澄与菊池武重的南朝军阻击，战死沙场。他虽有子行义，家督之位却由范氏继承。

en: Isshiki Yukiyoshi was the son of Isshiki Yoriyuki, the second head of the Isshiki clan. When Yoriyuki fell fighting in Kyushu in 1337, the clan headship passed not to Yukiyoshi but to Yoriyuki's half-brother Noriuji.
zh: 一色行义是一色氏第二代当主一色赖行之子。1337年赖行在九州战死后，家督之位没有传给行义，而由其叔父范氏继承。

en: Itō Sadasuke was the fifth head of the Itō clan and son of its fourth head, Itō Sukemune. His sons founded its main branches: Sukemochi led the clan to Hyūga Province in 1335 on Ashikaga Takauji's orders, and Sukefuji founded the Sadowara family.
zh: 伊东贞祐是伊东氏第五代当主、第四代当主伊东祐宗之子。他的儿子开创了主要分家：祐持于1335年奉足利尊氏之命下向日向国，成为日向伊东氏之祖；祐藤是佐土原氏之祖。

en: Sukemitsu Itō was a Kamakura-period warrior and the second head of the Hyūga Itō clan, born the sixth son of Suketoki Itō, the founder of the house. His sons were Sukemune Itō, who later carried on the clan, and Mitsuyori Kudō.
zh: 伊东祐光是镰仓时代武将，日向伊东氏第二代当主，为该氏始祖伊东祐时的第六子。其子有后来继承家族的伊东祐宗，以及工藤光赖。

en: Itō Sukemune (1266–1349) was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and the fourth head of the Hyūga Itō clan in Kyushu. When his father died, his kinsman Kiwaki Sukeyori took the headship as his self-styled guardian, but with his mother's backing Sukemune eventually succeeded as clan head. He and his clan retainers fought in the opening battles of the Genkō War, including the Battle of Akasaka Castle in 1331. He died in 1349.
zh: 伊东祐宗（1266—1349）是镰仓时代后期武将、日向伊东氏第四代当主。父亲去世后，亲族木胁祐赖以祐宗年幼为由，以后见的名义继任当主，祐宗最终靠母亲的支持继承家督。他率一族郎党参加了元弘之乱初期的多场战役，其中包括1331年的赤坂城之战。他于1349年去世。

en: Suketoki Itō (1185–1252) was an early Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin, remembered as the founder of the Hyūga Itō clan.
