As a small child called Inufusamaru, he lost his father Suketsune Kudō when the Soga brothers killed him in their famous revenge of 1193; although some sought to spare the captured Soga Tokimune, his tearful pleas led to Tokimune being handed over to the family and executed. He served the shogunate thereafter, joined its Tōkaidō army during the Jōkyū War of 1221, went to Kyoto as the shogun's envoy after the palace fire of 1227, and in 1235 became Governor of Yamato. He died in 1252, aged 68.
zh: 伊东祐时（1185—1252）是镰仓时代前期武将、御家人，被视为日向伊东氏之祖。他幼名犬房丸，1193年曾我兄弟复仇时，父亲工藤祐经被杀；被擒的曾我时致本有获赦之议，年幼的犬房丸流泪诉求，时致终被交予祐经一族处死。他此后仕于幕府，1221年承久之乱中加入幕府方东海道军，1227年内里火灾时以将军使者身份上洛，1235年就任大和守。1252年去世，享年六十八岁。

en: Prince Iwami was a Nara-period Japanese imperial prince who held the junior fifth rank, upper grade. He was the father of Takashina no Mineo, who in 844 received the surname Takashina and left imperial status, making Iwami an ancestor of the Takashina clan.
zh: 石见王是日本奈良时代的皇族，位至从五位上。其子高阶峰绪于844年获赐高阶真人之姓、降为臣籍，石见王由此被视为高阶氏的先祖。

en: Empress Jitō (645–703), born Princess Uno-no-sarara, was Emperor Tenji's daughter and the empress of her uncle Emperor Tenmu, whom she accompanied in the Jinshin War. After Tenmu's death in 686 she ran the court, and when her son Crown Prince Kusakabe died in 689 she upheld the claim of her young grandson Karu. Enthroned in 690 as Japan's third empress regnant, its 41st sovereign, she ruled from Fujiwara Palace and carried on Tenmu's centralising reforms. In 697 she abdicated for her grandson Emperor Monmu, becoming the first daijō-tennō, and continued ruling in retirement until her death in 703.
zh: 持统天皇（645—703）原名鸕野讚良皇女，是天智天皇之女，嫁给叔父天武天皇为皇后，壬申之乱时随军同行。686年天武天皇去世后她执掌朝政；689年儿子草壁皇太子去世，她扶持年幼的孙子轻，即后来的文武天皇。690年她即位，是日本第41代天皇、第三位女天皇，在藤原宫执政，延续天武天皇的中央集权改革。697年她让位于孙子文武天皇，成为第一位太上天皇，退位后仍掌握实权，直至703年去世。

en: Emperor Jomei (593–641), formerly Prince Tamura, ascended the throne in 629 as the 34th sovereign of Japan after the death of his great-aunt Empress Suiko. Soga no Emishi, head of the Soga clan, backed his claim against the rival candidate Prince Yamashiro, and the Soga family seized much of the political initiative during his reign. He took Princess Takara, later Empress Kōgyoku, as his empress; his sons by her became Emperors Tenji and Tenmu. He died in 641 without naming an heir. A poem of his climbing Mount Kagu and surveying the land is preserved in the Man'yōshū.
zh: 舒明天皇（593—641）原名田村皇子，于629年在姑祖母推古天皇去世后即位，是日本第34代天皇。苏我氏首领苏我虾夷支持他与竞争者山背大兄皇子争位，他在位期间苏我氏掌握了大量实权。他立宝皇女（后来的皇极天皇）为皇后，两人所生之子后来成为天智天皇与天武天皇。641年他去世，未指定继承人。《万叶集》中收录有他登临香具山眺望国土的和歌。

en: Emperor Junna (786–840) was the 53rd emperor of Japan, reigning from 823 to 833. A son of Emperor Kanmu, he was made crown prince in 810 after the Kusuko Incident and succeeded his half-brother Emperor Saga in 823. He promoted able officials such as Kiyohara no Natsuno and oversaw the legal commentary Ryō no Gige and the court chronicle Nihon Kōki. In 833 he abdicated in favor of his nephew Emperor Ninmyō and retired to the Junna-in villa. He died in 840, leaving orders for a simple burial; the disputed succession after his death sparked the Jōwa Incident.
zh: 淳和天皇（786—840）是日本第53代天皇，823年至833年在位。他是桓武天皇之子，810年药子之变后被立为皇太子，823年继异母兄嵯峨天皇即位。他任用清原夏野等能臣，并主持编纂律令注释《令义解》与国史《日本后纪》。833年他让位于侄子仁明天皇，退居淳和院。840年去世，遗命薄葬；他身后的继承之争最终引发承和之变。

en: Emperor Junnin (733–765) was the 47th emperor of Japan, reigning from 758 to 764. A son of Prince Toneri and grandson of Emperor Tenmu, he was named crown prince by Empress Kōken in 757 and enthroned when she abdicated the following year, though he ruled as little more than a figurehead. In 764, during Fujiwara no Nakamaro's Rebellion, the former empress reclaimed the throne as Empress Shōtoku and forced Junnin to abdicate. He died in exile on Awaji in 765, possibly by assassination, and was not included on the official imperial list until 1870.
zh: 淳仁天皇（733—765）是日本第47代天皇，758年至764年在位。他是舍人亲王之子、天武天皇之孙，757年被孝谦天皇立为皇太子，次年孝谦退位后登基，但不过是傀儡。764年藤原仲麻吕之乱中，退位的上皇以称德天皇之名重祚，逼迫淳仁退位。765年他在淡路流放地死去，一说遭暗杀。直到1870年，他才被正式列入历代天皇名单。

en: Juntoku (1197–1242), a son of Emperor Go-Toba, became crown prince in 1200 and succeeded his brother Tsuchimikado in 1210, after Go-Toba forced the elder emperor's abdication. Real power stayed with Go-Toba as cloistered emperor. In 1221 Juntoku abdicated in favour of his infant son Chūkyō and backed his father's rising against the Kamakura shogunate, the Jōkyū War. The court's forces were crushed within weeks; Juntoku was exiled to Sado Island and lived there for twenty-one years, dying in 1242. A pupil of the poet Fujiwara no Teika, he left a poem in the Ogura Hyakunin Isshu.
zh: 顺德天皇（1197—1242）是后鸟羽天皇之子，1200年立为太子，1210年后鸟羽逼迫土御门天皇退位，他接替兄长即位，实权仍由后鸟羽上皇以院政掌握。1221年，他让位给幼子仲恭天皇，支持父亲起兵讨伐镰仓幕府，即承久之乱。朝廷军队数周内即被击溃，顺德被流放佐渡岛，在岛上度过二十一年，1242年去世。他曾师从歌人藤原定家，有一首和歌收入《小仓百人一首》。

en: Kagami Tomitsu (1143–1230) was a Kai Genji warrior and founder of the Kagami clan, holding the Kagami estate in Koma district of Kai Province. Tradition records that in 1171, as a takiguchi guardsman, he performed the bow-sounding rite to quiet a haunting at Emperor Takakura's palace and was rewarded with an image of Fudo Myoo. He and his son Ogasawara Nagakiyo fought in the Genpei War, and in 1185 Minamoto no Yoritomo named him governor of Shinano and counted him among his closest vassals. His sons founded the Ogasawara and Nanbu clans, and he died in 1230.
zh: 加贺美远光（1143—1230）是甲斐源氏武将、加贺美氏初代当主，领有甲斐国巨摩郡加贺美庄。相传1171年，他以泷口武者身份在高仓天皇宫中鸣弦镇伏怪异，受赐不动明王像。治承寿永之乱中，他与次子小笠原长清一同参战；1185年，源赖朝任他为信浓守，将他列为近臣御门叶。他的儿子们开创了小笠原氏、南部氏等家族，他本人于1230年去世。

en: Kagawa Kagefusa was a 14th-century head of the Sanuki Kagawa, a warrior clan based in western Sanuki Province that served the Hosokawa as shugodai. His younger brother by the same mother, Kagawa Kagenaka, founded a cadet branch of the clan.
zh: 香川景房是14世纪赞岐香川氏的当主；该族以赞岐国西部为根据地，追随细川氏，世代担任守护代。他的同母弟香川景仲另立一支，其后代成为香川氏的支流。

en: Kagawa Kagenaka was a younger brother, born of the same mother, of Kagawa Kagefusa, head of the Sanuki Kagawa warrior clan of western Sanuki Province. His descendants made up a cadet branch of the clan, which served the Hosokawa as shugodai of western Sanuki.
zh: 香川景仲是赞岐国西部赞岐香川氏当主香川景房的同母弟。他的后代构成香川氏的一支支流，作为西赞岐的守护代家族效力于细川氏。

en: Kajiki Chikahira, called Hachiro Chikahira, was a member of the Kajiki clan whom a genealogy of 1195 records granting Higashimata and other lands in Satsuma's Mange-in to his fourth son Narihira, who appears as district magistrate there in 1197.
zh: 加治木亲平，通称八郎亲平，是加治木氏一员；1195年的《加治木氏系图》记载，他把萨摩国满家院的东俣等地分给四男业平，1197年的图田帐中，业平以满家院郡司的身份在案。

en: Fujiwara no Tsunehira was, by Kajiki family tradition, the third son of the Fujiwara regent (kampaku) Fujiwara no Yoritada (924–989). In the mid-Heian period the head of the local Ōkura clan of Kajiki in Ōsumi Province, Ōkura no Yoshinaga, had no male heir and took Tsunehira as an adopted son-in-law for his daughter. Tsunehira settled on the estate and took the place name as his family name, becoming the ancestor of the Kajiki warrior house, whose descendants served the Kamakura shogunate as gokenin and helped repel the Mongol invasions.
zh: 按加治木氏的家传，藤原经平是摄政关白藤原赖忠（924—989）的第三子。平安时代中期，大隅国加治木的在地豪族大藏良长没有男嗣，便招他为女儿的婿养子。经平就此在当地土着，以加治木为苗字，成为加治木武家之祖；其后人以御家人身份侍奉镰仓幕府，曾参加抵御元寇的战事。

en: Kajiki Tsunehira was a warrior of the Kajiki clan of Ōsumi Province in the early Kamakura period. In 1214 his rights to lands at Kōriyama in Manke-in, Satsuma Province, were confirmed; his son Yoshihira took Kōriyama as his family name. When the Kajiki lost influence after the Jōkyū War of 1221, Kōriyama passed into the hands of the Saisho clan.
zh: 加治木恒平是镰仓时代前期大隅国加治木氏的武将。1214年（建保2年），他对萨摩国满家院郡山的领地所有权得到安堵；其子良平以郡山为苗字。1221年承久之乱后加治木氏失势，郡山转入税所氏之手。

en: Emperor Kameyama (1249–1305), the 90th emperor of Japan and younger brother of Emperor Go-Fukakusa, reigned from 1260 to 1274. In 1265 a mission from Kublai Khan reached Japan demanding submission; the court favoured compromise, but the Kamakura shogunate sent the envoys away. He abdicated in 1274 to his son Emperor Go-Uda and ruled as cloistered emperor, praying at Ise Shrine during the second Mongol invasion of 1281. Distrusted by the shogunate, he lost power in 1287, took Zen vows in 1289, and helped found Kyoto's Nanzen-ji in 1291. His descendants made up the Daikakuji-tō line.
zh: 龟山天皇（1249—1305）是日本第90代天皇，后深草天皇之弟，1260至1274年在位。1265年，忽必烈派遣的使节抵达日本要求称臣，朝廷主张妥协，镰仓幕府却将使节遣返。1274年他让位给儿子后宇多天皇，以上皇身份理政，1281年蒙古第二次来袭时，他亲赴伊势神宫祈祷。他遭到幕府猜忌，1287年失势，1289年皈依禅宗出家，1291年参与创建京都南禅寺。他的后裔构成大觉寺统。

en: Kaneko no Iehiro was a warrior of the Kaneko clan in Musashi Province at the turn of the thirteenth century. The clan genealogy records him as a son of Kaneko no Ietada.
zh: 金子家广是12世纪末至13世纪初武藏国金子氏的武士，金子氏系图将他记为金子家忠之子。

en: Kaneko Iehiro (d. 1385) was a local lord of the Kaneko clan, an offshoot of the Murayama warrior party based at Kaneko in Iruma district, Musashi Province. In 1368 he joined the Musashi Heiikki rising on the side of Kawagoe Naoshige and the Kosaka, but the Kanto kubo Ashikaga Ujimitsu and Uesugi Noriaki crushed it; Iehiro then submitted and served the Uesugi, deputies of the Kanto region. In 1382 he campaigned in Shimotsuke Province against Oyama Yoshimasa's rebellion. He died in 1385, leaving a son, Ieshige.
zh: 金子家祐（？—1385）是武藏国入间郡金子乡的国人，其金子氏出自武藏七党之一村山党的支族。1368年武藏平一揆爆发，他加入河越直重和高坂氏一方参战，但叛乱被关东公方足利氏满与上杉宪显镇压；此后他归顺，侍奉担任关东管领的上杉氏。1382年，他随军前往下野国，参加讨伐小山义政的叛乱。1385年他去世，留下儿子家重。

en: Kaneko no Ienori was a warrior of the Murayama band in Musashi Province. A son of Taira no Yoriie, he settled at Kaneko in Iruma District and was the first to take Kaneko as his family name. His son was the warrior Kaneko no Ietada.
zh: 金子家范是武藏国村山党的武士，为平赖家之子。他定居入间郡金子乡，最先以金子为姓氏，是武藏金子氏之祖，其子为武将金子家忠。

en: Kaneko Ieshige was the son of Kaneko Iehiro, a local lord of the Kaneko clan of Iruma district in Musashi Province who died in 1385.
zh: 金子家重是武藏国入间郡金子氏国人金子家祐之子，家祐于1385年去世。

en: Kaneko no Ietada (1138–1216) was a Musashi Province samurai of the Murayama band, son of Kaneko no Ienori. At nineteen he won his first fame in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156, serving Minamoto no Yoshitomo and killing the famed Takama brothers in single combat, a feat celebrated in the Hōgen Monogatari. In 1180 he fought for the Taira at Kinugasa Castle, holding his ground after taking twenty-one arrows before retreating when another struck him under the jaw. He then submitted to Minamoto no Yoritomo and joined the chase of the Taira. His rewards made him steward of estates in Musashi, Iyo and Harima.
zh: 金子家忠（1138—1216）是武藏国入间郡的武士，属武藏七党之一的村山党，为金子家范之子。1156年保元之乱时，十九岁的他初次上阵，追随源义朝，在单挑中斩杀以勇武闻名的高间兄弟，其事为《保元物语》所传颂。1180年衣笠城之战中，他站在平家一方，身中二十一箭仍坚守阵地，随后下颚又中一箭才退却。他后来归降源赖朝，加入追讨平氏的大军，因功成为武藏金子、伊予新居及播磨鵤庄等地的地头。

en: Prince Kaneyoshi (c. 1329–c. 1381) was a son of Emperor Go-Daigo and the Southern Court's chief commander in Kyushu. In 1336 Go-Daigo named the young prince Seisei Shogun and sent him west; after years in Iyo and Satsuma he entered the Kikuchi stronghold of Waifu Castle in Higo in 1348 and built his Chinzei government with the Kikuchi clan. By 1365 he controlled all of Kyushu, and Ming envoys addressed him as King of Japan. Ashikaga forces landed in Ōita in 1371 and broke his northern Kyushu base, after which he withdrew to the Chikugo plain and died around 1381.
zh: 怀良亲王（约1329—约1381）是后醍醐天皇之子、南朝在九州的最高统帅，人称征西将军宫。1336年后醍醐天皇封幼年的他为征西大将军，派往西方；他先后滞留伊予、萨摩，1348年进入肥后菊池氏的隈府城，依靠菊池氏建立征西府。到1365年，他已控制整个九州，明朝使臣更以“日本国王”相称。1371年足利一方的军队在大分登陆，摧毁他在北九州的基业，他退往筑后川一带，约1381年去世。

en: Emperor Kanmu (737–806) was the 50th emperor of Japan, reigning from 781 to 806, the eldest son of Emperor Kōnin. In 784 he moved the capital from Nara to Nagaoka-kyō, and again in 794 to Heian-kyō, the move that opened the Heian period. His armies, led by Ōtomo no Otomaro and Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, campaigned against the Emishi of northern Honshū, and in 794 Otomaro became the first commander bearing the title sei-i taishōgun. Kanmu also sponsored the monks Saichō and Kūkai on their journeys to Tang China, after which they founded the Tendai and Shingon schools in Japan.
zh: 桓武天皇（737—806）是日本第50代天皇，781年至806年在位，为光仁天皇长子。784年他将都城从奈良迁至长冈京，794年再迁平安京，此举开启了平安时代。他以大伴弟麻吕和坂上田村麻吕为将征讨本州北部的虾夷，794年大伴弟麻吕成为首任征夷大将军。桓武还资助最澄与空海入唐求法，二人归国后分别创立天台宗与真言宗。

en: Kasai Kiyochika was a Kamakura-period gokenin of the Kasai clan. The main genealogies make him a son of the founder Kasai Kiyoshige and father of the later head Tokikiyo, though the family trees disagree. A daughter married Sasaki Yasukiyo, shugo of Izumo and Oki.
zh: 葛西清亲是镰仓时代葛西氏的御家人。主要系图将他列为葛西氏初代当主葛西清重之子、后来的当主葛西时清之父，但各家系图说法不一。一女嫁给出云、隐岐两国守护佐佐木泰清。

en: Kasai Kiyoshige (1161–1238) was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and founder of the Kasai clan, a Toshima cadet line. Third son of Toshima Kiyomoto, he inherited the Kasai manor in Shimōsa and joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's uprising in 1180, fighting through the Genpei War and the Ōshū campaign of 1189, winning praise at Atsukashiyama. Yoritomo made him the first Ōshū sōbugyō, entrusting him with Mutsu's government, and he helped crush the 1190 revolt of Ōkawa Kanetō. A trusted Hōjō elder, he fought in 1205 and 1213 and died a monk under Shinran.
zh: 葛西清重（1161—1238年）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代前期的武将，葛西氏的初代当主，葛西氏为丰岛氏的庶流。他是丰岛清元的三男，继承下总国的葛西御厨，1180年加入源赖朝的举兵，历经源平合战与1189年的奥州合战，在阿津贺志山之战中冲锋先阵，勇武深受赞誉。赖朝任命他为初代奥州总奉行，委托其统辖陆奥国，他还参与平定1190年的大河兼任之乱。此后他作为深受北条氏信任的宿老，参加1205年与1213年的战阵，晚年出家，成为亲鸾的弟子。

en: Kasai Kiyotsune was a Kamakura-period head of the Kasai clan known only from genealogies. The Sendai Kasai genealogy makes him the son and successor of Tokikiyo and the father of Munekiyo, while the Morioka genealogy instead names Kiyonobu as Tokikiyo's heir.
zh: 葛西清经是仅见于系图的镰仓时代葛西氏当主。《仙台葛西系图》以他为时清之子并继任当主，亦是葛西宗清之父；《盛冈葛西系图》则以清信为时清的继承人。

en: Kasai Munekiyo, also called Kiyomune, was a busho of the late Kamakura and early Nanboku-chō periods and the fifth, or by another count sixth, head of the Kasai clan in Mutsu Province. The Sendai Kasai genealogy makes him the son of Kasai Kiyotsune and grandson of Tokikiyo, while the Morioka genealogy identifies him with Kiyonobu, a son of Tokikiyo. The mune in his name is held to derive from the regent Hōjō Tokimune. In 1335 he and his son Sadakiyo joined Kitabatake Akiie's army marching west from Oshu against Ashikaga Takauji.
zh: 葛西宗清，一作葛西清宗，是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代前期的武将，葛西氏第五代（一说第六代）当主，据点在陆奥国。《仙台葛西系图》以他为葛西清经之子、时清之孙，《盛冈葛西系图》则认为他与时清之子清信是同一人。有研究认为，他名字中的“宗”字来自执权北条时宗。1335年，他与儿子贞清一同加入北畠显家从奥州西征、追讨足利尊氏的军队。

en: Kasai Sadakiyo, also called Kiyosada, was a late Kamakura and early Nanboku-chō busho of the Kasai clan in Mutsu Province, the son of Kasai Munekiyo. The sada of his name was granted by the Hōjō regent Sadatoki. In 1335 he and his father joined Kitabatake Akiie's army sent west from Oshu against Ashikaga Takauji; in 1337 he followed Akiie to Ryozen Castle in Date district and joined the renewed western campaign. After Akiie fell in 1338 he returned to Oshu and fought the Northern Court alongside Kitabatake Chikafusa, dying in 1350.
zh: 葛西贞清，一作葛西清贞，是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代前期陆奥国葛西氏的武将，葛西宗清之子。他名字中的“贞”字是执权北条贞时所赐的偏讳。1335年，他与父亲一同加入北畠显家从奥州西征、追讨足利尊氏的军队；1337年随显家移驻伊达郡灵山城，并再次参加西征。1338年显家战死后，他返回奥州，与北畠亲房等人协同对北朝势力作战，1350年去世。

en: Kasai Takakiyo (1312–1365) was the head of the Kasai clan, a warrior family that ruled central Mutsu Province around the Tome district. The son of the clan lord Sadakiyo, he received the character for “Taka” in his adult name from the Hōjō regent Takatoki. In the Genkō War of 1331 the Kamakura shogunate dispatched him with its punitive army to the capital region; the scholar Morone Shōichi identifies him with the Kasai Saburō Hyōe-no-jō named in that force. Kasai genealogies record his death on 17 April 1365, aged 54.
zh: 葛西高清（1312—1365）是葛西氏当主，该家族以登米一带为中心统治陆奥国中部。他是当主葛西贞清之子，成年名中的“高”字取自执权北条高时的偏讳。1331年元弘之乱时，镰仓幕府向畿内派遣讨伐军，军中有“葛西三郎兵卫尉”之名，学者诸根樟一将其比定为高清。据葛西氏系图记载，他于1365年4月17日去世，终年54岁。

en: Kasai Tokikiyo, also called Kiyotoki, was a mid-Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin, counted as either the third or fourth head of the Kasai clan. He was born at Hiraizumi in Ōshū. The genealogies disagree over his father, naming either Kasai Kiyochika or the founder Kiyoshige, and the character ‘toki’ in his given name is thought to have been granted by the Hōjō regents, probably Hōjō Yasutoki. Few of his deeds are recorded, but documents of the Bunryaku to Hōji eras (1234–1247) show him in attendance on the shogun Fujiwara no Yoritsune as the head of a leading gokenin house.
zh: 葛西时清（一作清时）是镰仓时代中期的武将、幕府御家人，被列为葛西氏第三代或第四代当主，出生于奥州平泉。关于他的父亲，诸系图说法不一，或作葛西清亲，或作初代当主清重；其名中的“时”字被认为是从北条执权（年代上看可能是北条泰时）处拜领。他作为当主的具体事迹多不分明，文历至宝治年间（1234—1247年），他曾以有力御家人当主的身份随侍将军藤原赖经。

en: Katō Kagekado (1156–1221) was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and a leading gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. A second son of Katō Kagekazu of Ise Province, he settled in Izu and in 1180 joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's uprising against the Taira, helping kill the Taira official Yamaki Kanetaka. He fought at Ishibashiyama, Hatoda and in the 1189 Ōshū campaign, and in 1203 killed Nitta Tadatsune on Hōjō orders during the Hiki incident. He took the tonsure after Shōgun Sanetomo's murder in 1219 and died in 1221 aged 66.
zh: 加藤景廉（1156—1221）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，镰仓幕府的有力御家人。他是伊势国加藤景员的次子，随父亲移居伊豆；1180年源赖朝举兵讨伐平氏时，他加入赖朝麾下，参与击杀平氏目代山木兼隆。此后他参加石桥山之战、钵田之战以及1189年的奥州合战，1203年又在比企能员之变中奉北条氏之命诛杀仁田忠常。将军源实朝于1219年遇刺后，他出家为僧，1221年以66岁去世。

en: Katō Kagekazu (dates unknown), also called Katō Go and Kagekazu Nyūdō, was a late-Heian warrior from Ise province, the son of Katō Kagekiyo and father of Mitsukazu and Kagekado. The Genpei Jōsuiki records that after killing a Taira retainer in Ise he fled to Izu, sheltering with the Kudō family. In 1180 he and his sons joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's uprising and fought at Ishibashiyama; old and a hindrance, he sent his sons on through the Hakone mountains and took Buddhist vows. Yoritomo confirmed his lands that October, and in 1184 he was ordered to pursue Taira remnants in Iga.
zh: 加藤景员（生没年不详），通称加藤五，后称景员入道，是平安时代末期伊势国的武将，加藤景清之子，光员、景廉之父。据《源平盛衰记》记载，他因在伊势杀死一名平家侍从而离开本领，逃往伊豆国，寄身于工藤氏。1180年，他与儿子们投奔源赖朝的举兵，参加石桥山之战；败走后，年迈的他不愿成为拖累，让儿子们穿过箱根山去寻找赖朝，自己则出家。同年10月，赖朝确认了他的本领；1184年，景员奉命前往伊贺追讨平氏残党。

en: Katō Kagekiyo, commonly called Katō Gorō Kagekiyo, was a warrior of the Ise Katō clan, father of Katō Kagekazu and grandfather of Katō Kagekado. The Sanjō Shrine near the clan's old residence at Anotsu in Ise province is said to have been dedicated to him.
zh: 加藤景清，通称加藤五郎景清，是伊势国加藤氏的武将，加藤景员之父、加藤景廉的祖父。相传伊势国安浓津附近加藤氏旧宅一带的山上神社，就是为祭祀他而建。

en: Katō Kagemichi, recorded as Fujiwara no Kagemichi, was a mid-Heian warrior of the northern Fujiwara Toshihito line, son of Fujiwara no Masashige and ancestor of the Katō clan. His roots lay in Mino province, though he also held estates in Sagami. With his son Kagesue he served Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and Yoshiie. In the Earlier Nine Years' War of 1051–1062 he fought Abe no Sadatō in Mutsu under Yoriyoshi; the Mutsu Waki ranks him first of the seven mounted warriors for his merit. Kagesue fell in the campaign, but Kagemichi's descendants prospered as the Katō.
zh: 加藤景通，朝廷系谱中记作藤原景通，是平安时代中期的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，藤原正重之子，被尊为加藤氏之祖。他本贯美浓国，同时在相模国拥有领地，与儿子景季一同侍奉源赖义、源义家父子。据《陆奥话记》记载，在1051—1062年陆奥的前九年之役中，他随源赖义攻打安倍贞任，战功位列七骑武者之首。景季在此役中阵亡，他的子孙则以加藤氏繁衍兴盛。

en: Kawakami Yorihisa was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods and founder of the Kawakami branch of the Shimazu of Satsuma. Eldest son of Shimazu Sadahisa, he was born of a concubine and never inherited the headship. In 1335 he followed his father to join Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1336 he led Satsuma troops at the siege of Nitta Yoshisada's Kanagasaki castle in Echizen. Sent home in 1337 to crush a Southern Court rising in Satsuma, he fought there for years. In 1352 he received the stewardship of half the Kaseda Beppu estate and took the name Kawakami.
zh: 川上赖久是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，萨摩岛津氏分家川上氏的初代当主。他是第五代当主岛津贞久的长子，因是庶出而未能继承宗家。1335年他随父亲投奔足利尊氏，1336年率领萨摩军队参加攻打新田义贞据守的越前金崎城之战。1337年萨摩的南朝势力举兵，他奉命回国镇压，转战多年。1352年，他获封加世田别府半分的地头职，自此以川上为氏。

en: Kawano no Chikakiyo, also written Ochi no Chikakiyo, was a warrior chieftain of the Kawano clan, the leading family of Iyo Province, which claimed descent from the ancient provincial rulers, the Ochi. In 1160 he was appointed vice-governor of Iyo. From his stronghold at Takanawayama Castle in Kazahaya District he is said to have used Kawano as his family name.
zh: 河野亲清（一作越智亲清）是平安时代后期伊予国的武将豪族。河野氏源出古代国造后裔越智氏，号称伊予第一名门。1160年他出任伊予权介。他以风早郡河野乡的高绳山城为据点，相传以河野为姓氏。

en: Kawano Michiari (1250–1311), head of the Kawano clan of Iyo Province, was a Kamakura gokenin who led the Iyo navy against the Mongols. In 1272 the shogunate mediated his settlement of the succession feud with his uncle Michitoki. In 1281 he moored his warships on the Hakata beach beyond the stone wall, placing it behind his force; his resolve became known as Kawano's rear wall. At Shikanoshima, after Michitoki was killed, he boarded a Yuan ship, was wounded by a crossbow bolt, and took a Mongol general alive. Grants in Hizen and Iyo restored the clan's lost estates, and he is remembered as the Kawano restorer.
zh: 河野通有（1250—1311）是伊予国河野氏当主、镰仓幕府御家人，统率伊予水军抵御元军。1272年，经幕府斡旋，他与伯父通时就惣领之争达成和解。1281年弘安之役中，他把战船停泊在博多石筑地外侧的海滩上，背靠石垒迎敌，其决心被称为河野的后筑地。志贺岛之战中通时战死，他跳上元军战船，虽中石弓负伤，仍生俘一名元军将领。战后受封肥前与伊予的领地，恢复了河野氏旧领，被后人视为河野氏中兴之祖。

en: Kawano Michihisa headed the Kawano clan of Iyo Province in the early Kamakura period, a son of Kawano Michinobu and reputedly of a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa. During the Jōkyū War of 1221 his father and most of the clan joined the imperial court, but Michihisa alone took the Kamakura shogunate's side through his mother's kin. After the defeat he became clan head, his relatives killed or exiled. He received the jitō post of Tonda manor in Awa, exchanging it in 1223 for Ishii manor in Iyo. In 1267 he disinherited his eldest son Michitoki and named Michitsugu heir.
zh: 河野通久是镰仓时代前期伊予国河野氏当主，河野通信之子，母亲传为北条时政之女。1221年承久之乱时，父亲与全族大多投奔朝廷，唯有他凭母方亲缘站在镰仓幕府一方。乱后族人或死或被流放，他继任当主。他受封阿波国富田庄地头职，1223年获准换成伊予国石井乡地头职。1267年，他与嫡子通时义绝，改立通时之弟通继为继承人。

en: Kawano no Michikiyo was a late-Heian warrior chieftain of the Kawano clan in Kazahaya District, Iyo Province, and a son of Chikakiyo. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose against the Taira in 1180, Michikiyo raised troops, drove out Taira no Koremori's provincial deputy and brought Iyo under his control. In 1181 a Taira army under Taguchi Shigeyoshi and Nuka Nyūdō Saijaku of Bingo invaded; Michikiyo held Takanawayama Castle until betrayed from within, then charged out of the castle and died fighting.
zh: 河野通清是平安时代末期伊予国风早郡河野乡的武将豪族，河野亲清之子。1180年源赖朝举兵讨伐平氏，通清随即响应，发兵驱逐平维盛所任的目代，将伊予纳入掌控。1181年，平氏一方的田口成良联合备后的奴可入道西寂攻入伊予，通清据守高绳山城，因内部有人背叛而大败，最终冲出城外力战而死。

en: Kōno Michimori (died 1364) was a warrior lord of Iyo Province and the seventh son of Kōno Michiari. In the Genkō War of 1333 he fought for the Rokuhara deputies in Kyoto, then surrendered and took the tonsure at Kenchō-ji. He joined Ashikaga Takauji in 1336 and was appointed shugo of Iyo. During the Kannō Disturbance after 1350 he sided with Takauji and rebuilt Kōno power, retiring in 1363 in favour of his son Michitomo. When Hosokawa Yoriyuki invaded Iyo in 1364, Michitomo was killed and Michimori died of illness weeks later.
zh: 河野通盛（？—1364）是伊予国的武士领主、河野通有的第七子。1333年元弘之乱时，他在京都为六波罗探题作战，兵败后出家于建长寺。1336年他投奔足利尊氏，被任命为伊予守护。1350年观应之扰乱爆发后，他站在尊氏一方，重振河野氏势力，1363年把家督让给儿子通朝后隐居。1364年细川赖之攻入伊予，通朝战死，约二十日后通盛也病逝。

en: Kawano no Michinobu (c. 1155–1223) was an Iyo Province warrior and commander of the Iyo naval forces, son of Michikiyo and grandfather of the preacher Ippen. After his father fell at Takanawayama in 1181, he harried the Taira from the Takanawa Peninsula, and in 1185 he brought his warships to Minamoto no Yoshitsune, fighting at Shido and Dannoura. He became a Kamakura vassal and campaigned in Ōshū in 1189. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he backed the retired emperor Go-Toba; defeat brought exile to Mutsu, where he died in 1223.
zh: 河野通信（约1155—1223）是伊予国武将、伊予水军将领，河野通清之子，也是时宗祖师一遍的祖父。1181年父亲战死于高绳山城后，他在高绳半岛以游击战继续抗击平氏；1185年率战船投奔源义经，在志度之战献船助战，又参加坛之浦海战。战后他成为镰仓幕府御家人，1189年随军参加奥州合战。1221年承久之乱中他站在后鸟羽上皇一方，兵败后被流放陆奥国，1223年死于流放地。

en: Kawano Michitomo (died 1364) was a commander of the Nanboku-chō period, the son of Kōno Michimori and father of Kōno Michitaka. He fought alongside his father for the Northern Court and was named governor of Tōtōmi Province through Ashikaga Yoshiakira's recommendation. In 1363 he succeeded to the Kōno headship on his father's retirement. The next year Hosokawa Yoriyuki invaded Iyo and in the ninth month besieged Michitomo in Setayama Castle. After two months' resistance the castle fell and Michitomo was killed on the sixth day of the eleventh month, 1364.
zh: 河野通朝（？—1364）是南北朝时代武将，河野通盛之子、河野通尧之父。他随父亲为北朝转战，经足利义诠举荐任远江守。1363年父亲隐居后，他继承河野氏家督。次年细川赖之入侵伊予，九月将他围困于世田山城。通朝坚守两个月，城破后于1364年十一月六日战死。

en: Kawano Michitsugu was a warrior of Iyo Province in the mid-Kamakura period who succeeded his father Kawano Michihisa as head of the Kawano clan. In 1237 his father granted him part of Ishii manor in Iyo, and in 1267 passed him the clan headship and the whole manor after the elder son Michitoki had been disinherited. Michitoki then sued him at the Kamakura shogunate, claiming Michitsugu was the one who had had the affair behind the family breach. A settlement was reached only in 1272, when Michitsugu was already dead; the compromise was made with his son Michiari.
zh: 河野通继是镰仓时代中期伊予国武士，继父亲河野通久之后担任河野氏当主，也是河野通有之父。1237年，父亲把伊予石井乡的一部分领地让给他；长兄通时被废嫡后，他又在1267年继承惣领地位和石井乡全境。通时反称与父亲妻妾私通者实是通继，向镰仓幕府提起诉讼。直到1272年双方才达成和解，此时通继已经去世，出面和谈的是其子通有。

en: Kawanobe Jiro was the son of Kawanobe Sukeshige, head of the Kawanobe warrior clan of Hitachi Province. In 1335 he rose with his father for Emperor Go-Daigo's Southern Court, fought at Mikanohara against the Northern Court military governor Satake Sadayoshi, and marched on Kyoto with Kitabatake Akiie. After the Kawanobe were crushed at Urizura in 1336, he took service under Kikuchi Takenao in Kyushu and won distinction, but later fell in battle at Yoshino. His son Michiyasu went on fighting for the Southern Court in Hitachi.
zh: 川野边次郎是常陆国武家川野边氏总领资镇之子。1335年，他随父亲为后醍醐天皇的南朝举兵，在瓮之原与北朝方的常陆守护佐竹贞义作战，随后随北畠显家上洛。1336年川野边氏在瓜连战败后，他投奔九州的菊地武直，立下战功，后来在吉野战死。其子通保仍在常陆为南朝效力。

en: Kawanobe Sukeshige was head of the Kawanobe, a Fujiwara-descent warrior clan of Naka and Kuji districts in Hitachi Province. In 1335 he and his son Jiro rose for the Southern Court of Emperor Go-Daigo, defeated the Hitachi military governor Satake Sadayoshi at Mikanohara, and marched on Kyoto with Kitabatake Akiie against Ashikaga Takauji; Go-Daigo granted the clan the chrysanthemum badge. In 1336 he fought around Urizura Castle under Kusunoki Masaie, but was defeated at Dokushōhō by Kimura Yoshimasa, and most of the clan perished.
zh: 川野边资镇是常陆国那珂郡至久慈郡一带武家川野边氏的总领，该族自称出自藤原氏。1335年，他与儿子次郎一同为后醍醐天皇的南朝举兵，在瓮之原击败常陆守护佐竹贞义，又随北畠显家上洛，与足利尊氏作战，蒙后醍醐天皇赐下菊纹。1336年，他在楠木正家麾下转战瓜连城一带，却在独松峰之战被木村义昌击败，一族大多自尽，家族濒临灭亡。

en: Emperor Kazan (968–1008), personal name Morosada, was the eldest son of Emperor Reizei and the sixty-fifth sovereign of Japan, reigning from 984 to 986. He commissioned the imperial waka anthology Shūi Wakashū, but his short rule was dominated by the Fujiwara regents. In 986 Fujiwara no Kaneie tricked the nineteen-year-old emperor into believing the imperial regalia had already passed to Prince Kanehito, and Kazan abdicated at Gangyō-ji and took Buddhist orders as the monk Nyūkaku. In later life he re-established the Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage of thirty-three temples. He died in 1008.
zh: 花山天皇（968—1008）名师贞，是冷泉天皇的长子、日本第六十五代天皇，984年至986年在位。他曾下诏编纂敕撰和歌集《拾遗和歌集》，但短暂的统治始终受制于藤原氏摄关。986年，藤原兼家哄骗十九岁的花山天皇，说神器已转交怀仁亲王，花山天皇遂在元庆寺退位出家，法名入觉。晚年他重新整备了由三十三处寺院组成的西国观音灵场。1008年去世。

en: Prince Kazurawara (786–853), third son of Emperor Kanmu, was a Japanese imperial prince and the ancestor of the Kanmu Taira clan. After coming of age in 798, he served as minister of the treasury and became minister of ceremonial in 810. In 812 he was also appointed governor-general of the Dazaifu. He moved to another office in 823, and in 825 his petition to demote his son to commoner status with the surname Taira was approved, beginning the clan's history. He returned as minister of ceremonial in 830 and in 831 received the highest princely rank, first grade. He died in 853.
zh: 葛原亲王（786—853）是日本桓武天皇第三皇子，桓武平氏之祖。798年元服，曾任大藏卿，810年出任式部卿。812年他又兼任大宰帅。823年他转任他职，825年上奏请求让儿子降为臣籍、赐姓平朝臣，获准，桓武平氏由此开祖。830年他复任式部卿，831年升至一品，为皇族最高品位。853年去世。

en: Keitai (c. 450–531), the 26th emperor of Japan in the traditional order of succession, reigned from 507. Before his accession he ruled in Echizen as Prince Ōdo, a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Ōjin. When Emperor Buretsu died without an heir in 506, the great minister Ōtomo no Kanamura secured the distant kinsman's elevation, and Keitai married Tashiraka, Buretsu's sister. His title long disputed, he entered the Yamato heartland only around 526. In 527 the Iwai Rebellion erupted in Kyushu; he sent Mononobe no Arakabi, who suppressed it. Three of his sons reigned in turn: Ankan, Senka and Kinmei.
zh: 继体天皇（约450—531）是日本传统世系中的第26代天皇，507年即位。即位前他称男大迹王，是应神天皇的五世孙，在越前一带为王。506年武烈天皇无嗣而终，权臣大伴金村主导迎立这位远支王族，他遂娶武烈之妹手白香皇女为皇后。其继承权长期存在争议，约526年、即即位约二十年后才进入大和的政治中心。527年九州爆发磐井之乱，他派大连物部麁鹿火将其平定。他死后有三子相继即位，即安闲、宣化、钦明天皇。

en: Utsunomiya Fuyutsuna, also known as Kii Fuyutsuna, was a Southern and Northern Courts commander and the seventh head of the Kii, or Buzen Utsunomiya, clan. Adopted by Utsunomiya Yorifusa, he first called himself Takafusa after receiving a character from Hōjō Takatoki. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji's Northern Court and became shugo of Chikugo and Buzen in 1352. In 1355 he surrendered to the Southern Court and took the name Fuyutsuna, possibly from Ashikaga Tadafuyu, but soon rejoined the North. In 1359 he fought Kikuchi Takemitsu at the Battle of the Chikugo River; defeat there began the Kii clan's rapid decline.
zh: 宇都宫冬纲，又称城井冬纲，是南北朝时代武将，城井氏（丰前宇都宫氏）第七代当主。他被宇都宫赖房收为养子，初名高房，得名于北条高时的偏讳。他初为足利尊氏的北朝而战，1352年成为筑后、丰前两国守护。1355年他向南朝投降，改名冬纲，可能受了足利直冬的偏讳，不久复归北朝。1359年，他在筑后川之战与菊池武光交锋，北朝兵败，城井氏由此迅速衰落。

en: Kii Kagefusa, also called Utsunomiya Kagefusa, was an early Kamakura-period warrior and the third head of the Buzen-Utsunomiya, or Kii, clan, based at Kiidani in Nakatsu District, Buzen Province, with the title Iki no kami. He distinguished himself in the pacification of Kyushu. His son Nobukage was made one of the shogunate's four Kyushu magistrates.
zh: 城井景房，亦称宇都宫景房，是镰仓时代前期的武将、丰前宇都宫氏（城井氏）第三代当主，以丰前国仲津郡城井谷为据点，官至壹岐守。他在平定九州的战事中立功。其子信景后来被赖朝任命为幕府九州四奉行之一。

en: Utsunomiya Michifusa, also called Kii Michifusa, was a mid-Kamakura warrior of the Buzen-Utsunomiya clan. His house had become a direct vassal of the Hojo tokuso, and during the Bun'ei era he went down to Kyushu as a Hojo deputy in response to the Mongol invasions. In 1286 he was made a head of the new Chinzei Council, hearing suits of Kyushu vassals. He later served as Chikugo shugo and as Hojo Sadatoki's deputy in Higo, and in 1290 received the stewardship of Sada manor in Usa District, Buzen, where his descendants settled as the Chinzei-Utsunomiya.
zh: 宇都宫通房，亦称城井通房，是镰仓时代中期丰前宇都宫氏的武将。其家此时已成为北条得宗的被官（御内人），文永年间他因元寇下向九州，担任北条氏的代官。1286年镇西谈议所设立，他被任为头人之一，审理九州御家人的诉讼；其后历任筑后守护、北条贞时的肥后守护代。1290年他得到丰前国宇佐郡佐田庄的地头职，子孙在当地定居，称镇西宇都宫氏。

en: Utsunomiya no Nobufusa (1156–1234) was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, the eldest son of Nakahara no Munefusa and founder of the Buzen Utsunomiya, later called the Kii clan. In 1180 he rode from Shimotsuke to join Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising, and in 1183 he won distinction suppressing Shida Yoshihiro's revolt. As Chinzei commissioner he campaigned against Taira remnants on Kikaigashima in 1187, and in 1192 Yoritomo granted him estates in Bungo and Hyūga. He died in 1234 at the age of seventy-nine.
zh: 宇都宫信房（1156—1234）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代前期的武将，中原宗房的长子，被奉为丰前宇都宫氏（后来的城井氏）之祖。1180年，他从下野国驰赴源赖朝举兵；1183年在讨伐志田义广叛乱时立下战功。1187年，他以镇西奉行的身份征伐鬼界岛的平氏残党，1192年获赖朝赐予丰后、日向两国的领地。他于1234年去世，享年79岁。

en: Kii Nobukage, also called Utsunomiya Nobukage, was a Kamakura warrior of the Buzen-Utsunomiya clan and son of Kagefusa. Minamoto no Yoritomo named him to the shogunate's Hyojoshu and as one of the four Kyushu magistrates, supervising the warriors of Kyushu.
zh: 城井信景，亦称宇都宫信景，是镰仓时代丰前宇都宫氏的武将、景房之子。源赖朝任命他为幕府评定众、九州四奉行之一，统辖九州的武士。

en: Utsunomiya Toyofusa (1293–1369) was the founder of the Iyo Utsunomiya clan and a son of Utsunomiya Yorifusa, sixth head of the Buzen Utsunomiya, or Kii, clan. In 1330 the Kamakura shogunate appointed him shugo of Iyo Province, and the next year he entered Ōzu, built Jizōgatake Castle, later Ōzu Castle, as his seat, and founded Jōgan-ji as the family temple. He held junior fourth court rank, lower grade. With no son of his own, he adopted Utsunomiya Muneyasu of the Chikugo Utsunomiya as his heir, and died on 19 September 1369.
zh: 宇都宫丰房（1293—1369）是伊予宇都宫氏的初代当主，丰前宇都宫氏（城井氏）第六代当主宇都宫赖房之子。1330年，镰仓幕府任命他为伊予国守护；次年他进入大洲，在地藏岳筑城，即后来的大洲城，作为伊予宇都宫氏的本城，同年又建城愿寺为菩提寺。他官至从四位下。因无亲生儿子，他收筑后宇都宫氏的宇都宫宗泰为养子继任，于1369年9月19日去世。

en: Utsunomiya Yorifusa, also called Kii Yorifusa, was a head of the Buzen-Utsunomiya clan who adopted Fuyutsuna, a son of Utsunomiya Sadatsuna of the main house in Shimotsuke.
zh: 宇都宫赖房，亦称城井赖房，是丰前宇都宫氏的当主，他收宗家下野宇都宫氏宇都宫贞纲之子冬纲为养子。

en: Kikkawa Sanetsune (fl. 1331–1363) was a warrior of the Aki Kikkawa clan, son of Tsunenaga, and fought as the main strength of the clan's weak head house in the Nanboku-chō wars. He changed sides with the times: in 1335 he helped the Ashikaga-aligned Takeda Ujinobu storm Yano Castle, but in 1336 he took Nitta Yoshisada's order and joined the Southern Court, later returning to the Northern side. In 1352 he captured Kotosaki Castle from Mōri Motoharu, who fled to Yoshida-Kōriyama Castle and surrendered the following month. In 1363 he granted land to his son Kogumamaru, who died young; Sanetsune eventually adopted Tsunemi of the rising Iwami branch.
zh: 吉川实经（活动于1331—1363年）是安艺国国人吉川氏一门，吉川经长之子。宗家当主经盛、经秋势力软弱，石见分家日益坐大，实经作为宗家的主力东征西战。他在南北朝之间几度改换阵营：1335年配合从属足利的武田氏信攻陷熊谷莲觉据守的矢野城，1336年又奉新田义贞的御教書加入南朝，后来复归北朝。1352年他从毛利元春手中攻下琴崎城，元春逃往吉田郡山城，次月投降。1363年他将所领让给儿子虎熊丸，虎熊丸夭折后，他最终收势力日盛的石见分家经兼之子经见为养子。

en: Kikkawa Tomokane (1159–1200) was the second head of the Kikkawa clan and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. He fought under Minamoto no Yoritomo in the Ōshū campaign of 1189, earning recognition for his bravery, accompanied Yoritomo's first entry into Kyoto in 1190, and stood guard at the Fuji no Makigari hunt of 1193 during the Soga brothers' revenge. In 1200, in the revolt against Kajiwara Kagetoki, he detected Kagetoki's party in Suruga, where he held lands, and joined local warriors in attacking them. He slew Kagetoki's third son Kagemochi, famed for his courage, but died of his own wounds. His son Tomotsune was rewarded with the jitō post of Fukui Manor in Ibo District, Harima.
zh: 吉川友兼（1159—1200）是吉川氏第二代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1189年随源赖朝出征奥州合战，武勇受到赏识；1190年又随赖朝首次上洛，1193年在富士卷狩时担任警护，经历曾我兄弟复仇的骚动。1200年梶原景时之变中，他在领地所在的骏河国察觉景时一行的异动，联合当地武士袭击，斩杀其三子、以豪勇闻名的梶原景茂，自己也因伤重而死。其子朝经因此受赏，被任为播磨国揖保郡福井庄的地头。

en: Kikkawa Tomotsune (1182–1240) was the third head of the Kikkawa clan and a Kamakura gokenin. In the purge of Kajiwara Kagetoki in 1200 his father Tomokane was killed fighting in Suruga; Tomotsune was rewarded for his own and his father's service with added lands and the jitō post of Fukui Manor in Harima Province, formerly Kajiwara territory. He died in 1240; his heir Tsunemitsu may already have succeeded him as clan head before then. As their recorded birth years are only ten years apart, Tsunemitsu may have been adopted from a kinsman.
zh: 吉川朝经（1182—1240）是吉川氏第三代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1200年梶原景时之变中，其父友兼在骏河战死；幕府追念其父之功、并嘉奖他本人，为他加封领地，任命他为原属梶原氏的播磨国福井庄地头。他于1240年去世，其继承人经光可能在此前已继承家督。因记载中两人生年仅相差十岁，经光也有可能是从亲族中收养的养子。

en: Kikkawa Tsuneaki was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods and the seventh head of the Aki Kikkawa clan, based at Surugamaru Castle. In 1350 he succeeded his father Tsunemori while the clan followed Ashikaga Takauji's Northern Court, but he could not hold the family together: the Iwami Kikkawa branch joined the Southern Court and grew powerful under Tsunekane and Tsunemi. Having no son, Tsuneaki married his daughter Mitoku to Tsunemi and made the Iwami leader his adopted heir. He died in 1383.
zh: 吉川经秋是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武士，安艺国国人吉川氏第七代当主，驻骏河丸城。1350年，他从父亲吉川经盛手中继承家督，当时吉川氏追随足利尊氏的北朝一方；但他无力统合一族，石见吉川氏的经兼、经见父子投奔南朝，势力大振。经秋没有儿子，便把女儿弥德嫁给经见，收其为婿养子继承家业。他于1383年去世。

en: Kikkawa Tsunehide was the second head of the Iwami branch of the Kikkawa clan and held the title Shinano-no-kami. He was the second son of Tsuneshige, founder of the Iwami line, and his sister married the Aki clan head Tsunemori. In the Kenmu and Engen years he fought for Ashikaga Takauji, earned a letter of commendation and was appointed governor of Shinano. After succeeding his father, he quarrelled with his mother Magayasha in 1349; his younger brother Tsunekane sided against him, and Tsunehide was disinherited. Tsunekane then took the Iwami headship.
zh: 吉川经任是吉川氏庶流石见吉川氏的第二代当主，官至信浓守。他是石见吉川氏开创者经茂的次子，姊妹嫁给安芸宗家当主经盛。建武、延元年间，他为足利尊氏作战，因战功获颁感状，被任为信浓守。父亲死后他继承家督，却在1349年与母亲孙夜叉对立，弟弟经兼站在母亲一边，经任因此被废嫡，石见吉川氏的家督遂由经兼继承。

en: Kikkawa Tsunekane was a warrior of the early Nanboku-chō period and the third head of the Iwami branch of the Kikkawa clan. In 1349 he took his mother the nun Ryōkai's side in her quarrel with his elder brother Tsunetō, drove Tsunetō out, and succeeded to the family. In the Kannō Disturbance he backed Ashikaga Tadayoshi and Tadafuyu, fighting with his son Tsunemi in Aki and Nagato. In 1358 the Southern Court emperor Go-Murakami appointed him acting governor of Suruga, and in 1368 Tadafuyu granted him the stewardship of Ōasa-no-shinshō.
zh: 吉川经兼是日本南北朝时代初期的武士，石见吉川氏第三代当主。1349年，母亲良海尼与兄长经任对立，他站在母亲一方，驱逐经任后继承家督。观应之扰乱中，他支持足利直义、足利直冬一方，与儿子经见转战安艺、长门两国。1358年，南朝后村上天皇任命他为骏河权守；1368年，足利直冬又将大朝新庄的地头职封赐给他。

en: Kikkawa Tsunemitsu (1192–1267) was the fourth head of the Kikkawa clan and a mid-Kamakura gokenin. He fought for the Kamakura shogunate in the Jōkyū War of 1221 and won distinction at the Battle of Uji Bridge outside Kyoto. Besides his family's Kikkawa Manor in Suruga and Fukui Manor in Harima, he was appointed jitō of Ōasa Honjō in Aki Province, the foothold in which the clan later settled. His sons founded the Aki, Iwami, Harima, Suruga and Sakai branches of the Kikkawa. He died in 1267.
zh: 吉川经光（1192—1267）是吉川氏第四代当主、镰仓时代中期的御家人。1221年承久之乱中，他站在镰仓幕府一方参战，在京都宇治桥之战立功。除本家的骏河国吉河庄与播磨国福井庄外，他又被任命为安艺国大朝本庄地头，吉川氏后来便以此为据点在当地定居。他的诸子分别成为安艺吉川氏、石见吉川氏、播磨吉川氏、骏河吉川氏和境吉川氏之祖。1267年去世。

en: Kikkawa Tsunemori (died 1358) was the sixth head of the Kikkawa clan of Aki Province and lord of Surugamaru Castle. He succeeded his father Tsunetaka in 1319. During the Nanboku-chō wars he backed the Ashikaga: in 1335, under the Aki shugo Takeda Nobutake, he attacked the Southern Court garrison at Yano Castle held by Kumagai Renkaku, and later campaigned for Ashikaga Tadayoshi in Iwami. His cousin Tsunekane and younger brother Tsunenaga both joined the Southern Court. Troubled by this split, he passed the headship to his son Tsuneaki in 1350 and died in 1358.
zh: 吉川经盛（？—1358）是安艺国国人吉川氏第六代当主、骏河丸城主。1319年父亲经高隐居，他继承家督。南北朝动乱中他站在足利一方：1335年随安艺守护武田信武攻打南朝方熊谷莲觉据守的矢野城，后来又从属足利直义，在石见国与南朝势力交战。然而同族纷纷背离，堂兄经兼、弟弟经长都归顺南朝。经盛忧心于一族分裂，1350年把家督让给嫡子经秋，1358年病死。

en: Kikkawa Tsunenaga, son of Tsunetaka and younger brother of the Aki head Tsunemori, fought for the Southern Court. Bearing Emperor Go-Daigo's edict, he joined the court at Mount Senjō in Hōki. His son was Sanetsune, to whom he granted lands in 1331.
zh: 吉川经长是吉川经高之子、安芸吉川氏第六代当主经盛之弟。南北朝动乱中他加入南朝，奉后醍醐天皇纶旨前往伯耆国船上山。其子为吉川实经，1331年他把所领的一部分让给实经。

en: Kikkawa Tsuneshige was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and the founder of the Iwami branch of the Kikkawa clan. A son of Kikkawa Tsunemitsu, he married the daughter of a local lord of Iwami Province and probably settled on her estate of Nagayasu-beppu to manage her household. In 1313 he probably administered the clan's holding at Ōasa in Aki Province before his elder brother Tsunetaka moved there. The brother later granted him the stewardship of Tsufuchi-no-shō in Iwami, making him first head of the Iwami line. He married his daughter to his nephew Tsunemori, head of the Aki Kikkawa.
zh: 吉川经茂是镰仓时代后期的武士，为吉川氏庶流石见吉川氏的始祖。他是吉川经光之子，娶石见国一位国人的女儿为妻，可能进入妻子在石见永安别符的领地打理家务。1313年，在兄长经高前往安芸之前，他可能负责管理家族在安芸国大朝庄的领地。后来兄长将石见津渊庄的地头职授予他，他由此成为石见吉川氏初代当主；他又把女儿嫁给侄子、安芸吉川氏当主吉川经盛。

en: Kikkawa Tsunetaka (1234–1319) was the fifth head of the Kikkawa clan and a late-Kamakura gokenin, remembered as the real founder of the Aki Kikkawa. He succeeded his father Tsunemitsu in 1267. After mismanagement allowed clan lands in Aki and Harima to be seized, he won their restoration from the Kamakura shogunate in 1313 and, nearing eighty, left the family's old base in Suruga for Ōasa Manor in Aki. There he built Surugamaru Castle, assigning his brothers holdings in Harima, Iwami and Suruga. In 1319 he retired in favour of his eldest son Tsunemori and died the same year aged eighty-six.
zh: 吉川经高（1234—1319）是吉川氏第五代当主、镰仓时代末期御家人，被视为安艺吉川氏事实上的始祖。1267年他继承父亲经光的家督。由于经营不善，吉川氏在安艺、播磨的领地不断遭人侵占；1313年他向镰仓幕府申诉成功、收回所领，年近八旬仍离开本领骏河，移居安艺国大朝庄。他在当地修筑骏河丸城作为居城，把诸弟分派到播磨、石见、骏河各处领地。1319年他把家督让给嫡子经盛，同年去世，享年八十六岁。

en: Kikkawa Tsuneyoshi (1132–1193), first known as Irie Tsuneyoshi, was a warrior of Suruga Province and great-great-grandson of Irie no Korekiyo. In 1183, after entering the service of Minamoto no Yoritomo, he received Kikkawa Manor in Suruga, built his residence there, and took its place name as his family name, founding the Kikkawa clan. A gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate, he died in 1193 and was succeeded by his son Tomokane.
zh: 吉川经义（1132—1193），初名入江经义，是骏河国武士、入江维清的玄孙，吉川氏之祖。1183年归附源赖朝后，他获赐骏河国吉河庄，在当地筑馆居住，并以地名作为家名，开创吉川氏。他身为镰仓幕府御家人，于1193年去世，其子友兼继任家督。

en: Kikuchi Noritaka (1029–1101), also recorded as Fujiwara no Noritaka, was the founder of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province. The genealogies name him a son of Fujiwara no Masanori and a grandson of the chūnagon Fujiwara no Takaie, famed for leading the defense of Dazaifu against the Toi raid of 1019. He died on 15 March 1101 as the first head of the clan.
zh: 菊池则隆（1029—1101），一作藤原则隆，是肥后国菊池氏的初代当主。据家系谱记载，他是藤原政则之子、中纳言藤原隆家之孙；隆家曾在1019年刀伊入寇时主持大宰府防务，立下战功。他于1101年3月15日去世。

en: Kikuchi Takamori, a Kamakura-period Kikuchi warrior, was the eldest son and heir of the tenth head Takefusa. He died before his father, who was therefore succeeded by Takamori's son Tokitaka; his younger son Taketoki later became the twelfth head.
zh: 菊池隆盛是镰仓时代菊池氏武将，第十代当主武房的长子与继承人。他先于父亲去世，武房遂由隆盛之子时隆继承；其幼子武时后来成为第十二代当主。

en: Kikuchi Takanao (1146–1188) was the sixth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province and a paramount warrior lord in Kyushu. Resenting Taira control of the trade with Song China, in 1180 he raised the Chinzei Rebellion with Aso Koreyasu and Kihara Morizane. Pardoned and then condemned by a court order, he submitted to Taira no Sadayoshi in 1182. He fought for the Taira at Dannoura in 1185 and surrendered to Minamoto no Yoshitsune, who handed him to his old rival Ogata Koreyoshi; the Heike Monogatari dates his beheading to that year, while clan genealogies give 1188.
zh: 菊池隆直（1146—1188）是肥后国菊池氏第六代当主，是统御九州海陆党羽的一国栋梁。因不满平家把持对宋贸易，1180年他与阿苏惟安、木原盛实等发动镇西反乱。平家先加赦免，旋又下发讨伐宣旨，隆直遂于1182年投降平贞能。1185年他从平家一方参加坛之浦之战，兵败后投降源义经，被交给长年敌对的绪方惟荣；《平家物语》载其当年被斩首，菊池氏系图则作卒于1188年。

en: Kikuchi Takasada (1167–1222) was the seventh head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province. His son Tsunetsugu died before him, so after his death the headship passed to his grandson Yoshitaka, who became the eighth head.
zh: 菊池隆定（1167—1222）是肥后国菊池氏第七代当主。其子经继先于他去世，故隆定死后由其孙能隆继承家督，为第八代当主。

en: Kikuchi Takayasu was the ninth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province. His third son Takefusa succeeded him and fought the Mongol invasions; his fourth son Aritaka founded the Akahoshi branch of the Kikuchi. By 1273 Takefusa was already leading the clan.
zh: 菊池隆泰是肥后国菊池氏第九代当主。其三子武房继为第十代当主，率众抵御蒙古袭来；四子有隆开创菊池氏庶流赤星氏。至迟1273年，武房已以当主身份主持一族。

en: Kikuchi Takefusa (1245–1298), third son of the ninth head Takayasu, was the tenth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo. In the 1274 Mongol invasion he and his brother Aritaka led the clan against Yuan troops at Akasaka, hurling them back to Sohara in a fight depicted in the Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba. He served again at Hakata during the 1281 invasion, yet received only armor from the court and no bakufu reward, which turned him against the Hōjō. His eldest son Takamori predeceased him, so at his death in 1298 his grandson Tokitaka became the eleventh head.
zh: 菊池武房（1245—1298）是肥后国菊池氏第十代当主，第九代当主隆泰第三子。1274年文永之役，他与弟弟有隆率一族在赤坂迎击元军，将其击退至麁原，其奋战被绘入《蒙古袭来绘词》。1281年弘安之役，他再赴博多参战；战后朝廷仅赐甲胄，镰仓幕府却毫无恩赏，武房由此背离北条氏掌权的幕府。长子隆盛早逝，1298年他死后由长孙时隆继任第十一代当主。

en: Kikuchi Takehito (1321–1352) was the fourteenth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo and the twelfth son of Taketoki. When his brother Takeshige, the thirteenth head, died in 1341, Takehito succeeded him over his older brothers because his mother was of high birth. He proved a weak leader: in 1343 the Ōtomo invaded Higo and the clan was sustained only by his brothers Takemochi and Taketoshi. His rule so dissatisfied the clan that his elder brother Takemitsu deposed him, after which Takehito took Buddhist vows. He died in 1352.
zh: 菊池武士（1321—1352）是肥后菊池氏第十四代当主，菊池武时的第十二子。1341年第十三代当主、次兄武重去世后，他因母亲出身高贵，越过诸位兄长与外甥继任当主。但他生性柔弱，缺乏当主才干：1343年大友氏入侵肥后，全靠五兄武茂、九兄武敏辅佐才勉强支撑家势。他的声望不敌夺回深川城的十兄武光，最终被废去家督之位，出家为僧，1352年去世。

en: Kikuchi Takemitsu (c. 1321–1373) became the fifteenth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo after displacing his ineffective brother Takehito. As the leading Southern Court general in Kyushu, he served the Seisei shōgun Prince Kanenaga: he defeated the Northern Court's Kyushu tandai Isshiki Noriuji at Harisuruhara in 1353, crushed the Shōni at the Chikugo River in 1359 and occupied Dazaifu in 1361. His eastward campaign of 1368 was blocked near Shimonoseki by the Ōuchi, and in 1372 the new tandai Imagawa Sadayo stormed Dazaifu. Takemitsu withdrew with Prince Kanenaga to Kōra-san in Chikugo and died in 1373.
zh: 菊池武光（约1321—1373）废黜柔弱的弟弟武士后，成为肥后菊池氏第十五代当主。作为南朝在九州的主将，他辅佐征西将军怀良亲王：1353年在针摺原击败北朝九州探题一色范氏，1359年在筑后川大破少贰氏，1361年攻取大宰府，迎来征西府的鼎盛期。1368年他的东征在下关附近被大内氏阻挡；1372年新任探题今川贞世攻陷大宰府，武光随怀良亲王退据筑后高良山，于1373年去世。

en: Kikuchi Takeshige (died August 1341) was the 13th head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province and a son of Kikuchi Taketoki. In 1333 he joined his father's attack on the Kamakura shogunate's Chinzei tandai Hōjō Hidetoki at Hakata; Ōtomo Sadamune and Shōni Sadatsune, who had secretly agreed to join Taketoki, instead counterattacked, and Taketoki was killed while Takeshige fled home to succeed him. Under Emperor Go-Daigo's Kenmu Restoration he was made governor of Higo for his father's merit. In 1335 he served under Nitta Yoshisada against Ashikaga Takauji, and from 1337 led Southern Court armies in Kyushu, winning at Inuzuka and Ishigakiyama.
zh: 菊池武重（?—1341年）是肥后国菊池氏第十三代家督，菊池武时之子。1333年，他随父亲进攻身在博多的镰仓幕府镇西探题北条英时；大友贞宗、少贰贞经倒戈反击，武时战死，武重逃回本国继任家督。后醍醐天皇推行建武新政，以其父之功封他为肥后守，领有肥后一国。1335年他隶属新田义贞麾下与足利尊氏作战；1337年起率领九州的南朝军队，在犬冢原、石垣山击败北朝军。

en: Kikuchi Taketoki (1292–1333) was the twelfth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province in Kyūshū. He succeeded as a child after his brother Tokitaka and their uncle destroyed one another in a family feud. In 1333, answering Emperor Go-Daigo's call to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate, he plotted with the Ōtomo and Shōni to attack the Chinzei tandai at Hakata. When the plan leaked and his allies held back, Taketoki attacked anyway on the thirteenth day of the third month and fell with two hundred clansmen. His failed rising opened Kyūshū's anti-shogunate revolt; the tandai fell two months later.
zh: 菊池武時（1292—1333）是九州肥后国菊池氏的第十二代当主。其兄第11代当主菊池时隆与叔父武本相争、同归于尽后，他幼年继任家督。1333年，他响应后醍醐天皇推翻镰仓幕府的号召，与大友贞宗、少贰贞经合谋进攻博多的镇西探题北条英时。计划泄露、盟友按兵不动，武时仍于三月十三日举兵，与约二百名族人一同战死。他这次失败的举兵揭开了九州倒幕运动的序幕，两个月后镇西探题便告覆灭。

en: Kikuchi Taketoshi (died 1357), ninth son of Kikuchi Taketoki, was a Kyushu warrior of the Southern Court in the Nanboku-chō wars. For his father's service to Emperor Go-Daigo he was made Kamon-no-suke. In 1335 he rose in Higo against Ashikaga Takauji and defeated Shōni Sadatsune. At Tatara-no-hama in 1336 Takauji defeated Taketoshi's larger army; his allies Aso Korenao and Kamachi Takehisa fell, and he fled alone into the hills. He died in Usa, Buzen, in 1357.
zh: 菊池武敏（？—1357）是菊池氏第十二代当主菊池武时的第九子，日本南北朝时期效力南朝的九州武将，通称菊池九郎。因父亲为后醍醐天皇效忠之功，他被任为扫部助。1335年他在肥后举兵反对足利尊氏，击败少贰贞经。1336年多多良滨之战中，尊氏大破武敏的军队，同盟阿苏惟直、蒲池武久战死，他仅以身免逃入山中。1357年他死于丰前国宇佐郡。

en: Kikuchi Takeyoshi (died 1377), also called Fukagawa Takeyoshi, was a son of the twelfth Kikuchi clan head Taketoki and a younger brother of Takemitsu, the fifteenth head. A warrior of noted bravery, he served the Southern Court in Kyushu and defeated an attack by the tandai Shiba Ujitsune. After Takemitsu and his heir Takemasa died, Takeyoshi and his nephew Takeyasu supported the twelve-year-old new head Taketomo. In 1377 he was killed fighting the tandai Imagawa Sadayo's army in Hizen.
zh: 菊池武义（？—1377），一作深川武义，是菊池氏第十二代当主菊池武时之子、第十五代当主武光之弟，以勇武著称，为南朝效力于九州。他击退了九州探题斯波氏经的进攻。武光及其继承人武政相继死后，他与侄子武安辅佐年仅十二岁的新当主武朝，苦撑南朝方的局势。1377年，他在肥前蜷打之战中迎战探题今川贞世，兵败战死。

en: Kikuchi Takezumi (died 1357), known as Rokurō, was a commander of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period and the sixth son of Kikuchi Taketoki, twelfth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province.
zh: 菊池武澄（?—1357年）是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，肥后国菊池氏第十二代家督菊池武时的第六子，通称六郎。

en: Kikuchi Tokitaka (1287–1304), childhood name Jirō, was the eleventh head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo and eldest son of Kikuchi Takamori. With his father already dead, he succeeded his grandfather Takefusa. One account says that in 1304 he and his uncle Kikuchi Takemoto killed each other after the Kamakura bakufu ruled in Tokitaka's favor in a land dispute; another says he died of illness. His younger brother Taketoki succeeded as the twelfth head.
zh: 菊池时隆（1287—1304），幼名次郎，是肥后国菊池氏第十一代当主，菊池隆盛的长子。因父亲早逝，他继承祖父武房的家督。一说1304年他与叔父菊池武本因土地争执涉讼，镰仓幕府裁决土地归时隆后，二人互刺而死；另有病死之说。其弟武时随后继任为第十二代当主。

en: The Kikuchi clan genealogies name Tsunemune as the fourth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province, succeeding his father Tsuneyori. His son Tsunenao became the fifth head, and his grandson Takanao led the clan during the Genpei War.
zh: 菊池氏系图以菊池经宗为肥后国菊池氏第四代当主，继其父第三代当主菊池经赖而立，子菊池经直继为第五代当主，孙菊池隆直活跃于源平合战时期。

en: The genealogies name Tsunenao as the fifth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo, succeeding his father Tsunemune. He was the father of Kikuchi Takanao, the sixth head, who rose against the Taira in Kyushu in 1180.
zh: 菊池氏系图以菊池经直为肥后国菊池氏第五代当主，继其父第四代当主菊池经宗而立。其子菊池隆直为第六代当主，于1180年在九州举兵反抗平家。

en: Kikuchi Tsunetaka (1053–1105), also called Fujiwara no Tsunetaka, was the second head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo and the third son of the founder Noritaka, whom he succeeded. During the Kanji era (1087–1094) he is credited with inviting the deities of the Akita Suwa and Hachiman shrines of Dewa to branch shrines in Kikuchi. He died on 28 June 1105; a grave was later said to stand at Ideda Wakamiya Shrine, though no gravestone remains.
zh: 菊池经隆（1053—1105），一作藤原经隆，是肥后菊池氏初代当主则隆的第三子，继承父业成为第二代当主。据认为，宽治年间（1087—1094）他将出羽国秋田诹访宫与八幡宫劝请至菊池，设立分社。他于1105年6月28日去世，相传熊本县菊池市的出田若宫神社建有其墓，但今已无墓碑存世。

en: Kikuchi Tsunetsugu (1187–1204), written Takatsugu in some clan genealogies, was the heir of the seventh head Takasada and father of the eighth head Yoshitaka. He died before his father, so his son Yoshitaka succeeded Takasada instead.
zh: 菊池经继（1187—1204），菊池氏系图一作隆继，是第七代当主菊池隆定的继承人、第八代当主菊池能隆之父。他先于父亲去世，后由其子能隆继承隆定的家督。

en: Kikuchi Tsuneyori, also called Fujiwara no Tsuneyori, was the third head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province, succeeding his father Tsunetaka, the second head. He was in turn succeeded by his son Tsunemune, the fourth head of the clan.
zh: 菊池经赖，一作藤原经赖，是肥后国菊池氏第三代当主，继其父、第二代当主经隆之后继任家督；他死后由其子、第四代当主经宗继任。

en: Kikuchi Yoshitaka (1201–1258), known as Yajirō, was the eighth head of the Kikuchi clan of Higo Province and a Kamakura bakufu vassal. His father Tsunetsugu died in 1204, leaving him heir to his grandfather Takasada, the seventh head. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he backed Retired Emperor Go-Toba; his uncles Ietaka and Takamoto fought at Uji, and after the court's defeat the clan's estates were greatly reduced. He kept the headship, married daughters of Fujiwara no Kinkiyo and Ōtomo Yoshinao, and died in 1258.
zh: 菊池能隆（1201—1258），通称弥次郎，是肥后国菊池氏第八代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。其父经继于1204年去世，他遂成为祖父、第七代当主隆定的继承人。1221年承久之乱中，他支持后鸟羽上皇，叔父菊池家隆、菊池隆元在宇治参战；朝廷败北后，菊池氏领地被大幅削减。他保住了家督，娶藤原公清之女及大友能直之女为妻，1258年去世。

en: Kimotsuki Kanefuji was the sixth head of the Kimotsuki clan of Ōsumi in the late Kamakura period. His son Kanehisa succeeded him as seventh head; another son, Kaneshige, first held the Ogihara branch lands at Mimata in Hyūga, then became eighth clan head.
zh: 肝付兼藤是镰仓时代后期大隅国肝付氏的第六代当主，儿子兼尚继为第七代当主；其子兼重起初领有庶流荻原氏在日向三俣的领地，后来成为第八代当主。

en: Kimotsuki Kanehisa was the seventh head of the Kimotsuki clan of Osumi, succeeding his father Kanefuji. Kept at Kamakura by a lawsuit in the early Nanboku-chō wars, he left the clan's lands to his brother Kaneshige, who succeeded him as eighth head.
zh: 肝付兼尚是大隅国肝付氏的第七代当主，继父亲兼藤之后统率家族。南北朝动乱初期，他因诉讼事件滞留镰仓，将家族领地交由弟弟兼重打理，后来兼重继他之后成为第八代当主。

en: Kimotsuki Kaneishi was the fifth head of the Kimotsuki clan, the warrior house based at Takayama in Ōsumi Province. He succeeded his father Kanekazu and was followed as head by his son Kanefuji.
zh: 肝付兼石是以大隅国高山为据点的武家肝付氏的第五代当主，继父亲兼员之后统率家族，死后由儿子兼藤继任。

en: Kimotsuki Kanekazu was the fourth head of the Kimotsuki clan, the warrior house based at Takayama in Ōsumi Province. He succeeded his father Kanemasu and was followed as head by his son Kaneishi.
zh: 肝付兼员是以大隅国高山为据点的武家肝付氏的第四代当主，继父亲兼益之后统率家族，死后由儿子兼石继任。

en: Kimotsuki Kanemasu was the third head of the Kimotsuki clan, the warrior house based at Takayama in Ōsumi Province. He succeeded his father Kanetsune and was followed as head by his son Kanekazu.
zh: 肝付兼益是以大隅国高山为据点的武家肝付氏的第三代当主，继父亲兼经之后统率家族，死后由儿子兼员继任。

en: Kimotsuki Kaneshige (d. 1349), second son of the Kimotsuki clan's sixth head Kanefuji, became its eighth head after managing the family lands as deputy for his brother Kanehisa. From late 1335 he held Takajō in Hyūga for the Southern Court, campaigning alongside Nobe Moritada and the Kikuchi against the Shimazu and Hatakeyama Noriaki. He repulsed Noriaki's attack on Takajō, but the fortress fell in 1339 and Kimotsuki power in Hyūga declined. He died of illness in 1349 shortly after attacking Ishii Shigenobu, and was succeeded by his son Arikane.
zh: 肝付兼重（？—1349）是肝付氏第六代当主兼藤的次子，曾代替兄长兼尚经营本家领地，最终成为第八代当主。1335年末，他以日向高城为据点归属南朝，与野边盛忠、菊池氏等协同转战，同岛津氏和畠山直显对抗。他在高城击退直显的进攻，但1339年高城陷落，肝付氏在日向的势力转衰。1349年他攻打石井重信，不久病死，其子秋兼继立。

en: Kimotsuki Kanetoshi was the first head of the Kimotsuki clan of Ōsumi Province. The eldest son of Tomo no Kanesada, an official of Kimotsuki district, he settled at Takayama in the district and took the clan name Kimotsuki from it. His younger brothers founded branch houses at Hagiwara, Anraku, Izumi and Umekita, with holdings across Satsuma, Ōsumi and Hyūga provinces. From Takayama the Kimotsuki grew into the greatest warrior house of southern Kyushu. His son Kanetsune succeeded him.
zh: 肝付兼俊是大隅国肝付氏的初代当主。他是肝属郡弁济使伴兼贞（一作平兼贞）的长子，迁居肝属郡的高山，并以郡名“肝付”为苗字。他的几个弟弟分别在萩原、安乐、出水、梅北建立分家，领地分布在萨摩、大隅、日向三国。肝付氏以高山为据点，逐渐成为南九州最大的武家豪族。他死后由儿子兼经继任。

en: Kimotsuki Kanetsune was the second head of the Kimotsuki clan, the warrior house based at Takayama in Ōsumi Province. He succeeded his father Kanetoshi, founder of the clan, and was himself succeeded by his son Kanemasu.
zh: 肝付兼经是以大隅国高山为据点的武家肝付氏的第二代当主，继初代当主、父亲兼俊之后统率家族，死后由儿子兼益继任。

en: Kinmei (509–571), the 29th emperor of Japan, reigned from 539 and is often regarded as the first historically verifiable Yamato sovereign. A son of Emperor Keitai, he succeeded his half-brother Senka and ruled from the Shikishima no Kanazashi palace with Soga no Iname and Mononobe no Okoshi as chief counselors. In 552 King Seong of Baekje sent a Buddha image and scriptures, marking Buddhism's official arrival in Japan and opening the Soga–Mononobe feud. Silla overran Japan's Korean foothold of Mimana, and his expeditions failed to recover it. Four of his children became sovereigns: Bidatsu, Yōmei, Sushun and Suiko.
zh: 钦明天皇（509—571）是日本第29代天皇，539—571年在位，常被视为第一位可由史料证实的大和王权君主。他是继体天皇之子，继异母兄宣化天皇即位，在矶城岛金刺宫理政，以苏我稻目、物部尾舆为大臣、大连。552年百济圣明王向他赠送佛像与经论，标志佛教正式传入日本，也开启了苏我氏与物部氏的对立。其间新罗攻灭日本在朝鲜半岛的据点任那，他多次出兵均未能收复。他的四名子女先后成为君主：敏达、用明、崇峻与推古。

en: Kira Mitsuie was the second Ōshū kanrei and eldest son of Kira Sadaie. When his father took up the northern post in 1345, the Tōjō Kira moved from Mikawa to Mutsu and based themselves at Taga Castle. In the Kannō Disturbance Mitsuie backed Ashikaga Tadayoshi and helped destroy his co-kanrei Hatakeyama Kuniuji, becoming sole Ōshū kanrei. He retook Taga Castle from a Southern Court army in 1352 and captured Utsumine in 1353. Driven out in 1354, he fled to the Date clan and recovered the castle that July. His last surviving documents date to October 1356.
zh: 吉良满家是第二代奥州管领、吉良贞家的嫡子。1345年其父就任奥州管领后，东条吉良氏全族从三河迁往陆奥，以多贺城为据点。观应之乱中，满家支持足利直义，参与攻灭同为奥州管领的畠山国氏，成为独任管领。1352年他从南朝军手中夺回多贺城，1353年攻陷宇津峰城。1354年他被逐出多贺城，逃往伊达氏处，于当年七月收复该城。其存世文书止于1356年10月。

en: Kira Mitsusada (died 1384) was lord of Saijō Castle in Mikawa Province, eldest son of Kira Mitsuyoshi and founder of the Saijō Kira branch. He joined Ashikaga Takauji's rising with his father, and in the Kannō Disturbance fought for Ashikaga Tadayoshi; after Tadayoshi's death he allied with the Southern Court and briefly seized Kyoto. In 1360 he blocked Hatakeyama Kunikiyo's retreat at Yahagi in Mikawa, but submitted to the shogunate in 1361. His Hikuma manor in Tōtōmi was restored in 1362, and from 1363 he served 21 years as a hikitsuke headman. He died in 1384.
zh: 吉良满贞（？—1384）是三河国西条城城主，吉良满义的嫡子，西条吉良氏之祖。他随父亲参加足利尊氏起兵，观应之乱中为足利直义作战；直义死后，他与南朝结盟，一度攻占京都。1360年他在三河矢作阻挡畠山国清撤退，1361年归顺幕府。1362年其远江国引马庄被发还，1363年起担任引付头人21年，1384年去世。

en: Kira Mitsuuji was a late-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, lord of Saijō in Mikawa, heir of Kira Osauji; his wife was a daughter of Ashikaga Yasuji, and he held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The Azuma Kagami first records him in 1252 escorting Shōgun Prince Munetaka into Kamakura; after guard service he returned to Kira Manor in 1263. In 1271 he invited Zen monk Enni from Tōfuku-ji to found Jissō-ji. After the first Mongol invasion he became shugo of Echizen, the only Ashikaga branch head with such a post. He took vows around 1284 and was killed in the Shimotsuki incident of 1285.
zh: 吉良满氏是镰仓时代后期武将、御家人，三河国西条领主、吉良长氏的嫡子，妻子为足利泰氏之女，位至从五位下。《吾妻镜》中他最早于1252年随新将军宗尊亲王进入镰仓时出现，担任番役之后于1263年回到吉良庄。1271年，他请来东福寺的禅僧圆尔创建实相寺。文永之役后，他出任越前国守护，是足利庶流中唯一担任守护者。他约于1284年出家，1285年在霜月骚乱中被杀于镰仓。

en: Kira Mitsuyoshi (died 1356) was lord of Saijō Castle in Mikawa Province and a Northern and Southern Courts era warrior. He took part in Ashikaga Takauji's assault on the Rokuhara Tandai in the Genkō War and in 1334 became a headman of the six Kantō hisaban guard units. He fought at the Battle of Aonogahara in Mino in 1338 and served as shugo of Shinano Province around 1340, later assisting Ashikaga Tadayoshi's administration in Kyoto. In the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Tadayoshi before returning to the Northern Court, and in 1355 he guarded Emperor Go-Kōgon. He died in 1356.
zh: 吉良满义（？—1356）是三河国西条城城主、南北朝时代武将。元弘之乱中，他随足利尊氏进攻六波罗探题，1334年任关东厢番六番头人。1338年他参加美浓国青野原之战，约1340年就任信浓国守护，其后在京都辅佐足利直义处理政务。观应之乱中他站在直义一方，后来归顺北朝；1355年奉命警卫后光严天皇，1356年去世。

en: Kira Osauji (1211–1290) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, the eldest son of Ashikaga Yoshiuji and founder of the Kira clan. Born to a low-ranking mother, he could not inherit the Ashikaga main line and took Kira Manor in Mikawa as his fief and his name. The Azuma Kagami first names him in 1228 escorting Shōgun Fujiwara no Yoritsune; he attended the shōgun's ceremonies until 1241, then returned to Kira Manor. In 1251 he built Tsurugasaki Tenmangū. After his heir Mitsuuji died in the Shimotsuki incident of 1285, he adopted his grandson Sadayoshi, and died in 1290 aged eighty.
zh: 吉良长氏（1211—1290），又称足利长氏，是镰仓时代中期的武将、御家人，足利义氏的庶长子，吉良氏之祖。因生母身份低微，他虽为长子却不能继承足利宗家，领有三河国吉良庄，遂以吉良为姓。《吾妻镜》中他最早于1228年以四代将军藤原赖经随兵的身份出现，此后承役至1241年，之后便回到吉良庄。1251年，他营造鹤崎天满宫。1285年继承人满氏在霜月骚乱中死去，他收孙子贞义为养子，最终于1290年去世，享年八十岁。

en: Kira Sadaie (died c. 1354) was a Northern and Southern Courts era warrior and the first Ōshū kanrei, the Muromachi shogunate's northern deputy. Eldest son of Kira Tsuneie of the Tōjō Kira branch in Mikawa, he fought at Hakone-Takenoshita in December 1335 and across Owari and Mikawa in 1336, later serving as shugo of Inaba and Tajima. In 1345 he was appointed Ōshū kanrei jointly with Hatakeyama Kuniuji. During the Kannō Disturbance he destroyed the Hatakeyama in 1351, retook Taga Castle in 1352 and stormed the Southern Court base of Utsumine in 1353, after which he disappears from the records.
zh: 吉良贞家（？—约1354）是南北朝时代武将、初代奥州管领，即室町幕府统辖北方诸州的代表。他是三河东条吉良氏吉良经家的嫡子，1335年12月参加箱根·竹之下之战，1336年转战尾张与三河，后任因幡、但马两国守护。1345年他与畠山国氏同任奥州管领。观应之乱中他于1351年攻灭畠山氏，1352年夺回多贺城，1353年攻陷南朝据点宇津峰城，此后便不见于史料。

en: Kira Sadatsune (fl. 1335–1367) was a warrior of the Tōjō Kira branch in Mikawa and younger brother of the Ōshū kanrei Kira Sadaie. When his brother marched east in 1336, Sadatsune stayed to hold Kira Manor and is the likely commander who defeated Nitta's Southern Court army there that April. During the Kannō Disturbance he alone of the Kira backed Takauji and Kō no Moronao. In 1352 and 1353 he fought in Mutsu, helping retake Taga Castle and storm Utsumine. After 1367 he vanishes from the records amid a feud within the clan.
zh: 吉良贞经（活动于1335—1367年）是三河东条吉良氏武将，奥州管领吉良贞家之弟。1336年其兄东进时，他留守吉良庄，很可能就是当年4月在吉良庄击退新田氏南朝军的大将。观应之乱中，吉良一族多支持足利直义，唯有他支持足利尊氏与高师直。1352至1353年他转战陆奥，参与夺回多贺城、攻陷宇津峰城。1367年族内争斗之后，他便下落不明。

en: Kira Sadayoshi (died 1343), also called Ashikaga Sadayoshi, was lord of Saijō Castle in Mikawa Province and a Kamakura vassal. During the Kōan invasion of 1281 he is said to have gone down to Iwami Province as a commander. After his father Mitsuuji was killed in the Shimotsuki Disturbance of 1285, he became heir to his grandfather Nagauji. In 1333 at Yatsuhashi he encouraged Ashikaga Takauji's decision to rebel against the Hōjō, and he went on to fight in the Nakasendai War of 1335 and the campaigns of 1336. He died in 1343.
zh: 吉良贞义（？—1343），又称足利贞义，是三河国西条城城主、镰仓幕府御家人。相传1281年弘安之役时，他以大将身份前往石见国。1285年父亲吉良满氏在霜月骚乱中被杀，他作为祖父吉良长氏的养子继承家业。1333年在三河八桥，他支持足利高氏起兵讨伐北条氏的决断，此后参加1335年的中先代之乱与1336年的诸役，于1343年去世。

en: Kira Tsuneie was a warrior of the Kamakura period (1185–1333) and the third head of the Oshu, or Musashi, branch of the Kira clan, the early Tojo Kira. A note in the Sonpi Bunmyaku gives him the style Fujitani; he is said to have held the Fujitani estate in Adachi district of Mutsu province and taken the Fujitani name. Tradition also credits him with building Yotsuhongamatsu Castle there, but the estate's location is unknown and the story is unconfirmed, perhaps confused with the career of his son Sadaie, who wielded great power as Oshu kanrei.
zh: 吉良经家是镰仓时代（1185—1333年）的武将，吉良氏奥州（武藏）家，即前期东条吉良氏的第三代当主。《尊卑分脉》在他的注下写有“号藤谷”；另有说法称他领有陆奥国安达郡的藤谷庄，并以藤谷为氏。相传他还在当地修筑四本松城并据守于此，但藤谷庄的位置至今不明，此说并无确证，可能是与其子贞家担任奥州管领、威势显赫的事迹混淆后产生的传承。

en: Kira Tsuneuji was a warrior of the Kamakura period (1185–1333) and the second head of the Oshu, or Musashi, branch of the Kira clan, the early Tojo Kira. He is usually called a son of Kira Yoshitsugu, but other accounts make him the natural son of Kira Mitsuuji of the Saijo Kira, or Yoshitsugu's son adopted by Mitsuuji after Yoshitsugu went to China and took Buddhist vows. The Sonpi Bunmyaku first attaches the Kira name to his line, suggesting his generation may have been the first to hold Tojo.
zh: 吉良经氏是镰仓时代（1185—1333年）的武将，吉良氏奥州（武藏）家，即前期东条吉良氏的第二代当主。一般认为他是吉良义继之子，但也有说法称他是西条吉良氏吉良满氏的亲生儿子，或本为义继之子，在义继渡唐出家后被满氏收为养子。《尊卑分脉》在他的名字下首次标注“号吉良”，因此有看法认为，东条吉良氏可能是从经氏这一代起才领有东条之地。

en: Kitabatake Akiie (1318–1338) was the eldest son of Kitabatake Chikafusa and a Southern Court general in the Nanboku-chō wars. In 1333 he accompanied his father and Prince Noriyoshi to Taga Castle in Mutsu and rallied the Date, Yūki and Nambu warrior houses of the northeast to the court. He later became chinjufu shōgun. In 1336 he marched west and helped Nitta Yoshisada drive Ashikaga Takauji from Kyoto. Campaigning south again in 1338 he captured Kamakura and won at Aonohara, but on 10 June was overwhelmed and killed by Kō no Moronao at the Battle of Ishizu in Izumi, aged twenty.
zh: 北畠显家（1318—1338）是北畠亲房的长子，南北朝时代的南朝武将。1333年，他随父亲护卫义良亲王进驻陆奥国多贺城，号召伊达、结城、南部等东北武士家族为朝廷效力，后来出任镇守府将军。1336年建武之乱中，他西上勤王，与新田义贞等合力将足利尊氏逐出京都。1338年他再度南下，攻陷镰仓并在青野原取胜，却于6月10日在和泉国石津之战中被高师直的军队围攻击杀，年仅20岁。

en: Kitabatake Akinari (c. 1335–1386) was a Southern Court noble in Japan's Nanboku-chō era and the legitimate son of Kitabatake Akiie, who died fighting for Emperor Go-Daigo in 1338. He first appears in court records in 1352 with junior fourth rank, and in 1378 was made provisional major counselor of junior second rank; one source hints he reached inner minister. Later traditions make him a co-author of the Taiheiki under the clerical name Gyōi, a follower of Prince Kanenaga in Kyushu, and ancestor of the Namioka Kitabatake family.
zh: 北畠显成（约1335—1386）是日本南北朝时代南朝的公卿，为1338年追随后醍醐天皇战死的北畠显家的嫡男。他于1352年（正平七年）首见记载，叙从四位上，1378年叙任从二位权大纳言，更有史料暗示他位至内大臣。后世传说称他出家后法号行意、参与撰写《太平记》，又有追随怀良亲王前往九州、成为浪冈北畠氏之祖等说法，这些事迹真伪难定。

en: Kitabatake Akinobu (1320–c. 1380) was the second son of Kitabatake Chikafusa and a Southern Court court noble of the Nanboku-chō wars, called the Kasuga Shōshō. In 1336 he raised troops in Ise for Emperor Go-Daigo and became Ise governor. After his brother Akiie fell in 1338 he succeeded him as chinjufu shōgun and fought on in Mutsu, holding Ryōzen Castle until 1347. In 1351 he routed a Northern Court army at the Hirose River and retook Taga Castle, but Kira Sadaie drove him out in 1352. He moved to Utsumine Castle and, after its fall in 1353, reportedly withdrew to Dewa. He died around 1380; his daughter became empress to Emperor Go-Kameyama.
zh: 北畠显信（1320—约1380）是北畠亲房的次子、北畠显家之弟，南北朝时代的南朝公卿，通称春日少将。1336年他在伊势国起兵援助后醍醐天皇，就任伊势国司。1338年兄长显家战死后，他继任镇守府将军，在陆奥坚持抵抗，据守灵山城直至1347年落城。1351年，他在广濑川击溃北朝军队、夺回多贺城，但于1352年被吉良贞家逐出。他转往宇津峰城，据传1353年城陷后退往出羽。他约于1380年去世，其女后来成为后龟山天皇的中宫。

en: Kitabatake Akiyoshi (c. 1326–c. 1383) was the third son of Kitabatake Chikafusa and the founder of the Ise Kitabatake house. He went to Ise Province in 1336, built Tamamaru Castle and was apparently appointed governor around 1338. After the castle fell in 1342, he held Taki as the Southern Court's bulwark. In 1352 he led three thousand Ise and Iga cavalry into Kyoto, routed Hosokawa Akiuji at Shichijō-Ōmiya alongside Kusunoki Masanori, and drove Ashikaga Yoshiakira into Ōmi to briefly restore Southern rule; defeated at Otokoyama, he escorted the emperor to Anō. Eighteen of his verses appear in the Shin'yō Wakashū; later war chronicles say he died at Taki in 1383.
zh: 北畠显能（约1326—约1383）是北畠亲房的第三子，伊势北畠氏的始祖。1336年他前往伊势国，修筑玉丸城，约于1338年受任伊势守；1342年玉丸城陷落后，他改以多气为据点，充当南朝在伊势的屏障。1352年，他率伊势、伊贺骑兵三千攻入京都，与楠木正仪等在七条大宫击败细川显氏，将足利义诠驱往近江，一度恢复南朝对京都的统治；男山战败后，他护送天皇退往贺名生。《新叶和歌集》收录其十八首和歌，后世军记称他于1383年在多气去世。

en: Kitabatake Chikafusa (1293–1354) was a Murakami Genji court noble and a chief advisor to Emperor Go-Daigo in the Kenmu restoration of 1333. That year he accompanied his son Akiie and Prince Noriyoshi, the future Emperor Go-Murakami, to Taga Castle in Mutsu to govern the northeast. After Ashikaga Takauji revolted he joined the Southern Court at Yoshino, and in 1339, directing resistance from Oda Castle in Hitachi, wrote the chronicle Jinnō Shōtōki in defence of the Southern imperial line. From 1344 he led the court under Go-Murakami, briefly retook Kyoto during the Kannō Disturbance, and died at Anō in 1354.
zh: 北畠亲房（1293—1354）出身村上源氏，是后醍醐天皇建武新政的核心谋臣。1333年，他随儿子显家，护卫后来成为后村上天皇的义良亲王前往陆奥国多贺城，经营东北。足利尊氏反叛后，他加入吉野南朝；1339年前后在常陆国小田城主持抵抗时，撰写《神皇正统记》，以日本通史论证南朝皇统的正统。1344年返回吉野后，他辅佐后村上天皇总揽南朝政务，在观应之乱期间一度收复京都，1354年在贺名生去世。

en: Kitabatake Masaie (1215–1275) was a court noble of the early to mid-Kamakura period and the founder of the Kitabatake house. He was born the second son of Senior Counselor Minamoto no Michikata, founder of the Nakanoin family, but was treated as a non-heir son while his younger brother Michishige carried on the main line. Masaie built his residence at Kitabatake, in the northern outskirts of Kyoto, and adopted that place name as his family name. He died in 1275; the house he founded rose to prominence only under his great-grandson Chikafusa.
zh: 北畠雅家（1215—1275）是镰仓时代前期至中期的公卿、北畠家之祖。他是中院家之祖、大纳言源通方的次男，被作为庶子对待，由弟弟通成继承中院家嫡系。雅家后来在京都北郊洛北的北畠营建宅邸，遂以地名为家名，开创北畠家。他于1275年去世，享年61岁；北畠家直到其曾孙亲房一代才登上历史舞台。

en: Kitabatake Morochika (1241–1315) was a court noble of the middle and late Kamakura period, the son of Kitabatake Masaie, founder of the Kitabatake house. He was the father of Moroshige and the grandfather of the later court statesman Chikafusa. In the ninth month of 1289, when the Retired Emperor Kameyama took Buddhist vows and became a cloistered emperor, Morochika entered religion alongside him. He died on the sixth day of the tenth month of 1315, at the age of seventy-five.
zh: 北畠师亲（1241—1315）是镰仓时代中期至后期的公卿，为北畠家开创者北畠雅家之子，师重之父、后来的朝廷重臣北畠亲房之祖父。1289年九月，龟山上皇出家成为法皇时，师亲也随之一同遁入佛门。他于1315年十月六日去世，享年75岁。

en: Kitabatake Moroshige (1271–1322) was a court noble of the late Kamakura period, son of the councillor Morochika and father of the statesman Chikafusa. A trusted attendant of the Retired Emperor Go-Uda, he rose through Iwami governor and guards offices to Junior Third Rank in 1291, joining the senior nobility, and became Provisional Major Counselor in 1303. He resigned that post in 1305, and in 1307 took Buddhist vows under the name Kyōgaku when Go-Uda himself became a monk. After fifteen years in retreat he died in 1322, aged fifty-three. Seven of his poems enter imperial anthologies.
zh: 北畠师重（1271—1322）是镰仓时代后期的公卿，为权大纳言师亲之子、名臣北畠亲房之父。他深受后宇多上皇信任，历任石见守、近卫府武官，1291年叙从三位跻身公卿，1303年升任权大纳言。1305年他辞去权大纳言之职，1307年后宇多上皇落饰时随其出家，法名经觉。隐居十五年后，于1322年去世，享年53岁。他有七首和歌被敕撰和歌集收录。

en: Uesugi Kiyoko (1270–1343) was the mother of Ashikaga Takauji and Tadayoshi, the brothers who founded the Muromachi shogunate. A daughter of Uesugi Yorishige of the Fujiwara-line Uesugi clan, she became a concubine of Ashikaga Sadauji and bore Takauji in 1305. After her husband's death she sustained the Ashikaga house and stayed with her sons through the wars that overthrew the Kamakura shogunate, then used her position to advance the Uesugi. Known as the Nun Ōkata, she was also a waka poet with verses in the Fūgashū; she died on 20 January 1343.
zh: 上杉清子（1270—1343）是开创室町幕府的足利尊氏、直义兄弟之母。她出身藤原姓劝修寺流的上杉氏，为上杉赖重之女，做了足利贞氏的侧室，1305年生下尊氏。丈夫死后她支撑足利家，尊氏、直义兄弟起兵倒幕时始终随行；幕府建立后，她又倾力提携娘家上杉氏。她世称锦小路殿、大方禅尼，还擅长和歌，作品入选《风雅集》，于1343年1月20日去世，墓在京都等持院。

en: Kobayakawa no Kagehira was an early Kamakura-period warrior, a shogunal gokenin ruling the Numata estate in Aki Province. Born the fifth son of Hiraga Yoshinobu, he was adopted by Dohi Tōhira, jitō of Numata, and took the Kobayakawa name. In 1206 he divided Numata between his eldest son Shigehira and second son Suehira, founding the Numata and Takehara branches, and secured confirmation from Minamoto no Sanetomo and Hōjō Masako in 1207. After his adoptive brother Korehira was captured and executed for supporting Wada Yoshimori in the Wada disturbance of 1213, he also inherited the Dohi main line. He died on 18 August 1244.
zh: 小早川景平是镰仓时代初期的武将、统治安艺国沼田庄的镰仓幕府御家人。他本是平贺义信第五子，被沼田庄地头土肥远平收为养子，改称小早川。1206年，他将领地沼田庄分给嫡子茂平与次子季平，分别开创沼田小早川氏和竹原小早川氏两支，并于1207年取得源实朝与北条政子的下文、获得幕府承认。1213年和田合战时，养父的嫡子土肥维平因追随和田义盛被捕处死，他于是又继承土肥氏嫡流。1244年8月18日去世。

en: Kobayakawa no Masahira succeeded his father Shigehira as head of the Numata-Kobayakawa at Takayama Castle in Aki, receiving the main Numata estate. In 1276 he built a fort across the Numata River, later Shin-Takayama Castle. His son Tomohira succeeded him.
zh: 小早川雅平继父亲茂平之后成为沼田小早川氏当主，领有安艺国高山城与沼田本庄。1276年，他在沼田川对岸修筑砦垒，即后来的新高山城。其子朝平继位。

en: Kobayakawa no Nobuhira was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts period who headed the Numata-Kobayakawa clan of Aki Province, succeeding his father Tomohira. He settled Numata estate lands on his sons: his heir Sadahira received Yasunao, a son Saizuru-maru took newly opened fields in 1341 and later founded the Ikuguchi family, and his seventh son Ujizane was enfeoffed at Ura in Toyota district, founding the Ura family. In his generation the clan expanded into the Geiyo Islands of the Seto Inland Sea, laying the base of the Kobayakawa navy.
zh: 小早川宣平是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，继父亲朝平之后担任安艺国沼田小早川氏的当主。他把沼田庄内的领地分给诸子：继承人贞平受封安直等地，一子道祖鹤丸于1341年分得新垦田地，后来开创生口氏，第七子氏实受封丰田郡浦乡，创立浦氏。在他这一代，小早川氏开始向濑户内海的艺予群岛扩张，为小早川水军奠定基础。

en: Kobayakawa no Sadahira was head of the Numata-Kobayakawa clan of Aki Province, active from the late Kamakura through the Northern and Southern Courts period. In 1333, aged about sixteen, he fought for the Kamakura shogunate in the Genkō War, following the Rokuhara tandai's fleeing followers to their suicide at Renge-ji in Ōmi, then escaped to his Numata estate. In 1337 he received junior fifth rank and the office of Bingo no Kami, and in 1341 inherited Yasunao lands from his father Nobuhira. In 1351 he was appointed shugo, or military governor, of Aki.
zh: 小早川贞平是安艺国沼田小早川氏的当主，活跃于镰仓末期至南北朝时代。1333年元弘之乱时，他年约十六岁，作为镰仓幕府一方出阵，追随六波罗探题败走的族人一直到近江国番场莲华寺，目睹四百余人集体自刃后脱身，逃回本领沼田庄。1337年，他获封从五位下、备后守；1341年从父亲宣平手中继承安直等地；1351年被任命为安艺国守护。

en: Kobayakawa no Shigehira (died 1264) was a Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin vassal who held the Numata estate in Aki Province. In 1206 he and his younger brother Suehira divided their father Kagehira's lands, and Shigehira built Takayama Castle, the future seat of the Numata-Kobayakawa. He won distinction on the shogunate side in the Jōkyū War of 1221, receiving the stewardship of the Tsū-Takehara estate in Aki. From 1247 to 1257 he served in Kyoto, guarding the capital and the Rokuhara tandai. He later enfeoffed his younger sons and left the main Numata lands to his heir Masahira.
zh: 小早川茂平（1264年卒）是镰仓时代中期的武将，作为镰仓幕府御家人领有安艺国沼田庄。1206年，他与弟弟季平分割父亲景平的领地，并修筑高山城，此地后来成为沼田小早川氏的本据。1221年承久之乱中，他加入幕府一方立下军功，获封安艺国都宇竹原庄的地头职。1247至1257年间，他驻留京都，负责洛中警备并护卫六波罗探题。晚年他将领地分封给诸子，沼田本庄大部传给嫡子雅平。

en: Kobayakawa no Tomohira was head of the Numata-Kobayakawa clan of Aki Province and a powerful gokenin vassal of the Kamakura shogunate. Succeeding his father Masahira, he enforced shogunate orders against pirates of the Seto Inland Sea, capturing Uemon-Gorō and Uzaemon-Jirō in 1314 and the Iyo pirate Yagorō Iehide in 1319. During the Genkō War of 1333 he sent his grandson Sadahira to Kyoto on the shogunate's side; after its defeat the Kenmu regime seized the clan's Numata estate, until the Takehara branch interceded to win a pardon, after which the clan served the Ashikaga.
zh: 小早川朝平是安艺国沼田小早川氏的当主，也是镰仓幕府的有力御家人。他继承父亲雅平的家督后，奉幕府之命清剿濑户内海海盗，1314年擒获海盗右卫门五郎与雅乐左卫门次郎，1319年又擒获伊予国海盗弥五郎家秀。1333年元弘之乱时，他派孙子贞平前往京都加入幕府一方；幕府败亡后，建武政权没收了小早川氏的沼田庄领地，后经分家竹原小早川氏斡旋才获赦免，小早川氏此后转仕足利氏。

en: Kondō Kagechika (dates unknown) is recorded in the medieval genealogy Sonpi Bunmyaku as a member of the Kondō line descended from Fujiwara no Hidesato, the son of Kondō Yukikage and father of Kondō Kageyori; the Mutō and Ōtomo houses branched from Kageyori's line.
zh: 近藤景亲（生卒年不详）见于中世纪系谱《尊卑分脉》，属藤原秀乡流近藤氏，被记为近藤行景之子、近藤景赖之父；后来的武藤氏与大友氏即从景赖一支分出。

en: Kondō Kageshige (dates unknown) appears in the medieval genealogy Sonpi Bunmyaku as a member of the Kondō line descended from Fujiwara no Hidesato, recorded there as the son of Kondō Kagechika and grandfather of the Kamakura-period warrior Kondō Kunihira.
zh: 近藤景重（生卒年不详）见于中世纪系谱《尊卑分脉》，属藤原秀乡流近藤氏，被记为近藤景亲之子、镰仓时代武将近藤国平的祖父。

en: Kondō Kageyori, also called Shimada Kageyori (dates unknown), was a late Heian warrior of Kondō stock who served in the capital's mushadokoro guard office, a post his son Mutō Yorihira also held. Genealogies also name him father of Kondō Yoshishige, grandfather of Ōtomo Yoshinao.
zh: 近藤景赖（生卒年不详），又作岛田景赖，是平安时代后期出身近藤氏的武士，曾出仕京都的武者所，其子武藤赖平后来也担任同样职务。系图还载他是近藤能成之父、大友能直的祖父。

en: Kondō Kunihira (dates unknown) was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods whose family had held lands in Izu Province since his grandfather's day. He joined Minamoto no Yoritomo at the start of the Jishō-Juei War in 1180 and served as a Kamakura vassal. In the second month of 1185 he went up to Kyoto as Yoritomo's deputy, with Nakahara Hisatsune, to suppress lawless warriors around the capital, and later performed the same duty in Kyushu. In 1199 he was appointed shugo of Sanuki Province; the Sanuki-based Ōhira house claimed him as ancestor.
zh: 近藤国平（生卒年不详）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，其家族自祖父一代起便在伊豆国拥有地盘。1180年治承·寿永之乱爆发时，他在源赖朝举兵之初便加入麾下转战各地，成为镰仓御家人。1185年2月，他作为赖朝的代官与中原久经一同上洛，负责平定在畿内近国趁乱为非作歹的武士，随后又奉命前往镇西执行同样任务。1199年，他被任命为赞岐国守护；以赞岐为本据的大平氏自称是他的后裔。

en: Kondō Nobuyuki (dates unknown), son of Fujiwara no Fumiyuki and great-great-grandson of Fujiwara no Hidesato, founded the Kondō name: the medieval genealogy Sonpi Bunmyaku records him as jō secretary of Ōmi Province who took the first character of Ōmi as his surname.
zh: 近藤修行（生卒年不详）是藤原文行之子、藤原秀乡的玄孙；中世纪系谱《尊卑分脉》记载他是近藤一名的始祖：他任近江掾，取“近江”的“近”字为姓。

en: Kondō Yoshishige was a warrior of the late Heian period and the biological father of Ōtomo Yoshinao, founder of the Ōtomo clan. Of Fujiwara-descended Kondō stock, he served as gōji headman of Furusho-gō in Aikō District, Sagami Province, and joined Minamoto no Yoritomo during the Jishō-Juei War. In 1182 monks of the local Kongōji accused him before Kamakura of seizing temple lands and expelling them for a hunt, and Yoritomo ordered the abuses stopped. He married a daughter of Ōtomo Tsuneie of the Hatano group; their son Yoshinao was treated as a son by Nakahara Chikayoshi and inherited his Kyushu estates.
zh: 近藤能成是平安时代末期的武士，大友氏始祖大友能直的生父。他出身自称藤原氏后裔的近藤氏，任相模国爱甲郡古庄乡的乡司，在治承·寿永之乱中追随源赖朝。1182年，爱甲郡金刚寺的僧侣向镰仓控诉他贪图寺领、为围猎驱散僧人，赖朝裁定寺院胜诉，下令停止其非法行为。他娶波多野一族大友经家之女为妻，所生之子能直后来成为中原亲能的猶子，继承了亲能在九州北部的领地。

en: Kondō Yukikage (dates unknown) appears in the medieval genealogy Sonpi Bunmyaku as a link in the Kondō line descended from Fujiwara no Hidesato, recorded there as the son of Kondō Nobuyuki and the father of Kondō Kagechika.
zh: 近藤行景（生卒年不详）见于中世纪系谱《尊卑分脉》，在藤原秀乡流近藤氏的世系中，被记作近藤修行之子、近藤景亲之父。

en: Konoe (1139–1155), a son of Emperor Toba, was named heir at birth and enthroned in 1141 at age three after Toba forced Emperor Sutoku to abdicate. Throughout his reign his father ruled as cloistered emperor, while Fujiwara no Tadamichi served as regent until 1150. In 1150 Konoe married two Fujiwara consorts, one connected with Tadamichi and another raised by his rival Yorinaga, deepening their feud. He died in 1155 at seventeen without an heir, and the succession dispute that followed brought his brother Go-Shirakawa to the throne and set the stage for the Hōgen Rebellion.
zh: 近卫天皇（1139—1155）是鸟羽天皇之子，出生即被立为储君，1141年鸟羽逼迫崇德天皇退位后，年仅三岁的他登基。在位期间由父亲实行院政，藤原忠通担任摄政至1150年。1150年，他先后迎娶两位藤原氏后妃，一位与忠通有关，另一位由其政敌赖长抚养，加剧了两位公卿的对立。1155年他以十七岁早逝且无子嗣，随之而来的继位之争使兄长后白河天皇登位，并为保元之乱埋下伏笔。

en: Kotō Takefuji was a younger son of the Nagato warlord Kotō Takezane and a younger brother of Takemura. During the Kannō Disturbance the clan split over allegiance: its heads Takenao and Yoshitake backed the Muromachi shogunate and its Kyushu tandai Isshiki Noriuji, while Takefuji sided with Ashikaga Tadafuyu, Takauji's disaffected son, and the Southern Court. In 1352, after Tadafuyu was defeated by Isshiki at Dazaifu, he withdrew to Nagato, where Takefuji's branch held sway.
zh: 厚东武藤是长门武将厚东武实之子、武村之弟。观应之扰乱中，厚东氏因效忠对象分裂：当主武直、义武支持室町幕府和九州探题一色范氏，武藤则投向足利尊氏的叛子足利直冬与南朝。1352年直冬在大宰府被一色范氏击败后退往长门，即武藤一派势力所在之地。

en: Kotō Takeharu, called the Kotō Kodayū, was the sixth head of the Kotō clan of eastern Asa District in Nagato Province. He was the father of Takemitsu, the seventh head, under whom the clan fought in the Genpei War and built Shimofuri Castle.
zh: 厚东武晴，号厚东小大夫，是长门国厚狭郡东部豪族厚东氏的第六代当主。他是七代当主武光之父，厚东氏在武光一代参与源平合战，并修筑了霜降城。

en: Kotō Takehito was the fifth head of the Kotō clan, a Mononobe-descended warrior family of eastern Asa District in Nagato Province. A son of Takemichi, he followed his brother Taketsuna and fathered Takeharu, the sixth head.
zh: 厚东武仁是长门国厚狭郡东部豪族厚东氏的第五代当主，该族自称物部氏后裔。他是三代当主武通之子，继其兄武纲之后统领一族，其子武晴为第六代当主。
