en: Kotō Takekage was the eighth head of the Kotō clan, a Mononobe-descended warrior family of Nagato Province, and the son of Takemitsu. As district magistrate of Kotō he bore the title Kotō Dayū, and he inherited from his father the post of shugo, or military governor, of Nagato. His career marks the point at which the clan entered the service of the Kamakura shogunate: he died in Kamakura itself during the Jōkyū era of 1219–1222, leaving the headship to his son Takeyoshi. His Buddhist name was Jakuson.
zh: 厚东武景是长门国豪族厚东氏的第八代当主，物部姓，为七代当主武光之子。他任厚东郡郡司，号厚东大夫，并从父亲手中继承了长门守护一职。武景一代被视为厚东氏成为镰仓幕府御家人的时期：他于承久年间（1219—1222）在镰仓去世，当主之位由其子武能继承，法名寂尊。

en: Kotō Takemasa was the twelfth head of the Kotō warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province, and bore the warrior byname Shirōzaemon.
zh: 厚东武政是长门国厚狭郡武士厚东氏的第十二代当主，通称四郎左卫门。

en: Kotō Takemichi was the third head of the Kotō clan, a Mononobe-descended warrior family of eastern Asa District in Nagato Province. A son of Takemoto, he fathered Taketsuna and Takehito, the fourth and fifth clan heads.
zh: 厚东武通是长门国厚狭郡东部豪族厚东氏的第三代当主，该族自称物部氏后裔。他是二代当主武基之子，其子厚东武纲、厚东武仁分别成为第四代、第五代当主。

en: Kotō Takemitsu was the seventh head of the Kotō, a warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province, and its leader in the Genpei War. He held the provincial titles of shugo and police chief before the war began. He first fought for the Taira at the Battle of Ichinotani in 1184, but as the Taira collapsed he joined the Minamoto, and at Dannoura in 1185 he furnished the boatmen of Kushizaki in Chōfu for their fleet. He took Buddhist orders as Nensai and built Shimofuri Castle at Tanoi, now Ube.
zh: 厚东武光是长门国厚狭郡豪族厚东氏的第七代当主，在源平合战中统领一族；合战之前，他已身任长门守护职与押领使。他初随平氏，1184年投身一之谷之战，平氏败局渐显后转投源氏，1185年坛之浦之战时为源氏调集长府串崎的船头助战。他剃发出家，号念西，并在一族本据棚井（今宇部市）修筑了霜降城。

en: Kotō Takemoto was the second head of the Kotō clan, a Mononobe-descended warrior family of eastern Asa District in Nagato Province. He succeeded his father Taketada, who had settled the clan at Tanoi, now in Ube, and was followed by his son Takemichi.
zh: 厚东武基是长门国厚狭郡东部豪族厚东氏的第二代当主，该族自称物部氏后裔。他继定居棚井（今宇部市）的初代当主武忠之后统领一族，后由其子武通继任。

en: Kotō Takemura was the fifteenth head of the Kotō warrior clan of Nagato Province and the son of Takezane. In 1333 he and his father turned against the Hōjō and attacked the Nagato tandai, and the next year he was enfeoffed with Kikuna District in Buzen Province for his service. In 1335 he served in Nitta Yoshisada's army against Ashikaga Takauji and fought at Hakone-Takeshita. He succeeded his father as shugo of Nagato in 1348, taking the style Suruga no Kami, and died in 1351.
zh: 厚东武村是长门国武士厚东氏第十五代当主，武实的嫡子。1333年他与父亲一同倒戈，攻打长门探题北条氏，翌年因功受封丰前国企救郡。1335年，他随新田义贞的讨伐军迎战足利尊氏，参加箱根·竹之下之战。1348年他接替父亲担任长门守护，自称骏河守，1351年去世。

en: Kotō Takenaka was the thirteenth head of the Kotō warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province. His son Takezane, the fourteenth head, was appointed shugo, military governor of Nagato Province, by the Kenmu government in 1334.
zh: 厚东武仲是长门国厚狭郡武士厚东氏的第十三代当主；其子、第十四代当主厚东武实于1334年被建武政权任命为长门守护。

en: Kotō Taketada is named in the Kotō clan genealogy as its first ancestor, a descendant of Mononobe no Moriya. The genealogy holds that he built his residence at Tanai in Nagato Province, now Ube in Yamaguchi Prefecture, beginning the clan's presence there.
zh: 《厚东氏系图》将武忠列为厚东氏初代，相传为物部守屋的后裔；他在长门国棚井（今山口县宇部市）修筑居馆，厚东氏由此在当地定居。

en: Kotō Taketoki was the eleventh head of the Kotō warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province. The Akiyoshi, a branch family of the Kotō, traced their descent to his third son.
zh: 厚东武时是长门国厚狭郡武士厚东氏的第十一代当主；厚东氏的支族秋吉氏，即以武时的第三子为始祖。

en: Kotō Taketomo was the tenth head of the Kotō warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province during the Kamakura period, succeeding his father Takeyoshi, the ninth head.
zh: 厚东武朝是镰仓时代长门国厚狭郡武士厚东氏的第十代当主，在第九代当主、其父厚东武能之后接任家督。

en: Kotō Taketsuna was the fourth head of the Kotō clan, a Mononobe-descended warrior family of eastern Asa District in Nagato Province. He was a son of the third head, Takemichi.
zh: 厚东武纲是长门国厚狭郡东部豪族厚东氏的第四代当主，该族自称物部氏后裔。他是三代当主武通之子。

en: Kotō Takeyo was a son of Kotō Takezane of the Nagato warrior clan and a brother of Takemura and Takefuji.
zh: 厚东武世是长门武士厚东武实之子，也是武村与武藤的兄弟。

en: Kotō Takeyoshi was the ninth head of the Kotō, a warrior clan based in Asa District, Nagato Province. Known as Kotō Kodayū, he was the son of Takekage, the eighth head, who died in Kamakura during the Jōkyū era in the early thirteenth century.
zh: 厚东武能是以长门国厚狭郡为根据地的武士厚东氏的第九代当主，通称厚东小大夫；他是第八代当主厚东武景之子，武景于13世纪初的承久年间在镰仓去世。

en: Kotō Takezane (died 1348) was the fourteenth head of the Kotō, a warrior clan of Asa District in Nagato Province. In the Genkō War he served the Nagato tandai Hōjō Tokinao, but in 1333 turned against him and helped drive him from Nagato, after which the Kenmu government made him shugo of Nagato in 1334. When Takauji rebelled, Takezane joined him in Kyushu in 1336 and fought the Southern Court, keeping the post under the Muromachi shogunate. After the 1348 fighting at Shijōnawate he fell ill, passed the office to his son Takemura, and died in Kyoto that November.
zh: 厚东武实（？—1348）是以长门国厚狭郡为根据地的武士厚东氏第十四代当主。元弘之乱中，他起初作为长门探题北条时直的部下为北条氏作战，1333年倒戈，参与将时直逐出长门。1334年建武政权任命他为长门守护。足利尊氏举兵后，武实于1336年在九州加入尊氏一方，与南朝军队作战，在室町幕府下继续担任长门守护。1348年四条畷之战后他病倒，将守护职让给儿子武村，同年11月在京都病没。

en: Kō no Koremasa was a son of Kō no Koreyori and a household retainer of Minamoto no Yoshiie (1039–1106). Genealogies record that he followed Yoshiie's third son Minamoto no Yoshikuni east to Ashikaga Manor in Shimotsuke Province and settled there, planting the Kō clan in the Ashikaga lands. From Koremasa's generation the Kō served the Minamoto-line Ashikaga as senior vassals and fought for them against the rival Fujiwara-line Ashikaga family. His descendants included the Ashikaga stewards Kō no Shigeuji and Kō no Moronao.
zh: 高惟真是高惟赖之子、源义家（1039—1106年）的家人。系图记载，他随源义家的第三子源义国东下，定居下野国足利庄，高氏从此在足利的领地扎根。自惟真一代起，高氏以重臣身份侍奉源姓足利氏，并在其与藤姓足利氏的争斗中为足利家作战。他的后人包括足利氏执事高重氏和高师直。

en: Kō no Korenaga was a member of the Kō clan of Shimotsuke, the Ashikaga's warrior house. The clan genealogy places him in its direct line as the son of Kō no Korenori, father of Kō no Koreshige and grandfather of Kō no Shigeuji.
zh: 高惟长属侍奉足利氏的下野武家高氏。高氏系图将他列入嫡流，记为高惟范之子、高惟重之父、高重氏的祖父。

en: Kō no Korenori was a member of the Kō clan, the Shimotsuke warrior house that served the Ashikaga. The clan genealogy places him in its direct line as the son of Kō no Koremasa and father of Kō no Korenaga.
zh: 高惟范属侍奉足利氏的下野武家高氏。高氏系图将他列入嫡流，记为高惟真之子、高惟长之父。

en: Kō no Koreshige was a member of the Kō clan of Shimotsuke, the Ashikaga's warrior house. The clan genealogy names him as the son of Kō no Korenaga and father of Kō no Shigeuji, the first Kō steward documented at the Ashikaga household.
zh: 高惟重属侍奉足利氏的下野武家高氏。高氏系图将他列入嫡流，记为高惟长之子、高重氏之父；高重氏是现存史料中最早可确认的足利氏执事。

en: Kō no Koreyori was an eleventh-century warrior from whom the Kō clan of Shimotsuke traced its line. Later genealogies, including the Sonpi Bunmyaku, name him as the fourth son of Minamoto no Yoshiie (1039–1106), given in infancy to Takashina no Koreaki to raise and styled Ōdaka no Tayū. Around Koreyori's time the Takashina house shortened its name to Kō, became warriors, and entered Yoshiie's service in the east, the beginning of the clan's martial identity.
zh: 高惟赖是11世纪的武将，下野高氏自认的先祖。《尊卑分脉》等后世系图将他记为源义家（1039—1106年）的第四子，自幼交给高阶惟章抚养，称大高大夫。大约在惟赖的时代，高阶一家开始简称为高氏，转为武士，到东国臣事源义家，高氏由此走上武家之路。

en: Kō no Moroaki was a Nanboku-chō commander, the son of Kō no Moroyuki and cousin of the powerful steward Kō no Moronao. He served Ashikaga Takauji's brother Tadayoshi, becoming shugo of Ise in 1338 and taking Kamiyama Castle from the Southern Court. In the Kannō Disturbance he and his son Moroari sided with Tadayoshi against Moronao, one grievance being that Moronao had killed his wife's brother Uesugi Shigeyoshi. When Tadayoshi fled to Hokuriku in 1351 Moroaki followed, and his son Moroari later entered the service of the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji.
zh: 高师秋是南北朝时代武将，高师行之子、执事高师直的堂兄弟。他出仕足利尊氏之弟足利直义，1338年就任伊势守护，曾攻陷南朝的神山城。观应之扰乱中，他与儿子高师有站在直义一方与师直作战，原因之一是师直杀害了他的妻兄上杉重能。1351年直义逃往北陆时师秋随行；其子师有后来出仕镰仓公方足利基氏。

en: Kō no Moroakira was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era and a son of Kō no Moronao, steward to Shogun Ashikaga Takauji. When his father and much of the Kō clan were killed during the Kannō Disturbance in 1351, Moroakira escaped and was made the clan's successor. Around 1352 he was named shugo of Tango Province and, in 1353, of Tajima, to watch the wavering Yamana Tokiuji. When Yamana rebelled for the Southern Court in 1353, Moroakira led the warriors of Tamba, Tango and Tajima against him, was defeated at Nishiyama Yoshimine and took his own life.
zh: 高师诠是日本南北朝时代的武将，为将军足利尊氏执事高师直之子。1351年观应之乱中，父亲师直及高氏一族多人遇害，师诠幸免于难，成为高家继承人。约1352年他受任丹后国守护，1353年又兼任但马国守护，以防态度反复的山名时氏。1353年山名时氏投靠南朝举兵叛乱，师诠集结丹波、丹后、但马的国人众迎战，在西山吉峰之战中兵败自尽。

en: Kō no Moroari (died 1364) was a Nanboku-chō commander, the son of Kō no Moroaki. During the Kannō Disturbance he and his father sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi against the rest of the Kō clan. After Tadayoshi's downfall at Kamakura in 1352 he entered the service of the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji. In 1362, when the Kantō steward Hatakeyama Kunikiyo was driven from office for opposing Motouji, Moroari was named his successor. His last issued document dates to 1363, and he died in the second month of 1364, the last Kantō steward chosen from outside the Uesugi clan.
zh: 高师有（？—1364）是南北朝时代武将，高师秋之子。观应之扰乱中，他与父亲站在足利直义一方，与高氏族人敌对。1352年直义在镰仓败亡后，他出仕镰仓公方足利基氏。1362年关东执事畠山国清因与基氏对立而失脚，师有被任命为继任关东执事。他存世的最后一份文书发于1363年，1364年二月去世，是上杉氏之外最后一任关东执事。

en: Kō no Morofuyu (died 1351) was a Nanboku-chō commander, shugo lord and waka poet, the son of Kō no Moroyuki and adopted heir of his cousin Kō no Moronao. He first appears in records fighting at Nishi-Sakamoto in 1336, helped defeat the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie in 1338 and, as Kantō steward from 1339, subdued the region by 1343, becoming shugo of Musashi and then Iga. In 1349 he was assigned to counsel the young Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji. During the Kannō Disturbance he fled Kamakura in late 1350 and, besieged at Sunzawa Castle in Kai, killed himself in early 1351.
zh: 高师冬（？—1351）是南北朝时代武将、守护大名兼和歌歌人，为高师行之子、堂兄高师直的养子。1336年六月他初见于记载，参加西坂本之战；1338年随养父师直转战，为击败南朝将领北畠显家立功。1339年起担任关东执事，与北畠亲房等南朝势力交战，至1343年冬平定关东，先后受任武藏、伊贺守护。1349年他受命辅佐年幼的镰仓公方足利基氏；观应之扰乱中与上杉宪显对立，1350年末逃离镰仓，困守甲斐国须泽城，于1351年正月十七日自尽。

en: Kō no Moronao (died 1351), son of Moroshige, was the chief retainer of Ashikaga Takauji and the first steward of the Muromachi bakufu. He fought for Takauji at the Minatogawa River in 1336 and slew the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie at Ishizu in 1338. In 1348 he destroyed Kusunoki Masatsura's army at Shijōnawate and burned the Southern Court base at Yoshino. His feud with Takauji's brother Tadayoshi ignited the Kannō Disturbance; after his defeat at Uchidehama in 1351 he took the tonsure, only to be killed with his brother Moroyasu on the Mukogawa River by Tadayoshi's men.
zh: 高师直（？—1351）是高师重之子、足利尊氏最倚重的家臣，室町幕府初代执事。1336年他随尊氏在凑川作战，1338年于和泉石津击杀南朝名将北畠显家。1348年四条畷之战中，他击破楠木正行所部并焚毁南朝据点吉野。他与尊氏之弟足利直义对立，引发观应之扰乱；1351年打出滨之战兵败后出家，却在被押送京都途中，与弟弟高师泰等人在武库川畔遭直义一方的上杉能宪杀害。

en: Kō no Moroshige was a retainer of the Ashikaga house from the late Kamakura into the Nanboku-chō period and the father of Kō no Moronao. Succeeding his father Morouji, he served Ashikaga Sadauji and Takauji as steward, appearing in that office in 1301 and again in 1320, while his brother Moroyuki held it in 1308; he also judged disputes among Ashikaga vassals. By 1333 he had passed the family headship to his son Moronao, alienating his nephew Moroaki, who took Tadayoshi's side against Moronao in the Kannō Disturbance. The diary Jōraku-ki dates his death to the fifth month of 1343.
zh: 高师重是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，出仕足利氏，为高师直之父。他继承父亲高师氏，以执事身份侍奉足利贞氏和足利尊氏：1301年已在执行执事事务，1308年由兄弟高师行担任，1320年又由师重出任，他还为足利家臣间的纠纷作出裁决。1333年之前，他已把高氏家督之位让给儿子师直，致使侄子师秋在观应之扰乱中没有追随师直，而站到足利直义一边。据《常乐记》记载，他于1343年五月去世。

en: Kō no Morouji was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Kō clan in Shimotsuke and the grandfather of Kō no Moronao. He succeeded his father Shigeuji as steward, or shitsuji, to the Ashikaga, serving Ashikaga Ietoki and the young Sadauji. When Ietoki committed suicide in 1284, he entrusted Morouji with his last affairs in a letter. In 1286 Morouji issued a steward's writ concerning a Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine appointment without his lord's sleeve signature, a mark of his standing among the Ashikaga retainers; Sadauji's youth and lack of a personal signature have been proposed as the reason for its absence. He remained steward until his death in 1301, when his son Moroshige succeeded him.
zh: 高师氏是镰仓时代中后期下野高氏的武将，高师直的祖父。他继承父亲高重氏出任足利氏执事，先后侍奉足利家时与年幼的足利贞氏。1284年足利家时自杀时，将后事托付给他，并留下书状。1286年，他就鹤冈八幡宫的僧职安堵发出执事奉书，未加主君袖判，足见其在足利氏被官中的地位；一种解释认为这是因为贞氏年少，尚无自己的花押。他一直担任执事，直至1301年去世，由其子高师重继任。

en: Kō no Moroyasu (died 1351) was a commander under Ashikaga Takauji and brother of Kō no Moronao. He fought in the 1333 rising against the Hōjō and helped defeat Hōjō Tokiyuki in the 1335 Nakasendai War. He fought at Minatogawa in 1336 as Tadayoshi's vice-general and against Kitabatake Akiie in 1338. As shugo of Kawachi he helped crush Kusunoki Masatsura and burn Yoshino in 1348. Leading his brother's faction against Ashikaga Tadayoshi, he was defeated at Uchidehama in 1351, took the tonsure, and was killed with Moronao and his son Moroyo on the Mukogawa River.
zh: 高师泰（？—1351）是足利尊氏麾下武将，高师直之弟。1333年他参加推翻北条氏的举兵，1335年中先代之乱中协助击败北条时行；1336年以足利直义副将身份在凑川作战，1338年又参与讨伐北畠显家。他身任河内守护，1348年协助攻灭楠木正行、焚毁吉野。作为师直派对抗足利直义的核心武将，他于1351年打出滨之战兵败后出家，随即在武库川畔与师直及儿子高师世一同遇害。

en: Kō no Moroyo (died 1351) was a Nanboku-chō commander of the Kō clan, the son of Kō no Moroyasu and nephew of the steward Moronao. When Moronao briefly resigned the stewardship amid his feud with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, Takauji appointed Moroyo to succeed him, though Moronao soon reclaimed the office. In the Kannō Disturbance he fought under his father and uncle for Takauji against Tadayoshi, and after the defeat at Uchidehama in 1351 he took the tonsure. While being escorted to Kyoto he was cut down at the Mukogawa River with Moronao, Moroyasu and their kinsmen.
zh: 高师世（？—1351）是南北朝时代高氏武将，高师泰之子、执事高师直的侄子。师直因与足利直义对立而一度辞去执事时，足利尊氏任命师世接任；师直复权后他又交出执事之职。观应之扰乱中，他随父亲与伯父拥戴尊氏、与直义作战，1351年打出滨兵败后出家，在被押送京都途中，于武库川畔与师直、师泰等族人一同遇害。

en: Kō no Moroyuki was a late-Kamakura retainer of the Ashikaga house who, like his father Morouji, served Ashikaga Sadauji as steward and is recorded acting in that office in 1308. He was the father of the Nanboku-chō commanders Kō no Moroaki and Kō no Morofuyu.
zh: 高师行是镰仓时代后期足利氏的家臣，与父亲高师氏一样担任足利贞氏的执事，1308年见在执事任上。他是南北朝武将高师秋、高师冬的父亲。

en: Kō no Shigemochi was a Nanboku-chō commander and waka poet, younger brother of the steward Kō no Moronao. He served Ashikaga Takauji from the 1333 rising, fighting at Tatarahama in Chikuzen and the Minatogawa River in 1336. In 1337 he was appointed shugo of Musashi and guarded the young Ashikaga Yoshiakira at Kamakura, but was removed after defeats by Kitabatake Akiie. He later headed the bakufu's Hikitsuke court, served as Kantō steward, and presented waka at Kōyasan in 1344. He survived the killing of his brothers in 1351 and resumed office under Yoshiakira; by 1352 he had become a monk.
zh: 高重茂是南北朝时代武将、和歌歌人，执事高师直之弟。他自1333年起兵起追随足利尊氏，1336年参加筑前多多良滨与凑川之战。1337年他就任武藏守护，在镰仓辅佐年幼的足利义诠，后因与北畠显家作战失利被罢免。此后他担任幕府引付头人、关东执事，并于1344年向高野山奉献和歌。1351年师直等兄弟遇害时他幸免于难，后在义诠手下复出任职；1352年见于记载时已出家。

en: Kō no Shigeuji was a mid-Kamakura warrior and steward, or shitsuji, to the Ashikaga lords Yoriuji and Ietoki in Shimotsuke Province; he was the great-grandfather of Kō no Moronao. A writ he issued in the eleventh month of 1281 is the oldest surviving evidence of a Kō heading the Ashikaga household, showing the stewardship had become hereditary by his generation. He had died by 1284, when his son Morouji received Ashikaga Ietoki's farewell letter at his suicide. Shigeuji also took part in the Utsunomiya waka circle as a poet.
zh: 高重氏是镰仓时代中期武将，在下野国侍奉足利赖氏、足利家时两代，担任执事，是高师直的曾祖父。他在1281年十一月签发的文书，是高氏主持足利家政现存最早的史料，可见最迟在他这一代，执事一职已经世袭。1284年足利家时自杀的遗书由其子高师氏接掌，可知重氏此前已经去世。他还是一名歌人，曾出入宇都宫歌坛。

en: Prince Ōtomo (648–672), posthumously called Emperor Kōbun, was Emperor Tenji's son by a low-ranking concubine, first named Prince Iga. In 671 his father named him the first Daijō-daijin, or prime minister. When Tenji died he took power at Ōmi, but his uncle Prince Ōama challenged the succession, fled Yoshino and raised the eastern provinces. The Jinshin War of 672 ended within a month: Ōama's eastern armies destroyed the Ōmi forces and Ōtomo killed himself in the mountains. No early source counts him an emperor; the posthumous title Kōbun was officially confirmed only in 1870.
zh: 大友皇子（648—672）即死后追尊的弘文天皇，是天智天皇与出身伊贺国的低阶采女之子，初名伊贺皇子。671年被父亲任命为第一位太政大臣。天智天皇死后他在近江掌权，叔父大海人皇子不服继位安排，逃出吉野、起兵东方。672年壬申之乱爆发，不出一个月，大海人的东国军队击溃近江军，大友逃入山中自尽。早期史料不把他算作天皇，直到1870年明治政府才确认“弘文”这一追号。

en: Kōgon (1313–1364), personal name Kazuhito, was the first emperor of Japan's Northern Court, reigning from 1331 to 1333. A son of Emperor Go-Fushimi of the Jimyōin line, he was made heir to Emperor Go-Daigo in 1326 under the throne-alternation agreement. After Go-Daigo's rising against the Kamakura shogunate in 1331, the Hōjō exiled him to Oki and enthroned Kōgon. Go-Daigo returned and deposed him in 1333. In 1336 Ashikaga Takauji placed Kōgon's brother Kōmyō on the Northern throne. Southern forces seized him at Kyoto in 1352 amid the Kan'ō Disturbance and kept him captive until his death in 1364.
zh: 光严天皇（1313—1364），名量仁，是日本北朝第一代天皇，1331年至1333年在位。他是持明院统后伏见天皇之子，1326年依照两统迭立的约定被立为后醍醐天皇的皇太子。1331年后醍醐天皇倒幕失败，被北条氏流放隐岐，光严随即被拥立为帝。1333年后醍醐天皇返京将他废黜。1336年足利尊氏拥立其弟光明天皇为北朝天皇。观应扰乱中，南朝军队于1352年攻入京都将他掳走，幽禁于南方直至1364年去世。

en: Empress Kōgyoku (594–661), born Princess Takara, ruled Japan twice: as the 35th sovereign, Kōgyoku, and from 655 as the 37th, Saimei. She ascended in 642 amid Soga clan domination. In 645 her son Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari killed Soga no Iruka in the Isshi incident, after which she abdicated for her brother Emperor Kōtoku. Her Saimei reign saw large building works at Asuka and the suppression of Prince Arima's plot. After Paekche fell in 660 she marched to its aid but died in Kyūshū the next year before the expedition sailed.
zh: 皇极天皇（594—661）名宝皇女，两度统治日本：先为第35代天皇皇极，655年起再为第37代天皇齐明。642年即位时朝中苏我氏专权。645年，她的儿子中大兄皇子与中臣镰足发动乙巳之变诛杀苏我入鹿，她随后退位，让位于弟弟孝德天皇。齐明一朝在飞鸟大兴土木，并镇压了有马皇子的谋反。660年百济灭亡，她率军赴援，次年病逝于九州，援军尚未渡海。

en: Empress Kōken (718–770), personal name Abe, was the 46th and 48th monarch of Japan, its only twice-reigning empress. A daughter of Emperor Shōmu and Empress Kōmyō, she succeeded her father in 749, suppressed the Tachibana no Naramaro plot in 757, and abdicated the next year for Junnin. After crushing Fujiwara no Nakamaro's rebellion in 764, she deposed Junnin and retook the throne as Empress Shōtoku. Her second reign was dominated by the monk Dōkyō, whom she made Buddhist king; the 769 Usa oracle claiming Hachiman wanted him emperor was challenged by Wake no Kiyomaro. She died in 770.
zh: 孝谦天皇（718—770）名阿倍，是日本第46代和第48代君主，也是唯一两度登基的女天皇。她是圣武天皇与光明皇后之女，749年受父禅让即位，757年镇压橘奈良麻吕的谋反，次年让位于淳仁天皇。764年平定藤原仲麻吕之乱后，她废黜淳仁，重祚称称德天皇。第二次在位期间，僧人道镜专权，被她封为法王；769年宇佐神托宣称八幡神有意让道镜即皇位，遭和气清麻吕驳斥。770年她去世。

en: Emperor Kōkō (830–887) was the 58th emperor of Japan, reigning from 884 to 887. The third son of Emperor Ninmyō, he received the highest princely rank in 882. After the deposition of Emperor Yōzei in 884, the kampaku Fujiwara no Mototsune placed him on the throne, and Kōkō entrusted him with government. On his enthronement he demoted all his own children to commoner rank, but on his deathbed in 887 he restored his son Minamoto no Sadami to imperial status as crown prince; Sadami succeeded him as Emperor Uda on the day Kōkō died.
zh: 光孝天皇（830—887）是日本第58代天皇，884年至887年在位。他是仁明天皇第三子，882年升至一品。884年阳成天皇被废后，关白藤原基经将他拥上皇位，光孝也把政务托付给基经。即位时他把自己的所有子女降为臣籍；但887年临终之际，他又恢复儿子源定省的皇族身份并立为太子，光孝去世当日，定省即位，是为宇多天皇。

en: Kōmyō (1322–1380), personal name Yutahito, was the second Northern Court emperor and the first backed by Ashikaga Takauji, reigning from 1336 to 1348. A younger son of Emperor Go-Fushimi and Kōgon's brother, he was enthroned at Kyoto after Takauji drove Go-Daigo from Kyoto in 1336, without the sacred imperial treasures; Go-Daigo then founded the Southern Court at Yoshino. In 1348 Kōmyō abdicated to his nephew Sukō. Southern forces took Kyoto in 1352 and carried him off with Kōgon and Sukō; held in Yamato until 1355, he returned to Kyoto and took monastic vows. He died in 1380.
zh: 光明天皇（1322—1380），名丰仁，是日本北朝第二代天皇，也是第一位得到足利尊氏支持的北朝天皇，1336年至1348年在位。他是后伏见天皇较年幼的儿子、光严天皇之弟。1336年足利尊氏将后醍醐天皇逐出京都后，他在没有三神器的情况下于京都即位；后醍醐天皇随后在吉野建立南朝。1348年光明让位给侄子崇光天皇。1352年南朝军队攻占京都，将他与光严、崇光二帝一同掳走，幽禁于大和国；1355年他返回京都出家，1380年去世。

en: Emperor Kōnin (708–782), personal name Shirakabe, was the 49th emperor of Japan and a grandson of Emperor Tenji. Long sidelined, he is said to have feigned a love of drink to survive the purges of the 760s and won credit for suppressing the Fujiwara no Nakamaro rebellion of 764. When Empress Shōtoku died without an heir in 770, the ministers placed the sixty-two-year-old Shirakabe on the throne. In 772 he deposed Empress Inoe and Crown Prince Osabe and later named his son Yamabe heir and, after attempting to restore state finances, abdicated to him in 781; Yamabe ruled as Emperor Kanmu.
zh: 光仁天皇（708—782），名白壁，是日本第49代天皇，天智天皇之孙。他长年远离权力中心，相传在760年代的政治清洗中以嗜酒佯狂避祸，后因平定764年藤原仲麻吕之乱立功。770年称德天皇无嗣而终，众大臣拥立六十二岁的白壁即位。772年，他废黜皇后井上内亲王与皇太子他户亲王，后立儿子山部亲王为嗣。他整顿财政，并于781年禅位于山部，即桓武天皇。

en: The fourth head of the Kōsaka clan of Shinano Province is recorded in the clan genealogy only by his court title Aki-no-kami, governor of Aki Province, succeeding his father Munezane.
zh: 信浓国香坂氏第四代当主在家谱系谱中只留下“安芸守”（安芸国长官）这一官职名，本名未传，他在父亲宗実之后继位。

en: The fifth head of the Kōsaka clan of Shinano Province appears in the clan genealogy only under his court title Dewa-no-gon-no-kami, provisional governor of Dewa Province, succeeding Aki-no-kami.
zh: 信浓国香坂氏第五代当主在家谱系谱中只以“出羽権守”（出羽国权守）这一官职名出现，本名未传，他继安芸守之后继位。

en: Kōsaka Muneatsu was, by the clan genealogy, the second head of the Kōsaka warrior family of Shinano Province, succeeding his father Munekiyo, the clan's founder.
zh: 香坂宗敦据家族系谱记载是信浓国武家香坂氏的第二代当主，继初代当主、父亲宗清之后统领香坂氏。

en: Kōsaka Munekiyo was, by clan tradition, the founder of the Kōsaka warrior family of Shinano Province, a branch of the Shigeno clan named after Kōsaka in Saku district. Local gazetteers and temple records name him among the new land stewards granted northern Shinano estates after the Shigeno fought for the Hōjō in the Jōkyū War of 1221. Temple traditions hold that he received Makinoshima in 1260 and founded Tensō-ji in the Bun'ō era of 1260–1261; his clan expanded from Makinoshima over the southern Zenkōji plain.
zh: 香坂宗清相传是信浓国武家香坂氏的初代当主。香坂氏是东信浓名族滋野一族的支流，因世居佐久郡香坂而得姓。据地方地志与寺院记载，1221年承久之乱中滋野一党为执权北条氏作战，宗清作为新补地头之一，获赐被没收的北信浓上皇方领地。寺传还称他于1260年（文应元年）得到牧之岛之地，并于1260—1261年的文应年间建立天宗寺；香坂氏由牧之岛在善光寺平南部逐步扩张势力。

en: Kōsaka Munezane was, by the clan genealogy, the third head of the Kōsaka warrior family of Shinano Province, succeeding his father Muneatsu.
zh: 香坂宗実据家族系谱记载是信浓国武家香坂氏的第三代当主，继承父亲宗敦之位。

en: Kōsaka Shinkaku was the sixth head of the Kōsaka clan, a warrior family of Shinano Province, and held Maki Castle in the Sarashina district. In 1336 he took up arms at Maki with the Hōjō remnants on the Southern Court side, together with an Uesugi force from Echigo. In the first and sixth months he fought bitter battles against the Northern Court clans of northern Shinano: the Ogasawara, Murakami, Takanashi and Ichikawa. In the first month Murakami Nobusada took Kiyotaki Castle in the Hanishina district and then attacked Shinkaku at Maki Castle.
zh: 香坂心觉是信浓国武家香坂氏的第六代当主，据有更级郡牧城。1336年，他与北条残党同以南朝一方在牧城举兵，并和越后的上杉兵库助合力，于一月、六月两度同北信浓的北朝方小笠原、村上、高梨、市河诸氏激战。一月，村上信贞攻下埴科郡英多庄的清泷城后，随即进攻据守牧城的心觉。

en: Emperor Kōtoku (596–654), personal name Karu, was Japan's 36th sovereign (r. 645–654) and Empress Kōgyoku's younger brother. Enthroned after the Isshi incident broke Soga power, he let his nephew Crown Prince Naka no Ōe direct policy. He proclaimed Taika, Japan's first era name, and the 646 Reform Edict launched the Taika reforms of centralised administration, census and equal land allotment. The court moved to Naniwa palace; a white pheasant tribute in 650 brought the Hakuchi era. In 653 the crown prince led most of the court back to Asuka; Kōtoku stayed behind and died at Naniwa in 654.
zh: 孝德天皇（596—654）名轻，是日本第36代天皇，645—654年在位。他是皇极天皇的弟弟。乙巳之变削弱苏我氏势力后，他被拥立为帝，实权则掌握在侄子皇太子中大兄皇子手中。他下诏启用日本第一个年号“大化”，646年颁布《改新之诏》，推行大化改新：建立中央集权官制、编订户籍、实行班田收授。朝廷迁至难波宫；650年进献白雉，改元“白雉”。653年，皇太子率朝廷大部分人迁回飞鸟，孝德天皇留在难波，于654年去世。

en: Kōzai Sukemura (1183–1235), also written Fujiwara no Sukemura, was a Kamakura-period warrior, founder of the Kōzai clan of Sanuki Province, and a son of Nii no Sukemitsu. Fighting for the shogunate in the Jōkyū War of 1221, he won distinction and became district magistrate of Aya and Kagawa districts. He set up his steward's residence at Saryō in Kasai, Kagawa District, from which he took the name Kōzai, and was appointed Lieutenant of the Left Inner Guards; he also built Katsuga Castle on Mount Shōga. He died on the seventh of the seventh month, 1235, aged fifty-three.
zh: 香西资村（1183—1235），又作藤原资村，是镰仓时代武将、赞岐国香西氏的始祖，新居资光之子。1221年承久之乱中，他为镰仓幕府方作战立功，被任命为阿野、香川两郡的郡司。他在香川郡笠居乡的佐料修建地头屋敷，并由“笠居”的读音改称香西，受任左近将监，又在胜贺山上修筑胜贺城。1235年七月初七日去世，享年五十三岁。

en: Kōzai no Tadasuke was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Kōzai clan in Aya District, Sanuki Province, and a son of Kōzai Sukemura, the clan's founder.
zh: 香西忠资是镰仓时代赞岐国阿野郡香西氏的武将，香西氏始祖香西资村之子。

en: Kudō Kagemitsu was a twelfth-century warrior of the Kudō clan active in Kai and Izu Provinces. He backed Minamoto no Yoritomo's 1180 rising, marching with Yasuda Yoshisada and helping rout Matano Kagehisa's Taira force at the Battle of Hashidayama below Mount Fuji. In the 1189 Ōshū campaign he and his son Yukimitsu served with distinction; on 12 September Yukimitsu received lands in Iwate District, founding the Kuriyagawa Kudō line. At Yoritomo's 1193 Fuji hunt, the aged Kagemitsu three times missed a great deer, declared it the mountain god's mount and his own death near, and fell ill that night.
zh: 工藤景光是12世纪活动于甲斐、伊豆两国的工藤氏武士。1180年源赖朝举兵，他起兵响应，随安田义定驰援，在富士山麓的波志田山合战中协助击溃俣野景久所率的平家军队。1189年奥州合战时，他与儿子工藤行光率一族从军立功；同年9月12日行光受封岩手郡领地，开创厨川工藤氏一脉。1193年赖朝举行富士卷狩，年迈的景光三射大鹿不中，称此鹿乃山神坐骑、自己命数将尽，当夜便病倒。

en: Kudō no Kageto was a member of the Izu Kudō regarded as the ancestor of the Ōshū Kudō, who moved to Kai Province and made Koma District his base.
zh: 工藤景任出身伊豆工藤氏，被视为奥州工藤氏之祖，他移居甲斐国，以巨摩郡为据点。

en: Kudō no Korekage was an eleventh-century warrior of the Kudō clan, counted in the Sonpi Bunmyaku as a grandson of the clan's founder Fujiwara no Tamenori and son of Kudō Tokisato, with the title Suruga no kami. Genealogies and local tradition record that he settled at the Kanō manor in Izu Province around 1050 and took its place name, becoming the ancestor of the Kanō warrior house, from which the painters of the Kanō school later claimed descent. His son Koremoto is recorded as ōryōshi, military chief of Izu.
zh: 工藤维景是11世纪的工藤氏武士，《尊卑分脉》等谱系将其列为工藤氏始祖藤原为宪之孙、工藤时理之子，官至骏河守。谱系与伊豆地方相传，他约于1050年迁入伊豆国狩野庄居住，以地名为号，成为狩野武家之祖，后世的狩野派画系即自称出自这一族。其子维职见于记载，曾任伊豆国押领使。

en: Kudō no Korekane was a figure in the Kudō genealogies. The Sagara genealogy names him as a son of Tokifumi and governor of Tōtōmi, and the Kyūma gaishi treats him as the ancestor of the Sagara clan, though scholars note these early lineages conflict.
zh: 工藤维兼是工藤氏系谱中的人物。相良系图将他记为时文之子，任远江守，《求麻外史》以他为相良氏之祖；学界指出这些早期系图异说甚多。

en: Kudō no Korekane was a Heian-period figure of the Kudō clan of the Southern Fujiwara. The Nikaidō genealogy makes him the son of Kudō no Koreto and father of Kudō no Koreyuki. The Higo chronicle Kyūma Gaishi counts him as ancestor of the Sagara clan.
zh: 工藤维兼是平安时代工藤氏的人物，该氏为藤原南家分出的武家。《二阶堂系图》载他是工藤维远之子、工藤维行之父。肥后地志《求麻外史》以维兼为相良氏之祖。

en: Kudō no Koremoto was a member of the Kudō family who served as ōryōshi, a military official, in Izu Province.
zh: 工藤维职是工藤氏的一员，曾任伊豆国押领使。

en: Kudō no Koretō was a figure in the Kudō genealogies of the Fujiwara Southern House. The Sonpi Bunmyaku's Nikaidō lineage records him as governor of Suruga with junior fifth rank, lower grade; his line supplied ancestors of the Nikaidō clan, officials of the Kamakura shogunate.
zh: 工藤维远是藤原南家工藤氏系谱中的人物。《尊卑分脉·二阶堂系图》载他任骏河守、叙从五位下；其一脉是镰仓幕府文官二阶堂氏的祖先。

en: Kudō no Koretsugu was a Heian-period warrior of the Kudō clan, a house descended from the Southern Fujiwara. Genealogies record him as the father of Kudō Suketaka, sixth head of the clan and founder of the Itō clan in Izu Province.
zh: 工藤维继是平安时代工藤氏的武士，工藤氏为藤原南家分出的武家。据家系图记载，他是工藤氏第六代当主工藤祐隆之父，祐隆为伊东氏之祖。

en: Kudō no Koreyori was a Heian-period courtier of the Kudō clan of the Southern Fujiwara. The Nikaidō genealogy in the Sonpi Bunmyaku records him as provisional governor of Tōtōmi, in a line holding junior fifth rank and governorships in Suruga and Tōtōmi.
zh: 工藤维赖是平安时代工藤氏的贵族，出自藤原南家。《尊卑分脉·二阶堂系图》载其任远江权守；其家系代代叙从五位下，出任骏河、远江等地的国司。

en: Kudō no Koreyuki was a Heian-period courtier of the Kudō clan of the Southern Fujiwara. Genealogies name him governor of Suruga with junior fifth rank, son of Kudō no Korekane and father of Kudō no Yukitō, grandfather of the Kamakura official Nikaidō Yukimasa.
zh: 工藤维行是平安时代工藤氏的贵族，出自藤原南家。系图载其任骏河守、叙从五位下，为工藤维兼之子、工藤行远之父；行远之子二阶堂行政是镰仓幕府政所令，维行即行政之祖父。

en: Kudō Sadasuke was a late-Kamakura inner retainer of the Hōjō Tokusō, the son of Kudō Tokimitsu. He received the character sada from Hōjō Sadatoki at his coming of age between 1284 and 1311, and served both Sadatoki and Hōjō Takatoki. From 1308 to 1331 he superintended the rebuilding of Tada-in in Settsu Province, and from 1309 to 1324 he was deputy shugo of Wakasa. In 1326 he took the field against the Andō rebellion in Ōshū and captured Andō Suenaga in the seventh month.
zh: 工藤贞祐是镰仓时代后期北条得宗家的御内人，工藤时光之子。他在1284至1311年间元服，获北条贞时授予偏讳‘贞’字，先后侍奉贞时与北条高时。1308至1331年担任摄津国多田院造营总奉行，1309至1324年任得宗分国若狭国的守护代。1326年，他随军出征奥州，镇压安藤氏之乱，同年七月擒获叛军首领安藤季长。

en: Kudō Sadayuki was a warrior of Tsugaru in the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods. A Hōjō retainer, he entered Inaka district as deputy steward and fought for Kamakura when the Andō rebelled in 1322. After the shogunate fell in 1333, he joined the imperial army under Kitabatake Akiie and served as battle commissioner at the Battle of Daikōji of 1333–1334 against Hōjō remnants. In 1335 he received the former estates of Kudō Sadasuke. With no legitimate son, he left the lands to his daughter, wife of Nambu lord Nobumasa of Nejo; they became the Nambu base in Tsugaru.
zh: 工藤贞行是津轻的武将，活跃于镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代。身为北条氏的御内人，他以地头代身份进入津轻田舍郡赴任，1322年安东氏之乱时为镰仓方作战。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他加入陆奥守北畠显家的朝廷军，在1333—1334年的大光寺合战中任合战奉行，征讨津轻的北条残党有功，1335年获赐工藤贞祐的旧领。因无嫡子，他把所领让给嫁给根城南部氏信政的女儿，南部氏日后以这些领地为进出津轻的据点。

en: Kudō Shigemitsu is known only from genealogies, which record him as a son of the warrior Kudō Kagemitsu and the ancestor of the Kudō Shigemitsu line. His son Kudō Takamitsu and grandson Kudō Tokimitsu later served the Hōjō Tokusō family as inner retainers.
zh: 工藤重光仅见于谱系记载：他是武士工藤景光之子，工藤氏“重光流”一支的先祖。其子工藤高光、其孙工藤时光后来都侍奉北条得宗家，成为御内人。

en: Kudō Sukenaga was an early-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, the third son of Kudō Suketsune. When his father was killed by the Soga brothers during the Fuji hunt in 1193, he was appointed jitō of Nagano in Ise Province, receiving the districts of Anō and Aki to subdue the remaining Taira followers there. His son Sukemasa settled at Nagano and took its name, founding the Nagano Kudō family, which grew into a powerful local warrior house in Ise.
zh: 工藤祐长是镰仓时代前期武将、御家人，工藤祐经的第三子。1193年父亲在富士卷狩中被曾我兄弟刺杀后，他受命担任伊势国长野的地头，获封安浓、奄艺两郡，负责讨伐伊势平氏残党。其子工藤祐政移居长野并以地名为姓，开创长野工藤氏，后来成为伊势国有力的国人家族。

en: Kudō Suketaka, also called Itō Ietsugu, was the sixth head of the Kudō clan and the lord who developed Kusumi Manor in Izu Province. He gave the clan's old Kanō Manor to his fourth son Shigemitsu, founder of the Kanō clan, and settled at Kusumi, where he founded the Itō clan. After his heir Sukeie died early, Suketaka divided the four manors of Kusumi between his son Suketsugu and his grandson Itō Sukechika. The disputed inheritance drew the Kudō, Itō and Kawazu lines into the blood feud that ended with the Revenge of the Soga Brothers in 1193.
zh: 工藤祐隆又称伊东家次，是工藤氏第六代当主、伊豆国久须美庄的开发领主。他把一族旧领狩野庄交给四子茂光，茂光为狩野氏之祖；自己则移居久须美，开创伊东氏。嫡子祐家早逝后，祐隆将久须美下辖的四处庄园分给儿子祐继与孙子伊东祐亲。这场继承纠纷把工藤、伊东、河津三家卷入仇杀，最终酿成1193年的曾我兄弟复仇事件。

en: Kudō Suketsugu (1120–1162), also called Takiguchi Suketsugu, was a warrior of the Kudō clan in Izu Province in the late Heian period. Kudō Suketaka's adopted son, also said to have been his son by his second wife, was not meant to be heir, but after Itō Sukeie died young he received the Itō Manor and succeeded as family head. Before dying he arranged for his son Suketsune to marry Mangō Gozen, daughter of Itō Sukechika, after coming of age; Sukechika became the boy's guardian. After Suketsugu's death in 1162 Sukechika seized Suketsune's lands, opening the feud that ended with the Revenge of the Soga Brothers.
zh: 工藤祐继（1120—1162）又称泷口祐继，是平安时代后期伊豆国工藤氏的武士。他是工藤祐隆的养子，也有说法称他是祐隆与继室所生之子；他本无继承之份，但伊东祐家早逝后，他获赐伊东庄并继承家督。临终前，他安排儿子祐经元服后娶伊东祐亲之女万劫御前，由祐亲担任后见人。1162年祐继死后，祐亲随即没收祐经的领地，由此引发的仇杀最终酿成曾我兄弟复仇事件。

en: Kudō Suketsune (1147–1193) was a late-Heian warrior of the Fujiwara Nanke line, heir of Kudō Suketsugu in Izu Province. While he served Taira no Shigemori in Kyoto, his guardian Itō Sukechika seized his estate and wife, and in 1176 Suketsune's men ambushed Sukechika and killed his son Kawazu Sukeyasu. After Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, Suketsune became his Kamakura attendant, valued for court music and knowledge of the capital, and joined the 1184 Taira campaign. In 1193, at Yoritomo's Fuji hunt, Sukeyasu's sons the Soga brothers slew him in revenge.
zh: 工藤祐经（1147—1193）是平安时代末期武士，出身藤原南家，为伊豆国工藤祐继的嫡子。他在京都侍奉平重盛期间，后见人伊东祐亲夺取了他的领地与妻子；1176年，祐经派郎党伏击祐亲，未能得手，却射杀其嫡子河津祐泰。1180年源赖朝举兵后，祐经前往镰仓臣从，以通晓都中风物与歌舞音乐成为赖朝的近侍，并参加1184年讨伐平氏的战役。1193年，在赖朝于富士山麓举行的卷狩中，祐泰之子曾我兄弟为报父仇将他刺杀。

en: Kudo Takakage was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and a miuchibito, a direct retainer serving the Tokuso line of the Hojo family. He was a son of Kudo Sadasuke.
zh: 工藤高景是镰仓时代后期的武士，身为御内人，即北条氏得宗家的直属被官。他是工藤贞祐之子。

en: Kudō Takamitsu, known in religion as Rikaku, was a powerful inner retainer of the Hōjō Tokusō in the late Kamakura period. When Daijō Takamoto, head of the Hitachi Daijō house, died in 1289, Takamitsu intervened in its succession, securing the expulsion of the heir Tsunemoto and installing his own grandson Chōju, later called Tokimoto, as family head; the brothers' lawsuit ran for more than twenty years and ended in Tokimoto's favour. Genealogies make him the son of Kudō Shigemitsu and the father of Kudō Tokimitsu.
zh: 工藤高光，法名理觉，是镰仓时代后期北条得宗家权势颇重的御内人。1289年，常陆国大掾氏当主大掾孝幹去世，高光出面干预其家督继承，使原定继承人经幹遭到放逐，改立自己的外孙长寿（后名时幹）为大掾氏当主；兄弟间的诉讼持续二十余年，最终以时幹胜诉告终。谱系以高光为工藤重光之子、工藤时光之父。

en: Fujiwara no Tamenori was a mid-Heian noble and warrior of the Fujiwara Southern House, son of Hitachi governor Fujiwara no Korechika and cousin of Taira no Masakado. Defeated by Masakado in 939, he fled to his kinsman Taira no Sadamori. In the second month of 940, as an imperial commander with Sadamori and Fujiwara no Hidesato, he helped destroy Masakado and freed his father. Rewarded with junior fifth rank and the office of moku no suke, he took the title Kudō Taifu, becoming ancestor of the Kudō clan, and later held provisional governorships in Izu, Suruga, Kai and Tōtōmi.
zh: 藤原为宪是平安时代中期贵族、武将，出身藤原南家，为常陆介藤原维几之子，与平将门是表兄弟。939年他败于将门，投奔表兄平贞盛。940年2月，他作为官军大将之一，与贞盛、藤原秀乡合力攻灭将门，并救出此前被将门扣留的父亲维几。因功叙从五位下、任木工助，遂以‘工藤大夫’为号，成为工藤氏之祖，此后历任伊豆、骏河、甲斐、远江等国权守。

en: Kudō no Tokifumi was a figure named in the Kudō and Sagara clan genealogies. The Sagara genealogy calls him a son of Fujiwara no Tamenori and governor of Izu, and father of Korekane, governor of Tōtōmi, while noting conflicting versions of these early generations.
zh: 工藤时文是工藤氏与相良氏系谱中的人物。相良系图将他记为藤原为宪之子，任伊豆守，其子维兼任远江守；系图同时注明这几代存在多种异说。

en: Kudō Tokimitsu was a late-Kamakura warrior and inner retainer of the Hōjō Tokusō, a member of the Ōshū Kudō lineage identified in the Southern House Itō Fujiwara genealogy as the son of Kudō Takamitsu. After taking the tonsure he was called the lay monk Jirōuemon Nyūdō, and was known by the dharma names Kōzen and Kōgyō. Under Tokusō Hōjō Sadatoki he served as steward of the Tokusō administrative office and deputy shugo of Wakasa Province. In 1301 his name stands first among the signatories of a joint order issued by the Tokusō office.
zh: 工藤时光是镰仓时代后期武士、北条得宗家的御内人，属奥州工藤氏一族；《南家伊东氏藤原姓大系图》将其比定为工藤高光之子。出家后称工藤二郎右卫门入道，法名有杲禅和杲晓。在得宗北条贞时麾下，他担任得宗家公文所执事，又出任得宗分国若狭国的守护代。1301年，得宗公文所奉行人的联署奉书中，他列名奉者首位。

en: Kudō no Tokinobu was a figure in the Kudō clan genealogies, a grandson of Fujiwara no Tamenori and a son of Kudō no Tokisada. His son Korekiyo, known as Irie no Korekiyo, is named as the ancestor of the Irie clan of Suruga Province.
zh: 工藤时信是工藤氏系谱中的人物，为藤原为宪之孙、工藤时贞之子。系图载其子维清称“入江马允维清”，是从骏河国工藤氏分出的入江氏之祖。

en: Kudō no Tokisato is known only from medieval genealogies as a son or grandson of Fujiwara no Tamenori, founder of the Kudō clan. The Sonpi Bunmyaku makes him father of Kudō Korekage, Suruga governor, who settled at Kanō in Izu.
zh: 工藤时理其人仅见于中世纪谱系：各系图或将其列为工藤氏始祖藤原为宪之子，或列为其孙。《尊卑分脉》载他是工藤维景之父，维景后任骏河守，定居伊豆国狩野。

en: Kudō no Yukitō was a Heian-period courtier of the Kudō clan, a Southern Fujiwara branch, holding Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The Nikaidō genealogy names him governor of Tōtōmi. The Sonpi Bunmyaku makes him the son of Kudō no Koreyuki who, in the Hōen era (1135–1141), killed the province's court-appointed governor and was exiled to Owari, taking the byname Shirao Saburō. He married a daughter of Fujiwara no Suekane of the Atsuta Daigūji house. His son Nikaidō Yukimasa became the Kamakura shogunate's Mandokoro chief and one of its thirteen councillors.
zh: 工藤行远是平安时代贵族，出身藤原南家工藤氏，叙从五位下。《二阶堂系图》称他曾任远江守。据《尊卑分脉》，他是工藤维行之子，保延年間（1135—1141）杀死远江国司，被流放尾张国，自称白尾三郎。他娶热田大宫司家藤原季兼之女，其子二阶堂行政后来成为镰仓幕府政所令、十三人合议制成员之一。

en: Prince Kusakabe (662–689) was the son of Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō and crown prince from 681. When Tenmu fell ill in 686 he and the empress were entrusted with the government; after the emperor died Kusakabe led his funeral and tomb-building but was never enthroned. He married Princess Abe, later Empress Genmei; their children included Emperor Monmu and Empress Genshō. He died suddenly in 689 aged 28, before his coronation, and was posthumously honoured as Emperor Okanomiyagyou. The throne passed instead to his mother Jitō, who held it for his young heirs.
zh: 草壁皇子（662—689）是天武天皇与持统天皇之子，681年被立为皇太子。686年天武天皇病重，把政务托付给他与皇后；天武天皇去世后，草壁主持了葬礼与陵墓营建，却始终没有即位。他娶阿閇皇女，即后来的元明天皇，子女包括后来的文武天皇与元正天皇。689年他在即位前突然去世，年仅28岁，被追尊为冈宫御宇天皇。皇位改由母亲持统天皇继承，为他年幼的后嗣代管。

en: Kusunoki Masanori (c. 1333–c. 1390) was the third son of Kusunoki Masashige and, after his brothers Masatsura and Masatoki fell at Shijōnawate in 1348, became the Southern Court's foremost general. As its commander he retook Kyoto from the Northern Court four times between 1352 and 1369, while leading the court's peace faction. When negotiations failed he defected to the Ashikaga shogunate, served Yoshimitsu as shugo of Kawachi and Izumi, and in 1373 led the storming of the Southern capital at Amano. After 1379 he returned to the Southern Court and died shortly before the 1392 reunification.
zh: 楠木正仪（约1333—约1390）是楠木正成的第三子。1348年兄长正行、正时在四条畷战死后，他成为南朝的首席大将，于1352至1369年间四度从北朝手中夺回京都，同时主持南朝的和平派。和谈失败后，他转投室町幕府，受足利义满委任为河内、和泉两国守护，并于1373年率军攻陷南朝首都天野。1379年后他复归南朝，在1392年南北朝合一的数年前去世。

en: Kusunoki Masashige (1294–1336) was a samurai commander of Kawachi Province who answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate in the Genkō War of 1331. His defenses of Akasaka and Chihaya castles tied down shogunal armies and helped clear the way for the Kenmu Restoration of 1333, after which he governed Izumi and Kawachi Provinces. When Ashikaga Takauji turned against the court in 1335, Masashige stayed loyal and, on imperial orders, attacked the Ashikaga army in Settsu. Defeated at the Battle of Minatogawa on 4 July 1336, he killed himself, becoming the paragon of the loyal warrior.
zh: 楠木正成（1294—1336）是河内国的武士将领，1331年响应后醍醐天皇的号召，在元弘之乱中起兵推翻镰仓幕府。他坚守赤坂城与千早城，长期牵制幕府大军，为1333年建武中兴铺平道路，此后受任和泉、河内两国守护。1335年足利尊氏背叛朝廷，正成始终效忠，奉天皇之命进军摄津迎战足利军。1336年7月4日，他在凑川之战兵败自尽，此后被视为日本忠义武士的典范。

en: Kusunoki Masasue, commonly called Shichirō, was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and the Kemmu government, remembered as Kusunoki Masashige's younger brother. In the Genkō War he fought at Tennō-ji in 1333 and served as deputy to Hirono Shōgen Nyūdō defending Kami-Akasaka castle, helping to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate. The Taiheiki presents him as Masashige's right arm and recounts that he took his own life beside his brother at the battle of Minatogawa on 4 July 1336, vowing to destroy the court's foes in seven lives.
zh: 楠木正季通称七郎，是镰仓时代末期至建武政权时期的武将，楠木正成之弟。元弘之乱中，他于1333年参加天王寺合战，并在楠木本城上赤坂城的防卫战中担任平野将监入道的副将，为推翻镰仓幕府立下战功。军记物语《太平记》把他写成正成的股肱臂膀，并记述他在1336年7月4日的凑川之战中随兄长一同自尽，临终发下“七生灭贼”之愿。

en: Kusunoki Masatoki (died 1348), commonly called Jirō, was a Southern Court warrior of the Nanbokuchō wars, the second son of Kusunoki Masashige and a younger brother of Kusunoki Masatsura. On 4 February 1348 he served as deputy commander of the Southern army at the Battle of Shijōnawate, fighting beside Masatsura against the shogunal host of Kō no Moronao. When the Southerners were overwhelmed he was killed together with his brother.
zh: 楠木正时（？—1348）是南北朝时代的南朝武将，楠木正成的次子、楠木正行之弟，通称次郎。1348年2月4日的四条畷之战中，他担任南朝军副将，随兄长正行迎战高师直统率的幕府大军；南朝军溃败时，他与兄长一同战死。

en: Kusunoki Masatoo was an akutō, a provincial outlaw chief, of Kawachi province in the late thirteenth and early fourteenth centuries, traditionally remembered as the father of Kusunoki Masashige and Masasue. His name appears in no contemporary record: it rests on the Tachibana genealogy preserved in the Sonpi Bunmyaku, while other family trees call him Masayasu or Masagen, and some scholars identify him with the tonsured strongman Kawachi no Kusunoki Nyūdō, a former steward of the Ōbe estate in Harima denounced by its peasants in a petition to Tōdai-ji in 1295. He is thought to have died around 1320.
zh: 楠木正远是13世纪后期至14世纪初河内国的恶党，即在地方上称雄的武装首领，相传为楠木正成与楠木正季之父。其名不见于一手记载，今据《尊卑分脉》所收《橘氏系图》；其他系图又将他写作正康、正玄。1295年，播磨国大部庄的庄民向东大寺递状，指控曾任杂掌的“河内楠入道”在地方横行，有学者将这名入道比定为正成之父。正远约卒于1320年前后。

en: Kusunoki Masatsura (c. 1326–1348) was the eldest son of Kusunoki Masashige and succeeded him as head of the Kusunoki family in the service of the Southern Court. From 1340 he administered Kawachi Province as its shugo. In 1347 he campaigned in Kii Province, rallied Southern Court supporters across Kii, Izumi and Settsu, and defeated a Northern Court army under Hosokawa Akiuji at Sakainoura. On 4 February 1348 the shogunal general Kō no Moronao overwhelmed his outnumbered force at the Battle of Shijōnawate, where Masatsura and his brother Masatoki killed themselves. He was revered as the “Little Nankō.”
zh: 楠木正行（约1326—1348）是楠木正成的嫡长子，在南朝继任楠木氏当主。1340年起，他以守护的身份治理河内国。1347年，他进军纪伊国，在纪伊、和泉、摄津各国聚集南朝势力，并在堺浦击败细川显氏率领的北朝军队。1348年2月4日，幕府大将高师直以优势兵力在四条畷之战中将其击败，正行与弟弟正时力竭自尽，后世尊称他为“小楠公”。

en: Kutsuna Kanehira, also called Fujiwara no Kanehira, was jitō of the Kutsuna islands off Iyo Province in the late Heian period. Tradition credits him with building the hall of Kuwana Shrine on Nakajima and with founding Tainoyama Castle on the island's Mount Taino in 1189.
zh: 忽那兼平又称藤原兼平，是平安时代后期伊予国忽那诸岛的地头。相传他在中岛修建了桑名神社的社殿，并于1189年在岛上的泰乃山修筑泰乃山城。

en: Kutsuna Kunishige slew Kawano Michitoshi at the Battle of Mount Takanawa on the fourteenth day of the seventh month during the Jōkyū War of 1221.
zh: 忽那国重于1221年承久之乱期间，在七月十四日的高绳山之战中击杀河野通俊。

en: Kutsuna Shigekiyo was a naval commander of the Kutsuna clan based on the Kutsuna Islands of Iyo Province. In 1331 he answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call to arms in the Genkō War and campaigned across Iyo against the Iyo-Utsunomiya. He then followed Nitta Yoshisada against Ashikaga Takauji, fighting under Tōin Saneyo at Ōi Castle in Shinano and in Kyoto. When Takauji marched from Kyushu in 1336, Shigekiyo defected to the Ashikaga, served under Yoshimi Ujiyori and Tadayoshi, and fought in Kyoto, Iyo and Aki. In his later years he was overshadowed by his Southern Court brother Yoshinori.
zh: 忽那重清是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代武将，出身以伊予国忽那群岛为据点的忽那水军。1331年元弘之乱时，他响应后醍醐天皇举兵，参与讨伐伊予宇都宫氏，转战伊予各地。后随新田义贞讨伐反叛建武政权的足利尊氏，隶属洞院实世麾下，经东山道进军，在信浓大井城破敌，又在京都为宫方作战。1336年尊氏由九州北上时，他转投足利方，在吉见氏赖麾下跟随足利直义，于京都扫荡宫方，在伊予协助细川、河野两氏，还转战安艺等地。晚年被归属南朝的弟弟义范压倒，退出历史舞台。

en: Kutsuna Shigetoshi commanded the Kutsuna Seven Islands navy in the late 13th century. In the Mongol invasions he served under Kawano Michiari, fighting at Hakata Bay in 1274 and at Takashima and Kashima in Imari Bay during the 1281 campaign.
zh: 忽那重俊在13世纪后期统率忽那七岛水军。元寇两场战役中，他率部加入河野通有麾下，1274年在博多湾奋战，1281年弘安之役中又转战伊万里湾的鹰岛和鹿岛，立下战功。

en: Kutsuna Shigeyoshi was a naval commander of the Kutsuna clan, whose power rested on the Kutsuna Islands off Iyo Province. In the Genkō War of 1331 he renounced the clan's vassalage to the Kōno and allied with the Doi and Tokunō. He sent his sons Shigekiyo and Yoshinori to storm Negoroji Castle and defeated the Nagato deputy Hōjō Tokinao at Hoshinooka. In April 1333 Emperor Go-Daigo named him Lesser Controller of the Left. He served the Southern Court into the 1340s and in 1339 aided Prince Kaneyoshi on his journey to Kyushu.
zh: 忽那重义是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，出身以伊予国忽那群岛为据点的忽那水军。1331年元弘之乱时，他摆脱历来对河野氏的从属，与伊予的土居、得能两氏联手。他派儿子重清、义范攻取喜多郡根来城，又在久米郡星之冈讨杀长门探题北条时直。1333年四月，他奉后醍醐天皇纶旨叙任左少弁，此后归属南朝直至1340年代；1339年征西将军怀良亲王下向九州途经忽那岛时，他与儿子义范一同加以援助。

en: Kutsuna Yoshinori was a naval commander of the Kutsuna clan who held Kōura Castle on Kutsuna Island in Iyo Province. Unlike his brother Shigekiyo, he served the Southern Court throughout and led the clan after his brother's death. In 1337 he fought the Ashikaga officer Hosokawa Kōkai. From 1339 he sheltered Emperor Go-Daigo's son Prince Kaneyoshi for three years and guarded him against the Kōno and the Aki-Takeda. He supported Wakiya Yoshisuke's landing in Iyo in 1342, raided the Shiaku Islands in 1348 and later fought alongside Ashikaga Tadafuyu.
zh: 忽那义范是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代武将，以伊予国忽那岛的神浦城为据点。其兄重清起初归属宫方、后来投奔足利，义范却始终归属南朝，兄长死后由他统率一族。1337年三月，他与吉良贞义派遣的代官及细川皇海交战。1339年起，他将驻留忽那岛三年的后醍醐天皇皇子怀良亲王保护起来，抵御伊予河野氏和安艺武田氏。1342年他协助胁屋义助进入伊予，1348年四月进攻赞岐国盐饱群岛，晚年又与转而归属宫方的足利直冬联手作战。

en: Prince Kuwata was a Nara-period imperial prince, the second son of Prince Nagaya. In 729 he was strangled together with his father and brothers in the purge known as the Nagaya Incident.
zh: 桑田王是日本奈良时代的皇族，长屋王次子。729年，他在长屋王之变中与父亲及兄弟一同被缢死。

en: Sasaki Dōyō (1296–1373), lay name Takauji, was a warrior lord of the Kyogoku branch of the Sasaki clan in Omi province. He served the Hojo regent Takatoki and later helped build the Muromachi shogunate, becoming military governor of six provinces. Under Shogun Yoshiakira he was the shogunate's most powerful figure, engineering Shiba Takatsune's fall in the 1366 Joji Disturbance. He was famed for his extravagant basara style and renga linked verse, contributing 81 poems to the Tsukubashu anthology, and died in 1373 at Shoraku-ji.
zh: 佐佐木道誉（1296—1373），俗名高氏，是近江国佐佐木氏京极分家的武将大名。他原仕于执权北条高时，后来参与建立室町幕府，历任六国守护。在二代将军义诠时代，他是幕府最有权势的人物，于1366年的贞治之变中扳倒斯波高经。他还以奢华的婆娑罗风尚和连歌闻名，有81首作品收入《菟玖波集》，1373年于胜乐寺去世。

en: She was a daughter of Sasaki Dōyō, the influential Kyōgoku clan lord and Muromachi bakufu power broker, and the wife of Akamatsu Norisuke (Sokuyū), head of the Akamatsu clan and shugo of Harima. Her son Akamatsu Yoshinori later succeeded as head of the Akamatsu clan.
zh: 她是权势显赫的京极氏当主佐佐木道誉之女，嫁给赤松氏当主、播磨国守护赤松则祐为妻，所生之子赤松义则后来继承赤松家督。

en: Sasaki Hidetsuna (died 1353), eldest son of Sasaki Doyo, was a Northern Court warrior who became head of the Board of Retainers and military governor of Kazusa province. In 1338 he helped block Kitabatake Akiie's advance on Kyoto on the Omi-Mino border, and in 1340 he and his father were briefly exiled to Kazusa after setting fire to a cloister of Myoho-in. He fought at the 1348 Battle of Shijonawate and in 1351 joined Ashikaga Takauji against Tadayoshi alongside his father, receiving appointment as governor of Kazusa that year. In 1353, guarding the fugitive Emperor Go-Kogon near Katada in Omi, he was killed in a Southern Court attack at Mano-ura by Horiguchi Sadayasu.
zh: 佐佐木秀纲（？—1353）是佐佐木道誉的长子，北朝武将，官至侍所头人、上总国守护。1338年，他在近江与美浓边境阻击北畠显家进军京都；1340年因随父亲火烧妙法院别院，父子一度被流放上总。他参加了1348年的四条畷之战，1351年观应扰乱时又随父投奔足利尊氏、讨伐直义，同年受任上总守护。1353年，他在近江坚田附近护卫出逃的后光严天皇时，于真野浦遭南朝方堀口贞祐袭击，战死阵中。

en: Sasaki Mitsunobu was a Kamakura-period gokenin, the third son of Sasaki Ujinobu, founder of the Kyōgoku line. He died before his father, so the headship passed to his younger brother Munetsuna, but his son Muneuji later became the fourth Kyōgoku head.
zh: 佐佐木满信是镰仓时代的御家人，京极氏始祖佐佐木氏信的第三子。他先于父亲去世，家督由弟弟宗纲继承，但其子宗氏后来成为京极氏第四代当主。

en: Sasaki Munetsuna (1248–1297), also called Kyōgoku Munetsuna, was the second head of the Kyōgoku clan. The fourth son of Sasaki Ujinobu, he won distinction in the Shimotsuki disturbance of 1285 and was appointed junior fifth rank, lower grade, and governor of Noto. In 1287 he served as the Kamakura shogunate's envoy pressing the court to accept the abdication of Emperor Go-Uda in favor of Emperor Fushimi, and in 1289 he accompanied the new shōgun Prince Hisaaki's procession to Rokuhara. He succeeded his father in 1295 but died only two years later.
zh: 佐佐木宗纲（1248—1297），又称京极宗纲，是京极氏第二代当主。他是佐佐木氏信的第四子，1285年在霜月骚动中立功，叙从五位下、任能登守。1287年，镰仓幕府敦促朝廷安排后宇多天皇让位给伏见天皇时，他出任赴朝廷的使者；1289年又随新任征夷大将军久明亲王的行列前往六波罗。1295年他继承家督，但仅两年后便去世。

en: Sasaki Muneuji (1269–1329), also called Kyōgoku Muneuji, was the fourth head of the Kyōgoku clan. Born the legitimate son of the gokenin Sasaki Mitsunobu, he succeeded his cousin Sadamune, the third head, when Sadamune died without a male heir in 1305. A devoted lover of waka poetry, he had poems included in the Shoku-Senzai Wakashū and Shin-Senzai Wakashū imperial anthologies. He died in 1329 aged 61, and the headship passed to his son Takauji, better known as Sasaki Dōyo.
zh: 佐佐木宗氏（1269—1329），又称京极宗氏，是京极氏第四代当主。他是御家人佐佐木满信的嫡子，1305年第三代当主堂兄贞宗无嗣而亡，由他继承家督。他酷爱和歌，作品收入敕撰和歌集《续千载和歌集》与《新千载和歌集》。1329年去世，享年61岁，家督由其子高氏继承——高氏即佐佐木道誉。

en: Sasaki Sadamune (1287–1305), also called Kyōgoku Sadamune, was the third head of the Kyōgoku clan. A son of Sasaki Munetsuna, he received the character sada in his given name from Hōjō Sadatoki, the ninth regent of the Kamakura shogunate, and succeeded his father in 1297. He died in 1305 at the age of 19, killed in the Kagen disturbance while campaigning against Hōjō Munekata. He left only a daughter, so the headship passed through his cousin Muneuji to his adopted nephew Takauji, later Sasaki Dōyo.
zh: 佐佐木贞宗（1287—1305），又称京极贞宗，是京极氏第三代当主，佐佐木宗纲之子。他从镰仓幕府第九代执权北条贞时的名字中受赐偏讳，取名贞宗，1297年继承父亲的家督。1305年去世，年仅19岁，在嘉元之乱中随讨伐北条宗方的军队作战时阵亡。他只留下一个女儿，家督于是经堂兄宗氏，传给养子外甥高氏，即后来的佐佐木道誉。

en: Sasaki Sadauji (died 1355), also called Kagami Sadauji, was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era and a son of Sasaki Muneuji, fourth head of the Kyogoku clan. He took the Kagami family name and became a monk in 1335. In 1341, on Ashikaga Tadayoshi's orders, he attacked the Yamato priest Seia, and in 1347 Ashikaga Takauji granted him the stewardship of Taga Shrine in Omi province. He died in 1355. His sons took the names Kagami, Ibuki and Nagaoka, founding branch houses.
zh: 佐佐木贞氏（？—1355），又称镜贞氏，是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，京极氏第四代当主佐佐木宗氏之子，自称镜氏。他于1335年出家。1341年，他奉足利直义之命攻打大和国神官西阿；1347年获足利尊氏授予近江国多贺社的地头职。他于1355年去世，诸子分别以镜氏、伊吹氏、长冈氏为姓，开创数个分家。

en: Sasaki Takahide (1328–1391) was a shugo daimyo and the third son of Sasaki Doyo. He became the Kyogoku heir after his brothers Hidemune and Hidetsuna fell in battle in 1348 and 1353, and after succeeding his father in 1373 ruled as military governor of Izumo, Hida and Oki. In the 1379 Koryaku Disturbance he raised troops in Omi to force the kanrei Hosokawa Yoriyuki from office, but lost all his domains, recovering only Hida in 1381. He campaigned against the rebel Toki Yasuyuki in 1390 and died in 1391. His third son Takahisa founded the Amago clan of Izumo.
zh: 佐佐木高秀（1328—1391）是南北朝时代的守护大名，佐佐木道誉的三子。两位兄长秀宗、秀纲先后于1348年、1353年战死，他因而成为京极氏嗣子，1373年继承家督，历任出云、飞驒、隐岐三国守护。1379年康历政变中，他在近江举兵，迫使管领细川赖之下台，却被没收全部领地，1381年仅领回飞驒一国。1390年他奉义满之命讨伐在美浓叛乱的土岐康行，翌年去世。其三子高久后来成为出云尼子氏的始祖。

en: Sasaki Ujinobu (1220–1295), also called Kyōgoku Ujinobu, was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the founder of the Kyōgoku branch of the Sasaki clan. The fourth son of Sasaki Nobutsuna, governor of Ōmi, on his father's death in 1242 he inherited six districts of northern Ōmi and the clan mansion at Kyōgoku-Takatsuji in Kyoto, from which his descendants took their name. He joined the Hikitsukeshu in 1265 and the Hyōjōshū in 1266, became governor of Ōmi in 1283, and founded Seiryōji, later the Tokugen-in temple. He died in 1295 aged 76.
zh: 佐佐木氏信（1220—1295），又称京极氏信，是镰仓时代中期的武将、御家人，佐佐木氏分支京极氏的始祖。他是近江守护佐佐木信纲的第四子，1242年父亲死后，继承北近江的高岛、伊香、浅井、坂田、犬上、爱智六郡以及京都的京极高辻宅邸，子孙由此得名京极氏。1265年他加入引付众，1266年加入评定众，1283年任近江守，并创建日后成为京极氏菩提寺的清泷寺（后改称德源院），1295年去世，享年76岁。

en: Mashiko no Masashige was an early Kamakura-period warrior and head of the Mashiko family, holders of Saimyōji Castle in Haga District, Shimotsuke Province, and retainers of the Utsunomiya. In 1189, when Minamoto no Yoritomo marched against the Northern Fujiwara of Ōshū, Masashige led the clan's Ki-tō warrior band under Utsunomiya Tomotsuna and fought with distinction alongside the Haga clan's Sei-tō. Yoritomo rewarded the Mashiko and the Haga each with a Minamoto white banner, an honour long treasured by the family.
zh: 益子正重是镰仓时代初期的武将、益子氏当主，一族领有下野国芳贺郡的西明寺城，为宇都宫氏的郎党。1189年源赖朝举兵讨伐奥州藤原氏，正重率领本族的纪党武士团追随宇都宫朝纲从军，与芳贺氏的清党并立战功。赖朝将源氏的白旗各赐一面给益子氏与芳贺氏，这份武勋成为益子氏长久相传的荣誉。

en: The Mashiko clan genealogies name Mashiko no Masataka, second son of Ki no Sadataka, as the founding head of the Mashiko family of Mashiko village in Haga District, Shimotsuke Province. He is called Ki Gon-no-kami, and the provincial gazetteer Shimotsuke-kokushi records that he built the clan's Saimyōji Castle during the Kōhei era of 1058–1065. His daughter married Fujiwara no Sōen, regarded as the founder of the Utsunomiya lords, binding the two houses together.
zh: 据益子氏系谱记载，益子正隆是纪贞隆的次子，被奉为下野国芳贺郡益子邑益子氏的初代当主。系谱称他为纪权守，《下野国志》记载他于康平年间（1058—1065年）修筑一族的居城西明寺城。其女嫁给被视为宇都宫氏始祖的藤原宗圆，两家由此结为姻亲。

en: Mashiko Masatsuna (c. 1250–1302) was a warrior of the late Kamakura period. Born the fourth son of Utsunomiya Yoritsuna of Shimotsuke Province, he married a daughter of Mashiko Munetomo and succeeded as head of the Mashiko clan, whose holdings lay around Mashiko in Haga district. During the Mongol invasion of 1281, the Kōan campaign, he took the field under his kinsman Utsunomiya Sadatsuna. He died on the twenty-ninth day of the second month of 1302.
zh: 益子政纲（约1250—1302）是镰仓时代后期的武将。他出生于下野国宇都宫氏，为宇都宫赖纲第四子，后娶益子宗朝之女，入嗣以芳贺郡益子为据点的益子氏。1281年弘安之役，即元朝第二次进攻日本时，他随同族宇都宫贞纲出阵。他于1302年（正安四年）二月二十九日去世。

en: Mashiko no Masayori was the second head of the Mashiko warrior family of Haga District in Shimotsuke Province. His second son Iehiro left the main house to found the Takahashi branch family.
zh: 益子正赖是下野国芳贺郡益子氏的第二代当主。其次男家广分出本家，另立高桥氏支系。

en: A Mashiko genealogy names Mashiko no Muneshige as a son of Masashige and the father of Tomosada, in the Mashiko family of Haga in Shimotsuke Province.
zh: 据益子氏系谱记载，益子宗重是正重之子、朝贞之父，属于下野国芳贺的益子氏。

en: Mashiko no Munetomo was a late-thirteenth-century head of the Mashiko warrior family of Haga District in Shimotsuke Province. He gave his daughter in marriage to Masatsuna, fourth son of Utsunomiya Yoritsuna, who took the Mashiko name and succeeded him as head of the clan.
zh: 益子宗朝是13世纪后期下野国芳贺郡益子氏的当主。他将女儿嫁给宇都宫赖纲的四男政纲，政纲因此成为益子家的女婿，改称益子并继承了益子氏家督。

en: Mashiko Sadamasa was a Nanboku-chō warrior and the eleventh head of the Mashiko clan, retainers of the Utsunomiya of Shimotsuke Province. The second son of Mashiko Sadashige, he held Saimyōji Castle in Haga District. Following Utsunomiya Ujitsuna, he switched from the Southern to the Northern Court and fought Southern Court armies in Hitachi. In 1339 a force sent by Kitabatake Chikafusa under Kasuga Akitoki seized his castles, including Saimyōji. In 1351, during the Kannō Disturbance, he led over seven hundred horse from the Ki and Sei warrior bands in Ujitsuna's rout of Momonoi Naotsune's far larger army, recorded in the Taiheiki.
zh: 益子贞正是南北朝时代的武将，下野国宇都宫氏的家臣、益子氏第十一代当主。他是益子贞重的次子，领有芳贺郡的西明寺城。贞正随主君宇都宫氏纲由南朝转投北朝，与从常陆方向逼来的南朝军连年作战。1339年，北畠亲房派遣春日显时率军来攻，他一度丢失西明寺城、八木冈城和上三川城。1351年观应之扰乱中，他追随氏纲，率领纪清两党七百余骑，击溃兵力数倍于己的桃井直常大军，事见《太平记》。

en: Mashiko Sadashige, titled Echigo-no-kami, was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Mashiko clan of Haga district in Shimotsuke Province. His second son Mashiko Sadamasa became the eleventh clan head and a leading Utsunomiya retainer in the Northern and Southern Courts wars.
zh: 益子贞重，官称越后守，是镰仓时代下野国芳贺郡益子氏的武将。其次子益子贞正后来成为益子氏第十一代当主，在南北朝动乱中担任宇都宫氏的重臣。

en: A Mashiko genealogy names Mashiko no Tomosada as a son of Muneshige in the Mashiko family of Haga in Shimotsuke Province.
zh: 据益子氏系谱记载，益子朝贞是宗重之子，属于下野国芳贺的益子氏。

en: Mashiko no Yukimune was the third head of the Mashiko warrior family of Haga District in Shimotsuke Province. His eldest son Iehira founded the Kurosaki branch family, and his third son Munemasa founded the Kawachi branch.
zh: 益子行宗是下野国芳贺郡益子氏的第三代当主。其长男家衡分出黑崎氏支系，三男宗政分出河内氏支系。

en: Kanehiro Masuda was the ninth head of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province during the Kamakura period, succeeding his father Kanetane. His son Kanekata succeeded him.
zh: 益田兼弘是镰仓时代石见国益田氏的第九代当主，继承父亲益田兼胤，后由其子益田兼方继嗣。

en: Kanehisa Masuda was the seventh head of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province during the Kamakura period, succeeding his father Kanetoki. His son Kanetane succeeded him.
zh: 益田兼久是镰仓时代石见国益田氏的第七代当主，继承父亲益田兼時，后由其子益田兼胤继嗣。

en: Kanekata Masuda was the tenth head of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province around the turn of the fourteenth century, succeeding his father Kanehiro. His son Kanemi succeeded him.
zh: 益田兼方是14世纪前后石见国益田氏的第十代当主，继承父亲益田兼弘，后由其子益田兼見继嗣。

en: Masuda Kanemi was a kokujin lord of the Masuda clan, based at Masuda in Iwami Province on the Sea of Japan. In July 1366 he cooperated with the army of Ōuchi Hiroyo, newly appointed shugo of Iwami, at the siege of Seiryūji Castle and helped subdue the province. During the Ōuchi civil war of 1380 to 1381 he sided with Ōuchi Mitsuhiro against his elder brother Yoshihiro; together with the Fukuya clan he pinned down the pro-Yoshihiro Misumi and Sufu clans. After Yoshihiro prevailed, Kanemi was confirmed in his hereditary lands and won over to the victor's side.
zh: 益田兼見是日本海沿岸石见国益田地方的国人领主，出自益田氏。1366年7月，他配合新任石见守护大内弘世的军队围攻青龙寺城，协助平定石见国。1380至1381年大内氏爆发家督之争，他站在大内满弘一边、与其兄大内义弘为敌，并联合福屋氏牵制拥戴义弘的三隅氏和周布氏。义弘获胜后，承认他对祖传领地的所有权，将他争取到胜利者一方。

en: Masuda Kanesue was the fifth head of the Masuda house of Iwami Province, succeeding his father Kanetaka. He divided the clan's large estates among his sons, from whom sprang the Shufu, Suemoto, Marumo and Tane branch families, while his son Kanetoki continued the main line.
zh: 益田兼季是石见国益田氏的第五代当主，继父亲兼高之后统领家族。他把家族在石见的庞大领地分封给诸子，由此分出周布氏、末元氏、丸茂氏、多根氏等庶流，其子兼时继承总领家，为第六代当主。

en: Kanetaka Masuda was a warrior of Iwami Province from the late Heian to the early Kamakura period, the fourth head of the Mikamoto house, later called Masuda, and eldest son of Mikamoto Kaneharu. In the Genpei War he was the only Iwami lord to answer Minamoto no Yoritomo's call, fighting at Ichinotani in 1184. Appointed Iwami's oryoshi that year, he went on to fight at Dannoura, where he took twenty-five enemy ships, and secured his family's twenty-two estates. In 1192 he moved to Masuda in Mino District and took the Masuda name, beginning Nanao Castle the next year. His son Kanesue succeeded him.
zh: 益田兼高是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期石见国的武将，御神本氏（后称益田氏）第四代当主，第三代当主御神本兼荣的长子。源平合战时，他是石见唯一响应源赖朝号召的豪族，1184年参加一之谷之战。同年他被补任为石见国押领使，后来在坛之浦之战中缴获二十五艘敌船，并确立了家族二十二处领地的所有权。1192年他迁居美浓郡益田并改称益田氏，翌年着手修建七尾城。其子兼季继位。

en: Kanetane Masuda was the eighth head of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province during the Kamakura period, succeeding his father Kanehisa. His son Kanehiro succeeded him.
zh: 益田兼胤是镰仓时代石见国益田氏的第八代当主，继承父亲益田兼久，后由其子益田兼弘继嗣。

en: Kanetoki Masuda was the sixth head of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province, succeeding his father Kanesue. His younger brothers founded the cadet Sufu, Suemoto, Marumo and Tane houses.
zh: 益田兼時是石见国益田氏的第六代当主，继承父亲益田兼季；他的诸弟另立周布氏、末元氏、丸茂氏、多根氏等庶流。

en: Aritsune Matsuda, also called Hatano Aritsune, was a late Heian and early Kamakura warrior in Sagami and the founder of the Matsuda clan. His father Hatano Yoshitsune opposed Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising in 1180 and was driven to suicide, so the boy was entrusted to his maternal uncle Ōba Kageyoshi. On 3 April 1188 his mounted archery at the yabusame before Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine so pleased Yoritomo that he was granted Matsuda-gō in Ashigara, the finest village of his father's old lands; he took the name Matsuda Jirō and became a Kamakura gokenin.
zh: 松田有常（又称波多野有常）是平安末期至镰仓初期相模国的武士，松田氏之祖。其父波多野义常于1180年源赖朝举兵时与之为敌，被迫自尽，有常被托付给母方舅父大庭景义照顾。1188年4月3日，他在鹤冈八幡宫的流镝马仪式上展现出众骑射，源赖朝大加赞赏，赐以他父亲旧领中最好的足柄松田乡；他自此称松田次郎，成为镰仓幕府的御家人。

en: Matsuda Moritomo was a warrior of the Ashigara Matsuda clan in Sagami Province, named in the chronicle Taiheiki during the wars of the Kenmu Restoration. Around 1334 he became shugo, military governor, of Bizen Province.
zh: 松田盛朝是相模国足柄松田氏的武将，军记物语《太平记》记载了他在建武年间战乱中的活动。约1334年，他出任备前国守护。

en: Matsuda Moritsune was a member of the Matsuda clan whom a family genealogy names as the son of Tsunemoto and father of Moritomo.
zh: 松田盛经是松田氏成员，一支家族系图称他是经基之子、盛朝之父。

en: Matsuda Tsunemoto was a member of the Matsuda clan whom a family genealogy names as the son of Yoshimoto and father of Moritsune.
zh: 松田经基是松田氏成员，一支家族系图称他是义基之子、盛经之父。

en: Matsuda Yoshimoto was a son of Matsuda Aritsune, founder of the Matsuda clan; a Matsuda family genealogy names Tsunemoto as his son.
zh: 松田义基是松田氏之祖松田有常之子；一支松田氏系图称松田经基是他的儿子。

en: Matsura no Hisashi (1064–1148) was a late-Heian samurai and the ancestor of the Matsura clan of Hizen Province. Said to descend from the warrior Watanabe no Tsuna, in 1069 he became steward of the Uno imperial estate in Matsura District and settled at Kajitani. He held roughly 2230 chō of fields across Matsura and Sonogi districts and Iki Province, took the name Matsura, and was made kebiishi at junior fifth rank. Calling himself Gendayū Hōgan, he ruled these lands and began the Hizen Matsura warrior band; family genealogies date his death to 1148 or 1154.
zh: 松浦久（1064—1148）是平安时代后期的武士，肥前国松浦氏之祖，相传为武士渡边纲的后人。1069年，他出任松浦郡宇野御厨的庄官，在梶谷定居，领有松浦郡、彼杵郡和壹岐国约2230町田地，遂以松浦为姓，后任检非违使，叙从五位。他自称源太夫判官，治理上述地区，肥前松浦党的历史由此开端。诸家谱对其卒年有1148年与1154年两说。

en: Matsuura no Sunao was a son of Matsura no Hisashi, founder of the Matsura clan of Hizen Province, and is named in genealogies as the ancestor of the Lower Matsura warrior party. His sons founded branch houses including the Arita and Yamashiro families.
zh: 松浦直是肥前国松浦氏之祖松浦久之子，家谱中被记为下松浦党武士团的始祖。他的儿子们分出有田氏、山代氏等若干松浦党支族。

en: Migita Hirohide, a late-Kamakura head of the Suo warrior house, was the first of his line to call himself Migita and is counted as its founder. Called Hachiro, he was ordained under the Zen master Issan Kokushi with the clerical name Jodo, and fathered Shigetoshi.
zh: 右田弘俊是镰仓时代后期周防国武家右田家的当主，初代自称右田，被奉为右田氏之祖。他通称八郎，师从禅僧一山国师出家，法名净道，生子重俊。

en: The Ouchi genealogy lists Migita Morihide, childhood name Ojumaru, title Kodayu, among the early heads of the Migita house in Suo province. It makes him the father of Sue Hirokata, founder of the Sue clan, and of Hirohide, the first head to call himself Migita.
zh: 《大内系图》将右田盛俊（幼名王寿丸，称小大夫）列为周防国右田家的早期当主，记其子陶弘贤为陶氏始祖，弘俊则是首位自称右田的当主。

en: Morinaga was the younger brother of Ouchi Morifusa, a provincial official of Suō in late Heian Japan, and founded the Migita branch of the Ouchi clan through his holding at Migita in Saba District.
zh: 盛长是日本平安时代末期周防国在厅官人大内盛房之弟，领有佐波郡的右田并以此分家，开创大内氏支流右田氏。

en: The Ouchi genealogy records Migita Moritsuna as the adopted son and heir of Migita Morinaga, who founded the Migita house at Migita in Suo province's Saba district. Called Rokuro and holding the courtier title Sani, he was followed as head by Morihide.
zh: 《大内系图》记载，右田盛纲是在周防国佐波郡右田开创右田家的右田盛长的养子与继承人。他通称六郎，叙散位，其后家督由盛俊承袭。

en: The Ouchi genealogy records Migita Shigetoshi, called Hachirotaro, as a Migita house head ordained under the Zen master Muso Kokushi with the clerical name Jokan. His sons included Shigesada, titled Owari no kami, and Sadahiro, killed in battle in Iyo at twenty-eight.
zh: 《大内系图》记载，右田重俊通称八郎太郎，师从禅僧梦窗国师出家，法名净观，为右田家当主。其子有尾张守右田重贞，以及二十八岁战死于伊予国的贞弘。

en: Mikamoto no Kaneharu was the third head of the Mikamoto house of Iwami, succeeding his father Kanezane; in his generation and his son Kanetaka's, the family grew into a powerful warrior band in Iwami, and Kanetaka moved its residence to Masuda and adopted that name.
zh: 御神本兼荣是石见国御神本氏第三代当主，继父亲兼实之后统领家族；到他与其子兼高两代，御神本氏发展成石见国有势力的武士团，兼高把居馆迁到益田，并改称益田氏。

en: Mikamoto no Kanezane was the second head of the Mikamoto house of Iwami Province and a son of Mikamoto no Kunikane, ancestor of the Masuda clan. Clan genealogies give his name variously as Kanezane or Suekane. His son Kaneharu succeeded as the third head.
zh: 御神本兼实是石见国御神本氏第二代当主，益田氏始祖御神本国兼之子。各系谱对其名字记载不一，或作兼实，或作季兼。其子兼荣继任第三代当主。

en: Fujiwara no Kunikane, later Mikamoto no Kunikane, was a noble counted as the ninth-generation descendant of Fujiwara no Tadahira and the ancestor of the Masuda clan of Iwami Province. Accounts differ over which branch of the Fujiwara produced him and even over the identity of his father. Appointed governor of Iwami, he journeyed west to take office in 1114 and stayed on after his term ended in 1118. He built his residence at Mikamoto in Hamada and adopted the name Mikamoto. His family is thought to have taken root among the local elite through marriage with powerful families.
zh: 藤原国兼，后称御神本国兼，相传为藤原忠平的九世孙，出任石见守，是石见国益田氏的初代当主。关于他出自藤原氏哪一支，乃至其父的身份，均有不同说法。1114年，他西下石见赴任，1118年任满后仍留居当地，在滨田的御神本筑馆，以御神本为氏。人们认为，他的家族通过与当地豪族联姻，在石见扎下根来。

en: Minami no Koremune was a member of the Takashina-surnamed Minami clan of Ashikaga in Shimotsuke Province, which served the Ashikaga as chief administrators of their Mandokoro. He was the son of the clan founder Minami no Yorimoto and the father of Minami no Munetsugu.
zh: 南惟宗是下野国足利庄高阶姓南氏的族人，该族世代为足利氏执掌政所。他是南氏家祖南赖基之子、南宗继之父。

en: Minami Munetsugu was a commander and administrator of the late Kamakura and early Nanboku-cho periods, head of the Takashina-surnamed Minami clan of Ashikaga in Shimotsuke Province. After the Nakasendai rebellion of 1335 he accompanied Ashikaga Takauji east and served the Muromachi bakufu as head of the Samurai-dokoro and shugo of Mikawa and Bitchu. During the Kanno Disturbance he fought for Takauji and Ko no Moronao against Ashikaga Tadayoshi, and after Moronao's murder in 1351 became one of Takauji's closest aides. He founded Seigen-ji temple in Ashikaga in 1357 and died in 1371.
zh: 南宗继是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代初期的武将与官僚，为下野国足利庄高阶姓南氏的栋梁。1335年中先代之乱爆发后，他追随足利尊氏东进，出仕室町幕府，历任侍所头人及三河、备中守护。观应之乱中，他站在高师直与尊氏一方与足利直义作战；1351年师直被杀后，他成为尊氏最倚重的亲信之一。1357年他在足利创建清源寺，1371年去世。

en: Minami no Yorimoto, also called Kō no Yorimoto, was the founder of the Takashina-surnamed Minami clan, which served the Ashikaga of Shimotsuke as Mandokoro administrators. A son of Kō no Shigeuji, he was the grandfather of Minami no Munetsugu through his son Koremune.
zh: 南赖基，又称高赖基，是高阶姓南氏的家祖，该族为下野国足利氏执掌政所。他是高重氏之子，其子惟宗之子即南宗继。

en: Minamoto no Akifusa (1037–1094) was a late-Heian court noble and poet of the Murakami Genji, the second son of the right minister Minamoto no Morofusa. He rose through court office to councillor in 1061 and provisional major counselor in 1072. After his daughter Kenshi, adopted into the regent house, was made empress to Emperor Shirakawa in 1074, he was appointed right minister in 1083. When Kenshi's son ascended as Emperor Horikawa in 1087, Akifusa became the sovereign's maternal grandfather, and his influence as an imperial relative surpassed that of his elder brother Toshifusa. He took junior first rank and died in 1094, aged fifty-eight.
zh: 源显房（1037—1094）是平安时代后期的公卿、歌人，村上源氏右大臣源师房的次子。他历任宫中职务，1061年任参议，1072年任权大纳言。其女贤子被摄关家收为养女，于1074年册立为白河天皇的中宫，显房遂于1083年任右大臣。1087年，贤子所生的善仁亲王即位为堀河天皇，显房成为天皇的外祖父，作为外戚的权势超过其兄俊房。他于1094年叙从一位，同年去世，终年58岁。

en: Minamoto no Akimichi (1081–1122) was a late-Heian court noble of the Murakami Genji, eldest son of the grand minister Minamoto no Masazane. He came of age in 1091, became head chamberlain in 1098, and joined the senior nobles as a councillor in 1100. He rose to provisional middle counselor in 1106 and middle counselor in 1115, and was made provisional major counselor early in 1122. He died of a chest illness a few months later, aged forty-two, holding senior second rank, and was remembered as the Koga Major Counselor. His son Masamichi carried on the family line.
zh: 源显通（1081—1122）是平安时代后期的公卿，村上源氏太政大臣源雅实的长子，号久我大纳言。他1091年元服，1098年任藏人头，1100年任参议，跻身公卿；1106年任权中纳言，1115年任中纳言，1122年初升任权大纳言。同年数月后，他因胸病去世，终年42岁，官位正二位。其子雅通延续了这一支脉。

en: Minamoto no Yoshikiyo, also called Ashikaga Yoshikiyo and known as Yata no Hangandai (c. 1145–1183), was a late Heian warrior, the eldest son of Ashikaga Yoshiyasu by a concubine and ancestor of the Niki and Hosokawa clans. After Prince Mochihito's rising in 1180 he fled his estate and joined Kiso Yoshinaka, entering Kyoto with him in 1183. Sent west as Yoshinaka's deputy commander to pursue the Taira, he met their fleet off Mizushima in Bitchū in the intercalary tenth month of 1183. His army was routed in the sea battle and he was killed amid a storm of arrows.
zh: 源义清，又称足利义清，通称矢田判官代（约1145—1183），是平安时代后期武将、足利义康的庶长子，仁木氏和细川氏的始祖。1180年以仁王举兵后，他逃离自己的领地，投奔木曾义仲，1183年随义仲进入京都。此后他作为义仲的代官率军西追平氏，于1183年闰十月在备中国水岛附近与平氏水军遭遇。义仲军在这场海战中大败，义清在箭雨中力战而死。

en: Minamoto no Atsuru (933-953) was a mid-Heian warrior of the Saga Genji, great-grandson of the sadaijin Minamoto no Toru and son of the Musashi governor Minamoto no Tsuko. Born at Mita in Adachi District of Musashi, his father's posting, he was known as Mita Genji, written with the character for two or the character for next. He married a daughter of Minamoto no Mitsunaka and died in 953 at only twenty-one. Watanabe no Tsuna, said to have been his son though his parentage is disputed, is thought to have been born in the same year. The Konjaku Monogatari preserves a tale of his single combat with Taira no Yoshifumi, governor of Mutsu.
zh: 源宛（933—953，名字又作充）是平安时代中期的武士，嵯峨源氏左大臣源融的曾孙、武藏守源仕之子。他生于父亲任地武藏国足立郡箕田村，号箕田源二（又作箕田源次）。他娶源满仲（多田满仲）之女为妻，953年仅21岁便去世。相传渡边纲是他的儿子，父系归属另有异说，纲生于同年。《今昔物语集》中载有他与陆奥守平良文一骑讨的逸话。

en: Minamoto no Han'en was a Buddhist monk of the early Kamakura period and a son of Minamoto no Noriyori. His father held Yoshimi in Musashi Province and was known as Yoshimi Gosho. Genealogies name Han'en as Noriyori's second son. When his father was disgraced and exiled to Izu on suspicion of treason in 1193, Han'en and his brother Gensho were spared through the plea of their great-grandmother, the nun Hiki-ama, and both took the tonsure. He was granted the Yoshimi estate in Yokomi district, Musashi Province, and his son Tameyori adopted the name Yoshimi, founding the Yoshimi house of Kamakura vassals.
zh: 源范圆是镰仓时代初期的僧人，源范赖之子。父亲领有武藏国吉见，被尊称为吉见御所。谱系记载范圆是范赖的次子。1193年父亲被疑谋反、流放伊豆时，他与弟弟源昭因外曾祖母比企尼求情而得免一死，兄弟二人都出家为僧。他受领武藏国横见郡吉见庄，其子吉见为赖遂以吉见为苗字，子孙作为镰仓御家人延续，称吉见氏。

en: Minamoto no Kiyomitsu (1110–1168), also called Kuro Genta and Henmi Kiyomitsu, was third head of the Kai Genji and son of Minamoto no Yoshikiyo. Born at Takeda-gō in Hitachi, he came of age in 1124, capped by Minamoto no Yoshikuni. Exiled with his father to Ichikawa manor in Kai after a 1130 boundary feud, he later took the name Henmi Kaja and settled below Mount Yatsugatake. He joined neither the Hōgen nor Heiji disturbances, expanding his power within Kai instead. His sons included Takeda Nobuyoshi, ancestor of the Takeda clan. He died in 1168 at 59.
zh: 源清光（1110—1168），通称黑源太，又称逸见清光，是平安时代末期武将，甲斐源氏第三代、源义清之子。他出生于常陆国武田乡，1124年由源义国加冠元服。1130年因庄园边界争斗，他与父亲一同被流放甲斐国市河庄，其后自称逸见冠者，在八岳山南麓定居。保元之乱、平治之乱他都没有参与，专心在甲斐国内扩张势力。诸子中有武田信义，即武田氏之祖。1168年去世，得年59岁。

en: Minamoto no Kunifusa (died 1119), also called Toki Kunifusa, was a Heian-period warrior, the sixth son of Minamoto no Yorikuni and ancestor of the Mino branch of the Seiwa Genji. In 1064 he clashed in Mino Province with Minamoto no Yoshiie, newly back from the Earlier Nine Years' War; the tale collection Kojidan says Yoshiie raided his mansion over a retainers' quarrel. In 1079 his private war with Minamoto no Shigemune in Tagi District brought confinement in Kyoto. He later governed Shinano and, from 1096, Izu, reaching junior fifth rank, upper grade, in 1099.
zh: 源国房（卒于1119年），又称土岐国房，是平安时代中后期的武将、源赖国第六子，被视为清和源氏美浓源氏之祖。1064年，他在美浓国与刚从前九年合战归来的源义家发生冲突；说话集《古事谈》称，争端起于双方郎党之间，义家随后突袭了他的宅邸。1079年，他因在美浓多芸郡与源重宗私斗，被召至京都拘禁。他后来历任信浓守，1096年起任伊豆守，1099年叙从五位上。

en: Minamoto no Masamichi (1118–1175) was a late Heian-period court noble and poet of the Murakami Genji's Koga line, the second son of Minamoto no Akimichi. Losing his father young, he became the adopted heir of his uncle, the udaijin Minamoto no Masasada. He served as provisional governor of Bingo and Kebiishi bettō, and in 1155 was raised to junior third rank. He rose to senior second rank and naidaijin. Ill after 1169, he died at his Koga villa in 1175 aged 58. Ten of his waka appear in imperial anthologies beginning with the Senzai Wakashū.
zh: 源雅通（1118—1175）是平安时代后期的公卿、歌人，出身村上源氏久我流，为权大纳言源顕通次子。他幼年丧父，被叔父右大臣源雅定收为养子。他曾任备后权守和检非违使别当，1155年叙从三位，最终官至正二位内大臣。1169年以后他卧病不起，1175年于久我别庄去世，享年58岁。作为歌人，他有十首和歌收入《千载和歌集》以来的敕撰和歌集。

en: Minamoto no Masanobu (920–993) was a leading court noble of the mid-Heian period, the third son of Imperial Prince Atsumi and ancestor of the Uda Genji. In 936 he left the imperial family and took the Minamoto name; he became a councillor in 951, minister of the right in 977 and minister of the left in 978, reaching junior first rank. Trusted by Emperors Enyū and Kazan, he ran the Council of State as ichinokami, balancing the Fujiwara regents. His daughter Rinshi married Fujiwara no Michinaga and bore the regent Yorimichi and Empress Shōshi.
zh: 源雅信（920—993）是平安时代中期的公卿，式部卿敦实亲王第三子，宇多源氏之祖。936年臣籍降下，赐姓源氏；951年任参议，977年任右大臣，978年升左大臣，官至从一位。他深得圆融、花山两天皇信任，作为一上主持太政官政务，与藤原摄关家相抗衡。其女伦子嫁给藤原道长，生下摄政赖通与一条天皇中宫彰子。

en: Minamoto no Masazane (1059–1127) was a late-Heian noble of the Murakami Genji, eldest son of the right minister Minamoto no Akifusa and maternal uncle of Emperor Horikawa. He became a councillor at nineteen in 1077 and inner minister in 1100, the third minister in as many generations of his line. He became right minister in 1115. In 1122 he was made grand minister of state, the first Minamoto to hold the highest court office, having reached junior first rank in 1113. Illness led him to take Buddhist vows in 1124, and he died in 1127; his descendants founded the Koga family.
zh: 源雅实（1059—1127）是平安时代后期的公卿，村上源氏右大臣源显房的长子、堀河天皇的外叔父。他1077年19岁任参议，1100年任内大臣，是家中连续第三代出任大臣者；1115年任右大臣。1113年叙从一位，1122年升任太政大臣，是源氏出任太政大臣的首例。1124年因病出家，1127年去世。他的子孙开创久我家。

en: Minamoto no Michichika (1149–1202) was a Murakami Genji noble and statesman of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods. He joined the kugyō as sangi in 1180 and became provisional chūnagon in 1185, receiving Inaba Province as his fief. In 1198 he secured the enthronement of his adopted daughter's son as Emperor Tsuchimikado, and as the emperor's maternal grandfather dominated the court, rising to naidaijin. Serving seven emperors, he brought the Murakami Genji to the height of their power. He died in 1202, posthumously granted junior first rank. A waka poet, he helped plan the Shin Kokin Wakashū.
zh: 源通亲（1149—1202）是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的村上源氏公卿、政治家。他于1180年任参议，跻身公卿，1185年任权中纳言，受领因幡国。1198年，他拥立养女之子为土御门天皇，以天皇外祖父的身份主宰朝政，官至内大臣。他历仕七代天皇，将村上源氏推向权势的顶峰。1202年他去世后被追赠从一位。他擅长和歌，曾参与《新古今和歌集》的编纂筹备。

en: Minamoto no Mitsukuni (1063–1148), also recorded as Toki Mitsukuni, was a late-Heian warrior and the eldest son of Minamoto no Kunifusa, ancestor of the Mino Genji. He served Retired Emperor Shirakawa as a guards officer and kebiishi, accompanying him to Kurama-dera in 1092 and the Iwashimizu Hachiman shrine in 1106. Appointed governor of Dewa, he joined Minamoto no Tameyoshi in the 1109 campaign against Minamoto no Yoshitsuna's family, but in 1110 he illegally entered the regent's Sagae estate and abandoned his post. In 1113 he helped defend Kyoto against the mass protest by Enryaku-ji and Kōfuku-ji monks.
zh: 源光国（1063—1148），又作土岐光国，是平安时代后期的武将，美浓源氏之祖源国房的长子。他以卫府武官和检非违使身份侍奉白河院，1092年随驾参诣鞍马寺，1106年又随院参诣石清水八幡宫。他后任出羽守，1109年与源为义一同参与追讨源义纲一族；但1110年他滥入摄关家领有的出羽寒河江庄，又擅自弃官。1113年延历寺与兴福寺发起大规模强诉时，他参与了京都的防卫。

en: Minamoto no Mitsukuni was a mid-Heian-period warrior, the eldest son of Minamoto no Mitsuyoshi and a nephew of Mitsunaka. Around 987 he built the Emi-no-yakata hall at Shukuno in Nose District, Settsu Province, and made it his residence. While serving as governor of Tōtōmi around 995–998, he was exiled to Mikawa Province for defying an imperial order; tradition holds that at Karijuku there he founded a temple and a shrine to pray for his late mother. His heir Tamemitsu married a daughter of Minamoto no Yorinobu, tying the line to the Kawachi Genji.
zh: 源满国是日本平安时代中期的武士，源满快长子、源满仲的侄子。约987年，他在摄津国能势郡宿野修建“撰见馆”居住。约995—998年的长德年间，他在任远江守期间因违背敕命被流放至三河国；相传他在流放地刈宿修建寺院与神社，为亡母祈求冥福。其嫡子源为满迎娶源赖信之女，与河内源氏结为姻亲。

en: Minamoto no Mitsunaga (died 1184), also called Toki Mitsunaga, was a Mino Genji warrior and head of the Toki clan, serving in Kyoto as a police commissioner under the Taira. In 1180 he led troops to arrest Prince Mochihito, who had already fled. In 1181 he joined the Mino and Ōmi revolt against the Taira, was defeated, and was exiled to Izu, where he met Minamoto no Yoritomo. In 1183 he entered Kyoto with Kiso Yoshinaka and became governor of Hōki, then died defending Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa at the Battle of Hōjūji in January 1184.
zh: 源光长（？—1184），一作土岐光长，是美浓源氏武将、土岐氏惣领，在平氏政权下担任京都的检非违使。1180年，他率兵追捕以仁王，但亲王已先行逃离。1181年，他参与美浓、近江两国反抗平家的叛乱，兵败后被流放伊豆，在那里结识源赖朝。1183年，他随木曾义仲入京，被任命为伯耆守，随后站在后白河法皇一方，于1184年1月的法住寺合战中战死。

en: Minamoto no Mitsunaka (912–997) was a Heian-period samurai and court official, son of Tsunemoto, who built the Seiwa Genji into a military power. He tied the clan to the Fujiwara regents: in 969 he accused Minamoto no Tsura and others of plotting to depose the crown prince, an affair that brought down Minamoto no Takaakira, and in 986 helped Fujiwara no Kaneie force Emperor Kazan to abdicate. As acting governor of ten provinces, above all Settsu, and chinjufu shōgun, he was among Japan's wealthiest courtiers, his warriors the Fujiwara's 'teeth and claws'. He took Buddhist vows in 987 and died at his Tada manor. His sons included Yorimitsu and Yorinobu.
zh: 源满仲（912—997）是日本平安时代的武士与朝廷官员，源经基之子，奠定清和源氏武力根基的人物。他把源氏绑定在藤原摄关家：969年密告源连等人谋废皇太子，此事导致源高明失势；986年又协助藤原兼家迫使花山天皇退位。他历任十国国司，以摄津国为根本，又任镇守府将军，是当时最富有的公卿之一，麾下武士被称为藤原家的“爪牙”。987年出家，法名满庆，最终在摄津多田庄去世。其子有源赖光、源赖信等。

en: Minamoto no Mitsunobu (c. 1093–1145), also called Toki Mitsunobu and the Tosa Lieutenant, was a late Heian warrior and eldest son of Dewa governor Minamoto no Mitsukuni. He served retired emperors Shirakawa and Toba as Northern Guardsman and Kebiishi, counted among the Four Warriors of Toba's court. In 1129 he nearly fought Minamoto no Tameyoshi over a pardoned retainer. In 1130 two men posing as the dead Minamoto no Yoshichika fought outside his Kyoto mansion; Mitsunobu raided ex-regent Fujiwara no Tadazane's residence and killed one, for which he was exiled to Tosa. Pardoned in 1143, he died in 1145.
zh: 源光信（约1093—1145），一作土岐光信，通称出羽判官、土佐判官，是平安时代末期武将，出羽守源光国的长男。他侍奉白河、鸟羽两上皇，历任北面武士、检非违使，列为鸟羽院四天王之一。1129年，他为一名获赦郎党的归属与源为义相争，几乎动武。1130年，两名冒充已故源义亲之人在他京都宅邸前相斗，光信袭击前关白藤原忠实的邸宅，杀死其中一人，因此被流放土佐。1143年获赦，1145年去世。

en: Minamoto no Mitsuyoshi was a mid-Heian-period warrior, the fifth son of Minamoto no Tsunemoto and a younger brother of Mitsunaka. He served as a middle-ranking capital official, including as a kebiiishi officer and governor of Shimotsuke, and his descendants settled as samurai in Shinano.
