zh: 源满快是日本平安时代中期的武将，源经基第五子、源满仲之弟，历任右卫门尉、检非违使、下野守等中级官职，其子孙后来作为武家在信浓国定居。

en: Minamoto no Morofusa (1008–1077) was a Heian noble, ancestor of the Nakanoin line of the Murakami Genji. The eldest son of Imperial Prince Tomohira, he received the Minamoto surname in 1020 and became a foster son of Regent Fujiwara no Yorimichi. In 1024 he married Sonshi, a daughter of Fujiwara no Michinaga, whose only non-imperial son-in-law he was, and took junior third rank at fifteen. Named inner minister in 1065, he was the first Minamoto minister in seventy years, then right minister in 1069 and junior first rank in 1074; he died in 1077 after taking the tonsure.
zh: 源师房（1008—1077）是平安时代的公卿，村上源氏中院流之祖。他是中务卿具平亲王的长子，1020年获赐源姓、降下臣籍，被摄政藤原赖通收为犹子。1024年，他娶藤原道长之女尊子为妻，是道长唯一的人臣女婿，15岁即叙从三位。1065年任内大臣，是70年来源氏出任大臣的第一人；1069年任右大臣，1074年升至从一位，1077年剃发出家后去世。

en: Minamoto no Muneyori was a son of the late Heian warrior Minamoto no Yoriyuki. After Yoriyuki's suicide in Kyoto in 1157, Muneyori and his brothers were adopted by their uncle Minamoto no Yorimasa. His descendants became the Oguni clan of Echigo.
zh: 源宗赖是平安时代末期武将源赖行之子。1157年赖行在京都自尽后，宗赖与兄弟被叔父源赖政收为养子。其后裔成为越后国的小国氏。

en: Minamoto no Nakamasa (born c. 1050), also called Baba no Nakamasa, was a late-Heian warrior and poet, the second son of Settsu Genji leader Minamoto no Yoritsuna. In 1095 he and his elder brother Akikuni were unusually named chamberlains to Emperor Horikawa through Shirakawa's favor. He served the Shirakawa and Toba courts as kebiishi and governor of Shimotsuke, reaching junior fourth rank. Around 1118–1124 he captured an impostor who claimed to be the rebel Minamoto no Yoshichika. Fifteen of his poems entered imperial anthologies, and between 1135 and 1142 he passed the family headship to his son Yorimasa.
zh: 源仲政（约1050年生），又称马场仲政，是平安时代后期的武将与和歌人，摄津源氏当主源赖纲次男。1095年，他与兄长明国一同被任命为堀河天皇的六位藏人，兄弟同任藏人极为罕见，背后有白河院的优遇。他后来侍奉白河、鸟羽两院，历任检非违使、下野守，官至从四位下。1118—1124年间，他擒获一名自称叛将源义亲的人，立下功勋。他有十五首和歌收入敕撰和歌集，1135—1142年间把家督让给儿子源赖政。

en: Minamoto no Noboru (848-918) was a Saga Genji noble, the second son of the sadaijin Minamoto no Toru. After taking junior fifth rank in 875 he held a string of guards posts, then entered Emperor Uda's inner circle as head chamberlain in 893 and became a councilor in 895, the year his father died and he inherited the famous Kawara-no-in villa. Promoted to middle counselor in 908 and major counselor in 914, he reached senior third rank in 916 and died in 918 aged seventy-one, known as the Kawara Major Counselor.
zh: 源昇（848—918）是嵯峨源氏公卿，左大臣源融的次子。875年叙从五位下，历任近卫、卫府武官，893年任藏人头，入侍宇多天皇近侧，895年拜参议，位列公卿；同年其父去世，他继承了著名的河原院宅邸。908年升中纳言，914年升大纳言，916年叙正三位，918年去世，享年71岁，世称河原大纳言。

en: Minamoto no Norifusa was a member of the Murakami Genji, recorded in the genealogy of the Nawa family as the son of Minamoto no Tadafusa and father of Norimasa.
zh: 源宪房是村上源氏一员，名和氏谱系记载他为源忠房之子、宪政之父。

en: Minamoto no Norimasa was a member of the Murakami Genji, recorded in the genealogy of the Nawa family as the son of Minamoto no Norifusa and a junior assistant minister of military affairs.
zh: 源宪政是村上源氏一员，名和氏谱系记载他为源宪房之子，官兵部少辅。

en: Minamoto no Noriyori (1150–1193), called Kaba no Kaja, was Yoshitomo's sixth son and a half-brother of Yoritomo and Yoshitsune. Raised in Totomi Province after his father's overthrow, he joined Yoritomo's uprising and in 1184 led an army west as his deputy against Kiso Yoshinaka and the Taira, campaigning through western provinces and Kyushu while Yoshitsune destroyed the Taira fleet at Dannoura. He fought in the Oshu campaign of 1189. After the Soga brothers' vendetta of 1193, a careless word to Hojo Masako made Yoritomo suspect him; he was exiled to Izu, where later accounts say he was killed in September 1193.
zh: 源范赖（1150—1193），通称蒲冠者，是源义朝第六子、源赖朝的异母弟、源义经的异母兄。父亲败死后，他在远江国长大，后来投奔赖朝举兵；1184年，他作为赖朝的代官率大军西上，追讨木曾义仲与平家，转战西国和九州，义经则在坛之浦歼灭平氏水师。他还参加了1189年的奥州合战。1193年曾我兄弟复仇事件后，他对北条政子的一句失言引起赖朝猜忌，被流放伊豆；后世记载称他于同年9月在当地遇害。

en: Minamoto no Suefusa was a son of the late-Heian court noble Minamoto no Akifusa of the Murakami Genji; his mother is unrecorded. Clan genealogies note only that he died in 1156, the year of the Hōgen Disturbance.
zh: 源季房是平安时代后期村上源氏公卿源显房之子，生母不见记载。家谱中仅记录他于1156年去世，时值保元之乱爆发的那一年。

en: Minamoto no Suenori was a twelfth-century Murakami Genji figure, a son of Minamoto no Suefusa. The Sonpi Bunmyaku genealogies make him the father of Minamoto no Yorinori and grandfather of the warrior Akamatsu Norikage, ancestor of the Akamatsu clan of Harima Province.
zh: 源季则是12世纪的村上源氏族人，源季房之子。《尊卑分脉》系统的家谱记载，他是源赖则之父、武将赤松则景的祖父，而赤松则景是播磨赤松氏之祖。

en: Minamoto no Sukenori (951–998) was a mid-Heian court noble of the Uda Genji, the fourth son of the Sadaijin Minamoto no Masanobu. Unlike most aristocratic heirs, he studied at the State Academy, becoming a literary scholar in 975 and a palace secretary in 977. After serving as provisional governor of Tōtōmi and Aki and governor of Kawachi, he served Emperor Ichijō, heading the imperial secretariat in 991 and joining the council as Sangi in 994; he became Ōkura-kyō in 997. His eldest son Nariyori was the ancestor of the Sasaki clan of Ōmi Province.
zh: 源扶义（951—998）是平安时代中期宇多源氏的公卿，左大臣源雅信第四子。与一般贵族子弟不同，他求学于大学寮，975年成为文章生，977年任进士藏人。此后历任远江权守、安艺权守、河内守等地方官，又回到天皇身边担任弁官，991年任藏人头，994年任参议兼右大弁，位列公卿，997年兼大藏卿。其长男成赖是近江佐佐木氏之祖。

en: Minamoto no Tadafusa was a member of the Murakami Genji, recorded in the genealogy of the Nawa family as a son of Minamoto no Suefusa.
zh: 源忠房是村上源氏一员，名和氏谱系记载他为源季房之子。

en: Minamoto no Tamemitsu was a late-Heian warrior, the eldest son of Minamoto no Mitsukuni. He married a daughter of Minamoto no Yorinobu of the Kawachi Genji, is said to have served as governor of Kai, and fathered Minamoto no Tamekimi.
zh: 源为满是日本平安时代后期的武士，源满国长子，迎娶河内源氏源赖信之女，生子源为公，据传亦曾任甲斐守。

en: Minamoto no Tamemitsu, or Iijima Tamemitsu, was an Ina Genji warrior and steward of Iijima in Shinano, son of Katagiri Tametsuna. For his service on shogunate side in the Jokyu War of 1221, he received the Misawa estate in Izumo Province as its new steward.
zh: 源为光，又称饭岛为光，是信浓伊那源氏武将、饭岛地头，片切为纲之子。1221年承久之乱中，他为幕府一方立下战功，获封出云国三泽庄，担任新补地头。

en: Minamoto no Tamemoto, called Katagiri Genpachi, was a late-Heian warrior, son of Shinano governor Minamoto no Tamekimi and ancestor of the Katagiri clan; he served as chamberlain and was said to have inherited holdings in Ina and lived in Katagiri.
zh: 源为基，通称片切源八，是平安时代后期的武将、信浓守源为公之子、片切氏之祖；他曾任藏人，相传继承了父亲在信浓国伊奈郡的部分势力，并居于片切乡。

en: Minamoto no Tamesuke, also called Ina Tarō, was a late-Heian warrior of the Ina Genji in Shinano Province, a son of Minamoto no Tamekimi, governor of Shinano. His descendants founded several local warrior houses, among them the Hayashi, Suwabe and Mitoya families.
zh: 源为扶，又称伊那太郎，是平安时代后期信浓国伊那源氏的武将，信浓守源为公之子，其后人形成了林氏、诹访部氏、三刀屋氏等当地武家。

en: Minamoto no Tametomo (1139–1170), called Chinzei Hachiro, was the eighth son of Minamoto no Tameyoshi and uncle of Yoritomo and Yoshitsune. The Hogen Monogatari relates that he was banished to Kyushu in his youth, subdued the region and took the name Chinzei Hachiro. In the Hogen Disturbance of 1156 he fought at the Shirakawa palace for Retired Emperor Sutoku against his brother Yoshitomo; the tale says that after the defeat his bow arm was crippled and he was exiled to Oshima. It relates that he made himself master of the Izu Islands and killed himself when a punitive force arrived in 1170, in an early account of seppuku.
zh: 源为朝（1139—1170），号镇西八郎，是源为义的第八子、源赖朝与义经的叔父。据《保元物语》记载，他年轻时被放逐九州，在当地称霸一方，遂号镇西八郎。1156年保元之乱中，他在白河殿为崇德上皇作战，对手正是其兄义朝；物语称他兵败后被割断臂筋，流放伊豆大岛。物语还记载，此后他实际控制了伊豆诸岛，1170年朝廷派军追讨，他切腹自尽，这是较早记载切腹的事例之一。

en: Minamoto no Tametomo (1005–1075) was a late-Heian warrior of the Seiwa Genji, son of the Kai governor Minamoto no Tamemitsu by a daughter of Minamoto no Yorinobu. Tradition records that he became governor of Shinano and settled in Ina District during the Eishō era of 1046 to 1053, where his descendants grew into local lords. He is counted the ancestor of the Shinano Genji and Ina Genji, and the Kaminohira fort in northern Ina is said to be his work. He died in 1075, aged seventy-one.
zh: 源为公（1005—1075）是平安时代后期的武将，属清和源氏，为甲斐守源为满之子，母亲是河内守源赖信之女。相传他出任信浓守，于永承年间（1046—1053年）在信浓国伊那郡定居，子孙逐渐成为当地有力武士。他被尊为信浓源氏、伊那源氏之祖，伊那郡北部的上平城相传为其所筑。他于1075年去世，终年七十一岁。

en: Minamoto no Tametsuna, also called Katagiri Tametsuna or Jirodayu, was a Shinano warrior of the Ina Genji and second son of Minamoto no Tameyuki. He held Iijima in Ina district as land steward and took the name Iijima, becoming the ancestor of the Iijima house.
zh: 源为纲，又称片切为纲、二郎大夫，是信浓国伊那源氏的武将、源为行的次子。他领有伊那郡饭岛乡，担任当地地头并改称饭岛氏，被后世奉为饭岛氏的始祖。

en: Minamoto no Tameyoshi (1096–1156), also called Mutsu Shirō, was head of the Kawachi Genji, the main Minamoto warrior line. The son of Minamoto no Yoshichika and grandson of Minamoto no Yoshiie, he was passed over at court in favour of Taira no Tadamori. Around 1113 he is said to have scattered fighting warrior-monks of Mii-dera and Enryaku-ji on the streets of Kyoto with a handful of mounted samurai. In 1156 he backed Retired Emperor Sutoku in the Hōgen Disturbance. Defeated, he took the vows and was handed to his son Yoshitomo, who beheaded him on 17 August 1156.
zh: 源为义（1096—1156），通称陆奥四郎，是河内源氏的栋梁。他是源义亲之子、源义家之孙，在朝廷任官上遭到冷遇，平忠盛更受器重。约1113年，三井寺与延历寺的僧兵在京都街头械斗，相传他率少数骑马武士驱散乱众。1156年保元之乱中，他支持崇德上皇，战败出家后被交给儿子源义朝，于1156年8月17日被义朝亲手斩首。

en: Minamoto no Tameyuki, known as Katagiri Genta, was a late Heian warrior of the Ina Genji in Shinano and second head of the Katagiri house. A son of Minamoto no Tamemoto, he held the title Hyōgo no suke. His dates are unknown.
zh: 源为行，通称片切源太，是平安时代后期信浓国伊那源氏片切氏第二代当主，源为基之子，任兵库助。生卒年不详。

en: Minamoto no Toru (822-895), a son of Emperor Saga, received the Minamoto surname in 838 and founded the Toru line of the Saga Genji. He rose to middle counselor in 864, major counselor in 870, and sadaijin, the senior minister, in 872, though Fujiwara no Mototsune held the real power; after 876 Toru largely withdrew to his Kyoto villa. His Kawara-no-in mansion, with a garden imitating the Shiogama scenery, and his Kokinshu poems made him famous; the Hyakunin Isshu calls him the Kawara Minister, and he is a leading candidate for the model of Hikaru Genji.
zh: 源融（822—895）是嵯峨天皇之子，838年元服时获赐源朝臣姓，为嵯峨源氏融流之祖。他历任要职，864年任中纳言，870年升大纳言，872年拜左大臣，位居太政官首班，但实权掌握在藤原基经手中；876年后他基本退居京都私邸。他在河原院的宅邸修筑仿盐灶景致的园林，和歌收入《古今和歌集》，在《小仓百人一首》中以河原左大臣闻名，也被视为《源氏物语》主人公光源氏的重要原型。

en: Minamoto no Tsuko (891-942) was a mid-Heian military aristocrat of the Saga Genji, second son of the major counselor Minamoto no Noboru and grandson of the sadaijin Minamoto no Toru. Holding junior fifth rank, upper grade, he served as governor of Musashi and went east to the Kanto. The Fuso Ryakki records that in 919 the former provisional vice-governor of Musashi seized official stores, burned government buildings, attacked the provincial headquarters, and sought to attack Governor Takamuko no Toshiharu; some sources name him Minamoto no Nin rather than Tsuko, and no punishment is recorded. His descendants flourished as the Mita Genji.
zh: 源仕（891—942）是平安时代中期的军事贵族，嵯峨源氏大纳言源昇的次子、左大臣源融之孙，官至从五位上武藏守、修理大夫。他作为国司东下关东。《扶桑略记》记载，919年，时任武藏前权介的源仕（部分史料记作源任）侵吞官物、烧毁官舍并袭击国府，企图攻击武藏守高向利春，但史书未见他受到处分的记载。他的子孙后来以箕田源氏之名在关东发展势力。

en: Minamoto no Tsunemoto (894–961) was a Heian-period warrior and founder of the Seiwa Genji line of the Minamoto clan. A son of Prince Sadazumi and grandson of Emperor Seiwa, he became vice-governor of Musashi Province in 938. After a clash with local magnates he fled to Kyoto and accused Taira no Masakado of plotting revolt; when Masakado rose in 939–940, Tsunemoto was sent against him but returned on learning he had already been defeated. In 941 he helped pursue Fujiwara no Sumitomo's followers. He held the title of chinjufu shōgun. His son was Mitsunaka.
zh: 源经基（894—961）是日本平安时代中期的武将，清和源氏经基流的始祖。他是贞纯亲王之子、清和天皇之孙，938年任武藏介赴任武藏国，与当地豪族冲突后逃回京都，告发平将门谋反。939—940年平将门起兵，经基奉命赴征，得知将门已被讨平后返回京都。941年，他又参与追捕藤原纯友的部属。他官至镇守府将军，其子是源满仲。

en: Minamoto no Yorichika (966–1057) was a mid-Heian warrior, second son of Mitsunaka and ancestor of the Yamato Genji; Yorinobu was his full brother. Serving Fujiwara no Michinaga, in 994 he was named among the warriors sent to suppress bandits. Denied the governorship of Settsu, where his estates lay, he built his power in Yamato as its three-term governor, fighting Kōfuku-ji and Kasuga Shrine over land. In 1017 he lost his posts for ordering the killing of the courtier Kiyohara no Motonobu, and in 1049 his son Yorifusa's clash with Kōfuku-ji brought Yorichika exile to Tosa. His subsequent fate is unknown.
zh: 源赖亲（966—1057）是日本平安时代中期的武将，源满仲次子、大和源氏之祖，与源赖信为同母兄弟。他出仕藤原道长，994年被列为追捕盗贼的“武勇人”之一。他受任摄津守的希望两度落空，便转而经营大和国，三度担任大和守，为庄园领地与兴福寺、春日大社相争。1017年，他因指使郎党杀害朝臣清原致信而被免官；1049年其次子源赖房与兴福寺交战，赖亲受牵连被流放土佐国，此后下落不明。

en: Minamoto no Yorikuni (died 1058) was a mid-Heian warrior and court official, eldest son of Yorimitsu and cousin of Yoriyoshi. He made his career as a middle-ranking officer in the capital, long serving Michinaga's daughter Shōshi and her son Emperor Go-Ichijō. More man of letters than soldier, he attended Michinaga's Chinese poetry gathering in 1007, gained access to the inner court, and married his daughters to high nobles including the regent Fujiwara no Morozane. His real deeds were police work, like arresting an assailant in 1019, though legend sends him with his father against Shuten-dōji and Ibaraki-dōji.
zh: 源赖国（？—1058）是日本平安时代中期的武将、官人，源赖光长子、源赖义的堂兄。他以中级京官身份在京都任职，长期侍奉藤原道长之女上东门院彰子与其子后一条天皇。他偏于文事，1007年出席道长举办的汉诗会，获准内昇殿，女儿们嫁与摄政藤原师实等公卿。他可考的事迹多为京城警备，如1019年逮捕暴汉；但在传说中，他随父征讨酒吞童子和茨木童子。

en: Minamoto no Yorimitsu (948–1021) was a Heian-period warrior, eldest son of Mitsunaka and third head of the Seiwa Genji. He inherited his father's Tada manor in Settsu, and his descendants became known as the Settsu Genji. Serving the Fujiwara regents, he attached himself to Fujiwara no Michinaga from about 990 and held governorships including Bizen in 992 and Mino in 1001. Later legend made him a monster-slayer who overthrew the oni chief Shuten-dōji of Ōeyama with his Four Retainers. He died in 1021, leaving his heir Yorikuni.
zh: 源赖光（948—1021）是日本平安时代中期的武将，源满仲长子、清和源氏第三代。他继承父亲在摄津国多田的庄园，子孙被称为“摄津源氏”。他出仕藤原摄关家，约990年起依附藤原道长，历任992年备前守、1001年美浓守等国司。后世传说把他塑造成斩杀大江山鬼王酒吞童子的英雄，麾下有“赖光四天王”相从。1021年去世，嫡子源赖国嗣立。

en: Minamoto no Yorinobu (968–1048) was a Heian-period commander, son of Mitsunaka, progenitor of the Kawachi Genji and holder of the chinjufu shōgun title. With his brother Yorimitsu he served Fujiwara no Michinaga, who counted him among his four warrior favourites. Yorinobu governed provinces including Ise, Shinano and Kai, and in 1030 was sent against Taira no Tadatsune of Kazusa, who had rebelled in 1028 and surrendered without resistance in 1031; the victory drew the warriors of the Bandō eastlands into Minamoto service. His son Yoriyoshi and grandson Yoshiie led the Kawachi Genji after him. He died in 1048, dharma name Renshin.
zh: 源赖信（968—1048）是日本平安时代的武将，源满仲之子、河内源氏之祖，曾任镇守府将军。他与兄赖光一同出仕藤原道长，被列为道长身边四大亲信武士之一。赖信历任伊势、信浓、甲斐等国守，1030年奉命讨伐1028年起事的上总介平忠常，忠常于1031年不战而降，此役使坂东武士纷纷投入源氏麾下。其子源赖义、孙源义家先后统领河内源氏。1048年去世，法名莲心。

en: Minamoto no Yorinori was a twelfth-century Murakami Genji warrior in Harima Province, son of Minamoto no Suenori. Genealogies record him as governor (kami) of Harima, an office his descendants inherited, and as the father of Akamatsu Norikage, ancestor of the Akamatsu and Uno clans.
zh: 源赖则是12世纪播磨国的村上源氏武士，源季则之子。家谱记载他曾任播磨守，子孙世袭此职；他又是赤松则景之父，为赤松氏、宇野氏的先祖。

en: Minamoto no Yoritsuna (1025–1097), also known as Tada no Yoritsuna, was a late Heian warrior and waka poet, the fifth son of Minamoto no Yorikuni who inherited the main Settsu Genji line. He served the regent Fujiwara no Morozane and held posts including chamberlain and kebiishi, rising to governor of Mikawa and junior fourth rank. In 1079 he helped defend Kyoto during the Enryaku-ji monks' protest. A noted poet, he joined six poetry contests, associated with Ōe no Masafusa and Nōin, and placed eight poems in imperial anthologies. He took Buddhist vows in 1096 and died the following year.
zh: 源赖纲（1025—1097），又称多田赖纲，是平安时代后期的武将与和歌人，美浓守源赖国第五子，继承了摄津源氏的嫡流。他以家司身份侍奉关白藤原师实，历任藏人、检非违使等职，官至三河守、从四位下。1079年延历寺强诉时，他参与了京都的防卫。他擅长和歌，先后参加六次歌合，与大江匡房、能因等人交游，共有八首和歌收入《后拾遗集》以来的敕撰和歌集。1096年出家，次年去世。

en: Minamoto no Yoriyoshi (988–1075), head of the Kawachi Genji and chinjufu shōgun, was the son of Yorinobu. As governor of Mutsu from 1051 he fought the Abe clan in the twelve-year Zenkunen War. He was crushingly defeated at the Battle of Kinomi in 1057, but with Kiyohara aid from Dewa he stormed the Abe stronghold of Kuriyagawa in 1062 and slew Abe no Sadato, ending the war. In 1063 he received the rich governorship of Iyo and founded Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine in Kamakura. His son Yoshiie fought beside him. Ordained in 1065, Yoriyoshi died in 1075.
zh: 源赖义（988—1075）是河内源氏首领、镇守府将军，源赖信之子。1051年他出任陆奥守，与安倍氏展开长达十二年的“前九年之役”。1057年他在黄海之战中惨败，此后得到出羽国清原氏援助，于1062年攻破安倍氏据点厨川栅，斩杀安倍贞任，结束战事。1063年他受任富庶的伊予守，并在镰仓创建鹤冈八幡宫。其子源义家随军征战。赖义于1065年出家，1075年去世。

en: Minamoto no Yoriyuki (d. 1157), also called Oguni Yoriyuki, was a late Heian warrior, second son of Minamoto no Nakamasa and a younger brother of Minamoto no Yorimasa. He served as a palace chamberlain and is recorded as governor of Tango Province. In 1157, after the Hōgen Disturbance, the court sentenced him to exile in Aki for unlawfully mustering soldiers. On 23 August, while escorted out of Kyoto, he killed his Kebiishi guard Nobuzumi at Nishi-Shichijō and then committed seppuku. His sons were adopted by Yorimasa; through Muneyori he was ancestor of the Oguni clan of Echigo.
zh: 源赖行（？—1157），一作小国赖行，是平安时代末期武将，兵库头源仲政次男、源赖政的弟弟。他曾任藏人，又有担任丹后守的记载。保元之乱次年的1157年七月，朝廷以擅自发兵为由下令将他流放安艺国；十七日（8月23日）押解出京途中，他在京都西七条杀死押送使检非违使信澄，随后自尽。诸子由赖政收养，其中宗赖的后裔成为越后国的小国氏。

en: Minamoto no Yoshichika (died March 1108) was a late-Heian warrior, the second son and heir of the celebrated Minamoto no Yoshiie. Appointed governor of Tsushima, he was accused in 1101 by the Dazaifu authority Ōe no Masafusa of seizing tribute and killing people, and after slaying more officials he was exiled to Oki in 1102. Instead he stayed in Izumo Province and again attacked officers and looted state goods. The court charged Taira no Masamori with his suppression; Masamori defeated and killed him in 1108 in the conflict known as the Yoshichika disturbance. His son was Minamoto no Tameyoshi.
zh: 源义亲（卒于1108年3月）是平安时代后期的武将，名将源义家的次男和嫡子。他出任对马守期间，于1101年被大宰权帅大江匡房控告掠夺官物、杀害良民；1102年又杀死官吏，被朝廷流放隐岐国，却滞留出云国，再度杀害官吏、夺取官物。朝廷命平正盛前往追讨，正盛于1108年将他讨平诛杀，史称源义亲之乱。其子为源为义。

en: Minamoto no Yoshiie (1039–1106), known as Hachimantarō, was the foremost late-Heian warrior and third-generation head of the Kawachi Genji, eldest son of Minamoto no Yoriyoshi. He fought beside his father against the Abe clan in the Earlier Nine Years' War, and from 1083 led the suppression of the Kiyohara in the Later Three Years' War, storming the Kanazawa stockade in 1087 with his brother Yoshimitsu and Fujiwara no Kiyohira. Retired Emperor Shirakawa called him the mightiest warrior in the land, and legend made him a son of the war god Hachiman. He died in 1106.
zh: 源义家（1039—1106），通称八幡太郎，是平安时代后期首屈一指的武将、河内源氏第三代当主，源赖义的长子。他早年随父在前九年之役中征讨奥州安倍氏；1083年起又率军在后三年之役中平定清原氏，1087年与弟弟源义光、藤原清衡合力攻陷金泽栅。白河法皇称他为“天下第一武勇之士”，相传他是战神八幡神之子。1106年去世。

en: Minamoto no Yoshikiyo (c. 1075–1145) was a late Heian warrior and second head of the Kai Genji, son of its founder Minamoto no Yoshimitsu. His father obtained Takeda-gō in Naka District, Hitachi, and enfeoffed him there; Yoshikiyo called himself Takeda Kaja. In 1130 his son Kiyomitsu clashed with the local Daijō family over a boundary, and father and son were exiled in 1131 to Ichikawa manor in Kai. Yoshikiyo became its steward around 1133 and later advanced into Henmi. He died at Ichikawa in 1145, and his descendants, led by the Takeda, became the Kai Genji houses.
zh: 源义清（约1075—1145）是平安时代后期武将，甲斐源氏始祖源义光（新罗三郎义光）之子、甲斐源氏第二代。源义光从常陆国豪族平清干处取得那珂郡武田乡，交给义清，他遂自称武田冠者。1130年，其子清光围绕庄园边界与常陆在厅官人大掾盛干相争，父子于1131年被流放甲斐国市河庄。约1133年，义清出任市河庄司，后来又进占逸见乡。1145年卒于市河庄，其子孙以武田氏为首，形成甲斐源氏诸家。

en: Minamoto no Yoshikuni (c. 1082–1155) was a Kawachi Genji warrior, third son of Minamoto no Yoshiie and ancestor of the Nitta and Ashikaga clans. He inherited the Hachiman manor in Kōzuke Province. In 1106 he fought his uncle Minamoto no Yoshimitsu in Hitachi during the Hitachi conflict and incurred imperial censure. He built up holdings in neighbouring Shimotsuke and in 1142 donated his Ashikaga lands to Anrakuju-in to form Ashikaga manor. His sons Yoshishige and Yoshiyasu founded the Nitta and Ashikaga houses. He took vows in 1154 and died at Nitta the next year.
zh: 源义国（约1082—1155）是河内源氏武将，源义家三男，新田氏与足利氏的共同祖先。他继承了上野国的八幡庄。1106年，他在常陆合战中与叔父源义光交战，受到朝廷处分。他在邻国下野稳步经营领地，1142年把足利的传领施入安乐寿院，正式立为足利庄。其子义重、义康分别开创新田氏与足利氏。1154年他出家，次年卒于新田。

en: Minamoto no Yoshimitsu (1045–1127), known as Shinra Saburō, was a late-Heian warrior, the third son of Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and younger brother of Yoshiie. He served in the Later Three Years' War of 1083–1087, after which he was made governor of Kai Province and settled there. Skilled in horsemanship and archery, he later fought his nephew Yoshikuni over land, and after Yoshiie's death was suspected of plotting the murder of Kawachi Genji head Yoshitada. His son Yoshikiyo took the name Takeda, making Yoshimitsu ancestor of the Takeda clan; tradition also credits him with founding Daitō-ryū jūjutsu.
zh: 源义光（1045—1127），又名新罗三郎，是平安时代后期的武将，河内源氏栋梁源赖义第三子、源义家之弟。他参加了1083—1087年的后三年之役，因功出任甲斐守并在当地定居。他擅长骑射，后来曾与侄子源义国争地；义家死后，他被疑策划暗杀河内源氏当主源义忠。其子源义清改姓武田，源义光由此成为武田氏之祖；相传他还创立了大东流合气柔术。

en: Minamoto no Yoshinari (1067–1133), first named Yoshishige, was a late-Heian warrior and the eldest son of Minamoto no Yoshimitsu, counted as the effective founder of the Satake clan, though he never used the Satake surname himself. In 1106 he and his father fought their cousin Minamoto no Yoshikuni in the Kantō region. In 1109 his brother-in-law Kashima Saburō assassinated the Kawachi Genji head Minamoto no Yoshitada, embroiling Yoshimitsu's line in the succession feud. Yoshinari supported his father and helped develop Yoshimitsu's line. He died of illness in 1133, leaving a son, Satake no Masayoshi.
zh: 源义业（1067—1133），初名义成，是平安时代后期的武将、源义光的嫡男，被视为佐竹氏实质上的初代当主，但他本人从未自称佐竹姓。1106年，他与父亲一同在关东和堂兄源义国交战。1109年，他的姻亲鹿岛三郎暗杀了河内源氏栋梁源义忠，使义光一支卷入继嗣之争。义业辅佐父亲，促进义光一支的发展，1133年病逝，子为佐竹昌义。

en: Minamoto no Yoshitomo (1123–1160) was the sixth head of the Kawachi Genji line of the Minamoto clan and father of Yoritomo, Noriyori and Yoshitsune. Sent east as a youth, he built a network of Kantō warrior houses and became governor of Shimotsuke. In the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 he fought for Emperor Go-Shirakawa against his own father Tameyoshi, and was named captain of the Left Stables. Three years later he joined Fujiwara no Nobuyori in the Heiji Disturbance, was defeated by Taira no Kiyomori, and was murdered by a treacherous retainer while fleeing through Owari in 1160.
zh: 源义朝（1123—1160）是河内源氏第六代栋梁，也是源赖朝、范赖、义经之父。他少年时前往东国，与关东诸武士团结盟，被任命为下野守。1156年保元之乱中，他为后白河天皇作战，对阵自己的父亲为义，因功任左马头。三年后，他追随藤原信赖卷入平治之乱，被平清盛击败，1160年在逃往东国途中于尾张国遭家人背叛杀害。

en: Minamoto no Yukiaki was a Murakami Genji clansman known only from the Nawa genealogy, which records his exile to Hoki Province, where he received Nagata in Aseri District and founded the Nagata line that later became the Nawa clan.
zh: 源行明是村上源氏族人，仅见于《名和系图》。系图记载他被流放至伯耆国，受领汗入郡长田之地，开创长田氏一系，即后来的名和氏。

en: Suwabe no Sukenaga was an early Kamakura warrior of the line that later took the name Mitoya, a clan claiming Seiwa Genji descent from Shinano Province. He fought for the Kamakura shogunate in the Jōkyū War of 1221 and was rewarded that same year with the jitō stewardship of Mitoya-gō in Iishi District, Izumo Province, where he then settled. His descendants made Mitoya their base and adopted the place as their family name.
zh: 诹访部助长是镰仓初期的武士，属后来以三刀屋为苗字的一族，该族自称是出身信浓国的清和源氏后裔。1221年承久之乱中，他为镰仓幕府作战，同年受封出云国饭石郡三刀屋乡的地头职，随后下向当地定居。其子孙以三刀屋为根据地，并将这一地名取为家名。

en: Mitoya Sukesada was a warrior of the Mitoya family in Izumo Province, recorded in the Mitoya documents as Suwabe Hikojūrō Sukesada. During Japan's Northern and Southern Courts period, he submitted a report of his arrival and military service in 1351. In May of that year, Ashikaga Tadafuyu issued him a letter of commendation. His name also appears in a document issued by an official of Yamana Tokiuji in June.
zh: 三刀屋扶贞是出云国三刀屋氏的武士，三刀屋文书称他为诹访部彦十郎扶贞。日本南北朝时期，他于1351年呈交到着及军忠状。同年5月，足利直冬向他颁发感状；6月，山名时氏奉行人的文书中也出现了他的名字。

en: Mitoya Sukeshige was a warrior associated with Mitoya in Izumo Province, also known as Suwabe Saburō and by his religious name Shinne. In 1335, Ashikaga Tadayoshi called on him to raise troops. Sukeshige submitted reports of military service in 1336 and 1338, during the wars between Japan's Northern and Southern Courts. In 1338, Kō no Moroyasu ordered that interference with the chief stewardship of Mitoya be stopped and the land placed under Sukeshige's control; the order was reported carried out in 1339.
zh: 三刀屋扶重是与出云国三刀屋有关的武士，也称诹访部三郎，入道后号信惠。1335年，足利直义向他发出征兵催促状。日本南北朝战乱期间，扶重于1336年和1338年呈交军忠状。1338年，高师泰命令停止对三刀屋惣领地头职的侵扰，并将土地交由扶重支配；1339年，有人报告这一命令已得到执行。

en: Suwabe no Yukisuke, remembered in Mitoya clan genealogy as a grandson of Ina no Tamesuke, was first of the Shinano Genji line to take the Suwabe name. His descendants won stewardship of Mitoya-gō in Iishi District, Izumo, and settled there as the Mitoya clan.
zh: 据出云国三刀屋氏的家族传承，诹访部幸扶是信浓源氏之祖伊那为扶之孙，也是这支族人中最先改称诹访部氏者；其后人后来取得饭石郡三刀屋乡的地头职，进入出云定居，并以三刀屋为苗字。

en: Miura Moritoki was a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate, born into the Sahara branch of the Miura clan of Sagami Province and a grandson of Sahara Yoshitsura. His mother Yabe-zenni had first been married to the regent Hōjō Yasutoki, so Moritoki stood close to Yasutoki's grandson Hōjō Tokiyori. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 he sided with Tokiyori against the Miura main family of Miura Yasumura. After its destruction he was made Miura no suke and inherited the head house, founding the Sagami Miura line. In 1263, after Tokiyori's death, he took Buddhist vows as Jōren.
zh: 三浦盛时是镰仓幕府御家人，出身相模国三浦氏的佐原支流，为佐原义连之孙。其母矢部禅尼先嫁执权北条泰时，后改嫁佐原盛连，因此他与泰时之孙北条时赖关系亲近。1247年宝治合战时，他站在北条时赖一边，与三浦泰村的宗家为敌；宗家覆灭后，他被任命为三浦介，继承三浦宗家，开创相模三浦氏一脉。1263年北条时赖死后，他出家为僧，法号净莲。

en: Miura Takamichi was a Nanbokuchō-period warrior, head of the Sagami Miura clan and Muromachi shogunate shugo of Sagami Province, titled Miura-no-suke. He fought beside his father Takatsugu at Aonogahara in 1338 and succeeded him in 1339, afterwards serving Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Yoshiakira. Made Sagami shugo by 1351, he backed Uesugi Noriaki during the Kannō Disturbance, lost the post, and in 1352 joined Nitta Yoshioki's attack on Kamakura, which they briefly occupied before abandoning it the following month. Later pardoned, he recovered his Miura lands in 1362, was reappointed shugo in 1364, yielded the headship to his son Takatsura, and died between 1367 and 1376.
zh: 三浦高通是南北朝时代武将，相模三浦氏当主、室町幕府相模守护，官称三浦介。1338年他随父高继参加美浓青野原之战，1339年继任家督与三浦介，出仕镰仓公方足利义诠。1351年前他受任相模守护，观应之扰乱中依附起兵的上杉宪显，不久被解职，1352年又随新田义兴等一度攻占镰仓，次月弃城离去。后来他获赦，1362年领回三浦郡所领，1364年重任相模守护，晚年把家督让给儿子高连，1367至1376年间去世。

en: Miura Takatsugu (died 1339) was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō periods and head of the Sagami Miura clan, titled Miura-no-suke. The son of Miura Tokitsugu, he probably received the character 高 in his name from Hōjō Takatoki. During the 1335 Nakasendai Rebellion his father joined Hōjō Tokiyuki and was executed, while Takatsugu sided with Emperor Go-Daigo and was confirmed as family head. He later joined Ashikaga Takauji, headed the Muromachi shogunate's Board of Retainers, and fought at Aonogahara in Mino in 1338 against Kitabatake Akiie. He died in 1339.
zh: 三浦高继（1339年卒）是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，相模三浦氏当主，官称三浦介。他是三浦时继之子，名中“高”字一般认为得自镰仓幕府执权北条高时的偏讳。1335年中先代之乱中，其父时继追随北条时行，败后被斩；高继始终站在后醍醐天皇一方，得承家督与三浦介之名。其后他归附足利尊氏，出任室町幕府侍所头人，1338年在美浓青野原之战中与北畠显家交战，1339年去世。

en: Miura Takatsura (died between 1402 and 1407) was a Muromachi-period warrior, head of the Sagami Miura clan and Muromachi shogunate shugo of Sagami Province, with the title Miura-no-suke. The son of Takamichi, he founded the temple Enichizan Tōshōji in Kazusa Province. He served as Sagami shugo from 1377 to 1402. Between 1395 and 1400 he became a Buddhist monk. He handed the headship and the title Miura-no-suke to Takamitsu sometime from 1402 to 1407 and died soon afterwards.
zh: 三浦高连（1402—1407年间卒）是室町时代武将，相模三浦氏当主、室町幕府相模守护，官称三浦介。他是高通之子，曾在上总国创建慧日山东照寺。1377—1402年他担任相模守护，1395至1400年间出家。1402—1407年间，他把家督与三浦介让给高明，不久去世。

en: Miura Tamemichi was a late-Heian warrior of the Kanmu Taira lineage, son of Taira no Tadamichi and regarded as the founder of the Miura clan. For his service under Minamoto no Yoriyoshi in the Earlier Nine Years' War, he was in 1063 granted Miura in Sagami province, took the name Miura, and built his seat at Kinugasa on the Miura Peninsula. He died on the fourteenth day of the third month of 1083, by the old Japanese calendar, with the clerical name Engaku.
zh: 三浦为通（？—1083年）是平安时代后期的武将，出身桓武平氏良文流，为平忠通之子，被尊为三浦氏之祖。1063年，他因在前九年之役中追随源赖义立有军功，受封相模国三浦乡，遂以三浦为苗字，并在三浦半岛中部的衣笠修筑居城衣笠城。他于日本旧历1083年三月十四日去世，法名圆觉。

en: Miura Tametsugu was a late-Heian warrior of Sagami province and a head of the Miura house, son of Miura Tamemichi; later Miura tradition regarded him as the clan's real founder. He followed Minamoto no Yoshiie in the Later Three Years' War of 1083 to 1087, winning distinction and laying the basis of the clan's rise. A war chronicle recounts that when the young Kamakura Kagemasa was shot in the eye, Tametsugu tried to pull out the arrow while treading on his face. Kagemasa angrily resisted, so Tametsugu knelt to remove it instead. His son Yoshitsugu succeeded him.
zh: 三浦为继是平安时代后期相模国的武将、三浦氏当主，三浦为通之子；三浦一族后来更把他视为真正的家祖。1083至1087年，他追随源义家参加后三年之役，立下军功，奠定三浦氏发展的根基。军记物记载，年轻的镰仓景正被箭射中右眼后，为继踩住他的脸试图拔箭；景正愤然反抗，为继于是跪下拔出了箭。其子义继后来统领三浦领地。

en: Miura Tokiaki was a warrior of the late Kamakura period who succeeded his father Miura Yorimori as head of the Sagami Miura clan and held the court title Miura no suke. He later yielded the headship and title to his son Miura Tokitsugu.
zh: 三浦时明是镰仓时代后期的武将，继其父三浦赖盛之后成为相模三浦氏当主，官位为三浦介。后来他将家督与三浦介之位让给儿子三浦时继，随后去世。

en: Miura Tokitsugu was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era and head of the Sagami Miura clan with the title Miura no suke, succeeding his father Miura Tokiaki. In 1331 he fought for the shogunate against Emperor Go-Daigo at the siege of Kasagi. In 1335 he joined Hōjō Tokiyuki's Nakasendai Rebellion against the Kenmu government; Hōjō forces seized Kamakura, but after Ashikaga Takauji retook the city in the eighth month Tokitsugu fled by sea to Atsuta in Owari Province. Captured and sent to Kyoto, he was beheaded and his head exposed.
zh: 三浦时继是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，继其父三浦时明之后成为相模三浦氏当主，官称三浦介。1331年元弘之乱时，他作为幕府军一员攻打据守笠置寺的后醍醐天皇，参加了笠置山之战。1335年北条时行发动中先代之乱，时继加入时行一方，起兵反对建武政权；北条军攻占镰仓。八月足利尊氏夺回镰仓后，时继乘船逃到尾张国热田，被擒获后押送京都处斩并枭首示众。

en: Miura Yasumura (1184?–1247) was head of the Miura clan and the second son of Yoshimura. In the Jōkyū Disturbance of 1221 he distinguished himself fighting with the shogunate army; his coming-of-age sponsor Hōjō Yasutoki gave him the character 'yasu', and he married Yasutoki's daughter. Made a councillor in 1238, he grew close to shōgun Kujō Yoritsune and aroused the suspicion of Regent Hōjō Tokiyori. In 1247, driven into revolt by Adachi Kagemori's plot, he was defeated in the Hōji Conflict and killed himself with his clansmen at the Hokkedō hall.
zh: 三浦泰村（1184？—1247）是三浦义村的次子、三浦氏当主。1221年承久之乱中，他随幕府军参战，立下战功；元服时由乌帽子亲北条泰时授予“泰”字，后又娶泰时之女。1238年他出任评定众，并与将军九条赖经过从甚密，引起执权北条时赖的猜忌。1247年，在安达景盛的谋划逼迫下，他于镰仓举兵，终在宝治合战中兵败，与一族郎党在法华堂自尽。

en: Miura Yorimori was a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate and the sixth son of Miura Moritoki, whom he succeeded as head of the Miura clan. He is first recorded in 1257, named with his cousin Miura Tsunemitsu among the guards at the Hōjō-e festival of Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine. In 1261 he served as guard to Shōgun Prince Munetaka at the festival, and in 1264 escorted the prince to his new residence in Komachi. In the eleventh month of 1290 he captured and beheaded a surviving son of Hōjō Tokisuke, who had plotted a coup and sought Yorimori's backing.
zh: 三浦赖盛是镰仓幕府御家人，三浦盛时的第六子，继承其父统领三浦氏宗家。1257年，他与堂兄弟三浦经光一同出现在鹤冈八幡宫放生会的供奉人名单中，此为史料首见。1261年放生会时，他担任将军宗尊亲王的随兵；1264年又护卫宗尊亲王迁入小町的新邸。1290年十一月，他捕获并斩首了北条时辅的遗子，此人曾策划政变并试图寻求赖盛的支持。

en: Miura Yoshiaki (1092–1180) was lord of Kinugasa Castle in the Miura district of Sagami Province and head of the Miura clan. As Miura-no-suke he followed Minamoto no Yoshitomo in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 and the Heiji Disturbance of 1160, and later kept contact with the exiled Minamoto no Yoritomo. When Yoritomo rose in 1180, he sent his son Yoshizumi with the clan host while staying, aged 89, to defend Kinugasa Castle against Hatakeyama Shigetada. After letting his kinsmen escape to Awa, he was killed when the castle fell.
zh: 三浦义明（1092—1180）是相模国三浦郡衣笠城城主、三浦氏当主。他自称三浦介，曾随源义朝参加1156年保元之乱与1160年平治之乱，败退回乡后仍与流放中的源赖朝保持往来。1180年赖朝举兵时，他派儿子义澄率族人前往会合，自己以八十九岁高龄留守衣笠城，抵御畠山重忠的进攻。他让族人逃往安房国，自己则在城破时战死。

en: Miura Yoshikata was an early Kamakura-period warrior of the Miura clan's Tsukui line, recorded in genealogies as the son of Yoshimitsu. He is said to have held Akiba in the Kamakura district of Sagami Province, from which the Akiba family took its name.
zh: 三浦义方是镰仓初期三浦氏津久井流的武将，系谱记载为义光之子。相传他以相模国镰仓郡秋庭乡为据点，后来的秋庭氏即以此地为苗字。

en: Miura Yoshimitsu was a warrior of the Tsukui branch of the Miura clan. Miura genealogies record him as the son of Tsukui Yoshiyuki and father of Yoshikata; one tradition also names him as ancestor of the Akiba family of Bitchū Province.
zh: 三浦义光是三浦氏支族津久井氏的武将。三浦氏系谱记载他是津久井义行之子、义方之父；另有一说以他为备中国秋庭氏之祖。

en: Miura Yoshimura (1168–1239) was head of the Miura clan and one of the most powerful gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. After Minamoto no Yoritomo's death in 1199 he helped bring down Kajiwara Kagetoki, took part in the destruction of Hatakeyama Shigetada in 1205 and sided with the Hōjō in the Wada conflict of 1213, then fought for the shogunate in the Jōkyū Disturbance of 1221. In 1225 he joined the new Council of State under Hōjō Yasutoki and in 1232 signed the Goseibai Shikimoku. He died suddenly late in 1239, the shogunate's ranking councillor after the Hōjō.
zh: 三浦义村（1168—1239）是三浦氏当主、镰仓幕府最有权势的御家人之一。1199年源赖朝死后，他参与策划扳倒梶原景时，1205年参与攻灭畠山重忠，1213年在和田合战中倒向北条一方，1221年承久之乱时又为幕府而战。1225年他出任北条泰时麾下的评定众，1232年在《御成败式目》上署名，1239年末骤然病亡，时为幕府中地位仅次于北条氏的宿老。

en: Miura Yoshitaka was an early Kamakura-period warrior of the Miura clan's Tsukui line, the son of Yoshikata. One Miura genealogy identifies him with the young Akiba warrior who fought for the shogunate at the Battle of the Uji River in 1221, during the Jōkyū Disturbance.
zh: 三浦义高是镰仓初期三浦氏津久井流的武将，义方之子。有三浦氏系谱将他比定为承久之乱中的年轻武者秋庭三郎，此人于1221年宇治川之战为幕府军奋勇作战。

en: Miura Yoshitsugu (1067?–1159) was a late Heian-period warrior who ruled the Miura district in Sagami Province and styled himself Miura-no-suke. Succeeding his father Tametsugu, his sons founded the Tsukui, Ashina and Okazaki branch houses.
zh: 三浦义继（1067？—1159）是平安时代后期统治相模国三浦郡的武将，自称三浦介，继父亲三浦为续统领一族。他的儿子义行、为清、义实分别开创津久井氏、芦名氏与冈崎氏。

en: Miura Yoshiyuki, also called Tsukui Yoshiyuki, was the second son of Miura Yoshitsugu and founder of the Tsukui branch of the Miura clan in Sagami Province.
zh: 三浦义行又称津久井义行，是三浦义继的次子，也是相模国三浦氏支族津久井氏之祖。

en: Miura Yoshizumi (1127–1200) was a son of Miura Yoshiaki and head of the Miura clan, a leading gokenin of the early Kamakura shogunate. In 1180 he led the Miura host to join Minamoto no Yoritomo but arrived too late for Ishibashiyama; after repulsing Hatakeyama Shigetada at Yuigahama he escaped to Awa while his father died at Kinugasa Castle. He fought at Ichinotani, Dannoura and in the Ōshū campaign, became one of Yoritomo's senior councillors, and in 1199 joined the thirteen-man council assisting shōgun Yoriie. He died in 1200, days after Kajiwara Kagetoki's overthrow.
zh: 三浦义澄（1127—1200）是三浦义明之子、三浦氏当主，镰仓幕府初期的有力御家人。1180年他率三浦一族投奔源赖朝，却未能赶上石桥山之战；在由比浜击退畠山重忠后逃往安房国，父亲义明则战死在衣笠城。此后他随军参加一之谷之战、坛之浦之战和奥州合战，成为赖朝的宿老之一，1199年又位列辅佐将军源赖家的十三人合议制。1200年梶原景时败死后数日，他随之去世。

en: Miyoshi Hideaki was the eighth head of the Miyoshi clan, the Bingo Province kokujin lords of Miyoshi-gō. He was the son of the seventh head, Iehide, and father of Teruhide, who followed him as the ninth head.
zh: 三吉秀明是备后国三吉乡国人领主三吉氏的第八代当主，第七代当主家秀之子，其子照秀继他之后成为第九代当主。

en: Miyoshi Hidetaka was the fourth head of the Miyoshi clan, which ruled as kokujin lords from Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province. The son of Nobukane, he led the clan after his father and was succeeded by his own son Mitsutaka.
zh: 三吉秀高是在备后国三吉乡以国人领主身份立足的三吉氏第四代当主，信兼之子，继父亲之后统领家族，后由其子光高接任。

en: Miyoshi Hirohide was a head of the Bingo Miyoshi, a warrior house of local lords based at Hieo-yama Castle in Miyoshi, Bingo Province. He served the Yamana family, shugo governors of Bingo, and received one character of his name from Yamana Tokihiro.
zh: 三吉熈秀是备后三吉氏的当主之一。三吉氏是以备后国三吉乡比叡尾山城为据点的国人领主豪族。他侍奉担任备后守护的山名氏，名字中的“熈”字得自山名时熙的偏讳。

en: Miyoshi Iehide was the seventh head of the Miyoshi clan, kokujin lords based at Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province. He succeeded his father Takaie, and the headship later passed to his son Hideaki, the eighth head of the clan.
zh: 三吉家秀是盘踞备后国三吉乡的国人领主三吉氏第七代当主，继父亲高家之后接任，后来当主之位由其子、第八代当主秀明继承。

en: Miyoshi Kaneie was the second head of the Miyoshi clan, the kokujin lords of Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province. He was a son of Kanemune, the clan's first head, whose line claimed descent from the Fujiwara through Fujiwara no Kanenori.
zh: 三吉兼家是备后国三次郡三吉乡国人领主三吉氏的第二代当主，初代当主三吉兼宗之子。三吉氏自称经由藤原兼范一脉为藤原镰足的后裔。

en: Miyoshi no Kanemune, son of Fujiwara no Kanenori and father of Kaneie, took the style Miyoshi no Taifu and was the first head of the Miyoshi clan in Bingo Province.
zh: 三吉兼宗是藤原兼范之子、兼家之父，称三吉大夫，为备后国三吉氏的初代当主。

en: Miyoshi Mitsutaka was the fifth head of the Bingo Miyoshi, the kokujin lords of Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province. He succeeded his father Hidetaka as head of the clan and in time passed the headship to his son Takaie.
zh: 三吉光高是备后国三吉乡国人领主备后三吉氏的第五代当主，继父亲秀高之后统领家族，后来当主之位由其子高家接任。

en: Miyoshi Nobukane was the third head of the Miyoshi clan, kokujin lords of Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province. He succeeded his father Kaneie and was followed by his son Hidetaka. The clan claimed Fujiwara descent through Kanenori, who settled in Bingo in the twelfth century.
zh: 三吉信兼是备后国三吉乡国人领主三吉氏的第三代当主，父亲是兼家，其子秀高继任当主。三吉氏自称是12世纪迁居备后的藤原兼范之后，出自藤原镰足一脉。

en: Miyoshi Takaie was the sixth head of the Miyoshi clan of Bingo Province, descended from the Fujiwara settler Fujiwara no Kanenori. As kokujin lords the family held Miyoshi-gō; Takaie followed his father Mitsutaka and was succeeded by his son Iehide.
zh: 三吉高家是备后国三吉氏的第六代当主，其族出自迁居当地的藤原兼范，世代为领有三吉乡的国人领主。高家继父亲光高之后任当主，后由其子家秀继任。

en: Miyoshi Teruhide was the ninth head of the Miyoshi clan, kokujin lords of Miyoshi-gō in Bingo Province, and the son of Hideaki. His son Hirohide succeeded him; Hirohide received a character for his name from Yamana Tokihiro, the shugo of Bingo.
zh: 三吉照秀是备后国三吉乡国人领主三吉氏的第九代当主，秀明之子。其子熙秀继他之后担任当主，名字中的一字得自时任备后守护的山名时熙。

en: Miyoshi Toyohide succeeded his father Hirohide as head of the Bingo Miyoshi, the local lord house of Miyoshi in Bingo Province. He served the Yamana, shugo governors of Bingo, and received one character of his name from Yamana Mochitoyo, better known as Yamana Sōzen.
zh: 三吉豊秀继其父三吉熈秀之后担任备后三吉氏当主，该家族是备后国三吉乡的国人领主豪族。他侍奉担任备后守护的山名氏，名字中的“豊”字得自山名持丰（即山名宗全）的偏讳。

en: The Iijima-origin genealogy of the Izumo Mizawa clan names Mizawa Hirotada as an early head of the family, a son of Minamoto no Tametada and the father of Mizawa Tamenaga.
zh: 出云三泽氏的饭嶋氏起源说系图记载，三泽广忠是该家的早期当主，源为忠之子、三泽为长之父。

en: Mizawa Tamenaga, also called Tamenaka, founded the Izumo branch of the Mizawa clan. After his kinsman Iijima Tamemitsu was granted the Mizawa manor in Nita district as jitō for his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221, Tamenaga came there in 1302 by way of Kano in Inaba. He grew powerful mining iron sand, running tatara furnaces and opening new fields, and in 1305 built Mizawa Castle on Mount Kamokura, a height commanding Nita and the Shimane peninsula; he then moved the family from Shinano and took the name Mizawa.
zh: 三泽为长（一作为仲）是三泽氏出云宗家的开创者。其亲族饭嶋为光在1221年承久之乱中立功，以新补地头身份获封出云国仁多郡三泽庄；1302年，为长经因幡国鹿野来到当地，靠开采优质砂铁、经营踏鞴制铁和开垦山野壮大势力，1305年在可俯瞰仁多郡乃至岛根半岛的要冲鸭仓山修筑三泽城，同时将家族自信浓迁居于此，此后改称三泽姓，出云三泽氏由此而始。

en: Tametada Mizawa was the head of the Mizawa warrior house of Nita district in Izumo province, based at Mizawa Castle, which the clan had built in 1305. The Mizawa served the Yamana family, shugo of Izumo. In 1391 Tametada followed Yamana Mitsuyuki when the shugo joined the Meitoku War against the Muromachi shogunate, and fell in the campaign.
zh: 三泽为忠是出云国仁多郡三泽氏武士家族的当主，据点为家族于1305年修筑的三泽城。三泽氏臣事出云守护山名氏。1391年，守护山名满幸加入反抗室町幕府的明德之乱，为忠随军出征，战死沙场。

en: The Mizawa genealogy names Tametsune as an early head of the clan at Mizawa manor in Nita district, Izumo, the son of Mizawa Tamenaga and father of Mizawa Tametada, who held the title Owari no Kami.
zh: 三泽氏家谱记载，为常是出云国仁多郡三泽庄的早期当主，三泽为长之子、三泽为忠之父，其子为忠曾任尾张守。

en: Shiba Kaneyori, also called Mogami Kaneyori, was the second son of the Oshu governor Shiba Iekane. In 1336, before coming of age, he fought in Namegata district against the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie. In 1356, calling himself inspector of Dewa, he entered Yamagata in Mogami district to subdue Southern Court clans such as the Sagae Oe, and built Yamagata Castle in 1357. Around 1373 the Muromachi shogunate granted him the yakata title, after which he took the name Mogami from his domain. In 1375 he was succeeded by his son Naoie; he died in 1379, founder of the Mogami clan.
zh: 斯波兼赖（亦称最上兼赖）是奥州探题斯波家兼的次子。1336年元服以前，他在行方郡与南朝将领北畠显家交战。1356年，他自称出羽按察使，进入最上郡山形，压制寒河江大江氏等南朝势力，并于1357年修筑山形城。约1373年获室町幕府准许使用“屋形”号，随后以领地最上郡改姓最上氏。1375年家督由嫡子直家继任，他于1379年去世，被尊为最上氏之祖。

en: Momonoi Akinobu was a son of Momonoi Tadanobu, the Nanboku-cho period shugo of Etchu Province, and a member of the Ashikaga-related Momonoi clan.
zh: 桃井诠信是南北朝时代越中守护桃井直信之子，出自与足利氏同族的桃井氏。

en: Momonoi Mitsuuji was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Momonoi clan of Kōzuke Province. Clan genealogies record him as a son of Momonoi Taneuji and the father of Momonoi Naoyoshi, who fell fighting for Nitta Yoshisada at Kamakura in 1333.
zh: 桃井满氏是镰仓时代上野国桃井氏的武将。族谱记载他为桃井胤氏之子、桃井尚义之父；其子尚义于1333年随新田义贞攻打镰仓时战死。

en: Momonoi Moriyoshi was a Northern Court commander in the Nanboku-chō wars. In 1336, at Takauji's war council in Murotsu, Harima, he was posted to Bitchū and Bingo together with the Kobayakawa to check Nitta Yoshisada's westward advance, and he held office as shugo of Tajima from 1336 to 1338. In May 1338, during the Northern army's assault on the Southern Court stronghold of Shinmeiji Castle in Tajima, he ordered Date Yoshitsuna to cover his troops; the Southern Court defenders were driven from the temple fortress. He may also have served as shugo of Noto around 1349 to 1351.
zh: 桃井盛义是日本南北朝时代的北朝方武将。1336年，在播磨室津召开的军议上，足利尊氏将他与小早川氏部署到备中、备后，以阻击新田义贞西进；1336至1338年间他担任但马守护。1338年5月，北朝军总攻南朝在但马的据点进美寺城时，盛义命令伊达义纲为自己的部队警护，南朝守军最终被逐出这座寺院城塞。约1349至1351年间，他可能还担任过能登守护。

en: Momonoi Naoyoshi (died 1333), known as Jirō, was a gokenin of the late Kamakura period and head of the Momonoi, a branch clan of the Ashikaga of Seiwa Genji stock. In 1333 he joined Nitta Yoshisada's rising against the Kamakura shogunate and fell in the fighting at the assault on Kamakura.
zh: 桃井尚义（？—1333），通称次郎，是镰仓时代末期的御家人，清和源氏足利氏支族桃井氏的当主。1333年，他追随新田义贞举兵，参与讨伐镰仓幕府的战事。同年，他随军进攻镰仓，在镰仓的战斗中战死。

en: Momonoi Sadayori was a warrior of the Momonoi clan of Kōzuke Province. Genealogies record him as the father of Momonoi Tadatsune and Tadanobu, brothers who won fame as Northern Court generals and provincial shugo during the Nanboku-chō wars.
zh: 桃井贞赖是上野国桃井氏的武将。谱系记载他是桃井直常、直信兄弟之父；兄弟二人在南北朝动乱中作为北朝方的名将，历任诸国守护。

en: Momonoi Tadakazu was a military commander of the early Nanboku-chō period and a member of the Ashikaga clan, the son of Momonoi Tadatsune, shugo of Etchu Province. He held the court rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and served as Nakatsukasa-no-taifu and Uma-no-suke. In 1362 he took up arms in Etchu for the Southern Court, fortifying Mount Isurugi against the Muromachi bakufu's forces in Noto. In 1370 his father sent him to Nagasawa, where he was defeated and killed by the army of Shiba Yoshimasa, shugo of Etchu, at the Battle of Nagasawa.
zh: 桃井直和是南北朝时代初期的武将，出自足利氏一门，为越中守护桃井直常之子，叙从五位下，曾任中务大辅、右马助。1362年（正平十七年），他在越中举兵归附南朝，布阵石动山，与能登的幕府军交战。1370年（应安三年），父亲直常将他派往越中长泽，他在长泽之战中被幕府任命的越中守护斯波义将击败，战死。

en: Momonoi Tadanobu was a Nanboku-chō general and a son of Momonoi Sadayori, younger brother of the better-known Tadatsune. He first appears in 1338 fighting Southern Court forces at Kanegasaki Castle and Tsuruga in Echizen, and thereafter campaigned at his brother's side. In the Kannō Disturbance he followed Ashikaga Tadayoshi, fighting Takauji's partisans in Noto in 1350, and after Tadayoshi's death served the Southern Court under Ashikaga Tadafuyu. He submitted to the Muromachi bakufu in 1367 and briefly held office as shugo of Etchū that year. By 1372 he was living in Kyoto; his death date is unknown.
zh: 桃井直信是日本南北朝时代武将，桃井贞赖之子，声名更著的直常之弟。1338年，他在越前国金崎城与敦贺和南朝军作战，此事首见于记载，此后便随兄长转战各地。观应之乱中他追随足利直义，1350年在能登国与足利尊氏一派交战；直义死后归降南朝，效力于足利直冬麾下。1367年他归顺室町幕府，同年短期出任越中守护。到1372年，他已在京都居住，卒年不详。

en: Momonoi Tadatsune was a Northern Court general of the Nanboku-chō wars and a son of Momonoi Sadayori of Shimotsuke. In 1338 he fought at Aonogahara and, with his brother Tadanobu, blocked Kitabatake Akiie's army from entering Kyoto at Hannyazaka in Nara. He was made shugo of Wakasa (1338), Iga (c. 1340) and Etchū (1344), building several castles. In the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, and in 1355 he backed Ashikaga Tadafuyu and briefly occupied Kyoto. Submitting in 1367, he rebelled and was routed at Nagasawa in 1370, where his son Tadakazu fell, and disappeared after defeat in 1371.
zh: 桃井直常是日本南北朝时代的北朝方武将，下野桃井氏桃井贞赖之子。1338年他参加青野原之战，又与弟弟直信在奈良般若坂合力阻击北畠显家的军队，阻止其进入京都。他于同年出任若狭守护，约1340年改任伊贺守护，1344年转任越中守护，并在越中修筑多处城砦作为统治据点。观应之乱中他追随足利直义对抗足利尊氏，1355年拥立足利直冬，一度占领京都。1367年归顺后他再度举兵，1370年在长泽之战大败，儿子直和战死，1371年再败后下落不明。

en: Momonoi Taneuji was a Kamakura-period gokenin of the Momonoi clan of Kōzuke Province. The clan genealogy names him as the founder of the Momonoi Saburō branch, whose descendants included Momonoi Naoyoshi, killed in the assault on Kamakura in 1333.
zh: 桃井胤氏是镰仓时代上野国桃井氏的御家人。桃井氏谱系以他为三郎系之祖，其后人中有1333年攻打镰仓时战死的桃井尚义。

en: Momonoi Yorinao, called Kojirō, was a Kamakura-period gokenin of the Momonoi clan in Kōzuke Province. The clan genealogy names him as the founder of the Momonoi Kojirō branch, from which came the Nanboku-chō generals Momonoi Tadatsune and Tadanobu.
zh: 桃井赖直，通称小二郎，是镰仓时代上野国桃井氏的御家人。桃井氏谱系以他为小二郎系之祖，南北朝名将桃井直常、直信兄弟即出自这一支。

en: Momonoi Yoriuji was a Kamakura-period gokenin of Kōzuke Province, recorded as a son of Momonoi Yoshitane. Clan genealogies trace the Momonoi's two later branches, the Saburō line and the Kojirō line, to his sons Taneuji and Yorinao.
zh: 桃井赖氏是镰仓时代上野国的御家人，谱载为桃井义胤之子。桃井氏后来的三郎、小二郎两支，谱系上分别出于其子胤氏与赖直。

en: Momonoi Yoshisuke (died 1221), also called Ashikaga Yoshisuke, was a warrior commander of the early Kamakura period and the second son of Ashikaga Yoshikane. He served the Kamakura shogunate, holding the offices of Sahyōe-no-jō and Hyōbu-no-shō. He built Momonoi Castle in Momonoi manor, Gunma district, Kōzuke Province, and took the name Momonoi, becoming the ancestor of the clan. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he fought for the shogunate against the court and was killed on 3 July at the battle of the Uji River, leaving a posthumous son, Yoshitane.
zh: 桃井义助（？—1221），亦称足利义助，通称足利次郎，是镰仓时代前期的武将，足利义兼的次子。他出仕镰仓幕府，历任左兵卫尉、兵部少辅。他在上野国群马郡桃井乡修筑桃井城，以桃井为号，被视为桃井氏之祖。1221年承久之乱爆发，他作为幕府方将领出阵，在宇治川会战中于7月3日战死，身后留下遗腹子义胤。

en: Momonoi Yoshitane (fl. thirteenth century), also recorded as Ashikaga Yoshitane, was a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate and the posthumous son of Momonoi Yoshisuke. After his father fell in the Jōkyū War in 1221, he was enfeoffed with the family estate at Momonoi in Gunma district, Kōzuke Province, settled there and adopted Momonoi as his surname. First known as Ashikaga Shirō, he later styled himself Momonoi Ōmi-no-kami, holding junior fifth rank, lower grade, and the offices of Sahyōe-no-jō, Umanosuke and Hyōbu-no-taifu. Genealogies name his sons as Yoriuji and Yorinao.
zh: 桃井义胤（生卒年不详），一作足利义胤，是镰仓幕府御家人，桃井义助的遗腹子。1221年父亲在承久之乱战死后，他受领上野国群马郡桃井乡的所职，入部定居，以桃井为苗字。他初称足利四郎，后称桃井近江守，叙从五位下，历任左兵卫尉、右马介、兵部大辅。据谱系记载，其子有赖氏和赖直。

en: Emperor Monmu (683–707), personal name Karu, was the 42nd emperor of Japan and ruled from 697 to 707. The son of Crown Prince Kusakabe and the future Empress Genmei, and a grandson of Emperor Tenmu, he was enthroned at fourteen when Empress Jitō abdicated in his favor. In 701 he proclaimed the Taihō era name, and the Taihō Code, Japan's first comprehensive Ritsuryō legal system, was enacted in 701 and 702. He died in 707 at twenty-five, leaving the throne to his mother because his son Prince Obito was still young; Obito later ruled as Emperor Shōmu.
zh: 文武天皇（683—707），名珂瑠，是日本第42代天皇，697年至707年在位。他是草壁皇子与后来的元明天皇之子、天武天皇之孙，697年因持统天皇禅让而十四岁即位。701年他下诏启用大宝年号，701至702年施行日本第一部完备的律令法典《大宝律令》。707年他以二十五岁之龄去世，因子首亲王年幼，皇位由母亲元明继承；首亲王后来即位为圣武天皇。

en: Emperor Montoku (827–858) was the 55th emperor of Japan, reigning from 850 to 858. The eldest son of Emperor Ninmyō, he was made crown prince during the Jōwa Incident of 842 and succeeded his father in 850. Later that year Fujiwara no Yoshifusa secured the appointment of his own infant grandson, Prince Korehito, as crown prince ahead of Montoku's eldest son, marking the rising power of the Fujiwara regents. In poor health throughout his reign, Montoku died suddenly in 858 at the age of thirty-two. His reign saw work begin on the court chronicle Shoku Nihon Kōki.
zh: 文德天皇（827—858）是日本第55代天皇，850年至858年在位。他是仁明天皇长子，842年承和之变中被立为皇太子，850年继位。同年晚些时候，藤原良房将自己尚在襁褓的外孙惟仁亲王推上皇太子之位，排在文德长子之前，标志着藤原摄关势力的崛起。文德天皇在位期间一直体弱，858年突然病逝，时年32岁。其朝开始编纂国史《续日本后纪》。

en: Mōri Chikahira (died 1375) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and steward of Yoshida-no-shō in Aki Province. He first fought for the Southern Court with his father Sadachika in Echigo, then submitted to the Northern Court through his grandfather Tokichika and moved to Aki. Since his son Motoharu had already inherited the clan headship, Chikahira built Kusakazu Castle and founded a branch house, the Bann. In the Kannō Disturbance of 1350 he joined the anti-bakufu side, allied with the Ōuchi of Suō, attacked Motoharu's lands while his son fought in Kyushu, and repulsed Aki shugo Takeda Ujinobu's siege.
zh: 毛利亲衡（？—1375年）是南北朝时代武将，任安艺国吉田庄地头。他起初随父亲贞亲在越后为南朝效力，后来经祖父时亲调停归顺北朝，举族迁往安艺。由于嫡子元春已经继承毛利氏总领之位，亲衡修筑日下津城另立一家，其后代以坂为姓。1350年观应之乱爆发，他站在反幕府一方，与周防大内氏结盟，趁元春出征九州时袭击其领地，并击退了安艺守护武田氏信对日下津城的围攻。

en: Mōri Motoharu (1323–?) was a lord of Aki Province from the Nanboku-chō wars into the Muromachi period and steward of Yoshida-no-shō. He served Ashikaga Takauji from his teens, first named Morochika for a character from Kō no Moroyasu, then renamed Motoharu when the Kō fell in 1351. In 1341, aged nineteen, he succeeded his great-grandfather Tokichika as clan head, known as Lord Kōriyama. He fought for the Northern Court in Kyushu under Imagawa Ryōshun while his father Chikahira raided Aki with Southern Court allies. After his heir Hirofusa fell in 1385, he secured the succession of his grandson Mitsufusa.
zh: 毛利元春（1323年—？）是南北朝至室町时代安艺国的国人，任吉田庄地头。他从少年时起侍奉足利尊氏，因获足利家执事高师直之弟高师泰赐予一字而初名师亲，1351年高师泰失势后改名元春。1341年，19岁的他继承曾祖父时亲的家督之位，人称郡山殿。他追随九州探题今川了俊下九州为北朝作战，而父亲亲衡却勾结南朝势力袭击安艺。1385年嫡子广房战死后，他立孙儿光房为继承人并加以辅佐。

en: Mōri Sadachika (died 1351) was a warrior of the Mōri clan of Ōe descent, active from the late Kamakura period into the Nanboku-chō wars. The son of Mōri Tokichika, he is thought to have come of age while Hōjō Sadatoki held the regency, possibly receiving the character sada from his name. In 1334, after his father retired to Yoshida in Aki Province, Sadachika and his heir Chikahira rose in Echigo against Ashikaga Takauji, backing a Daikakuji-line prince called Asonomiya. The revolt failed; Sadachika was placed in Nagai custody, then took the tonsure as a follower of Emperor Go-Daigo, calling himself Rōjō.
zh: 毛利贞亲（？—1351年）是大江姓毛利氏的武将，活跃于镰仓时代末期至南北朝战乱。他是毛利时亲之子，据信在北条贞时担任执权期间元服，名字中的“贞”字可能得自贞时。1334年，父亲前往安艺国吉田隐居，贞亲与嫡子亲衡随即在越后举兵，拥戴大觉寺统的阿曾宫，反叛足利尊氏。举兵失败后，贞亲被交给长井高冬看管，后来追随后醍醐天皇出家，法号朗乘。

en: Mōri Suemitsu (1202 – 8 July 1247), fourth son of Ōe no Hiromoto, took the name Mōri from his Sagami estate, founding the Mōri clan. A Kamakura gokenin, he served Shōgun Minamoto no Sanetomo and in the Jōkyū War of 1221 fought under Hōjō Yasutoki at the Kiso, Uji and Yodo rivers, winning jitō posts at Yoshida manor in Aki and Sahashi in Echigo; in 1233 he joined the Kantō council. In the 1247 Hōji War he sided with his wife's Miura kin, was beaten by Hōjō Tokiyori, and killed himself at Kamakura's Hokkedō with his sons; only Tsunemitsu's line survived.
zh: 毛利季光（1202—1247年7月8日）是大江广元第四子，以相模国的领地取“毛利”为姓，被视为毛利氏之祖。他身为镰仓幕府御家人，侍奉将军源实朝；1221年承久之乱中随北条泰时作战，在木曾川、宇治川、淀川的突破战中立功，获封安艺国吉田庄和越后国佐桥庄的地头职，1233年又被任命为关东评定众。1247年宝治合战时，他因妻子出身三浦一族而加入三浦一方，被北条时赖击败，与诸子在镰仓法华堂自尽，唯有儿子经光一支存续。

en: Mōri Tokichika (c. 1250 – 26 August 1341) was a Kamakura-period gokenin and the fourth son of Mōri Tsunemitsu, from whom he inherited in 1270 the jitō stewardship of Yoshida manor in Aki, founding the Aki Mōri line. He sat on the Rokuhara council in Kyoto. After the shogunate's fall in 1333, he saved his house in the Nanboku-chō wars: his son Sadachika and grandson Chikahira joined the Southern Court, but in 1336 Tokichika went to Aki and arranged their submission to Ashikaga Takauji. In 1337 he passed Yoshida manor to his great-grandson Motoharu, ancestor of the later Mōri lords.
zh: 毛利时亲（约1250—1341年8月26日）是镰仓时代的御家人，毛利经光第四子。1270年，他从父亲手中继承安艺国吉田庄的地头职，开创安艺毛利氏一脉，并曾在京都出任六波罗评定众。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他在南北朝战乱中保全家族：儿子毛利贞亲和孙子毛利亲衡投奔南朝，时亲却在1336年亲赴安艺，斡旋二人归降足利尊氏。1337年，他把吉田庄让给曾孙毛利元春，日后的毛利大名即出自元春一脉。

en: Mōri Tsunemitsu was a Kamakura gokenin and the fourth son of Mōri Suemitsu, named with a character granted by Shōgun Fujiwara no Yoritsune or Regent Hōjō Tsunetoki; he later took monk's vows as Jakubutsu. During the Hōji War of 1247 he was in Echigo and escaped the ruin that killed his father and brothers: the clan's Sagami estate was lost, but through the Nagai family's intercession he kept the jitō posts of Sahashi in Echigo and Yoshida in Aki. He later passed Yoshida to his fourth son Tokichika, ancestor of the warlord Mōri Motonari. His birth and death dates are unrecorded.
zh: 毛利经光是镰仓时代的御家人、毛利季光第四子，名字得自将军藤原赖经或执权北条经时所赐的一字，后来出家，法号寂佛。1247年宝治合战时，他身在越后，未直接参战，躲过了使父亲与诸兄丧命的大祸：毛利氏虽失去相模国的毛利庄，但借同族长井氏从中斡旋，他得以保留越后国佐桥庄与安艺国吉田庄的地头职。后来他把吉田庄交给四子时亲继承，战国大名毛利元就即出自时亲一脉。其生卒年史料无载。

en: Prince Morisada (1179–1223), a son of Emperor Takakura, was carried west by the fleeing Taira in 1183 with the young Emperor Antoku and returned to Kyoto after their fall in 1185. He married a daughter of Jimyōin Motoie and took Buddhist vows in 1212 as the monk-prince Gyōjo. After the Jōkyū War of 1221, the Kamakura shogunate exiled Go-Toba and put Morisada's son Toyohito on the throne as Go-Horikawa. Morisada was exceptionally made retired emperor, ruled in cloister until his death, and was posthumously called Go-Takakura-in.
zh: 守贞亲王（1179—1223）是高仓天皇之子，1183年平家逃离京都时，他随年幼的安德天皇一同被带往西国，1185年平家灭亡后被送还京都。他娶持明院基家之女为妃，1212年出家，法号行助，称行助入道亲王。1221年承久之乱后，镰仓幕府流放后鸟羽上皇，迎立守贞之子茂仁王为后堀河天皇。守贞被破例尊为太上天皇，以上皇身份实行院政直至去世，死后追号后高仓院。

en: Prince Moriyoshi (1308–1335), also read Morinaga and known as the Ōtōnomiya, was a son of Emperor Go-Daigo. Sent into Buddhist orders as a child, he became head of the Tendai sect, then returned to secular life and led the imperial armies that overthrew the Kamakura shogunate in the Genkō War of 1333. Under the Kenmu Restoration he was appointed Sei-i Taishōgun. His hostility to Ashikaga Takauji cost him the office and his freedom: he was confined at Kamakura and there, on 12 August 1335 during the Nakasendai Rebellion, was killed on the orders of Ashikaga Tadayoshi.
zh: 护良亲王（1308—1335），通称大塔宫，是后醍醐天皇之子。他幼年出家，曾任天台座主，后来还俗，在1333年元弘之乱中统领倒幕官军，为攻灭镰仓幕府立下首功，建武新政时被任命为征夷大将军。他因敌视足利尊氏而遭解除将军职务并幽禁于镰仓。1335年8月12日中先代之乱期间，他在镰仓被足利直义下令杀害。

en: First known as Prince Kōen, Munakata no Kiyōuji was by tradition a son of Emperor Uda and the founder of the hereditary priestly line of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province. In 898 he became the adopted son of Grand Minister Minamoto no Kiyohiro, received the Minamoto name, and rose to senior third rank and middle counselor. In 914, after the former Munakata head took the Naniwa clan name and left the shrine lands, Kiyōuji was appointed the shrine's priest, adopted the Munakata name, and served until 938. His son Ujio succeeded him.
zh: 宗形清氏初名光远亲王，相传为宇多天皇之子，是筑前国宗像大社世袭大宫司家的始祖。898年，他成为太政大臣源清广的犹子，受赐源姓，官至正三位中纳言。914年，旧豪族宗形千世受赐难波氏、离开宗像之地后，清氏就任宗像神社宫司，改姓宗形，在任至938年。其子孙世代承袭宫司之职，继任者是其子宗像氏男。

en: Munakata Munetoki was the fifth hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, in office from 1013 (Chōwa 2) to 1032 (Chōgen 5). He succeeded Munakata Ujino, and Munakata Taetada followed him in 1033.
zh: 宗像宗时是筑前国宗像大社第五代世袭大宫司，1013年（长和二年）至1032年（长元五年）在任。他继宗像氏能之后接任，1033年由宗像妙忠继任。

en: Munakata no Nagauji was the son of the daiguji Ujinari, who in 1251 placed the still-youthful Nagauji in the head priesthood of Munakata Taisha while guarding the shrine's affairs himself. From around 1273 Nagauji directed the shrine in name and fact. When the Mongols invaded Kyushu, the Kamakura shogunate reinstated him as daiguji in 1279 for coastal defense, and after the 1281 Kōan campaign he was granted five chō of Kanzaki manor in Hizen Province for his service.
zh: 宗像长氏是大宫司氏业之子。1251年，氏业把宗像大社大宫司之职传给尚在幼年的长氏，自己监护社务。约1273年起长氏名实兼具地主持神社。蒙古来袭期间，镰仓幕府于1279年为防御异国重新任命他为大宫司；1281年弘安之役后，他因战功受领肥前国神埼庄五町的恩赏。

en: Munakata Taetada was the sixth hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, in office from 1033 (Chōgen 6) to 1050 (Eishō 5). Tradition credits him with founding Tsutagatake Castle in the eleventh century on the ridge between Munakata and Onga districts. The fortress later became the Munakata clan's seat for five centuries.
zh: 宗像妙忠是筑前国宗像大社第六代世袭大宫司，1033年（长元六年）至1050年（永承五年）在任。相传他于11世纪在宗像与远贺两地交界的山脊上修筑茑岳城。这座山城后来成为宗像氏五百年的居城。

en: Tradition holds that Munakata Tametada was a high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, placed between Taetada, the sixth priest to 1050, and Ujitaka, the seventh from 1051.
zh: 相传宗像为忠曾任筑前国宗像大社大宫司，其位置在第六代妙忠（在任至1050年）与第七代氏高（1051年起）之间。

en: Munakata no Ujiakira was a son of the daiguji Ujikuni. He served as the forty-fourth head priest of Munakata Taisha from 1236 to 1247.
zh: 宗像氏昌是大宫司氏国之子，于1236—1247年任宗像大社第44代大宫司。

en: The list of hereditary high priests (daiguji) of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province records a Munakata Ujifusa in office in 1120–1122, 1124–1129 and 1132.
zh: 筑前国宗像大社的世袭大宫司名单在1120年至1122年、1124年至1129年及1132年三次记载名为宗像氏房的大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujihira served as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, holding the shrine headship four times, in 1130, 1131, 1144–1145 and 1151–1153, as the office alternated between kinsmen of the Munakata clan.
zh: 宗像氏平担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，曾四度出任该职，在任年份为1130年、1131年、1144—1145年和1151—1153年，当时大宫司一职在宗像氏族人之间交替。

en: Munakata Ujiie served as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, at the end of the Genpei War, taking office in 1183 and again in 1184, when the shrine headship alternated rapidly between him and Ujisane.
zh: 宗像氏家在源平合战末期担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，于1183年和1184年两度在任，这一时期大宫司之职在他与氏实之间频繁交替。

en: Munakata Ujikatsu served as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, holding office in 1162 as the twenty-sixth shrine head, between the tenures of Ujisane and Ujiyuki.
zh: 宗像氏胜担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，于1162年在任，为第26代大宫司，前后任分别为氏实与氏幸。

en: Munakata Ujikuni, a son of Ujisane, was a Kamakura gokenin and daiguji of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province. During the Genpei War he held Shiroyama Castle and ruled the central Munakata lands. He first became daiguji in 1189 and returned to the office in 1213. In 1222 the Kamakura shogunate confirmed his rule over the shrine domain, and in 1232 he resigned after granting the office to Munakata Ujitsune.
zh: 宗像氏国是氏实之子，为筑前国宗像大社的大宫司、镰仓幕府御家人。源平合战期间，他以白山城为居城，统治宗像地方中部。他于1189年首次就任大宫司，1213年再次还任。1222年，镰仓幕府承认他作为大宫司的支配权；1232年，他把职位让给宗像氏经后辞职。

en: Munakata Ujimasa was the 51st hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, holding office from 1278 (Kōan 1) to 1290 (Shōō 3). Munakata Ujitoshi succeeded him in 1291.
zh: 宗像氏正是筑前国宗像大社第51代世袭大宫司，于1278年（弘安元年）至1290年（正应三年）在任。1291年，宗像氏俊继任。

en: Munakata Ujimichi was the tenth hereditary high priest (daiguji) of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, holding office in 1107 and 1108. He was a son of Ujisuke, the eighth high priest.
zh: 宗像氏道是筑前国宗像大社第十代世袭大宫司，1107年至1108年在任。他是第八代大宫司氏助之子。

en: Munakata no Ujimori, childhood name Yoshimatsu, was a son of the daiguji Nagauji. The succession list makes him the forty-ninth head priest of Munakata Taisha, serving from 1265 to 1277; his tenure covered the first Mongol invasion of 1274.
zh: 宗像氏盛幼名弥松，是大宫司长氏之子。世系表列其为宗像大社第49代大宫司，1265—1277年在任，任职期间经历1274年第一次蒙古来袭（文永之役）。

en: Munakata Ujina was the 53rd hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, in office from 1325 (Shōchū 2) to 1335 (Kenmu 2), as the Kamakura bakufu fell and the Kenmu Restoration began. Munakata Ujitoshi succeeded him in 1336.
zh: 宗像氏名是筑前国宗像大社第53代世袭大宫司，于1325年（正中二年）至1335年（建武二年）在任，其间镰仓幕府灭亡、建武新政开始。1336年，宗像氏俊继任。

en: Munakata Ujinaga served as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, holding office in 1185, the year the Genpei War ended.
zh: 宗像氏永担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，于源平合战结束的1185年在任。

en: Munakata no Ujinaka was a son of Ujitada and grandson of the daiguji Ujizane. He served as the thirty-seventh head priest of Munakata Taisha in 1198.
zh: 宗像氏仲是氏忠之子、大宫司氏实之孙，于1198年担任宗像大社第37代大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujinao was the eleventh hereditary high priest (daiguji) of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, serving from 1109 to 1118. He was a son of Ujisue, the ninth high priest, and was followed by Ujifusa.
zh: 宗像氏尚是筑前国宗像大社第十一代世袭大宫司，1109年至1118年在任。他是第九代大宫司氏季之子，之后由氏房继任。

en: Munakata no Ujinari was a biological son of the daiguji Ujitsune, adopted in childhood by his uncle Ujikuni, who passed him the head priesthood of Munakata Taisha in 1231. The traditional list names him the forty-seventh daiguji in 1250, and in 1251 he transferred the office to his son Nagauji but stayed on as guardian. For decades he settled shrine-land suits before the Kamakura shogunate, enlarging the domains and fixing the direct succession. Ordained as the monk Jōei, he issued a further transfer document in 1273 and was still living in 1274.
zh: 宗像氏业是大宫司氏经的亲生子，自幼被伯父氏国收为养子，氏国于1231年把宗像大社大宫司之职传给他。传统世系表列其为第47代大宫司，时在1250年；1251年他把职务传给儿子长氏，自己则继续以监护人身份掌权。此后数十年间，他在镰仓幕府处理一系列社领诉讼，扩大社领，确立大宫司嫡流相承的体制。出家后法名净惠，1273年再下让状，1274年仍在世。

en: Munakata Ujino was the fourth hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, in office from 987 (Eien 1) to 1012 (Chōwa 1). He succeeded Munakata Ujiyo, and Munakata Munetoki followed him in 1013.
zh: 宗像氏能是筑前国宗像大社第四代世袭大宫司，987年（永延元年）至1012年（长和元年）在任。他在宗像氏世之后接任，1013年由宗像宗时继任。

en: Munakata no Ujino served as the forty-first head priest of Munakata Taisha in 1216.
zh: 宗像氏能于1216年担任宗像大社第41代大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujinobu was daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, serving in 1138–1143 and again in 1146–1150. He was the father of Munakata Ujisane, who took the clan into vassalage to the Kamakura shogunate.
zh: 宗像氏信是筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，在任时间为1138—1143年及1146—1150年。他是宗像氏实之父，氏实后来率全族成为镰仓幕府的御家人。

en: Munakata Ujinori was a head of the Munakata house of Chikuzen Province, the clan that monopolized the high-priesthood of Munakata Taisha. He was its 50th high priest, holding office in 1277 (Kenji 3). Munakata Ujimasa followed him in 1278.
zh: 宗像氏范是筑前国宗像氏的当主，该族世代独占宗像大社的大宫司之职。他是第50代大宫司，于1277年（建治三年）在任。1278年，宗像氏正接任大宫司。

en: Munakata no Ujio was the second hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, said to be a son of the line's founder, Munakata no Kiyōuji. He held office from 939 to 963. During the Tengyō War, when the pirate leader Fujiwara no Sumitomo rebelled against the Heian court, Ujio fought the rebel forces in Kyushu and killed a younger brother of Sumitomo. In 964 he was followed in the priesthood by Munakata Ujiyo, generally counted as his son.
zh: 宗像氏男是筑前国宗像大社第二代世袭大宫司，相传为大宫司家始祖宗形清氏之子，939年至963年在任。天庆之乱时，海贼首领藤原纯友举兵反叛平安朝廷，氏男在九州与叛军作战，斩杀了纯友的一个弟弟。964年，宗像氏世继任大宫司，一般认为氏世是氏男之子。

en: Munakata Ujisane was daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the clan shrine of Chikuzen Province, holding the office five times between 1160 and 1188. A son of daiguji Ujinobu, he married a daughter of the Ō family, Hakata merchants engaged in overseas trade. In the eighth month of 1187 Minamoto no Yoritomo confirmed his rule over the Munakata lands and made him a gokenin, turning the shrine house into a warrior house. He died on 27 November 1189, leaving sons Ujitada and Ujikuni.
zh: 宗像氏实是筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，为氏信之子，曾在1160—1188年间五度出任该职。他娶从事海外贸易的博多商人王氏之女为妻。1187年八月，源赖朝承认他对宗像领地的统治，将其列为御家人，大宫司家由此发展为统治一方的武士团。他于1189年11月27日去世，留下氏忠、氏国等子嗣。

en: Munakata Ujishige was a younger son of Ujitoshi and brother of Ujiyori, of the Chikuzen house holding the high-priesthood of Munakata Taisha. In 1391 Ujiyori made over the family headship to him; Ujishige's son Shigekatsu moved with Ujiyori to Niwa District in Owari.
zh: 宗像氏重是筑前宗像大宫司家宗像氏俊之子、氏赖之弟。1391年氏赖将宗像本家当主之位让给他；氏赖迁居尾张国丹羽郡时，氏重之子重胜随行。

en: Munakata no Ujishige served as the thirty-ninth head priest of Munakata Taisha in 1212.
zh: 宗像氏重于1212年担任宗像大社第39代大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujisue, said to be a son of Ujitaka, served as the ninth hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province from 1094 to 1106; his sons Ujinao and Ujinaga later held the same office.
zh: 宗像氏季相传是氏高之子，1094年至1106年担任筑前国宗像大社第九代世袭大宫司，其子氏尚和氏永后来也出任大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujisuke, a son of the seventh daiguji Ujitaka, was the eighth hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen, serving from 1072 to 1093. His son Ujimichi later became the tenth high priest.
zh: 宗像氏助是第七代大宫司氏高之子，1072年至1093年任筑前国宗像大社第八代世袭大宫司。其子氏道后来成为第十代大宫司。

en: Munakata no Ujisumi served as the forty-fifth head priest of Munakata Taisha in 1248.
zh: 宗像氏澄于1248年担任宗像大社第45代大宫司。

en: Munakata no Ujitada was a son of Ujizane, the daiguji, or head priest, of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province. He married a daughter of the Zhang family, Song merchants settled in Hakata, tying the shrine house to Kyushu's trade with China. His daughter married Mutō Sukeyori, founder of the Mutō warrior house, while his son Ujinaka briefly served as the shrine's thirty-seventh daiguji in 1198. In 1220 his wife adopted Mutō Tameyori and passed him three villages, prompting a long lawsuit over the lands.
zh: 宗像氏忠是筑前国宗像大社大宫司宗像氏实之子。他娶定居博多的宋商张氏之女为妻，使大宫司家与九州的对华贸易相连。他的女儿嫁给武藤武士家的开创者武藤资赖，儿子氏仲则于1198年短暂出任第37代大宫司。1220年，氏忠之妻收养武藤为赖，把三个村庄让给他，由此引发长期的领地诉讼。

en: Munakata Ujitaka was the seventh hereditary daiguji, high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, holding office from 1051 to 1071. His sons Ujisuke and Ujisue succeeded him in turn as the shrine's eighth and ninth high priests.
zh: 宗像氏高是筑前国宗像大社的第七代世袭大宫司，1051年至1071年在任。他的儿子氏助和氏季先后继任，成为大社第八代和第九代大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujitoshi served as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, holding the shrine headship three times, in 1131, from 1132 to 1137 and again from 1154 to 1159, as the office passed between kinsmen of the Munakata clan.
zh: 宗像氏俊担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，曾三度在任，分别在1131年、1132—1137年和1154—1159年，当时该职在宗像氏族人之间交替相传。

en: Munakata Ujitoshi was a head of the Munakata clan of Chikuzen, the maritime warrior house that monopolized the high-priesthood of Munakata Taisha. From 1344 the clan held the jitō office of Ishida estate on Iki, and in 1365 the Muromachi bakufu appointed Ujitoshi shugo of Iki Province, an office he is recorded holding until some years after 1365; sources describe him as attached to the Isshiki faction. His son Ujiyori succeeded him as both Iki shugo and high priest.
zh: 宗像氏俊是筑前国宗像氏的当主；宗像氏是世代垄断宗像大社大宫司之职的海洋豪族。1344年起，宗像氏兼任壹岐石田乡的地头，1365年室町幕府又任命氏俊为壹岐国守护，据记载他在1365年之后数年仍在任，史料称其隶属于一色氏一系。他死后，其子氏赖同时继任壹岐守护与宗像大社大宫司。

en: Munakata no Ujitsune was a son of the daiguji Ujizane. He served as the forty-third head priest of Munakata Taisha from 1232 to 1235 and again as the forty-sixth in 1249. His son Ujinari later became daiguji.
zh: 宗像氏经是大宫司氏实之子，于1232—1235年任宗像大社第43代大宫司，1249年再任第46代。其子氏业后来成为大宫司。

en: Munakata Ujiyo was the third hereditary high priest of Munakata Taisha in Chikuzen Province, in office from 964 to 986. He is generally said to be a son of the second priest, Munakata no Ujio, though the record naming him third is unreliable.
zh: 宗像氏世是筑前国宗像大社第三代世袭大宫司，964年至986年在任。一般认为他是第二代大宫司宗像氏男之子，但将他列为第三代大宫司的记载并不可靠。

en: Munakata Ujiyori was the son of Munakata Ujitoshi, head of the Chikuzen house that supplied the hereditary high priests of Munakata Taisha. In 1369 he held the post of shugo of Iki Province, succeeding his father, and he also inherited the family's hereditary high-priesthood. In 1391 he made over the headship of the main Munakata family to his younger brother Ujishige and moved east to Niwa District in Owari Province, adjoining the Isshiki shugo's domains, taking Ujishige's son Shigekatsu with him.
zh: 宗像氏赖是筑前宗像大宫司家当主宗像氏俊之子。1369年，他继父亲之后出任壹岐国守护，同时承袭了宗像大社大宫司的世职。1391年，他将宗像本家的当主之位让给弟弟氏重，自己东迁，移居到与一色氏守护领地相邻的尾张国丹羽郡，还带上氏重之子重胜同行。

en: Munakata Ujiyuki served twice as daiguji of Munakata Taisha, the great shrine of Chikuzen Province, the twenty-seventh shrine head, in office in 1163–1164 and again in 1173–1175, between the repeated tenures of his kinsman Ujisane.
zh: 宗像氏幸两度担任筑前国宗像大社的大宫司，为第27代大宫司，在任时间为1163—1164年及1173—1175年，两次任职之间为族人氏实在任。

en: Prince Muneyoshi (Munenaga, 1311–1385) was a son of Emperor Go-Daigo by Nijō Ishi. He entered Myōhō-in in 1325 and became Tendai zasu in 1330, but was exiled to Sanuki after the Genkō War and, on returning to secular life, fought for the Southern Court. In 1338, sailing to Mutsu with Kitabatake Chikafusa, he was wrecked in Tōtōmi, and from 1344 made Ōgawara in Shinano his base for thirty years, earning the name Shinano no Miya. Appointed seii taishōgun in 1352, he led Southern armies in the east and later compiled the quasi-imperial anthology Shin'yō Wakashū, completed in 1381.
zh: 宗良亲王（1311—1385）是后醍醐天皇与二条为子之子。1325年入妙法院，1330年任天台座主；元弘之变后被流放赞岐，还俗后为南朝征战。1338年，他随北畠亲房乘船前往陆奥，途中座礁漂流至远江；1344年起以信浓伊那郡大河原为据点达三十年，人称“信浓宫”。1352年他被任命为征夷大将军，在东国统领南朝军队；晚年编订准敕撰和歌集《新叶和歌集》，于1381年完成。

en: Emperor Murakami (926–967), personal name Nariakira, reigned as Japan's 62nd emperor from 946 to 967. The fourteenth son of Emperor Daigo, he was named crown prince in 944 and succeeded on his brother Suzaku's abdication. Fujiwara no Tadahira remained regent until 949, after which Murakami ruled personally; his rule was remembered as the Tenryaku age of good government, though Saneyori and Morosuke dominated the court. In 951 he ordered the Gosen Wakashū compiled, and the palace suffered its first fire in 960. A skilled flautist and koto player, he died in 967; his sons became Emperors Reizei and En'yū.
zh: 村上天皇（926—967），名成明，是日本第62代天皇，946年至967年在位。他是醍醐天皇的第十四子，944年被立为太子，在兄长朱雀天皇退位后继位。藤原忠平继续担任摄政至949年，此后村上亲理政务，其治世被后世誉为天历之治，不过藤原实赖与藤原师辅兄弟把持着朝廷。951年他下令编纂《后撰和歌集》，960年皇宫遭遇首次大火。村上擅长吹笛与弹筝，967年去世，他的两个儿子后来成为冷泉天皇与圆融天皇。

en: Mutō Sukeyori (1160–1228) was an early Kamakura shogunate warrior and the founder of the Shōni clan. He first served under Taira no Tomomori but surrendered to Minamoto no Yoritomo after the Battle of Ichinotani in 1184, and fought for him in the Ōshū campaign of 1189. Sent to Kyūshū as Chinzei commissioner in the 1190s, he became military governor of Hizen, Chikuzen, Buzen, Iki and Tsushima provinces. In 1226 he became the first shogunal retainer to hold the junior assistant post at Dazaifu; his son Sukeyoshi inherited the office and took the name Shōni. Sukeyori died in 1228.
zh: 武藤资赖（1160—1228）是镰仓幕府初期的武将、御家人，少贰氏的始祖。他初为平知盛的部将，1184年一之谷之战后投降源赖朝，被赦免后成为赖朝的家人，1189年参加奥州合战立下战功。1190年代他被派往九州，任镇西奉行，并成为肥前、筑前、丰前、壹岐、对马五国的守护。1226年，他成为首位以御家人身份出任大宰少贰者；该职由儿子资能继承并世袭，资能遂以少贰为姓。资赖于1228年去世。

en: Mutō Yorihira was a warrior and gokenin of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods. Like his father Kondō Kageyori, he served in the imperial mushadokoro and lived in Musashi Province as mokudai deputy of the Taira commander Taira no Tomomori, whose son Tomoakira was born to Yorihira's sister. During the Jishō-Juei War that began in 1180 he submitted to Minamoto no Yoritomo and became a Kamakura vassal. His son Ujihira's descendants took the name Daihōji, while those of Sukeyori, whom he treated as a son, took the name Shōni; his grave was at Morooka in Musashi's Kuraki District.
zh: 武藤赖平是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将、御家人。他与父亲近藤景赖一样出仕武者所，作为平氏大将平知盛的目代居住在武藏国；他的姊妹嫁给知盛，生下平知章。在1180年开始的治承·寿永之乱中，他归顺源赖朝，成为镰仓幕府的御家人。其子氏平的后裔称大宝寺氏，猶子资赖的后裔称少弐氏；墓相传位于武藏国久良岐郡师冈乡。

en: Mochishige Nagai was a Kamakura-period retainer of the shogunate, a son of Nagai Yasushige, shugo of Suo, Bizen and Bingo, and younger brother of Yorishige. Like his father and brother he served as a councillor at the Rokuhara headquarters in Kyoto.
zh: 长井茂重是镰仓幕府御家人，身兼周防、备前、备后三国守护的长井泰重之子，赖重之弟。他与父兄一样，在京都的六波罗探题麾下担任评定众。

en: Nagai Munehide (1265–1327) was a Kamakura-period gokenin, son of Nagai Tokihide. At his coming of age he took a character from the eighth shikken, Hōjō Tokimune. In 1282, aged eighteen, he joined the hikitsuke court and became Kunai no gon no taifu, but the Shimotsuki incident of 1285 drove him from office as a kinsman of the Adachi. He returned after the Heizenmon disturbance of 1293, headed the appeals office and sat on Hōjō Sadatoki's new shisō council, and went to Kyoto as a bakufu envoy in 1294. He led the hikitsuke from 1298 to 1309, took the monk's name Dōyū, and died in 1327, aged sixty-three by traditional reckoning.
zh: 长井宗秀（1265—1327）是镰仓时代后期御家人，长井时秀之子。元服时他从第八代执权北条时宗名中领受偏讳。1282年，年仅18岁的他就任引付众和宫内权大辅，但1285年霜月骚动时因与安达氏是亲族而失势。1293年平禅门之乱后他复归，出任越诉头人，并进入北条贞时新设的执奏任职，1294年作为幕府使者上京。1298年他升任引付头人，一直任职至1309年；出家后称道雄，于1327年去世，享年63岁。

en: Nagai Sadahide (c. 1278–1308) was a late Kamakura politician and warrior, son of Nagai Munehide and of a daughter of Hōjō Sanetoki. At his coming of age he received a character from the ninth shikken, Hōjō Sadatoki. In 1294 he was made a kurōdo of junior sixth rank, later rising to Nakatsukasa shōyū and Hyōgo no kami. In 1306 he pilgrimaged to Tsurugaoka Hachiman and the Izu and Hakone shrines as deputy for the shōgun Prince Hisaaki. He kept company with his cousin Hōjō Sadaaki, the Kanesawa patron of letters, and contributed to cultural activities. He died in 1308 aged about thirty.
zh: 长井贞秀（约1278—1308）是镰仓时代后期的政治家与武将，长井宗秀与北条实时之女所生之子。元服时他从第九代执权北条贞时名中领受偏讳。1294年他任从六位藏人，后历任中务少辅、兵库头。1306年，他作为将军久明亲王的代官，参拜鹤冈八幡宫及伊豆、箱根二所权现。他与母方表亲、好学的金泽北条贞显交游，参与文化活动，于1308年去世，终年约30岁。

en: Nagai Sadashige (1272–1331) was a late Kamakura gokenin and head of the Nagai clan's Kyoto cadet line, the Rokuhara hyōjōshū house founded by his grandfather Yasushige. The son of Nagai Yorishige, he took a character of his name from the ninth shikken, Hōjō Sadatoki, at his coming of age. He served in Kyoto as a Rokuhara hyōjōshū and inherited the family post of shugo of Bingo, governing the province from its shugo seat at Seto Nagawanosho. He died in 1331, said to be aged sixty.
zh: 长井贞重（1272—1331）是镰仓时代后期御家人，长井氏京都旁支——由祖父泰重开创的六波罗评定众家——的当主。他是长井赖重之子，元服时从第九代执权北条贞时名中领受偏讳。他在京都担任六波罗评定众，世袭备后国守护，以濑户长和庄为守护所治理该国，于1331年去世，享年60岁。

en: Sadayori Nagai was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era, the fourth head of the Nagai house of Bingo province and a son of Yorishige. He served the Kamakura shogunate, then after the Kenmu Restoration of 1333 followed Ashikaga Takauji, acquiring stewardships over manors in Harima, Echigo and Izumo alongside his Bingo lands. When the Kannō Disturbance threw Bingo into disorder after 1351, he sent reinforcements to the provincial shugo Iwamatsu Raiyu. In 1363 he fought the party of Ashikaga Tadafuyu at the battle of Miyauchi in Bingo alongside Miya Kanenobu and was killed.
zh: 长井贞赖是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，备后国长井氏第四代当主，赖重之子。他初仕镰仓幕府，1333年建武新政后追随足利尊氏，除备后的本领外，还获得播磨、越后、出云三国境内庄园的地头职。1351年观应之乱波及备后，他出兵支援备后守护岩松赖宥。1363年，他与宫兼信在备后宫内合战中与足利直冬一党交战，战死沙场。

en: Takafuyu Nagai (1314–1347), also called Uma no suke, headed the main line of the Nagai, descendants of Oe no Hiromoto. His first name used a character from the regent Hojo Takatoki, and by the later 1320s he succeeded Nagai Munehide as steward of Akana manor in Mino. In 1331, at the outbreak of the Genko War, he went up to Kyoto as an eastern envoy. When the shogunate fell in 1333 he dropped Takatoki's character, took the name Takafuyu, and joined the Kenmu Court of Miscellaneous Claims. He later served Ashikaga Takauji and died in 1347, succeeded by Ujimoto.
zh: 长井举冬（1314—1347），通称右马助，是大江广元后裔长井氏嫡流的当主。他初名高冬，名字中的“高”字得自执权北条高时；1320年代后期，他继长井宗秀之后任美浓国茜部庄正地头。1331年元弘之乱爆发时，他作为东使上洛。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他弃用高时下赐的偏讳，改名举冬，出任建武新政杂诉决断所成员，此后追随足利尊氏，1347年去世，由氏元继位。

en: Takahiro Nagai was the eldest son of Nagai Sadashige, head of the Kyoto-based Nagai house that staffed the Rokuhara council and held the hereditary shugo post of Bingo. From 1349 to 1351 Takahiro served as shugo of Nagato province at the western end of Honshu, during the years of the Kannō Disturbance between Ashikaga Takauji and Tadayoshi.
zh: 长井高广是长井贞重的嫡男。贞重一族居于京都，世代出任六波罗评定众并世袭备后国守护。1349年至1351年，高广出任本州西端长门国的守护，其间足利尊氏与直义之间爆发了观应之乱。

en: Nagai Tokihide (dates unknown, active 1247–1284), also called Ōe no Tokihide, was a Kamakura gokenin, son of Nagai Yasuhide and heir of the clan's main line. The Azuma Kagami first names him in 1247 as Nagai Tarō, a guard at the Tsurugaoka Hachiman festival. In 1254 he joined the hikitsuke board, became a hyōjōshū in 1265 and Bizen no kami in 1271, and went to Kyoto as the bakufu's envoy in 1257, 1264 and 1282. In 1277 he served as guardian and carried a ceremonial cup at Hōjō Sadatoki's coming of age; after Tokimune's death in 1284 he took the tonsure as Saiki.
zh: 长井时秀（生卒年不详，活跃于1247—1284年），又称大江时秀，是镰仓幕府御家人，长井泰秀之子、长井氏嫡流继承人。《吾妻镜》于1247年首次提到他，以“长井太郎”之名担任鹤冈八幡宫放生会的随兵。1254年他就任引付众、参与幕政，1265年任评定众，1271年任备前守，并于1257、1264、1282年作为幕府东使前往京都。1277年北条贞时元服时他担任持杯的后见役；1284年北条时宗去世后他出家，法号西规。

en: Nagai Tokihiro was an early Kamakura gokenin, the second son of Ōe no Hiromoto, the shogunate's first Mandokoro chief. Holding the Nagai manor in Okitama district, Dewa province, he took its name and founded the Nagai clan. As a kurodo courtier he attended the shōgun Minamoto no Sanetomo and witnessed his assassination at Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine in 1219. After his brother Chikahiro's fall in the 1221 Jōkyū War and Hiromoto's death in 1225, he headed the Ōe house, later served as shugo of Bingo, and is credited with building Yonezawa Castle in 1238. He died in 1241.
zh: 长井时广是镰仓幕府前期的御家人，幕府初代政所别当大江广元的次子。他领有出羽国置赐郡长井庄，遂以庄园为姓，成为长井氏之祖。他曾任藏人，随侍将军源实朝，1219年实朝在鹤冈八幡宫拜贺时被公晓暗杀，时广也在场。兄长大江亲广在1221年承久之乱中失势、广元又于1225年去世后，他继任大江氏总领，活跃于幕府中枢，后来出任备后国守护，相传1238年修筑了米泽城。他于1241年去世。

en: Nagai Yasuhide (1212–1254), also called Ōe Yasuhide, was a Kamakura gokenin, the legitimate heir of Nagai Tokihiro and grandson of Ōe no Hiromoto. At his coming of age he received a character from the regent Hōjō Yasutoki's name. Promoted swiftly, he held junior fifth rank by 1229 and became Kai no Kami in 1238. After his father's death in 1241, the thirty-year-old Yasuhide joined the Hyōjōshū shogunal council alongside Hōjō Tsunetoki. In the Hōji conflict of 1247 he backed the regent Hōjō Tokiyori, securing the Nagai house in bakufu politics. He died in 1254, leaving a son, Tokihide.
zh: 长井泰秀（1212—1254），又称大江泰秀，镰仓幕府御家人，长井时广的嫡子、大江广元之孙。元服时获执权北条泰时赐以偏讳，取名泰秀。他晋升迅速，1229年已叙从五位下，1238年任甲斐守。1241年父亲去世后，年方三十的他与北条经时等人同列幕府评定众；1247年宝治合战中，他始终支持执权北条时赖，确立了长井氏在幕府中的地位。他于1254年去世，子长井时秀继嗣。

en: Nagai Yasushige (dates unknown, alive in 1264) was a Kamakura-period gokenin, a son of Nagai Tokihiro and grandson of Ōe no Hiromoto. At his coming of age he took one character of his name from Hōjō Yasutoki, the third shikken. While his elder brother Yasuhide's main line kept the clan's Dewa lands, Yasushige's branch settled in Kyoto under the Rokuhara Tandai.
