In 1252 he became shugo of Suō and accompanied the new shōgun Prince Munetaka to Kamakura, later holding Bizen and inheriting Bingo as shugo as well.
zh: 长井泰重（生卒年不详，1264年仍在世）是镰仓时代的御家人，长井时广之子、大江广元之孙。元服时他从第三代执权北条泰时名中领受偏讳，取名泰重。兄长泰秀的嫡流领有家族在出羽的领地，泰重这一支则定居京都，在六波罗探题麾下任职。1252年他就任周防国守护，随新将军宗尊亲王前往镰仓，此后又出任备前国守护，并继承了备后国守护之职。

en: Nagai Yorishige (dates unknown, alive in 1286) was a Kamakura-period gokenin, son of Nagai Yasushige and father of Nagai Sadashige. At his coming of age, between 1246 and 1263, he took one character of his name from the fifth shikken, Hōjō Tokiyori. He continued his family's Kyoto branch as a Rokuhara hyōjōshū, inherited the post of shugo of Bingo, and was appointed Inaba no kami like his father. In 1282 he was exiled to Echigo after a forceful appeal by the Nara monastery Kōfuku-ji, but the sentence was soon withdrawn, and records of 1286 show him back as Bingo shugo.
zh: 长井赖重（生卒年不详，1286年仍在世）是镰仓时代御家人，长井泰重之子、长井贞重之父。他在1246至1263年间元服，从第五代执权北条时赖名中领受偏讳。他延续家族的京都旁支，担任六波罗评定众，世袭备后国守护，并与父亲一样出任因幡守。1282年，因奈良兴福寺的强诉，他被流放至越后国，但处分不久即被撤回，1286年的史料显示他已再任备后守护。

en: Nagano Nagamori was an early head of the Buzen Nagano, a warrior clan of Buzen in northern Kyushu. The family death register gives him the title of Buzen-no-kami with junior fifth rank, and records his death in 1215 at age seventy-one.
zh: 长野长盛是九州北部丰前国武士家族丰前长野氏的早期当主。长野家《过去账》记载，他官至丰前守、从五位下，于1215年去世，享年71岁。

en: Nagano Naomori was a head of the Buzen Nagano warrior clan of Buzen in northern Kyushu. The family death register gives him the title of Buzen-no-kami with junior fifth rank, and records his death in 1219 at age forty-one.
zh: 长野直盛是九州北部丰前国武士家族丰前长野氏的当主。长野家《过去账》记载，他官至丰前守、从五位下，于1219年去世，享年41岁。

en: Nagano Sukefuji was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nagano clan, also called the Nagano-Kudō, a powerful kokujin family of Ise Province, and the son of Nagano Sukemasa. Around 1274 his clan built Nagano Castle in Ise, which became the family's base for centuries.
zh: 长野祐藤是镰仓时代武将，出身伊势国的有力国人长野氏（亦称长野工藤氏），为长野祐政之子。约1274年，长野氏在伊势的山地修筑长野城，此后数百年间这里都是该家族的据点。

en: Nagano Sukemasa, also called Kudō Sukemasa, was a Kamakura-period warrior, the son of Kudō Sukenaga. He settled at Nagano in Ise Province, where his father held the jitō post, and took the place name as his family name, founding the Nagano clan of Ise.
zh: 长野祐政（亦称工藤祐政）是镰仓时代武将，工藤祐长之子。他在父亲担任地头的伊势国长野定居，并以地名为姓氏，成为伊势长野氏（长野工藤氏）的初代。

en: Nagano Takamori was a head of the Buzen Nagano warrior clan of Buzen in northern Kyushu. The family death register gives him the title of Buzen-no-kami with junior fifth rank, and records his early death in 1303 at age thirty-five.
zh: 长野高盛是九州北部丰前国武士家族丰前长野氏的当主。长野家《过去账》记载，他官至丰前守、从五位下，1303年早逝，享年35岁。

en: Nagano Tanemori was a head of the Buzen Nagano, a local warrior clan of Kiku District in Buzen on northern Kyushu, and held the title of Buzen-no-kami with junior fifth rank. Local Buzen gazetteers credit his day with building a ring of clan castles, including Ōmitsudake, Komitsudake, Shimonagano, Marugaguchi, Fukuōji, Hiegahata and Shii-no-jō, which became strongholds of the Nagano kindred. The family death register records that he died in 1286 at age seventy.
zh: 长野种盛是九州北部丰前国企救郡国人武士丰前长野氏的当主，官至丰前守、从五位下。据丰前地方志记载，在他所处的时代，修筑了大三岳、小三岳、下长野、丸箇口、福相寺、稗畑、椎城等一批城砦，都成为长野一族的据点。长野家《过去账》记载，他于1286年去世，享年70岁。

en: Nagano Tsunemori was a head of the Buzen Nagano warrior clan of Buzen in northern Kyushu. The family death register gives him the court post of Saemon-no-suke with junior fifth rank, and records his death in 1252 at age sixty-five.
zh: 长野常盛是九州北部丰前国武士家族丰前长野氏的当主。长野家《过去账》记载，他官任左卫门佐、从五位下，于1252年去世，享年65岁。

en: Nagano Yasumori was, as local Buzen gazetteers record, the sixth son of Taira no Tokimori, himself said to be a cousin of Taira no Kiyomori. In 1157 he was appointed governor of Buzen in northern Kyushu, built a castle at Nagano in Kiku District, and took the place name as his family name, founding the Buzen Nagano clan. He held the court title of Shuri-no-daibu with junior fourth rank, and the family death register records his death in 1178 and his Buddhist name Sūzan Hakuei. His descendants held the district as local lords for some four hundred years.
zh: 据丰前地方志记载，长野康盛是平时盛的第六子，而平时盛相传是平清盛的堂兄弟。1157年，他被任命为九州北部的丰前国司，在企救郡长野筑城居住，并以地名作为家名，开创丰前长野氏。他官至修理大夫、从四位下；长野家《过去账》记载他于1178年去世，法名崇山伯荣。此后约四百年间，其子孙作为国人领主世代盘踞丰前。

en: Nagano Yoshifusa was a local lord of the Buzen Nagano clan in Kyushu's Buzen province, holding Junior Fifth Rank and an office in the Left Outer Palace Guards. He died in 1314, and his son Motomori died in Kamakura in 1334.
zh: 长野义房是九州丰前国丰前长野氏的国人领主，叙从五位下，任左卫门尉，1314年去世；其子基盛1334年在镰仓病死。

en: Naganuma Hidenao headed the main line of the Naganuma warriors during Japan's Nanboku-chō wars. When the clan could no longer keep its home manor of Naganuma in Shimotsuke Province, he moved the main house to its Nagae manor in Mutsu Province, also called the Minamiyama manor. The move split the clan into the Mutsu Naganuma and Shimotsuke Naganuma branches.
zh: 长沼秀直是日本南北朝战乱时期长沼武家嫡流的当主。家族已难以维持在下野国的本领长沼庄，他便把宗家迁往陆奥国的长江庄（又称南山庄），长沼氏由此分为陆奥长沼氏与下野长沼氏两支。

en: Naganuma Hideyuki was a Japanese warrior who held the title of Acting Governor of Echizen Province and served as shugo of Awaji Province from 1331 to 1333.
zh: 长沼秀行是日本武将，官居越前权守，1331年至1333年担任淡路国守护。

en: Naganuma Munehide was a Japanese warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods, whose father Naganuma Muneyasu held the Nagae manor in Mutsu Province. In 1299 the Kamakura shogunate confirmed him in that manor and his father's other lands under Muneyasu's deed of transfer. In 1310 he built the Naganuma Minami-Furudate residence, and in 1312 he granted the jitō office of Naruhara village to Munezane. When the imperial schism opened in the 1330s, he took the side of the Northern Court.
zh: 长沼宗秀是日本镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，其父长沼宗泰领有陆奥国长江庄。1299年，镰仓幕府依据宗泰的让状，承认他领有长江庄以下的诸所领。1310年，他营造长沼南古馆；1312年，又将长江庄内奈良原乡的地头职让予宗实。1330年代南北朝分裂后，他站在北朝一方。

en: Naganuma Munemasa (1162–1240) was a warrior and gokenin of the early Kamakura period, the second son of the Shimotsuke magnate Oyama Masamitsu and founder of the Naganuma clan. He joined Minamoto no Yoritomo in 1180, fought at the Battle of Nogi in 1183, and served in the campaigns against the Taira and the Northern Fujiwara of Ōshū, receiving the Minamiaizu lands in 1189. He backed the Hōjō through the troubles of 1203–1213, fought in the Jōkyū War of 1221, and became shugo of Settsu and Awaji. In 1230 he passed the headship to his son Tokimune.
zh: 长沼宗政（1162—1240）是镰仓时代前期的武将、御家人，下野国豪族小山政光的次子，长沼氏之祖。1180年起追随源赖朝，1183年在野木宫合战中讨伐志田义广，后又参加攻灭平家与奥州藤原氏的战事，1189年受领陆奥国南会津之地。1203至1213年间的比企能员之变、畠山重忠之乱中他都站在北条一方，1221年承久之乱后受任摄津、淡路两国守护。1230年，他把家督让给嫡子时宗。

en: Naganuma Muneyasu was a Kamakura-period warrior, gokenin and waka poet, the son of Naganuma Tokimune. In 1245 he guarded Prince Munetaka at the Hōjō-e festival of Tsurugaoka Hachimangū. As shugo of Awaji he was ordered by the shogunate in 1258 to suppress akutō bands, and in 1277 he joined the Rokuhara hyōjōshū council in Kyoto. As a poet he had eight poems included in imperial anthologies such as the Shoku-Shūi Wakashū.
zh: 长沼宗泰是镰仓时代的武将、御家人兼歌人，长沼时宗之子。1245年鹤冈八幡宫举行放生会时，他担任宗尊亲王的警护；任淡路守护期间，他于1258年奉幕府之命取缔恶党，1277年出任京都六波罗评定众。他还以和歌闻名，有八首作品收入《续拾遗和歌集》等敕撰和歌集。

en: Naganuma Tokimune was a Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin, son of Naganuma Munemasa. In 1230 his father passed him the Naganuma manor in Shimotsuke, lands in southern Aizu, and the shugo post of Awaji. The Azuma Kagami records him as a gokenin between 1228 and 1241.
zh: 长沼时宗是镰仓时代武将、御家人，长沼宗政之子。1230年父亲将下野国长沼庄、陆奥国南山之地和淡路国守护职让给他。《吾妻镜》1228至1241年间有其活动记载。

en: Nagaya (684–729) was the most powerful imperial prince of the early Nara court. The eldest son of Prince Takechi and a grandson of both Emperors Tenji and Tenmu, he was raised directly to senior fourth rank in 704 and in 718 became grand councillor over the usual intermediate offices. After Fujiwara no Fuhito died in 720, Nagaya dominated the court as minister of the left. In 729 Fuhito's four sons accused him of treason and forced him to kill himself; his wife Princess Kibi and several of his children perished with him, an event known as the Nagaya Incident.
zh: 长屋王（684—729）是奈良时代前期最有权势的皇族。他是高市皇子长子，兼具天智、天武两天皇的血统，704年由无位直接叙为正四位上，718年又越过参议、中纳言等职位直接拜为大纳言。720年藤原不比等去世后，他以左大臣之尊总揽朝政。729年，不比等的四个儿子以谋反罪名逼迫他自尽，妻子吉备内亲王与几名子女同时遇难，史称“长屋王之变”。

en: Nakahara no Munefusa was a court official of the late Heian period and the recorded founder of the Buzen Utsunomiya, or Kii, clan. A younger son of the Utsunomiya founder Fujiwara no Sōen, he served the empress Fujiwara no Shōshi, becoming senior secretary of her chūgū office when she was enthroned in 1118, and deputy secretary of her Taikenmon'in household after she took the nun-empress title in 1124; many surviving documents from that office were drafted by him. Genealogies name Utsunomiya no Nobufusa as his son, though the Azuma Kagami makes Nobufusa his grandson.
zh: 中原宗房是平安时代后期的朝廷官员，被奉为丰前宇都宫氏（即城井氏）之祖。他是宇都宫氏始祖藤原宗圆的次子，出仕中宫藤原璋子：1118年璋子立后时出任中宫大属，1124年璋子受院号称待贤门院后，改任其院厅的主典代，该院厅留存的文书多出自他的手笔。各家系图把宇都宫信房记作他的儿子，但《吾妻镜》将信房记作他的孙子。

en: Nakamura no Iechika was a late-Heian palace official of the Fujiwara Hokke Yamakage line, holding junior fifth rank, lower grade, as an otoneri guard in the capital. He was the son of Nakamura no Suetaka, a former governor of Shimotsuke who gave Haga District the name Nakamura, and father of Nakamura no Mitsutaka, whose son Date Tomomune founded the Date clan in 1189. The Kanno shrine priests' genealogy records that after his daughter's husband Kanno Masamitsu died, Iechika adopted their son Masamichi, who later served the Date in the Oshu War and became priest of Yanagawa Hachiman Shrine.
zh: 中村家周是平安时代后期的朝廷官人，出自藤原北家山荫流，在京都任从五位下大舍人。他是曾任下野守、将芳贺郡改称中村的中村季孝之子，也是中村光隆之父；光隆之子伊达朝宗于1189年受封伊达郡，开创伊达氏。据《梁川八幡神主菅野氏系谱》，家周之女嫁给菅野政光，政光死后他收养外孙菅野正道；正道后来在奥州合战中随军出征，战后出任梁川八幡宫神主。

en: Nakamura no Mitsutaka was a late-Heian court official, son of Nakamura no Iechika, holding junior fifth rank, lower grade, as a hikurodo secretary serving the retired empress Taikenmon'in. He married a daughter of Minamoto no Tameyoshi, head of the Kawachi Genji. Thanks to this bond his son Date Tomomune joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's gokenin after 1180, fought in the Oshu War of 1189, and was enfeoffed with the Date district of Mutsu, founding the Date clan. Tradition makes Mitsutaka's granddaughter Daishin no Tsubone a concubine of Yoritomo and mother of the monk Jogyo.
zh: 中村光隆是平安时代后期官人，中村家周之子，官任从五位下，为待贤门院的非藏人。他娶河内源氏栋梁源为义之女为妻。凭借这层姻亲关系，其子伊达朝宗在1180年后成为源赖朝的御家人，参加1189年的奥州合战，因功受封陆奥国伊达郡，开创伊达氏。相传光隆的孙女大进局为源赖朝侧室，生下僧人贞晓。

en: Nakamura no Munehira was a warrior official of Sagami Province who took his name from Nakamura village in Yurugi District, near Odawara. In 1144 he appears among the followers of Minamoto no Yoshitomo during the Ōba estate dispute, and he turned his own lands into the Nakamura manor as its steward. His sons and grandsons, including Dohi no Sanehira and Tsuchiya no Munetō, formed the Nakamura warrior party. In 1180 they joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising, and Munehira repaired the Matsuda residence in Kamakura; in 1186 he distributed rice to the poor of Sagami on Yoritomo's orders.
zh: 中村宗平是相模国余绫郡中村乡（今小田原市东部）的在厅官人，以地名为自己的苗字。1144年源义朝侵攻大庭御厨时，他已作为义朝的属下见诸记载，并将自领寄进给权门，建成中村庄、自任庄官。他的子孙中有土肥实平、土屋宗远等人，结成号称“中村党”的武士团，于1180年随源赖朝举兵。同年他修缮镰仓的松田亭，1186年又奉赖朝之命向相模的贫民施米。

en: Nakamura no Sanemune was a late-Heian court official of the Fujiwara Hokke Yamakage line, son of Fujiwara no Sadato. In 1100 he was appointed governor of Mutsu and general of the Chinjufu garrison, and in 1107 he led the memorial rites after Emperor Horikawa died. As vice-governor of Hitachi from 1111 he built Isa Castle in Isa manor and, through the scholar Oe no Masafusa, won relief from an extraordinary tax for his exhausted province. In 1113 he aided the rebuilding of Kashima Shrine and crushed the Yokoyama revolt in Musashi, then settled at Nakamura and took that clan name.
zh: 中村实宗是平安时代后期的朝廷官员，出自藤原北家山荫流，为式部少辅藤原定任之子。1100年他就任陆奥守兼镇守府将军，1107年堀河天皇驾崩时担任法会使者。1111年起任常陆介，在伊佐庄修筑伊佐城，并通过学者大江匡房为疲敝的领地争取免除一次临时征税。1113年，他协助营建鹿岛神宫，又追讨平定武藏国的横山党之乱，此后移居中村之地，以中村为氏，是中村氏与伊佐氏的始祖。

en: Nakamura no Suetaka was a late-Heian courtier, the son of Nakamura no Sanemune, who took the Nakamura clan name in 1113. Suetaka held junior fourth rank, lower grade, and served as palace secretary, junior secretary in the empress's office, chamberlain, and governor of Shimotsuke. He first lived at Yamao in Hitachi's Isa manor, where he was called the Yamao secretary. As governor of Shimotsuke he settled in Haga District and, tradition says, renamed the place Nakamura after his own clan. After his term he retired to Shimodate and was known as the Shimodate chamberlain.
zh: 中村季孝是平安时代后期官人，其父中村实宗于1113年以中村为氏。季孝官至从四位下，历任藏人、皇后宫少进、侍从和下野守。他起初住在常陆国伊佐庄的山尾，被称为山尾藏人；出任下野守后定居下野国芳贺郡，相传以自己的氏名将当地改称中村。任满后他退居伊佐庄下馆，人称下馆侍从。

en: Nakanoin Michikata (1189–1239) was an early Kamakura-period court noble and the fifth son of Minamoto no Michichika. He became head of the Kurōdo-dokoro in 1211 and joined the kugyō the following year, later serving as sangi, Kebiishi bettō and provisional chūnagon. After the Jōkyū War of 1221 he was disciplined and suspended from court. He afterwards supported his half-sister Shōmeimon-in and her grandson Prince Kunihito, the future Emperor Go-Saga. Promoted to chūnagon in 1227 and dainagon in 1238, he founded the Nakanoin house, wrote a treatise on court ceremonial, and left ten poems in imperial anthologies including the Shinchokusen Wakashū.
zh: 中院通方（1189—1239）是镰仓时代前期的公卿，源通亲的第五子，中院家之祖。他于1211年任藏人头，次年跻身公卿，历任参议、检非违使别当、权中纳言。1221年承久之乱后受到处分，闭门谨慎。乱后他辅佐异父姐承明门院及其孙邦仁王，即后来的后嵯峨天皇。他于1227年任中纳言，1238年升大纳言，著有宫廷仪轨方面的著作；作为歌人，有十首作品收入《新敕撰和歌集》等敕撰和歌集。

en: Nanbu Hiroyuki was the seventh head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan, following Muneyuki and preceding Masatsura; a Nanbu genealogy preserved in Kai records him as the son of Nanbu Masayuki, though he was generally considered Masayuki's nephew.
zh: 南部祐行是三户南部氏第七代当主，继宗行之后、政连之前担任家督；通说以他为南部政行之侄，一份流传于甲斐的《南部氏系图》则将他记作政行之子。

en: Nanbu Masamitsu (1245–1265), childhood name Magojirō, was the fourth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan and the legitimate son of Nanbu Tokizane; the Nanbu genealogy records that he died in Kamakura in the seventh month of 1265, and his brother Munetsune succeeded him.
zh: 南部政光（1245—1265），幼名孙次郎，是三户南部氏第四代当主、南部时实的嫡男；《南部系谱》记载他于1265年七月在镰仓去世，其弟宗经继承了家督。

en: Nanbu Masanaga was a Southern Court warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars, the fourth son of Nanbu Masayuki. In 1333 he fought in Nitta Yoshisada's Kamakura campaign and received lands at Shichinohe in Nukanobu, Mutsu. He helped Kitabatake Akiie root out Hōjō remnants and later held Nejō Castle; after his brother Moroyuki fell at Ishizu in 1338 he inherited the family and repeatedly refused Ashikaga calls to surrender. Fighting beside Kitabatake Akinobu, he routed the Hienuki at Kanya in 1341 and received a sword and armor from Emperor Go-Murakami. He died in 1360, leaving Hachinohe to his grandson Nobumitsu.
zh: 南部政长是南北朝时代的南朝武将，南部政行第四子。1333年，他参加新田义贞的镰仓攻略之战，受封陆奥国糠部七户乡的领地。他协助北畠显家肃清北条残党，后来镇守根城；1338年其兄师行在石津战死后，他继承家督，屡次拒绝足利方的劝降。他与北畠显信并肩作战，1341年在栗屋河之战中重创稗贯氏，并获后村上天皇赐予太刀与铠甲。1360年他去世，将八户乡让给孙子南部信光。

en: Nanbu Masatsura was the eighth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan, following Hiroyuki and preceding Sukemasa.
zh: 南部政连是三户南部氏第八代当主，继祐行之后、祐政之前担任家督。

en: Nanbu Masayuki, also called Jirō Yukinaga, was a warrior of the mid-Kamakura period and the second son of Nanbu Tokizane, third head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan. Later genealogies name him as the ancestor of the Higashi clan and record that he married into the Kudō clan as a son-in-law, while Nanbu family documents make his wife a daughter of Nanbu Sanetsugu. His sons Tokinaga, Moroyuki, Masanaga and Sukeyuki later disputed the landed legacy of their grandfather Tokizane.
zh: 南部政行又称次郎行长，是镰仓时代中期的武士、三户南部氏第三代当主南部时实的次子。后世系谱称他为东氏之祖，并记载他以婿养子身份入赘工藤氏；南部家文书则称他的妻子是南部实继之女。他的儿子时长、师行、政长与资行，后来围绕祖父时实留下的领地发生争执。

en: Nanbu Masayuki (1328–1388) was the twelfth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan in the Nukanobu district of Mutsu province, succeeding his father, the eleventh head Nobunaga, although one genealogy makes him Nobunaga's adopted heir. A weak lord, he saw kinsmen usurp his estates. After the Kamakura shogunate fell he at first sided with the Southern Court, then dominant in Oshu under Kitabatake Akiie. One account says that in 1346 he accepted Ashikaga Takauji's overtures, joined the Northern Court, and fought Southern Court forces in Oshu to expand his power. He died in 1388 aged sixty-one, and his son Moroyuki succeeded.
zh: 南部政行（1328—1388）是陆奥国糠部郡三户南部氏的第12代当主，继父亲、第11代当主南部信长之后继位，也有系谱称他是信长的养子。他掌家无力，领地遭到同族侵占。镰仓幕府灭亡后，因北畠显家经略奥州的缘故，他起初依附南朝。另有一说称他于1346年接受足利尊氏的策反，转投北朝，与奥州的南朝势力交战以扩张势力。他于1388年去世，终年61岁，其子南部守行继位。

en: Nanbu Mitsuyuki (1165 – 1236?) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the founder of the Nanbu clan. The third son of Kagami Tōmitsu of the Seiwa Genji, he fought for Minamoto no Yoritomo at the Battle of Ishibashiyama in 1180 and was enfeoffed at the Nanbu lands in Kai Province, from which he took his family name. He accompanied Yoritomo to Kyoto in 1190 and afterwards resided in Kamakura. His six sons became ancestors of the Sannohe, Hachinohe, Shichinohe, Shinohe, Kunohe and Ichinohe branches. He was posthumously awarded Junior Third Rank.
zh: 南部光行（1165—1236年？）是镰仓时代前期的武将、南部氏的始祖，为清和源氏加贺美远光的第三子。1180年，他在石桥山之战中为源赖朝立下战功，受封甲斐国南部牧（今山梨县南部町一带），由此以南部为姓。1190年他随赖朝上洛，此后长住镰仓。他的六个儿子分别成为三户、八户、七户、四户、九户、一户诸家之祖。死后获赠从三位。

en: Nanbu Moroyuki was a Kamakura–Southern Court warrior, fourth head of the Hekii (Nejō) Nanbu branch and a son of Nanbu Masayuki. In 1333 he fought in Nitta Yoshisada's Kamakura campaign, then followed Kitabatake Akiie north to Mutsu, where he built Nejō Castle in Nukanobu, served as district governor and helped crush Hōjō remnants. In 1338 he marched on Kyoto with Akiie, winning at Aonogahara in Mino before both fell to Kō no Moronao at Ishizu in Izumi that fifth month.
zh: 南部师行是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的武将，波木井（根城）南部氏第四代当主，南部政行之子。1333年，他与兄弟随新田义贞攻打镰仓，继而跟随陆奥守北畠显家，奉义良亲王北上陆奥；他在糠部修筑根城、担任郡代，并参与镇压北条残党。1338年，他随显家进军京都，在美浓青野原获胜，同年5月在和泉国石津之战中与显家一同战死于高师直军前。

en: Nanbu Munetsugu was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō era, son of Nanbu Nagatsugu, head of the Hakii Nanbu branch in Kai. The Taiheiki shows him, styled Governor of Tōtōmi, campaigning for Ashikaga Takauji with his younger brother: at Tatarahama, at the storming of Enryakuji on Mount Hiei after Minatogawa in 1336, and at Shijōnawate in 1348 with Kō no Moronao, where Kusunoki Masatsura and his kinsman Nanbu Nobumasa of the Hachinohe branch fell. After Shijōnawate the chronicle writes his name as Minami; one theory equates him with the Muromachi councillor Minami Munetsugu, who died in 1371.
zh: 南部宗继是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，为甲斐国波木井南部氏首领南部长继之子。《太平记》载其自称南部远江守，与弟弟一同追随足利尊氏转战，参加过多多良滨之战、1336年凑川之战后攻打比叡山延历寺，以及1348年高师直军中的四条畷之战，楠木正行与他同族的八户南部氏的南部信政都在该役败死。四条畷之战后，《太平记》将其姓氏写作“南”；有异说认为他就是1371年去世的室町幕府重臣南宗继。

en: Nanbu Munetsune (1246–1283), childhood name Hikosaburō, was a warrior of the mid-Kamakura period and the fifth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan, the third son of the third head, Nanbu Tokizane. His brother Masamitsu, the fourth head, had no children and chose Yoshiyuki as his successor, but Yoshiyuki returned to Kai against Masamitsu's wishes, so Munetsune inherited the headship. Under him the clan's fortunes declined and it gave up its guard service in Kyoto and attendance at Kamakura. He died in 1283 aged 38.
zh: 南部宗经（1246—1283），幼名彦三郎，是镰仓时代中期的武士，据《南部系谱》为三户南部氏第五代当主、第三代当主南部时实的第三子。第四代当主、其兄政光因无子而选定义行为继承人，但义行违背政光的意向返回甲斐，宗经于是继承家督。在他当家期间家运衰落，家族停止了京都大番役和赴镰仓的参勤。他于1283年去世，享年38岁。

en: Nanbu Muneyuki was the sixth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan, following Nanbu Munetsune and preceding Nanbu Hiroyuki.
zh: 南部宗行是三户南部氏第六代当主，继南部宗经之后、南部祐行之前担任家督。

en: Nanbu Nagatsugu was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern Court period and the third head of the Hekii, later Nejō, Nanbu branch, son of Nanbu Sanetsugu. In 1327 the Kamakura shogunate sent him to Nukanobu in Mutsu to help crush the Andō revolt. In 1330 he went to Kyoto and served Prince Morinaga under Kusunoki Masashige; after the prince was killed in 1335, he took Buddhist orders as Hōtatsu and backed Morinaga's son Prince Okiyo. He is thought to have fallen fighting for Okiyo against the turncoat Akamatsu Norisuke at Mount Kabuto in Settsu in 1352.
zh: 南部长继是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武士，波木井（根城）南部氏第三代当主，南部实继之子。1327年，他受镰仓幕府之命前往陆奥国糠部，协助镇压安藤氏之乱。1330年他上洛，在楠木正成麾下侍奉护良亲王；1335年护良亲王遇害后，他出家取法号法达，转而拥戴亲王之子兴良亲王。1352年，兴良亲王在摄津国甲山山麓与倒戈的赤松则祐交战兵败，长继据传战死于此役。

en: Nanbu Nobumasa was a Southern Court warrior of the Nanboku-chō period, the son of Nanbu Masanaga and sixth head of the Nejō Nanbu. In the twelfth month of 1335 he accompanied Kitabatake Akiie's march on Kyoto as his uncle Moroyuki's deputy and fought with distinction. In 1345 Akinobu recommended him to a guards post at the Yoshino court, serving the imperial lady Tatchimon-in. He died before succeeding his father, and his son Nobumitsu became the next head. A later warrior chronicle makes him fall against Kō no Moronao at the battle of Shijōnawate in the first month of 1348.
zh: 南部信政是南北朝时代的南朝武将，南部政长之子，被列为根城南部氏第六代当主。1335年12月，他代伯父师行随从北畠显家上洛，在各处战斗中立功。1345年，经北畠显信推举，他出任吉野朝廷的右近藏人，侍奉达智门女院。他先于父亲去世而未能继承家督，后来由其子信光继为当主。据《东北太平记》记载，1348年1月他在四条畷之战中迎战高师直的军队，力战而死。

en: Nanbu Nobunaga was the eleventh head of the Sannohe Nanbu of Mutsu. In 1337 he brought Nanbu troops from Ise to join Kitabatake Akiie's second march on Kyoto, serving under Akiie's younger brother Akinobu at Otokoyama for the Southern Court.
zh: 南部信长是陆奥三户南部氏第十一代当主。1337年，他从伊势率军加入北畠显家第二次上洛的南朝大军，在男山隶属于显家之弟北畠显信麾下。

en: Nanbu Nobuyuki, also called Rokurō or Suketoki and later titled Satsuma no Kami, was a Southern Court warrior and a son of Nanbu Yoshiyuki. In 1319 he went with his brothers to Nukanobu. In 1333 he helped Hōjō Yasuie flee to Mutsu before joining his brothers on the imperial side, and in 1335 he marched west under Kitabatake Akiie. In early 1338 he attended the Yoshino court and was named Satsuma no Kami. In 1360 he was enfeoffed at Kuroishi and Medani in Tsugaru, and in 1363 he dedicated a bronze gong with a Southern Court date to Tendai-ji.
zh: 南部信行，又名六郎、祐时，官称萨摩守，是南朝武将，南部义行之子。1319年，他随兄长们前往糠部。1333年，他先助北条泰家逃往陆奥，随后与兄长们一同投身勤王；1335年他随北畠显家西上，1338年初谒见吉野行宫，被任命为萨摩守。1360年，他受封津轻的黑石乡与目谷乡；1363年，他向天台寺奉献一口刻有南朝年号的铜制鳄口。

en: Nanbu Sanemitsu (born 1181) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the second head of the Nanbu clan, succeeding as the second son of its founder Mitsuyuki. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he joined Hōjō Yasutoki's army and fought at the Uji River alongside the Takeda and Ogasawara. The Azuma Kagami records him serving as a guard when Shogun Fujiwara no Yoritsune went to Kyoto in 1238, and in 1252 attending the new shogun, Prince Munetaka, at Tsurugaoka Hachiman shrine together with his heir Tokizane.
zh: 南部实光（1181年生）是镰仓时代中期的御家人、南部氏第二代当主，为始祖光行的次子。1221年承久之乱时，他加入北条泰时的军队，与武田氏、小笠原氏等一同在宇治川作战。《吾妻镜》记载，1238年四代将军藤原赖经上洛时他担任随兵；1252年，他又与嫡子时实一同供奉新任将军宗尊亲王参诣鹤冈八幡宫。

en: Nanbu Sanenaga (1222–1297) was a gokenin of the mid-Kamakura period and the third son of Nanbu Mitsuyuki, who enfeoffed him with the Hakiri valley in Kai Province, where he served as jitō. In 1238 he and his elder brother Sanemitsu escorted Shogun Fujiwara no Yoritsune to Kyoto. Around 1269 he became a leading lay patron of the monk Nichiren, and in 1274 he welcomed the pardoned exile back to Hakiri and built his retreat on Mount Minobu. In 1281 he founded Kuon-ji temple and took vows as Nichien. His eldest son Sanetsugu's line became the Hachinohe Nanbu.
zh: 南部实长（1222—1297）是镰仓时代中期的御家人、南部光行的第三子，受封甲斐国波木井乡并担任地头。1238年，他与兄长实光一同随将军藤原赖经上洛。约1269年，他皈依僧人日莲，成为其重要檀越；1274年将遇赦归来的日莲迎入波木井，并在身延山为其建造草庵。1281年，他舍建久远寺并出家，号法寂院日圆。长子实继的后裔发展为以陆奥国为根基的八户氏，即根城南部氏。

en: Nanbu Sanetsugu (c. 1250–1332) was the second head of the Hakiri, or Nejime, Nanbu clan in the late Kamakura period, succeeding his father Sanenaga, Nichiren's lay patron. In 1282 he escorted the frail Nichiren from Mount Minobu to Ikegami, where the monk died. In 1331, already over seventy, he joined the Genkō War for Emperor Go-Daigo and held Akasaka Castle with Princes Morinaga and Takayoshi. Captured on the castle's fall, he was beheaded at Kyoto's Rokujō-gawara in the twelfth month of 1332, first of the rebels executed. His son Nagatsugu succeeded him.
zh: 南部实继（约1250—1332）是镰仓时代后期的武士，波木井南部氏（根城南部氏）第二代当主，继承了日莲檀越、其父实长的家业。1282年，他护送衰老的日莲自身延山下山前往池上，日莲最终在当地圆寂。1331年元弘之变时，年逾七旬的实继投身后醍醐天皇一方，随护良亲王、尊良亲王据守赤坂城。城池陷落后他被幕府军俘获，于1332年十二月在京都六条河原被斩首，是同批受刑者中最先就义之人。家督由其子长继继承。

en: Nanbu Shigetoki (1299–1333), counted in Nanbu genealogies as the clan's tenth head, was a late Kamakura-period warrior and, by family tradition, the second son of Nanbu Yoshiyuki. Born to a Hōjō mother, he won Regent Hōjō Takatoki's trust at Kamakura and in 1329 took Junior Fifth Rank as captain of the Right Stables. In 1333 he fought for the shogunate at Akasaka, Yoshino and Rokuhara. After the Hōjō defeat at Bubaigawara and the clan's suicide at Tōshō-ji, he broke out to Fujisawa and killed himself at Shōjōkō-ji. Iwate scholarship identifies him with the Hōjō Shigetoki of the Taiheiki.
zh: 南部茂时（1299—1333）是镰仓时代后期的武将，南部氏谱系称其为第十代当主，据家族传承为南部义行的次子。因母亲出身北条氏，他得到执权北条高时的信任，居于镰仓，1329年叙任从五位右马头。元弘之乱中，他站在幕府一方，1333年先后参战赤坂城、吉野城并救援六波罗。北条军在分倍河原战败、北条一族在东胜寺集体自尽后，他突围至藤泽，在清净光寺切腹自尽。《岩手县史》考证，他的经历或本于《太平记》所载的北条氏族人茂时。

en: Nanbu Sukemasa was the ninth head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan, following Masatsura and preceding the tenth head, Nanbu Shigetoki.
zh: 南部祐政是三户南部氏第九代当主，继政连之后、第十代当主南部茂时之前担任家督。

en: Nanbu Sukenaga was a Nanbu warrior of the Nanboku-chō era, identified in Nanbu genealogies as another name for Nanbu Shigeyuki, son of Nanbu Shigetoki. A 1360 record notes him receiving family lands in Tsugaru, Mutsu, though scholars question the identification.
zh: 南部祐长是南北朝时代的南部氏武将，南部氏家谱将其视为南部茂时之子南部茂行的别名。1360年的一份记录称他继承了陆奥国津轻的家族领地，但学者对这一身份比定存有疑问。

en: Nanbu Tameshige, also called Nakayuki and titled Sakon no Shōgen, was a Southern Court warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars, a figure in the confused early Nanbu genealogy who by one tradition was a son of Nanbu Yoshiyuki. In 1322 he helped storm Fujisaki Castle and subdue the rebel Andō Takitoyo. He marched west with Kitabatake Akiie in 1335 and again in 1337, and after the 1338 victory at Aonogahara was received with Akiie at the Yoshino court, where he was appointed Sakon no Shōgen. He then guarded Kazuno in the far north, earning Kitabatake Akinobu's praise for a victory there in 1345, and died in 1346.
zh: 南部为重，又名仲行，官称左近将监，是南北朝时代的南朝武将，在南部氏早期纷乱的谱系中身份不一，一说为南部义行之子。1322年，他参与攻陷藤崎城，降服反叛的安藤尧势。1335年、1337年他两度随北畠显家西上，1338年青野原获胜后随显家谒见吉野行宫，获任左近将监。此后他北返镇守糠部边地鹿角，1345年因征讨鹿角反贼有功获北畠显信嘉奖，1346年去世。

en: Nanbu Tokinaga was a warrior of the Kamakura–Southern Court period, legitimate son and heir of Nanbu Masayuki. As clan head he fought a long land lawsuit against his cousin Takeyuki and half-brother Sukeyuki, who used forged documents and backing from the Nagasaki, Hōjō house vassals. In 1333 he joined Emperor Go-Daigo with his brothers, fighting under Nitta Yoshisada in the storming of Kamakura; the Kenmu regime appointed him Kai no Kami. When Ashikaga Takauji rebelled he served the Southern Court with Yoshisada, and after the 1336 defeat at Minatogawa he vanished from the records.
zh: 南部时长是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的武士，南部政行的嫡男与继承人。继任家督后，他与堂弟武行、异母弟资行长期争讼领地，对方伪造文书，并依仗北条得宗被官长崎氏的势力。1333年，他与弟弟们投奔后醍醐天皇，随新田义贞参与攻陷镰仓；建武政权任命他为甲斐守。足利尊氏反叛后，他追随义贞效力南朝，1336年凑川之战失败后便从史料中消失。

en: Nanbu Tokizane was the third head of the Sannohe Nanbu clan in Kai Province and the legitimate heir of the second head, Nanbu Sanemitsu. The Azuma Kagami records that in 1252 father and son served together as attendants when the new shogun, Prince Munetaka, worshipped at Tsurugaoka Hachimangū in Kamakura. His sons included Masamitsu, who succeeded as fourth head, Munetsune and Masayuki. In later years his grandsons fought over his landed legacy.
zh: 南部时实是甲斐国三户南部氏第三代当主、第二代当主南部实光的嫡子。《吾妻镜》记载，1252年新任将军宗尊亲王参拜镰仓鹤冈八幡宫时，他与父亲一同担任供奉人。他的儿子有政光、宗经、政行等，其中政光继任第四代当主。多年以后，他的诸孙曾围绕其遗留的领地发生争执。

en: Nanbu Yoshimoto was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and the first head of the Kai branch of the Nanbu clan. The fifth son of Nanbu Tokizane, third head of the main Nanbu line, he was enfeoffed by his father with the Nanbu-no-shō estate in Kai Province and established his own house there. During the Genkō War, Nitta Yoshisada rose in 1333 at Prince Morinaga's call and the Hōjō regime fell, whereupon Yoshimoto returned to Kai. His heir Yoshiyuki succeeded him as second head of the Kai Nanbu.
zh: 南部义元是镰仓时代后期的武将，甲斐南部氏初代当主。他是南部氏宗家第三代当主南部时实的第五子，受父亲分封甲斐国南部庄，在当地开创家门。元弘之乱中，新田义贞于1333年奉护良亲王的令旨举兵，北条政权覆灭，义元于是返回甲斐。嫡子义行继他之后担任甲斐南部氏第二代当主。

en: Nanbu Yoshiyuki was a warrior of the late Kamakura period and the second head of the Kai Nanbu branch, based at Nambu-no-shō in Kai Province. The legitimate son of branch founder Nanbu Yoshimoto, he was chosen as successor by Nanbu Masamitsu, fourth head of the main Nanbu line, but returned to Kai against that decision. In the fifth month of 1333 he marched with the Hōjō army sent to stop Nitta Yoshisada's advance on Kamakura and fought at Bubaigawara in Musashi, where the Hōjō forces were routed, opening the way for the fall of the Kamakura shogunate.
zh: 南部义行是镰仓时代后期的武将，甲斐南部氏第二代当主，本据在甲斐国南部庄。他是初代当主南部义元的嫡男，曾被宗家第四代当主南部政光定为继承人，却违背其安排返回甲斐。1333年（正庆二年）5月，他随北条军出征，在武藏国分倍河原迎战进攻镰仓的新田义贞军，北条军全线溃败，镰仓幕府随后灭亡。

en: Prince Nariyoshi (1326–1338 or 1344) was a son of Emperor Go-Daigo by Ano Renshi, younger brother of Prince Tsuneyoshi. In 1334 he was made head of the Kamakura shogun office and sent east with Ashikaga Tadayoshi to govern Kantō. He returned to Kyoto during the Nakasendai War of 1335 and was briefly appointed seii taishōgun. In 1336 Takauji named him crown prince under his Northern Court puppet Emperor Kōmyō, then deposed him. The Taiheiki says he was poisoned with Tsuneyoshi in 1338, though Moromori-ki records a son of Go-Daigo and former crown prince dying in 1344, which may instead refer to him.
zh: 成良亲王（1326—1338或1344）是后醍醐天皇与阿野廉子之子，恒良亲王的同母弟。1334年，他被任命为镰仓将军府将军，由足利直义奉送东下镰仓，负责治理关东。1335年中先代之乱时他回到京都，一度被任命为征夷大将军。1336年足利尊氏把他立为北朝傀儡光明天皇的皇太子，随后又将他废黜。《太平记》说他1338年与恒良一同被毒杀；但《师守记》载1344年有一位后醍醐天皇的皇子、前皇太子去世，也可能就是他。

en: Nasu no Mitsusuke was a Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin, the fifth head of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke and a son of Yorisuke. In 1193 he received estates in Shimotsuke from Shogun Minamoto no Yoritomo and served as host when Yoritomo held his grand hunt at Nasu; he worked to strengthen his house's position among the shogunate's vassals. The Azuma Kagami names Nasu Tarō Mitsusuke in its accounts from around the time of the hunt. In 1199 he founded the temple Tenshōji within his domains.
zh: 那须光资是镰仓时代武士、御家人，下野国那须氏第五代当主，四代当主赖资之子。1193年，他从源赖朝处获赐下野国内的领地，并在赖朝到那须举行卷狩时担任接待役，致力于提高那须氏作为幕府御家人的地位。《吾妻镜》在卷狩前后的记载中出现“那须太郎光助”之名。1199年，他在领地内创建天性寺。

en: Nasu no Sukefuji (died 1355) was the ninth head of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke Province, succeeding his father Suketada. During the wars of the Northern and Southern Courts he took the Northern Court side, and in the Kannō Disturbance from 1349 he campaigned for Ashikaga Takauji. In 1355 he was killed fighting Ashikaga Tadafuyu, together with his younger brother Ashino Sukekata, founder of the Ashino clan. His son Sukesuyo succeeded him as family head; the Kanamaru, Kanae and Kotaki houses branched from Sukefuji's line.
zh: 那须资藤（?—1355）为下野国那须氏第九代当主，父为第八代当主那须资忠。南北朝动乱时他依附北朝，在1349年起的观应扰乱中随足利尊氏转战。1355年，他在与足利直冬的作战中，与弟弟芦野资方（芦野氏之祖）等人一同战死。家督由其子资世继承；资藤的子孙分出金丸氏、金枝氏、小泷氏等支流。

en: Nasu no Sukeie was a Kamakura warrior, Sukemura's son and, in clan genealogy, seventh head of the Nasu of Shimotsuke and provisional governor of Kaga. One modern theory holds that the headship was restored in his generation through Hōjō Tokusō ties.
zh: 那须资家是镰仓时代武士，按那须氏系图为下野国那须氏第七代当主、资村之子，官称加贺权守。近年有一说认为，到他这一代，那须氏凭借与北条得宗家的关系恢复了家督。

en: Nasu no Sukemura was a Kamakura-period warrior and the sixth head of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke, born the son of Mitsusuke. He embraced Pure Land nenbutsu teaching, became a disciple of the monk Shinran, and took the clerical name Shinganbō Kyōnen; in 1223 he founded Jigan-ji in the Nasu lands. Genealogies credit him with a long life of seventy-eight years. A modern theory holds that he never held the headship, which passed to his uncle Sukenaga's Iōno line and was recovered only under his son Sukeie through ties with the Hōjō Tokusō house.
zh: 那须资村是镰仓时代武士、下野国那须氏第六代当主，五代当主光资之子。他皈依念佛宗，成为亲鸾上人的弟子，号信愿房教念，并于1223年创建慈愿寺，相传享寿78岁。不过近年有异说认为，光资之后家督由其弟伊王野资长一系承袭，资村并未继任；直到其子资家一代，才凭借与北条得宗家的关系恢复家督。

en: Nasu no Suketada was the eighth head of the Nasu warrior clan of Shimotsuke Province, titled Aki no kami. Genealogies call him the restorer of the Nasu. His son Sukefuji became the ninth head, and his fourth son Sukekata founded the Ashino branch.
zh: 那须资忠是下野国那须武士家族的第八代当主，官至安艺守，家谱称其为那须氏的“中兴”之主。其子资藤继任第九代当主，第四子资方开创了支流芦野氏。

en: Nasu no Suketaka was a warrior of the late Heian period and, in clan tradition, the first head of the Nasu of Shimotsuke Province; his father was Sudō Munesuke. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose against the Taira in Izu in 1180, only two of Suketaka's many sons, Tametaka and the celebrated Yoichi, joined the Minamoto, while his other nine sons sided with the Taira. His sons founded Nasu branch houses such as Fukuhara and Senbon, and his fifth son Sukeyuki followed Yoichi as clan head.
zh: 那须资隆是平安时代后期的武士，按那须氏系图为下野国那须氏初代当主，须藤宗资之子、那须与一之父。1180年源赖朝在伊豆举兵反抗平氏时，他的众多儿子中只有十郎为隆和与一投奔源氏，其余九子都依附平氏。诸子分别成为那须各支族之祖，如福原氏、千本氏，五男资之在与一之后继任当主。

en: Nasu no Sukeyuki was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and the third head of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke, the fifth son of its founder Suketaka. When the Genpei War broke out in 1180, he at first backed the Taira like most of his brothers, but later submitted to the Minamoto and received lands from his younger brother Yoichi, who had inherited the clan. When Yoichi took monastic vows without an heir, Sukeyuki succeeded him. With no available son of his own, he married his daughter to Yorisuke and made him the next clan head.
zh: 那须资之是平安末期至镰仓初期的武将、下野国那须氏第三代当主，初代当主资隆的五男。1180年源平合战爆发，他与多数兄长起初依附平氏，后来归顺源氏，从已继承家督的弟弟与一处受领领地。与一无子出家后，资之继任当主。他没有合适的儿子继承家督，便将女儿嫁给赖资，由赖资继承家督。

en: Nasu no Yoichi (c. 1169–c. 1189) was a warrior of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke Province, famed through the war tale Heike Monogatari. It relates that he fought under Minamoto no Yoshitsune in the Genpei War and at the Battle of Yashima in 1185 rode into the sea to shoot down the fan target raised on a Taira warship, earning manors in five provinces from Yoritomo. Though the eleventh son, he succeeded as clan head after nine of his brothers joined the Taira and another, Tametaka, incurred punishment. He is said to have pardoned and enfeoffed his brothers.
zh: 那须与一（约1169—约1189）是下野国那须氏武将，因军记物语《平家物语》中“扇靶”的故事闻名。据《平家物语》记载，源平合战中他随源义经作战，1185年屋岛之战时策马入海，一箭射落平氏战船上升起的扇靶，因此被源赖朝赐予五国庄园。他虽是第十一子，但因九位兄长投靠平氏，另一位兄长为隆后来获罪，遂继承家督。相传他后来赦免流亡各地的兄长并分给领地。

en: Nasu no Yorisuke was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and the fourth head of the Nasu clan of Shimotsuke. Genealogies make him a son of the Kamakura gokenin Utsunomiya no Tomotsuna, adopted as heir by the third head Sukeyuki, though one tradition calls him an illegitimate son of the founder Suketaka. His name bears the character yori granted at his coming-of-age by his sponsor Minamoto no Yoritomo. If the genealogical order of succession is correct, his tenure may have been short: at Yoritomo's Nasu hunt in 1193, his son Mitsusuke had already succeeded. Another son, Sukenaga, founded the Iōno branch house.
zh: 那须赖资是平安末期至镰仓初期的武将、下野国那须氏第四代当主。系图多称他是镰仓幕府有力御家人宇都宫朝纲之子，被三代当主资之收为养子、立为继承人；也有说法认为他是初代当主资隆的庶子。其名中的“赖”字，相传来自乌帽子亲源赖朝赐予的偏讳。若系图所载继承顺序无误，他在任时间可能很短：1193年源赖朝到那须举行卷狩时，其子光资已经继任当主。另一子资长是后来那须七骑之一伊王野氏的始祖。

en: Nawa Akinaga, a son of Nawa Motonaga, was a Southern Court warrior in Kyushu. In 1364 he served in the allied Nawa and Kikuchi army that defeated Ōuchi Hiroyo's invasion of Buzen, forcing him to retreat to Mount Kaharu.
zh: 名和显长是名和基长之子、九州的南朝方武将。1364年，他在名和氏与菊池氏的联军中作战，击败入侵丰前的大内弘世，迫使其退往香春岳。

en: Nawa Akioki, son of Nawa Motonaga, was a Southern Court warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts era. After Nawa Nagatoshi and his heir Yoshitaka were killed fighting Ashikaga Takauji and the clan broke, Akioki was adopted as Yoshitaka's heir and withdrew to Higo Province under Kikuchi Takemitsu. He settled at Yatsushiro, building Hatchōdake Castle and holding Furumoto Castle, and with the Kikuchi formed the core of the Southern Court cause in Kyushu, taking Ashikita district from the Sagara. He resisted the Kyushu tandai Imagawa Ryōshun until 1391, when Furumoto was besieged and he surrendered, his lands confirmed.
zh: 名和显兴是南北朝时代的南朝方武将，名和基长之子。名和长年与其嫡子义高在和足利尊氏的交战中战死后，名和一族没落，显兴作为义高的养子继承家督，投奔菊池武光，南下肥后国。他在八代定居，修筑八丁岳城，以古麓城为据点，与菊池氏同为南朝在九州的核心力量，并从相良氏手中夺取苇北郡。他长期抵抗九州探题今川了俊，至1391年古麓城被围后出降，所领得到安堵。

en: Nawa Motonaga, second son of Nawa Nagatoshi, was a warrior across the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts years. In 1333, after Emperor Go-Daigo escaped his exile on Oki, Motonaga and his clan welcomed the emperor at Mount Senjō in Hōki Province and rose against the Kamakura shogunate, defeating the shogunate's punitive commander Enya Takasada in battle. His sons included Akioki, Akinaga and Yasuoki. Known as Magosaburō and titled Saemon-no-jō, he took the Buddhist name Shin'a and is said to have later entered religion on Mount Kōya.
zh: 名和基长是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武士，名和长年的次子。1333年后醍醐天皇逃出隐岐的流放地后，基长与一族在伯耆国船上山迎驾，举兵反抗镰仓幕府，并在交战中击败幕府追讨军将领盐冶高贞。他的儿子有显兴、显长、泰兴。基长通称孙三郎，官任左卫门尉，法名心阿，相传后来登上高野山出家为僧。

en: Nawa Nagatoshi (c. 1250 – 7 August 1336) was head of the wealthy Nawa shipping clan of Hōki Province. In 1333, when Emperor Go-Daigo escaped exile on Oki, Nagatoshi welcomed him to Mount Senjō and fought the Kamakura shogunate's forces there. Under the Kenmu Restoration he was made governor of Hōki and ranked among the emperor's closest generals, the Three Trees and One Grass. He opposed Ashikaga Takauji and helped arrest Prince Morinaga. After the imperial defeat at Minatogawa, he was killed fighting Takauji's troops in Kyoto on 7 August 1336.
zh: 名和长年（约1250—1336年8月7日）是伯耆国富甲一方、经营海运的名和氏当主。1333年后醍醐天皇从隐岐配所逃出，长年将天皇迎至船上山，并在此迎战镰仓幕府的军队。建武新政时，他被任命为伯耆守，位列天皇最亲信的“三木一草”。他与足利尊氏对立，曾参与拘捕护良亲王。1336年宫方在凑川战败后，他于8月7日在京都与尊氏军队作战时战死。

en: Nawa Yasuoki was a son of Nawa Motonaga and a grandson of the Southern Court warrior Nawa Nagatoshi; Akinaga was among his brothers.
zh: 名和泰兴是名和基长之子、南朝武将名和长年之孙，显长是他的兄弟。

en: Nawa Yoshitaka (1302–1338) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts period and the eldest son of Nawa Nagatoshi, lord of Nawa in Hōki Province. He fought beside his father at Mount Senjō in 1333 helping Emperor Go-Daigo escape exile on Oki, and entered Kyoto with the imperial army. Under the Kenmu government he served in the Mushadokoro and in 1334 received the stewardship of Yatsushiro manor in Higo, donating lands there to the Kitsuki and Kumano shrines. When Ashikaga Takauji rebelled he served under Kitabatake Akiie and fell at the Battle of Sakaiura on 10 June 1338.
zh: 名和义高（1302—1338）为南北朝时代武士，是伯耆国名和领主名和长年的长子。1333年，他随父亲参加船上山之战，协助后醍醐天皇逃出隐岐，并随天皇的军队进入京都。建武政权成立后，他在武者所任职，1334年受领肥后国八代庄的地头职，并把八代庄的部分领地捐赠给杵筑大社和熊野神社。足利尊氏反叛后，他随北畠显家迎战足利军，于1338年6月10日在堺浦之战中战死。

en: Nawa no Yukitaka was head of the Nawa clan, a shipping family based at Nawa in Hōki Province. He was father of Nawa Nagatoshi, the Southern Court general who served Emperor Go-Daigo. A retreat Nagatoshi built for his sixtieth birthday later became the temple Chōkō-ji.
zh: 名和行高是伯耆国名和庄经营海运的名和氏当主，也是后来效忠后醍醐天皇的南朝武将名和长年之父。长年为庆祝他的还历而建的隐居所，后来改为长纲寺。

en: Niiro Sanehisa was a Nanboku-chō-period warrior and the second head of the Niiro family, Shimazu retainers in Hyūga, and the second son of its founder Niiro Tokihisa. In 1357, after the Southern Court partisan Nirei Yorichika killed himself at Matsuo castle in Shibushi, Sanehisa occupied it and, together with Shimazu Ujihisa, repelled an invasion by Hatakeyama Naoaki. He then helped Ujihisa administer Ōsumi province. In 1379 he led the left wing under Ujihisa at the Battle of Minohara against the Kyūshū deputy Imagawa Ryōshun, using the Tsuki-ikki formation to defeat a larger army; the formation became a standard Shimazu tactic.
zh: 新纳实久是日本南北朝时代的武将，日向岛津氏的家臣、新纳氏第二代当主，为初代当主新纳时久的次子。1357年，在志布志松尾城举兵的南朝方武将榆井赖仲自刃之后，实久进驻该城；同年他遭到畠山直显进攻，与后来成为岛津氏第六代当主的岛津氏久合力将其击退，此后协助氏久经营大隅国。1379年氏久与九州探题今川了俊交战，实久在氏久指挥下统领左翼，以“月一揆”阵势击破兵力占优的今川军，是为蓑原之战；这一阵势后来成为岛津家的基本战术。

en: Niiro Tokihisa was a Nanboku-chō-period warrior and the first head of the Niiro family, the fourth son of Shimazu Tadamune, head of the Shimazu of Satsuma. In 1335 he was made jitō, or land steward, of Niiro-in in Koyu district, Hyūga province, entered Takajō and took the name Niiro. In the war between Emperor Go-Daigo and Ashikaga Takauji he followed the main Shimazu house onto Takauji's side. In 1349 he joined the faction of Takauji's brother Tadayoshi and received Kuni-in in Hyūga, but in 1350 Takajō fell to Hatakeyama Naoaki's attack and he moved his base to Kuni-in.
zh: 新纳时久是日本南北朝时代的武将，新纳氏初代当主，为萨摩岛津氏第四代当主岛津忠宗的第四子。1335年，他被任命为日向国儿汤郡新纳院的地头，进入高城，遂以新纳为氏。后醍醐天皇与足利尊氏交兵时，他随岛津本家站在尊氏一方。1349年，他转投尊氏之弟足利直义一派，受领日向的救仁院；但1350年高城在畠山直显的攻打下陷落，他把据点移往救仁院。

en: Nijō (1143–1165) was the eldest son of Emperor Go-Shirakawa, who abdicated in his favour in 1158 and kept ruling as cloistered emperor. The Heiji Disturbance of 1159–1160 marked his early reign. Nijō built his own power on the grand minister Fujiwara no Koremichi and Taira no Kiyomori, whom he made commander of the capital police. In 1161 he foiled a plot to name the infant Norihito crown prince, purged his father's aides and ruled in person, continuing Shinzei's reforms. Gravely ill in 1165, he named his son Nobuhito heir, abdicated, and died weeks later at twenty-two.
zh: 二条天皇（1143—1165）是后白河天皇的长子，1158年父亲让位给他后以上皇身份继续执政，1159至1160年的平治之乱就发生在他在位初年。他依靠太政大臣藤原伊通与平清盛巩固权力，任命清盛为检非违使别当，掌管京城治安。1161年，他挫败立襁褓中的宪仁亲王为太子的图谋，罢免后白河上皇的近臣，停止上皇干政，亲自执政，延续信西的改革。1165年他病重，立儿子顺仁亲王为太子并于当日让位，数周后去世，年仅二十二岁。

en: Nikaidō Moritsuna was a Kamakura-period gokenin, son of Administrative Board steward Nikaidō Yukitsuna and father of Nikaidō Tokitsuna. He held the post of governor of Ise Province and in 1295 joined the shogunate's Council of State, later taking Buddhist vows with the Dharma name Gyōshin.
zh: 二阶堂盛纲是镰仓时代的御家人，为政所执事二阶堂行纲之子、二阶堂时纲之父。他曾任伊势守，1295年出任镰仓幕府评定众，后出家，法名行真。

en: Nikaidō Sadafuji (1267–1335), known by his Dharma name Dōun, was a Kamakura gokenin, Administrative Board steward and shugo of Kai Province. Son of Nikaidō Yukifuji, he held the Maki estate in Kai, where he invited Zen master Musō Soseki to restore Jōkyōji in 1305 and found Erin-ji in 1330. In 1331 he went to Kyoto to press Emperor Go-Daigo's abdication and joined the siege of Chihaya Castle, and in 1332 he served as steward assisting Hōjō Takatoki. Pardoned after the shogunate fell, he joined the Kenmu regime but was executed in 1335 for Saionji Kinmune's Hōjō-restoration plot.
zh: 二阶堂贞藤（1267—1335），法名道蕴，是镰仓时代后期的御家人，曾任政所执事、甲斐守护。他是二阶堂行藤之子，领有甲斐国山梨郡牧庄，于1305年从镰仓请来禅僧梦窗疎石重兴净居寺，1330年又在甲斐创立惠林寺。1331年，他作为使者上洛敦促后醍醐天皇让位，并参加了攻打千早城的战役；1332年担任政所执事，辅佐北条高时。镰仓幕府灭亡后他一度获赦，加入建武政权，却因卷入西园寺公宗复兴北条氏的阴谋，于1335年在六条河原被处死。

en: Nikaidō Sadahira (1291–1332) was a late Kamakura gokenin and head steward of the shogunate's Administrative Board. The son of Nikaidō Yukisada, he received a character of his name from Regent Hōjō Sadatoki. He took Buddhist vows in 1326, styling himself Gyōe, and in the fifth month of 1329 he succeeded his late father as Administrative Board steward. He held the post only briefly, dying in the first month of 1332 at the age of 42. His son Yukinao later served the Muromachi shogunate in the same office.
zh: 二阶堂贞衡（1291—1332）是镰仓时代后期的御家人，曾任镰仓幕府政所执事。他是二阶堂行贞之子，由第九代执权北条贞时赐以偏讳。1326年出家，法号行惠；1329年5月继任亡父的政所执事之职。他在任不久，于1332年1月去世，终年42岁。其子行直后来在室町幕府也担任政所执事。

en: Nikaidō Sadatsuna was a Kamakura-period gokenin, son of Administrative Board steward Nikaidō Yoritsuna and father of Nikaidō Yukitomo. He served as governor of Shimōsa Province and lieutenant of the Left Gate Guards.
zh: 二阶堂贞纲是镰仓时代的御家人，为政所执事二阶堂赖纲之子、二阶堂行朝之父，曾任下总守、左卫门尉。

en: Nikaidō Tokitsuna (born c. 1280) was a samurai administrator of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, the son of Nikaidō Moritsuna. He first served on the Kamakura shogunate's Council of State, then took Buddhist vows in 1311 under the name Gyōin. In 1333 the Kenmu Restoration named him the first head of the Administrative Board of the Kamakura governor's office, and the Muromachi shogunate reappointed him to that post four times between 1346 and 1350. During the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi. His daughter became the wife of Sasaki Dōyō.
zh: 二阶堂时纲（约1280年生）是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武士行政官僚，二阶堂盛纲之子。他原任镰仓幕府评定众，1311年出家，法名行諲。1333年建武新政时，他被任命为镰仓将军府（后来的镰仓府）首任政所执事；室町幕府时期又于1346年至1350年间四度出任该职。观应之扰乱中，他站在足利直义一方。其女儿嫁给了佐佐木道誉。

en: Nikaidō Yoritsuna (1239–1283) was a Kamakura-period gokenin and head steward of the shogunate's Administrative Board. The second son of Nikaidō Yukitsuna, he became heir after his elder brother died young. Named a police commissioner in 1269 and governor of Shimōsa Province in 1274, he joined the Board of Adjudicants in 1275 and in 1278 went to Izu with Councillor Miyoshi Michitsuna to suppress a rising by monks of the Izu Gongen shrine. He succeeded his father as steward in 1281 and joined the Council of State in 1282, but died in 1283 aged 45; his uncle Yukitada succeeded him.
zh: 二阶堂赖纲（1239—1283）是镰仓时代的御家人，曾任镰仓幕府政所执事。他是政所执事二阶堂行纲的次男，因长兄夭折而作为嫡男长大。1269年任检非违使，1274年任下总守，1275年加入引付众。1278年伊豆权现的僧徒发起争乱，他与评定众三善伦经一同前往伊豆镇抚。1281年父亲去世后他继任政所执事，1282年成为评定众。1283年去世，终年45岁，由叔父行忠继任。

en: Nikaidō Yukiari (1220–1292), second son of Nikaidō Yukiyoshi, was a Kamakura shogunate samurai. By 1258 he had become a police commissioner, but served chiefly in Kamakura as a close attendant to three successive shoguns sent from Kyoto, Yoritsune, Yoritsugu and Prince Munetaka, escorting them on shrine pilgrimages. When Yoritsugu was deposed in 1252 and returned to Kyoto, Yukiari oversaw the journey. A skilled mounted archer, he joined the Board of Adjudication in 1265 and the Council of State in 1270, taking Buddhist vows the same year. In 1272 he was named confirmations commissioner, and he died in 1292.
zh: 二阶堂行有（1220—1292）是二阶堂行义的次子，镰仓幕府武士。到1258年他已担任检非违使，但主要活动在镰仓，作为近习侍奉从京都迎来的三位将军——藤原赖经、藤原赖嗣和宗尊亲王，随侍他们参拜神社。1252年赖嗣被废返回京都时，由他负责沿途奉行事务。他擅长流镝马骑射，1265年出任引付众，1270年列名评定众，同年出家，法号道证。1272年被任命为安堵奉行，1292年去世。

en: Nikaidō Yukifuji (1246–1302) was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nikaidō house's Oki branch who rose to become head steward of the shogunate's Administrative Board. After joining the Board of Adjudicants in 1282 and serving as governor of Dewa Province from 1288, he was made steward in 1293 in place of the dismissed Nikaidō Yukisada. He went to Kyoto as the shogunate's envoy in 1294 and again in 1301, when he pressed Emperor Go-Fushimi to abdicate in favor of Emperor Go-Nijō. He died in 1302 aged 57, after which Yukisada returned to the stewardship.
zh: 二阶堂行藤（1246—1302）是镰仓时代中期二阶堂氏隐岐流的武士，官至镰仓幕府政所执事。他于1282年成为引付众，1288年任出羽守，1293年接替被罢免的二阶堂行贞就任政所执事。他曾于1294年作为东使上洛，又于1301年作为东使进京，向后伏见天皇奏请让位，天皇最终让位给后二条天皇。1302年去世，终年57岁，死后行贞复任政所执事。

en: Nikaidō Yukimasa (c. 1140 – after 1219) was a court official and a chief civilian administrator of the early Kamakura shogunate, ancestor of the Nikaidō house. Entering Yoritomo's service around 1184, he served as a yorihito in the new records office under Ōe no Hiromoto and in 1189 handled paperwork for the Ōshū campaign. In 1191 he became deputy head of the Mandokoro under Ōe no Hiromoto, rising to the fifth rank and co-head in 1193. In 1199 he was named among the thirteen councilors governing after Yoritomo's death. His signatures vanish from documents under Sanetomo, and his death date is unrecorded.
zh: 二阶堂行政（约1140—1219年后）是平安末期至镰仓初期的官人、镰仓幕府的核心文官，二阶堂氏的始祖。他约在1184年前后出仕源赖朝，在新设的公文所任寄人，供职于大江广元之下，1189年承办奥州合战相关的文书事务。1191年他在大江广元之下任政所令，1193年叙五位、升为政所别当，辅佐广元。1199年，他入选赖朝去世后裁决政务的“十三人合议制”。到源实朝任将军时期，他的署名从政所文书中消失，卒年不详。

en: Nikaidō Yukimitsu (1164–1219), son of Nikaidō Yukimasa and younger brother of Yukimura, was a Kamakura shogunate vassal who became chief steward of the Administrative Board, serving under Hōjō Yoshitoki. As governor of Shinano Province and a trusted aide to the nun-shogun Hōjō Masako, he directed the shogunate's daily administration and its dealings with the Kyoto court. After Shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo was assassinated early in 1219, Masako sent him to Kyoto to seek a son of Retired Emperor Go-Toba as shogun, but Go-Toba refused. He died later that year; his son Yukimori eventually inherited the stewardship.
zh: 二阶堂行光（1164—1219）是二阶堂行政之子、行村之弟，身为镰仓幕府御家人，升任政所执事，在北条义时之下掌管政所实务。他官至信浓守，作为“尼将军”北条政子的心腹部下，主持幕府日常行政，并负责与京都朝廷的交涉。1219年初源实朝遇刺后，政子派他前往京都，请求迎接后鸟羽上皇之子出任将军，遭到后鸟羽上皇拒绝。他于同年去世，其子行盛后来世袭了政所执事一职。

en: Nikaidō Yukimori (1181–1253) was a Kamakura shogunate vassal and the son of Nikaidō Yukimitsu. After his father's death in 1219 the stewardship of the Administrative Board passed to his cousin Iga Mitsumune; when Mitsumune was exiled in the Iga incident of 1224, Yukimori succeeded to the post. He took Buddhist vows in 1225, taking the name Gyōnen, but kept his office rather than retire. He remained chief steward of the board and a member of the Council of State until he died in 1253, founding a line that held the stewardship hereditarily after him.
zh: 二阶堂行盛（1181—1253）是镰仓幕府御家人、二阶堂行光之子。1219年父亲去世后，政所执事由堂兄伊贺光宗继任；1224年光宗在伊贺氏事件中被流放，行盛遂接任此职。1225年他出家，法名行然，但并未退出政务。他一直担任政所执事兼评定众，直到1253年去世，开启了其家族此后世袭政所执事的传统。

en: Nikaidō Yukimune was a Kamakura-period gokenin, heir of Administrative Board steward Nikaidō Yukitada and father of Nikaidō Yukisada. He served on the shogunate's Board of Adjudicants but died in 1286, before his father; when Yukitada died in 1290 the stewardship passed to Yukisada, aged 22.
zh: 二阶堂行宗是镰仓时代二阶堂家的御家人，为政所执事二阶堂行忠的嫡子、二阶堂行贞之父。他官至幕府引付众，却于1286年先于父亲去世，因此1290年行忠死后，政所执事之职由其子行贞以22岁之龄继任。

en: Nikaidō Yukimura (1155–1238), son of Nikaidō Yukimasa, was a samurai official of the early Kamakura shogunate. After serving as police commissioner in Kyoto, he became an investigating magistrate of the Board of Retainers in Kamakura. In 1213 he held military command on the Hōjō side in the Wada War and received the Ōi estate in Sagami Province. Named governor of Oki Province in 1218, he took Buddhist vows after Shogun Sanetomo was slain at Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine the next year. Joining the Council of State in 1225, he died in 1238 at the Masuda estate in Ise Province.
zh: 二阶堂行村（1155—1238）是二阶堂行政之子，镰仓幕府初期的武士文官。他曾在京都担任检非违使，后来到镰仓出任侍所检断奉行。1213年和田合战中，他在北条一方担任军奉行，因战功获封相模国大井庄。1218年他出任隐岐守；翌年源实朝在鹤冈八幡宫拜贺时遇刺，他随即出家，法号行西。1225年起担任评定众，1238年在其担任地头的伊势国益田庄去世。

en: Nikaidō Yukinao (died 2 July 1348), originally named Takahira, was a Nanbokuchō-era samurai, the son of Nikaidō Sadahira. In 1340 he succeeded Nikaidō Yukitomo as head of the Administrative Board, the Muromachi shogunate's chief civil office, and held the post until 1346. His legitimate son was Nikaidō Ujisada, but after Yukinao's death the family's position passed to his younger brother Yukimoto.
zh: 二阶堂行直（？—1348年7月2日），旧名高衡，是南北朝时代的武士，二阶堂贞衡之子。1340年，他接替二阶堂行朝出任室町幕府政所执事，即幕府的最高民政官职，一直任至1346年。他有嫡子二阶堂氏贞，但在他死后，家族的地位传给了弟弟行元。

en: Nikaidō Yukisada (1269–1329) was a late Kamakura gokenin who twice served as head steward of the shogunate's Administrative Board. Son of Nikaidō Yukimune, he succeeded his grandfather Yukitada in 1290 at age 22. In 1293 Hōjō Sadatoki killed Taira no Yoritsuna and overturned appointments from his time; Yukisada was dismissed that year and replaced by Nikaidō Yukifuji of the rival Oki branch. He took Buddhist vows in 1301 and was restored after Yukifuji's death in 1302, holding the post until he died. Regarded as one of the compilers of the Azuma Kagami, he died in 1329 aged 61 and was succeeded by his son Sadahira.
zh: 二阶堂行贞（1269—1329）是镰仓时代后期的御家人，曾两度担任镰仓幕府政所执事。他是二阶堂行宗之子，1290年祖父行忠死后以22岁之龄继任政所执事。1293年北条贞时诛杀平赖纲，推翻其当权时期的人事安排；行贞同年被罢免，由隐岐流的二阶堂行藤接任。1301年他出家；1302年行藤死后复职，一直任职到去世。他被视为《吾妻镜》的编纂者之一，1329年去世，终年61岁，由嫡子贞衡继任。

en: Nikaidō Yukitada (1221–1290), a son of Nikaidō Yukimori, was a veteran councillor of the Kamakura shogunate. He took Buddhist vows in 1256 after the regent Hōjō Tokiyori retired, and later sat on the Council of State. After his brother Yukitsuna died in 1281, the chief stewardship of the Administrative Board passed to Yukitsuna's son Yoritsuna, who died within two years. Yukitada, already sixty-three, then took the post himself. His son Yukimune died before him, and his grandson Yukisada also held the stewardship. Yukitada died in 1290.
zh: 二阶堂行忠（1221—1290）是二阶堂行盛之子，镰仓幕府的资深评议官员。1256年执权北条时赖出家后，他也随之出家，后来担任评定众。其兄行纲1281年去世后，政所执事传给行纲之子赖纲，但赖纲不到两年便死去；已63岁的行忠遂亲自接任。他的嫡子行宗先他去世，孙子行贞也曾担任政所执事。行忠于1290年去世。

en: Nikaidō Yukitomo (died 1353) was a bureaucratic samurai of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, the son of Nikaidō Sadatsuna. He first served the Hōjō regent Takatoki, but took Buddhist vows in 1326 as Gyōchin. The Muromachi shogunate named him head of the Administrative Board three times, in 1335, 1338 and 1352, and he held a string of judicial posts including head of the Board of Claims. In the Kannō Disturbance he first backed Ashikaga Tadayoshi, then surrendered to Takauji. He died in 1353 after falling from his horse while accompanying Takauji to Kyoto.
zh: 二阶堂行朝（？—1353）是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武士官僚，二阶堂贞纲之子。他起初侍奉北条高时，1326年出家，法名行珍。室町幕府时期，他于1335年、1338年、1352年三度被任命为政所执事，并担任引付方头等一系列司法职务。观应之扰乱中，他先站在足利直义一方，后来归降足利尊氏。1353年，他作为尊氏的随从上洛，途中落马，因此身亡。

en: Nikaidō Yukitsuna (1216–1281), second son of Nikaidō Yukimori, was a senior Kamakura shogunate official. Appointed governor of Ise Province in 1245, he joined the new Board of Adjudication in 1249 and took Buddhist vows in 1256, when the regent Hōjō Tokiyori retired from worldly life. Named to the Council of State in 1264, he became chief steward of the Administrative Board in 1269. In 1275 the Nikaidō family provided two hundred kan for the construction of a new building at Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine in Kyoto. He held the stewardship until his death in 1281, when his son Yoritsuna succeeded him.
zh: 二阶堂行纲（1216—1281）是二阶堂行盛的次子，镰仓幕府的高级文官。1245年任伊势守，1249年出任新设立的引付众；1256年执权北条时赖出家时，他也随之出家，法名行愿。1264年就任评定众，1269年任政所执事。1275年，二阶堂氏为京都若宫八幡宫新宫的建设提供了两百贯。他一直担任政所执事，直到1281年去世，由其子赖纲继任。

en: Nikaidō Yukiyasu (1211–1265), son of Nikaidō Yukimori, was a senior Kamakura shogunate official. Appointed governor of Chikuzen Province in 1243, he went to Kyoto in 1247 as a bakufu envoy to report on the new debt-cancellation edict. Named to the new Board of Adjudication in 1249, he became one of its heads in 1253 and succeeded his father as chief steward of the Administrative Board. He took Buddhist vows in 1256, joined the Council of State in 1259, and resumed the stewardship after his son Yukiyori died in 1263. He died in 1265, succeeded by his son Yukizane.
zh: 二阶堂行泰（1211—1265）是二阶堂行盛之子，镰仓幕府的高级文官。1243年任筑前守，1247年作为幕府使者上洛，就新颁的德政令向朝廷奏报。1249年幕府设立引付方，他出任引付众，1253年升任引付头人，同年父亲去世，他接任政所执事。1256年出家，1259年成为评定众；1263年其子行赖去世后，他重新就任政所执事。1265年去世，由另一子行实继任。

en: Nikaidō Yukiyori (1230–1263) was a Kamakura shogunate vassal and the son of Nikaidō Yukiyasu. In 1260 he was granted the lower junior fifth rank and appointed governor of Kaga Province. Two years later, in 1262, he succeeded his father as chief steward of the shogunate's Administrative Board, an office his grandfather Yukimori had made hereditary in the family. His tenure was short: he died the following year, in 1263, and the stewardship reverted to his father, who outlived him.
zh: 二阶堂行赖（1230—1263）是镰仓幕府御家人、二阶堂行泰之子。1260年叙从五位下，任加贺守。1262年他从父亲手中接任政所执事，这一职位自其祖父行盛以来已为其家族世袭。但他在任仅一年，1263年便去世，政所执事之职又重新回到比他长寿的父亲手中。

en: Nikaidō Yukiyoshi (1203–1268) was a Kamakura-period samurai and a son of Nikaidō Yukimura. The Azuma Kagami records his service at the shogunate from 1225 onward. In 1238 he was appointed to the Council of State, where he sat for nearly thirty years. In 1252, when the residence of the new shogun Prince Munetaka was rebuilt, Yukiyoshi oversaw arrangements for the shogun's ritual change of direction. He appears in the Azuma Kagami for the last time in 1266 and died in 1268, aged about sixty-six.
zh: 二阶堂行义（1203—1268）是镰仓时代前期至中期的武士、二阶堂行村之子。《吾妻镜》记载了他自1225年起在幕府的活动。1238年他就任评定众，在任近三十年。1252年新任将军宗尊亲王的御所改建时，他担任将军方违相关事务的奉行。《吾妻镜》中关于他的最后记载见于1266年，他于1268年去世，享年66岁。

en: Nikaidō Yukizane (1236–1269) was the sixth head of the Nikaidō family and a Kamakura shogunate vassal, the son of Nikaidō Yukiyasu. In 1265 he joined the Board of Adjudication and succeeded his father, who died that year, as chief steward of the Administrative Board. In 1268 he was granted the lower junior fifth rank and appointed governor of Shinano Province. He died the following year, in 1269, after which the stewardship passed to his uncle Yukitsuna.
zh: 二阶堂行实（1236—1269）是二阶堂氏第六代当主、镰仓幕府御家人，二阶堂行泰之子。1265年，他出任引付众，并在父亲当年去世后接任政所执事。1268年叙从五位下，任信浓守。他于翌年1269年去世，此后政所执事之职传给了叔父行纲。

en: Emperor Ninmyō (810–850) was the 54th emperor of Japan, reigning from 833 to 850, and the first emperor born in Heian-kyō. The second son of Emperor Saga, he was named crown prince in 823 and succeeded his uncle Emperor Junna in 833. Tang-style rites and Chinese poetry flourished at his court, and a last embassy to Tang China sailed in 838–839. After the Jōwa Incident of 842, the heir Prince Tsunesada was deposed and Ninmyō's own son Prince Michiyasu made crown prince. Chronically ill, Ninmyō abdicated in 850 and died two days later.
zh: 仁明天皇（810—850）是日本第54代天皇，833年至850年在位，也是第一位在平安京出生的天皇。他是嵯峨天皇次子，823年被立为皇太子，833年继叔父淳和天皇即位。在位期间唐风礼仪与汉诗鼎盛，838年至839年还派出了最后一批遣唐使。842年承和之变后，皇太子恒贞被废，仁明之子道康被立为太子。仁明天皇体弱多病，850年退位，两天后去世。

en: Nitsuki Moroyoshi was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan in Mikawa Province. Clan genealogies record him as a son of Yoshitsugu and father of Yoshikatsu, whose sons Yoriaki and Yoshinaga became the clan's leading generals under Ashikaga Takauji.
zh: 仁木师义是三河国仁木氏的镰仓时代武将。仁木氏谱系载其为义继之子、义胜之父；义胜所生的赖章、义长，后来是足利尊氏麾下仁木氏最主要的武将。

en: Nitsuki Sanekuni was a Kamakura-period warrior of Seiwa Genji stock, the eldest son of Hirosawa Yoshizane and grandson of Ashikaga Yoshikiyo. After Ashikaga Yoshiuji was appointed shugo of Mikawa Province for his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221, Sanekuni moved into Niki village in Nukata district and styled himself Niki Tarō, becoming the founder of the Nitsuki house. His younger brother Yoshisue founded the Hosokawa house, and both houses served the Ashikaga main line as hereditary retainers.
zh: 仁木实国是镰仓时代的武将，出自清和源氏，为广泽义实的长子、足利义清之孙。1221年承久之乱后，足利宗家的足利义氏凭军功就任三河守护，实国遂迁往三河国额田郡仁木乡居住，自称仁木太郎，成为仁木氏之祖。其弟义季开创细川氏；两家同为足利嫡流的谱代被官。

en: Niki Yoriaki (1299–1359) was a senior general and steward to Ashikaga Takauji, founder of the Muromachi shogunate. Son of Niki Yoshikatsu, he was born in Mikawa and followed Takauji from 1333, holding Tanba against the Southern Court when Takauji fled to Kyūshū. He rejoined him after Minatogawa in 1336, helped retake Kyoto from Nitta Yoshisada, and fought at Kanegasaki and Shijōnawate. In the Kannō Disturbance he backed Takauji and became steward in 1351, holding several governorships as the office grew into the kanrei post. He took vows after Takauji's death in 1358 and died in Kyoto in 1359.
zh: 仁木赖章（1299—1359）是室町幕府初代将军足利尊氏麾下的重臣与执事。他生于三河国，为仁木义胜之子，1333年起追随尊氏；尊氏败走九州时，他固守丹波国抵御南朝追兵。1336年凑川之战后他与尊氏会合，协助从新田义贞手中夺回京都，又转战金崎城与四条畷。观应之扰乱中他始终支持尊氏，1351年被任命为执事，身兼数国守护，其职务后来演变为管领。1358年尊氏去世后他出家，1359年在京都去世。

en: Niki Yorikatsu (active 1353–1365) was a warrior of the Niki clan, an Ashikaga kinsman house from Mikawa Province. He served the Muromachi shogunate as military governor of Tango from 1353 to 1360 and of Tajima from 1361 to 1365. The Taiheiki records an attack by Southern Court forces on Ara Castle in Tajima, where Yorikatsu is thought to have held out with the castle lord Ara Jūrōzaemon.
zh: 仁木赖胜（活跃于1353—1365年）是仁木氏的武士，仁木氏是出自三河国的足利同族。他在室町幕府历任丹后国守护（1353—1360年）与但马国守护（1361—1365年）。《太平记》记载南朝军进攻但马国安良城，赖胜被认为曾与城主安良十郎左卫门在城中固守。

en: Nitsuki Yoshihide was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan, the Ashikaga branch seated at Nitsuki-gō in Nukata District, Mikawa Province. The clan genealogies record him as the son of Yoshitsugu and the father of Yoshimasa.
zh: 仁木义秀是镰仓时代仁木氏的武将，仁木氏是世居三河国额田郡仁木乡的足利氏分支。谱系载义秀为义继之子、义政之父。

en: Nitsuki Yoshikatsu was a late-Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan in Mikawa Province, genealogically recorded as the father of Yoriaki and Yoshinaga. Both sons served Ashikaga Takauji in the Nanboku-chō wars, Yoriaki as the shogun's steward and Yoshinaga as shugo of many provinces.
zh: 仁木义胜是镰仓后期三河国仁木氏的武将。他在谱系中被记为赖章、义长之父；二子均在南北朝时代侍奉足利尊氏，赖章任幕府执事，义长历任多国守护。

en: Nitsuki Yoshimasa was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan, the Ashikaga branch settled at Nitsuki-gō in Mikawa Province. Genealogies record him as the son of Yoshihide and the father of Yoshishige, a generation before the Nanboku-chō wars.
zh: 仁木义政是镰仓时代仁木氏的武将，仁木氏是定居三河国仁木乡的足利氏分支。谱系载义政为义秀之子、义重之父，在世时正值南北朝战乱之前的一代。

en: Niki Yoshinaga (c. 1300–1376) was a Muromachi-era general, younger brother of Niki Yoriaki, son of Niki Yoshikatsu of Mikawa. He served Ashikaga Tadayoshi in Kamakura, fled the Hōjō rising of 1335, then fought for Takauji at Tatara Beach in Kyūshū and stayed to subdue the Kikuchi. He governed Ise, Iga and other provinces, and the brothers once held nine between them. After Yoriaki died in 1359 his arrogance isolated him; attacked by Hosokawa Kiyouji's coalition, he failed to seize the shōgun Yoshiakira, fled to Ise, and surrendered to the Southern Court in 1361. Later pardoned and returned to the shogunate, he died in 1376.
zh: 仁木义长（约1300—1376）是室町时代前期的武将，仁木赖章之弟、仁木义胜之子，生于三河国。他先在镰仓侍奉足利直义，1335年北条余党起兵时逃出镰仓，后随足利尊氏在九州多多良滨奋战，并留在九州压制菊池氏。他历任伊势、伊贺等国守护，与兄长一度合计占有九国。1359年赖章死后，他因骄横遭到细川清氏等人联合讨伐，试图挟持将军足利义诠失败，逃回伊势，于1361年投降南朝。数年后他获赦重返幕府，1376年去世。

en: Niki Yoshinao (born c. 1300) was a warrior of the Niki clan, an Ashikaga kinsman house based in Mikawa Province. The early Muromachi shogunate appointed him military governor of Iga Province, an office he held from 1337 to 1339.
zh: 仁木义直（约1300年生）是仁木氏的武士，仁木氏是以三河国为根据地的足利同族。室町幕府初年他被任命为伊贺国守护，任职时间为1337年至1339年。

en: Nitsuki Yoshishige was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan, the Ashikaga branch of Mikawa Province. Genealogies record him as the son of Yoshimasa and the father of Yoshitaka, in the generation just before the clan rose under Ashikaga Takauji.
zh: 仁木义重是镰仓时代仁木氏的武将，仁木氏是出于三河国的足利氏分支。谱系载义重为义政之子、义高之父，在世时正值仁木氏随足利尊氏崛起的前一代。

en: Nitsuki Yoshitaka (died 1336) was a Nanboku-chō warrior from a cadet line of the Nitsuki clan, the Mikawa offshoot of the Ashikaga. In April 1336 a Southern Court army from Tōtōmi under Nitta Samanosuke invaded Mikawa; Yoshitaka, his son Mijirō Yoshinaga and Hosokawa Yoritane defeated it at Kira-no-shō and Hō District and cleared the province. That September the Ashikaga forces invaded Tōtōmi, and on the thirteenth day Yoshitaka was killed by the Tenryū River while pursuing the Nitta army past Shinohara, east of Lake Hamana.
zh: 仁木义高（？—1336）是日本南北朝时代的武将，出身仁木氏庶流，仁木氏为足利氏在三河国的分支。1336年4月，新田左马助率领远江国的南朝军攻入三河，义高与儿子弥二郎义长、细川赖种等迎战，在吉良庄和宝饭郡连败敌军，将其逐出三河。同年9月，足利氏攻入远江，13日义高在滨名湖以东的筱原追击新田军时，战死于天龙川畔。

en: The Kansei Chōshū Shokafu genealogy records Nitsuki Yoshitoshi, also known as Matatarō, as the son of Nitsuki Sanekuni and the father of Yoshitsugu.
zh: 据《宽政重修诸家谱》记载，仁木义俊通称又太郎，是仁木实国之子、义继之父。

en: Nitsuki Yoshitsugu was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Nitsuki clan, the Ashikaga branch seated at Nitsuki-gō in Nukata District, Mikawa Province. Nitsuki genealogies record him as the son of Yoshitoshi and the father of Yoshihide and Moroyoshi.
zh: 仁木义继是镰仓时代仁木氏的武将。仁木氏是世居三河国额田郡仁木乡的足利氏分支，仁木氏谱系载义继为义俊之子，生义秀、师义二人。

en: Nitta Masauji (1208–1271) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, the fifth head of the Nitta main house and eldest son of Nitta Masayoshi. After his father's unauthorized tonsure in 1244, real power over the Nitta passed to collaterals Serada Yoshisue and Iwamatsu Tokikane. Masauji recovered his position when Yoshisue's son Serada Yoriuji was exiled to Sado Island, and again led the clan. A maternal grandson of Ashikaga Yoshiuji, he took the character uji of his name from an Ashikaga patron, beginning a Nitta naming custom. He died in 1271.
zh: 新田政氏（1208—1271）是镰仓时代中期的武将、御家人，新田氏本宗家第五代当主，新田政义的长子。1244年父亲擅自出家失势后，新田氏的实权落入世良田义季与岩松时兼等庶家手中。义季之子世良田赖氏被流放佐渡岛后，政氏借机恢复地位，重新统领新田氏。他是足利义氏的外孙，名字中的“氏”字得自足利氏当主的偏讳，此后新田历代当主沿袭此例。1271年去世。

en: Nitta Masayoshi (c. 1187–1257) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the fourth head of the Nitta main house, succeeding his father Yoshifusa at the age of thirteen under family guardianship. He married a daughter of Ashikaga Yoshiuji. In 1242 the shogunate fined him three thousand hiki after prisoners escaped his custody. In 1244, while on guard duty in Kyoto, he sought court office without Kamakura's leave, then took the tonsure, left his duty and withdrew to Nitta Manor, refusing to serve the shogunate. He lost part of his lands and the sōryō headship, founded Enpuku-ji temple in retirement, and died in 1257 aged seventy-one.
zh: 新田政义（约1187—1257）是镰仓时代中期的武将、新田氏本宗家第四代当主，13岁时在亲族后见之下继承父亲义房。他娶了权势御家人足利义氏之女。1242年，因幕府交由他看管的囚犯逃走，他被课以三千疋的过怠料。1244年在京都担任大番役期间，他未经镰仓许可便谋求朝廷任官，事后又擅自出家、中止服役回到新田庄，拒不出仕幕府。他被没收部分所领与总领职，隐居并创建圆福寺，1257年以71岁去世。

en: Nitta Motouji (1253–1324) was a Kamakura warrior and gokenin, the sixth head of the Nitta main house. Although he was the fifth son of Nitta Masauji, he became clan head at nineteen over his elder brothers, possibly because his mother was a daughter of Akahashi Hidetoki of the ruling Hōjō family. In a dispute over rice fields he backed his kinsman Ōdate Muneyuji against Sonoda Hidetoshi, Iwamatsu Tsunekane and the latter's sons Tomokane and Masatsune, but the Kamakura shogunate ruled in his rivals' favour. He died in 1324 aged seventy-two and was buried at Enpuku-ji; Nitta Yoshisada was his grandson.
zh: 新田基氏（1253—1324）是镰仓时代的武将、御家人，新田氏本宗家第六代当主。他虽为新田政氏的第五子，却在19岁时越过诸位兄长继任当主，有说法认为其生母出自当权北条氏的赤桥流，即赤桥秀时之女。在一场围绕水田的纷争中，他支持同族大馆宗氏，与园田秀俊、岩松经兼及其子朝兼、政经兄弟对抗，镰仓幕府却作出有利于对手的裁决。1324年他以72岁去世，葬于圆福寺；新田义贞是他的孙子。

en: Nitta Tomouji (1274–1318) was a Kamakura gokenin and the seventh head of the Nitta main house, the eldest son of Nitta Motouji and father of the celebrated Nitta Yoshisada and Wakiya Yoshisuke. Documents from Chōraku-ji in 1314 name him Tomokane, showing he later changed his name to Tomouji while the Nitta lived under strong Ashikaga influence. About 1313 he summoned his kinsmen the Asaya brothers, notorious bandits in southern Hitachi, to Nitta Manor and favoured them with lands and his sister's hand. He died of illness in 1318 at forty-five, before his father, leaving the young Yoshisada as his heir.
zh: 新田朝氏（1274—1318）是镰仓幕府御家人、新田氏本宗家第七代当主，新田基氏的长子，名将新田义贞与胁屋义助之父。1314年的长乐寺文书称他为“源朝兼”，可知他后来改名朝氏，当时新田宗家深受足利氏影响。约1313年，他把在常陆国南部以“恶党”闻名的远亲朝谷义秋、正义兄弟召至新田庄，优赐领地，并以妹妹相许。1318年他病故，年仅45岁，先于父亲离世，由年轻的义贞作为继承人。

en: Nitta Yoshiaki (c. 1318–1337), the eldest son of Nitta Yoshisada, joined his father's rising that overthrew the Kamakura shogunate in 1333. Under the Kenmu government of 1334 he was named governor of Echigo and headed the first unit of the Board of Retainers. After Ashikaga Takauji turned against the restoration, he followed his father north, and in the tenth month of 1336 entered Kanegasaki Castle in Echizen guarding the imperial princes Tsunenaga and Takanaga. Besieged for half a year by Shiba Takatsune's forces, he fired the castle and killed himself with Prince Takanaga when it fell in 1337, aged twenty.
zh: 新田义显（约1318—1337）是新田义贞的长子。1333年，他参加父亲推翻镰仓幕府的举兵；1334年建武政权时任越后守，并担任武者所一番（第一队）的头人。足利尊氏背叛建武政权后，他随父北上，1336年10月奉恒良、尊良两位亲王进入越前国金崎城。城池遭到斯波高经等部长达半年的围攻，1337年城陷之际，他放火烧城，与尊良亲王一同自尽，年二十岁。

en: Nitta Yoshifusa (1162–1195), also called Nitta Kurōdo, was a Kamakura-period warrior and the third head of the Nitta main line. The eldest and only son of Nitta Yoshikane, he served the imperial consort Jōsaimon-in at court in his youth. He died in 1195 at the age of thirty-four, before his father, leaving his young son Masayoshi to inherit the Nitta estates in Kōzuke Province; the boy's grandfather and great-grandfather, Yoshikane and Yoshishige, acted as his guardians. The Edo scholar Arai Hakuseki later claimed descent from Yoshifusa's son Kakugi.
zh: 新田义房（1162—1195），又称新田藏人，是镰仓时代的武将、新田氏本宗家第三代总领，新田义兼的长子兼独子。他年轻时在宫中出仕上西门院。1195年，他以34岁之龄先于父亲去世，年幼的儿子政义继承上野国的新田庄，由祖父义兼与曾祖父义重共同担任后见。江户时代的学者新井白石，相传是义房之子新井觉义的后裔。

en: Nitta Yoshikane (1139–c. 1206), an early Kamakura warrior and gokenin, was the second head of the Nitta main line and the second son of Nitta Yoshishige. He served Empress Kōka-mon'in as a court secretary before joining Minamoto no Yoritomo with his father, after an early bid for independence failed. As a Kamakura vassal he took part in the 1189 Ōshū campaign but won no distinction or court rank. His heir Yoshifusa died young, so Yoshikane helped guard his grandson Masayoshi's succession; documents show he lived until at least August 1205.
zh: 新田义兼（1139—约1206）是平安末期至镰仓时代的武将、御家人，新田氏本宗家的第二代总领，新田义重的次子。他曾任崇德天皇中宫皇嘉门院藤原圣子的藏人，早年与父亲一同谋求自立，受挫后随父亲归顺源赖朝。他参加了1189年的奥州合战，却没有立下显著军功，也未受任官位。嫡子义房早逝，他与父亲一同担任嫡孙政义的后见；文书证明他至少活到1205年8月。

en: Nitta Yoshimune (c. 1331–1368) was the third son of Nitta Yoshisada and a Southern Court commander in the Nanbokuchō Wars. After his father fell in 1338 he was raised in hiding among the Nitta in Echigo and treated as the clan's heir. In 1352 he and his brother Yoshioki rose in Kōzuke, fought Ashikaga Takauji at Kanaihara in Musashi and briefly retook Kamakura, before defeat drove him back to Echigo. In 1358 a new rising collapsed when Yoshioki was murdered at the Yaguchi ferry. In 1368 Yoshimune joined the Musashi revolt and fell at the Numata estate in Kōzuke.
zh: 新田义宗（约1331—1368）是新田义贞第三子，南北朝时代的南朝方武将。1338年父亲战死后，他由越后国的新田一族藏匿抚养，被视为嫡子。1352年，他与兄长义兴在上野举兵，在武藏国金井原与足利尊氏交战，一度夺回镰仓，但战败后退回越后。1358年他计划趁尊氏去世再起，义兴却在矢口渡被谋杀，计划落空。1368年，义宗响应武藏的起义举兵，在上野国沼田庄战败，战死沙场。

en: Nitta Yoshioki (c. 1331–1358), the second son of Nitta Yoshisada, rose in Kōzuke in 1337 and joined Kitabatake Akiie's northern army, fighting at Sugimoto and Aonogahara; at Yoshino, Emperor Go-Daigo gave him his adult name. In 1352, during the Kannō Disturbance, he raised troops for Prince Muneyoshi and briefly seized Kamakura. Taking arms again in 1358, he was murdered with twelve retainers at the Yaguchi ferry on the Tama River by men sent by the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji, aged twenty-eight. The Taiheiki made his vengeful ghost famous, and he was later worshipped as the god Nitta Daimyōjin.
zh: 新田义兴（约1331—1358）是新田义贞的次子。1337年他在上野举兵，加入北畠显家的奥州军，转战杉本城、青野原，后在吉野谒见后醍醐天皇，由天皇赐名。1352年观应之扰乱期间，他奉宗良亲王举兵，一度攻占镰仓。1358年他再度举兵，在多摩川的矢口渡口与十二名随从一同被镰仓公方足利基氏派来的人谋杀，年仅二十八岁。《太平记》渲染他的怨灵复仇，后来他被奉为新田大明神。

en: Nitta Yoshisada (1301–1338) was a lord of Nitta Manor in Kōzuke Province and head of the Nitta clan, succeeding his father Tomouji in 1317. Answering Emperor Go-Daigo's call against the Hōjō, he marched on Kamakura in 1333, besieged it and captured the shogunal capital, bringing down the Kamakura shogunate. Sent against Ashikaga Takauji and his brother Tadayoshi by imperial commission in 1335, he fought from the Yahagi River to Mishima before they beat him back and advanced on Kyoto. He lost again at Minatogawa in 1336. That year, as the emperor agreed to Takauji's terms and returned to Kyoto, he entrusted Yoshisada with escorting two princes to Echizen. Yoshisada escaped the fall of Kanegasaki in 1337, but his son Yoshiaki and the two princes died there. At Kuromaru on 17 August 1338 his horse was felled by arrows; pinned beneath it, he is said to have cut off his own head with his short sword.
zh: 新田义贞（1301—1338）是上野国新田庄领主、新田氏当主，1317年继承父亲新田朝氏。他响应后醍醐天皇讨伐北条氏，1333年进军镰仓，围城并攻陷幕府所在地，终结镰仓幕府。1335年朝廷下诏讨伐足利尊氏、直义兄弟，义贞领兵出战，从矢作川一路打到三岛，被兄弟二人击退，对方随即进军京都。1336年他又在凑川之战中败北。同年天皇接受尊氏的条件返回京都，临行前托义贞护送两位亲王前往越前。1337年金崎城陷落时他突围而出，其子新田义显与两位亲王丧命。1338年8月17日，他在围攻黑丸时战马中箭倒地，被压在马下，相传用短刀割下了自己的头颅。

en: Minamoto no Yoshishige (1114–1202), later called Nitta Yoshishige, was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and the founder of the Nitta clan. Eldest son of Minamoto no Yoshikuni and grandson of Yoshiie, he opened the Nitta Manor in Kōzuke Province, securing its charter in 1157, and defeated rival Chichibu and Ashikaga forces after forcing a crossing of the Watarase River. In 1180 he held aloof from Yoritomo's uprising before submitting late, and remained an uneasy vassal of the Kamakura shogunate. Tonsured as Jōsei, he died at Nitta in 1202.
zh: 源义重（1114—1202），后称新田义重，是平安时代后期至镰仓时代初期的武将、新田氏的始祖。他是源义国的长子、名将源义家之孙，以上野国新田庄为据点，1157年成功为新田庄立券，并在强渡渡良濑川的合战中击败秩父氏与藤姓足利氏。1180年源赖朝起兵时，他先持观望态度，迟迟才归顺，在镰仓政权中始终处境微妙。他出家后法号上西，1202年于新田庄去世。

en: Oda no Chikamoto was a military commander active in the early Kamakura period, held to be a son of Taira no Chikazane and an ancestor of the Oda clan. His sons were Oda no Chikayuki and Motoyuki.
zh: 织田亲基是镰仓时代初期活动的武将，相传为平亲真之子，被视为织田氏的祖先，其子有织田亲行与基行。

en: Oda no Chikayuki was a military commander of the late Kamakura period and a son of Oda no Chikamoto. He held an estate at Tsuda in Gamō District, corresponding to present-day Hiroe, and was the father of Oda no Yukihiro.
zh: 织田亲行为镰仓时代后期武将，织田亲基之子。他领有蒲生郡津田的领地，其地相当于今广江；其子为织田行广。

en: Chikazane, also called Imibe no Chikazane or Oda Chikazane, was a Shinto official of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, claimed ancestor of the Oda clan. The Oda genealogy names him a son of the Taira lord Taira no Sukemori, hidden with his mother in Ōmi when the Taira fell in 1185, but modern scholars regard this as a later fabrication. In 1233 he became head priest of the Tsurugi Shrine at Oda-no-shō in Echizen, and took Buddhist vows in 1258 as Kakusei. His death is dated to either 1260 or 1290. He was the father of Oda no Chikamoto.
zh: 亲真又称忌部亲真、织田亲真，是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的神官，被织田氏奉为始祖。织田家流传的系图称他是平资盛之子，1185年平家灭亡时随母被藏匿于近江；现代学者认为此说系后世假托。1233年，他出任越前国丹生郡织田庄织田神社（剑神社）神主，1258年出家，法号觉盛（一作觉性）。他的卒年有1260年和1290年两说。其子为织田亲基。

en: Oda Norihiro is known only from Oda clan genealogies, which name him as a son of Oda Suehiro and trace one of the recorded Oda lineage branches from him.
zh: 织田教广仅见于织田氏系谱：系图称他是织田末广之子，织田氏有一支记载的血脉即从他传出。

en: Oda Suehiro was a Japanese bushi of the Nanboku-chō to Muromachi periods, recorded in the early Oda clan genealogies as a son of Oda Yukihiro. He used the common name Saburō and held the style Tarō Hyōe-no-jō. The genealogies record sons named Oda Hirosada and Oda Motozane, and Oda Norihiro, after whom one of the Oda lineage branches is named, is also said to have been his son.
zh: 织田末广是南北朝至室町时代的日本武将，织田氏早期系谱载其为织田行广之子。他通称三郎，官称太郎兵卫尉。系谱记载他有织田广定、织田基实二子；织田氏一支以其名命名的织田教广，相传也是他的儿子。

en: Oda Yukihiro was a Japanese bushi of the late Kamakura to Muromachi periods and an early documented figure of the Oda clan, the warrior house that arose at Oda-no-shō in Nyū District of Echizen Province. Genealogies make him the son of Oda Chikayuki and give him the style Tarō Hyōe-no-jō. From his father's generation the family holding lay at Tsuda in Gamō District of Ōmi Province. The genealogies name Oda Suehiro, a bushi of the Nanboku-chō to Muromachi periods, as his son.
zh: 织田行广是镰仓时代后期至室町时代的日本武将，也是织田氏早期有文字可考的人物；织田氏发源于越前国丹生郡的织田庄。系谱记载他是织田亲行之子，通称太郎兵卫尉。自其父一代起，家族领地位于近江国蒲生郡的津田。系谱载其子为织田末广，末广是南北朝至室町时代的武将。

en: Ogamo Ujimoto was head of the Ogamo clan of Kume district in Hōki province. The Ogamo genealogy records that in 1333 he led three hundred horsemen to join Emperor Go-Daigo's rising at Mount Senjō, and that his mother was a daughter of Nanjō Gohaku.
zh: 小鸭氏基是伯耆国久米郡小鸭氏的当主。《小鸭家系图》记载，1333年他率三百骑投奔在船上山举兵倒幕的后醍醐天皇，其母则为南条元伯之女。

en: Ogasawara Ienaga was a Kamakura warrior and the second head of the Iwami Ogasawara, son of the line's founder Nagachika. When his father died in 1313, he inherited the Kawamoto and Mura estates in Ōchi district, Iwami Province, and moved there from Awa with his heir Nagatane. Father and son developed the two estates for about twenty years. Tradition holds that Ienaga died in battle in the turmoil of the wars that brought down the Kamakura shogunate in 1333, and he was succeeded by Nagatane.
zh: 小笠原家长是镰仓时代的武士、石见小笠原氏第二代当主，该氏始祖小笠原长亲之子。1313年父亲去世后，他继承石见国邑智郡的河本乡与村之乡，与嫡子长胤一起从阿波国移居村之乡，在此后约二十年间经营这两处庄园。相传他在镰仓幕府灭亡前后的战乱中战死，时为1333年，死后由长胤继任家督。

en: Ogasawara Masanaga (1319–1365) was a Northern Court general and head of the Shinano Ogasawara, Sadamune's son. He fought across the country under Ashikaga Takauji, and in 1345 his father transferred to him the Shinano shugo post and the clan's core estates. During the Kannō Disturbance he went over to Ashikaga Tadayoshi in 1351 and fought at Uchidehama, but returned to Takauji within months and was reinstated as shugo. He led Takauji's vanguard into Tōtōmi, then in 1355 helped crush the loyalist rising of Prince Muneyoshi at Kikyōgahara in Shinano. He died in 1365, leaving the military treatise Gunjutsu Heiyōki.
zh: 小笠原政长（1319—1365）是南北朝时代武将、信浓小笠原氏当主，小笠原贞宗之子。他随父亲追随足利尊氏，作为北朝方武将转战各地。1345年，父亲将信浓守护职及小笠原氏的主要领地让给他，由他继承家督。观应之扰乱中，他于1351年转投足利直义一方并参加打出滨之战，数月后又回归尊氏麾下，恢复守护之职。他曾率尊氏军先锋出兵远江，1355年又在信浓桔梗原之战中参与镇压宗良亲王的南朝方举兵。1365年去世，终年47岁，著有兵书《军术兵用记》。

en: Ogasawara Munenaga (1273–1330) was a late-Kamakura warrior, head of the Ogasawara clan and father of Sadamune, the future shugo of Shinano. Born at Matsuo in Shinano, he came of age in 1284 and in 1296 received from his father Nagauji the transmission of the Ogasawara school's mounted-archery teachings. In 1307 he appears as Ogasawara Magojirō in the service roster of Engaku-ji in Kamakura, identified as him by the Sonpi Bunmyaku. He took Buddhist vows in 1323 and died in 1330, aged 59.
zh: 小笠原宗长（1273—1330）是镰仓时代后期的武将、小笠原氏当主，即后来的信浓守护小笠原贞宗之父。他生于信浓国松尾，1284年元服，1296年从父亲长氏处受传小笠原流弓术。1307年，镰仓圆觉寺“每月四日大斋番文”中出现“小笠原孙次郎”之名，据《尊卑分脉》等谱系考证即为宗长。1323年他出家，1330年去世，享年59岁。

en: Ogasawara Nagachika, also called Awa no Matatarō, was a Kamakura warrior and a son of Ogasawara Nagafusa, shugo of Awa Province. For his service in the Kōan campaign against the second Mongol invasion in 1281, he was granted the Mura estate in Ōchi district, Iwami Province, where he settled and founded the Iwami Ogasawara line. He married a daughter of the local lord Masuda Kanetoki and was charged with guarding the unsettled Iwami coast after the invasion.
zh: 小笠原长亲，通称阿波又太郎，是镰仓时代的武将，阿波国守护小笠原长房之子。1281年弘安之役，即元朝第二次入侵日本时，他立有军功，受封石见国邑智郡村之乡，遂移居该地，成为石见小笠原氏的始祖。他娶当地有力国人益田氏当主益田兼时之女为妻，在弘安之役后负责警备局势不稳的石见国沿海。

en: Ogasawara Nagafusa (1213–1276) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, ancestor of the Awa Ogasawara line. The second son of Ogasawara Nagatsune, he took over as shugo of Awa Province after the Jōkyū War of 1221, when his elder brother Nagatada, who had been appointed to the post, chose to return to Shinano. In 1267, on the Kamakura shogunate's orders, he destroyed Taira no Moritaka, district chief of Miyoshi, and was rewarded with over twenty-six thousand chō of land in the Mima and Miyoshi districts. He ruled Awa from Iwakura Castle; his descendants held the Awa shugo post until the fall of Kamakura.
zh: 小笠原长房（1213—1276）是镰仓时代中期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，阿波小笠原氏之祖。他是小笠原长经的次子，1221年承久之乱后，兄长小笠原长忠被任命为阿波国守护，但长忠希望返回本国信浓，长房遂接任阿波守护。1267年，他奉镰仓幕府之命讨杀三好郡郡领平盛隆，受赐美马郡与三好郡二万六千余町的土地，以阿波岩仓城为据点。他的子孙世代担任阿波守护，直至镰仓幕府灭亡。

en: Ogasawara Nagakiyo (1162–1242) was a Kai Province warrior, the second son of Kagami Tōmitsu of the Kai Genji, who held the Ogasawara estate in Koma District and became the first head of the Ogasawara clan, traditionally the ancestor of Ogasawara-ryū archery and etiquette. In 1180 he left Kyoto and joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising, fighting at Ichinotani in 1184 and taking part in the Fuji hunt of 1193. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he commanded the Tōsandō army against the court and was made shugo of Awa Province. He died in Shinano in 1242, aged eighty-one.
zh: 小笠原长清（1162—1242）是甲斐国武将，甲斐源氏加贺美远光的次子，领有巨摩郡小笠原乡，为信浓守护家小笠原氏初代当主，相传是弓马礼法小笠原流之祖。1180年他离开京都投奔源赖朝，1184年参加一之谷之战，1193年参加富士卷狩。1221年承久之乱中，他出任东山道军大将军击败朝廷军，战后受封阿波国守护。1242年卒于信浓，享年81岁。

en: Ogasawara Nagamasa was a Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin who succeeded his father Nagatada as head of the Ogasawara clan. Modern research holds that, far from ruling the family's Shinano lands, he may have held only an estate in Koma district, Kai Province, while the Tomono line controlled the Shinano holdings with the shogunate's backing.
