Appointed a councilor of the Rokuhara tandai, he appears to have been based in Kyoto. When the Tomono were destroyed in the Shimotsuki Incident of 1285, the clan's headship passed to his son Nagauji, ancestor of the later Shinano shugo house.
zh: 小笠原长政是镰仓时代的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，继父亲长忠之后担任小笠原氏当主。据近年研究，他并未像通说那样领有小笠原氏在信浓国的土地，那些所领由受幕府重用的伴野氏把持，长政可能只领有甲斐国巨摩郡的领地。他被任命为六波罗探题的评定众，据点似乎在京都。1285年伴野氏在霜月骚动中没落，小笠原氏惣领之位遂传给其子长氏，长氏的子孙后来出任信浓守护。

en: Ogasawara Nagatada (1202–1264) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, the third head of the Ogasawara clan, succeeding his father Nagatsune; he was also called Matsuo Nagatada after his seat at Matsuo in Shinano's Ina district. His father had passed the Awa shugo post to his kinsman Nagafusa and returned to Shinano. In Nagatada's day the clan's standing in Shinano belonged to the Tomono main line, while his elder brother Nagamura fled after backing the Miura in the Hōji War of 1247. His son Nagamasa succeeded him, and Nagamasa's son Nagauji later recovered the family headship.
zh: 小笠原长忠（1202—1264）是镰仓时代中期信浓国的武将、镰仓幕府御家人、小笠原氏第三代当主，继父亲长经之后继任；因居住在信浓国伊那郡的松尾，又称松尾长忠。其父将阿波守护职让给同族长房，自己回到信浓定居。长忠的时代，小笠原氏在信浓的地位由嫡家伴野氏把持；兄长小笠原长村在1247年宝治合战中支持三浦氏，兵败后逃亡。长忠死后由其子长政继任，长政之子长氏后来恢复了小笠原氏的当主之位。

en: Ogasawara Nagatane was the third head of the Iwami Ogasawara, a warrior clan based at Kawamoto in Ōchi district, Iwami province. When his father Ienaga fell in battle in 1333, he took over the family lands. In 1335 he first supported the Southern Court against Ashikaga Takauji, but in 1336 he switched to the Northern side, and with his son Nagauji defeated the Kusunoki forces at Mikusu in Nima district, enlarging the clan's domain. In his later years he built Yunoyu Castle as his seat, and died in 1346.
zh: 小笠原长胤是石见国邑智郡河本乡国人石见小笠原氏的第三代当主。1333年父亲家长战死后，他继承家业。1335年足利尊氏与后醍醐天皇对立时，他最初归顺南朝，1336年又转投北朝，与嫡子长氏在迩摩郡三久须击败楠木氏的宫方军队，逐步扩大所领。晚年他在河本修筑温汤城作为居城，1346年去世。

en: Ogasawara Nagatsune (1179–1247) was a Kamakura-period warrior and second head of the Ogasawara clan, son of Nagakiyo. In 1189 he campaigned with his father in the Ōshū War, later attending the second shogun Minamoto no Yoriie as a mounted archer. In the Hiki purge of 1203 he was imprisoned as a Hiki partisan and left Kamakura. After the Jōkyū War of 1221 he became jitō of a manor in Awa Province and is recorded as Awa shugo by 1223. Ordained a monk, he led a yabusame rite at Kyoto's New Hie Shrine in 1247 and died aged 69.
zh: 小笠原长经（1179—1247）是镰仓时代前期的武将、小笠原氏第二代当主，小笠原长清之子。1189年，他随父亲参加奥州合战，后来担任二代将军源赖家的近习，以流镝马射手侍奉。1203年比企能员之变中，他被视作比企一方而遭拘禁，随后离开镰仓。1221年承久之乱后，他被任命为阿波国麻殖保的地头，1223年已有担任阿波守护的记录。出家后称小笠原入道，1247年在京都新日吉社主持流镝马神事，同年去世，享年69岁。

en: Ogasawara Nagauji was a Kamakura-period warrior who recovered the Ogasawara clan's headship for his line. The son of Nagamasa and great-grandson of Nagatsune, he became sōryō in 1285, when the Tomono collateral house was destroyed in the Shimotsuki Incident and its head Tomono Nagayasu was killed. His father Nagamasa served as a councilor of the Rokuhara tandai in Kyoto. In 1296 he transmitted the Ogasawara-school mounted-archery teachings to his son Munenaga, whose mother was a daughter of Tomono Nagafusa and whose son Sadamune later became shugo of Shinano.
zh: 小笠原长氏是镰仓时代的武将，为长政之子、长经曾孙。1285年霜月骚动中，执掌小笠原氏惣领职的庶流伴野氏当主伴野长泰被杀，伴野氏没落，长氏遂接掌小笠原氏惣领之位，使该职回到长经一脉。他的父亲长政曾在京都六波罗探题处任评定众。1296年，他向其子宗长传授小笠原流弓术；宗长的母亲是伴野长房之女，宗长之子贞宗后来成为信浓守护。

en: Ogasawara Nagauji was the fourth head of the Iwami Ogasawara, warriors based at Yunoyu Castle in Ōchi District, Iwami Province, and son of the third head Nagatane. In 1336 he joined his father, now with the Northern Court, in defeating Southern Court Kusunoki forces at Mikusu, and the two built Yunoyu Castle around 1340. He succeeded as head in 1346. In 1350 he helped Kō no Moroyasu storm Aoyagi Castle and kill Saba Aritsura, then opened the Dōgamaru mines. Ashikaga Tadafuyu briefly drove him from the castle in 1354. He died on 1 August 1383, followed by his son Nagayoshi.
zh: 小笠原长氏是南北朝时代的武士，是以石见国邑智郡温汤城为据点的国人、石见小笠原氏第四代当主，第三代当主小笠原长胤之子。1336年，他随改投北朝的父亲在迩摩郡三久须击败南朝方楠木氏，约1340年父子又筑成温汤城。1346年父亲死后，他继任家督。1350年，他与高师泰一同攻破佐波顕连的青杉城并将其讨死，同时开始经营铜个丸矿山。1354年足利直冬来攻，他一度退出温汤城。1383年8月1日去世，由嫡子长义继任。

en: Ogasawara Sadamune (30 April 1292–5 July 1347) was head of the Shinano Ogasawara clan and shugo of Shinano. He first served the Kamakura shogunate, fighting Go-Daigo's forces at Akasaka in 1331, but switched sides with Ashikaga Takauji in 1333 and was made shugo after the fall of Kamakura. In 1336 he helped defeat Nitta Yoshisada in Ōmi and cut off the Southern Court's supplies on Lake Biwa. Inheriting his family's archery tradition, he taught kyūjutsu and yabusame to Takauji and Go-Daigo, shaped the Ogasawara school and wrote on mounted archery. He died in Kyoto in 1347.
zh: 小笠原贞宗（1292年4月30日—1347年7月5日）是信浓小笠原氏当主、信浓守护。他初仕镰仓幕府，1331年曾参与攻打赤坂城的后醍醐天皇方军队；1333年随足利尊氏倒幕，镰仓陷落后被任命为信浓守护。1336年，他在近江击败新田义贞，并封锁琵琶湖切断南朝的粮道。他继承家传弓术，向尊氏与后醍醐天皇教授弓术与流镝马，奠定小笠原流，还著有骑射论书，1347年在京都去世。

en: Ogasawara Sadanaga was a warrior of the Ogasawara clan of Shinano Province in the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts period, a son of Ogasawara Munenaga. The Kansei Choshu Shokafu calls him the younger brother of Sadamune, while older genealogies name him either the eldest son or an adopted heir of his grandfather Nagauji. He lived in Shinano, and his son Takanaga carried on the family.
zh: 小笠原贞长是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代信浓国小笠原氏的武将，为小笠原宗长之子。《宽政重修诸家谱》称他是贞宗的同母弟，而更早的谱系或说他是长子，或说他被祖父长氏收为养子。他定居信浓，其子高长继承家业。

en: Oguni Masamitsu was the head of the main line of the Oguni, a warrior clan of Kariwa District in Echigo Province, and fought for the Southern Court in the Northern and Southern Courts wars. In 1335 he built Kanbarazu Castle on Mount Kanbachi as a base for loyalist commanders in lower Echigo. In 1341 Masamitsu and his allies came under attack from Northern Court forces at Kanbarazu.
zh: 小国政光是越后国刈羽郡豪族小国氏的嫡流当主，在南北朝动乱中作为南朝方武将作战。1335年，他在金钵山筑起蒲原津城，作为下越地方南朝诸将的据点。1341年，政光等人在蒲原津遭到北朝军队的攻击。

en: Oguni Yoritaka was the son of Oguni Yoritsugu, founder of the Oguni clan based at Oguni in Kariwa district, Echigo Province, and was the father of Yorimura.
zh: 小国赖隆是越后国刈羽郡小国氏家祖小国赖连之子，生子小国赖村。

en: Oguni Yoritsugu was an early-Kamakura warrior and gokenin, founder of the Oguni clan based at Oguni in Kariwa district, Echigo. A grandson of Minamoto no Yoriyuki and son of Minamoto no Muneyori, he was summoned as the first archer at Shogun Sanetomo's yumi-hajime ceremony in 1212; having brought no bow, he used an Araki bow given him for the occasion and showed such strength and skill that the shogun granted him the jitō post of the Inazu manor in Echizen. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he served in Hōjō Tomotoki's army on the Hokuriku road.
zh: 小国赖连（一作赖继）是镰仓时代前期的武将、御家人，是以越后国刈羽郡小国保为据点的小国氏家祖。他是源赖行之孙、源宗赖之子。1212年正月，他被召为将军源实朝弓始仪式的第一射手，当日却未带弓，便使用赐予的荒木弓射箭，凭刚力与出众弓术令实朝叹赏，获赐越前国稻津保的地头职，事见《吾妻镜》。1221年承久之乱中，他加入北条朝时的幕府军，沿北陆道进军。

en: Prince Okiyoshi (born c. 1326) was a Southern Court prince, a grandson of Emperor Go-Daigo by Prince Moriyoshi and a Kitabatake mother. Soon after Go-Murakami's accession he was appointed seii taishōgun, or palace general. In 1341 he went east to join Kitabatake Chikafusa at Oda Castle in Hitachi, holding Daihō and Oyama castles in turn until loyalist strongholds fell in 1343. In the west he campaigned with the Akamatsu in Harima and Tamba, but in 1360 he rebelled against the Southern Court: with Akamatsu Ujinori he burned the residence at Anō in Yoshino, was defeated and vanished from the records.
zh: 兴良亲王（约1326年生）是南朝皇族，后醍醐天皇之孙、护良亲王之子，母亲出自北畠家。后村上天皇即位不久，他被任命为征夷大将军，人称“宫将军”。1341年他东下常陆，投奔据守小田城的北畠亲房，先后转移到大宝城、小山城，1343年宫方据点陷落后西走。回到西国后，他在播磨、丹波随赤松氏转战；但1360年举兵背叛南朝，与赤松氏范一起火烧吉野贺名生行宫，兵败后下落不明。

en: Ōe no Hiromoto (1148–1225), a Kyoto court noble, was a chief architect of the Kamakura shogunate. A great-grandson of the scholar Ōe no Masafusa, he was summoned east by Minamoto no Yoritomo in 1184 and became the first bettō of the Kumonjo and, in 1191, of the Mandokoro. In 1185 he urged Yoritomo to appoint jitō stewards and shugo governors, binding the provinces to Kamakura. After Yoritomo's death he backed Hōjō Masako, helped bring down the Hiki and Wada, and in the Jōkyū War of 1221 pressed a march on Kyoto. His son Suemitsu founded the Mōri clan.
zh: 大江广元（1148—1225）出身京都公卿，是镰仓幕府制度的主要缔造者之一，为学者大江匡房的曾孙。1184年他被源赖朝召往东国，同年就任公文所首任别当，1191年又成为政所首代别当。1185年，他建议赖朝在各国设置地头与守护，把地方纳入幕府的控制。赖朝死后，他支持北条政子，协助扳倒比企氏与和田氏；1221年承久之乱中，他力主主动进兵京都。其子季光开创了毛利氏。

en: Ōgimachisanjō Hideko (1311–1353) was a court woman of the Northern and Southern Courts period, the daughter of Inner Minister Kinhide. She served the cloistered Emperor Kōgon longest among his ladies, holding the rank of assistant handmaid and receiving junior third rank in 1337. She bore Kōgon two sons who both took the throne, Emperors Sukō and Go-Kōgon. Falling ill in 1352, she was granted the honorary rank of empress and the cloister title Yōrokumon-in, took Buddhist vows, and died early in 1353, aged forty-two.
zh: 正亲町三条秀子（1311—1353）是南北朝时代的宫廷女性，内大臣公秀之女。她以典侍之身最久侍奉光严上皇，1337年叙从三位。她为光严生下两个后来都登基的儿子——崇光天皇与后光严天皇。1352年她卧病后，受封准三宫、院号阳禄门院，随即出家，于次年初薨去，享年四十二岁。

en: Kinhide Ōgimachisanjō (1285–1363) was a court noble of the late Kamakura period, the son of Provisional Major Councillor Sanemi. Ranked Senior Second Rank and known as the Hachijō Minister, he climbed the court hierarchy from his first ennoblement in 1286 to provisional major councillor in 1321, and served as inspector in 1332–1333 and provisional viceroy of Dazaifu from 1336. In 1352 the Northern Court named him inner minister; he took Buddhist vows and resigned the next year. Through his daughter Hideko he was the maternal grandfather of Emperors Sukō and Go-Kōgon.
zh: 正亲町三条公秀（1285—1363）是镰仓时代后期的公卿，权大纳言实躬之子，官至正二位内大臣，号八条。他1286年叙爵，历任宫中诸职，1321年任权大纳言，1332至1333年任按察使，1336年任大宰权帅。1352年，北朝任命他为内大臣，次年出家辞官。他是崇光、后光严两位天皇的外祖父，其母为公秀之女秀子。

en: Ōgimachisanjō Kintsura (1238–1313) was a Kamakura-period court noble, the eldest son of Councilor Sanekage. After his father's early death he was adopted by the Minister of the Left Tōin Saneo. He became Head Chamberlain in 1274 and Councilor in 1275, then Provisional Middle Counselor in 1286, surpassing his father's highest office. He attained Senior Second Rank in 1288, served as Minister of Popular Affairs, and was promoted to Provisional Major Counselor in 1300. He resigned the next year, took Buddhist vows in 1303 as Kūen, and died in 1313 aged seventy-eight.
zh: 正亲町三条公贯（1238—1313）是镰仓时代公卿，参议实荫的嫡子。他幼年丧父，被左大臣洞院实雄收为犹子。1274年他补任藏人头，1275年任参议，1286年升任权中纳言，超过了父亲的最高官职。他于1288年叙正二位，此后出任民部卿，1300年升任权大纳言。他翌年辞去官职，1303年出家，法名空圆，1313年以七十八岁高龄去世。

en: Ōgimachisanjō Kin'uji (1182–1237) was a court noble of the early Kamakura period and the third son of Sanjō Sanefusa, minister of the left. He received his first court rank in 1191, became a councillor in 1211 and provisional middle counsellor in 1220, rose to senior second rank in 1223 and became provisional major counsellor in 1231, styled the Sanjō Major Counsellor. He also used the names Saga and Saikō, and founded the Ōgimachisanjō house, a branch of the Sanjō family. He died in 1237.
zh: 正亲町三条公氏（1182—1237）是镰仓时代前期的公卿，左大臣三条实房的第三子。他1191年叙爵，1211年任参议，1220年任权中纳言，1223年升正二位，1231年任权大纳言，号三条大纳言，又有嵯峨、西郊等别号。他从三条家分出，开创了正亲町三条家。1237年去世。

en: Ōgimachisanjō Sanekage (1199–1241) was a court noble of the early Kamakura period, the son of Provisional Major Counselor Ōgimachisanjō Kin'uji; his first name was Sanemochi. He entered court service as a chamberlain in 1215 and rose through the guard ranks to Right Middle Captain. In 1238, after completing mourning for his father, he was appointed Head Chamberlain, and in 1239 he joined the senior nobility as Councilor with the rank of Junior Third Rank, later adding the post of Provisional Governor of Bitchū. He died in 1241 while still serving as Councilor, aged about forty-three.
zh: 正亲町三条实荫（1199—1241）是镰仓时代前期的公卿，为权大纳言正亲町三条公氏之子，初名实茂。1215年他任侍从出仕，之后在近卫府诸职中升迁，官至右近卫中将。1238年为父亲服丧期满后，他被补任为藏人头；1239年叙从三位、任参议，跻身公卿之列，翌年兼任备中权守。1241年，他在参议任内去世，年约四十三岁。

en: Ōgimachisanjō Sanemi (1264–after 1317) was a Kamakura-period court noble, the third son of Kintsura and fourth head of the family, who served the Daikakuji imperial line. He was appointed Head Chamberlain in 1295 and Councilor in 1298, and became Middle Counselor in 1303 before being forced to resign in 1305. In 1316 he was made Provisional Major Counselor, but took Buddhist vows the following year as Jitsuen, after which nothing more is recorded of him. His diary, the Sanemi-kyō-ki, survives in more than seventy autograph scrolls, most of them designated Important Cultural Properties.
zh: 正亲町三条实躬（1264—1317年后）是镰仓时代公卿，公贯的第三子、正亲町三条家第四代当主，出仕大觉寺统皇室。他于1295年补任藏人头，1298年任参议，1303年任中纳言，但1305年被迫辞职。1316年他受任权大纳言，翌年便出家，法名实圆，此后事迹不详。他留有日记《实躬卿记》，现存自笔本七十余卷，其中大部分被指定为重要文化财。

en: Ōgo Mitsukane belonged to the Ōgo warrior house of Kōzuke Province; genealogies name him as the son of Toshimitsu and father of Mitsushige.
zh: 大胡光兼属于上野国的大胡武士家族；家谱称他是俊光之子、光重之父。

en: Ōgo Mitsushige belonged to the Ōgo warrior house of Kōzuke Province and was named in genealogies as a son of Mitsukane.
zh: 大胡光重属于上野国的大胡武士家族，家谱称他是光兼之子。

en: Ōgo Nariie was a member of the Ōgo warrior house of Kōzuke Province, recorded in genealogies as a son of its founder, Ōgo Shigetoshi.
zh: 大胡成家是上野国大胡武士家族的一员，家谱记载他是家族始祖大胡重俊之子。

en: Ōgo Shigekiyo was a warrior of the Ōgo clan of Seta district in Kōzuke province. His younger brother Shigeyuki held the title Ōinosuke and is said to have taken the name Kamiizumi, counted by one tradition among the ancestors of the swordsman Kamiizumi Nobutsuna.
zh: 大胡重清是上野国势多郡大胡氏的武士。其弟重之官至大炊介，相传改称上泉氏，为剑豪上泉信纲的先祖之一。

en: Ōgo Shigetoshi, known as Ōgo Tarō, was a warrior of the late Heian period and an illegitimate son of Ashikaga no Nariyuki, chieftain of the Fujiwara-descended Ashikaga clan of Shimotsuke Province. He took his name from the Ōgo estate in Seta District of Kōzuke Province, beneath Mount Akagi, founding the Ōgo warrior house, later counted among the eight leading clans of Jōshū. Temple tradition credits him with founding Chōzenji.
zh: 大胡重俊，通称大胡太郎，是平安时代末期的武士，为下野国藤姓足利氏当主足利成行的庶子。他以赤城山下上野国势多郡的大胡乡为号，开创大胡氏，该家族后来被列为“上州八家”之一。寺院相传他开创了长善寺。

en: Ōgo Toshimitsu belonged to the Ōgo warrior house of Kōzuke Province; one genealogy names him as the son of Toshiyuki and father of Mitsukane.
zh: 大胡俊光属于上野国的大胡武士家族；一份家谱称他是俊行之子、光兼之父。

en: Ōgo Toshiyuki belonged to the Ōgo warrior house of Kōzuke Province; a later genealogy names him as the son of Nariie and father of Toshimitsu.
zh: 大胡俊行属于上野国的大胡武士家族；后世家谱称他是成家之子、俊光之父。

en: Ōhira Katsukuni appears between Kuninobu and Kunitsugu in the genealogy of the Ōhira clan, a warrior house based at Hasuike Castle in Takaoka District, Tosa Province.
zh: 大平胜国列于大平氏系谱中，位于国信与国嗣之间；大平氏是以土佐国高冈郡蓮池城为据点的豪族。

en: Ōhira Kuninobu was an early Kamakura-period warrior, the son of Kondō Kunihira, who served the Minamoto in the Genpei War of 1180 to 1185 and was made shugo of Sanuki Province. Kuninobu moved to Tosa Province and became jitō of the Takaoka and Hasuike manors in Takaoka District, taking the name Ōhira and making Hasuike Castle his seat. He thus founded the Tosa Ōhira clan, which ruled the district until 1566.
zh: 大平国信是镰仓时代初期的武将，近藤国平之子。国平在1180至1185年的治承·寿永之乱中为源氏效力，被任为赞岐守护。国信移居土佐国，成为高冈郡高冈庄与蓮池庄的地头，改称大平氏，以蓮池城为本据，开创了土佐大平氏，该家族在此统治至1566年。

en: Ōhira Kunisuke was a head of the Ōhira clan of Hasuike Castle in Takaoka District, Tosa Province, the son and successor of Ōhira Toshikuni. He was followed as clan head by Kunimitsu.
zh: 大平国助是土佐国高冈郡蓮池城豪族大平氏的当主，大平敏国之子并继其之后担任当主，下任为大平国满。

en: Ōhira Kunitsugu appears between Katsukuni and Toshikuni in the genealogy of the Ōhira clan, a warrior house based at Hasuike Castle in Takaoka District, Tosa Province.
zh: 大平国嗣列于大平氏系谱中，位于胜国与敏国之间；大平氏是以土佐国高冈郡蓮池城为据点的豪族。

en: Ōhira Toshikuni was a head of the Ōhira, a warrior clan based at Hasuike Castle in Takaoka District, Tosa Province. He succeeded his father Kunitsugu and was in turn followed as clan head by his son Kunisuke.
zh: 大平敏国是以土佐国高冈郡蓮池城为据点的豪族大平氏当主，接替父亲大平国嗣，其后由儿子大平国助继任。

en: Ōida Tsunetaka was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts period, from a branch of the Nitta clan settled at Ōida in Uonuma District, Echigo Province. When Nitta Yoshisada rose against the Hōjō at Nitta-no-shō in Kōzuke in 1333, Tsunetaka led his Echigo kinsmen, the Satomi, Toriyama, Hakawa and Tanaka houses, to join him. In the Battle of Kamakura he broke through the Keshōzaka pass and helped overthrow Hōjō Takatoki, bringing down the Kamakura shogunate.
zh: 大井田经隆是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，其家族大井田氏是定居于越后国鱼沼郡大井田乡的新田氏支族。1333年新田义贞在上野国新田庄举兵讨伐北条氏时，经隆率领里见、鸟山、羽川、田中等同族从越后赶来会合，参加镰仓之战。他在镰仓越过化妆坂，击破北条高时，为攻灭镰仓幕府立下战功。

en: Ōida Ujitsune was a Southern Court warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts period, from a Nitta branch clan settled at Ōida in Echigo's Uonuma District and the son of Ōida Tsunetaka. In 1333 he and his father joined Nitta Yoshisada's rising and fought at the Battle of Kamakura against Hōjō Takatoki. He then served Yoshisada across the country, holding Fukuyama in Bitchū against Ashikaga Takauji before defeat by Tadayoshi, and later suffering defeat at Minatogawa. He followed Yoshisada to Hokuriku and, after his lord's death, protected Nitta Yoshimune, thrice battling the Ichikawa of Shinano and campaigning through Hokuriku and Musashi.
zh: 大井田氏经是南北朝时代的南朝方武将，出身于定居越后国鱼沼郡大井田乡的新田支族大井田氏，为大井田经隆之子。1333年，他随父亲会合新田义贞的举兵，参加镰仓之战，击破北条高时。此后他追随义贞转战各国，曾据守备中国福山以阻止足利尊氏东上，被足利直义军击败，后又在凑川之战中战败。义贞败走北陆时他随行左右；义贞死后，他保护新田义宗，与信浓国志久见乡的市河氏三度激战，并转战北陆与武藏各地。

en: Ōida Yoshitsugu was a Kamakura-period warrior, the second son of Satomi Yoshinari of Kōzuke Province. He was granted a holding at Ōidagō in Hataki Manor, Uonuma District in Echigo Province, which he and his son Ujitsugu held. The branch house they founded took the name Ōida, and with houses such as the Toriyama and Tanaka it formed the Echigo Nitta league, whose horsemen joined Nitta Yoshisada's rising against the Hōjō in 1333.
zh: 大井田义继是镰仓时代武将，上野国里见义成的次子。他受领越后国鱼沼郡波多岐庄大井田乡的领地，与儿子氏继曾领有该地。他们开创的分家以地名称大井田氏，与鸟山氏、田中氏等组成越后新田党，其同族骑兵后来在1333年加入了新田义贞讨伐北条氏的举兵。

en: Ōkura Hidehira was the second head of the Ōkura clan of Hita District in Bungo Province and a son of the sumō champion Ōkura Nagasue, the clan's first historically recorded head. His brother Nagahira succeeded him as the third head.
zh: 大藏秀平是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第2代当主，大藏氏首位见诸史籍的当主、相扑名手大藏永季之子，其弟永平继为第3代当主。

en: Ōkura Kuginaga was the twelfth head of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province in Kyushu, and a son of the eleventh head Nagatoshi.
zh: 大藏栓永是九州丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第12代当主，第11代当主大藏永敏之子。

en: Ōkura Nagahide was the fifth head of the Ōkura clan of Hita District in Bungo Province, following his father Nagahira and his elder brother Nagamune as head. His son Nagatsuna succeeded him as the sixth head.
zh: 大藏永秀是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第5代当主，在父亲永平、兄长永宗之后统领一族，其子永纲继为第6代当主。

en: Ōkura Nagahira was the third head of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province, and a son of Ōkura Nagasue. His sons Nagamune and Nagahide succeeded in turn as the fourth and fifth heads.
zh: 大藏永平是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第3代当主，大藏永季之子，其子永宗、永秀相继出任第4代、第5代当主。

en: Ōkura Nagamoto was the eighth head of the Ōkura clan of Hita District in Bungo Province, a son of the seventh head, Naganobu. His son Nagashide succeeded him as the ninth head.
zh: 大藏永基是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第8代当主，第7代当主大藏永信之子，其子永资继为第9代当主。

en: Ōkura Nagamune was the fourth head of the Ōkura clan, the local warrior house of Hita District in Bungo Province in Kyushu, and a son of the third head, Nagahira. His brother Nagahide followed him as the fifth head.
zh: 大藏永宗是九州丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第4代当主，第3代当主大藏永平之子，其弟永秀继为第5代当主。

en: Ōkura Naganobu was the seventh head of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province in Kyushu, succeeding his father Nagatsuna. His son Nagamoto followed as the eighth head.
zh: 大藏永信是九州丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第7代当主，继父亲大藏永纲统领一族，其子永基继为第8代当主。

en: Ōkura Nagaoki was the fourteenth head of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province in Kyushu, and a son of the eleventh head Nagatoshi, whose sons supplied the clan's successive heads.
zh: 大藏永息是九州丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第14代当主，第11代当主大藏永敏之子；永敏一脉相继出任大藏氏当主。

en: Ōkura Nagasada was the tenth head of the Ōkura clan, who ruled part of Hita District in Bungo Province as hereditary district officials, or gunji. The family were vassals of the Kamakura shogunate. Around 1299 he began building Gakurinji, a Rinzai Zen temple in Hita, and gave thirteen years to the work. Under an edict of Emperor Go-Daigo and with Ashikaga Takauji's support it became an imperial prayer temple. His son Nagatoshi, the eleventh head, continued his father's work and completed the temple halls in 1342.
zh: 大藏永贞是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第10代当主，一家世袭日田郡司，统辖日田郡的一部分，亦为镰仓幕府御家人。约1299年，他在日田动工兴建临济宗禅寺岳林寺，前后历时13年。该寺凭后醍醐天皇的纶旨与足利尊氏的支援，成为敕愿寺。其子第11代当主永敏承继其业，于1342年建成寺院堂塔。

en: Ōkura Nagashide was the ninth head of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province, and a son of the eighth head, Nagamoto. His son Nagasada succeeded as the tenth head and built the Zen temple Gakurinji.
zh: 大藏永资是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第9代当主，第8代当主大藏永基之子，其子永贞继为第10代当主，后创建禅宗寺院岳林寺。

en: Ōkura Nagasue (1056–1104?) was a lord of the Ōkura clan, local magnates of Hita District in Bungo Province, Kyushu, and the first of the clan to enter recorded history, appearing in courtier diaries under the names Nagasue and Chōki. A champion wrestler, he fought at the sumai no sechie bouts in Kyoto, and Hita district records credit him with ten appearances without a single defeat; Ōe no Masafusa is said to have brushed a shrine plaque praying for his victory. In 1104, returning from the capital, he fell ill and died at Ōoi Manor.
zh: 大藏永季（1056—1104？）是九州丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的领主，也是该族第一个走出传说、见于信史的人物，在《御堂关白记》《后二条师通记》等公卿日记中以“永季”“长季”之名出现。他是相扑名手，曾参加在京都举行的相扑节会；据《丰后国日田郡司职次第》记载，他十次出场未尝一败，相传大江匡房曾为他题写大原八幡宫的祈胜匾额。1104年，他在从京都返回途中染病，殁于大肥庄。

en: Ōkura Nagatoku was a son of the ninth head Ōkura Nagashide and a brother of Nagasada, the tenth head of the Ōkura clan of Hita District in Bungo Province; his own son was Nagazumi.
zh: 大藏永德是丰后国日田郡大藏氏第9代当主大藏永资之子、第10代当主大藏永贞的兄弟，其子是大藏永澄。

en: Ōkura Nagatoshi was the eleventh head of the Ōkura clan of Hita in Bungo Province, succeeding his father Nagasada. In 1342 he completed Gakurinji, the Zen temple his father had built under an edict of Emperor Go-Daigo.
zh: 大藏永敏是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第11代当主，继父亲大藏永贞之后统领一族。1342年，他完成了父亲奉后醍醐天皇纶旨始建的禅宗寺院岳林寺。

en: Ōkura Nagatsuna was the sixth head of the Ōkura clan, the local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province, and a son of the fifth head, Nagahide. His son Naganobu succeeded him as the seventh head.
zh: 大藏永纲是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏的第6代当主，第5代当主大藏永秀之子，其子永信继为第7代当主。

en: Ōkura Nagazumi was a member of the Ōkura clan, local lords of Hita District in Bungo Province, and the son of Ōkura Nagatoku, brother of the tenth clan head Nagasada.
zh: 大藏永澄是丰后国日田郡土豪大藏氏一族，大藏永德之子；永德是第10代当主大藏永贞的兄弟。

en: Ōsaki Tadamochi (1327–1383) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, the first head of the Ōsaki clan and eldest son of Shiba Iekane. In 1352, as his father's deputy in Wakasa, he led Wakasa troops to aid Ashikaga Yoshiakira in Kyoto. When Iekane became Ōshū kanrei in 1354, Tadamochi followed him into Mutsu and succeeded to the post on his father's death in 1356. Around 1366 he took the surname Ōsaki, after a Shimōsa estate of his Ashikaga ancestors. In 1367 Shogun Yoshiakira ordered Yūki Akitomo to join Ishibashi Muneyoshi and the two Ōshū kanrei, including Tadamochi, in attacking the rebel Kira Haruie. He died in 1383.
zh: 大崎直持（1327—1383）是日本南北朝时代的武将、奥州管领，大崎氏初代当主，斯波家兼的嫡长子。1352年，他以父亲的若狭国守护代身份率领若狭军上洛，支援足利义诠警备持明院御所。1354年父亲就任奥州管领后，他随军进入陆奥国，并于1356年父亲死后接任该职。约1366年，他以先祖足利家氏在下总国香取郡的领地大崎为号，改称大崎氏。1367年，将军足利义诠命结城显朝与石桥栋义及包括直持在内的奥州两管领一同夹击谋叛的吉良治家。他于1383年去世。

en: Ōta no Yukimasa was a provincial official in Musashi Province in the late Heian period, whose family claimed descent from the warrior Fujiwara no Hidesato. He is named as the father, or grandfather, of Ōyama no Masamitsu, founder of the Ōyama house of Shimotsuke.
zh: 太田行政是平安时代后期武藏国的在厅官人，其家族自称是武家贵族藤原秀乡的直系后裔。史书记载他是下野小山氏始祖小山政光之父，一说为其祖父。

en: Ota no Yukitaka (born c. 1040) was a Musashi warrior of the Fujiwara Hidesato line, recorded as heir of Fujiwara no Yoriyuki and father of Ota no Yukimasa. Called Ota Daibu, he is credited with opening the Ota manor in Saitama district.
zh: 太田行尊（约1040年生）是出自藤原秀乡流的武藏国武士，家谱记为藤原赖行的继承人、太田行政之父，人称太田大夫。相传他开垦了埼玉郡的太田庄。

en: Ōtomo Chikahide (c. 1195–1248) was the second head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. Working with his younger brother Takuma Yoshihide, he consolidated the clan's hold on its Kyūshū domains. In 1236 he secured the succession by retiring and passing the headship to his son Yoriyasu. After the line of Minamoto shōguns ended, he served the sesshō shōgun Fujiwara no Yoritsune and accompanied him to Kyoto in 1238. He died in 1248 at the age of fifty-four.
zh: 大友亲秀（约1195—1248）是镰仓时代前期御家人，大友氏第二代当主。他与弟弟诧摩能秀协力处理国政，巩固大友氏在九州的领地根基。1236年，他把家督之位让给儿子赖泰后隐居，使继嗣安排稳妥。源氏将军绝嗣后，他侍奉摄家将军藤原赖经，并于1238年随赖经上洛。1248年他去世，终年五十四岁。

en: Ōtomo Chikatoki (c. 1236–1295) was the fourth head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo and the third son of Yoriyasu. He may have fought alongside his kinsmen against the Mongol Yuan invasions. He took the headship after his father retired, but died before him in 1295, and the succession passed to his younger brother, or possibly his son, Sadachika. His sons Hidenao and Morochika founded the Nyūta and Nozu branch houses, while his daughter married Shimazu Sadahisa and bore him Morohisa and Ujihisa.
zh: 大友亲时（约1236—1295）是丰后大友氏第四代当主，赖泰的第三子。元军入侵时，他可能曾随一族出阵作战。父亲赖泰隐居后他继承家督，却于1295年先于父亲去世，家督由其弟（一说其子）贞亲继承。他的儿子秀直、师亲分别开创入田氏和野津氏；女儿嫁给岛津贞久，生下师久和氏久。

en: A daughter of Ōtomo Chikatoki, fourth head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo Province, she became the wife of Shimazu Sadahisa, fifth head of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma, and mother of his sons Munehisa, Morohisa and Ujihisa.
zh: 她是丰后国大友氏第四代当主大友亲时之女，嫁给萨摩岛津氏第五代当主岛津贞久，生子岛津宗久、岛津师久与岛津氏久。

en: Ōtomo Sadachika (1246–1311) was the fifth head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo, most likely the second son of Yoriyasu rather than of Chikatoki, as older genealogies claim. When Chikatoki died in 1295, he succeeded to the headship on the retired elder's order. The character sada in his name was presumably granted by Hōjō Regent Sadatoki, who ordered him in 1305 to establish Manju-ji temple in Bungo; he founded it in 1306. He died in 1311 aged sixty-six, with the Buddhist name Shōon, and his younger brother Sadamune succeeded him.
zh: 大友贞亲（1246—1311）是丰后大友氏第五代当主。1295年亲时去世后，他奉隐居的长辈之命继承家督；从年龄推断，他更可能是赖泰的次子，而非旧谱系所说的亲时之子。他名字中的“贞”字一般认为是执权北条贞时所赐。1305年，他奉贞时之命，于1306年在丰后建立万寿寺。1311年他去世，终年六十六岁，法号正温，家督由弟弟贞宗继承。

en: Ōtomo Sadamune (c. 1265 – 9 January 1334) was the sixth head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo in the final years of the Kamakura shogunate. He succeeded his brother Sadachika in 1311 and served the Chinzei tandai Hōjō Hidetoki. In March 1333 he refused to join Kikuchi Taketoki's rising and helped defeat and kill him. Two months later, once the Rokuhara headquarters had fallen, he switched sides with Shōni Sadatsune and destroyed Hidetoki, earning the shugo post of Bungo. He died suddenly in Kyoto that December, leaving the headship to his son Ujiyasu.
zh: 大友贞宗（约1265—1334年1月9日）是镰仓幕府末期丰后大友氏第六代当主。1311年兄长贞亲死后他继为当主，出仕镇西探题北条英时。1333年3月菊池武时举兵，邀他同反，他拒绝参与，并协助击败击杀武时。同年5月六波罗探题陷落的消息传来，他随即与贞经倒戈攻灭英时，因此受封丰后守护。同年十二月他在京都突然去世，家督由儿子氏泰继承。

en: Ōtomo Sadayori was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras, the illegitimate eldest son of Ōtomo Sadamune, sixth head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo Province. Excluded from the succession when Sadamune made his younger brother Ujiyasu heir in 1333, Sadayori broke from the main house after their father's death in 1334. In 1336 he fought on the Southern Court side with the Kikuchi against Ashikaga Takauji at Tatarahama. He reconciled with Ujiyasu and rejoined the Northern Court in 1345, receiving Takauji's pardon and confirmation of his lands, but later rebelled again and, attacked by Northern Court forces, took his own life.
zh: 大友贞顺是镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，为丰后国大友氏第六代当主大友贞宗的庶长子。1333年贞宗绕过年长的贞顺，把家督之位传给其弟千代松丸，即后来的大友氏泰；1334年父亲死后，贞顺脱离宗家，与氏泰对立。1336年多多良滨之战中，他随南朝方的菊池氏与足利尊氏作战。1345年他与氏泰和解、归附北朝，获尊氏赦免并安堵所领；但此后再度举兵反叛宗家，最终在北朝方的进攻下自尽。

en: Ōtomo Ujitoki (c. 1325–1368), childhood name Miyamatsumaru, was eighth head of the Ōtomo clan and a Nanbokuchō shugo daimyō, seventh son of Ōtomo Sadamune. With his brother Ujiyasu he was a nominal son of Ashikaga Takauji, receiving the Genji surname and the character uji. In 1348 he took the headship and Bungo shugo post from Ujiyasu, later gaining Buzen, Higo and Chikugo. He briefly joined the Southern Court, then fought for the North, and in 1359 was defeated by Kikuchi Takemitsu at the Chikugo River, weakening the Ōtomo. He ceded his lands and posts to his heir Ujitsugu in 1364 and died of illness in 1368.
zh: 大友氏时（约1325—1368），幼名宫松丸，是南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，大友氏第八代当主，大友贞宗第七子。他与兄长氏泰同受足利尊氏宠爱，被收为猶子，获赐源姓与“氏”字。1348年，他从氏泰手中继承家督与丰后守护职，后来又补任丰前、肥后、筑后守护。他一度归降南朝，不久复归北朝，1359年在筑后川之战中被菊池武光打得大败，大友氏势力由此衰退。1364年他把所领与职务让给嫡子氏继，1368年病死。

en: Ōtomo Ujiyasu (c. 1321–1362), childhood name Chiyomatsumaru, was the seventh head of the Ōtomo clan of Bungo Province. In 1333 his father Sadamune, before marching against the Hōjō in Kyushu, passed the headship to the boy, who formally succeeded on Sadamune's death in December that year. When Ashikaga Takauji fled to Kyushu in 1336, Ujiyasu helped him regain his footing; Takauji made him a nominal son and granted the character uji, and the Muromachi bakufu made him shugo of Bungo, Buzen, Hizen and Hyūga. He died in 1362 and was followed by his brother Ujitoki.
zh: 大友氏泰（约1321—1362），幼名千代松丸，是丰后国大友氏第七代当主。1333年，父亲大友贞宗在起兵讨伐镇西探题北条英时之前，把家督让给年幼的氏泰；同年12月父亲去世，氏泰正式继为当主。1336年足利尊氏败走九州时，氏泰助其重新起兵，尊氏将他收为猶子并赐以“氏”字，室町幕府开设后任命他为丰后、丰前、肥前、日向四国守护。1362年氏泰去世，家督由其弟大友氏时继承。

en: Ōtomo Yoriyasu (1222–1300) was the third head of the Ōtomo clan. He inherited in 1236 and served as a gokenin at Kyoto and Kamakura, changing his name from Yasunao after receiving a character from Regent Hōjō Tokiyori. As the Mongol threat grew, the shogunate made him eastern Chinzei magistrate, and he moved to Bungo in 1272 to share Kyūshū's defense with the Shōni. He helped repel the Yuan invasions at Torikaigata in 1274 and at Shikanoshima in 1281. He died in Sagami in 1300, aged seventy-nine, having settled the clan in Bungo.
zh: 大友赖泰（1222—1300）是大友氏第三代当主。1236年他继承家督，早年以御家人身份在京都、镰仓活动，后因获执权北条时赖赐“赖”字，由泰直改名赖泰。蒙古威胁日迫，幕府任命他为镇西东方奉行，他于1272年下向丰后，与少贰氏共同负责九州防务。1274年文永之役中，他在鸟饲潟之战击败元军；1281年弘安之役中，又在志贺岛之战奋战，击退元军。1300年他在相模去世，终年七十九岁；大友氏在他这一代迁居丰后，在当地扎下根来。

en: Ōtomo Yoshinao (29 January 1172 – 20 December 1223), born Kondō Ichihōshimaru in Sagami, was a gokenin of the early Kamakura shogunate and the founder of the Ōtomo clan. Adopted by the court official Nakahara no Chikayoshi, he became a close favourite of Shogun Minamoto no Yoritomo, called his matchless favourite in the Azuma Kagami. He fought in the Ōshū campaign of 1189 and shielded Yoritomo during the Soga brothers' revenge in 1193. In 1196 he was made shugo of Buzen and Bungo and Defense Commissioner of the West, carrying the Ōtomo name into Kyūshū. He died in Kyoto in 1223.
zh: 大友能直（1172年1月29日—1223年12月20日），幼名近藤一法师丸，相模国出身，镰仓时代初期御家人，大友氏初代当主。他被朝廷官人中原亲能收为养子，深受将军源赖朝宠爱，《吾妻镜》称他是赖朝“无双的宠人”。1189年他随军参加奥州合战，1193年曾我兄弟复仇事件中挺身护住赖朝。1196年他就任丰前、丰后两国守护兼镇西奉行，把大友氏带入九州。1223年，他在京都去世。

en: Hiroie Ōuchi was a warrior of Suō Province and the 21st head of the Ōuchi clan, succeeding his father Hirosada. Tradition places his birth in 1274 at Yada in Yamato Province, far from the family's Suō base. He died on the 28th day of the third month of 1300 at the age of 27, and the headship passed to his son Shigehiro.
zh: 大内弘家是周防国的武士、大内氏第二十一代当主，继父亲弘贞之后继位。相传他于1274年（建治二年）生于大和国矢田乡，远离大内家在周防的根基之地。1300年（正安二年）三月二十八日，弘家去世，年仅27岁，家督由其子重弘继承。

en: Ōuchi Hiromori was a Suō warrior and the seventeenth head of the Ōuchi clan, then still named Tatara. Exiled in 1177 for the Shishigatani conspiracy and pardoned in 1178, he came to dominate the provincial office, styling himself Ōuchisuke from the Juei era. In the Genpei War he gave Minamoto no Noriyori's army Suō as a forward base against the Taira and backed the Genji. After 1185 he was the province's strongest man; in 1191 the monk Chōgen accused him of blocking timber for the Tōdai-ji rebuild, a suit the Kamakura bakufu dismissed.
zh: 大内弘盛是周防国的在厅官人与武士，大内氏第十七代当主，当时其家仍称多多良氏。1177年他因鹿谷阴谋被处流刑，1178年获赦，此后在国衙势力日重，寿永年间起自称大内介、权介。源平合战时，他把周防作为前进基地提供给源范赖讨伐平氏的军队，转而支持源氏。1185年坛之浦之战后，他成为周防最有权势者；1191年僧人重源指控他妨碍东大寺造营的木材搬运，镰仓幕府驳回了诉讼。

en: Hironari Ōuchi was a warrior of Suō Province and the 19th head of the Ōuchi clan, succeeding his father Mitsumori. His years continued the family's rise, and the Rokuhara tandai, the Kamakura shogunate's deputies in Kyōto, treated him in practice almost as a shugo, or military governor. He died around the 18th day of the ninth month of 1244, and the headship passed to his son Hirosada.
zh: 大内弘成是周防国的武士、大内氏第十九代当主，继父亲满盛之后继位。他在世时延续了大内家的上升势头，镰仓幕府派驻京都的六波罗探题在实际上几乎将他按守护（军事长官）对待。他于1244年（宽元二年）九月十八日前后去世，家督由其子弘贞继承。

en: Hirosada Ōuchi was a provincial official of Suō Province and the fourth head of the Ōuchi line there, succeeding his father Hironari. Where earlier heads had kept the Kamakura shogunate at arm's length, Hirosada acted much like a shogunal vassal and helped build the Kan'in palace for the shogunate. A devout Buddhist, he founded Daishō-ji in 1266 and built a Kannon hall at Migadake in 1274. During the second Mongol invasion of 1281 he advanced into Buzen Province by shogunal order to guard against the Yuan army. He died in 1286.
zh: 大内弘贞是周防国的在厅官人、大内氏在当地的第四代当主，继父亲弘成之后继位。此前的大内氏当主一直与镰仓幕府保持距离，弘贞却几乎以幕府御家人自居，还奉命参与了闲院御所的营造。弘贞信仰虔诚，于1266年（文永三年）创建大照寺，1274年（文永十一年）在右田岳建起观音堂。1281年（弘安四年）元军第二次入侵时，他奉幕府之命进军丰前国，防备元军。他于1286年去世。

en: Ōuchi Hiroyo (c. 1326–1380) was the ninth head of the Ōuchi clan and a Nanbokuchō shugo daimyō, son of Ōuchi Hiroyuki. In 1351 he submitted to the Southern Court and was named Suō shugo; after his father's death in 1352 he fought the Washizu, made peace and brought their faction under his authority, and took Nagato as shugo in 1358. In 1360 he moved the clan seat from Ōuchi residence to Yamaguchi, laying out a town modeled on Kyoto that became the base of later Ōuchi culture. He submitted to the Muromachi bakufu in 1363, added Iwami as a third shugo province in 1366, and died in 1380.
zh: 大内弘世（约1326—1380）是南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，多多良姓大内氏第九代当主，大内弘幸之子。1351年他归顺南朝，被任为周防守护；1352年父亲死后，他与鹫头氏交战，继而议和并将鹫头一派收为麾下，1358年又取得长门守护职，坐拥周防、长门两国。1360年他把本据从大内馆迁到山口，仿照京都规划街市，为后来的大内文化奠定基础。1363年他归顺室町幕府，1366年再任石见守护，身兼三国守护，1380年去世。

en: Ōuchi Hiroyuki (c. 1305–1352) was the eighth head of the Ōuchi clan of Suō Province in the late Kamakura period. He inherited on his father's death in 1320 and marched to Kyoto on Hōjō Takatoki's orders in the Genkō War of 1332, after which the Kenmu regime gave his clan's Suō shugo post to his uncle Washizu Nagahiro. Hiroyuki joined Ashikaga Takauji in 1335, and in 1350 marched against Nagahiro with his son Hiroyo, declaring his intention to submit to the Southern Court. He submitted in 1351, and the court made Hiroyo Suō shugo. Hiroyuki died in 1352, the feud unresolved.
zh: 大内弘幸（约1305—1352）是镰仓时代后期周防国的武将，大内氏第八代当主。1320年父亲死后他继承家督，1332年元弘之乱中奉北条高时之命上洛作战，建武政权因此把大内氏的周防守护职转给了他的叔父鹫头长弘。1335年弘幸与足利尊氏结交，加入武家方；1350年他与儿子大内弘世一同出兵讨伐长弘，表明归顺南朝的意愿。1351年他归顺南朝，南朝任命弘世为周防守护。1352年弘幸去世，与鹫头氏的争执始终没有了结。

en: Mitsumori Ōuchi was the 18th head of the Ōuchi clan of Suō Province, succeeding his father Hiromori. He styled himself Ōuchinosuke, and from his day the clan heads took the title Suō no gon-no-suke. In 1206 he founded the temple Zuiun-ji on Mount Hōju at Shiraishi in Yamaguchi, the family's first foothold in the Yamaguchi basin where the Ōuchi would later centre their power. After his death the headship passed to his son Hironari.
zh: 大内满盛是周防国大内氏第十八代当主，继父亲弘盛之后统领家族。他自称大内介，从他开始，大内氏当主改用周防权介之称。1206年（建永元年），他在山口白石的宝珠山创建瑞云寺，这是大内家在山口盆地的第一个立足点，大内氏日后正是以这一带为势力中心。他去世后，家督由其子弘成继承。

en: Ōuchi Morifusa, then known as Tatara Morifusa, was a provincial official of Suō Province and head of the Tatara clan, the house that later took the name Ōuchi. In June 1177 he was caught in the Shishigatani conspiracy against Taira no Kiyomori and exiled with his kinsmen, including his son Hiromori; all were pardoned in October 1178. By 1182 he headed the signatories of a provincial document as gon-no-suke, or deputy governor. Around 1200 he was the strongest magnate in Suō, and his main line made the gon-no-suke post hereditary under the title Ōuchisuke.
zh: 大内盛房，当时仍称多多良盛房，是周防国的在厅官人、多多良氏当主，其家族后来以大内为姓。1177年6月，他受反对平清盛的鹿谷阴谋牵连，与儿子弘盛等族人一同被处流刑，四人于1178年10月全部获赦。到1182年，他已以权介“多良（盛房）”居于在厅文书联署者的首位。1200年前后，他是周防最有实力的豪族，其嫡流世代承袭权介之职，被称为“大内介”。

en: Shigehiro Ōuchi was a warrior of Suō Province and the 22nd head of its provincial-official Ōuchi line, succeeding his father Hiroie in 1300. The Ōuchi genealogy records him as a councilor of the Rokuhara tandai in Kyōto, and as leader of the provincial officials he opposed Tōdai-ji monks who seized estates across Suō through the temple's fundraising office. From 1312 he lobbied the shogunate and court and backed rival monks' armed petitions against the administrator Shingen, securing his removal by the end of 1318. He died on the sixth day of the third month of 1320, and his legitimate heir Hiroyuki succeeded.
zh: 大内重弘是周防国的武士、在厅官人大内氏第二十二代当主，1300年（正安二年）父亲弘家去世后继承家督。《大内氏系图》记载，他曾在京都担任六波罗探题的评定众；作为在厅官人的盟主，他对抗东大寺僧人借劝进职权在周防各地没收庄园的行动。1312年（正和元年）起，他向幕府和朝廷展开活动，并支持对立僧众发起强诉，最终在1318年（文保二年）年底迫使大劝进心源去职。1320年（元应二年）三月六日重弘去世，嫡男弘幸继位。

en: Prince Oshisaka no Hikohito no Ōe, eldest son of Emperor Bidatsu by Princess Hirohime, was unusual among Emperor Kinmei's descendants in carrying no Soga blood, making him the leading non-Soga prince. He held an independent base through the Osakabe and Marikobe service groups and kept court at Mimata Palace, away from the capital. After Emperor Yōmei died in 587 he was a succession candidate, but Soga-backed princes prevailed and he vanishes from the chronicles; some suspect assassination, others place his death around 600. His sons included the future Emperor Jomei and Prince Chinu, ancestors of the later imperial line.
zh: 押坂彦人大兄皇子是敏达天皇与广姬所生的长子。在钦明天皇的众多子孙中，他罕见地没有苏我氏血统，是非苏我系皇族中最有实力的皇子。他以忍坂部、丸子部等服役集团为独立的经济基础，在远离都城的水派宫自成势力。587年用明天皇死后，他被视为皇位继承人选，但苏我系皇子得势，他从此在史籍中销声匿迹：有人猜测他被苏我氏暗杀，也有学者推断他约于600年前后去世。他的儿子包括后来的舒明天皇和茅渟王，后世皇室均出自他的男系血脉。

en: Oyama Hidetomo (?–1335), first named Takatomo, was a commander of the late Kamakura and early Southern and Northern Courts period, the eighth head of the Oyama clan of Shimotsuke Province and lord of Oyama Castle. He first served the Hōjō and fought in the shogunal army at the sieges of Kasagi and Shimo-Akasaka in 1331 during the Genkō War. In 1333 he defected to Nitta Yoshisada and helped overthrow the Kamakura shogunate, after which Emperor Go-Daigo appointed him governor of Shimotsuke. In 1335 he met Hōjō Tokiyuki's Nakasendai Rebellion at Fuchū in Musashi, where he was defeated and killed.
zh: 小山秀朝（？—1335），初名高朝，是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，下野国小山氏第八代当主、小山城城主。他起初从属北条氏，1331年元弘之乱时作为幕府军一员参加了笠置城与下赤坂城的攻城战。1333年新田义贞举兵进攻镰仓，他倒戈响应，参与攻灭镰仓幕府，事后被后醍醐天皇任命为下野守。1335年北条时行发动中先代之乱，他在武藏国府中迎战，兵败战死。

en: Masamitsu Oyama was a late Heian and early Kamakura warrior and the founder of the Oyama clan, whose estates around the Shimotsuke provincial capital made him leader of the province's largest warrior band. Born into the Ōta house of Musashi, which claimed descent from Fujiwara no Hidesato, he was first called Ōta Masamitsu and moved to the Oyama estate around 1150. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, Masamitsu's wife Samukawa, Yoritomo's wet nurse, pledged the family's warriors to him; Masamitsu and his sons then served Yoritomo as gokenin. He died before 1199.
zh: 小山政光是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将、御家人，小山氏的始祖。他在下野国国府周边拥有大片领地，统领下野最大的武士团。政光出身武藏国太田家，该族自称是藤原秀乡的后裔，他初名太田政光，约1150年（久安六年）移居下野小山庄，开创小山氏。1180年（治承四年）源赖朝举兵时，政光之妻、赖朝的乳母寒河尼将全族武士投效赖朝；此后政光与诸子成为赖朝的御家人。他于1199年以前去世。

en: Oyama Munenaga was the sixth head of the Oyama clan, a powerful warrior family of Shimotsuke Province, and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate. A document of 1282 records him serving as shugo of Harima Province. His son Oyama Sadatomo succeeded him.
zh: 小山宗长是下野国有力武士豪族小山氏的第六代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1282年的一份文书记载他担任播磨国守护，其子小山贞朝继为第七代当主。

en: Nagamura Oyama was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the fourth head of the Oyama, leading lords of Shimotsuke. Skilled with the bow, he first appears in the Azuma Kagami in 1228 as a yabusame archer. His father Tomonaga died young, and in 1230 his grandfather Tomomasa passed the headship to him. He later often attended Shogun Prince Munetaka on pilgrimages to Tsurugaoka Hachiman. In 1250 he petitioned the shogunate after the hereditary office of Shimotsuke no ōsuke was reassigned following a complaint by Ise shrine officials; the council ruled that it should be returned to him. He also held the Harima shugo post. He died in 1269.
zh: 小山长村是镰仓时代中期武将、幕府御家人，下野有力豪族小山氏的第四代当主。长村擅长弓矢，《吾妻镜》1228年（安贞二年）已记载他担任流镝马射手。父亲朝长早逝，1230年（宽喜二年）祖父朝政将家督与所领官职传给他。后来他又多次随将军宗尊亲王参拜鹤冈八幡宫。1250年（建长二年），下野大介一职在伊势神宫杂掌的控诉下被改授他人，经长村申诉，幕府评定决定将职务返还；他还担任播磨守护。1269年（文永六年）长村去世。

en: Oyama Sadatomo (1282–1330) was a commander of the late Kamakura period and a gokenin of the Kamakura shogunate, the seventh head of the powerful Oyama clan of Shimotsuke Province and lord of Oyama Castle. He received the character sada in his name from the regent Hōjō Sadatoki. In 1323, under the title Oyama Shimotsuke no Zenshi, he donated a hundred kanmon in cash at the thirteenth-anniversary memorial for Sadatoki. The record Jōraku-ki states that he died in 1330 aged forty-nine, and his son Hidetomo succeeded him.
zh: 小山贞朝（1282—1330）是镰仓时代末期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，下野国有力豪族小山氏的第七代当主、小山城城主。他名字中的“贞”字取自执权北条贞时的偏讳。1323年，他以“小山下野前司”之名，在北条贞时的十三回忌法会上捐钱百贯文。《常乐记》记载他于1330年去世，终年四十九岁，由其子秀朝继任。

en: Tokinaga Oyama was the fifth head of the Oyama clan of Shimotsuke Province, succeeding his father Nagamura and followed by his son Munenaga.
zh: 小山时长是下野国小山氏第五代当主，继父亲长村之后继位，家督后来由其子宗长继承。

en: Tomomasa Oyama was the second head of the Oyama clan and a leading gokenin of the early Kamakura shogunate, serving Minamoto no Yoritomo from 1180. In 1183 he feigned alliance with Shida Yoshihiro and ambushed him at Nogi-no-miya in Shimotsuke; wounded by an arrow, he still routed the rebel with his brother Munemasa. He fought the Taira under Minamoto no Noriyori, including Dan-no-ura in 1185, and joined the Ōshū campaign of 1189. He held the Shimotsuke and later Harima shugo posts, became Shimotsuke no kami in 1225, took the tonsure in 1234, and died in 1238 aged 84.
zh: 小山朝政是小山氏第二代当主、镰仓幕府早期的有力御家人，从1180年（治承四年）起便追随源赖朝。1183年（寿永二年），他假装加入志田义广一方，在下野野木宫设伏；虽中箭负伤，仍与弟弟长沼宗政合力将叛军击溃。此后他随源范赖追讨平氏，参加了1185年的坛之浦之战，1189年又随军出征奥州。他历任下野、播磨守护，1225年（嘉禄元年）出任下野守，1234年（天福二年）出家，1238年（嘉祯四年）去世，终年84岁。

en: Tomonaga Oyama was a Kamakura-period warrior, shugo of Shimotsuke and castellan of Oyama Castle, the legitimate heir of Tomomasa. Originally named Masayoshi and titled Saemon-no-jō, he first appears in 1193 as a yabusame archer at Tsurugaoka. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he served as a general of the Tōsandō army, helping defeat court forces at the Ōido crossing before entering Kyōto, and afterwards beheaded Hamuro Muneyuki in Suruga by shogunal order. He is thought to have received the Kaitō estate in Owari as a reward, and succeeded to the family headship. He died in 1229 aged 42, before his father.
zh: 小山朝长是镰仓时代武将，官至下野守护、小山城城主，为朝政的嫡子。他初名政义，任左卫门尉，1193年（建久四年）曾作为流镝马射手在鹤冈登场。1221年（承久三年）承久之乱中，他担任东山道大将，在大井户渡口击败京方军队，随后进入京都；乱后奉命在骏河国将叶室宗行斩首。据推测，他因功受封尾张国海东庄，并继承家督。1229年（宽喜元年）朝长先于父亲去世，年仅42岁。

en: Oyama Tomosato (died 1346), childhood name Jōkenmaru and first called Tomouji, was the ninth head of the Oyama warrior house of Shimotsuke Province. In 1335 his father Hidetomo was killed in the Nakasendai Rebellion, and Tomosato inherited the family domains and its shugo post while still a child, ruling under a guardian. In 1337 Kitabatake Akiie's Southern Court army seized Oyama Castle and captured him, but Yūki Munehiro interceded and spared his life. Around 1340 he was reportedly at war with his Northern Court-aligned brother Ujimasa. Tomosato died suddenly in May 1346 without children, and Ujimasa succeeded him.
zh: 小山朝郷（？—1346），幼名常犬丸，初名朝氏，是下野国小山武家的第九代当主。1335年中先代之乱中，父亲小山秀朝战死，朝郷幼年继承家族领地与守护职，在监护人辅佐下统治。1337年，南朝将领北畠显家的军队攻陷小山城，将他俘虏，因结城宗广进言而保住性命。约1340年，他与投靠北朝的弟弟氏政对立，据传兄弟之间爆发交战。1346年5月朝郷突然去世，没有子嗣，由氏政继位。

en: Oyama Ujimasa (1329–1355) was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts period and shugo of Shimotsuke Province. His father Hidetomo was killed fighting Hōjō Tokiyuki in the Nakasendai Rebellion of 1335, and the headship passed to Ujimasa's elder brother Tomosato. When Tomosato died without an heir in 1346, Ujimasa inherited the Oyama domains and the shugo post. He joined Ashikaga Takauji against Ashikaga Tadayoshi, fighting at Sattamine Pass in 1351 and Fuefuki Pass in 1352, then campaigned around Kyoto until his death in 1355, aged twenty-seven.
zh: 小山氏政（1329—1355）是日本南北朝时代的武将，任下野国守护。1335年中先代之乱中，父亲小山秀朝迎战北条时行时战死，家督由兄长小山朝郷继承。1346年朝郷无嗣而终，氏政遂继承小山氏领地与守护之职。他随足利尊氏讨伐足利直义，参加1351年的萨埵峠之战和1352年的笛吹峠之战，此后在京都周边转战，于1355年去世，年二十七岁。

en: Emperor Reizei (950–1011), personal name Norihira, was the 63rd emperor of Japan, reigning from 967 to 969. The second son of Emperor Murakami, he was made crown prince in infancy through the influence of the Fujiwara brothers Morosuke and Saneyori, displacing Murakami's eldest son. He grew up mentally ill, so when he ascended at eighteen Fujiwara no Saneyori governed as regent. In 969 the Anna Incident brought down the minister Minamoto no Takaakira, and Reizei abdicated the same year after a two-year reign. He lived forty-four years in retirement, dying in 1011; his sons became Emperors Kazan and Sanjō.
zh: 冷泉天皇（950—1011），名宪平，是日本第63代天皇，967年至969年在位。他是村上天皇的第二子，因藤原师辅、藤原实赖兄弟的影响，在襁褓中即被立为太子，取代了村上长子的地位。他成年后患有精神疾病，因此十八岁即位时由藤原实赖以摄政身份主政。969年安和事件扳倒了大臣源高明，冷泉也于同年退位，在位仅两年。退位后他又度过了四十四年，1011年去世；他的儿子后来成为花山天皇与三条天皇。

en: Rokkaku Tokinobu (1306–1346) was head of the Rokkaku, the main Sasaki line, and shugo of Ōmi Province. He succeeded his father Yoritsuna in 1311 and came of age in 1314. In the Genkō War of 1331 he fought for the Kamakura shogunate against Enryaku-ji monks at Karasaki and joined the siege of Kasagiyama, later guarding the captured Prince Takayoshi. In 1333 he submitted to the imperial court and served in the Kenmu government. After following Ashikaga Takauji, he lost the Ōmi shugo post to Sasaki Dōyo of the Kyōgoku branch, took vows, passed the family headship to his son Ujiyori, and died in 1346.
zh: 六角时信（1306—1346）是佐佐木氏嫡流六角氏的第三代当主、近江国守护。1311年父亲赖纲死后继承家督，1314年元服。1331年元弘之乱中，他站在镰仓幕府一方，在近江唐崎与响应后醍醐天皇的延历寺僧众交战，又参加笠置山之战，战后看管被俘的尊良亲王。1333年他归降朝廷，在建武政权的杂诉决断所任职。追随足利尊氏后，近江守护职被庶流京极氏的佐佐木道誉夺走，遂出家，将家督让给儿子氏赖，1346年去世。

en: Rokkaku Ujiyori (1326–1370) was a Nanboku-chō warlord and shugo of Ōmi Province, the fourth head of the Rokkaku. He succeeded his father Tokinobu as family head and Ōmi shugo around 1335 while still a child and was overshadowed by Sasaki Dōyo of the Kyōgoku branch, whose daughter he married. In 1338 he helped check Kitabatake Akiie's Southern Court army on the Ōmi–Mino border, and in 1344 he was made a palace police chief. During the Kannō Disturbance he switched to the Tadayoshi faction, took vows and resigned as shugo in 1351. He returned as Ōmi shugo in 1354 and in 1361 founded Eigen-ji, dying in 1370.
zh: 六角氏赖（1326—1370）是日本南北朝时代的武将、近江国守护，六角氏第四代当主。约1335年父亲时信出家后，他幼年继承家督与近江守护职，地位长期受庶流京极氏的佐佐木道誉压制，后娶道誉之女改善关系。1338年，他与道誉一同在近江、美浓边境抵御南朝北畠显家的军队，1344年任检非违使。观应之扰乱中他改投足利直义一方，1351年出家并辞去守护职。1354年他重任近江守护，1361年迎寂室元光开创永源寺，1370年去世。

en: Sasaki Yasutsuna, also called Rokkaku Yasutsuna (1213–1276), was a Kamakura-period gokenin and shugo of Ōmi Province, regarded as the founder of the Rokkaku branch of the Sasaki; the name came from his residence at Rokkaku-Higashinotōin in Kyoto. The third son of Sasaki Nobutsuna, he served as kebiishi and on the Rokuhara council. Favoured by Shogun Kujō Yoritsune, he drew Hōjō suspicion and lost scattered Ōmi estates in a 1243 feud with his brother. He later passed the headship to his son Yoritsuna, took the tonsure as Seisei, and died in 1276.
zh: 佐佐木泰纲，又称六角泰纲（1213—1276），镰仓时代中期武将、御家人，官至近江国守护，被视为佐佐木氏六角流（六角氏）之祖，“六角”得自其在京都六角东洞院的居所。他是佐佐木信纲第三子，曾任检非违使与六波罗评定众。因受将军九条赖经宠爱而遭北条氏忌惮，1243年与兄长争夺领地时，散在近江的领地被没收。后来他把家督让给儿子赖纲，出家号生西，于1276年去世。

en: Sasaki Yoritsuna, also called Rokkaku Yoritsuna (1242–1311), was a Kamakura-period gokenin, shugo of Ōmi Province, and the second head of the Rokkaku house. In 1250 he came of age at Hōjō Tokiyori's residence, taking the character yori from Tokiyori's name, and served the shogunate as saemon-no-jō and governor of Bitchū. He joined the Rokuhara council in 1277 and extended his shugo powers, even taxing the shrine lands of Chikubushima. A territorial quarrel with the monks of Kōfuku-ji in 1307 led to his exile to Owari in 1308, and he died there in 1311.
zh: 佐佐木赖纲，又称六角赖纲（1242—1311），镰仓时代中期武将、御家人，近江国守护，六角氏第二代当主。1250年在北条时赖邸元服，受时赖偏讳取名赖纲，随后出仕幕府，任左卫门尉、备中守。1277年加入六波罗评定众，并向竹生岛寺社领地征税，强化守护权力。1307年他因领土争端与兴福寺对立，1308年被流放尾张国，1311年死于当地。

en: Rokujō (1164–1176), the infant son of Emperor Nijō, was named crown prince before his first birthday and enthroned in 1165 at eight months old, when his dying father abdicated. Government was run throughout by his grandfather, retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa. In 1168 the Taira clan pressed for his removal, and Go-Shirakawa deposed him in favour of his uncle Takakura. Rokujō lived on as a retired emperor and died of dysentery in 1176 at the age of eleven, leaving neither consort nor children.
zh: 六条天皇（1164—1176）是二条天皇尚在襁褓中的儿子，未满周岁即被立为太子，1165年病笃的父亲让位时，他出生仅八个月便登基。政务始终由祖父后白河上皇以院政裁断。1168年，平家施压要求废帝，后白河将他废黜，改立其叔父高仓天皇。六条以退位上皇身份度过余生，1176年死于痢疾，年仅十一岁，没有后妃与子女。

en: Imperial Prince Sadasumi (873–916), also called Prince Momozono, was the sixth son of Emperor Seiwa. Invested as an imperial prince in 873, he held senior court posts under Emperor Uda, serving as titular governor of the princely provinces of Kazusa and Kōzuke and as head of the Nakatsukasa and Hyōbu ministries, though his rank never rose above the fourth imperial grade. He died in 916. His son Minamoto no Tsunemoto founded the Seiwa Genji, from whom the Kamakura, Ashikaga and Tokugawa shogunal houses claimed descent.
zh: 贞纯亲王（873—916），号桃园亲王，是清和天皇的第六子。他于873年获亲王宣下，宇多天皇朝历任上总、上野两个亲王任国的太守，又任中务卿、兵部卿，位阶止于四品，916年去世。其子源经基开创清和源氏，镰仓、足利、德川三个武家政权都自称出自这一血脉。

en: Emperor Saga (786–842) was the 52nd emperor of Japan, reigning from 809 to 823. A son of Emperor Kanmu, he succeeded his brother Heizei and in 810 defeated the retired emperor's attempt to reclaim the throne in the Kusuko Incident. He founded the kurōdo-dokoro and the kebiishi police to strengthen court administration. His peaceful reign saw a flowering of Tang-style culture: he was counted among the three great calligraphers of the early Heian age, and from 814 he gave many of his children the surname Minamoto, originating the Saga Genji. He abdicated in 823 in favor of Emperor Junna.
zh: 嵯峨天皇（786—842）是日本第52代天皇，809年至823年在位。他是桓武天皇之子，继兄长平城天皇即位，810年在药子之变中挫败了上皇复位的企图。他设立藏人所与检非违使，强化朝廷治理。其治世长久太平，唐风文化兴盛，他本人被列为平安初期“三笔”之一；自814年起，他将众多皇子皇女赐姓源氏，是为嵯峨源氏之祖。823年他让位于淳和天皇。

en: Ōe no Chikahiro was a Kamakura-period gokenin, the eldest son of Ōe no Hiromoto, first head of the shogunate's Mandokoro. In 1192 he inherited the jitō post of Sagae manor in Dewa province, seed of the Sagae clan. He served the shōguns in Kamakura and married a daughter of Hōjō Yoshitoki. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he sided with Retired Emperor Go-Toba, fought the shogunate army in Ōmi, and disappeared after the defeat at Uji. Tradition says he retired to Sagae manor, where he died on 17 January 1242 and was buried at the Amida hall in Yoshikawa.
zh: 大江亲广是镰仓时代前期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，为政所初代别当大江广元的长子。1192年，他继承出羽国寒河江庄的地头职，这一领地后来成为寒河江氏的根基。他在镰仓侍奉历代将军，娶北条义时之女为妻。1221年承久之乱中，他响应后鸟羽上皇加入官军，在近江与幕府军交战，宇治战败后下落不明。相传他隐居寒河江庄，1242年1月17日在吉川去世，葬于阿弥陀堂旁。

en: Ōe no Hirotoki was a Kamakura-period gokenin, a son of Ōe no Chikahiro and grandson of Ōe no Hiromoto. Although his father had backed the losing court side in the Jōkyū War of 1221, Hirotoki entered shogunate service through his elder brother Sukefusa's war record, appearing in the Azuma Kagami by 1238 as an official in the shōgun's retinue. After his brother Takamoto, who held Sagae manor, died young in 1254, Takamoto's wife briefly inherited it before Hirotoki succeeded to the Dewa estate, though its northern portion passed to the Hōjō. He stayed in Kamakura and governed Sagae through a deputy. His eldest son was Masahiro.
zh: 大江广时是镰仓时代前期的幕府御家人，大江亲广之子、大江广元之孙。尽管父亲在1221年承久之乱中站在失败的朝廷一方，他仍凭兄长佐房的战功出仕幕府，《吾妻镜》1238年的记载中他已作为随将军上洛的官吏登场。领有寒河江庄的兄长高元于1254年早逝，高元之妻短暂接管后，广时继承了这处出羽庄园，但其北部被没收成为北条氏领地。他本人留驻镰仓，派代官管理寒河江庄。长子为大江政广。

en: Ōe no Masahiro was a Kamakura-period gokenin and the fourth head of the Sagae line, great-grandson of Ōe no Hiromoto and son of Ōe no Hirotoki. On his father's death in 1262 he succeeded to Sagae manor in Dewa, but like him remained in Kamakura, administering the estate through a deputy. In 1266 he presented a large bell to the Ōnuma Daigyō-in monastery, and in 1275 he contributed fifteen kan toward the building of the new Rokujō Hachiman Shrine. He died in 1277 and was succeeded by his heir Mototaka, who is thought to have gone to Sagae manor around 1285.
zh: 大江政广是镰仓时代前期的幕府御家人、寒河江氏第四代当主，大江广元的曾孙、大江广时之子。1262年父亲去世后，他继承出羽国寒河江庄，但和父亲一样留居镰仓，派代官管理庄园。1266年，他向大沼大行院奉献大钟一口；1275年又为六条八幡新宫的营造捐钱十五贯。他于1277年去世，由继承人元显继任，元显据认为约于1285年前往寒河江庄。

en: Sagae Motomasa, also recorded as Ōe no Motomasa (died 1359), was a Nanbokuchō-era commander and head of the Sagae branch of the Ōe clan at Sagae manor in Murayama district, Dewa Province, and a fifth-generation descendant of Ōe no Hiromoto. He succeeded his father in 1322. Siding with the Southern Court, he marched on Kyoto with Kitabatake Akiie in 1335 and helped rout Ashikaga Takauji at Teshimagawara in Settsu in January 1336, driving him to Kyushu. By 1351 he had recovered the Kita-Sagae manor seized by the Hōjō. In 1359 he fell fighting Shiba Kaneyori.
zh: 寒河江元政（即大江元政，？—1359）是南北朝时代的武将，出羽国村山郡寒河江庄寒河江大江氏的当主，大江广元的五世孙。1322年父亲大江元顕死后，他继任家督。南北朝纷争中他站在南朝一方，1335年随北畠显家上京与足利尊氏军作战，1336年1月又在摄津国丰岛河原合战中击败尊氏，迫其逃往九州。到1351年，他收复了此前被北条氏没收的北寒河江庄。1359年，他在与斯波兼赖的交战中战死。

en: Sagae Mototaka, also called Ōe no Mototaka, was a Kamakura-period gokenin and the fifth head of the Sagae house of Dewa Province. In 1277 he succeeded his father Ōe no Masahiro as head of the family, serving the shogunate in Kamakura. After the Shimotsuki Disturbance of 1285 killed several of his Ōe kinsmen, he withdrew to the Sagae manor to escape Hōjō pressure, rebuilt the burned Jion-ji temple, and consolidated rule over the estate. He died in 1322 and was succeeded by his eldest son Motomasa.
zh: 寒河江元显，又称大江元显，是镰仓时代的御家人，出羽寒河江氏第五代当主。1277年父亲大江政广去世后，他继承家督，起初在镰仓担任幕府职务。1285年霜月骚动中大江氏族人多人战死，他为避北条氏的压力移居寒河江庄，重建烧毁的慈恩寺，并确立对庄内的支配。1322年他去世，由长子大江元政继位。

en: Sagae Tokishige, also recorded as Ōe no Tokishige (died 1373), was the seventh head of the Sagae Ōe clan in Dewa Province. Succeeding his father Motomasa after he fell fighting Shiba Kaneyori in 1359, he posted his sons and kinsmen in new forts across Sagae manor. At the battle of Urushigawa in 1368 his heir Shigenobu led the clan against Shiba Kaneyori and Osaki Naomochi and was crushingly defeated, with sixty-one clansmen killing themselves. Tokishige kept the main manor but lost Kita-Sagae. He died in 1373, bidding his surviving fourth son Tokiuji to make peace with the Northern Court.
zh: 寒河江时茂（即大江时茂，？—1373）是出羽国寒河江大江氏第七代当主。1359年父亲元政在与斯波兼赖的交战中战死后，他继任家督，把儿子与一族子弟分派到寒河江庄各地，新筑楯堡设防。1368年漆川之战中，嫡男茂信率领一族迎战斯波兼赖与大崎直持，结果惨败，一族61人自尽。时茂虽保住寒河江庄本处，却失去了北寒河江庄。他于1373年去世，临终遗命幸存的四男时氏向北朝请和。

en: Sagara Chikayori, born Kudō no Chikayori, was a Heian-period warrior who settled at Sagara manor in Tōtōmi Province and took Sagara as his family name. He had no son, so adopted Mitsuyori, grandson of his Itō kinsman Suketoki, as heir.
zh: 相良周赖，本姓工藤，是平安时代的武士，定居远江国相良庄，首次以相良为家族苗字。他没有儿子，于是收亲族伊东祐时之孙光赖为养子，令其继承家督。

en: Sagara Mitsuyori was a Heian-period warrior born into the Itō house, a Kudō offshoot of Fujiwara descent. The son of Itō Sukemitsu and grandson of Suketoki, he was adopted by childless Sagara Chikayori and so continued the Sagara line in Tōtōmi Province.
zh: 相良光赖是平安时代的武士，出身工藤氏支族伊东家，为伊东祐光之子、伊东祐时之孙。无子的相良周赖收他为养子，他由此继承了远江国的相良家。

en: Sagara Nagauji (died c. 1355), fourth head of the Sagara clan in Higo Province, Kyushu, succeeded his father Yoritoshi in 1287 and in 1311 left a testament of clan rules. In 1326 he took vows as Rendō and passed the headship to his son Yorihiro, yet kept real authority. In 1333 he sent three sons to join Prince Takayoshi's anti-Hōjō rising, helping destroy the Chinzei tandai at Dazaifu. In 1338 Shōni Yorihisa granted him the northern Hitoyoshi lands, which he gave to his grandson Sadayori. He later mediated peace among warring kinsmen and died around 1355, outliving his son.
zh: 相良长氏（？—约1355）是九州肥后国相良氏第四代当主。1287年他从父亲赖俊手中继任家督，1311年留下记载一族规范的置文。1326年他剃发出家，法号莲道，把家督让给儿子赖广，但仍掌握实权。1333年元弘之乱中，他派三个儿子投奔尊良亲王的倒幕军，参与攻灭设在大宰府的镇西探题。1338年少贰赖尚把人吉庄北方的旧北条氏领地赏给他，他却越过赖广直接给了孙子定赖。后来他调解一族间的战事，促成和议，约1355年去世，死时赖广已先他而去。

en: Sagara Nagayori (1177–1254) was a Kamakura vassal and the first Sagara lord of Hitoyoshi in Higo. Born at Sagara manor in Tōtōmi, he was sent to Kyushu by Yoritomo in 1198 and, with local warrior Hirakawa Yoshitaka, destroyed the Yaze and seized Hitoyoshi Castle. In 1205 his vanguard service at the Battle of Futamatagawa won him the jitō post of Hitoyoshi manor; in the 1221 Jōkyū War he fought at the Uji River and recovered the family's Tōtōmi lands. He died at Hitoyoshi in 1254 and was succeeded by his son Yorichika.
zh: 相良长赖（1177—1254）是镰仓幕府御家人，也是相良氏在肥后人吉的初代当主。他生于远江国相良庄，1198年奉源赖朝之命下向九州，借助当地豪族平川义高讨灭矢濑氏，夺取人吉城。1205年二俣川之战他立下先锋之功，获任人吉庄地头；1221年承久之乱中，他在宇治川奋战，恢复了家族在远江的旧领。1254年他在人吉去世，由儿子赖亲继任。

en: Sagara Sadayori (died 1372) was the sixth head of the Sagara clan in Higo Province and a Northern Court commander in the Nanbokuchō wars. In 1335 he and his grandfather Nagauji submitted to the Shōni of Kyushu. From 1336 he fought the Southern Court partisan Taraki Tsuneyori in Kuma, took Kiue Castle, and in 1338 a land grant from Nagauji made him lord of Hitoyoshi. He rejected Prince Kanenaga's overtures in 1346, campaigned in Hyūga, and was named Ōsumi no kami in 1352. He retired as the monk Keia about 1370 and died in 1372, several retainers dying after him.
zh: 相良定赖（？—1372）是肥后国相良氏第六代当主，南北朝纷争中始终支持北朝武家政权。1335年，他与祖父长氏一同归顺九州的少贰氏。1336年起，他在球磨郡与南朝方的多良木经赖连年交战，攻落木上城；1338年长氏把人吉庄北方的领地转给他，他成为名实相符的人吉城主。1346年他拒绝怀良亲王一方的劝诱，后来又出兵日向，1352年叙任大隅守。约1370年他出家隐居，法名契阿，1372年去世，数名家臣为他殉死。

en: Sagara Yorichika (1197–1264), the second Sagara lord of Hitoyoshi, was the eldest son of Nagayori. Coming of age in Kamakura, he attended shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo; when Sanetomo was assassinated in 1219, he took Buddhist orders and later received a Zen master title from Emperor Go-Fukakusa, becoming Kansen Zenji. He long managed the family's affairs at Hitoyoshi while his father served in the east, and founded Inokuchi Hachiman shrine in 1247. He succeeded as head in 1254 but later yielded the lordship to his brother Yoritoshi and retired.
zh: 相良赖亲（1197—1264）是相良氏第二代当主、长赖的长子。他在镰仓元服，曾随侍将军源实朝；1219年实朝遇刺后，他剃发出家，后获后深草天皇赐禅师号，称观仙禅师。父亲长期赴东国期间，他留守人吉，掌管家族内政，并于1247年创建井口八幡神社。1254年他继任家督，后来将家督让给弟弟赖俊，自己隐居。

en: Sagara Yorihiro was a son of Mitsuyori and an ancestor of Yorishige in a genealogy of the Sagara family of Tōtōmi.
zh: 相良赖宽是远江相良氏系谱所载的光赖之子、赖繁的祖先。

en: Sagara Yorihiro (died c. 1338) was the fifth head of the Sagara clan in Higo Province. In 1326 his father Nagauji passed him the headship, and the Kamakura shogunate appointed him jitō of the Hitoyoshi and Naritsune manors, though Nagauji kept real influence. In 1333 he joined Nitta Yoshisada's attack on Kamakura, then marched to Kyushu to serve Prince Takayoshi under the Shōni, winning court confirmation of the clan's Higo and Buzen lands. In 1334 he helped crush a Hōjō remnant revolt, and in 1336 he raided Ashikaga Takauji's estate in Hyūga. He had yielded the Kuma lands to Sadayori and died around 1338.
zh: 相良赖广（？—约1338）是肥后国相良氏第五代当主。1326年父亲长氏把家督让给他，镰仓幕府也承认他对人吉庄、成恒庄等地的地头职，但长氏作为后见人仍握有实权。1333年他参加新田义贞攻打镰仓，随后率兵前往九州，在少贰氏麾下护卫尊良亲王，使朝廷承认相良家在肥后、丰前两国的领地。1334年他参与讨伐北条氏残党的起兵，1336年又随新田一方的武士袭击足利尊氏在日向国的领地。他此前已把球磨郡领地让给定赖，约1338年前后去世。

en: Sagara Yorikage was steward of Sagara manor in Tōtōmi Province when Minamoto no Yoritomo rose against the Taira in 1180, and he fought on the Taira side until their fall in 1185. His lands were confiscated, but repeated apologies won his pardon and a place among the Kamakura shogunate's vassals. In 1193 he received Taragi manor in Kuma district, Higo, and went down to Kyushu. In 1197 he met Yoritomo at Kamakura, joined the pilgrimage to Zenkō-ji, and was confirmed in Taragi as his holding.
zh: 相良赖景是远江国相良庄的庄司。1180年源赖朝举兵讨伐平氏时，他站在平氏一方作战，直到1185年平氏灭亡。其领地一度被没收，但他再三谢罪而获赦，出仕镰仓幕府成为御家人。1193年，他受领肥后国球磨郡的多良木庄，下向九州；1197年他前往镰仓谒见赖朝，随赖朝参拜善光寺，被列入御家人之列，多良木庄也正式成为他的所领。

en: Sagara Yorishige was the father of Yorikage and a descendant of Yorihiro in a genealogy of the Sagara family of Tōtōmi.
zh: 相良赖繁是远江相良氏系谱所载的赖景之父、赖宽的后裔。

en: Sagara Yoritoshi was the third Sagara lord of Hitoyoshi and a younger son of Nagayori. His father granted him lands south of Hitoyoshi manor in 1246, and he received Naritsune manor in Buzen as a reward for military service in 1251. He took the headship when his brother Yorichika stepped aside. During the second Mongol invasion in 1281, though already old, he led Sagara troops under Kikuchi Takefusa at Hakata, capturing enemy soldiers driven onto Mount Goryū by the typhoon and beheading them on the beach. He was rewarded with Ashikita district and yielded the headship to his son Nagauji in 1287, dying around 1311.
zh: 相良赖俊是相良氏第三代当主、长赖之子。1246年他从父亲手中获封人吉庄南方的领地，1251年又因军功受领丰前国的成恒庄；兄长赖亲让位后，他继任当主。1281年弘安之役时，他虽已年迈，仍亲自率兵在博多跟随菊池武房迎战元军，把被台风卷上五龙山的敌兵尽数俘获、在博多津处斩，因功受封苇北郡。1287年他把家督让给儿子长氏后隐居，约于1311年去世。

en: Sahara Mitsumori was a Kamakura-period warrior, the fourth son of Sahara Moritsura and Yabe Zenni, daughter of Miura Yoshimura. He inherited the headship of the Sahara house, a Miura clan offshoot holding Aizu since his grandfather Sahara Yoshitsura received it after the Ōshū campaign of 1189. When the main Miura house was destroyed in the Hōji Conflict of 1247, Mitsumori and his brothers fought for the Hōjō and survived. A branch of the Sahara in Aizu took the name Ashina, from which the later Ashina lords of Aizu descended. His sons included Ashina Tsunemitsu and Ashina Yasumori.
zh: 佐原光盛是镰仓时代武将，佐原盛连与三浦义村之女矢部禅尼的第四子。他继承了佐原氏家督；佐原氏是三浦氏的支流，自其祖父佐原义连在1189年奥州之战后受封会津以来，便领有该地。1247年宝治合战中三浦本宗覆灭，光盛与兄弟站在北条一方作战，得以幸存。佐原氏在会津的一支以芦名为姓，后来的会津芦名氏即出自这一支。其子有芦名经光、芦名泰盛等。

en: Sahara Moritsura was a warrior of the early Kamakura period and the second son of Sahara Yoshitsura. He married Yabe-zenni, formerly wife of the regent Hōjō Yasutoki, and became stepfather to Hōjō Tokiuji. In 1221 he fought for the shogunate in the Jōkyū War under Miura Yoshimura. While in Kyoto in 1226 he rioted drunkenly as far as Uji, wounding people, which earned him the nickname Aku-Tōtōmi-no-kami, the wicked governor of Tōtōmi. In disgrace he wandered the provinces; attempting to force his way into Kyoto in 1233, he was killed in the fifth month.
zh: 佐原盛连是镰仓时代前期的武将，佐原氏始祖佐原义连的次子。他娶了执权北条泰时的前妻、三浦义村之女矢部禅尼，由此成为北条时氏的继父。1221年承久之乱时，他隶属三浦义村麾下为幕府而战。1226年在京都期间，他醉酒行凶，一路闹到宇治伤人，由此得了“恶远江守”的绰号。失势后他流落各国数年，1233年试图强行进入京都，于五月被杀。

en: Sahara Tokitsura, also called Yokosuka Tokitsura, was a Kamakura warrior, a son of Sahara Moritsura by Yabe Zenni, daughter of Miura Yoshimura. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 he and his brothers fought for the Hōjō, so their line survived the ruin of the Miura.
zh: 佐原时连，又称横须贺时连，是镰仓时代武将，佐原盛连之妻、三浦义村之女矢部禅尼所生之子。1247年宝治合战时，他与兄弟为北条一方作战，三浦氏覆灭后，其一支得以保全。

en: Sahara Yoshitsura was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, the youngest son of the Sagami magnate Miura Yoshiaki; he took the name Sahara from his castle southeast of the Miura seat at Kinugasa. In 1180 he joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's uprising and became a founding gokenin. He fought under Minamoto no Yoshitsune at the Battle of Ichinotani, where the Heike Monogatari depicts him as the first rider to charge down the Hiyodorigoe descent. He later held posts in Kii and Tōtōmi and served as shugo of Izumi from 1196 until his death around 1203.
zh: 佐原义连是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，相模豪强三浦义明的末子，因居住在三浦氏本据点衣笠城东南的佐原城而称佐原氏。1180年源赖朝举兵时，他随一族投奔，成为幕府御家人。治承寿永之乱中，他在一之谷之战隶属源义经的搦手军，《平家物语》描写他在“鹎越逆落”中最先纵马冲下陡坡。他后来在纪伊和远江任职，1196年起担任和泉国守护，约1203年去世。

en: Saitō no Iden was a tenth-century warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line and grandson of Fujiwara no Nobumochi. As ōryōshi, military commander of Echizen Province, he founded the Echizen Saitō; his sons Tamenobu and Norimitsu began the Hikita and Yoshihara branches.
zh: 斋藤伊传是10世纪的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，为藤原叙用之孙。他任越前国押领使，开创越前斋藤氏，其子为延、则光分别是疋田斋藤氏与吉原斋藤氏之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Masashige was an eleventh-century warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line, son of Fujiwara no Sadamasa. His son Fujiwara no Kagemichi served the Kawachi Genji and fought against Abe no Sadatō in the Zenkunen War; he was counted ancestor of the Katō clan.
zh: 藤原正重是11世纪的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，为藤原贞正之子。其子藤原景通侍奉河内源氏，在陆奥的前九年之役中与安倍贞任作战，被视为加藤氏之祖。

en: Saitō no Sōsuke was an eleventh-century warrior of the Hirooka Saitō house in Kaga Province and son of Saitō no Yoshimune. Genealogies name him father of Togashi no Iekuni; the Hirooka Saitō later gave rise to the Togashi and Hayashi clans.
zh: 斋藤宗助是11世纪的武将，属加贺国弘冈斋藤氏，为斋藤吉宗之子。谱系以他为富樫家国之父；弘冈斋藤氏后来分出富樫氏与林氏。

en: Fujiwara no Nobumochi was a nobleman of the mid-tenth century and the second son of Chinjufu shōgun Fujiwara no Toshihito, of the Northern House of the Fujiwara. He rose to junior fifth rank, upper grade, served as an imperial secretary and around 950 was appointed Saigū no kami, director of the office serving the Ise princess. From the title Saigū and his Fujiwara surname he took the new name Saitō, becoming the ancestor of the Saitō clan.
zh: 藤原叙用是10世纪中叶的贵族，为镇守府将军藤原利仁的次子，出自藤原北家鱼名流。他叙从五位上，曾任藏人，约950年出任斋宫头，掌管侍奉伊势斋宫的机构。他从斋宫一职与藤原本姓中各取一字，以斋藤为号，成为斋藤氏之祖。

en: Fujiwara no Sadamasa was a mid-Heian warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line and a son of Bungo no kami Fujiwara no Shigemitsu. In 985 he joined the Takiguchi palace guard on the recommendation of Fujiwara no Sanesuke, head chamberlain of the imperial secretariat. In 989 he and his cousin Fujiwara no Tamenobu shot dead Mikuni Yukimasa, a strongman of Echizen Province, at Awataguchi in Kyoto; the court sent Kebiishi police to arrest him, but in vain. His son Masashige's descendants took the name Katō and served the Kawachi Minamoto.
zh: 藤原贞正是平安时代中期的武士，出自藤原北家利仁流，为丰后守藤原重光之子。985年，经藏人头藤原实资推举，他成为泷口武者。989年，他在京都粟田口与表亲藤原为延合谋，射杀越前国豪族三国行正；朝廷派检非违使前往搜捕，却未能拿获。其子正重的后代以加藤为姓，成为河内源氏的郎党。

en: Fujiwara no Shigemitsu was a tenth-century warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line who served as Bungo no kami. Genealogies name him a son of Fujiwara no Yoshinobu and father of Fujiwara no Sadamasa; the Katō and Tōyama clans traced their descent to him.
zh: 藤原重光是10世纪的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，曾任丰后守。谱系以他为藤原吉信之子、藤原贞正之父，加藤氏与远山氏都从他这一支分出。

en: Saitō no Tadayori was a tenth-century warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line and grandson of Fujiwara no Nobumochi. Appointed Kaga no suke, he extended Saitō power from Echizen into Kaga and founded the Kaga and Hirooka Saitō houses; his son was Yoshimune.
zh: 斋藤忠赖是10世纪的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，为藤原叙用之孙。他出任加贺介，把斋藤氏的势力从越前扩展到加贺，开创加贺斋藤氏与弘冈斋藤氏，其子为吉宗。

en: Saitō no Yoshimune was a late-tenth-century warrior of the Fujiwara Toshihito line, the son of Kaga no suke Saitō no Tadayori. He founded the Hirooka Saitō house in Kaga Province, from which the Togashi and Hayashi clans later sprang.
zh: 斋藤吉宗是10世纪后期的武将，出自藤原北家利仁流，为加贺介斋藤忠赖之子。他开创加贺国弘冈斋藤氏，后来的富樫氏与林氏都从这一支分出。

en: Fujiwara no Yoshinobu was a mid-Heian nobleman, a son of the Saigū no kami Fujiwara no Nobumochi, who founded the Saitō name. Genealogies name him father of Tadayori, Shigemitsu and Iden.
zh: 藤原吉信是平安时代中期的贵族，为创立斋藤之号的斋宫头藤原叙用之子。据谱系记载，他生子忠赖、重光与伊传。

en: Samukawa no Ama (1138–1228) was a daughter of Hatta Munetsuna and a wet nurse of Minamoto no Yoritomo. She became the second wife of the Shimotsuke warrior chieftain Oyama Masamitsu and the mother of Yūki Tomomitsu. In 1180, while Masamitsu was on guard duty in Kyoto, she brought her fourteen-year-old son to Yoritomo's camp at Sumida in Musashi; Yoritomo personally presided over his coming-of-age, and the Oyama warrior band joined the rising against the Taira. In 1187 Yoritomo appointed her land steward of Samukawa District and Ajito in Shimotsuke in recognition of her merit.
zh: 寒河尼（1138—1228）是八田宗纲之女、源赖朝的乳母之一，后嫁与下野国豪族小山政光为继室，生下结城朝光。1180年源赖朝举兵讨伐平氏时，政光正以大番役身份在京，她携十四岁的朝光前往武藏国隅田宿谒见赖朝，赖朝亲自为朝光主持元服，小山氏武士团就此加入赖朝阵营。1187年，赖朝称她虽为女性却立有大功，任命她为下野国寒川郡与网户乡的地头。

en: Sanjō Kiminori (1103–1160) was a late-Heian court noble, son of Sanjō Saneyuki and second head of the Sanjō house. Through his cousin Bifukumon'in he won the cloistered Emperor Toba's trust as steward of the retired-emperor's office. In 1155 he joined the council that placed Go-Shirakawa on the throne, and in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 served him with Tadamichi and Shinzei, becoming minister of the centre in 1157. During the Heiji Disturbance he helped Emperor Nijō flee the palace to Taira no Kiyomori at Rokuhara. He died of dysentery in 1160, before his father; his diary was called Kyōgyōki.
zh: 三条公教（1103—1160）是平安时代后期的公卿，太政大臣三条实行之子，三条家第二代当主。他凭借与表亲美福门院的关系得到鸟羽法皇的信任，被委任为院厅的执事别当。1155年，他参与决定拥立雅仁亲王（后白河天皇）的秘密会议；1156年保元之乱时，他与藤原忠通、信西一同侍奉后白河天皇，1157年升任内大臣。平治之乱中，他设计让二条天皇脱出内里，行幸平清盛所在的六波罗。1160年他因赤痢急逝，死在父亲之前，著有日记《教业记》。

en: Sanjō Sanefusa (1147–1225) was a late-Heian to early-Kamakura court noble and poet, the third son of Sanjō Kiminori and third head of the Sanjō house. He took his first rank in 1152 and joined the senior nobility at junior third rank in 1160, aged fourteen. After Minamoto no Yoritomo's court reforms he became a gisō councillor and steward of the retired Go-Shirakawa's office. He became minister of the right in 1189 and minister of the left in 1190, resigned through illness in 1196 and took Buddhist vows as Seikū. His diary is the Gumaiki.
zh: 三条实房（1147—1225）是平安时代后期至镰仓时代前期的公卿、歌人，内大臣三条公教的第三子，三条家第三代当主。他1152年叙爵，1160年十四岁时叙从三位，跻身公卿之列。源赖朝改革朝政后，他被任命为议奏公卿，又兼任后白河院的别当。1189年任右大臣，1190年转任左大臣，1196年因病辞职，次月出家，法名静空。其日记名为《愚昧记》。

en: Sanjō Saneyuki (1080–1162), also called Fujiwara no Saneyuki, was a late-Heian court noble and the second son of Fujiwara no Kinzane. As the half-brother of Taikenmon'in, mother of Emperors Sutoku and Go-Shirakawa, he served the retired Emperor Sutoku and rose with backing from Sutoku and Fujiwara no Yorinaga: he was named minister of the right in 1149 and junior first-rank grand minister in 1150. After Yorinaga's disgrace in 1155 he parted from the Sutoku faction and escaped the Hōgen Disturbance. He retired in 1157, took Buddhist vows as Renkaku in 1160, and founded the Sanjō house.
zh: 三条实行（1080—1162）又名藤原实行，是平安时代后期的公卿、藤原公实的次子。他是崇德、后白河两位天皇生母待贤门院的异母兄，因此近侍崇德上皇，并依靠崇德上皇与藤原赖长的支持步步高升，1149年任右大臣，1150年叙从一位太政大臣。1155年赖长失势后，他脱离崇德上皇一派，因而未被卷入保元之乱。1157年他上表致仕，1160年出家，法名莲觉。三条家由他而始。

en: Emperor Sanjō (976–1017), personal name Okisada, was the second son of Emperor Reizei and the sixty-seventh sovereign of Japan. Named crown prince in 986 after his younger cousin Ichijō became emperor, he only took the throne in 1011. Prince Atsunari became crown prince that year, while Sanjō's relations with Fujiwara no Michinaga grew strained. Having lost his sight, Sanjō abdicated in 1016 on condition that his eldest son Atsuakira become crown prince. He took Buddhist vows in 1017 and died months later; that year Atsuakira withdrew from the succession under Michinaga's pressure. His daughter Teishi became mother of Emperor Go-Sanjō.
zh: 三条天皇（976—1017）名居贞，是冷泉天皇的次子、日本第六十七代天皇。986年，年纪比他小的堂弟一条天皇即位后，他被立为皇太子，直到1011年才即位。同年敦成亲王被立为皇太子，而三条天皇与藤原道长的关系日渐紧张。1016年三条天皇因双目失明，以长子敦明亲王立为皇太子为条件退位。1017年他出家，数月后去世；同年敦明在道长的压力下辞去储位。其女祯子内亲王是后三条天皇的生母。

en: Sasaki no Hideyoshi (1112–1184) was lord of Sasaki Manor in Gamō District, Ōmi Province, and father of the four Sasaki brothers who served Minamoto no Yoritomo. He fought under Minamoto no Yoshitomo in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 and the Heiji Disturbance of 1159; after the defeat he sheltered for twenty years with Shibuya no Shigekuni in Sagami. In 1180 he sent his son Sadatsuna to warn Yoritomo of a planned attack and committed his sons to his rising. In 1184 he fell fighting Taira remnants at Kaminomura in Kōga, and was posthumously made provisional governor of Ōmi.
zh: 佐佐木秀义（1112—1184）是近江国蒲生郡佐佐木庄的领主，也是后来侍奉源赖朝的佐佐木四兄弟之父。1156年保元之乱和1159年平治之乱中，他都随源义朝作战；兵败后逃往关东，在相模国涩谷重国处受庇护达二十年。1180年，他派儿子定纲向源赖朝通报讨伐密谋，并让诸子投奔赖朝举兵。1184年，他在甲贺郡上野村讨伐伊贺、伊势的平氏残党时战死，死后被追赠为近江权守。

en: Minamoto no Nariyori (976–1003) was a mid-Heian noble of the Uda Genji line, the eldest son of the councillor Minamoto no Sukenori. The Sonpi Bunmyaku gives him junior fifth rank and posts in the imperial guards, while the diary of Fujiwara no Yukinari styles him a middle captain, suggesting he reached fourth rank. Genealogies relate that he settled on the Sasaki Manor in Gamō District, Ōmi Province, and was the ancestor after whom the Sasaki clan named itself, although modern scholars note this identification is debated. Skilled with bow and horse, he died in 1003, aged only twenty-eight.
zh: 源成赖（976—1003）是平安时代中期的贵族，出自宇多源氏，为参议源扶义的长子。《尊卑分脉》载其叙从五位下，历任左近卫将监、兵库助，而藤原行成的日记《权记》称他为近卫中将，官位可能达到四位。诸系图记载他定居于近江国蒲生郡佐佐木庄，被奉为佐佐木氏得名之祖，但近代有学者认为这一身份尚存争议。他弓马娴熟，于1003年去世，年仅二十八岁。

en: Sasaki no Nobutsuna (c. 1181–1242), fourth son of Sasaki no Sadatsuna, was a Kamakura gokenin and head of the Sasaki clan. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 his crossing of the Uji River was held up; after calling for reinforcements, he crossed with Hōjō Tokiuji and broke the court forces. He received the Sasaki ancestral estates in Ōmi, while his elder brother Hirotsuna, who had joined the retired emperor, was executed. Nobutsuna later served as Ōmi no kami and, in 1226, as envoy to the court for Fujiwara no Yoritsune's shogunal commission. After his death his four sons divided Ōmi and founded the Ōhara, Takashima, Rokkaku and Kyōgoku houses.
zh: 佐佐木信纲（约1181—1242）是佐佐木定纲的四男，镰仓幕府御家人，后成为佐佐木氏总领。1221年承久之乱中，他加入幕府军参加宇治川之战，渡河受阻后请求援军，与北条时氏共同渡河击破京方军队。乱后他受赐近江的佐佐木氏祖传领地，而追随上皇的长兄广纲被斩首。此后他历任近江守，1226年还作为幕府使者，为藤原赖经受任征夷大将军一事出使朝廷。他去世后，四个儿子瓜分近江，分别开创大原氏、高岛氏、六角氏与京极氏。

en: Sasaki no Noritsune (1000–1058), originally named Akitsune, was a warrior of the late Heian period counted as the founder of the Sasaki clan of Uda Genji descent. A son of Minamoto no Nariyori, he reached junior fifth rank, lower grade, and served as Hyōbu-no-jō in the Ministry of Military Affairs, styling himself Hyōbu-no-taifu. By his wife Aya-no-kata, a lady-in-waiting to Emperor Go-Reizei, he fathered Sasaki no Tsunekata, who settled at Sasaki Manor in Gamō District of Ōmi Province and took the Sasaki name.
zh: 佐佐木义经（1000—1058），初名章经，是平安时代后期的武将，被视为宇多源氏佐佐木氏之祖。他是源成赖之子，叙从五位下，任兵部丞，号兵部大夫。他娶后冷泉院女房绫御方，生子佐佐木经方，经方后来在近江国蒲生郡佐佐木庄定居并以佐佐木为姓。

en: Sasaki no Sadatsuna (1142–1205), eldest son of Sasaki no Hideyoshi, was a leading general of the early Kamakura shogunate. He served Minamoto no Yoritomo from his exile in Izu, joined his rising in 1180, and fought at Ishibashiyama and Fujigawa; after the Genpei War he became shugo of Ōmi, Nagato, Iwami and Oki. In 1191 a bloody clash with Enryakuji monks over manor dues caused his exile to Satsuma, but he was pardoned in 1193 and restored. He took vows on his deathbed in 1205 and died two days later in Kamakura, aged sixty-four.
zh: 佐佐木定纲（1142—1205）是佐佐木秀义的嫡男，镰仓幕府初期的核心武将。他年轻时便侍奉流放伊豆的源赖朝，1180年协助赖朝举兵，参加石桥山、富士川之战；平氏灭亡后出任近江、长门、石见、隐岐四国守护。1191年，因佐佐木庄千僧供料之争与延历寺僧侣发生流血冲突，他被流放萨摩，1193年获赦并恢复官职。1205年他病中出家，两天后在镰仓去世，终年六十四岁。

en: Sasaki no Tametoshi, also called Suesada, was the eldest son and heir of Sasaki no Tsunekata, leader of the Sasaki clan in Ōmi Province, and father of Sasaki no Hideyoshi. He held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and the office of Shikibu-no-jō.
zh: 佐佐木为俊（一称季定）是近江国佐佐木氏栋梁佐佐木经方的嫡男，生子佐佐木秀义；他叙从五位下，官居式部丞。

en: Sasaki no Tsunekata was an eleventh-century Uda Genji warrior in Ōmi Province, after whom the Sasaki clan is named. Genealogies make him the eldest son of Sasaki no Yoshitsune and grandson of Minamoto no Nariyori, and record him as the first of his line to settle at Kowaki in the Sasaki Manor of Gamō District, serving as its steward and as priest of Sasaki-no-miya Shrine. He held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and the office of Hyōgo-no-suke. His grandson Sasaki no Hideyoshi, born in 1112, fought in the Hōgen and Heiji disturbances.
zh: 佐佐木经方是11世纪近江国宇多源氏的武将，佐佐木氏的苗字即得自于他。系图将他列为佐佐木义经的长子、源成赖之孙，记载他率先在近江国蒲生郡佐佐木庄的小胁楯定居，担任该庄下司并出任佐佐木宫神主。他叙从五位下，官至兵库助。其孙佐佐木秀义生于1112年，曾参加保元之乱与平治之乱。

en: Sasaki no Yasukiyo (died 1282), second son of Sasaki no Yoshikiyo, was a Kamakura gokenin who held the shugo posts of Oki and Izumo. He inherited them in 1251 after his elder brother Masayoshi was tonsured without leave and stripped of office. Yasukiyo sat on the Rokuhara council and held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and the title of Shinano no kami. His sons included Tokikiyo and Yoriyasu. He died in 1282 as the monk Taikaku.
zh: 佐佐木泰清（？—1282）是佐佐木义清的次男，镰仓幕府御家人，领有隐岐、出云两国守护职。1251年，其兄政义因擅自出家被没收官职，泰清于是继任两国守护。他位列六波罗探题评定众，叙从五位下，历任信浓守。他的儿子包括时清与赖泰。他于1282年去世，法名泰觉。

en: Sasaki no Yoshikiyo (c. 1160–c. 1248), fifth son of Sasaki no Hideyoshi, was a Kamakura gokenin and ancestor of the Izumo Genji. Raised at Shibuya Manor in Sagami, he fought for the Taira against Minamoto no Yoritomo at Ishibashiyama in 1180 before changing sides after Fujigawa, and thereafter served the shogunate. After the Jōkyū War of 1221 his long service won him the shugo posts of Oki and Izumo, and he escorted the exiled Emperor Go-Toba to Oki. In old age he yielded his offices to his sons; he was last recorded in 1248, near ninety.
zh: 佐佐木义清（约1160—约1248）是佐佐木秀义的五男，镰仓幕府御家人，出云源氏之祖。他在相模国涩谷庄长大，1180年石桥山之战时先随平氏一方与源赖朝作战，富士川之战后转投赖朝，此后长期侍奉镰仓幕府。1221年承久之乱后，他凭多年军功获任隐岐、出云两国守护，并护送被流放的后鸟羽上皇前往隐岐。晚年他把守护职让给儿子，史料中最后见于1248年的记载，当时已近九十岁。

en: Satake Hideyoshi (1151–1226) was the third head of the Satake clan of Hitachi. In 1180 he and his clansmen held Kinsaja Castle against Minamoto no Yoritomo; after the castle fell through the treachery of his uncle Satake Yoshisue, he fled to Hanazono and succeeded his father Takayoshi in 1183. He resisted Yoritomo until 1189, when he submitted and fought in the Ōshū campaign; the fan-on-white-banner emblem Yoritomo ordered for him became the Satake crest. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he sent his son Yoshishige to fight for the bakufu. He died at Kamakura in 1226.
zh: 佐竹秀义（1151—1226）是常陆国佐竹氏第三代当主。1180年，他与族人据守金砂城抵抗源赖朝，因叔父佐竹义季内应而城破，随后逃往花园城；1183年父亲隆义去世，他继承家督。他抵抗赖朝直至1189年才归顺，参加奥州合战；赖朝命他在白旗上加绘扇印，由此产生佐竹氏定纹五本骨扇月丸。1221年承久之乱时他年已71岁，派嫡子义重等率军加入幕府军。1226年，秀义在镰仓去世。

en: Satake Masayoshi (1081–1147) was a late Heian warrior and the founder of the Satake clan of Hitachi Province. A grandson of Minamoto no Yoshimitsu of the Seiwa Genji and eldest son of Minamoto no Yoshinari, he settled at Satake in Kuji district and styled himself Satake Kaja. Genealogies record that in 1106 he helped repel his uncle Minamoto no Yoshikuni's invasion of Hitachi. He married a daughter of Fujiwara no Kiyohira of the Ōshū Fujiwara, and their son Takayoshi succeeded him, laying the base of Satake power in northern Hitachi.
zh: 佐竹昌义（1081—1147）是平安时代后期武将，常陆国佐竹氏的家祖、初代当主。他出身清和源氏义光流，为源义光之孙、源义业长子，定居常陆国久慈郡佐竹乡，通称佐竹冠者。谱系类文献记载，1106年常陆合战时，他随父祖击退攻入常陆的叔父源义国。他迎娶奥州藤原氏初代藤原清衡之女，所生之子隆义后来继承家督，奠定了佐竹氏在北常陆的势力基础。

en: Satake Moroyoshi was a Nanboku-chō warrior, the seventh son of the Hitachi shugo Satake Sadayoshi by a concubine. He joined Ashikaga Tadayoshi's army with his half-brother Yoshiatsu when the Ashikaga marched on Kyōto, then followed Takauji to Kyushu and fought at Tatarahama and Minatogawa in 1336. While Yoshiatsu returned to govern Hitachi, Moroyoshi remained Takauji's close retainer; in 1345 he served at the Tenryū-ji dedication and in 1349 backed Kō no Moronao against Tadayoshi. A renga poet anthologized in the Tsukubashū, he received the Yamauchi lands in Kuji district from Takauji and founded the Yamauchi Satake and Kuniyasu clans.
