zh: 佐竹师义是南北朝时代的武将，常陆守护佐竹贞义与侧室所生的第七子。足利氏起兵上洛时，他随异母兄义笃加入足利直义的军队，随后跟随尊氏前往九州，1336年在多多良滨和凑川的战斗中立功。义笃归国经营本领后，师义留在尊氏身边近侍：1345年天龙寺落庆供养时担任后阵随兵，1349年直义与高师直对立时支持师直。他擅长连歌，作品收入《菟玖波集》；后来尊氏将常陆国久慈郡的山入一地赐给他为领地，他由此成为山入佐竹氏与国安氏的始祖。

en: Satake Nagayoshi (1207–1272) was the fifth head of the Satake clan of Hitachi and eldest son of Yoshishige. He held the office of Hitachi no suke and served as Satake bettō. In 1252 he was assigned to attend the shogun Prince Munetaka's visit to Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine, though the ceremony was canceled; in 1261 he was excused from the shrine's hōjō-e festival on grounds of illness. In 1267 he founded Yōun-ji for his grandmother's memorial, and in 1269 he restored the family temple Satake-dera. He died in 1272.
zh: 佐竹长义（1207—1272）是常陆国佐竹氏第五代当主，义重的长子。他与父亲一样担任常陆介，并称佐竹别当。1252年，第六代将军宗尊亲王参拜鹤冈八幡宫时，他被指定为供奉人，仪式后被取消；1261年又奉命参加鹤冈八幡宫放生会，他以患病为由请辞获准。1267年他为祖母追善建立阳云寺，1269年再兴佐竹寺。1272年长义去世，享年66岁。

en: Satake Sadayoshi (1287–1352) was the eighth head of the Satake clan of Hitachi Province. He took one character of his name from Hōjō Sadatoki and founded Kōzen-ji in Taga district in 1303. In 1331 he became shugo of Hitachi and fought for the Kamakura bakufu at the siege of Mount Kasagi, but was won over by Ashikaga Takauji and joined the imperial side. In 1335 Takauji confirmed him as shugo of Hitachi, an office that became hereditary in the clan, and he occupied Satake-tate, the later Ōta Castle. He died in 1352 and was succeeded by his son Yoshiatsu.
zh: 佐竹贞义（1287—1352）是常陆国佐竹氏第八代当主，活跃于镰仓时代后期至南北朝战乱时期。他元服时取北条贞时名字中的一字为名，1303年在多珂郡建立兴禅寺。1331年他被补任为常陆国守护，作为幕府军参加笠置山攻城战，后经足利尊氏策反而倒向讨幕一方。1335年足利尊氏承认他的常陆守护之职，此后该职由佐竹氏世袭；同年他进驻佐竹楯，即后来的太田城。1352年贞义去世，由嫡子义笃继任家督。

en: Satake Takayoshi (1118–1183) was the second head of the Satake clan of Hitachi Province. A grandson of Fujiwara no Kiyohira through his mother, he moved the clan base from Masasaka to Ōta Castle and extended its rule over the seven inland districts of northern Hitachi. After 1159 he served Taira no Kiyomori in Kyoto. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, the Satake stood against him: their heir Yoshimasa was murdered at Ōyabashi and Kinsaja Castle, where Hideyoshi and others had taken refuge, was stormed, so most Satake lands were seized. Takayoshi died in 1183 and his son Hideyoshi succeeded him.
zh: 佐竹隆义（1118—1183）是常陆国佐竹氏第二代当主。他的母亲是奥州藤原氏藤原清衡之女；隆义把本据从马坂城移到太田城，将佐竹氏的支配扩展到北常陆的奥七郡。1159年平治之乱后，他上京侍奉平清盛。1180年源赖朝举兵，佐竹氏与之敌对：嫡子义政在大矢桥被谋杀，秀义等人退守的金砂城被攻破，大部分领地遭到没收。1183年隆义去世，其子秀义继任家督。

en: Satake Yoshiatsu (1311–1362) was the ninth head of the Satake clan of Hitachi Province and Sadayoshi's second son; he inherited because his elder brother was an illegitimate monk. When the Nanboku-chō war began he sided with Ashikaga Takauji, was appointed shugo of Hitachi, and after returning east led the Northern Court faction there. In Kyōto from 1354 to 1357, he held the title uma no gon no kami and headed the Muromachi bakufu's Samurai-dokoro. In his last years he took Zen vows as Shunzan Jōki and founded Seion-an, later Seion-ji, in Naka district.
zh: 佐竹义笃（1311—1362）是常陆国佐竹氏第九代当主，贞义的次子；因长兄为庶子、已出家为僧，由他继承家督。南北朝战乱爆发后，他追随足利尊氏，被任命为常陆守护，归国后成为常陆国内北朝势力的核心。1354至1357年间，他在京都任职，获授右马权头官衔，并出任室町幕府侍所头人。晚年他皈依禅宗，出家后号春山净喜，在常陆国那珂郡古内乡建立清音庵，即后来的清音寺。

en: Satake Yoshifuyu was a son of the Hitachi shugo Satake Sadayoshi and a Satake warrior at the start of the Nanboku-chō wars. In 1336 he fought for the Ashikaga side in Hitachi and was killed by Kusunoki Masaie.
zh: 佐竹义冬是常陆守护佐竹贞义之子，南北朝战乱初期的佐竹氏武将。1336年，他在常陆为足利一方作战，被楠木正家所杀。

en: Satake Yoshinao was a son of the Hitachi shugo Satake Sadayoshi and a warrior of the Satake clan.
zh: 佐竹义直是常陆守护佐竹贞义之子，也是一名佐竹氏武将。

en: Satake Yoshishige (1186–1252) was the fourth head of the Satake clan of Hitachi. With his father Hideyoshi he fought for the Kamakura bakufu in the Jōkyū War of 1221, serving in Hōjō Yasutoki's Tōkaidō army and taking heads at the Uji River battle. He succeeded around 1226 and was appointed Hitachi no suke in 1245, restoring the clan to the shodaibu rank it had held before the Genpei War. He also established the cadet Nukata, Okada and Okabe houses. He died in 1252 and his son Nagayoshi succeeded him.
zh: 佐竹义重（1186—1252）是常陆国佐竹氏第四代当主。1221年承久之乱时，他随父亲秀义为镰仓幕府出战，加入北条泰时的东海道军，在宇治川之战中斩敌立功。约1226年他继承家督，1245年被任命为常陆介，使佐竹氏恢复了源平合战以前的诸大夫家格。他还让诸子分家，建立额田、冈田、冈部等庶家。1252年义重去世，其子长义继任。

en: Satake Yoshitane (1227–1278) was the sixth head of the Satake clan of Hitachi, succeeding his father Nagayoshi in 1272. He kept a residence at Hikigayatsu in Kamakura, held junior fifth rank, lower grade, and served as Sanuki no kami and Hitachi no suke. He married a daughter of the Iwasaki of Iwaki district in Mutsu, and used the marriage to extend Satake influence into southern Mutsu, where his sons founded cadet branches. In 1276 he founded the Rinzai temple Shōgin-ji in Naka district. He died in 1278 and his son Yukiyoshi succeeded him.
zh: 佐竹义胤（1227—1278）是常陆国佐竹氏第六代当主，1272年继承父亲长义。他在镰仓比企谷建有宅邸，叙从五位下，历任赞岐守、常陆介。他娶陆奥国岩城郡在地豪族岩崎氏之女为妻，借此把佐竹氏势力扩展到陆奥南部的磐城地方，诸子在当地分家定居。1276年，他在常陆国那珂郡建立临济宗东福寺派的松吟寺。1278年义胤去世，嫡子行义继任。

en: Satake Yukiyoshi (1263–1305) was the seventh head of the Satake clan of Hitachi, succeeding his father Yoshitane in 1278. He deepened ties with the Kamakura bakufu by marrying a daughter of Nikaidō Yoritsuna, whose family ran the mandokoro, and held the offices of Saemon no jō and Hitachi no suke. In the Kōan era he founded the Shōhō-in subtemple at the family mortuary temple Shōraku-ji in Ōta and endowed it with lands; Emperor Fushimi granted it an imperial plaque during the Einin era. He died in 1305 and his son Sadayoshi succeeded him.
zh: 佐竹行义（1263—1305）是常陆国佐竹氏第七代当主，1278年继承父亲义胤。他迎娶世袭政所执事的幕府得宗被官二阶堂赖纲之女为正室，加深与镰仓幕府中枢的联系，历任左卫门尉、常陆介。弘安年间，他在太田乡增井的家族菩提所胜乐寺境内建立支院正法院，并寄进土地；永仁年间获伏见天皇赐予敕额。1305年行义去世，享年43岁，嫡子贞义继任。

en: Satomi Yoshinari (1157–1234) was a Kamakura warrior based at Satomigō in Usui District, Kōzuke Province, son of Satomi Yoshitoshi and grandson of Nitta Yoshishige. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, Yoshinari slipped out of Kyoto by pretending to rejoin his grandfather against him and hastened to Kamakura, earning Yoritomo's favor. In 1195 he rode as second archer in the yabusame before Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine, and in 1204 was made Iga no kami. He lost office after his patron Hiraga Tomomasa was killed in 1205. He died in 1234 aged seventy-eight; the Azuma Kagami called him Yoritomo's cherished man.
zh: 里见义成（1157—1234）是镰仓时代武将，以上野国碓冰郡里见乡为据点，为里见义俊之子、新田义重之孙。1180年源赖朝举兵时，身在京都的义成谎称要回上野与祖父一同讨伐赖朝，借机脱身驰赴镰仓，由此深得赖朝信任。1195年，他在鹤冈八幡宫的流镝马仪式中担任第二射手，1204年出任伊贺守。1205年，他的庇护者平贺朝雅被诛，义成随之丢官失势。他于1234年去世，享年七十八岁，《吾妻镜》称他是赖朝的宠臣。

en: Satomi Yoshitoshi, also called Nitta Yoshitoshi, was a warrior of the late Heian period and the eldest son, born of a concubine, of Nitta Yoshishige, first head of the Nitta clan. He yielded the succession to his legitimate half-brother Yoshikane and founded a branch house, receiving Chikuringō in Nitta-no-shō, Kōzuke Province. Around 1154 to 1155 he moved to Usui Castle near Satomigō in Usui District, built a mountain fortress there and took the name Satomi. He died before his father and was buried at Kōmyōji.
zh: 里见义俊（亦称新田义俊）是平安时代末期的武将，为新田氏初代当主新田义重的庶长子。他把家督让给嫡出的异母弟义兼而另立分家，受领上野国新田庄竹林乡。约1154至1155年，他迁居碓冰郡里见乡一带的碓冰城，在那里筑起山城，改称里见氏。他先于父亲去世，葬于里见山光明寺。

en: Emperor Seiwa (850–881), personal name Korehito, was the 56th emperor of Japan, reigning from 858 to 876. The fourth son of Emperor Montoku, he was made crown prince through the influence of his maternal grandfather Fujiwara no Yoshifusa and ascended at nine, leaving Yoshifusa to rule as sesshō, the first Fujiwara regent. After the Ōtenmon gate incident of 866, the regent purged his court rivals. Seiwa abdicated in 876 in favour of his young son Emperor Yōzei, took Buddhist vows in 878, and died in 881. His descendants led the Seiwa Genji warrior line.
zh: 清和天皇（850—881），名惟仁，是日本第56代天皇，858年至876年在位。他是文德天皇的第四子，因外祖父藤原良房的影响被立为太子，九岁即位，朝政由良房以摄政身份执掌，这是藤原氏首次担任摄政。866年应天门之变后，良房铲除朝中政敌。876年清和天皇让位于年幼的儿子阳成天皇，878年出家，881年去世。他的后裔是武士家族清和源氏的始祖。

en: Senka (467–539), the 28th emperor of Japan in the traditional order, was the second son of Emperor Keitai by Menokohime of the Owari clan and the full younger brother of Emperor Ankan. The chronicles call him Prince Hinokuma no Takata. He took the throne in 536 after Ankan's death and ruled a little over three years; his reign marks the close of the Kofun period on the eve of the Asuka period. His empress was Tachibana no Nakatsu, a daughter of Emperor Ninken, and their daughter Ishi-hime became empress to his half-brother and successor, Emperor Kinmei.
zh: 宣化天皇（467—539）是日本传统世系中的第28代天皇，继体天皇与尾张目子媛的次子，安闲天皇的同母弟，史籍中称他为桧隈高田皇子。536年安闲天皇死后即位，在位仅三年余，其统治时期标志着古坟时代结束、飞鸟时代前夜。皇后橘仲皇女是仁贤天皇之女，两人所生的石姬皇女后来成为他的异母弟、继位者钦明天皇的皇后。

en: Shiba Iekane (1308–1356) was son of Shiba Muneuji and younger half-brother of Shiba Takatsune. He joined Ashikaga Takauji's uprising against the Kamakura shogunate in 1333 and was made shugo of Wakasa in 1336, fighting Southern Court general Nitta Yoshisada in Hokuriku, whom he helped destroy in 1338. During the Kannō disturbance he sided with Takauji against his own brother and was appointed head of the judicial board, or hikitsuke. In 1354 he was appointed kanrei of Ōshū, where he defeated rival generals, made the office hereditary in his clan, and founded the Ōsaki and Mogami lines. He died there in 1356.
zh: 斯波家兼（1308—1356）是斯波宗氏之子、斯波高经的异母弟。1333年，他随足利尊氏举兵推翻镰仓幕府，1336年被任命为若狭守护，在北陆与南朝大将新田义贞作战，并于1338年攻灭新田。观应之扰乱中，他没有附和兄长高经，而是站在尊氏一方，出任引付头人。1354年，他就任奥州管领，在奥州击败诸路对手，确立斯波氏对管领职的世袭，成为大崎氏、最上氏等奥羽斯波氏之祖。1356年他在奥州管领任上去世。

en: Shiba Ienaga (1321–1338) was the eldest son of Shiba Takatsune and fought for Ashikaga Takauji from boyhood. On 30 August 1335 he was named commander-in-chief of Ōshū, holding the front against the Southern Court's Mutsu government under Kitabatake Akiie from Takamizushiro castle in Shiwa. He then served as Kantō steward at Kamakura, assisting the young Ashikaga Yoshiakira, and eroded Akiie's authority among the warriors of the north. In December 1337 he tried to stop Akiie's army before Kamakura and was killed at the battle of Sugimoto castle, aged seventeen.
zh: 斯波家长（1321—1338）是斯波高经的长子，自幼随父为足利尊氏作战。1335年8月30日，他被任命为奥州总大将，进驻志和郡高水寺城，承担对抗北畠显家陆奥将军府的最前线。此后他在镰仓出任关东执事，辅佐年幼的足利义诠，逐步瓦解显家在北方武士中的权威。1337年12月，他试图在镰仓城下阻击显家大军，在杉本城之战中战死，年仅17岁。

en: Ieuji was the eldest son of the Kamakura gokenin Ashikaga no Yasuuji by a daughter of the Nagoe Hōjō Tomotoki. First recorded in the shogun's retinue in 1245, he apparently lost his place as heir after his father married a Tokusō Hōjō wife, yet became Nakatsukasa-dayū in 1253 and in 1261 Kebiishi and Saemon-dayū, styled Hangan-daibu. He became Owari no kami in 1265, guarded the young clan head Ietoki and acted as de facto sōryō until c. 1269, and died as the monk Ren'a. Enfeoffed with Shiba district in Mutsu, he founded the future Shiba line; his son was Muneie.
zh: 家氏是镰仓御家人足利泰氏与名越流北条朝时之女所生的长子。1245年他以将军随从身份首见于记载；父亲迎娶得宗家北条氏之女后，他似乎被夺去嫡子地位，但仍于1253年任中务大辅，1261年任检非违使、左卫门大尉，人称“足利判官大夫”。他于1265年叙任尾张守，幼主家时继位后担任后见人，至约1269年一直代行家督之职，晚年出家，法号莲阿。他受领陆奥国斯波郡，开创了后来的斯波氏，儿子是宗家。

en: Muneie (dates unknown) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and second head of the Shiba (Owari-Ashikaga) house, succeeding his father Ieuji. Probably born in the 1250s, he likely came of age in the early 1260s and served the shogunate as an independent gokenin, taking the ‘Mune’ of his name from Hōjō Tokimune. He held Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, with the post of Sakon no shōgen, and was known as Owari Saburō; tradition makes him the first Shiba by name. He survived the 1285 Shimotsuki purge, losing many lands, and was still active in the Kagen disturbance of 1305. His son was Muneuji.
zh: 宗家（生卒年不详）是镰仓时代中期武将，斯波氏（尾张足利氏）第二代当主，继自家氏。他可能生于1250年代，于1260年代前期元服，作为独立于足利本家的御家人侍奉幕府，名中的“宗”字得自北条时宗的偏讳。他叙从五位下，任左近将监，通称尾张三郎；相传“斯波”这一苗字即由他而始。1285年霜月骚动中他虽失去不少家氏时代的领地，但幸免于难，1305年嘉元之乱时仍以有力御家人身份活动。儿子是斯波宗氏。

en: Shiba Muneuji (also Ashikaga Muneuji; c. 1250–1312) was the third head of the Shiba, the Owari branch of the Ashikaga clan, and father of the prominent generals Shiba Takatsune and Shiba Iekane. The eldest son of Shiba Muneie, he was known as Matasaburō and held the title Owari no Kami. In 1309 he submitted documents under questioning by the Kamakura shogunate, evidence he had succeeded as head. He was also a waka poet, whose verses entered the imperial anthologies Shoku-Goshūi Wakashū and Shinsenzai Wakashū. A Mount Kōya gorintō dated the twelfth month of 1312 likely records his death.
zh: 斯波宗氏（又称足利宗氏，约1250—1312）是斯波氏（足利氏尾张流）第三代当主，也是南北朝时期名将斯波高经、斯波家兼之父。他是斯波宗家的嫡子，通称又三郎，曾任尾张守。1309年，他在镰仓幕府的讯问中提交证文，可知当时已继任家督。他亦是和歌歌人，作品被选入《续后拾遗和歌集》《新千载和歌集》等敕撰和歌集。高野山发现的五轮塔铭文署正和元年（1312年）十二月，当是其卒年。

en: Shiba Takatsune (1305–1367) was the fourth head of the Shiba, a powerful branch of the Ashikaga, and shugo of Echizen, Wakasa and Etchū. In 1333 he joined Ashikaga Takauji's attack on the Rokuhara tandai that overthrew the Kamakura shogunate. He commanded a wing at the battle of Minatogawa in 1336, and his troops killed the Southern Court general Nitta Yoshisada at Fujishima in 1338. After Shōgun Takauji died in 1358 he had his son Yoshimasa made kanrei in 1362 and ran the bakufu, until the Jōji purge of 1366 drove him out. He died at Somayama castle in 1367.
zh: 斯波高经（1305—1367）是足利氏有力一门斯波氏的第四代当主，兼任越前、若狭、越中守护。1333年，他随足利高氏（尊氏）举兵倒幕，参加攻打六波罗探题。1336年，他作为山手军大将参加凑川之战；1338年藤岛之战中，其部击杀南朝大将新田义贞。1358年尊氏去世后，他于1362年让四子义将出任管领，自己掌握幕府实权，史称“高经政权”。1366年贞治之变中他被放逐，仍据城抵抗，1367年在条山城去世，享年63岁。

en: Shiba Ujitsune was the second son of Shiba Takatsune and a Northern Court general. He first appears in 1349 among the generals at Ashikaga Tadayoshi's mansion. In 1355, when his father rebelled with Ashikaga Tadafuyu, Ujitsune stayed loyal to Takauji and was made shugo of Echizen in his father's place. In 1360 the bakufu named him tandai of Kyūshū, but in October 1362 his army was shattered by the Southern Court forces of Prince Kanenaga and Kikuchi Takemitsu at Chōjabaru. He fled to Suō, returned to Kyoto, and in 1367 took the tonsure as Dōei and retired to Saga.
zh: 斯波氏经（生没年不详）是斯波高经的次子、北朝武将，历任越前守护、九州探题。1349年，他首次在史料中登场，列名于足利直义府邸的诸将之中。1355年其父勾结足利直冬再度反叛时，他没有追随，被足利尊氏任命为越前守护以取代父亲。1360年，幕府任命他为九州探题；但1362年10月，他的军队在长者原合战中被怀良亲王与菊池武光的南朝军击溃，逃往周防。他返回京都，1367年出家，法号道荣，隐居嵯峨。

en: Shiba Ujiyori was the third son of Shiba Takatsune and a Northern Court commander who held the court posts of left palace guard lieutenant and left gates assistant and was made shugo of Wakasa. He married a daughter of Sasaki Dōnyū, the strongest man in the Muromachi bakufu. After his eldest brother Ienaga fell in battle in 1338 and Ujitsune was disgraced after his Kyūshū campaign of 1362, many backed Ujiyori for the vacant office of kanrei, but Takatsune favored his younger sons and passed him over. Disillusioned, Ujiyori took Buddhist vows and withdrew to Ōmi province.
zh: 斯波氏赖（生没年不详）是斯波高经的三子、北朝武将，历任左近卫将监、左卫门佐，出任若狭守护，并娶幕府实权人物佐佐木道誉之女为妻。长兄家长于1338年战死，次兄氏经在1362年九州之役后失脚，当室町幕府执事（管领）出缺时，众人曾推举氏赖继任，视其为斯波氏继承人；但父亲高经偏爱其弟义将、义种而加以排斥。氏赖心灰意冷，不久出家，隐居近江。

en: Shigenoi Sanekuni (1140–1183), also called Fujiwara no Sanekuni, was a court noble and poet at the end of the Heian period and the second son of Sanjō Kiminori. He received his first court rank in 1147, became a councillor in 1160, and in 1165 was made provisional middle counsellor, eventually reaching senior second rank and provisional major counsellor, styled the Sanjō Major Counsellor. He founded the Shigenoi house, a branch of the Sanjō family, and died early in 1183, soon after his mother.
zh: 滋野井实国（1140—1183）又名藤原实国，是平安时代末期的公卿、歌人，内大臣三条公教的次子。他1147年叙爵，1160年任参议，1165年升任权中纳言，最终官至正二位权大纳言，号三条大纳言。他从三条家分出，开创了滋野井家。1183年正月二日，他在母亲去世后不久离世。

en: Shijō Arisuke was a Southern Court noble in the Nanboku-chō wars, a son of the Dainagon Shijō Takasuke. Appointed governor of Iyo Province and Sachūjō, Middle Captain of the Left Guards, he traveled to his province in 1337. Based at Uwa Manor, he led Southern Court forces in the local fighting, crossing to Kutsuna Island to take command in battle, and worked with the Kutsuna clan to extend Southern Court control over Iyo. In 1343 he ordered Kutsuna Yoshinori to arrange the follow-up matters of Nametsu Castle.
zh: 四条有资是日本南北朝时代的南朝公家，为大纳言四条隆资之子，官任伊予国司、左中将。1337年，他以伊予国司身份赴任，进驻宇和庄，并渡海至忽那岛指挥合战，联合忽那氏扩大南朝在伊予国的势力。1343年，他命令忽那义范处理伊予名越城的善后事宜。

en: Shijō Fusana (1229–1288) was a Kamakura-period court noble, the fifth head of the Shijō house and eldest son of Shijō Takachika. He received his first rank in 1237, served as governor of Mikawa Province and reached junior third rank in 1249, joining the senior nobles. After rising to senior second rank in 1257 he waited more than twenty years without a substantive post, only becoming councillor in 1279. Dismissed in 1282 for missing the New Year ceremony, he was reinstated within a fortnight, and briefly served as grand councillor in 1285 before retiring. He died in 1288.
zh: 四条房名（1229—1288）是镰仓时代公卿、四条家第五代当主，四条隆亲的长子。1237年叙爵，曾任三河守，1249年叙从三位，跻身公卿。1257年升正二位后，他长达二十余年无实际官职，直到1279年才任参议。1282年他因未出席元日节会被解职，十二天后复任；1285年短暂就任大纳言后辞职，1288年去世，享年60岁。

en: Shijō Takaaki (1243–after 1277) was a Kamakura-period court noble, the second son of Shijō Takachika and head of the Zenshōji cloister, known as the Zenshōji Grand Councillor. Appointed councillor in 1257, he rose to senior second rank and provisional grand councillor. In 1276 his father returned to the post of grand councillor and Takaaki resigned, and the next year he took Buddhist orders, said to be over his bitter estrangement from Takachika. Nothing is recorded of him after 1277. His line, continued through Takazane, Takasuke and Takatoshi, served the Southern Court and later died out.
zh: 四条隆显（1243—1277年后）是镰仓时代中期至后期的公卿，四条隆亲的次子，曾任善胜寺长者，人称善胜寺大纳言。1257年任参议，后升正二位、权大纳言。1276年父亲隆亲还任大纳言，隆显遂辞去权大纳言之职，翌年出家，据传原因是与父亲不和；出家之后事迹不详。他这一系经隆实、隆资、隆俊延续，后来追随南朝，在南北朝时代绝嗣。

en: Shijō Takachika (1202–1279) was a Kamakura-period court noble and waka poet, the fourth head of the Shijō house and the second son of Shijō Takahira. Ranked in 1205, he became head chamberlain in 1222, councillor in 1225, provisional grand councillor in 1238 and grand councillor in 1250. When Emperor Shijō died in 1242, the Kamakura shogunate placed Prince Kunihito on the throne as Emperor Go-Saga at Takachika's residence, where his wife had nursed the prince. He resigned in 1260 but returned as grand councillor in 1276 after quarrelling with his heir Takaaki, and died in 1279.
zh: 四条隆亲（1202—1279）是镰仓时代前期至中期的公卿、和歌歌人，四条家第四代当主、四条隆衡的次子。1205年叙爵，1222年任藏人头，1225年任参议，1238年任权大纳言，1250年任大纳言。1242年四条天皇崩御，镰仓幕府拥立邦仁王为后嵯峨天皇，践祚仪式即在隆亲的宅邸举行，他的妻子曾为邦仁王的乳母。1260年他辞任大纳言，后与继承人隆显不和，1276年隆显辞职出家后他还任大纳言，1279年去世，享年78岁。

en: Fujiwara no Takafusa (1148–1209), also called Shijō Takafusa, was a court noble of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and the second head of the Shijō house. The eldest son of Fujiwara no Takasue, he married a daughter of Taira no Kiyomori. Ranked in 1158, he governed Kaga and Inaba provinces, commanded the Palace Guards and became head chamberlain. He reached junior third rank in 1184, provisional middle councillor in 1189, senior second rank in 1199 and provisional grand councillor in 1204. He took the tonsure in 1206 as Jakue and died in 1209.
zh: 藤原隆房（1148—1209），又称四条隆房，是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的公卿、四条家第二代当主，权大纳言藤原隆季的长子，娶平清盛之女为妻。他于1158年叙爵，历任加贺国、因幡国国司、左右近卫中将、藏人头等职，1184年叙从三位，1189年任权中纳言，1199年升正二位中纳言，1204年官至权大纳言。1206年出家，法名寂惠，1209年去世，享年62岁。

en: Shijō Takahira (1172–1255), or Fujiwara no Takahira, was a Kamakura-period court noble and the third head of the Shijō house. The eldest son of Fujiwara no Takafusa by a daughter of Taira no Kiyomori, he was Kiyomori's maternal grandson. He married a sister of Shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo's wife and kept rising after the Taira fell. He became head chamberlain in 1201, councillor in 1202, senior second rank in 1214 and provisional grand councillor in 1219, and his house rose with Emperor Go-Horikawa's accession in 1221. He took the tonsure in 1227 and died in 1255.
zh: 四条隆衡（1172—1255），又称藤原隆衡，镰仓时代公卿、四条家第三代当主。他是藤原隆房与平清盛之女所生的长子，即平清盛的外孙。他娶将军源实朝正室之妹为妻，在平家没落后仍不断升迁，1201年任藏人头，1202年任参议，1214年升正二位，1219年任权大纳言；1221年后堀河天皇即位，四条家备受重用。1227年出家，1255年去世，享年83岁。

en: Shijō Takamune (died 1358), originally named Takamoto, was a court noble of the late Kamakura and Nanbokuchō eras and the seventh head of the Shijō family, the son of Senior Third Rank Shijō Takana. He served as chamberlain, governor of Tango and head of the Palace Storehouse Bureau. He took the name Takamune in 1332, rose to Junior Third Rank in 1351 and Senior Third Rank in 1358, and was murdered by robbers at his home that year; his severed head was afterwards found set upon a road.
zh: 四条隆宗（？—1358）是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的公卿，四条家第七代当主，正三位四条隆名之子，初名隆基。他历任侍从、丹后守、内藏头，1332年改名隆宗；1351年叙从三位，跻身公卿，1358年升正三位，同年10月6日夜在自宅被盗贼杀害。他的首级后来被人发现放在道路之上。

en: Shijō Takana (died 1322) was a court noble of the late Kamakura period and the sixth head of the Shijō house. Born the son of Junior Assistant Minister of Central Affairs Fujiwara no Takatomo, he was adopted as heir by his third cousin Shijō Fusana. First named Takayoshi, he took the name Takasuke in 1268 and Takana in 1283. After serving as governor of Inaba Province and lieutenant of the Left Gate Guards, he reached junior third rank in 1308 as a non-councillor noble and senior third rank in 1315. He died in 1322.
zh: 四条隆名（？—1322）是镰仓时代后期的公卿、四条家第六代当主。他本是中务少辅藤原隆朝之子，被三从兄弟四条房名收为养子。他初名隆能，1268年改称隆右，1283年改名隆名。历任因幡守、左卫门佐后，1308年叙从三位，以非参议身份跻身公卿，1315年升正三位，1322年去世。

en: Shijō Takasato (1326–1410) was a court noble of the early Muromachi period, the son of the Kuraryō no Kami Shijō Takamune and the eighth head of the Shijō family. He rose through the court ranks from Junior Third Rank, conferred in 1360, to Gondainagon, Provisional Major Counselor, at Junior First Rank. He also served as chōja, superior of the family temple Zenshō-ji, and ended his life as a monk under the clerical name Sōi.
zh: 四条隆乡（1326—1410）是日本室町时代前期的公卿，为内藏头四条隆宗之子、四条家第八代当主。他于1360年叙从三位，最终官至从一位权大纳言，并担任家族菩提寺善胜寺的长者。晚年出家，法名宗怡。

en: Fujiwara no Takasue (1127–1185) was a late Heian court noble, eldest son of Chūnagon Fujiwara no Ienari, a favourite of Retired Emperor Toba. Ranked in 1133 at age seven, he held provincial governorships and entered the kugyō in 1158. He bound his family to the Taira, marrying his heir Takafusa to a daughter of Kiyomori, became Sangi in 1161 and Gon-Dainagon in 1168, and ran Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa's office. In the 1179 coup Kiyomori appointed him Dazai gon-no-sochi. He took vows in 1182, died in 1185, and founded the Shijō house.
zh: 藤原隆季（1127—1185）是平安时代后期的公卿，鸟羽上皇宠臣中纳言藤原家成的长子。1133年他七岁叙爵，历任多国国司，1158年升从三位、进入公卿之列。他与平氏联姻，让嫡子隆房迎娶清盛之女，1161年任参议，1168年升任权大纳言，执掌后白河院的院厅事务。1179年治承政变中，清盛任命他为大宰权帅。1182年他出家，1185年去世，是四条家之祖。

en: Shijō Takasuke (1292–1352) was a noble and pillar of the Southern Court in the Nanbokuchō wars. Close to Emperor Go-Daigo, he became provisional middle counselor and Kebiishi bettō in 1330. In the Genkō War of 1331 he followed the emperor to Mount Kasagi, escaped its fall by taking vows, and backed Prince Morinaga until the Hōjō fell in 1333. From 1339 he ran Southern Court administration with Tōin Saneyo. Named Dainagon in 1350, he was probably given Junior First Rank around the end of 1351. He was killed in 1352 covering Emperor Go-Murakami's retreat from Otokoyama against Akamatsu troops, and was posthumously made Sadaijin in 1356.
zh: 四条隆资（1292—1352）是镰仓后期至南北朝时代的公卿，南朝的柱石之臣。他早年即追随后醍醐天皇，1330年任权中纳言兼检非违使别当。1331年元弘之乱中，他随天皇退守笠置山，城破后剃发脱身，暗中支持护良亲王，直到1333年北条氏灭亡。1339年后村上天皇即位后，他与洞院实世共同主持南朝政务。1350年任大纳言，约于1351年末叙从一位。1352年男山八幡之战，他在掩护后村上天皇从男山撤退时迎战赤松军而死，1356年被追赠左大臣。

en: Shijō Takatoshi was a Southern Court noble during the Nanboku-chō wars, the son of the Dainagon Shijō Takasuke. When his father fell fighting the Northern Court in 1352, he succeeded as family head, and in 1372 he was appointed Naidaijin. A leader of the war party, he commanded Southern Court armies in the repeated attacks on Kyoto, and in 1369 stormed Tōjō Castle on Emperor Chōkei's order after Kusunoki Masanori defected. In 1373 he died fighting in the rear guard during the retreat from the Amanosan Kongō-ji. His poetry appears in the Shin'yō Wakashū anthology.
zh: 四条隆俊是日本南北朝时代的南朝公卿，为大纳言四条隆资之子。1352年其父在与北朝交战时战死后，他继任家督，1372年就任内大臣。作为主战派核心人物，他多次担任南朝军总大将进攻京都；1369年楠木正仪投降北朝后，他奉长庆天皇之命攻打东条城。1373年天野山金刚寺遭幕府军进攻，他在撤退时担任殿军，力战而死。其和歌收录于《新叶和歌集》。

en: Shijō Takazane was a Kamakura-period court official, the son of Shijō Takaaki and father of Shijō Takasuke. He held the post of middle captain of the Left Palace Guards but died young, after which his young son was adopted and raised by Takaaki.
zh: 四条隆实是镰仓时代的朝廷官员，四条隆显之子、四条隆资之父。他官至左近卫中将，却早逝，身后年幼的儿子隆资由祖父隆显收为养子抚养。

en: Emperor Shijō (1231–1242), the 87th emperor of Japan, came to the throne in 1232 at barely two when his father Emperor Go-Horikawa abdicated, and was left an infant sovereign by his father's death in 1234. His maternal grandfather Kujō Michiie and the courtier Saionji Kintsune then ran affairs under the Kamakura shogunate, while Princess Kinshi served as his honorary mother. A mischievous boy, he died at ten after slipping on talcum powder he had scattered in a palace corridor to make attendants fall, leaving the succession in dispute.
zh: 四条天皇（1231—1242）是日本第87代天皇。1232年父亲后堀河天皇退位，年仅两岁的秀仁亲王继位，1234年父皇又去世，他成了幼主。此后，外祖父九条道家与公卿西园寺公经在镰仓幕府之下主持政务，近卫长子则作为准母入宫。他生性顽皮，1242年在宫中走廊撒下滑石粉想让近侍滑倒，自己却失足摔伤，十岁便夭折，死后皇位继承再起争端。

en: Prince Shiki (c. 668–716) was the seventh son of Emperor Tenji and an imperial prince of the late Asuka period. In 679 he joined the other princes at Yoshino in swearing unity before Emperor Tenmu, the Yoshino Covenant. Keeping clear of succession struggles, he devoted himself to waka poetry, and Kasa no Kanamura's elegy on his death is preserved in the Man'yōshū. He rose gradually to the second imperial rank under Empresses Genmei and Genshō and died in 716. When his sixth son, Prince Shirakabe, ascended as Emperor Kōnin in 770, Shiki was posthumously honored as Emperor Kasuga.
zh: 志贵皇子（约668—716）是日本飞鸟时代末期的皇族，天智天皇第七子。679年，他与众皇子一同在吉野向天武天皇盟誓团结，史称“吉野盟约”。他远离皇位之争，潜心和歌，《万叶集》中存有笠金村为其去世所作的挽歌。元明、元正两朝他位阶渐升至二品，于716年去世。770年，其第六子白壁王即位为光仁天皇，他被追尊为春日宫御宇天皇。

en: Shimazu Hisatsune (1225–1284), first named Hisatoki, was the third head of the Shimazu clan and a Kamakura vassal. In 1265 he succeeded his father Tadatoki and went to Kamakura, where he served in the shogun's day guard. In 1275 he returned to Kyushu against the Mongol invasions and was posted to defend Chikuzen; in the 1281 Kōan invasion he led the Shimazu army with distinction, a feat pictured in the Mongol Invasion scrolls. He founded Jōkōmyō-ji in Kagoshima in 1284 and died that year at Hakozaki in Chikuzen, aged sixty, succeeded by his son Tadamune.
zh: 岛津久经（1225—1284），初名久时，是岛津氏第三代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1265年，他从父亲忠时手中接过家督，前往镰仓，担任将军的昼番众。1275年，因元军来袭他返回九州，受命守备筑前；1281年弘安之役中，他率领岛津军奋战立功，其事迹被绘入《蒙古袭来绘词》。1284年他在鹿儿岛建立净光明寺，同年在筑前筥崎役所去世，享年六十岁，由其子忠宗继任。

en: Shimazu Morohisa (1325–1376) was a commander of the Northern and Southern Courts period and the sixth head of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma. The third son of the fifth head Sadahisa, he fought for Ashikaga Takauji and was made steward of estates in Satsuma and Hizen. In 1363, after an elder brother's early death, he succeeded to the clan headship and the post of shugo of Satsuma, founding the Sōshū branch while his brother Ujihisa took Ōsumi. In 1375 he broke with Imagawa Ryōshun over the murder of Shōni Fuyusuke, and died the following year.
zh: 岛津师久（1325—1376）是日本南北朝时代的武将，出任萨摩岛津氏第六代家督，也是总州家的初代当主。他是第五代当主岛津贞久的第三子，因追随足利尊氏立下战功，被任命为萨摩、肥前国内的地头。1363年次兄宗久早逝，他在父亲去世前后继承家督与萨摩守护职，大隅守护则由弟弟氏久继承。1375年水岛之变中，今川了俊设计暗杀少贰冬资，师久激愤之下与了俊对立，次年去世，终年52岁。

en: Shimazu Munehisa (1322–1340) was a Nanboku-chō-period warrior and the legitimate second son of the fifth Shimazu head, Shimazu Sadahisa, born to Sadahisa's wife, a daughter of Ōtomo Chikatoki. In 1338 he fought alongside his father in Kō no Moronao's army against the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie and won distinction. He was the leading candidate to succeed as head of the Shimazu, but in 1340, aged nineteen, he died after falling from his horse while travelling in Satsuma. His early death opened the succession dispute that split the family into the Sōshū and Ōshū houses.
zh: 岛津宗久（1322—1340）是日本南北朝时代的武将，岛津氏第五代当主岛津贞久的嫡子（次男），母亲为贞久正室、大友亲时之女。1338年，他随父亲加入高师直的军队，与南朝大将北畠显家作战，立有战功。他本是继承家督的最有力人选，却于1340年在萨摩从山门院前往平佐的途中坠马，年仅十九岁而死。他的早逝使弟弟师久与氏久围绕守护国的分配发生争斗，岛津氏由此分裂为总州家与奥州家两支。

en: Shimazu Sadahisa (1269–1363) was fifth head of the Shimazu and shugo of Satsuma, Ōsumi and Hyūga. He succeeded his father Tadamune as shugo of Satsuma in 1318, and in 1333, answering Ashikaga Takauji's call to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate, he helped destroy the Chinzei deputy Hōjō Hidetoki, gaining Ōsumi and Hyūga as reward. He aided Takauji at Tatara beach in 1336 and then spent decades fighting Southern Court forces in southern Kyūshū, at one point submitting to them during the Kannō disturbance. In 1363 he divided Satsuma and Ōsumi between his sons Morohisa and Ujihisa and died aged ninety-five.
zh: 岛津贞久（1269—1363）是岛津氏第五代当主，萨摩、大隅、日向三国的守护。1318年，他继父亲忠宗之后就任萨摩守护；1333年响应足利尊氏推翻镰仓幕府的举兵，参与攻灭镇西探题北条英时，因功获任大隅、日向两国守护。1336年，他在多多良滨之战中援助尊氏，此后数十年在南九州与南朝势力苦战，观应之扰乱期间还曾一度归降南朝。1363年，他把萨摩与大隅分别让给儿子师久和氏久，以九十五岁高龄去世。

en: Shimazu Tadahisa (died 1227), born Koremune no Tadahisa, was a Kamakura shogunate vassal and founder of the Shimazu clan. In 1185, on Minamoto no Yoritomo's recommendation, he became a deputy administrator of the Shimazu estate in southern Kyushu and soon afterwards its chief steward; he later took his name from the estate. He joined Yoritomo's 1189 Ōshū campaign and became shugo of Satsuma and Ōsumi in 1197 and Hyūga shortly afterwards. Implicated in the Hiki purge of 1203, he lost his governorships but recovered Satsuma after backing the Hōjō in the 1213 Wada conflict, and took Echizen as shugo in 1221. He died at Kamakura in 1227.
zh: 岛津忠久（卒于1227年），原名惟宗忠久，是镰仓幕府御家人、岛津氏的始祖。1185年，经源赖朝推荐，他出任九州南部岛津庄的下司，不久又任惣地头，后来以岛津为氏。他曾随赖朝参加1189年的奥州合战，1197年出任萨摩和大隅守护，不久又任日向守护。1203年比企之变中，他受比企能员牵连，被没收三国守护之职；1213年和田合战时他站在北条一方，得以恢复萨摩职位，1221年又补任越前守护。1227年，他在镰仓去世。

en: Shimazu Tadamune (1251–1325) was the fourth head of the Shimazu clan and a Kamakura shogunate vassal. He fought beside his father Hisatsune in Kyushu during the Mongol invasions and succeeded as clan head in 1284. During the Einin era (1293–1299), he served under the Kyushu deputy Hōjō Sanemasa on the board of appeals judging suits from western Japan. In 1317 he was made steward of estates including Kōchibio in Hyūga and Matsuura in Hizen, which he parcelled out among his sons, including his heir Sadahisa; these grants founded such Shimazu branch houses as the Hongō, Kabayama and Niiro. He died in 1325, aged seventy-five, and was succeeded by his son Sadahisa.
zh: 岛津忠宗（1251—1325）是岛津氏第四代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。元军来袭时，他在九州随父亲久经作战立功，1284年父亲去世后继承家督。永仁年间（1293—1299），他在镇西探题北条实政手下担任引付，参与裁决西国的诉讼。1317年，他被任命为日向国高知尾庄、肥前国松浦庄等地的地头，并把这些领地分给以嫡子贞久为首的诸子，北乡氏、桦山氏、新纳氏等分家由此产生。1325年他去世，享年七十五岁，由其子贞久继任。

en: Shimazu Tadatoki (1202–1272), first named Tadayoshi, was the second head of the Shimazu clan and a Kamakura shogunate vassal. He fought with distinction in the shogunate army in the Jōkyū War of 1221 and also held the shugo post of Wakasa province. Succeeding his father Tadahisa in 1227, he stayed in Kamakura rather than governing Satsuma in person, rose among the shogun's inner vassals through guard service, and received stewardships in Iga, Sanuki, Izumi, Echizen and Ōmi. In 1265 he passed the clan leadership to his heir Hisatsune. He died in 1272, aged seventy-one.
zh: 岛津忠时（1202—1272），初名忠义，是岛津氏第二代当主、镰仓幕府御家人。1221年承久之乱时，他随幕府军出征并立下战功，还兼任若狭国守护。1227年父亲忠久去世后他继承家督，但没有前往领国，而是住在镰仓，以有力御家人的身份担任近习番役等职，在幕政中颇有分量，并因此获赐伊贺、赞岐、和泉、越前、近江等国的地头职位。1265年，他把家督让给嫡子久经，1272年去世，享年七十一岁。

en: Shimazu Tadatsune was a son, said to be the seventh, of Shimazu Tadatoki, second head of the Shimazu clan of Satsuma. His fourth son Toshitada obtained the Ijūin stewardship in Hioki district, moved to Ijūin and founded the Ijūin branch of the clan.
zh: 岛津忠经是萨摩岛津氏第二代当主岛津忠时之子，相传为第七子。他的第四子俊忠受封日置郡伊集院地头一职，迁居伊集院，开创了岛津氏的伊集院分家。

en: Shimazu Ujihisa (1328–1387) was a Northern and Southern Courts commander and the fourth son of the Shimazu head Sadahisa. In 1352 his father gave him military command over Ōsumi, where he fought the Hatakeyama governor Naoaki, briefly joining the Southern Court in 1356 before returning to the Ashikaga side and becoming shugo of Ōsumi in 1363. He expanded into Hyūga and traded with Ming China. Enraged by Imagawa Ryōshun's murder of Shōni Fuyusuke in 1375, he repeatedly rebelled and submitted, defeating Ryōshun's cousin at Minohara in 1379. He died in 1387.
zh: 岛津氏久（1328—1387）是日本南北朝时代的武将，岛津氏第五代当主贞久的第四子。1352年，隐居的父亲将大隅的军事指挥权交给他，他在大隅与畠山直显交战，1356年一度转投南朝，后又归顺足利一方，于1363年就任大隅守护。他向日向扩张势力，并与明朝开展贸易。1375年今川了俊谋杀少贰冬资，氏久愤而反复叛服，于1379年在蓑原之战击败了俊的从兄弟今川满范，1387年去世。

en: Emperor Shirakawa (1053–1129), personal name Sadahito, was the 72nd emperor of Japan and the founder of cloistered rule. The son of Emperor Go-Sanjō, he reigned from 1073, seeking to rule directly and keep the Fujiwara regent houses in check; in 1077 he founded the temple Hosshō-ji, first of his vow temples. In January 1087 he abdicated in favour of his young son Horikawa, took the title daijō-tennō, and for the next 43 years directed government from his retirement palace, through the reigns of Horikawa and Toba. Ordained a monk in 1096, he kept power until his death in 1129.
zh: 白河天皇（1053—1129），名贞仁，日本第72代天皇，院政制度的开创者。他是后三条天皇之子，1073年即位，力图亲政、抑制藤原摄关家；1077年发愿修建法胜寺，这是他所建一系列御愿寺中的第一座。1087年1月，他让位于幼子善仁（堀河天皇），自号太上天皇，在此后43年间退居白河院，通过堀河、鸟羽两代天皇执掌朝政。1096年他出家受戒，仍紧握大权，直到1129年去世。

en: Honjō Aritsugu, also called Shō Aritsugu, was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Kodama band's Ietsugu line, likely a son of Shō Tomotsugu. Genealogies count him as a possible castellan of Sarukake Castle in Bitchū; his son was Shō Sukefusa.
zh: 本庄有次，亦称庄有次，是镰仓时代儿玉党家次系的武士，一般认为是庄朝次之子。诸系谱推测他曾任备中猿挂城城主，其子为庄资房。

en: Shō Iehiro, also called Kodama no Iehiro, was a late-Heian warrior and fourth head of the main house of the Kodama band, the largest of Musashi Province's seven great warrior parties. Son of Kodama Ieyuki, he settled at Kurisaki, now Honjō in Saitama Prefecture, replaced the name Kodama with Shō, and built Kurisaki Hall. He was an ancestor of the Honjō clan.
zh: 庄家弘，又称儿玉家弘，是平安时代末期的武士，出任武藏国七大武士团中最大的儿玉党本宗家第四代当主。作为儿玉家行之子，他定居于栗崎（今埼玉县本庄市），改儿玉氏为庄氏，并修筑栗崎馆。他是本庄氏之祖。

en: Shō Ienaga, known as Tarō, was a late-Heian and early-Kamakura warrior and fifth head of the Kodama band's main house in Musashi, succeeding his father Iehiro as second lord of Kurisaki Hall. In 1175 he led the Kodama party in a clash over the Takayama manor across the Kōzuke border. At the Battle of Ichinotani in 1184 he killed Taira no Tomoaki and captured the fleeing Taira commander Taira no Shigehira, but his eldest son Yoriie fell. Rewarded with the jitō post of Kusanagi manor in Bitchū, he built Sarukake Castle there and founded the Bitchū Shō line.
zh: 庄太郎家长是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，继承父亲家弘出任武藏国儿玉党本宗家第五代当主，为栗崎馆二代馆主。1175年，他率儿玉党卷入与相邻上野国高山御厨的争端。1184年一之谷之战中，他讨平平知章，又在须磨浦生擒败退的平军副将平重衡，但长子赖家战死此役。凭此战功，他获任备中国草壁庄地头，在当地修筑猿挂城，成为备中庄氏之祖。

en: Shō Ietsugu, known as Saburō, was an early-Kamakura warrior of the Kodama band in Musashi, the third son of Shō Ienaga. After his elder brother Yoriie, the sixth head, fell at the Battle of Ichinotani in 1184, Ietsugu was made Yoriie's adopted heir and became the seventh head. When Ienaga was rewarded with the jitō post of Kusanagi manor in Bitchū, Ietsugu went west to take it up, settled there, and became ancestor of the Bitchū Shō. The Azuma Kagami mentions him once, in 1250, serving in Kyoto with his brother Tokiie.
zh: 庄家次，通称三郎，是镰仓时代初期武藏国儿玉党的武将，庄家长的第三子。1184年，其兄、第六代当主赖家在一之谷之战战死后，家次被家长立为赖家的养子，出任儿玉党本宗家第七代当主。后来家长因战功获封备中国草壁庄地头，家次西赴备中就任并在当地定居，成为备中庄氏之祖。《吾妻镜》中仅在1250年提到他一次，记载他与弟弟时家一同在京都奉公。

en: Shō Sukefusa, known as Saemon Shirō, was a warrior of the late Kamakura period from Oda District in Bitchū Province, now southern Okayama Prefecture, and the first castellan of Kōyama and Takayama castles. He is thought to have been a son of Shō Aritsugu; he held Katayama village and the two castles, and from his day the Bitchū Shō took 'suke' as their generational character. During the Genkō War he served the shogunate under Hōjō Nakatoki, the Echigo governor; in 1333 he fled east with Nakatoki's kin after the Rokuhara tandai fell, reached Banba in Ōmi Province, and died with them at Renge-ji temple.
zh: 庄资房，通称左卫门四郎，是镰仓时代末期备中国小田郡（今冈山县南部）的武将，幸山城与高山城的初代城主。他相传为庄有次之子，领有片山村和两座城池，从他这一代起，备中庄氏以“资”字为通字。元弘之乱中，他追随幕府方的越后守北条仲时；1333年六波罗探题陷落后，他随仲时一族向东败退，至近江国番场宿莲华寺时，与之一同忠死。

en: Shō Sukemasa, known as Saemon, was a warrior of Oda District in Bitchū Province from the end of the Kamakura period. A son of Shō Sukefusa, he was adopted by his elder brother Sukeuji and entered the main line as lord of Sarukake Castle. Genealogies record that he served the Southern Court under Kitabatake Akiyoshi, repeatedly fighting Kō no Moronao, steward of Ashikaga Takauji, and that he received a letter of commendation in 1353; since Moronao was executed in 1351, the fighting must date to the 1340s. His son Shō Sukeaki succeeded him.
zh: 庄资政，通称左卫门，是镰仓末期至南北朝时代备中国小田郡的武将，庄资房之子。他被兄长庄资氏收为养子，由此进入嫡流，成为猿挂城主。据家谱记载，他追随南朝的北畠显能，与足利尊氏的执事高师直屡次交战，并因军功于1353年获赐感状；高师直已于1351年被处死，故这些战斗应发生在1340年代。其子庄资昭继嗣。

en: Shō Sukeuji, known as Shichirō, was a warrior of Oda District in Bitchū Province at the end of the Kamakura period. His father Shō Sukefusa died fighting for the Hōjō in 1333 during the Genkō War, and Sukeuji succeeded him as second lord of Takayama Castle, also called Kōyama Castle. He then took service with Emperor Go-Daigo on the Southern Court side in the Nanboku-chō wars, and adopted his younger brother Sukemasa, who became lord of Sarukake Castle.
zh: 庄资氏，通称七郎，是镰仓时代末期备中国小田郡的武将，高山城（又称幸山城）第二代城主。1333年元弘之乱中，父亲庄资房随北条仲时作战而死，资氏继任城主，随后投奔后醍醐天皇，在南北朝动乱中为南朝效力。他收弟弟庄资政为养子，资政后来成为猿挂城主。

en: Shō Tomotsugu, also called Honjō Tomotsugu, was a Kamakura-period warrior, the legitimate son of Shō Ietsugu and possibly the second of the Bitchū Shō line; he may have been born at Sarukake Castle in Bitchū or at Kurisaki in Musashi. In 1238 the Azuma Kagami names him among the vanguard guards who escorted the fourth shogun, Fujiwara no Yoritsune, into Kyoto, and later that year as a guard of the shogun's palanquin. He did not inherit the Kodama main-house lands, settling instead at Ōtaki in Chichibu District while his uncle Tokiie took the main line. He was the father of Aritsugu.
zh: 庄朝次，亦称本庄朝次，是镰仓时代的武士，庄家次的嫡子，可能是备中庄氏第二代，可能生于备中猿挂城，也可能生于武藏栗崎馆。1238年，《吾妻镜》记载他作为先锋随兵护卫第四代将军藤原赖经入洛，同年又担任将军舆驾的警卫。他没有继承儿玉党本宗家的领地，而是移居武藏国秩父郡的大泷，本宗家由叔父时家继承。其子为有次。

en: Shō Yoriie, known as Kotarō, was a late-Heian warrior from Kurisaki in Musashi, seat of the Kodama band. The legitimate son of Shō Ienaga, he is counted as the sixth head of the Kodama main house. In 1184 he followed Minamoto no Noriyori with his father and uncles against the Taira and fought at the Battle of Ichinotani, where he was killed. He left no heir, so the headship passed to his younger brother Ietsugu, and his young widow, the nun Myōsei, founded Yūsō-ji near his grave in 1202.
zh: 庄赖家，通称小太郎，是平安时代末期武藏国栗崎（儿玉党本据）的年轻武将。他是庄家长的嫡子，被列为儿玉党本宗家第六代当主。1184年，他随父亲与叔父们追随源范赖讨伐平家，在一之谷之战中奋战而死。他身后无嗣，家督由弟弟家次继承；年轻的夫人后出家为尼，法号妙清禅尼，于1202年在其墓旁建立宥庄寺。

en: Emperor Shōmu (701–756), the 45th emperor of Japan, reigned from 724 to 749. A devout Buddhist, he ordered a network of provincial monasteries and nunneries in 741 and in 743 commissioned Tōdai-ji's sixteen-metre Vairocana Buddha, the Daibutsu, in Nara. His rule saw the smallpox epidemic of 735 to 737 and the Fujiwara no Hirotsugu rebellion of 740, after which he moved the capital to Kuni-kyō. He made the Fujiwara-born Kōmyō his empress, the first consort born outside the imperial family. Shōmu abdicated in 749 for his daughter Kōken, took Buddhist vows, and attended the Daibutsu's consecration in 752.
zh: 圣武天皇（701—756）是日本第45代天皇，724年至749年在位。他笃信佛教，741年下令在各国建立国分寺与国分尼寺，743年发愿铸造奈良东大寺高约十六米的卢舍那大佛。在位期间发生735至737年的天花大流行和740年的藤原广嗣之乱，乱后迁都恭仁京。他立藤原氏出身的光明子为皇后，是首位非皇族出身的皇后。749年圣武让位于女儿孝谦，出家为僧，并于752年出席大佛开眼供养法会。

en: Shōni Fuyusuke was a Kyushu warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars, the second son of Shōni Yorihisa and eighth head of the clan. After his brother Tadasuke fell in 1359 and their father retired in 1361, he succeeded as clan head and fought the Southern Court alongside the Ōtomo and Shimazu. In 1371 he welcomed the new Kyushu deputy Imagawa Sadayo, and in 1372 helped retake Dazaifu. In 1375, after reluctantly joining Sadayo's Higo campaign at Mizushima, he was cut down by Imagawa Nakaaki at a welcoming banquet on Sadayo's orders in the Mizushima Incident. His brother Yorizumi succeeded him.
zh: 少贰冬资是日本南北朝时代的九州武将，为少贰赖尚的次子、少贰氏第八代当主。1359年兄长直资战死后，父亲又于1361年隐居，他遂继承家督，联合大友氏、岛津氏与南朝作战。1371年，他迎接新任九州探题今川贞世（了俊），并于1372年协助其收复大宰府。1375年，他勉强前往肥后水岛参加贞世的军阵，却在欢迎宴会上被贞世授意的今川仲秋斩杀，史称水岛之变。家督由弟弟赖澄继承。

en: Shōni Moritsune (1254–1308) was a military commander of the mid-Kamakura period and the fourth head of the Shōni clan of Kyushu. He is thought to have been the eldest son of Shōni Tsunesuke, from whom he inherited the shugo posts of Chikuzen, Tsushima and Iki, while the clan's former provinces of Chikugo, Buzen and Hizen passed into Hōjō hands. In 1297 the shogunate posted the first Chinzei tandai, Hōjō Kanetoki, to Hakata, tightening Hōjō rule over Kyushu as Moritsune prepared against a third Mongol invasion. He died in Kamakura in 1308.
zh: 少贰盛经（1254—1308）是镰仓时代中期的武将、九州少贰氏第四代当主，一般认为是少贰经资的长子。他继承了父亲的筑前、对马、壹岐守护之职，而少贰氏三代相传的筑后、丰前、肥前三国守护则落入北条得宗之手。1297年，镰仓幕府向博多派出首任镇西探题北条兼时，在防备蒙古第三次来袭的同时，北条氏对九州的控制日益加强。1308年，盛经在镰仓去世。

en: Shōni Sadatsune (1272–1336) was a military commander of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō eras and the fifth head of the Shōni clan. In 1333 he first helped the Chinzei tandai defeat Kikuchi Taketoki's revolt, then defected to Ashikaga Takauji once the Rokuhara tandai fell, forcing the Chinzei tandai Hōjō Hidetoki to kill himself. Under the Kenmu Restoration he was made shugo of Chikuzen, Buzen and Chikugo. He joined Takauji's revolt in 1335; in 1336, with his son Yorihisa away leading the main army, he was attacked by Kikuchi Taketoshi at Uchiyama Castle and took his own life.
zh: 少贰贞经（1272—1336）是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将、少贰氏第五代当主。1333年菊池武时举兵时，他起初协助镇西探题将其击败；得知六波罗探题陷落后便倒向足利尊氏，迫使镇西探题北条英时自尽。建武新政时期，他被任命为筑前、丰前、筑后三国守护。1335年他追随足利尊氏反叛；1336年因子赖尚率主力远征在外，他在有智山城遭菊池武敏攻打，自尽身亡，享年65岁。

en: Shōni Sukeyoshi (1198–1281) was a Kamakura-period warrior and the second head of the Shōni clan, first to take the Shōni name. As the shogunate's Chinzei commissioner he ruled much of northern Kyūshū and in 1268 received envoys from the Mongol Yuan. He took Buddhist orders as Kakue before the first Mongol invasion of 1274 and passed family leadership to his son Tsunesuke, yet still led Kyūshū's forces against the invaders. In 1281 he fought at Iki Island during the second invasion and helped drive the Mongols out, dying soon afterwards from his wounds at the age of eighty-four.
zh: 少贰资能（1198—1281）是镰仓时代前期至中期的武将、御家人，少贰氏第二代当主，也是家族中最先以少贰为姓者。作为幕府的镇西奉行，他在北九州势力极大，1268年曾负责接待元朝使者。1274年文永之役前夕他出家，法号觉惠，将家督让给长子经资，但仍以高龄出任九州总指挥官迎战元军，将其击退。1281年弘安之役，他再度以老躯出征，在壹岐岛之战中奋力将元军逐出壹岐，却因战伤不久后去世，享年84岁。

en: Shōni Tadasuke was a Kyushu warrior of the Nanboku-chō wars, the eldest son of Shōni Yorihisa and seventh head of the clan. By 1350 his father had transferred to him the hereditary title of Dazai Shōni, and the character 'tada' in his name was granted by Ashikaga Tadafuyu, husband of his sister. He led the Shōni under his father, and in 1359 fell at the Battle of Chikugogawa, also called Ōbara, against Kikuchi Takemitsu's Southern Court army. Genealogies name his sons Yorikuni, said to have died fighting, and Yorioki; his brother Fuyusuke succeeded him.
zh: 少贰直资是日本南北朝时代的九州武将，为少贰赖尚的长子、少贰氏第七代当主。约1350年，父亲将世代相传的大宰少贰名号让给他，名字中的‘直’字则得自其姐妹之夫足利直冬的偏讳。他随父亲领兵征战，1359年在筑后川之战（又称大保原之战）中对阵菊池武光的南朝军，战死沙场。家谱记载他有儿子赖国（相传亦战死）与赖兴，家督由弟弟冬资继承。

en: Shōni Tsunesuke (1229–1292) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the third Shōni head, succeeding his father Sukeyoshi. In Kyūshū he organised the anti-Mongol coastal defences, including the Hakata stone wall, and dealt with Yuan envoys. Already Dazai Shōni by 1274, he inherited the family headship in 1275. At the 1281 Battle of Iki Island he fought wounded and drove off the Mongols, but lost his son Suketoki. Ordained in 1284, he sided against his brother Kagesuke in the Shimotsuki conflict of 1285, and the Shōni were stripped of several governorships. He died in 1292 and was succeeded by Moritsune.
zh: 少贰经资（1229—1292）是镰仓时代中期的武将、御家人，少贰氏第三代当主，继承父亲资能。他在九州负责整备抵御蒙古的沿海防御，统括博多石垒的修筑，并处理元朝使节事宜。1274年前已任大宰少贰，1275年继承家督。1281年壹岐岛之战，他带伤奋战、击退元军，却失去了儿子资时。1284年出家；1285年霜月骚乱中与弟弟景资兵戎相向，少贰氏随后被剥夺数国守护职。1292年去世，家督由盛经继承。

en: Shōni Yorihisa (1294–1372) was sixth head of the Shōni house of Kyushu. In 1333 he joined the Genkō War and helped his father Sadatsune destroy the Hōjō deputy at Hakata. He fought beside Ashikaga Takauji at Tatarahama in 1336 and Minatogawa, receiving the shugo posts of Chikuzen, Buzen, Higo and Tsushima. In 1349 he backed Ashikaga Tadafuyu, marrying him to his daughter, and later joined the Southern Court's Prince Kanenaga against the Isshiki. Defeated by Kikuchi Takemitsu at the Chikugogawa in 1359 and driven from Dazaifu in 1361, he retired to Kyoto in 1367 and died in 1372.
zh: 少贰赖尚（1294—1372）是九州武家少贰氏第六代当主。1333年他参加元弘之乱，随父亲少贰贞经攻灭博多的北条氏镇西探题。他追随足利尊氏，在1336年的多多良滨之战和凑川之战中作战，受封筑前、丰前、肥后、对马等国守护。1349年他扶植逃到九州的足利直冬并招其为婿，后又与南朝的怀良亲王结盟对抗一色氏。1359年他在筑后川之战败于菊池武光，1361年被逐出大宰府，1367年隐居上京，1372年在京都去世。

en: Soga no Iname (c. 506–570) led the Soga clan and became the first verifiable Ōomi, or great minister, in 536, serving Emperors Senka and Kinmei. He strengthened his house by marrying two daughters, Kitashihime and Oanegimi, to Emperor Kinmei; their children included Emperor Yōmei, Emperor Sushun and Empress Suiko. After Buddhism reached the Yamato court from Baekje in 552, he became its leading patron and built a temple at his Mukuhara residence, drawing the hostility of Mononobe no Okoshi and the Nakatomi clan. He died in 570, and his son Soga no Umako inherited his power.
zh: 苏我稻目（约506—570）是苏我氏首领，536年成为日本史上第一位可考的大臣，侍奉宣化、钦明两天皇。他把坚盐媛、小姊君两个女儿嫁给钦明天皇，所生子女中包括用明天皇、崇峻天皇和推古天皇。552年佛教自百济传入大和朝廷后，他成为最主要的崇佛者，在向原的宅邸建寺，由此招致物部尾舆与中臣氏的敌视。他于570年去世，其子苏我马子继承了他的权势。

en: Soga no Kitashihime was a daughter of the Soga clan leader Soga no Iname and a consort of Emperor Kinmei, as her father worked to bind his family to the Yamato throne. She bore the emperor seven sons and six daughters, among them Emperor Yōmei and the Princess Nukatabe, who reigned as Empress Suiko, Japan's first empress regnant. After her death she received the title kōtaifujin, and in 612 a grand state funeral re-interred her beside Emperor Kinmei in his Hinokuma tumulus, a ceremony that displayed the Soga clan's power.
zh: 苏我坚盐媛是苏我氏首领苏我稻目之女，嫁给钦明天皇为妃，这是其父联姻大和朝廷的安排。她为钦明天皇生下七男六女，其中包括用明天皇，以及后来成为日本首位女帝的额田部皇女，即推古天皇。她去世后被尊为皇太夫人，612年朝廷举行盛大葬礼，将她改葬于钦明天皇的桧隈大陵，这场仪式彰显了苏我氏的权势。

en: Soga no Oane no Kimi was a daughter of the Soga clan leader Soga no Iname and a sister of Soga no Umako. She followed her sister Kitashihime into the palace as a consort of Emperor Kinmei and bore him five children. They included Prince Hatsusebe, who reigned as Emperor Sushun from 587 until his assassination in 592, and Princess Anahobe no Hashihito, wife of Emperor Yōmei and mother of Prince Shōtoku.
zh: 苏我小姊君是苏我氏首领苏我稻目之女、苏我马子的姐妹。她随姐姐坚盐媛入宫，成为钦明天皇之妃，生下五名子女，其中包括587年即位、592年遇刺身亡的泊濑部皇子，即崇峻天皇，以及用明天皇之妻、圣德太子之母穴穗部间人皇女。

en: Sō Moriakira was a Kamakura-period warrior and deputy steward (jitō-dai) of Tsushima, the eldest son of Sō Sukekuni. In 1274 his father was killed opposing the Mongol landing at Sasuura in the Bun'ei campaign; Moriakira escaped because he was then serving at Dazaifu, and succeeded him as the Sō family's head on the island. He fought the Mongols once more when they returned in force during the Kōan campaign of 1281. His common name was Umatarō.
zh: 宗盛明是镰仓时代武将，任对马国地头代，宗助国的长子。1274年文永之役中，父亲在佐须浦迎击登陆的蒙古军时战死；盛明因当时正在大宰府出仕而幸免于难，随后继任为宗氏在对马的当主。1281年弘安之役蒙古大军再度来袭时，他再次与元军作战。他的通称为右马太郎。

en: Sō Morikuni was the fourth head of the Sō clan, the warrior family that ruled Tsushima Island, succeeding his father Moriaki. As earlier heads had done, he received a character for his name from the Shōni of northern Kyushu, his suzerains. After the Muromachi shogunate was founded in 1336, he acknowledged its authority over Tsushima and governed the island as the Shōni's deputy through the wars of the Northern and Southern Courts. His son Tsuneshige succeeded him as head of the clan.
zh: 宗盛国是统治对马岛的武家宗氏第四代当主，继承父亲宗盛明之位。与此前的当主一样，他从主家北九州少贰氏处接受偏讳。1336年室町幕府开设后，他承认幕府对对马国的支配，在南北朝动乱中以少贰氏代理的身份统治对马岛。其子宗经茂后来继任家督。

en: Sō Morinao was a warrior of the Northern and Southern Courts period and the eldest son of Sō Morikuni. Born in Chikuzen, he lost a struggle for the family headship to Tsuneshige, Morikuni's designated heir. While Tsuneshige joined the Northern Court, Morinao served Kikuchi Takemitsu on the Southern Court's side. He fought the forces of Imagawa Ryōshun, the shogunate's commissioner in Kyushu, and was killed in battle in 1372.
zh: 宗盛直是日本南北朝时代的武将，宗盛国的长子。他出身筑前，在家督之争中败给盛国的嫡子宗经茂。经茂投向北朝，盛直则在南朝一方侍奉菊池武光。他与幕府九州探题今川了俊的军队作战，1372年战死。

en: Sō Naoshige was a member of the Sō clan of Tsushima, a son of Sō Tsuneshige and the father of Sō Sadashige.
zh: 宗尚茂是对马宗氏一员，为宗经茂之子、宗贞茂之父。

en: Sō Shigehisa was a legendary Kamakura-period warrior whom the Sō clan of Tsushima called its founder. Tradition makes him a son of Taira no Tomomune. In 1245, after Abiru Kuninobu of Tsushima defied orders from Dazaifu, Shigehisa defeated him and was appointed deputy steward (jitō-dai) of the island, the foundation of the Sō family's rule there. His grave is shown at Kifurugoba Shrine.
zh: 宗重尚是传说中的镰仓时代武将，被对马宗氏尊为始祖。相传他是平知宗之子。1245年，对马的阿比留国信违抗大宰府之命，重尚将其讨伐，并因功被任为对马地头代，这成为宗氏统治对马的根基。木武古婆神社存有相传为他的坟墓。

en: Sō Sukekuni (1207–1274) was a mid-Kamakura warrior, deputy steward and shugo deputy of Tsushima for the Shōni family, counted as the second Sō head on the island. In the Bun'ei campaign a Mongol fleet said to number four hundred and fifty ships and thirty thousand men landed at Sasuura on 4 November 1274. Sukekuni rode through the night with only eighty-odd horsemen. The next morning he sent an interpreter to question the invaders, who opened fire with arrows, and his men hastily formed ranks to fight. The chronicle Hachiman Gudōkun recounts that he fell with his sons and all his men in the Mongol invasions' first battle. He is enshrined at Komodahama Shrine.
zh: 宗助国（1207—1274）是日本镰仓时代中期武将，任对马国地头代兼守护代，被视为对马宗氏第二代当主，代少贰氏管理对马。文永之役时，据称四百五十艘船只、三万人的元丽联军于1274年11月4日在佐须浦登陆，助国仅率八十余骑连夜穿山驰赴战场。次日清晨，他派通译前去问询，来军随即射箭，助国等人仓促列阵应战。据《八幡愚童训》记载，他与儿子及全体郎党一同战死，这是蒙古袭日的首场战斗。他被祭祀于小茂田浜神社。

en: Sō Tsuneshige, also called Sōkei, was the fifth head of the Sō clan of Tsushima and a son of Morikuni. He received a character for his name from Shōni Sadatsune of northern Kyushu, to whom the Sō were vassals. In 1349 he made his younger brother Yoritsugu his deputy on the island and moved him to Nii village. After the Shōni ceased issuing orders on Tsushima around 1362, Tsuneshige began turning the Sō family's holdings there into a domain of their own. Sumishige succeeded him as head of the clan.
zh: 宗经茂，一称宗庆，是对马宗氏第五代当主，宗盛国之子。他从宗氏的主君、北九州的少贰贞经处接受偏讳。1349年，他任命弟弟宗赖次为对马的代理，让其移住仁位村。1362年以后，少贰氏不再向对马下发文书，经茂开始将宗氏在岛上的领地经营为独立领国。宗澄茂后来继他之后成为当主。

en: Sō Yoritsugu, better known as Nii Shūkō, was a commander of the Northern and Southern Courts period and a younger son of the Tsushima lord Sō Morikuni. In 1349 his elder brother Tsuneshige made him deputy governor of Tsushima, and he moved from Dazaifu to Nakamura in Nii village on the island. He banned reckless mountain logging and in 1362 set the crop tax at two bu five rin, working to stabilize the island's government. After his death the islanders honored his achievements by enshrining him at the Jinushi shrine.
zh: 宗赖次，通常以仁位宗香之名著称，是日本南北朝时代的武将，对马领主宗盛国之子。1349年，兄长宗经茂任命他为对马守护代，他遂从大宰府迁往岛上的仁位村中村。他禁止滥伐山林，并于1362年将田租定为二分五厘，致力于安定民政。死后岛民感念其功绩，在地主社祭祀他。

en: Sōma Chikatane (dates unknown) was the seventh head of the Mutsu Sōma clan and lord of Odaka Castle, who accompanied his father Shigetane when the clan migrated from Shimōsa to Mutsu. He inherited the headship in 1335 and fought for Ashikaga Takauji against the Kenmu regime, seeing action at Hakone and Takenoshita. While he campaigned as far as Kyushu, his father fell at Kamakura and Odaka fell to the Southern Court; returning north, he rallied the clan survivors, defeated Kitabatake Akiie, and retook the old domains. He appears to have retired as a monk in 1358.
zh: 相马亲胤（生没年不详）是陆奥相马氏第七代当主、小高城城主，在父亲重胤一代随一族从下总迁往陆奥。1335年他继承家督，追随足利尊氏反抗建武政权，在箱根、竹之下等地作战。他转战至九州期间，父亲在镰仓战死，小高城被南朝攻陷；亲胤返回陆奥后聚拢残党，击败北畠显家，收复旧领。据推测他于1358年出家隐居。

en: Sōma Morotane was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Sōma clan, a Chiba branch house in Shimōsa, and the fifth head of the line later called the Mutsu Sōma. A son of Sōma Tanemura by a later wife, he claimed after his father's death that Tanemura's will named him heir over his elder half-brother Sōma Ujiuji. The headship was confirmed to Ujiuji and Morotane remained without court rank or office. In the Shōō era (1288–1293) he ceded his lands to his son Sōma Shigetane; he had died by the Einin era (1293–1299).
zh: 相马师胤是镰仓时代武将，出自下总国千叶氏庶流相马氏，被列为日后陆奥相马氏一脉的第五代当主。他是相马胤村后妻所生之子，父亲去世后声称胤村遗命立自己为继承人，与异母兄相马胤氏对立；最终家督由胤氏继承，师胤无位无官。正应年间（1288—1293），他将所领让给儿子相马重胤，至永仁年间（1293—1299）已经去世。

en: Sōma Morotsune (1139?–1205) was a son of Chiba Tsunetane and the first head of the Sōma warrior house. With his father he joined Minamoto no Yoritomo's rising of 1180 and campaigned under Yoritomo's brother Noriyori across the provinces; his service in the 1189 Ōshū campaign is said to have earned him a banner of Hachiman Daibosatsu from Yoritomo. When Tsunetane died in 1201 he took Buddhist orders, said to have become a disciple of the monk Hōnen, and passed leadership to his son Yoshitane. He is said to have died seated at his Kamakura mansion in 1205 while chanting the nenbutsu.
zh: 相马师常（1139？—1205）是千叶常胤之子、相马氏初代当主。他与父亲一同参加源赖朝1180年的举兵，隶属赖朝之弟源范赖的军队转战各地；相传他在1189年奥州合战时立功，获赖朝赐予“八幡大菩萨”旗帜。1201年父亲常胤去世后他出家为僧，相传成为法然的弟子，把家督让给儿子义胤。相传他于1205年在镰仓的相马邸端坐念佛而终。

en: Sōma Shigetane was the sixth head of the line that became the Mutsu Sōma and its effective founder in Mutsu. Repeatedly worsted in land disputes with the main Sōma line in Shimōsa, in 1323 he led eighty-odd mounted followers, with temples and willing peasants, north to Namekata District, where he built Odaka Castle and extended his holdings along the Ota River. After the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333 he joined the Kenmu Restoration, then sided with Ashikaga Takauji. He died in 1336 defending Kamakura against Kitabatake Akiie's Southern Court army.
zh: 相马重胤是日后陆奥相马氏一脉的第六代当主，也是该氏在陆奥的实际开创者。他与下总相马氏嫡流因领地屡次相争、渐处下风，遂于1323年率八十余骑，连同寺社和愿从的百姓北上进入陆奥国行方郡，修筑小高城，沿太田川扩张势力。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他先归附建武新政，后转投足利尊氏。1336年，他在镰仓抵御南朝方北畠显家的进攻时战死。

en: Sōma Tanemura was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Sōma clan in Shimōsa Province, the fourth head of the line that later became the Mutsu Sōma. He was a son of Sōma Tanetsuna, and after he died his sons Ujiuji and Morotane disputed the headship.
zh: 相马胤村是镰仓时代武将，出自下总国相马氏，为日后陆奥相马氏一脉的第四代当主，相马胤纲之子。他去世后，儿子相马胤氏与相马师胤围绕家督之位发生争执。

en: Sōma Tanetsuna was the third head of the Sōma clan, son of Sōma Yoshitane. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he fought beside his father at the Uji River and Seta Bridge. His daughter married Shimazu Hisatsune and mothered the fourth Shimazu head Tadamune.
zh: 相马胤纲是相马氏第三代当主，相马义胤之子。1221年承久之乱时，他随父亲在宇治川和濑田桥作战。他的女儿嫁给岛津久经，是第四代当主岛津忠宗的生母。

en: Sōma Yoshitane was the second head of the Sōma clan and a Kamakura shogunate vassal, succeeding his father Morotsune when the latter retired in 1201. In 1205, although related to Hatakeyama Shigetada by marriage, he took Hōjō Yoshitoki's side against Shigetada and helped destroy him, receiving the stewardship of Takagi in Mutsu province as his reward. During the Jōkyū War of 1221 he and his son Tanetsuna fought for the shogunate at the Uji River and at Seta Bridge in Ōmi. He afterwards also held estates in Echigo and Yamato.
zh: 相马义胤是镰仓时代武将、相马氏第二代当主，1201年父亲师常隐居后继承家督。1205年畠山重忠之乱时，尽管他与重忠有姻亲关系，仍站在北条义时一方讨伐重忠，因功被任命为陆奥国高城保的地头。1221年承久之乱爆发，他与儿子胤纲一同加入幕府军，在宇治川之战和近江濑田桥之战中立下军功。此后他继续忠仕幕府，在越后、大和两国也获得了领地。

en: Sue Hirokata, a warrior of the Migita branch of the Ōuchi house in Suō Province, settled in Sue village in Yoshiki District and took its name, founding the Sue clan. His son Sue Hiromasa succeeded him.
zh: 陶弘贤是周防国大内氏支流右田氏的武士，他迁居吉敷郡陶村（今山口市）并以地名为姓，开创陶氏，后由其子陶弘政继嗣。

en: Sue Hiromasa was the second head of the Sue, a warrior clan of Suō Province that served the Ōuchi as hereditary retainers. The son of the clan founder Sue Hirokata, he held the Tonda estate in Tsuno District before the 1352 war between Ōuchi Hiroyo and Washizu Sadahiro, and built a fortified residence called Hirajō there. He founded Shōeiji, whose grounds were surrounded by earthen ramparts and a moat, and placed outlying forts on Nanao-yama, Kōzu-yama and Bessho. He founded Shōgo-ji in Sue village, where his grave remains.
zh: 陶弘政是周防国武家陶氏的第二代当主，陶氏世代为大内氏的谱代重臣。他是陶氏始祖陶弘贤之子，在1352年大内弘世与鹫头贞弘交战之前，已领有都浓郡富田保，并在当地修筑居城平城。他创建了胜荣寺，寺院旧址环有土垒与壕沟；他又在七尾山、上野山、别所等地设置城砦。他在陶村创建正护寺，其墓所即在该寺境内。

en: Sue Hironaga was the third head of the Sue clan of Suō Province and the son of Sue Hiromasa. In 1399 he followed Ōuchi Yoshihiro in the Ōei Rebellion against the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu. Hironaga urged Yoshihiro to return to Suō and try again, but Yoshihiro fought on and was killed. Hironaga later supported Ōuchi Moriharu in his struggle for the succession. In 1401 the Ōuchi appointed him shugodai, deputy military governor of Nagato Province, under Moriharu. He held the court title of Owari-no-kami. He was killed campaigning at Inodake in Buzen Province, and was given the dharma name Dōrin. His cousin Morinaga succeeded him as head of the Sue.
zh: 陶弘长是周防国陶氏第三代当主，陶弘政之子。1399年，他随大内义弘参加反抗将军足利义满的应永之乱。他劝义弘返回周防以图再起，义弘却继续作战并战死。此后，弘长在大内氏的家督之争中支持大内盛见。1401年，他在盛见任内被大内氏任命为长门国守护代。他官称尾张守，后来出征丰前国，在猪岳战死，法名道琳。其堂兄弟盛长继承了陶氏家督。

en: Sue Hirotsuna was a son of the Sue clan founder Sue Hirokata and an Ōuchi retainer in Suō Province. Holding the court titles kunaishōyū and Suō-no-kami, he served as shugodai, deputy military governor of Nagato Province, under Ōuchi Hiroyo from 1358 to 1374.
zh: 陶弘纲是陶氏始祖陶弘贤之子，出仕周防大内氏，官称宫内少辅、周防守。1358年至1374年间，他在守护大内弘世麾下担任长门国守护代。

en: Suetsugu Kiyoshige was a warrior of the Suetsugu clan, a branch of the Izumo Minamoto in Izumo Province. Genealogies name him as a son of Suetsugu Tanekiyo and record that he took the field during the Mongol invasions around 1281.
zh: 末次清镇是出云国武士，出自末次氏，该族为出云源氏的支流。系谱记载他是末次胤清之子，在1281年前后蒙古袭来时随军出阵。

en: Suetsugu Suketaka was a grandson of the Izumo warrior Suetsugu Kiyoshige. In 1333 he followed Enya Takasada in helping Emperor Go-Daigo return to Kyoto after the emperor's exile on the Oki Islands.
zh: 末次佐隆是出云武士末次清镇之孙。1333年，他跟随盐冶高贞，为被流放隐岐岛的后醍醐天皇返回京都尽力。

en: Suetsugu Takamune was a warrior of the Suetsugu clan, a local landholding family of Izumo Province descended from the Sasaki branch of the Uda-Genji. He fought with distinction for the Northern Court under Ashikaga Takauji.
zh: 末次隆宗是出云国国人末次氏的武士，末次氏出自宇多源氏佐佐木氏流。南北朝动乱中，他在足利尊氏麾下为北朝立下战功。

en: Suetsugu Tanekiyo founded the Suetsugu house of Izumo Genji; a genealogy names him as the fourth son of Toda Yoshiyasu.
zh: 末次胤清是出云源氏末次氏的始祖，系谱称他为富田义泰的四子。

en: Suiko (554–628), Japan's 33rd sovereign and first recognised empress, was a daughter of Emperor Kinmei and Soga no Kitashihime, and empress to her half-brother Emperor Bidatsu from 576. After Soga no Umako had Emperor Sushun murdered in 592, she was enthroned in 593. She named her nephew Shōtoku regent, and their rule promoted Buddhism with the Flourishing Three Treasures Edict of 594, opened relations with Sui China in 600, and introduced the Twelve Level Cap and Rank system and Seventeen-Article Constitution. In 624 she rejected Umako's bid for the Kazuraki district; she died in 628 after a 35-year reign.
zh: 推古天皇（554—628）是日本第33代君主，也是第一位得到广泛承认的女帝。她是钦明天皇与苏我坚盐媛之女，576年成为异母兄敏达天皇的皇后。592年苏我马子弑杀崇峻天皇后，她于593年被拥上皇位。她立侄儿圣德太子为摄政，在位期间以594年的《兴隆三宝诏》弘扬佛教，600年与中国隋朝建立关系，并推行冠位十二阶与《十七条宪法》。624年，她断然拒绝马子索要葛城县封地的请求；628年去世，在位35年。

en: Sukō (1334–1398), personal name Okihito, was the third emperor of the Northern Court in Kyoto and the eldest son of Emperor Kōgon and Ōgimachisanjō Hideko. He became crown prince and ascended in 1348 after Emperor Kōmyō abdicated, while Kōgon directed affairs as cloistered emperor. In 1351 Ashikaga Takauji made peace with the Southern Court and forced Sukō from the throne. In 1352 Southern troops carried him off to Yoshino with Kōgon and Kōmyō; he returned to Kyoto in 1357. His great-grandson became Emperor Go-Hanazono in 1428.
zh: 崇光天皇（1334—1398）名兴仁，是京都北朝第三代天皇，为光严天皇与正亲町三条秀子的长子。1348年光明天皇让位后，他被立为皇太子并即位，由光严上皇开设院政。1351年，足利尊氏与南朝议和，逼迫崇光退位。1352年，南军将他连同光严、光明两位上皇一同劫往吉野，他于1357年才返回京都。1428年，其曾孙即位为后花园天皇。

en: Sushun (c. 553–592), the 32nd emperor of Japan, was a son of Emperor Kinmei who ascended in 587 as Prince Hatsusebe. His reign was dominated by the great minister Soga no Umako, on whose support his throne rested. Resenting the constraint, Sushun planned to do away with Umako, but the minister struck first: in 592 he sent an agent, Yamatonoaya no Koma, who murdered the emperor. He is the only Japanese sovereign whose assassination by a subject the official chronicles record outright. The throne then passed to his half-sister, Empress Suiko.
zh: 崇峻天皇（约553—592）是日本第32代天皇，钦明天皇之子，587年以泊濑部皇子的身份即位。在位期间，朝政完全受制于拥立他的大臣苏我马子。崇峻心怀不满，图谋除掉马子，马子却抢先下手，于592年派刺客东汉直驹将他弑杀。他是日本正史中唯一一位明载被臣下暗杀的天皇。他死后，皇位由其异母姐推古继承。

en: Emperor Sutoku (1119–1164), personal name Akihito, was the 75th emperor of Japan, a son of Emperor Toba by Fujiwara no Tamako. Put on the throne at three in 1123, he was a figurehead under the cloistered Shirakawa and then Toba, who in 1141 forced him to abdicate in favour of his younger brother Konoe. In 1151 he commissioned the waka anthology Shika Wakashū. After Toba's death he rose in the Hōgen Rebellion of 1156, was defeated by Go-Shirakawa's forces, and died in 1164 in exile in Sanuki Province. He was later counted among Japan's three vengeful spirits and enshrined at Shiramine Shrine in Kyoto.
zh: 崇德天皇（1119—1164），名显仁，日本第75代天皇，鸟羽天皇与中宫藤原璋子（待贤门院）之子。1123年他3岁时被扶上皇位，先后在白河、鸟羽两位上皇的院政下形同傀儡，1141年鸟羽上皇迫使他让位给弟弟近卫天皇。1151年他下命编纂敕撰和歌集《词花和歌集》。鸟羽法皇死后，他在1156年的保元之乱中举兵，被后白河天皇一方击败，流放赞岐国，1164年死于流放地。他死后被列为日本三大怨灵之一，后来在京都白峰神宫受到祭祀。

en: Suwa Morishige was a mid-Kamakura warrior and a trusted miuchibito, or houseman, of the Hōjō tokusō. First appearing in the Azuma Kagami in 1230, he kept a residence inside the compound of Regent Hōjō Yasutoki from 1236 and handled dealings with the court. After taking the tonsure he was known as the lay monk Renbutsu. As spokesman for the tokusō's housemen he calmed the warriors gathering at Kamakura on the eve of the Hōji War of 1247 and was praised by Hōjō Tokiyori for matchless service. He died around the fourth month of 1267.
zh: 诹访盛重是镰仓时代中期的武士，身为北条得宗的亲信御内人。《吾妻镜》中他最早见于1230年；1236年北条泰时的新邸建成后，他在邸内构屋而居，负责与朝廷交涉。出家后以法名莲佛入道著称。作为得宗御内人的代表，1247年宝治合战前夕，他安抚聚集镰仓的武士，被北条时赖誉为“无双之功”。他于1267年4月前后去世。

en: Suwa Naoyori was the name taken by the Suwa Upper Shrine high priest Yoritsugu after he received a character from Ashikaga Tadayoshi. During the Kannō Disturbance of 1350 to 1352 he fought as a leading Tadayoshi-faction general in Shinano and in 1351 captured Suzawa Castle, where the Takauji commander Kō no Morofuyu took his own life. After Tadayoshi's fall he served the Southern Court's Prince Munenaga, fighting at Musashino in 1352, but returned to the Muromachi shogunate by 1359. Ordained as Fukan, he remained the elder statesman of the Suwa clan until his death around 1395.
zh: 诹访直赖是诹访上社大祝赖嗣接受足利直义偏讳后改用的名字。1350年至1352年观应之乱中，他作为直义派主力武将转战信浓，1351年攻陷须泽城，尊氏派名将高师冬在城中自尽。直义失势后，他投奔南朝的宗良亲王，1352年参加武藏野合战，至1359年已回归室町幕府。出家后法号普宽，他作为诹访一族的元老仍保有影响力，约1395年去世。

en: Suwa Nobutsugu was a son of the Suwa Upper Shrine high priest Suwa Tokitsugu and younger brother of Suwa Yoritsugu. After the Nakasendai Rebellion of 1335, Suwa Enchū deposed the acting high priest Fujisawa Masayori and installed Nobutsugu as ōhōri of the Upper Shrine.
zh: 诹访信嗣是诹访上社大祝诹访时继之子、诹访赖嗣之弟。1335年中先代之乱后，诹访圆忠废黜代理大祝藤泽政赖，迎立信嗣为上社大祝。

en: Suwa Tokitsugu was high priest of the Upper Shrine of Suwa and the legitimate heir of Suwa Yorishige, with the title Provisional Governor of Aki. He is thought to have fought for the shogunate at the 1331 siege of Akasaka Castle against Kusunoki Masashige. After the shogunate's fall he joined his father in sheltering Hōjō Tokiyuki. In the second month of 1335 he passed the high-priesthood to his seven-year-old son Yoritsugu, and that summer father and son rose in the Nakasendai War and briefly held Kamakura. Defeated by Ashikaga Takauji, Tokitsugu killed himself on 6 September 1335.
zh: 诹访时继是诹访大社上社大祝、诹访赖重的嫡子，官居安艺权守。一般认为，1331年元弘之乱时，他作为幕府军参加了攻打楠木正成据守的赤坂城之战。幕府灭亡后，他与父亲一同庇护北条时行。1335年2月，他把大祝之位传给年仅七岁的儿子赖嗣；同年夏天，父子拥时行发起中先代之乱，一度占领镰仓。被足利尊氏击败后，时继于1335年9月6日自尽。

en: Suwa Yorishige, known in religion as Shōun, was high priest of the Upper Shrine of Suwa in Shinano and leader of the Suwa Shrine warrior league, with the title Provisional Governor of Mikawa. After the Kamakura shogunate fell in 1333, he sheltered the tokusō's orphaned heir Hōjō Tokiyuki. In the seventh month of 1335 he and his son Tokitsugu raised Tokiyuki and launched the Nakasendai War, routing Ashikaga Tadayoshi and taking Kamakura. Ashikaga Takauji marched east and crushed the rising. On 6 September 1335 Yorishige and his chief commanders killed themselves in Kamakura, letting Tokiyuki escape.
zh: 诹访赖重法名照云，是信浓国诹访大社上社的大祝、诹访神党的盟主，官居三河权守。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，他庇护了得宗家的遗孤北条时行。1335年7月，他与儿子时继奉时行为主发起中先代之乱，击败足利直义，攻占镰仓。足利尊氏随即东上，将叛乱镇压。1335年9月6日，赖重与主要部将在镰仓自尽，使时行得以逃脱。

en: Suwa Yoritsugu (1329–c. 1395) was the ōhōri, high priest of the Upper Shrine of Suwa in Shinano Province, and the son of Suwa Tokitsugu. His father and grandfather died backing Hōjō Tokiyuki in the Nakasendai Rebellion of 1335, so he inherited the priesthood as a child. In 1347 he petitioned the Muromachi shogunate for the rank of Shinano-no-kami rather than the lesser gon-no-kami, and became a commander in Ashikaga Tadayoshi's faction, rivalling the Ogasawara clan for mastery of Shinano. He later took the names Naoyori and then Yorihiro.
zh: 诹访赖嗣（1329—约1395）是信浓国诹访大社上社的大祝，诹访时继之子。1335年，其父与祖父因支持北条时行发动中先代之乱而死，他幼年继任大祝。1347年，他向室町幕府求官，辞回信浓权守的任命，坚持受任信浓守，随后成为足利直义麾下武将，与小笠原氏争夺信浓的霸权。他后来先后改名直赖、赖宽。

en: Emperor Suzaku (923–952), personal name Yutaakira, reigned as Japan's 61st emperor from 930 to 946. The eleventh son of Emperor Daigo, he ascended at eight after his elder brother and nephew died young, while his uncle Fujiwara no Tadahira ruled as regent. His reign saw the Shōhei–Tengyō rebellions: Taira no Masakado's revolt in the Kantō was crushed by Fujiwara no Hidesato in 940, and Fujiwara no Sumitomo's rising in the west by Tachibana no Tōyasu in 941. Sickly and heirless, Suzaku abdicated to his younger brother Emperor Murakami in 946, took vows at Ninna-ji, and died in 952.
zh: 朱雀天皇（923—952），名宽明，是日本第61代天皇，930年至946年在位。他是醍醐天皇的第十一子，因兄长与侄儿早夭而被立为太子，八岁即位，舅父藤原忠平以摄政身份掌权。他在位期间爆发承平、天庆年间的叛乱：平将门在关东起兵，940年被藤原秀乡讨平；藤原纯友在西方作乱，941年被橘远保镇压。朱雀体弱无嗣，946年让位于同母弟村上天皇，后在仁和寺出家，952年去世。

en: Taira no Kiyomori (1118–1181) succeeded his father Tadamori as head of the Taira in 1153. In 1156 he crushed the Hōgen Rebellion with Minamoto no Yoshitomo, then defeated Yoshitomo in the 1160 Heiji Disturbance, leaving the Taira supreme in Kyoto. In 1167 he became the first warrior appointed daijō-daijin, Japan's chief minister and de facto ruler. He married his daughter Tokuko to Emperor Takakura, seized power in a coup in 1179, and placed his grandson Antoku on the throne in 1180. The Genpei War began that year, and Kiyomori died in 1181.
zh: 平清盛（1118—1181）于1153年继承父亲忠盛成为平氏首领。1156年，他与源义朝一同平定保元之乱，1160年又在平治之乱中击败义朝，平氏从此独霸京都。1167年，他成为首位出任太政大臣的武士，是日本实际上的最高统治者。他将女儿德子嫁给高仓天皇，1179年发动政变夺取大权，1180年扶外孙安德天皇即位。源平合战于同年爆发，清盛于1181年病逝。

en: Taira no Korehira was a mid-Heian warrior, the fourth son of Taira no Sadamori, who built a power base in Ise Province and founded the Ise Taira line, from which Taira no Kiyomori later sprang. In 998 his battles with his kinsman Taira no Muneyori in Ise's shrine districts brought him before the court; he submitted an apology and was removed to Awaji. In 1006 his appointment as governor of Ise, forced through over Fujiwara no Michinaga's opposition, was revoked within two months. He later held posts in Kōzuke, Bizen and Hitachi, and he was still alive in 1031.
zh: 平维衡是平安时代中期的武将，平贞盛第四子，在伊势国建立势力根基，开创伊势平氏，后来的平清盛即出自这一脉。998年，他与同族平致赖在伊势神郡交战，被召至朝廷问罪，提交谢状后被迁往淡路国。1006年，他的伊势守任命在藤原道长反对下仍获通过，却仅两个月后即被解任。他后来历任上野介、备前守、常陆介，1031年时仍在世。

en: Taira no Koremasa was a mid-Heian warrior, a son of Taira no Sadamori, and is counted a remote ancestor of the later Hōjō clan. In 973 he moved from the Right to the Left Outer Palace Guards and was appointed assistant governor of Sagami Province. In 995 he was appointed governor of Hizen in Kyūshū in recognition of his service hunting down bandits in 994. He kept a residence at Nijō-Madenokōji in the Left Capital of Kyōto. Some genealogies instead name Taira no Shigemori as his natural father. His son was Taira no Koretoki.
zh: 平维将是平安时代中期的武将，平贞盛之子，被视为后来北条氏的远祖。973年，他由右卫门尉转任左卫门尉，并出任相模介；994年因搜捕盗贼有功，于995年被任命为九州肥前守。他的宅邸位于京都左京二条万里小路。也有系图认为他其实是平繁盛的亲生儿子。其子为平维时。

en: Taira no Koretoki was a mid-Heian warrior, the biological son of Taira no Koremasa who was adopted by his grandfather Taira no Sadamori. Serving in the capital as a police commissioner and Left Outer Palace Guards officer, he was chosen in 996 as the escort who conducted the disgraced Fujiwara no Korechika into exile at Dazaifu. He later served as assistant governor of Hitachi and then Kazusa Province, and retired in 1031 on the grounds of old age and illness. Through his son Taira no Naokata he was the great-great-grandfather of Hōjō Tokimasa.
zh: 平维时是平安时代中期的武将，平维将之子，被祖父平贞盛收为养子。他在京都任检非违使、左卫门尉时，于996年担任领送使，押送失势的藤原伊周流放大宰府。此后历任常陆介、上总介，1031年以年老多病为由致仕。通过其子平直方，他是北条时政的高祖父。

en: Taira no Kunika (872–935) was the eldest son of Taira no Takamochi and, through his son Sadamori, the ancestor of the Hitachi and Ise Taira lines. In 898 he went east with his father and established himself at Ishida in Makabe district, Hitachi Province, west of Mount Tsukuba. Marrying a daughter of the former provincial officer Minamoto no Mamoru, he succeeded to his father-in-law's position and extended the family's local power. In 935 his nephew Taira no Masakado, counterattacking a son of Minamoto no Mamoru, burned the Ishida hall and killed Kunika, the first bloodshed of the Tengyō War.
zh: 平国香（872—935）是平高望的长子，经其子平贞盛成为常陆平氏与伊势平氏之祖。898年他随父亲东下坂东，以常陆国真壁郡东石田（筑波山西麓）为据点。他娶前任常陆大掾源护之女，继承了岳父的地位，扩张坂东平氏的势力。935年，侄子平将门反击源护之子时烧毁石田馆，国香死于兵火，这是承平天庆之乱的开端。

en: Taira no Masahira was a mid-Heian warrior of the Ise Taira and the fifth son of Taira no Masanori, the clan's head. Based in Ise Province, in 1075 he backed a Tendai monk's forced seizure of the Tado Jingū-ji estates in Kuwana district, which the court later ruled invalid. In Kyoto he served Fujiwara no Morozane as a guards officer and police commissioner, and in 1079 he helped defend the capital against protesting Enryaku-ji warrior monks. Appointed governor of Dewa in 1099, he vanishes from the records afterward. His son Masamori laid the groundwork for the Taira rise.
zh: 平正衡是平安时代中期的伊势平氏武将，为平氏栋梁平正度的第五子。他以伊势国为据点活动，1075年勾结天台宗僧人强占桑名郡多度神宫寺的庄园，事后被朝廷裁定无效。在京都他侍奉藤原师实，任右卫门尉、检非违使；1079年延历寺僧兵强诉时，他参与防卫都城。1099年他出任出羽守，此后事迹不详。其子正盛为日后平家的兴盛奠定了基础。

en: Taira no Masamori was a late-Heian warrior and head of the Ise Taira, son of Taira no Masahira and grandfather of Taira no Kiyomori. He rose under Retired Emperor Shirakawa as a palace guard and provincial governor. In 1108 he crushed Minamoto no Yoshichika's rebellion in Izumo and received Tajima Province as his reward, though contemporaries doubted he had killed the famed rebel. He suppressed pirates in 1114 and the rebel magnate Taira no Naosumi in Hizen in 1119, spreading Taira power across the western and southern seas. Named governor of Sanuki in 1120, he died around 1121.
zh: 平正盛是平安时代后期的伊势平氏当主、北面武士，平正衡之子、平清盛之祖。他受白河法皇重用，历任诸国国守。1108年，他平定出云国的源义亲之乱，以功受任但马守，但时人怀疑他是否真的讨杀了以勇猛著称的义亲。1114年他追讨海贼，1119年又讨伐肥前国的叛将平直澄，将平氏势力扩展到西海、南海。1120年任赞岐守，约1121年去世。

en: Taira no Masanori was a mid-Heian warrior, the eldest or, by another account, second son of Taira no Korehira, under whom the Ise Taira consolidated their power. He expanded the family's holdings in Ise, acquiring the Kozukuri estate in Ichishi district, and rose through guards and provincial posts, including Hitachi no suke and the governorships of Dewa and Echizen, reaching the junior fourth rank, lower grade. His son Masahira's line led to Taira no Kiyomori, while another son, Suehira, founded the house that later served as stewards of the Muromachi shogunate. Masanori was dead by 1067.
zh: 平正度是平安时代中期的武将，伊势平氏始祖平维衡的长子（一说次子），在他这一代巩固了伊势平氏的势力。他扩张家族在伊势的领地，领有一志郡木造庄；历任左卫门尉、常陆介、出羽守、越前守等职，叙从四位下。其子正衡的后裔后来出了平清盛，另一子季衡的一支则称伊势氏，世代出任室町幕府政所执事。至迟1067年时他已经去世。

en: Taira no Masatsune was a mid-Heian warrior of the Kanmu Taira line and founder of the Chichibu clan of Musashi Province, born to Taira no Tadayori and Haruhime, a daughter of Taira no Masakado. In 1023 he led Sagami and Kazusa troops against the assistant governor of Musashi, who had defied an imperial order, and defeated him at Toshima, receiving lands in Suruga, Musashi, Kazusa and Shimōsa for his service. He took no part in his brother Taira no Tadatsune's Bōsō revolt of 1028, and so kept his lands. Based in Chichibu district, he is said to have fallen in the Earlier Nine Years' War aged fifty-one.
zh: 平将恒是平安时代中期的桓武平氏武将、武藏国秩父氏的始祖，父亲为平忠赖，母亲春姬是平将门之女。1023年，武藏介违抗敕命在武藏起兵，将恒率领相模、上总两国军队前往讨伐，在丰岛将其平定，因而得到骏河、武藏、上总、下总各国的领地。1028年，其兄平忠常在房总半岛发动大规模叛乱，他没有参与，因而保住了自己的势力。他在秩父郡称秩父氏，相传在“前九年之役”中战死，时年五十一岁。

en: Taira no Michimasa was the fourth son of Taira no Tadamasa. In the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 he fought for Retired Emperor Sutoku; defeated, he fled with his father to Ise and later surrendered to Taira no Kiyomori, who executed his father and brothers.
zh: 平通正是平忠正的第四子。1156年保元之乱中，他随父亲和兄长们站在崇德上皇一方参战；兵败后随父逃往伊势，后来向平清盛投降，其父与兄长们被清盛处死。

en: Taira no Motomune, also written as Taira no Motomune with a different character, was the father of Taira no Yorito, a warrior of Tama district in Musashi Province, and Noyo no Motonaga.
zh: 平元宗又写作平基宗，是武藏国多摩郡武将平赖任与野与基永的父亲。

en: Taira no Naokata was a mid-Heian warrior and head of the Kanmu Taira, a capital-based military aristocrat in the service of the regent's house. In 1028 the court named him and Nakahara no Narimichi commissioners to subdue Taira no Tadatsune's revolt; they failed, and he was dismissed in 1030. He held an estate at Kamakura in Sagami, and after marrying his daughter to Minamoto no Yoriyoshi he made over his Kamakura lands and hereditary retainers to the groom. She bore Yoriyoshi Minamoto no Yoshiie, Yoshitsuna and Yoshimitsu. The Hōjō and Kumagai clans claimed descent from him.
zh: 平直方是平安时代中期的武将、桓武平氏的当主，身为在京军事贵族，以家人身份侍奉摄关家。1028年，朝廷任命他与明法官人中原成通为追讨使，讨伐平忠常的叛乱，却未能成功，1030年被解任。他在相模国镰仓建有宅邸；把女儿嫁给源赖义后，他将镰仓的领地和桓武平氏嫡流相传的郎党都交给了女婿。其女为赖义生下源义家、源义纲、源义光。后来的北条氏与熊谷氏都自称是他的后裔。

en: Taira no Sadamori (died 989) was a warrior of the Kammu Taira line and the legitimate son of Taira no Kunika. In 935 his father was killed in the rising of their cousin Taira no Masakado. Sadamori fought Masakado for years, once fleeing to the capital after defeat in Shinano, and in 940 joined Fujiwara no Hidesato to kill Masakado at the battle of Kojima in Shimōsa. Rewarded with the junior fifth rank, he later became Chinjufu shōgun and governor of Mutsu, reaching the junior fourth rank and being called the Taira General. His son Korehira founded the Ise Taira branch.
zh: 平贞盛（？—989年）是桓武平氏的武将、平国香的嫡子。935年，父亲在堂兄弟平将门发动的叛乱中被杀。贞盛连年追讨将门，曾在信浓战败后逃入京都；940年，他与藤原秀乡合兵，在下总国小岛之战中攻杀将门。因功叙从五位，后历任镇守府将军、陆奥守，叙从四位下，人称“平将军”。他的儿子维衡开创了伊势平氏一支。

en: Taira no Shigemori (1138–1179) was the eldest son of Taira no Kiyomori. He fought beside his father in the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 and the Heiji Disturbance of 1159, rising to become inner minister and commander of the inner palace guards. Known as the Komatsu minister from his Rokuhara mansion, he was the Taira leader closest to Cloistered Emperor Go-Shirakawa and struggled to mediate between the emperor and his father. Torn between loyalty and filial duty, he died of illness in 1179, aged forty-two, two years before Kiyomori; his brother Munemori then inherited the clan's leadership.
zh: 平重盛（1138—1179）是平清盛的长子。他在1156年保元之乱和1159年平治之乱中随父征战，累升至内大臣和近卫军统领。他因居于六波罗小松第而被称为小松殿，是平氏一门中与后白河法皇最亲近的人，曾竭力调停法皇与父亲的对立。他夹在忠诚与孝道之间，于1179年病逝，年四十二岁，先清盛两年而亡；其弟宗盛随后接掌了平氏的主导权。

en: Taira no Shigemori was a mid-Heian warrior, the second son of Taira no Kunika and younger brother of Taira no Sadamori. He fought beside Sadamori to suppress Taira no Masakado's revolt of 939–940 and won fame, but received little reward and was left resentful. Appointed daijō, senior secretary of Hitachi Province, he became known as Daijō Shigemori and the founder of the Hitachi Taira and Daijō warrior houses. In 986 he dedicated six hundred scrolls of the Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra to Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei, an offering his rivals Taira no Tadayori and Tadamitsu obstructed in Musashi.
zh: 平繁盛是平安时代中期的武将，平国香的次子、平贞盛之弟。他随兄长贞盛参与平定939—940年的平将门之乱，以武勇闻名，却所得恩赏甚少，心怀不满。他受任常陆大掾，被称为“大掾繁盛”，是常陆平氏与大掾氏事实上的始祖。986年，他将六百卷《大般若经》奉献比叡山延历寺，途经武藏国时遭到仇敌平忠赖、平忠光阻挠。

en: Taira no Suehira was a mid-Heian warrior of the Ise Taira, a son of clan leader Taira no Masanori and elder brother of Taira no Masahira. In 1079 he helped defend Kyoto against protesting Enryaku-ji warrior monks. His descendants became the Ise clan.
zh: 平季衡是平安时代中期的伊势平氏武将，平氏栋梁平正度之子、平正衡之兄。1079年延历寺僧兵强诉时他参与防卫京都，其后代称伊势氏。

en: Taira no Sukemori (1161–1185) was the second son of Taira no Shigemori and a grandson of Kiyomori. In 1170 a quarrel with the retinue of Regent Matsudono Motofusa, known as the carriage incident, ended in an armed revenge attack on the regent's men and stalled his court career. A gifted poet whose verses appear in the Shinchokusen and Fūga anthologies, he became a favourite of Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa and later fought in the Genpei War. He was routed at Mikusa-yama in 1184, and after the Taira defeat at Dannoura in 1185 he drowned himself in the straits, aged twenty-five.
zh: 平资盛（1161—1185）是平重盛次子、平清盛之孙。1170年，他与摄政松殿基房的随从发生争执，随后引发武士袭击基房车队的报复，即“殿下乘合事件”，他的升迁也由此停滞。资盛擅长和歌，作品收入《新敕撰和歌集》与《风雅和歌集》，并深受后白河法皇宠爱。源平合战中，他于1184年在三草山遭击溃；1185年坛之浦平家败亡后，他投水自尽，年二十五岁。

en: Taira no Tadamasa (died 1156) was an Ise Taira warrior, a younger brother of Tadamori and uncle of Taira no Kiyomori. He first served Retired Emperor Shirakawa, and in 1119 was appointed guardian of the newborn Prince Akihito, the future Emperor Sutoku. Dismissed by Retired Emperor Toba in 1133, he became a retainer of the regent Fujiwara no Yorinaga. In the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 he fought for Retired Emperor Sutoku, holding the Shirakawa palace; defeated, he fled to Ise, surrendered to Kiyomori, and was executed at Rokuhara.
zh: 平忠正（？—1156）是平安时代末期的伊势平氏武将，平正盛之子、忠盛之弟，即平清盛的叔父。他早年仕于白河法皇，1119年被任命为新生皇子显仁亲王（后来的崇德天皇）的御监；1133年遭鸟羽上皇勘当后，成为摄关家藤原赖长的家人。1156年保元之乱中，他随赖长支持崇德上皇，据守白河北殿，兵败后逃往伊势，继而向侄儿清盛投降，终在六波罗被清盛处死。

en: Taira no Tadamichi was a mid-Heian warrior counted as the ancestor of the Miura and Kamakura clans of Sagami. His son Miura no Tamemichi is said to have been the first of the line to bear the name Miura.
zh: 平忠通（亦作平忠道）是平安时代中期的武将，被奉为相模国三浦氏、镰仓氏之祖。其子三浦为通据称是这一脉中首称“三浦”者。

en: Taira no Tadamitsu was a mid-Heian warrior and landowner of the eastern provinces, a son of Taira no Yoshifumi and younger brother of Taira no Tadayori. Adopted as heir by his eldest brother Tadasuke, who died young, he inherited Tadasuke's estates. After Taira no Masakado's revolt the brothers feuded bitterly with Taira no Shigemori; in 986 Tadamitsu helped block Shigemori's sutra dedication to Enryaku-ji, and the court once issued pursuit orders against them.
