His son Taira no Tadamichi was counted an ancestor of the Miura clan; tradition holds that Yoshifumi, Tadamitsu and Tadamichi are buried together at Niden-ji in Sagami.
zh: 平忠光是平安时代中期的武将、东国豪族，平良文之子、平忠赖之弟。他被早逝的长兄忠辅收为养子，继承了其领地。平将门之乱后，忠赖、忠光兄弟与平繁盛长期对立；986年，忠光参与阻挠繁盛向延历寺奉纳经书，朝廷一度对他们发出追讨官符。其子平忠通被视为三浦氏之祖；相传良文、忠光、忠通三代同葬于相模国的二传寺。

en: Taira no Tadamori (1096–1153) was head of the Taira clan and father of Taira no Kiyomori. Serving the retired emperors Shirakawa and Toba as a palace guardsman, he became the first samurai admitted to the imperial court. From 1129 he led campaigns against pirates along the San'yōdō and Nankaidō coasts and confronted the warrior monks of Nara and Mount Hiei. He governed provinces including Harima, Ise, Bizen and Tajima, grew rich from trade with Song China, and built Kyoto's Rengeō-in, home of the Sanjūsangen-dō hall. His power and wealth laid the foundations of Taira rule.
zh: 平忠盛（1096—1153）是平安时代后期的武将、伊势平氏首领，也是平清盛之父。他仕于白河、鸟羽两位上皇，以北面武士身份成为首位获准升殿的武士。1129年起，他追讨山阳道、南海道沿海的海贼，并与奈良和比叡山的僧兵对抗。他历任播磨、伊势、备前、但马等国国司，借对宋朝贸易积累巨资，又在京都建造莲华王院，即三十三间堂所在。他的武力与财力为日后的平氏政权奠定了基础。

en: Taira no Tadatsune (c. 975–1031) was a warrior chieftain of the Bōsō peninsula, son of Taira no Tadayori and maternal grandson of Taira no Masakado. Heir to great estates in the eastern provinces, he held the title Kazusa no suke but defied officials and withheld taxes. In 1028 he burned the Awa provincial headquarters and killed its governor, raising the revolt named after him. He resisted Taira no Naokata's punitive army for years, but in 1031, his forces spent, he took vows and surrendered to Minamoto no Yorinobu, then died at Nogami in Mino en route to the capital.
zh: 平忠常（约975—1031）是房总半岛的武将豪族，平忠赖之子、平将门的外孙。他继承东国大片领地，官任上总介，却抗拒国司、不纳租税。1028年，他袭烧安房国府，烧死安房守，发动了史称“平忠常之乱”的叛乱。他连年抵御平直方率领的追讨军；1031年军力疲敝，遂出家向源赖信投降，在押往京都途中病死于美浓国野上。

en: Taira no Tadayori (930–1019) was a mid-Heian warrior of the Kammu Taira, a son of Taira no Yoshifumi and cousin of Taira no Masakado. He styled himself Muraoka Jirō and held the post of assistant governor of Musashi Province. In 986 he and his younger brother Tadamitsu obstructed Taira no Shigemori's dedication of six hundred gold-lettered Great Perfection of Wisdom Sutra scrolls to Enryaku-ji, branding Shigemori, who had helped destroy Masakado, their enemy. He died early in 1019, in his ninetieth year. His son Taira no Tadatsune later led a major rising in the eastern provinces.
zh: 平忠赖（930—1019）是平安时代中期的桓武平氏武将，平良文之子、平将门的堂兄弟。他自称村冈次郎，官至武藏介。986年，他与弟弟平忠光阻挠平繁盛向比叡山延历寺奉献六百卷金泥《大般若经》，斥曾参与攻灭将门的繁盛为仇敌。他于1019年初去世，享年九十岁。其子平忠常后来在东国发动大规模叛乱。

en: Taira no Takamochi (839–911), born Prince Takamochi, was a great-grandson of Emperor Kanmu. In 889, by order of Emperor Uda, he received the surname Taira and left the imperial family, becoming vice-governor of Kazusa Province. Unlike many absentee officials, he took up his post with his sons Kunika, Yoshikane and Yoshimasa, built a residence in Kazusa in 898, and stayed in the east after his term. Marrying into local families and opening new rice lands, he built up the warrior bands on which the Kanmu Taira clans, including the Taira of the Genpei War, were founded.
zh: 平高望（839—911），原称高望王，是桓武天皇的曾孙。889年，他奉宇多天皇敕命获赐平朝臣姓、降为臣籍，并出任上总介。与许多遥任的国司不同，他带着国香、良兼、良将等儿子赴任，898年在上总国武射郡营造居所，任满之后也不返京，就此留居东国。他与当地豪族联姻、开垦荒地，培植起武士团，奠定了高望王流桓武平氏的根基，后世坂东平氏诸家均奉其为祖。

en: Taira no Taketsune, also called Chichibu no Taketsune, was the second son of Taira no Masatsune of the Chichibu Taira. Toshima clan tradition names him as the founder of the Toshima line. He followed Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and Minamoto no Yoshiie on their Ōshū campaigns and fell in either the Earlier Nine Years' War of 1051–1062 or the Later Three Years' War of 1083–1087. His son was Taira no Tsuneie.
zh: 平武常又称秩父武常，是秩父平氏平将恒的次男。按照丰岛氏的谱系传说，他是丰岛氏的始祖。后来他追随源赖义、源义家出兵奥州，在1051—1062年的“前九年之役”或1083—1087年的“后三年之役”中战死。其子为平常家。

en: Taira no Tanemune was a son of the Bandō warlord Taira no Tadatsune and a brother of Taira no Tsunemasa.
zh: 平胤宗是坂东豪族平忠常之子、平常将的兄弟。

en: Taira no Tokimori was a Taira warrior whom Buzen genealogies call a cousin of Taira no Kiyomori. His sixth son Yasumori, appointed governor of Buzen Province in 1157, built a stronghold at Nagano in Kiku District and founded the Buzen Nagano warrior clan.
zh: 据丰前地方文献记载，平时盛是平氏一门武将，被称为平清盛的从兄弟。他的第六子康盛于1157年出任丰前国司，在企救郡长野筑城定居，开创了丰前长野氏。

en: Taira no Tomomori (1152–1185) was a son of Taira no Kiyomori and one of the Taira clan's foremost generals in the Genpei War. He defeated the Minamoto at the Uji River in 1180 and again at the Yahagi River in 1181, and in 1183 he won the naval battle of Mizushima. After the Taira reverses at Kurikara and Ichinotani, where his eldest son was killed, he held Hikoshima in Nagato. At the decisive naval battle of Dannoura in 1185, he strapped an anchor to his body and leapt into the sea rather than be captured.
zh: 平知盛（1152—1185）是平清盛之子，源平合战中平家一方的主要将领。1180年他在宇治川击败源氏，1181年又在矢作川获胜，1183年于水岛海战取胜。俱利伽罗峠与一之谷接连失利后，其长子在一之谷阵亡，他则镇守长门国彦岛。1185年坛之浦海战平家覆灭，知盛背负船锚投海自尽。

en: Taira no Tomomune (1184–1255) was a son of Taira no Tomomori, born while the Taira fled the capital during the Genpei War. After the clan's destruction at Dannoura in 1185, he was sheltered in Kyūshū by Mutō Sukeyori, the Chinzei deputy, and his wet nurse's Koremune family, eventually becoming Sukeyori's adopted son. In 1200 he was appointed dazai daikan at Dazaifu. He also used the names Koremune Tomomune, Sō Tomomune and Mutō Tomomune, and died at Dazaifu's northern hall in 1255. The Sō lords of Tsushima claimed him as their ancestor.
zh: 平知宗（1184—1255）是平知盛之子，生于源平战争中平家逃离京都、辗转各地之时。1185年平家在坛之浦之战覆灭后，他在九州受到镇西奉行武藤资赖与乳母惟宗氏的庇护，后来成为武藤资赖的养子。1200年，他出任太宰大监。他也曾使用惟宗知宗、宗知宗、武藤知宗等名字，1255年卒于大宰府北殿。对马的宗氏自称是他的后裔。

en: Taira no Tsuneie, also called Toshima no Tsuneie, was a warrior of Musashi Province named in Minamoto no Yoritoshi's 1086 memorial for service in the campaign against the Ezo.
zh: 平常家又称丰岛常家，是武藏国的武将，源赖俊1086年请求恩赏的申文将他列为征讨虾夷的有功者。

en: Taira no Tsunekane (1045–1126) was a warrior of the mid-Heian period and the first head of the Chiba clan. A son of Taira no Tsunenaga, he is said to have taken the title Chiba Daisuke from the Chiba estate in Shimōsa Province, giving the clan its name. Chronicles credit him with distinguished service alongside his father in the Later Three Years' War of 1083–1087. His third son Tsuneshige, adopted by Tsunekane's younger brother Tsuneharu, vice-governor of Kazusa, inherited both the Chiba name and the headship of the Bōsō Taira, a succession that later split the clan.
zh: 平常兼（1045—1126）是日本平安时代中期的武将，千叶氏初代当主。他是平常长之子，相传因下总国千叶乡而号称“千叶大介”，千叶氏由此得名。据记载，他在1083—1087年的后三年之役中随父出征，立下战功。三男常重被常兼之弟、上总介常晴收为养子，同时继承千叶之名与房总平氏的惣领地位，这一安排日后成为一族内部抗争的根源。

en: Taira no Tsunemasa (1010–1076) was a mid-Heian warrior of the Bandō Taira and a son of Taira no Tadatsune. After his father rose against the court in 1028 and surrendered in 1031, Tsunemasa and his younger brother Tsunechika escorted him toward the capital; Tadatsune died of illness in Mino Province and the brothers were pardoned. Back in Shimōsa, Tsunemasa styled himself Chiba no suke, and Chiba genealogies such as the Chiba Taikeizu count him as the first head of the Chiba clan. He was the father of Taira no Tsunenaga.
zh: 平常将（1010—1076）是平安时代中期至后期的坂东平氏武士，平忠常之子。1028年父亲举兵反抗朝廷，史称“平忠常之乱”，1031年投降；常将与弟弟常近奉命押送父亲前往平安京，忠常途经美浓国时病逝，常将兄弟获赦。他回到下总国后自称千叶介，因此《千叶大系图》等家谱多将他奉为千叶氏第一代当主。其子为平常长。

en: Taira no Tsunemune was a member of the Taira family, a son of Taira no Tsunetō and the father of Nakamura no Munehira.
zh: 平常宗是平氏一员，为平常远之子、中村宗平之父。

en: Taira no Tsunenaga (1024–1108) was a Heian warrior and the son of Taira no Tsunemasa. He fought for Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and Minamoto no Yoshiie in the Earlier Nine Years' War and the Later Three Years' War. After the campaigns he built a residence at Ōi in Kazusa Province and then advanced into the Chiba district of Shimōsa, taking the title Chiba daibu. He died in 1108. Of his many sons, the second, Tsunekane, founded the Chiba clan while the fifth, Tsuneharu, founded the Kazusa clan.
zh: 平常长（1024—1108）是平安时代武士，平常将之子。他在“前九年之役”和“后三年之役”中追随源赖义、源义家父子作战，立下战功。战后他在上总国大椎兴建宅邸，随后进占下总国千叶乡，号千叶大夫，于1108年去世。他的众多儿子繁衍出房总平氏诸家，其中次男常兼成为千叶氏之祖，五男常晴成为上总氏之祖。

en: Taira no Tsunetō was a member of the Taira family, recorded in the Chiba genealogy as a son of Raison and the father of Taira no Tsunemune.
zh: 平常远是平氏一员，千叶氏系图载他为赖尊之子，他的儿子是平常宗。

en: Taira no Yoriie, also called Murayama no Yoriie, was an eastern warrior of Musashi Province and a son of Taira no Yoritō, founder of the Murayama warrior party. His son Kaneko no Ienori settled at Kaneko in Iruma District and founded the Kaneko clan.
zh: 据《武藏七党系图》记载，平赖家又称村山赖家，是武藏国的东国武士、村山党始祖平赖任之子。其子金子家范居于入间郡金子乡并以金子为姓，开创了金子氏。

en: Taira no Yoritaka, son of Taira no Tadayori of the Kanmu Taira line, is named in genealogies as the ancestor of the Nakamura clan of Sagami Province. He took Buddhist vows as Master Yamabe, and his son Tsunetō was policing commissioner of Musashi.
zh: 平赖尊是桓武平氏良文流平忠赖之子，家谱以他为相模国中村氏的始祖。他出家后号山边禅师，子常远曾任武藏国押领使。

en: Taira no Yorito, also known as Murayama no Yorito, was a late-Heian warrior of Tama district in Musashi Province, a son of Taira no Motomune and the father of Murayama no Yoriie.
zh: 平赖任又称村山赖任，是平安时代后期武藏国多摩郡的武将，为平元宗之子、村山赖家之父。

en: Taira no Yoshifumi (886–953) was the fifth son of Taira no Takamochi, born in Kyoto. Unlike his elder brothers he did not go east with his father in 898, but in 923 Emperor Daigo ordered him to suppress bandits in Sagami, and he settled in the Kantō. In 939 he was appointed general of the chinjufu, northern defence headquarters, and the following year he carried to the capital the first report of Taira no Masakado's defeat and death. Known as Muraoka Gorō after his stronghold, he is called the ancestor of the eight Taira clans of Bandō.
zh: 平良文（886—953）是平高望的第五子，生于京都。与兄长们不同，898年父亲东下时他并未随行；923年醍醐天皇下诏命他讨伐相模国盗贼，他由此前往东国并定居下来。939年他被任命为镇守府将军；次年，他向都城送去平将门败死的第一份奏报。他以据点村冈自称“村冈五郎”，被视为坂东八平氏的祖先。

en: Takakura (1161–1181), a son of retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa, was placed on the throne in 1168 when Emperor Rokujō was deposed. Real power rested with his father through cloistered rule and, after 1172, with his father-in-law Taira no Kiyomori, whose daughter Tokuko became his empress. Their son Tokuhito was born in 1178 and named heir within weeks. Pressed by the Taira, Takakura abdicated in March 1180 in favour of the year-old Tokuhito, the future Emperor Antoku. He joined the court's brief move to Kiyomori's new capital at Fukuhara that summer and died in Kyoto in January 1181, aged nineteen.
zh: 高仓天皇（1161—1181）是后白河上皇之子，1168年六条天皇被废后，他被扶上皇位。实权先由父亲以院政掌握，1172年他娶平清盛之女德子为皇后，岳父清盛也把持朝政。1178年德子生下言仁亲王，婴儿出生仅数周即被立为太子。在平家压力下，高仓于1180年3月让位给年仅一岁的言仁，即后来的安德天皇。同年夏他随朝廷短暂迁往清盛营建的新都福原京，1181年1月在京都去世，年仅十九岁。

en: Sasaki Takanobu, also called Takashima Takanobu, was an early Kamakura-period warrior of Ōmi Province and the second son of Sasaki Nobutsuna, head of the Sasaki clan and shugo of Ōmi. As jitō of Tanaka village in Takashima district he founded the Takashima clan. In 1235 a dispute with the Hiyoshi Shrine escalated when his deputy killed one of its monk-attendants; Enryakuji monks marched on Kyoto with portable shrines, and the court, backed by the Kamakura shogunate, sentenced Takanobu to exile in Bungo Province. Houses descended from him and the unrelated Yamazaki clan became known together as the Seven Heads of Takashima.
zh: 佐佐木高信，又称高岛高信，是镰仓时代前期近江国武士，近江守护、佐佐木氏惣领佐佐木信纲的次子。他担任高岛郡田中乡的地头，成为高岛氏之祖。1235年，他与日吉社发生争端，其地头代杀死社中僧人成万法师，延历寺僧众抬神舆进入京都强诉；朝廷在镰仓幕府追认下将高信流放丰后国。他的后裔形成的诸家与另系的山崎氏合称高岛七头。

en: Takashima Yasunobu was the eldest son of Takashima Takanobu and succeeded him as head of the Takashima clan of western Ōmi. He served the Kamakura shogunate as a distinguished gokenin, and his heir was appointed governor of Etchū Province.
zh: 高岛泰信是高岛高信的长子，后继任西近江高岛氏本家当主，作为名门御家人侍奉镰仓幕府，其嫡子经幕府推举出任越中守。

en: Takashina no Koreaki was a son of Takashina no Narisuke, governor of Chikuzen. Later genealogies say he raised Kō no Koreyori from infancy—the boy the Sonpi Bunmyaku calls a son of Minamoto no Yoshiie—and the Kō clan regarded Koreaki as its house founder.
zh: 高阶惟章是筑前守高阶成佐之子。后世系图称，他自幼抚养高惟赖——《尊卑分脉》把惟赖记作源义家之子——而高氏将惟章奉为家祖。

en: Takashina no Mineo was an early Heian aristocrat, the son of Prince Iwami and great-grandson of the minister Prince Nagaya. In 844 he received the Takashina surname and left imperial status, then served as governor of Iyo, Higo and provisional governor of Ise. In 868 he reached junior fourth rank, upper, and became head of the Department of Divinities. His line endured: later genealogies trace the Kō clan, hereditary stewards of the Ashikaga, back to him. Tradition also says he took in a boy born to Ariwara no Narihira and the Ise priestess Princess Yasuko, making him the adopted son of his own son Shigenori; the boy was called Moronao.
zh: 高阶峰绪是日本平安时代前期贵族，石见王之子、左大臣长屋王的玄孙。844年，他获赐高阶真人之姓、脱离皇族，此后历任伊予守、肥后守、伊势权守。868年升从四位上，出任神祇伯。他的一支延续后世，系图将世代担任足利氏执事的高氏追认为其后人。相传他还收留了在原业平与伊势斋宫恬子内亲王私通所生的男孩，将其过继给儿子茂范，男孩名叫师尚。

en: Takashina no Moronao was a noble of the early Heian period and a son of Takashina no Shigenori, governor of Shimotsuke Province. He rose to Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade, and served as Middle Captain of the Right. A famous tradition, grounded in interpretations of The Tales of Ise, holds that he was really born of the affair between Ariwara no Narihira and the Ise Saiō, Princess Yasuko, and was then raised as Shigenori's adopted son; later genealogies repeat the claim, though it remains only a tradition. His recorded son Takashina no Yoshiomi was born in 898.
zh: 高阶师尚是平安时代前期贵族，下野守高阶茂范之子，官位为从四位上、右近卫中将。自古流传一种说法：依据对《伊势物语》的解读，他实为在原业平与伊势斋宫恬子内亲王私通所生，为遮掩此事而被高阶峰绪收养，记为茂范的养子，后世各类系图也如此书写，但此说终究没有超出传说的范围。系图所载的儿子高阶良臣生于898年。

en: Takashina no Narisuke was an eleventh-century aristocrat titled governor of Chikuzen and a son of the courtier Takashina no Naritō. Later genealogies name him the ancestor of the warrior Kō clan; his son Koreaki raised Kō no Koreyori.
zh: 高阶成佐是11世纪的贵族，官居筑前守，为廷臣高阶业远之子。后世系图将他奉为武家高氏的祖先；其子惟章收养了高惟赖。

en: Takashina no Naritō (965–1010) was a mid-Heian noble, son of Takashina no Toshitada. He served as governor of Etchū Province and served Crown Prince Okisada, later Emperor Sanjō, rising to Provisional Director of the Crown Prince's Quarters with Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade. In 1004 his work on the Rajōmon relocation earned him Tanba again, and in 1005 he was charged with building the Buraku-in hall. Reappointed in 1007, he resigned ill in 1010 and died on the tenth of the fourth month, aged forty-six. As a steward of Regent Fujiwara no Michinaga he was called without equal.
zh: 高阶业远（965—1010）是平安时代中期贵族，高阶敏忠之子。他曾任越中守，并在春宫居贞亲王（后来的三条天皇）的春宫坊历任少进、大进、亮，最终官位为从四位上、春宫权亮。1004年，他因罗城门移建之功被重任为丹波守；1005年又受宣旨负责丰乐院的营造。1007年再任丹波守，1010年三月因病辞官，四月初十日去世，享年四十六岁。作为左大臣藤原道长的家司，他被评为当世无双。

en: Takashina no Shigenori was a noble of the early Heian period and a son of the Jingi-haku Takashina no Mineo. In 883, holding the post of Shikibu-shōjō, he was appointed together with Ōkura no Yoshiyuki as reception envoy for the embassy from Balhae, and oversaw its reception in the capital. He later served as governor of Shimotsuke Province. Genealogies name him as the father of Takashina no Moronao, whom a famous tradition linked with the poet Ariwara no Narihira.
zh: 高阶茂范是平安时代前期贵族，神祇伯高阶峰绪之子。883年，他以式部少丞身份与大藏善行一同被任命为存问兼领渤海客使，负责在京城接待渤海国使节团，后来出任下野守。各类系图都把他记作高阶师尚之父，而自古流传的说法将师尚与歌人在原业平联系在一起。

en: Takashina no Toshitada was a mid-Heian noble, the son of the Imperial Household Minister Takashina no Yoshiomi and a grandson of Takashina no Moronao. In the first month of 988 he was appointed governor of Hizen Province. After serving in the Right Gate Guards, he was named governor of Settsu in 989 while holding the post of Provisional Assistant Captain of the Left Gate Guards, and his rank reached Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade. He died suddenly on the twentieth day of the sixth month, 990.
zh: 高阶敏忠是平安时代中期贵族，宫内卿高阶良臣之子、高阶师尚之孙，最终位阶为从五位上，官职为左卫门权佐。988年正月除目，他被任命为肥前国司，其后曾任右卫门权佐，989年在左卫门权佐任上受命兼任摄津守。990年六月二十日，他突然去世。

en: Takashina no Yoshiomi (898–980) was a mid-Heian noble, the son of Takashina no Moronao. In 939 the court sent him, then a Lesser Lieutenant of the Left Gate Guards, to verify Minamoto no Tsunemoto's report of Taira no Masakado's revolt in the east; he and his two colleagues refused to go and were dismissed together in 940. Pardoned in 941, he later held civil and guard posts and rose to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade, as Minister of the Imperial Household. Deeply devout, he took vows in summer 980 and died on the fifth of the seventh month.
zh: 高阶良臣（898—980）是平安时代中期贵族，高阶师尚之子。939年，朝廷派遣时任左卫门少尉的良臣等人，去核查源经基告发平将门在东国谋反的密报；他与两名同僚借故不肯东行，于940年一同被解官。941年获赦后，他历任文官与近卫职务，最终官至从四位下宫内卿。他深笃佛法，980年夏出家，同年七月初五日去世。

en: Taira no Koremoto was a mid-Heian warrior and founder of the Hitachi Taira. A nephew adopted by Taira no Sadamori, he was posted to Hitachi after Sadamori's victory in the Jōhei-Tengyō War of 935 to 940. Settling at Take in Tsukuba District, he styled himself Take-gon-no-daibu and built the clan's power. The Konjaku Monogatari records his feud with Taira no Tadatsune before 1016, and during Tadatsune's revolt he led three thousand cavalry under Minamoto no Yorinobu. In Kyoto he served the courtier Fujiwara no Sanesuke.
zh: 平维干是平安时代中期的武将，常陆平氏之祖。他是平繁盛之子，被伯父平贞盛收为养子；935—940年承平天庆之乱后，贞盛在常陆得到大批庄园，便派维干前往赴任。他定居常陆国筑波郡多气，自称多气权大夫，以此为据点扩张势力。《今昔物语集》记载，1016年以前他便与平忠常争利结怨；忠常之乱时，他率三千骑兵跟随源赖信作战。在京都，他还与平维敏等人一同臣事藤原实资。

en: Taira no Shigemoto, also called Take no Shigemoto, was a powerful lord of the Hitachi Taira in the late Heian period. From Take Castle in Tsukuba District, inherited from his grandfather Koremoto and father Tamemoto, he led the clan under the title Take-gon-no-daibu. In 1106 he joined Minamoto no Yoshimitsu in repelling Yoshimitsu's nephew Yoshikuni, who had invaded Hitachi; the Kyoto court then ordered his arrest, but his local power held. His sons divided his lands, founding the Yoshida, Makabe and other Hitachi warrior houses.
zh: 平重干，一称多气重干，是平安时代后期常陆平氏的有力领主。他继承祖父维干与父亲为干在常陆国筑波郡多气的基业，以多气城为据点，自称多气权大夫。1106年，源义国攻入常陆，重干与源义光等人率族人合力迎击，击退义光之侄义国的军队；朝廷随后下令拘拿义光、平重干等人，他却保住了在常陆的地盘。他的儿子们分割所领，各自以地名为苗字，派生出吉田、真壁等常陆武士家族。

en: Taira no Tamemoto, eldest son of Taira no Koremoto, succeeded him as head of the Hitachi Taira at Take; genealogies call him Daijō of Hitachi. His brother Tamekata founded the Isa house, and his son was Shigemoto.
zh: 平为干是平维干的长子，继承了其父在常陆国筑波郡多气的常陆平氏惣领地位，系图中标作常陆大掾。其弟为贤另立伊佐氏，他的儿子即平重干。

en: Prince Takechi (c. 654–696) was the eldest son of Emperor Tenmu. In the Jinshin War of 672 he escaped the Ōmi court, joined his father in Iga and commanded at Fuwa in Mino, where blocking the highway helped win Tenmu the throne. In 679 he joined his brothers in the Yoshino oath. Under Empress Jitō he became Daijō-daijin, head of the Council of State and the highest subject in the land. He died suddenly in 696, amid rumours of assassination. His son by Princess Minabe was Prince Nagaya, and three of his love poems survive in the Man'yōshū.
zh: 高市皇子（约654—696）是天武天皇的长子。672年壬申之乱中，他逃出近江大津京，在伊贺与举兵的父亲会合，并受命在美浓国不破总领军事、封锁要道，为天武天皇取胜立下大功。679年他与诸兄弟在吉野盟誓互助。持统天皇即位后，他出任太政大臣，居于天皇、皇太子之下的百官之首。696年他突然去世，有遇刺之说。他与御名部皇女所生之子是长屋王；《万叶集》中存有他的三首恋歌。

en: Takeda Masatsuna was a mid-Kamakura-period warrior of the Takeda clan and a miuchibito, a direct vassal of the Hojo tokuso family. The Azuma Kagami records him as an archer at shogunate ceremonies: he shot at the annual yumi-hajime in 1251 and prepared the target for Hojo Tokimune's kasagake in 1261. In 1263 he was one of seven favored vassals allowed to attend Hojo Tokiyori on his deathbed. While his elder brother Nobutoki moved to Aki as shugo, Masatsuna kept the family base at Isawa in Kai and became ancestor of the Isawa Takeda line.
zh: 武田政纲是镰仓时代中期的武田氏武将、北条得宗家的御内人。《吾妻镜》记载他常在幕府仪式中担任射手：1251年正月在弓始仪式上射箭，1261年为北条时宗的笠悬准备靶子；1263年北条时赖临终时，他是获准在侧侍奉的七名得宗被官之一。其兄武田信时出任安艺守护后移居安艺，政纲则留在甲斐，以石和为本据，开创了石和流武田氏。

en: Takeda Masayoshi (c. 1300–1343), commonly called Saburō, headed the Ishikawa branch of the Kai Genji Takeda and is the only attested governor of Kai in the late Kamakura period. In 1331 he led Kai troops for the shogunate against Emperor Go-Daigo, fighting at the fall of Mount Kasagi and at Akasaka Castle. After the Kamakura shogunate fell he joined the Kenmu government, then followed Ashikaga Takauji, invading Suwa District of Shinano in 1336. He later went over to the Southern Court and was killed in 1343 when a shogunal governor-deputy attacked him.
zh: 武田政义（约1300—1343），通称三郎，是甲斐源氏石和流武田氏的当主，镰仓末期唯一可确认的甲斐守护。1331年后醍醐天皇在笠置山举兵时，他率甲斐军为镰仓幕府出征，参与攻陷笠置山和攻打赤坂城。镰仓幕府灭亡后，他加入建武新政，随后又追随足利尊氏，于1336年攻入信浓国诹访郡；后来他转投南朝，1343年在幕府方守护代的进攻下战死。

en: Takeda Naonobu is named in medieval genealogies such as the Sonpi Bunmyaku as a son of Takeda Nobutake who held the court post of danjō shōhitsu; some genealogies identify him with Takeda Nobuaki, founder of the Ōi clan of Kai.
zh: 《尊卑分脉》等中世系图载武田直信为武田信武之子，曾任弹正少弼；也有系图认为他即入居甲斐大井庄、创立大井氏的大井信明。

en: Takeda Nobuie, later Munenobu, was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Isawa Takeda in Kai, son of Masatsuna. Given a character from Hojo Tokimune's name, he held the title Izu no kami and was possibly Kai shugo; his son was Sadanobu, father of Masayoshi.
zh: 武田信家，后改名宗信，是镰仓时代甲斐国石和流武田氏的武将，武田政纲之子。他获赐北条时宗名字中的偏讳而改名宗信，官至伊豆守，一说曾任甲斐守护；他是武田贞信之父、武田政义的祖父。

en: Takeda Nobumasa (1196–1265) was the third Takeda clan head, heir of Nobumitsu by a daughter of Nitta Yoshishige. At his coming of age in 1204, Regent Hojo Tokimasa capped him and gave him the character masa. As a young man he was exiled to Aki on a false charge but later pardoned. He fought beside his father for the Kamakura shogunate in the Jokyu War of 1221 and succeeded as clan head when Nobumitsu became a monk, holding the titles of Izu, Aki and Wakasa kami. He died in 1265 and was succeeded by his son Nobutoki.
zh: 武田信政（1196—1265）是武田氏第三代家督、武田信光的嫡子，母亲为新田义重之女，通称小五郎。1204年元服时，由执权北条时政担任乌帽子亲，并获赐其名字中的“政”字。他年轻时遭人谗害，被流放安艺国，后来获赦归国。1221年承久之乱时，他与父亲一同为镰仓幕府作战，信光出家后他继任家督，官至伊豆守、安艺守、若狭守。1265年他去世，由嫡子武田信时继任家督。

en: Takeda Nobumitsu (1162–1248), fifth son of Nobuyoshi, was the second Takeda clan head and a master of bow and horse, one of the Four Heavenly Kings of archery. In 1180 he joined his father's rising and captured the Taira-appointed Suruga deputy Tachibana no Toshige at the Battle of Hatta, and he fought at Ichinotani in 1184. In the Jokyu War of 1221 he commanded the shogunate's Tosando army, entered Kyoto, and executed the courtier Fujiwara no Mitsuchika. Made shugo of Aki, he became a monk in 1239, passed the clan to Nobumasa, and died in 1248 aged about 87.
zh: 武田信光（1162—1248）是武田信义第五子、武田氏第二代家督，精于弓马，与小笠原长清等人并称弓马四天王。1180年他随父起兵，在钵田之战擒获平家任命的骏河目代橘远茂，1184年又在一之谷之战立功。1221年承久之乱中，他受镰仓幕府之命担任东山道军大将，率军攻入京都，处死朝廷公卿藤原光亲，战后受封安艺国守护。1239年他出家，将家督让给儿子信政，1248年去世，享年约87岁。

en: Takeda Nobumune (1269–1330) was the sixth head of the Takeda clan, son of Tokitsuna. At his coming of age at Kamakura in 1277, Regent Hojo Tokimune capped him and gave him the character mune, and he served the shogunate as a trusted gokenin. He recovered the office of shugo of Aki Province for the main Takeda line and is credited with founding Kanayama Castle there. He became a monk in 1320 under the name Koa and died in 1330. A genealogical record also numbers him among the waka poets included in an imperial anthology.
zh: 武田信宗（1269—1330）是武田氏第六代家督、武田时纲之子。1277年他在镰仓元服，由执权北条时宗担任乌帽子亲，获赐“宗”字，作为深受北条氏信任的御家人为镰仓幕府效力。他为武田宗家重新取得安艺守护之职，相传还修筑了安艺银山城。1320年他出家，法号光阿（一称向阿），1330年去世。《甲斐信浓源氏纲要》称他的和歌被收入敕撰集，也是一位歌人。

en: Takeda Nobunari (d. 1394) was the eighth head of the Takeda and the eldest son of Takeda Nobutake. From 1339 he acted as shugo-dai in Kai ahead of his father, donating Ichijōgō in Koma District to Ichiren-ji. During the Kannō Disturbance he mustered Kai warriors for the battles of Hakone and Takeshita in 1351 and for the Musashino campaign of 1352. After Nobutake died in 1359 he took the family headship and the Kai governorship, while his brother Ujinobu held Aki. In 1370 he rebuilt Daizōkyō-ji, and in 1380 he endowed the Kōgaku-an of Bottaï Tokushō.
zh: 武田信成（？—1394）是武田信武的嫡男，武田氏第八代当主。1339年他先于父亲以守护代身份进入甲斐，将巨摩郡一条乡寄进给一莲寺。观应之乱中，他为足利方动员甲斐武士，参加1351年的箱根、竹下之战和1352年的武藏野合战。1359年信武死后，他继承家督与甲斐守护职，安艺守护由弟弟氏信继任。1370年他改建大藏经寺，1380年向拔队得胜的向岳庵寄进寺领。

en: Takeda Nobutake (1292–1362) was the seventh head of the Kai Genji Takeda and governor of Aki Province. He campaigned for the Kamakura shogunate during the Genkō War of 1332, then answered Ashikaga Takauji's summons against the Kenmu government, storming Kumagai Renkaku's Yano Castle in 1335 and fighting loyalist forces in the Kinai. During the Kannō Disturbance he was governor of Kai and entered the province; he also helped Takauji build Tenryū-ji. His waka appear in the Shinsenzai Wakashū. His sons Nobunari and Ujinobu founded the Kai and Aki Takeda lines.
zh: 武田信武（1292—1362）是甲斐源氏武田氏第七代当主、安艺国守护。1332年元弘之乱时他作为镰仓幕府一方出征，其后响应足利尊氏举兵，与建武政权为敌，1335年攻落熊谷莲觉的据点矢野城，又在畿内与朝廷一方作战。观应之乱中他担任甲斐守护并进入甲斐，还协助尊氏营造天龙寺。他擅长和歌，作品收入《新千载和歌集》，其子信成、氏信分别开创甲斐武田氏与安艺武田氏。

en: Takeda Nobutoki (1220–1289) was the fourth Takeda clan head, heir of Nobumasa and ancestor of the line that later held the Kai shugo office. At his coming of age in 1229, Regent Hojo Yasutoki capped him and gave him the character toki. The Azuma Kagami names him among the mounted guards of Shogun Kujo Yoritsune between 1237 and 1240. In 1269 he was sent west with Kamakura vassals against the Mongol threat, probably serving as shugo of Aki. He became a monk in 1279 as Kokai, died in 1289, and was succeeded by his son Tokitsuna.
zh: 武田信时（1220—1289）是武田氏第四代家督、武田信政的嫡子，也是后来世代担任甲斐守护的信时流武田氏之祖，通称五郎次郎。1229年元服时，由执权北条泰时担任乌帽子亲，获赐“时”字。《吾妻镜》记载，1237至1240年间他多次作为随兵护卫将军九条赖经。1269年，为防备蒙古袭来，他奉命率御家人前往西国，一般认为他当时在任安艺守护。1279年他出家，法号光海，1289年去世，由其子武田时纲继任。

en: Takeda Nobuyoshi (1128–1186) was a Kai Genji warrior in Kai Province, the second son of Minamoto no Kiyomitsu and first head of the Takeda clan. He came of age at Takeda Hachiman shrine in 1140 and took the Takeda name. In 1180 he answered Prince Mochihito's call against the Taira, led Kai Genji troops into Suruga, and joined Minamoto no Yoritomo to win the Battle of Fujikawa. His forces later fought at Ichinotani and Dannoura. After Yoritomo had his son Ichijo Tadayori killed in 1184 and forced him to swear submission, Nobuyoshi died in 1186.
zh: 武田信义（1128—1186）是甲斐国的甲斐源氏武将、源清光的次子，也是武田氏初代家督。1140年，他在武田八幡宫元服，取武田为姓。1180年，他响应以仁王讨伐平家的令旨起兵，率甲斐源氏攻入骏河，与源赖朝会合，在富士川之战击败平家军，此后又随军参加一之谷、坛之浦等战役。1184年，其子一条忠赖在镰仓遇害，信义被迫向源赖朝递交誓书臣服，最终于1186年去世。

en: Takeda Sadanobu was a warrior of the Ishikawa branch of the Kai Genji Takeda. The Takeda genealogy in the medieval Sonpi Bunmyaku records him as the father of Takeda Masayoshi, the governor of Kai who was killed fighting in 1343.
zh: 武田贞信是甲斐源氏石和流武田氏的武将，中世谱系书《尊卑分脉》所收武田氏系图载其为1343年战死的甲斐守护武田政义之父。

en: Takeda Tokitsuna (1245–1307) was the fifth Takeda clan head, son of Nobutoki. At his coming of age in 1253 Regent Hojo Tokiyori capped him and gave him the character toki. Around 1275 he apparently followed his father to Aki and guarded Nagato, succeeding as clan head in 1289. His headship was largely nominal: his uncle Masatsuna's Isawa branch, allied with the Hojo, held real power in Kai and a Hojo kinsman held the Aki shugo post. He became a monk in 1300 as Kojun and died in 1307. His son Nobumune later recovered the Aki shugo office.
zh: 武田时纲（1245—1307）是武田氏第五代家督、武田信时之子。1253年元服时，由执权北条时赖担任乌帽子亲，获赐“时”字。1275年前后，他似乎随父亲前往安艺，在长门担任警固，1289年父亲去世后继承家督。他的家督之位近乎虚名：叔父政纲的石和流与北条氏结盟，掌握着甲斐的实权，安艺守护一职也由北条族人担任。1300年他出家，法号光润，1307年去世。其子武田信宗后来重新夺回了安艺守护之职。

en: Takeda Ujinobu (1312–1380) was a son of Takeda Nobutake and founder of the Aki Takeda line. In 1322 he came of age with Ashikaga Sadauji as his crowning patron. During the Kannō Disturbance his father sent him into Aki, where with the Kikkawa he routed Ashikaga Tadafuyu's followers at Saijō and Yoshida. Succeeding as governor of Aki around 1359, he was removed by the shogunate in 1368 for failing to check the Ōuchi, made partial governor of Satō district in 1378, and retired the next year. His son Nobuari succeeded him.
zh: 武田氏信（1312—1380）是武田信武之子，安艺武田氏的初代当主。1322年元服时由足利贞氏担任乌帽子亲。观应之乱时，他被父亲派往安艺，与吉川氏等人在西条、吉田之战击败足利直冬一派。1359年前后他继任安艺守护，但因未能牵制大内氏，1368年被幕府解除守护职，1378年改任佐东郡分郡守护，翌年隐居，由子武田信在继嗣。

en: Takō Kagemune was the fourth head of the Takō clan, a cadet line of the Shimotsuke Utsunomiya clan based at Takō Castle in Kawachi district. He succeeded his father Tomotsune and was later followed by Munehide.
zh: 多功景宗是下野国河内郡多功氏的第四代当主，该氏是以多功城为居城的下野宇都宫氏庶流。他继承父亲朝经，之后由宗秀继任。

en: Takō Munetomo was a mid-Kamakura-period gokenin and the seventh son of Utsunomiya Yoritsuna of Shimotsuke. In 1238 he accompanied the shogun Fujiwara no Yoritsune on his progress to Kyoto and Rokuhara, and he appears frequently in the Azuma Kagami; in 1240 he was briefly suspended from guard service along with his kinsman Shionoya Yasutomo. In 1248 he built Takō Castle and founded the Takō clan. He held the post of governor of Iwami Province by 1258 and had left it by 1261, founded the Sainenji temple, and died in 1292 aged seventy-three.
zh: 多功宗朝是镰仓时代中期御家人，下野国宇都宫赖纲第七子。1238年将军藤原赖经上洛进入六波罗，宗朝随侍左右，其名亦屡见于《吾妻镜》；1240年他与同族盐谷泰朝同被幕府停职，处分不久即解除。1248年他修筑多功城，创立多功氏。1258年时他已担任石见守，约1261年前卸任，又创建西念寺，1292年去世，享年73岁。

en: Takō Tomotsugu was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Takō clan of Shimotsuke Province, a cadet branch of the Utsunomiya. Clan genealogies name him as the son and successor of Takō Munetomo, founder of the clan and builder of Takō Castle in 1248.
zh: 多功朝继是镰仓时代武士，出身下野国宇都宫氏的庶流多功氏。多功氏谱系记载，他是1248年筑多功城、开创多功氏的多功宗朝之子，并继其父领有多功城。

en: Takō Tomotsune was the third head of the Takō clan of Kawachi district in Shimotsuke Province, a cadet branch of the Utsunomiya clan established at Takō Castle in 1248. He succeeded his father Tomotsugu and was followed in turn by his son Kagemune.
zh: 多功朝经是下野国河内郡多功氏的第三代当主；多功氏是下野宇都宫氏的庶流，1248年入部河内郡、筑多功城为居城。他继承父亲朝继，之后由其子景宗继任。

en: Taku no Munenao was an early Kamakura-period warrior and head of the Taku house of Hizen Province in northern Kyushu, a family that traced its descent from the Tsukui. The Taku had long been based at their mansion in Minami-Taku when, around 1193, Munenao built Kajimine Castle on the mountain above Taku, together with outer forts and a new residence. Also known as Taku Castle, it served as the seat of the Taku lords for more than 350 years.
zh: 多久宗直是镰仓时代初期的武将，任肥前国（九州北部）多久氏当主，该家族自称出自津久井氏。多久家早年以位于南多久的居馆为据点，约1193年，宗直在多久地方的梶峰山上修筑梶峰城，并配置城砦与居馆。梶峰城又名多久城，此后350余年间一直是多久氏的居城。

en: Tatara no Sadanari was a head of the Tatara clan, the local-official family of Suo Province. The Ōuchi genealogy makes him father of Morifusa, the first head to take the name Ōuchi, and of Morinaga, ancestor of the Migita house.
zh: 多多良贞成是周防国在厅官人多多良氏的当家。据大内系图，他是盛房之父，盛房是最早以大内为苗字的当主；另一子盛长则分出右田氏。

en: Emperor Tenji (626–672), formerly Naka no Ōe, son of Jomei and Kōgyoku, was Japan's 38th sovereign. In 645 he and Nakatomi no Kamatari killed Soga no Iruka in the Isshi incident, and as crown prince he drove the Taika reforms. His Paekche relief armies were crushed by Tang China at Baekgang in 663, after which he fortified Kyushu. He issued the Ōmi-ryō code, moved the court to Ōtsu, and was enthroned in 668, granting Kamatari the surname Fujiwara the next year. When he died in 672 his brother Prince Ōama defeated his son Prince Ōtomo in the Jinshin War.
zh: 天智天皇（626—672）初名葛城，后称中大兄皇子，是舒明天皇与皇极天皇之子、日本第38代天皇。645年，他与中臣镰足发动乙巳之变诛杀苏我入鹿，又以皇太子身份主导大化改新。他派军援助百济复国，663年在白江口之战中被唐朝大军击败，此后在九州修筑防御。他制定《近江令》，迁都大津，668年正式即位，次年赐镰足藤原之姓。672年他去世后，弟弟大海人皇子在壬申之乱中击败其子大友皇子。

en: Emperor Tenmu (c. 631–686), born Prince Ōama, was Japan's 40th sovereign, younger son of Jomei and Kōgyoku. In 671 he renounced the succession and became a monk at Yoshino Palace. In 672 he overthrew his nephew Prince Ōtomo in the Jinshin War after fleeing Yoshino and raising the eastern provinces. Enthroned in 673, he built a Tang-style centralised state, reformed the noble ranks, began the chronicles later the Nihon Shoki, and probably first used the title tennō. He patronised Buddhism and the Ise Shrine of Amaterasu. He died in 686; his consort succeeded him as Empress Jitō.
zh: 天武天皇（约631—686）名大海人皇子，是日本第40代天皇、舒明天皇与皇极天皇之子。671年他辞让继承权，到吉野宫出家。672年，他逃出吉野、召集东方诸国兵马，在壬申之乱中推翻侄子大友皇子。673年即位后，他效仿唐朝建立中央集权国家，改革冠位，下令编纂后来成为《日本书纪》的史书，并可能是首位使用“天皇”称号的统治者。他既护持佛教，也尊崇祭祀天照大神的伊势神宫。686年他去世，皇后继位为持统天皇。

en: Emperor Toba (1103–1156), personal name Munehito, was the 74th emperor of Japan. Raised by his grandfather, the cloistered Emperor Shirakawa, after his mother's early death, he was placed on the throne at four in 1107 and forced to abdicate in 1123 in favour of his young son Sutoku. Only on Shirakawa's death in 1129 did Toba take power. As cloistered sovereign he dominated the reigns of Sutoku, Konoe, and Go-Shirakawa for 28 years, compelling Sutoku in 1141 to abdicate for Konoe, Nariko's son. Ordained in 1142, he died in 1156; the ensuing succession feud became the Hōgen Rebellion.
zh: 鸟羽天皇（1103—1156），名宗仁，日本第74代天皇。母亲早逝，他由祖父白河法皇抚养，1107年4岁登基，1123年又在白河法皇主持下，被迫让位于皇子崇德天皇。1129年白河法皇去世后他才亲自执掌院政，左右崇德、近卫、后白河三代天皇的朝务实权达28年；1141年更迫使崇德天皇让位给藤原得子所生的近卫天皇。1142年他受戒出家，1156年去世后，随即爆发的皇位之争便是保元之乱。

en: Toda Yoshiyasu was a Kamakura-period gokenin, the fourth son of Sasaki no Yasukiyo and ancestor of the Sasaki-line Toda clan. Around 1278, when his brother Yoriyasu succeeded to the Izumo shugo post and took the Enya name, Yoshiyasu received the Toda Manor in Ou District of Izumo and adopted the surname Toda. He made his seat at Gassan-Toda Castle, built by his grandfather Sasaki no Yoshikiyo. He held the titles of saemon-no-jō and daibu hōgan.
zh: 富田义泰是镰仓时代的御家人，佐佐木泰清的四男，佐佐木流富田氏之祖。1278年前后，其兄赖泰继任出云守护、另立盐冶氏，义泰也分得出云国意宇郡富田庄，遂以富田为姓，并以祖父佐佐木义清所筑的月山富田城为居城。他官居左卫门尉、大夫判官。

en: Togashi no Iekuni was a Heian-period warrior of Kaga province, the son of Saitō no Sōsuke of a warrior house that claimed descent from the general Fujiwara no Toshihito. Genealogies of the Togashi record that Iekuni held Togashi village in Kaga and was the first of his line to take the place name as his surname, calling himself Togashi Iekuni, so he is counted as the clan's founder and first head. His son Nobuie succeeded him.
zh: 富㭴家国是平安时代加贺国的武士，斋藤宗辅之子，其家族自称出自镇守府将军藤原利仁一脉。富㭴氏的家谱记载，家国领有加贺国的富㭴乡，并首次以乡名为苗字、自称富㭴家国，因此被奉为富㭴氏的初代当主。其子信家继为当主。

en: Togashi Iemichi appears in Togashi clan genealogies as the third head of the Kaga warrior house, succeeding his father Nobuie and followed as head by his son Ietsune.
zh: 富㭴家通见于富㭴氏家谱，列为加贺武士家族的第三代当主，父为信家，其子家经继为当主。

en: Genealogies name Togashi Ienao as the fifth head of the Togashi clan of Kaga, a son of the fourth head Ietsune and, in the traditional line of descent, the father of Yasuie.
zh: 家谱列富㭴家直为加贺富㭴氏第五代当主，第四代当主家经之子，并按传统世系记作泰家之父。

en: Togashi Ienao is counted in the genealogies as the eighth head of the Togashi clan of Kaga, succeeding the seventh head Yasuharu and followed in turn by his son Yasuaki.
zh: 家谱列富㭴家尚为加贺富㭴氏第八代当主，上承第七代泰春，下传其子泰明。

en: Togashi Ietsune was the fourth head of the Togashi clan of Kaga and the father of Togashi Yasuie, the sixth head, famed as the keeper of the Ataka barrier.
zh: 富㭴家经是加贺富㭴氏的第四代当主，其子即第六代当主、以守卫安宅关闻名的富㭴泰家。

en: Genealogies name Togashi Nobuie as the second head of the Togashi warrior clan of Kaga, succeeding his father Iekuni, the clan's founder, and followed in turn by his son Iemichi.
zh: 家谱以富㭴信家为加贺富㭴氏的第二代当主，上承初代家国，下传其子家通。

en: Takaie Togashi was a warrior of the early Northern and Southern Courts period who is recorded, with uncertainty, as shugo, or military governor, of Kaga Province between 1336 and 1337.
zh: 富㭴高家是日本南北朝初期的武将，史料存疑地记载他于1336至1337年担任加贺国守护。

en: Ujiharu Togashi, eleventh head of his clan, was shugo of Kaga Province from 1355 to 1357. When he died of illness his young son Masaie inherited the post under a kinsman's guardianship; the Taiheiki records Sasaki Dōyō plotting to seize Kaga for the Shiba clan.
zh: 富㭴氏春是富㭴氏第十一代当主，1355至1357年任加贺国守护。他病死后，幼子昌家在族人辅佐下继任；《太平记》记载，佐佐木道誉曾图谋让斯波氏夺取加贺。

en: Togashi Yasuaki is the ninth head in the genealogical line of the Kaga Togashi, succeeding Ienao and followed by his son Takaie, who took office as shugo of Kaga in 1335.
zh: 富㭴泰明是加贺富㭴氏家谱中的第九代当主，上承家尚，下传其子高家；高家于1335年就任加贺守护。

en: Genealogies place Togashi Yasuharu seventh in the line of Togashi clan heads of Kaga, between Yasuie of the Ataka barrier and the eighth head, Ienao.
zh: 家谱中，富㭴泰春在加贺富㭴氏历代当主中列第七代，上承镇守安宅关的泰家，下接第八代家尚。

en: Togashi Yasuie was a late-Heian and early-Kamakura warrior, sixth head of the Togashi clan of Kaga, seated at Nonoichi. In 1183 he joined Minamoto no Yoshinaka against the Taira and fought at Kurikara Pass, where torches tied to oxen were driven burning into Taira no Koremori's camp in a night attack. After Yoshinaka's fall in 1184 he became shugo of Kaga and guarded the Ataka barrier. In 1187, tradition holds, he recognized Yoshitsune disguised as a yamabushi but let him pass, moved by Benkei's kanjinchō; stripped of office, he took the name Shigezumi and ended his days at Nonoichi.
zh: 富㭴泰家是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，加贺富㭴氏第六代当主，据点在野野市。1183年，他投奔源义仲讨伐平氏，在俱利伽罗峠之战中命人把燃着的松明绑在牛角上，趁夜冲入平维盛的大营，大破平军。1184年义仲败亡后，他被任为加贺守护，守卫安宅关。相传1187年，他在关前识破扮成山伏的源义经，却被弁庆诵读劝进帐的忠义打动，放一行人过关；事后因此被免官，出家改名重纯，最后回到野野市终老。

en: Toki Mitsuhira (died 1206) was a late-Heian warrior and Kamakura gokenin, the third son of Minamoto no Mitsunaga and effective founder of the Toki clan of Mino Province. Adopted by his uncle Mitsumoto, he held back when his father and elder brother died fighting with Kiso Yoshinaka in 1180, and only in 1184 led his kin to join Minamoto no Yoritomo; after the Taira fell, he became a shogunate vassal. Around 1201 he was made shugo of Mino Province with military and police authority, ruling from Hitoichiichiba manor in Toki district. He died in 1206 and was buried at Kozen-ji, succeeded by his son Mitsuyuki.
zh: 土岐光衡（卒于1206年）是平安末期至镰仓初期的武将、镰仓幕府御家人，伯耆守源光长的第三子，也是美浓国土岐氏的实际始祖。他被伯父源光基收为养子，1180年父亲与兄长随木曾义仲起兵战死后他没有参战，直到1184年才率一族投奔源赖朝，平家灭亡后成为幕府御家人。约1201年他被任命为美浓国守护，掌握国内的军事指挥与治安警察之权，以土岐郡的一日市场馆为本据并自称土岐。他于1206年去世，葬于光善寺，由嫡子土岐光行继任。

en: Toki Mitsusada was a late Kamakura-period commander and head of the Toki clan, the main line of Mino-Genji, and fifth son of Toki Mitsuyuki. He married into the Hōjō Tokusō family and held a jitō post in Iyo Province, raising the Toki to leading gokenin standing in Mino. The Azuma Kagami first names him in 1250, and he became governor of Oki Province after seizing an outlaw called Sanuki Jūrō. Buddhist records credit him with fighting the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281. Late in life he took the tonsure as Teikō and died around 1281.
zh: 土岐光定是镰仓时代后期武将，美浓源氏嫡流土岐氏当主，土岐光行第五子。他与北条得宗家联姻，并担任伊予国地头，使土岐氏成长为美浓的有力御家人。《吾妻镜》1250年条首次记载其名；他因追捕恶党赞岐十郎之功，出任隐岐守。佛教文献记载他在1274年和1281年两次元军来袭中立下战功。晚年出家，法号定光，约1281年去世。

en: Toki Mitsuyuki (died 1249) was the second head of the Toki clan, eldest son of Mitsuhira. A Kamakura gokenin, he served Retired Emperor Go-Toba in Kyoto as a Saimen warrior. In 1216 he was appointed Saemon-no-jo and served as a guard at the ceremony celebrating Sanetomo's appointment as shogun, receiving a palace-forged sword from Go-Toba. One account identifies him with the court warrior who fought with a thousand men in the Jokyu War of 1221, was routed by Ashikaga Yoshiuji on the Kiso River, lost the Mino shugo office and escaped punishment through Chiba patronage. Another holds that Mitsuyuki fought for the shogunate. He moved to Asano manor, took the name Asano Mitsuyuki, and died in 1249.
zh: 土岐光行（?—1249）是土岐氏第二代家督、土岐光衡的长子。他身为镰仓幕府御家人，与朝廷关系深厚，曾在京都担任后鸟羽上皇的西面武士。1216年他任左卫门尉，在将军源实朝叙任征夷大将军的拜贺式上担任随兵，并获后鸟羽上皇下赐院中锻造的御刀。一说认为他就是1221年承久之乱中率一千兵力加入京方的武士，在木曾川被足利义氏击败，失去美浓守护之职，靠千叶氏庇护免于问罪；另一说则认为光行参加了幕府方。后来他移居浅野馆，自称浅野光行，1249年去世。

en: Toki Naouji (born c. 1331) was a warrior lord of the Nanboku-chō period, a son of Toki Yorikiyo and younger brother of the powerful shugo daimyō Yoriyasu. He was adopted by Ōno Naotoshi, also called Doi Naotoshi, of the Ōno clan in Iyo Province, and took the name Ōno or Doi Naouji. His career unfolded mainly in Iyo on Shikoku, far from the main Toki lands in Mino. He later died of apoplexy at his residence in Kyoto.
zh: 土岐直氏（约1331年生）是南北朝时代的武将，土岐赖清之子、权势守护大名赖康的弟弟。他被伊予国大野氏的大野直利（又称土居直利）收为养子，改称大野直氏或土居直氏，主要在四国的伊予国活动，远离土岐氏本据的美浓。后来他因中风在京都的宿所去世。

en: Toki Yoriaki was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō periods, the twelfth and youngest son of Toki Yorisada, the first Muromachi shugo of Mino Province. He first served the Hōjō regents and the Rokuhara tandai alongside his father, then answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call and fought across the country under Ashikaga Takauji. After his elder brother Yoritō, the shugo of Mino, was executed in Kyōto in 1342, Yoriaki supported his nephew Yoriyasu and campaigned under Kō no Moronao. He was killed in 1348 at the Battle of Shijōnawate in Kawachi Province against the Southern Court's Kusunoki Masatsura.
zh: 土岐赖明是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，为美浓国初代室町守护土岐赖贞的第十二子，也是最小的儿子。他起初随父亲侍奉镰仓幕府执权北条得宗家及六波罗探题，后响应后醍醐天皇举兵，投入足利尊氏麾下转战各地。1342年，出任美浓守护的兄长赖远在京都被处死，赖明遂辅佐继承家业的侄子赖康，跟随高师直转战。1348年，他在河内国四条畷与南朝方的楠木正行交战，战死沙场。

en: Toki Yorikatsu was a Nanboku-chō warrior, a son of Toki Yorikiyo and a younger brother of Yoriyasu. When Yoriyasu made Kawate Castle in Atsumi district his base, Yorikatsu established himself in Ibi district in western Mino. Together with his younger brother Yoritada, who held the Ikeda district, he consolidated the Toki clan's grip on western Mino. He later called himself Ibi Yorikatsu and died in 1380. His son Yasuyuki was adopted by Yoriyasu and eventually succeeded to the headship of the main Toki line.
zh: 土岐赖雄是南北朝时代的武将，土岐赖清之子、赖康之弟。兄长赖康在美浓厚见郡筑革手城作为据点后，赖雄也在美浓西部揖斐郡立足，与居于池田郡的弟弟赖忠一起巩固了土岐氏在西美浓的根基。他后来自称揖斐赖雄，于1380年去世。其子康行被赖康收为养子，后来继承了土岐氏本家的家督之位。

en: Toki Yorikiyo was a commander and shugo daimyō of the late Kamakura and early Nanboku-chō period, a son of Toki Yorisada, the first Muromachi shugo of Mino. He made his home in Ikeda district of Mino Province, and under the Kenmu Restoration he was appointed shugo of Iyo Province. He died on 4 July 1336, before his father; the Toki headship passed first to his younger brother Yoritō and later to Yorikiyo's son Yoriyasu, who brought the clan to its height as shugo of three provinces.
zh: 土岐赖清是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，初代美浓守护土岐赖贞之子，居于美浓国池田郡。建武新政时，他被任命为伊予守护。1336年7月4日去世，先于父亲而亡；土岐氏家督之位先由其弟赖远继承，后由赖清之子赖康接续，赖康身兼美浓、尾张、伊势三国守护，将土岐氏推向全盛。

en: Toki Yorisada (1271–1339), seventh son of Toki Mitsusada, built the Toki into the dominant warrior house of Mino Province. In 1281 he married a daughter of Hōjō Muneyori as his second wife and established Hitotsuichiba Hall as his seat, planting clan branches across the province. Suspected of joining the Shōchū plot against the Kamakura shogunate in 1324, he nevertheless survived to serve Ashikaga Takauji and became the Muromachi shogunate's first governor of Mino. A friend of the Zen master Musō Soseki, he spread Rinzai Zen in the Toki district and left nearly ten poems in imperial anthologies.
zh: 土岐赖贞（1271—1339）是土岐光定的第七子，他把土岐氏经营成美浓国最有权势的武士家族。1281年他娶北条宗赖之女为后妻，以一日市场馆为本据，把一族子弟分派到美浓各地。1324年正中之变时，他被镰仓幕府怀疑参与后醍醐天皇的倒幕密谋，却免于覆灭，其后出仕足利尊氏，成为室町幕府的初代美浓守护。他与禅僧梦窗疎石交好，在土岐郡传播临济宗，还有近十首和歌入选敕撰和歌集。

en: Toki Yoritada (1323–1397), also known as Yoriyo, was a Nanboku-chō and Muromachi warrior, the sixth son of Toki Yorikiyo. Adopted young by his grandfather Yorisada after his father's early death, he held the Ikeda district of Mino and supported his eldest brother Yoriyasu. When his nephew Yasuyuki rose against Shōgun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in 1390, Yoritada joined the shogunal army with his second son Yorimasu to crush him. Appointed shugo of Mino after the revolt, he founded the Toki Nishi-Ikeda line, yielded the post to Yorimasu in 1395, and died in 1397 aged seventy-five.
zh: 土岐赖忠（1323—1397），又名赖世，是南北朝至室町时代的武将，土岐赖清的第六子。父亲早逝后，他被祖父赖贞收为养子，以美浓池田郡为据点辅佐长兄赖康。1390年，侄子康行受第三代将军足利义满逼迫而起兵，赖忠与次子赖益加入幕府军将其讨灭。乱后他被任命为美浓守护，开创土岐西池田家，1395年把守护职让给赖益，1397年去世，享年75岁。

en: Toki Yoritō (d. 1342), seventh son of Toki Yorisada, was a basara daimyō and governor of Mino. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji at Tatarahama and in Kyōto in 1336 and at Aonogahara against Kitabatake Akiie in 1338, where the Taiheiki credits his thousand picked horsemen with pinning the great loyalist army. Succeeding his father in 1339, he moved the Toki seat to Nagamori Castle and kept harrying Southern Court forces. In 1342, drunk, he reviled and overturned Retired Emperor Kōgon's ox cart; on Ashikaga Tadayoshi's order he was beheaded at Rokujōgawara that December.
zh: 土岐赖远（？—1342）是土岐赖贞的第七子，世称婆娑罗大名，美浓国守护。他追随足利尊氏，参加1336年的多多良滨之战与京都之战，1338年又在青野原迎战北畠显家；《太平记》称他率一千精骑死战，牵制住声势浩大的朝廷大军。1339年父亲死后他继承家督，把土岐氏本据移到长森城，继续追讨南朝势力。1342年他酒醉途中辱骂光严上皇，踢翻其牛车，被足利直义下令逮捕，同年十二月在京都六条河原斩首。

en: Toki Yoriyasu (1318–1388) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and shugo daimyō, the eldest son of Toki Yorikiyo and grandson of Yorisada. After his uncle Yoritō was executed for insulting the retired Emperor Kōgon in 1342, he succeeded as head of the Toki clan and shugo of Mino. A steadfast supporter of Ashikaga Takauji during the Kannō Disturbance, he received Owari in 1351 and Ise in 1360, holding all three provinces at the height of Toki power. He served as head of the Samurai-dokoro, helped engineer the fall of kanrei Hosokawa Yoriyuki in 1379, and died at Zuigan-ji in 1388.
zh: 土岐赖康（1318—1388）是南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，土岐赖清的长子、赖贞之孙。1342年，叔父赖远因对光严上皇施暴被处死后，他继任土岐氏家督和美浓守护。观应之扰乱中他始终支持室町幕府初代将军足利尊氏，1351年受封尾张守护，1360年又得到伊势，身兼三国守护，奠定土岐氏的全盛期。他曾任侍所头人，1379年参与策划推翻管领细川赖之，1388年在瑞岩寺去世。

en: Tokunō Michihide was an Iyo warrior and son of Tokunō Michitoshi, founder of the Tokunō house. The clan genealogy makes him father of Michizumi and Michimura, and grandfather of Michitsuna, who died fighting for the Southern Court in 1337.
zh: 得能通秀是伊予武士、得能氏始祖得能通俊之子。得能氏系图载其为通纯、通村之父，通纲之祖；通纲于1337年为南朝战死。

en: Tokunō Michimura was an Iyo warrior of the Tokunō house, holders of the Tokunō estate in Kuwamura district. The clan genealogy names him only as the father of Tokunō Michitsuna, who rose for Emperor Go-Daigo in 1333 and fell at Kanagasaki Castle in 1337.
zh: 得能通村是得能氏的伊予武士，该族领有桑村郡得能庄。系图中仅载其为得能通纲之父；通纲于1333年举兵响应后醍醐天皇，1337年战死于金崎城。

en: Tokunō Michitoshi was a son of the Iyo commander Kawano Michinobu and the ancestor after whom the Tokunō clan was named; the family held the Tokunō estate in Kuwamura district of Iyo, and genealogies trace his descendants to Hyūga in service to the Itō clan.
zh: 得能通俊是伊予武将河野通信之子，也是得能氏的得名始祖，该族领有伊予国桑村郡得能庄；家谱记载其后人移居日向国，为伊东氏效力。

en: Tokunō Michitsuna was a commander of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-chō period and head of a warrior house holding the Tokunō estate in Iyo Province. In the leap second month of 1333 he rose for Emperor Go-Daigo with Kawano kinsmen, stormed the Fuchū castle of Iyo shugo Utsunomiya Sadamune, and drove the Nagato tandai Hōjō Tokinao from the province. Under the Kenmu government he became governor of Bingo Province. He then joined the Southern Court under Nitta Yoshisada, fighting at Teshimagawara and Minatogawa in 1336, and was killed in 1337 defending Kanagasaki Castle in Echizen.
zh: 得能通纲是镰仓时代至南北朝时代武将，为领有伊予国桑村郡得能庄的得能氏当主。1333年闰二月，他与河野一族举兵响应后醍醐天皇，攻陷伊予守护宇都宫贞宗的府中城，并将长门探题北条时直逐出伊予。建武政权下叙任备后守。南北朝战乱中，他追随新田义贞加入南朝，1336年参加丰岛河原合战与凑川之战，1337年在越前金崎城之战中战死。

en: Tokunō Michizumi was an Iyo warrior of the Tokunō house and a son of Tokunō Michihide. The clan genealogy names him as the father of Tokunō Michikage, whose descendants founded a cadet branch of the house in Iyo.
zh: 得能通纯是得能氏的伊予武士、得能通秀之子。得能氏系图载其为得能通景之父，通景的后人另立分家。

en: Prince Tomohira (964–1009), the seventh son of Emperor Murakami by Princess Sōshi, was named an imperial prince in 965 and came of age in 977. He served as minister of war and later minister of central affairs, reaching the second court rank in 1007. Known to contemporaries as Go-Chūshō-ō or the Lord of Rokujō Palace, he was a gifted poet in both Chinese and Japanese verse: forty-one of his waka appear in imperial anthologies, and he helped compile the Wakanshōrōshū and Honchō monzui. His son Morofusa took the surname Minamoto, founding the Murakami Genji line.
zh: 具平亲王（964—1009）是村上天皇与庄子女王所生的第七皇子，965年获封亲王，977年元服。他历任兵部卿、中务卿，1007年升至二品，时人称他为后中书王、六条宫。具平长于汉诗与和歌，敕撰和歌集共收录其和歌四十一首，并参与编纂《和汉朗咏集》与《本朝文粹》。其子师房获赐姓源氏，子孙称村上源氏。

en: Prince Toneri (676–735), sixth son of Emperor Tenmu, was a leading imperial prince of the early Nara period. Raised to the first imperial rank in 718, he supervised the compilation of the Nihon Shoki and presented the thirty-scroll chronicle to the court in 720. After Fujiwara no Fuhito's death that same year, he became head of the Council of State, sharing power with Prince Nagaya, and in 729 he interrogated Nagaya during the Nagaya Incident. He died in 735. When his son Prince Ōi ascended as Emperor Junnin, Toneri received the posthumous title Emperor Sudōjinkei.
zh: 舍人亲王（676—735）是天武天皇第六子，奈良时代前期皇族势力的核心人物之一。718年升叙一品，主持《日本书纪》的编修，并于720年将这部三十卷史书奏上朝廷。同年藤原不比等去世后，他出任知太政官事，成为太政官首班，与长屋王共同执政；729年长屋王之变时，他负责审问长屋王。735年去世。其子大炊王后来即位为淳仁天皇，他被追尊为崇道尽敬皇帝。

en: Tōyama Kagefusa, also called Yajirō, was a lord of Akechi Castle in Mino Province of the Akechi Tōyama lineage. In July 1331 the Kamakura shogunate confirmed his rights as jitō over Akechi and neighboring holdings in Ena district. He fought for the Ashikaga at the Battle of Minatogawa on 4 July 1336, earning two thirds of Ichijima gō in Gujō district. In 1347 he won the suit over Tamuke gō for Tomokado against Nagai Sadayasu, and in March 1352 his military service earned him an estate in Awa Province. His son Yorikage became jitō in 1390.
zh: 远山景房（通称弥次郎）是美浓国明知城主，属明知远山氏一系。1331年7月，镰仓幕府安堵他对惠那郡明知及上下村、荒木村、洼原、佐佐良木、安主等领地的地头职。1336年7月4日，他在凑川之战中从足利一方参战，因功获赐郡上郡市岛乡三分之二的地头职。1347年朝廉与长井贞泰争夺手向乡时，他代朝廉一方胜诉；1352年3月又因军功受封安房国领地。1390年，其子赖景继任地头。

en: Tōyama Kagenaga was a Kamakura-period warrior of Mino and the second head of the Akechi Tōyama, succeeding his father Kageshige at Akechi Castle in the Tamuke district of the Tōyama manor. In 1261 the Azuma Kagami records him attending the hōjō-e festival at Tsurugaoka Hachiman Shrine in Kamakura, and in 1263 he and Kagekazu of the Iwamura Tōyama accompanied Shogun Prince Munetaka on his journey to Kyoto. In 1272 the bakufu stripped him of the Tamuke jitō post and granted it to Nagai Tokihide. His son Tomokado succeeded him.
zh: 远山景长是镰仓时代美浓国武将、明知远山氏第二代当主，继父亲景重领有远山庄手向乡的明知城。《吾妻镜》记载，1261年他在镰仓供奉鹤冈八幡宫的放生会；1263年，他与岩村远山氏的景员一同随将军宗尊亲王上洛。1272年，幕府没收他在手向乡的地头职，转授长井时秀。其子朝廉继嗣。

en: Tōyama Kageshige, called Saburōhyōe, was a Kamakura-period warrior of Mino Province and the second son of Tōyama Kagetomo, founder of the Tōyama clan. He inherited the Awaki district, also called Tamuke, in the southern Tōyama manor, and in 1247 built Akechi Castle there. From that seat he founded the Akechi Tōyama, one of the three leading Tōyama houses alongside the Iwamura and Naegi lines, and was succeeded by his son Kagenaga.
zh: 远山景重，通称三郎兵卫，是镰仓时代美浓国武将、远山氏初代景朝的次子。他领有远山庄南部的淡气乡（又称手向乡），于1247年在当地修筑明知城，开创明知远山氏，与岩村、苗木两家并称远山氏的三大支系，后由其子景长继嗣。

en: Tōyama Kagetada was a fourteenth-century warrior of the Akechi Tōyama lineage of Mino Province, recorded in family genealogies as the son of Tomokado and father of Kagefusa, successive lords of Akechi Castle in Ena district.
zh: 远山景忠是14世纪美浓国明知远山氏的武将，家谱世系记载他是朝廉之子、景房之父，前后相继为惠那郡明知城主。

en: Tōyama Kagetomo was a Kamakura-period warrior and founder of the Tōyama clan in Mino Province. The eldest son of Yoritomo's retainer Katō Kagekado, he inherited the Tōyama manor in Ena district as jitō, took the name Tōyama, and ruled from Iwamura Castle. In 1203 he and his father killed Nitta Tadatsune after the Hiki purge. In the Jōkyū War of 1221 he led the fifty-thousand-strong Tōsandō army with Takeda Nobumitsu, fought through to Kyoto, and on Hōjō Yasutoki's order beheaded the courtier Ichijō Nobuyoshi at Iwamura. He last appears in records between 1249 and 1256.
zh: 远山景朝是镰仓时代武将、美浓国远山氏初代当主。他是源赖朝亲信加藤景廉的长子，作为地头继承了惠那郡远山庄，遂称远山氏，以岩村城为本据。1203年比企能员之变后，他与父亲一同讨杀仁田忠常。1221年承久之乱中，他与武田信光率领五万东山道大军，攻入京都，奉北条泰时之命把公卿一条信能押到岩村斩首。其名最后见于1249—1256年间的记载。

en: Tōyama Tomokado was a lord of Akechi Castle in Ena district, Mino Province, and a head of the Akechi Tōyama lineage, son of Kagenaga and father of Kagetada. In 1333 the court issued him an edict granting Tamuke gō, and in 1336 he took service under Ashikaga Takauji. In March 1339 he received one half of Tamuke gō and in December the other half. In 1347 he disputed its possession with Nagai Sadayasu, and the suit ended in favour of his side through his kinsman Kagefusa.
zh: 远山朝廉是美浓国惠那郡明知城主、明知远山氏当主，系图作景长之子、景忠之父。1333年，朝廷下纶旨将手向乡宛行于他；1336年他投效足利尊氏。1339年3月他领有手向乡的一半，同年12月又获宛行另一半。1347年，他与长井贞泰就手向乡的领有权发生争议，经诉讼，其一方由同族景房代表胜诉。

en: Toshima Aritsune was a Kamakura-era warrior of the Musashi Toshima clan and provisional governor of Kii. In August 1184, serving under Minamoto no Yoshitsune, he occupied the Denbōin manor at Negoro-ji in Kii, levying troops and provisions on its peasants; the Kamakura regime had already appointed him Kii's military governor. In 1186 he arranged the transfer of former Taira lands, the Shinomura manor in Tamba, to the monk Enrō, and in 1189 attended Yoritomo's Tsurugaoka Hachiman service. In 1191 the bakufu ended his jitō rights over Mikami manor after a court suit, but gave him replacement land.
zh: 丰岛有经是镰仓时代武将，出身武藏国丰岛氏，官居纪伊权守。1184年8月，他随源义经进驻纪伊国高野山的传法院领根来寺，向庄民征发兵役与粮米，可见镰仓政权此时已任命他为纪伊守护人。1186年，他经手把丹波国篠村庄的平氏旧领转付僧人延朗；1189年供奉源赖朝参拜鹤冈八幡宫。1191年，因朝廷方面的诉讼，幕府停止了他对纪伊三上庄的地头职，但另给替地作为补偿。

en: Toshima Kagemura was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period, lord of Shakujii Castle in Musashi Province. Genealogies record that after his elder brother Yasukage died he held the family headship while his nephew Tomoyasu was a child, and that he restored the Ōji Gongen shrine. After the Nakasendai War of 1335 he is said to have sheltered the fugitive Hōjō Tokiyuki and adopted his son Terutoki. Tradition makes him a Southern Court follower under Nitta Yoshisada, awarded junior fifth rank, who later returned the headship to Tomoyasu.
zh: 丰岛景村是镰仓时代后期至南北朝时代的武将，担任武藏国石神井城主。据丰岛氏系图记载，兄长泰景死后，因侄朝泰年幼，由他继任家督；他还修造复兴了王子权现社。相传1335年中先代之乱后，他藏匿败逃的北条时行，并收时行之子辉时为养子。系图称他追随新田义贞效忠南朝，受任从五位下，待朝泰成人后又归还家督。

en: Toshima Kiyomoto was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods and head of the Toshima clan, which held Toshima district in Musashi Province and the Kasai manor in Shimōsa; his house had served the Minamoto since Minamoto no Yoshiie's campaigns. In 1177 he donated a new main hall to Katori Shrine in Shimōsa. After Minamoto no Yoritomo's defeat at Ishibashiyama in 1180, Kiyomoto and his son Kasai Kiyoshige joined Yoritomo's army and became gokenin of the new Kamakura shogunate. In 1189 the pair fought in the Ōshū campaign against the Northern Fujiwara.
zh: 丰岛清元是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将、武藏国丰岛郡丰岛氏当主，另领有下总国葛西御厨，其家族自源义家出征前九年、后三年之役起便世代为源氏家人。1177年，他为下总国香取神社造进正神殿。1180年源赖朝在石桥山之战败北后，清元与儿子葛西清重投奔赖朝，镰仓幕府开创后列为御家人。1189年，父子二人参加讨伐奥州藤原氏的奥州合战。

en: Toshima Terutoki, first called Kotarō Kagehide, is a warrior of the Southern and Northern Courts period known only from the Toshima genealogy and a temple necrology. They make him a son of Hōjō Tokiyuki, the last heir of the regent house, who was sheltered by the Toshima after his defeat in 1335; the childless Kagemura adopted him as heir. He is said to have held junior fifth rank as Hyōbu no taifu, met the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji and received permission to inherit the headship, and founded Dōjōji as the Toshima family temple in 1372. His sons were Kagenori and Hidetoki, though modern scholars doubt the story.
zh: 丰岛辉时（初名小太郎景秀）是南北朝时代的武将，事迹仅见于《泰盈本丰岛氏系图》和道场寺过去账。系图称他是镰仓幕府执权继承人北条时行之子：1335年时行在中先代之乱中败逃，受到丰岛景村庇护，无子的景村遂收他为养子以继家督。相传他官至从五位下兵部大辅，后谒见镰仓公方足利基氏，获许继承家业，1372年创建道场寺作为丰岛氏菩提寺，生子景则、秀时。近代学者多怀疑这一传说。

en: Toshima Tomotsune, called Tarō, was an early Kamakura gokenin and the heir of Toshima Kiyomoto, head of the Musashi warrior clan; his court rank was Uma-no-jō. In July 1201 he was appointed shugo of Tosa Province, and a surviving letter from Hōjō Tokimasa orders him to enforce a jitō stewardship grant in that province. In August 1203 he was replaced as shugo by Miura Yoshimura. That November, when Enryaku-ji's warrior monks barricaded themselves on Mount Hachiōji near Kyoto, he fell in the shogunate assault of 20 November, one of three hundred killed recorded by the Azuma Kagami.
zh: 丰岛朝经，通称太郎，官居右马允，是镰仓幕府初期的御家人、武藏豪族丰岛氏当主清元的嫡子。1201年7月，他出任土佐国守护，北条时政致他的一封文书命其在当地执行地头职的授封。1203年8月，土佐守护之职由三浦义村接替。同年11月，比叡山僧兵据守京都附近的八王子山，幕府发兵攻打，朝经在11月20日的激战中战死，《吾妻镜》记载此役共有三百人阵亡。

en: Toshima Tomoyasu was a fourteenth-century head of the Toshima clan in Musashi Province, son of Toshima Yasukage. His uncle Kagemura held the headship until he came of age. An Ashikaga muster notice addressed to him survives from 1342, and his son Munetomo succeeded him.
zh: 丰岛朝泰是14世纪武藏国丰岛武士团的当主，丰岛泰景之子。他年幼时由叔父景村代行家督，成人后景村将家督与宗家领地归还给他。足利方1342年发给他的着到状留存至今，后继者为其子宗朝。

en: The Edo-period genealogies of the Toshima clan name Tsuneyasu as a head of the clan's main line in Musashi Province, the son of Aritsune and father of Yasutomo.
zh: 丰岛氏的江户时代家系图把经泰列为武藏国丰岛氏本宗的一代，为有经之子、泰友之父。

en: Toshima Yasuie, known as Saburō, was a Heian-period local magnate of southern Musashi Province, from the Taira-surnamed Chichibu line that produced the Toshima clan. The son of Toshima Tsuneie, he took a daughter of Chichibu Shigehiro as wife for his son Kiyomoto, and when his daughter wed Fujiwara Tōkane he gave her part of Adachi District. By the Hōgen Disturbance of 1156 Kiyomoto led the clan for Minamoto no Yoshitomo. Yasuie is also named as founder of Seikōji temple.
zh: 丰岛康家（通称三郎）是平安时代武藏国南部的地方豪族，出自赐平姓的秩父氏一脉，即丰岛氏所属的家族。他是丰岛常家之子，为儿子清元娶了秩父重弘之女；女儿嫁给藤原远兼（后来的足立氏）时，又把足立郡的一部分分给女儿。到1156年保元之乱时，其子清元已率一族在源义朝麾下参战。此外，清光寺也有以他为开基祖的说法。

en: The Toshima clan genealogies name Yasukage a head of the Musashi Toshima clan, son of Yasutomo and elder brother of Kagemura. On his death his son Tomoyasu was still a child, so Kagemura took the headship and held Shakujii Castle.
zh: 丰岛氏诸系图把泰景列为武藏国丰岛氏当主，泰友之子、景村之兄。他死后儿子朝泰年幼，由弟弟景村继承家督，成为石神井城主。

en: The Toshima clan genealogies name Yasutomo as a head of the Musashi warrior house, the son of Tsuneyasu and father of Yasukage and Kagemura, the latter a Toshima commander of the Nanbokuchō wars.
zh: 丰岛氏诸系图把泰友列为武藏国丰岛氏的当主，经泰之子，下有泰景、景村二子；其中景村是南北朝时代的丰岛氏武将。

en: Tō no Sadatsune was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Tō clan, the Gujō cadet line of the Chiba in Mino Province, genealogically recorded as a son of Tō no Tokitsune.
zh: 东贞常是镰仓时代东氏的武将，东氏是千叶氏在美浓国郡上的庶流；谱系把他记为东时常之子。

en: Tō no Shigetane (1177–1247) was the second head of the Tō clan and a trusted attendant of the third Kamakura shogun, Minamoto no Sanetomo. He succeeded his father Taneyori around 1190, and in 1199 his name appeared among the sixty-six gokenin who signed the impeachment of Kajiwara Kagetoki. A waka poet like his father, he joined Sanetomo's inner circle; in 1206 the shogun sent him poems urging his return from Higashi Manor to Kamakura, later collected in the Kinkai Wakashū. After Sanetomo's assassination in 1219 he took vows and yielded the headship to his son Taneyuki.
zh: 东重胤（1177—1247）是东氏第二代当主，镰仓幕府第三代将军源实朝的侧近。他约在1190年前后从父亲胤赖手中继承家督，1199年梶原景时之变时，列名于六十六名御家人联名弹劾的状纸。他与父亲一样是歌人，因而得到实朝宠信，入为近习。1206年他回下总国东庄久居不归，实朝特意赠和歌催他返回镰仓，这些歌后收入《金槐和歌集》。1219年实朝遇刺后，他出家为僧，把家督让给儿子胤行。

en: Tō no Taneyori (1155–1228), called Tō Rokurō Daibu, was the sixth son of Chiba Tsunetane and ancestor of the Tō and Endō warrior houses. Serving as a capital guard at Prince Mochihito's rising in 1180, he brought word of it to Minamoto no Yoritomo in Izu. In the Genpei War he urged his father to join Yoritomo and with his nephew Naritsune destroyed the Shimōsa deputy's force. He held Higashi Manor in Shimōsa, was famed for his waka, and ended as a disciple of Hōnen; in 1227 he helped guard the transfer of Hōnen's remains during the Karoku persecution.
zh: 东胤赖（1155—1228），通称东六郎大夫，是千叶常胤的第六子，东氏与远藤氏的始祖。1180年以仁王举兵时，他正在京都担任大番役，事后赶赴伊豆，把举兵的消息报给源赖朝。治承·寿永之乱中，他力劝父亲投奔赖朝，并与侄子成胤一同攻灭下总目代。他领有下总国东庄，以和歌见长；晚年拜在法然上人门下，1227年嘉禄法难时还参加了护送法然遗骸移葬的行动。

en: Tō no Taneyuki, also called Sosen, was the third head of the Tō clan and founder of its Gujō branch in Mino Province. A waka poet like his father Shigetane, he served four successive Kamakura shoguns from Sanetomo to Prince Munetaka. For his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221 he received Yamada Manor in Gujō. In 1233 he visited Fujiwara no Teika in Kyoto seeking a place in the new imperial anthology, but was turned away. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 he stormed Chiba Hidetane's stronghold in Kazusa and saved his maternal grandson.
zh: 东胤行，法名素暹，是东氏第三代当主，也是美浓国郡上东氏的开祖。他和父亲重胤一样是歌人，凭借文笔与和歌先后出仕源实朝、藤原赖经、藤原赖嗣、宗尊亲王四代镰仓将军。因1221年承久之乱的军功，他获封郡上的山田庄。1233年，他拜访藤原定家，希望自己的和歌入选新的敕撰集，却被定家称病拒见。1247年宝治合战时，他参加攻打上总国千叶秀胤据点玉崎庄大柳馆的战斗，并以战功换得自己外孙活命。

en: Tō no Tokitsune (1253–1314) was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Tō clan's Gujō line in Mino Province, the son of the clan head Tō no Yukiuji. The genealogy records a son, Sadatsune.
zh: 东时常（1253—1314）是美浓国郡上东氏的镰仓时代武将，当主东行氏之子；谱系记载他有子名贞常。

en: Tō no Tsuneaki was a warrior of the Tō family, a cadet line of the Chiba clan, during the Nanbokuchō wars. In August 1345 he joined Chiba Ujitane and other Chiba kinsmen in attending the memorial service at Tenryū-ji.
zh: 东常显是南北朝动乱时期的武将，出自千叶氏庶流东氏。1345年8月，他随千叶氏胤等千叶氏一族参加了在天龙寺举行的供养法会。

en: Tō no Ujimura was the fourth head of the Tō clan of Gujō in Mino Province, a warrior house descended from the Chiba clan. His father Taneyuki had been enfeoffed with Yamada Manor in Gujō for his service in the Jōkyū War of 1221. Early in the fourteenth century Ujimura moved the clan's seat from Achiba Castle, and the Yamato village history records that Shinowaki Castle was completed under him, becoming the family's residence. He died in 1377.
zh: 东氏村是美浓国郡上东氏的第四代当主，该族是出自千叶氏的武家。其父东胤行因1221年承久之乱的军功受封郡上的山田庄。14世纪初，氏村把据点从阿千叶城迁出；据《大和村史》记载，筱胁城在他任内正式完工，成为一族的居城。他于1377年去世。

en: Tō no Yukiuji (1228–1300), or Tō Rokurō, was a Kamakura warrior and head of the Tō clan's Gujō line, the son of the poet Tō no Taneyuki. Family tradition made his mother a daughter of Fujiwara no Tameie, but Teika's Meigetsuki diary disproves this.
zh: 东行氏（1228—1300），又称东六郎，是镰仓时代武将、东氏美浓系当主，歌人东胤行之子。东氏传说称其母为藤原为家之女，但藤原定家的《明月记》否定了这一说法。

en: Akahashi Tōshi (1306–1365) was the legal wife of Ashikaga Takauji, founder of the Muromachi shogunate. Born into the Hōjō regent house of Akahashi, she married the Ashikaga heir Takauji and bore their eldest son Yoshiakira in 1330. In 1333 she and the boy were held as hostages in Kamakura and narrowly escaped when Nitta Yoshisada overthrew the Hōjō. As midaidokoro she held the junior second rank, and in 1340 bore Takauji's son Motouji, the first Kamakura kubō. Widowed in 1358 she took the veil, died on 25 May 1365 aged sixty, and was posthumously granted junior first rank.
zh: 赤桥登子（1306—1365）是室町幕府开创者足利尊氏的正室。她出身把持镰仓幕府执权之职的北条氏赤桥流，嫁给足利家继承人尊氏，1330年生下嫡男千寿王（即后来的义诠）。1333年她与幼子作为人质留在镰仓，新田义贞攻灭北条氏时母子险些遇难，侥幸逃脱。身为御台所，她叙任从二位，1340年又生下后来的初代镰仓公方足利基氏。1358年尊氏去世后她落发出家，称大方殿；1365年5月25日去世，享年60岁，追赠从一位。

en: The Tozawa genealogy names Chikamori as the third head of the clan, bearing the court title Hida no kami. He was a son of the second head, Kanemori, and the father of Katsumori, who succeeded him as fourth head.
zh: 户泽氏系图列亲盛为第三代当主，带有飞驒守的头衔。他是第二代当主兼盛之子，也是继他之后成为第四代当主的克盛之父。

en: Tozawa Gensei headed the Tozawa clan of Shizukuishi in Mutsu; he may have been associated with the Shizukuishi troops mobilized by Kitabatake Akinobu in 1341, and his son Hidemori had succeeded him by 1356.
zh: 户泽玄盛是陆奥滴石户泽氏的当主，1341年北畠显信动员的滴石之兵可能与他有关；到1356年，其子英盛已继任家督。

en: Genealogies name Taira no Hidemori, later called Tozawa Hidemori, as founder of the Tozawa clan and a son of Taira no Michimasa of the Kammu Heike, while the Hankanfu calls him a son of Taira no Koremori. He first served Kiso Yoshinaka, then withdrew to the Shizukuishi manor in Iwate district, Mutsu. In 1185 he submitted to Minamoto no Yoritomo, fought at Yashima and in the Ōshū campaign, and was enfeoffed with lands in Shizukuishi, taking the name Tozawa from the village where he settled. Modern scholars suspect he was really a local retainer of the Northern Fujiwara.
zh: 系图将平衡盛，又称户泽衡盛，列为户泽氏的家祖及桓武平氏平通正之子；《藩翰谱》则称他是平维盛之子。他起初追随木曾义仲，后来前往陆奥国磐手郡的滴石庄。1185年他臣服于源赖朝，在屋岛之战和奥州合战中立功，受封滴石庄内的大片土地，并以定居的户泽邑取姓“户泽”。现代学者则推测，他实际上可能是奥州藤原氏麾下的当地豪族。

en: Tozawa Hidemori succeeded his father Gensei as head of the Tozawa clan of Shizukuishi in Mutsu. In 1356 he is recorded travelling to Kamakura to enter service, by which time the clan, like many other local warriors, had gone over to the Northern Court.
zh: 户泽英盛继其父玄盛之后成为陆奥滴石户泽氏的当主。1356年史料记载他前往镰仓出仕，此时户泽氏与许多地方武士一样，已经转投北朝一方。

en: The Hankanfu genealogy makes Tozawa no Kanemori the second head of the Tozawa clan, with the title Hida no kami, and a son of the founder Hidemori. In 1206, hard pressed by the Nanbu clan, he left the family's Shizukuishi manor in Mutsu and withdrew west across the Ōu Mountains to Kadoya-kodate in Semboku district of Dewa. In 1220 he moved his seat from Kadoya-kodate to Kadoya, and in 1228 he built Kadoya Castle, planting the clan in its Dewa lands, from which it later grew powerful around Kakunodate.
zh: 《藩翰谱》系图列户泽兼盛为户泽氏第二代当主，称飞驒守，是家祖衡盛之子。1206年，在南部氏的攻势下，他放弃陆奥的滴石庄，向西越过奥羽山脉，迁至出羽国仙北郡的门屋小馆。1220年，他又把据点从门屋小馆移到门屋，1228年修筑门屋城，使户泽氏在出羽的领地扎下根基，后来的势力即以角馆一带为中心壮大。

en: The Tozawa genealogy names Katsumori as the fourth head of the clan. He was a son of the third head, Chikamori, and fathered the fifth head, also called Katsumori but written 勝盛, who held the title Hida no kami, as well as Hisamori.
zh: 户泽氏系图列克盛为第四代当主。他是第三代当主亲盛之子，生下第五代当主胜盛（带有飞驒守头衔）和久盛。

en: Tsuchimikado (1196–1231), the eldest son of Emperor Go-Toba, was placed on the throne in 1198 at the age of two when his father abdicated; Go-Toba held real power as cloistered emperor. In 1210 Go-Toba made him yield the throne to his younger brother Juntoku, whose views better suited the plan to overthrow the shogunate. Tsuchimikado took no part in the Jōkyū War of 1221, yet after its failure he asked to share his father's punishment and was exiled to Tosa and then Awa province, where the shogunate treated him leniently. He died in Awa in 1231, aged thirty-five.
zh: 土御门天皇（1196—1231）是后鸟羽天皇的长子，1198年父亲让位时，年仅两岁的他登基，实权由后鸟羽上皇以院政掌握。1210年，后鸟羽偏爱更赞同倒幕的守成亲王，迫使他让位给弟弟顺德天皇。1221年承久之乱时他没有参与举兵，但乱事失败后主动请求与父亲同受流刑，先被流放土佐国，后改配阿波国，幕府对他颇为礼遇。1231年他在阿波去世，终年三十五岁。

en: Tsuchimochi Koretsuna was, in clan genealogies, the third head of the Agata Tsuchimochi of northern Hyūga Province, succeeding his father Michitsuna and followed by his son Masatsuna.
zh: 土持惟纲在土持氏系图中是日向国北部县土持氏第三代当主，上承其父通纲，下传其子政纲。

en: Tsuchimochi Kunitsuna was, in clan genealogies, the fifth head of the Agata Tsuchimochi, the main line of the Tsuchimochi family of northern Hyūga Province. During the Kenmu wars he went up to Kyoto with his kinsmen and, in January 1336, fought there for Ashikaga Takauji, falling in the fighting at Ōwatari.
zh: 土持国纲在土持氏系图中是日向国北部土持氏宗家县土持氏的第五代当主。建武战乱期间，他与族人一同上京，1336年1月在京都加入足利尊氏一方作战，最终在大渡的战斗中阵亡。

en: Clan genealogies place the Kamakura-period warrior Tsuchimochi Masatsuna as the fourth head of the Agata Tsuchimochi of northern Hyūga Province, succeeding his father Koretsuna and followed by his son Kunitsuna, the fifth head.
zh: 镰仓时代武士土持政纲，在土持氏系图中是日向国北部县土持氏第四代当主，上承其父惟纲，下传第五代当主、其子国纲。

en: Tsuchimochi Michitsuna, also recorded as Dōtsuna, was the second head in the Tsuchimochi clan genealogy; the family tree names him as the ancestor of the Agata Tsuchimochi of northern Hyūga Province. He was the son of Nobutsuna and father of Koretsuna.
zh: 土持通纲（一作道纲）是土持氏系图中的第二代，被记为日向国北部县土持氏之祖。他是宣纲之子、惟纲之父。

en: Nobue Tsuchimochi was a warrior of the Agata-Tsuchimochi house of northern Hyūga who fought for Ashikaga Takauji and the Northern Court in the Kenmu wars. In the twelfth month of 1335 his men stormed the Mukasa-in manor office near modern Miyazaki, where the Southern Court lord Itō Sukihiro had barricaded himself; his own battle report, the Tsuchimochi Nobue gunchūjō issued in 1336, is the first record of Mukasa Castle. In 1336 he defended Takauji's private fief of Mukasa-in against Sagara Yorihiro's attack.
zh: 土持宣荣是日向北部县土持氏的武士，在建武年间的战乱中为足利尊氏和北朝效力。1335年十二月，他率部攻打今宫崎附近的穆佐院政所，将据守于此的南朝方领主伊东祐广逐出；他本人于1336年上报的《土持宣荣军忠状》是穆佐城最早的史料记载。1336年，相良赖广来攻尊氏的直领穆佐院，宣荣据地抵御。

en: Tsuchimochi Nobutsuna, called Tarō, was the head of the Tsuchimochi warrior family of northern Hyūga Province in the late twelfth century. Under him the clan, remembered as the Seven Tsuchimochi Heads, held sway over Agata, Takarabe, Obi and four other strongholds. From the twelfth century the Tsuchimochi strengthened ties with the Kusakabe, the long-serving local officials of Hyūga, and acquired their offices and interests. As a Kamakura shogunate vassal he held steward rights over Usa Hachiman shrine lands; the 1197 Hyūga cadastral register lists his holdings at 1436 chō.
zh: 土持宣纲（通称太郎）是12世纪后期日向国北部武士家族土持氏的当主。在他的时代，全族号称“土持七头”，在县、财部、饫肥等七处要地称雄。自12世纪起，土持氏加强与世代担任日向在国司的日下部氏的关系，取得其官职和权益。镰仓幕府时代他成为御家人，领有宇佐八幡宫庄园的地头职权，据1197年的《日向国图田帐》记载，其名下领地达1436町。

en: Tokie Tsuchimochi, called Minbu, was descended from Kunitsuna, the fifth head of the Agata-Tsuchimochi of northern Hyūga. In 1395 he had Taishaku-ji at Shimokitakata repaired and changed from Tendai to Sōtō. His son Katsumitsu became a senior Shimazu retainer.
zh: 土持时荣，官称民部，出自日向北部县土持氏第5代当主国纲一脉。1395年，他重修下北方町的帝释寺，将其由天台宗改为曹洞宗。其子荣胜成为岛津氏的家老。

en: Prince Tsuneyoshi (1325–1338?) was the eldest son of Emperor Go-Daigo by his favourite consort Ano Renshi. Named crown prince in 1334, he was taken from Kyoto in 1336 after Ashikaga Takauji's victory at Minatogawa, when Nitta Yoshisada escorted him and his half-brother Prince Takayoshi north to Kanagasaki Castle in Echizen. There he issued imperial commands, heading a short-lived Hokuriku court. The castle fell to the Ashikaga army in 1337; the Taiheiki says he was captured and, with his brother Prince Nariyoshi, poisoned in Kyoto in May 1338, though he may have survived in the north until around 1346.
zh: 恒良亲王（1325—1338？）是后醍醐天皇与宠姬阿野廉子的长子，1334年被立为皇太子。1336年足利尊氏在凑川获胜后，新田义贞奉他与异母兄尊良亲王北上，进入越前金崎城。他在那里以天皇名义发布纶旨，主持短暂的“北陆朝廷”。1337年金崎城被足利军攻陷；《太平记》称他被俘，与弟弟成良亲王一同于1338年5月在京都被毒杀，但也有迹象表明他可能在北陆活到1346年前后。

en: Emperor Uda (866–931), personal name Sadami, was the 59th emperor of Japan, reigning from 887 to 897. The seventh son of Emperor Kōkō, he was demoted to commoner with the Minamoto surname in 884, then reinstated and enthroned three years later by the regent Fujiwara no Mototsune. His attempt to curb Mototsune in the Akō controversy failed, but after 891 he ruled directly, promoted Sugawara no Michizane, and halted the missions to Tang China in 894. In that year he established Ninna-ji as an imperial temple. He abdicated to his son Emperor Daigo in 897, took Buddhist vows in 899, and died in 931.
zh: 宇多天皇（866—931），名定省，是日本第59代天皇，887年至897年在位。他是光孝天皇的第七子，884年被赐姓源氏、降为臣籍，三年后却被摄政藤原基经迎回皇室并拥立为帝。他在阿衡事件中试图压制基经，未能成功；891年起亲政，重用菅原道真，并于894年废止遣唐使。同年他将仁和寺定为御愿寺。897年他让位于儿子醍醐天皇，899年出家，931年去世。

en: Ueno Giben, first named Yoshiari and called the Ueno Risshi, was a warrior and Buddhist monk of the mid-Kamakura period and the ancestor of the Ueno and Hanabusa clans, of Minamoto descent. The eighth son of Ashikaga Yasuuji, he is said to have been adopted by his grandfather Ashikaga Yoshiuji and married a daughter of Kira Nagauji. He held the jitō office of the Ueno manor, a Hachijō-in estate in Mikawa Province, giving him standing within the Ashikaga house. His sons included Yoritō, Sadatō and Hanabusa no Tomimichi, who died in 1316.
zh: 上野义弁初名义有，称上野律师，是镰仓时代中期的武将与僧侣，被尊为上野氏与花房氏之祖，本姓源氏。他是足利泰氏的第八子，相传被祖父足利义氏收为养子，娶吉良长氏之女为妻。义弁领有三河国八条院领地内的上野庄地头职，在足利氏一门中保有相当地位。其子包括上野赖远、上野贞远和花房职通，花房职通于1316年去世。

en: Ueno Tadakatsu (dates unknown), also called Ueno Tarōjirō, was a general of the Northern and Southern Courts period from the Ueno clan, a cadet branch of the Ashikaga. He is held to be the same man as Ueno Ujikatsu, younger brother of Ueno Yorikane, and during the Kannō Disturbance of 1350–1352 he stood with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, from whose name he received the character choku in his own. His court offices were Kamo-no-suke and Sakyō-no-suke.
zh: 上野直胜（生卒年不详），通称上野太郎二郎，是日本南北朝时代的武将，出身足利氏的支流上野氏。一般认为他与上野赖兼之弟上野氏胜是同一人；在1350—1352年的观应之扰乱中，他站在足利直义一方，名字中的“直”字即得自直义的偏讳。他历任扫部助、左京亮。

en: Ueno Yorikane (died 23 September 1351) was a Northern and Southern Courts period general of the Ueno clan, a cadet branch of the Ashikaga. In 1336, during Ashikaga Takauji's retreat to Kyushu, he led the attack on Kuroki Castle in Chikugo as a grand general. As shugo of Iwami he fought Southern Court forces there in 1337, 1343 and 1348. During the Kannō Disturbance he sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi, who made him shugo of Tajima and Tango in 1351. He followed Tadayoshi north and fell in battle in Tajima that September.
zh: 上野赖兼（？—1351年9月23日）是日本南北朝时代的武将，出身上野氏，即足利氏的支流、源自清和源氏。1336年足利尊氏西走九州时，他担任大将军，率军攻打筑后国黑木城。其后他出任石见国守护，于1337年、1343年和1348年在当地与南朝军队交战。观应之扰乱时他站在足利直义一方，1351年先后就任但马、丹后两国守护；他随直义北逃，同年9月战死于但马。

en: Ueno Yoritō, later called Yorikatsu, was the eldest son of the monk-warrior Ueno Giben and succeeded him as head of the Mikawa Ueno clan, an Ashikaga offshoot. Genealogies name his son as Ueno Yorikane, who continued the main line.
zh: 上野赖远后改名赖胜，是武将僧侣上野义弁的长子，继为足利氏分流的三河上野氏当主。家谱载其子为上野赖兼，由赖兼延续嫡流。

en: Nichijō was a monk of the Nichiren, or Hokke, sect in the Northern and Southern Courts period, born in Suruga Province as a son of Uesugi Yorishige; his courtesy name was Hōryū and his gō Myōryū-in. His elder sister Kiyoko (c. 1270–1343) was the mother of Ashikaga Takauji, founder of the Muromachi shogunate, making Nichijō the shōgun's uncle. He founded the sect's Rokujō lineage and wrote the Kamakura Denchū Mondō, recording his master Nichiin's debate victory over every other sect at the palace of the Kamakura shogunate.
zh: 日静是日本南北朝时代日莲宗（法华宗）的僧人，生于骏河国，为上杉赖重之子，字丰龙，号妙龙院。其姐清子（约1270—1343）是室町幕府开创者足利尊氏的生母，因此日静是尊氏的舅父。他开创了日莲宗的六条门流，并撰有《镰仓殿中问答》，记述其师日印在镰仓幕府殿中当众论破各宗派僧人的经过。

en: Uesugi Noriaki (1306–1368) was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era, founder of the Yamanouchi Uesugi line and the first Kantō kanrei. A cousin of Ashikaga Takauji, he served the Kamakura government from 1334 and, after his father Norifusa fell fighting in Kyoto in 1336, succeeded him as shugo of Kōzuke. From 1341 he held Echigo too, subduing Southern Court risings there. He sided with Ashikaga Tadayoshi in the Kannō Disturbance and was driven out in 1351; pardoned in 1361, he became Kantō kanrei in 1363 and died in 1368.
zh: 上杉宪显（1306—1368）是日本镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，山内上杉氏之祖，首任关东管领。他与足利尊氏是表兄弟，1334年起供职于镰仓将军府；1336年父亲上杉宪房在京都战死后，他继任上野国守护。1341年起他又兼任越后国守护，镇压当地的南朝势力。观应之扰乱中他追随足利直义，1351年失势流亡；1361年获赦，1363年就任关东管领，1368年去世。

en: Uesugi Norifuji (1318–1338) was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era, son of Uesugi Norifusa and maternal cousin of Ashikaga Takauji and Tadayoshi, and the ancestor of the Inukake Uesugi house. He served Takauji and his heir Senjuō, and in February 1338 marched with Takauji on Kyoto to stop the Southern Court general Kitabatake Akiie. On 15 March 1338 he fell in the battle at Watanabe in Settsu Province, aged twenty-one. His two infant sons, Tomofusa and Tomomune, were raised under protection and grew to lead the Inukake house.
zh: 上杉宪藤（1318—1338）是日本镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪房之子、足利尊氏与直义兄弟的表弟，犬悬上杉氏之祖。他出仕尊氏及其继承人千寿王；1338年2月随尊氏上洛，阻击南朝大将北畠显家。同年3月15日，他在摄津国渡边之战中奋战而死，年仅21岁。他留下朝房、朝宗两个幼子，由人保护长大，后来支撑起犬悬上杉氏一门。

en: Uesugi Norifusa was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts era, third head of the Uesugi clan and maternal uncle of Ashikaga Takauji. For helping overthrow the Kamakura shogunate he received a jitō post in Izu Province in 1333 and served on the Kenmu government's board of civil suits. When war resumed he became shugo of Kōzuke Province to watch Nitta Yoshisada. He marched on Kyoto with Takauji and died fighting at Shijō Kawara on 10 March 1336, covering Takauji's flight to Kyushu. His sons Noriaki and Norifuji founded the Yamanouchi and Inukake Uesugi lines.
zh: 上杉宪房是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，上杉氏第三代当主，也是足利尊氏的母方伯父。他因倒幕有功，于1333年获封伊豆国的地头职，在建武政权的杂诉决断所供职。战事再起后，他出任上野国守护，负责牵制新田义贞。宪房随尊氏进军京都，尊氏逃往九州，他于1336年3月10日在京都四条河原的战斗中为掩护尊氏脱逃而战死。其子宪显、宪藤分别成为山内上杉家与犬悬上杉家之祖。

en: Uesugi Noriharu (died 1379) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, a son of Uesugi Noriaki who attended the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Motouji and his son Ujimitsu. In 1368 he helped his brother Yoshinori crush Nitta Yoshimune's revolt, and in 1371 he became shugo of Kōzuke, the Yamanouchi Uesugi's home province, a post that unsettled the clan. He succeeded Yoshinori as Kantō kanrei in 1378. When Ujimitsu prepared to march on Kyoto during the 1379 Kōryaku Disturbance, Noriharu's remonstrances were ignored, and he killed himself at his Kamakura mansion on the seventh day of the third month; Ujimitsu then abandoned the campaign.
zh: 上杉宪春（？—1379）是日本南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，上杉宪显之子，自幼近侍镰仓公方足利基氏、足利氏满父子。1368年他随兄长能宪镇压新田义宗等人的叛乱立功，1371年被任命为上野守护——这一山内上杉氏根本之地的职位曾在一族中引起动摇。1378年能宪死后，他就任关东管领。1379年康历政变时，氏满打算趁乱上洛，宪春苦苦谏止却不被采纳，遂于3月7日在镰仓的宅邸自尽，氏满因此放弃出兵。

en: Uesugi Norikata (1335–1394) was a Muromachi warrior, a son of Uesugi Noriaki, and the founder of the Yamanouchi Uesugi line. In 1376 his brother Yoshinori, dying, passed him the clan headship and the Izu shugo post, and in 1379 Norikata became Kantō kanrei to Ashikaga Ujimitsu, also holding Kōzuke, Musashi and Awa. During his term the kanrei's practice of issuing enforcement orders alongside the Kamakura kubo's edicts became standard. He led the early campaigns of the 1380–1382 Oyama Yoshimasa revolt in Shimotsuke and founded Kamakura's Meigetsu-in temple. He died in the tenth month of 1394, aged sixty.
zh: 上杉宪方（1335—1394）是日本室町时代初期的武将、守护大名，上杉宪显之子，开创了山内上杉氏，也是镰仓明月院的开基者。1376年，兄长能宪在病榻上将山内家督与伊豆守护职传给他；1379年他出任镰仓公方足利氏满的关东管领，并兼任上野、武藏、安房等国守护。在他任内，关东管领在镰仓公方御教书之外附发施行状的做法成为定例。1380至1382年小山义政之乱时，他曾任讨伐军大将。他于1394年10月去世，终年60岁。

en: Uesugi Norimasa (died 1366) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and heir of his father Uesugi Noriaki, Kantō kanrei and shugo of Echigo. In the Kannō Disturbance he fought for Ashikaga Tadayoshi: he entered Echigo against the Northern Court in 1350, and in the first month of 1351 marched into Kai Province and destroyed Kō no Morofuyu. Later that year he was defeated by Takauji's army at the Sattatōge Pass in Suruga. He rose again in Echigo in 1355, then fought on in Shinano, and died in 1366, before his father.
zh: 上杉宪将（？—1366）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪显的嫡子，宪显官至关东管领、越后守护。观应之乱中他为足利直义作战：1350年进入越后与北朝交锋，1351年正月进军甲斐国，攻灭高师冬。同年12月，他在骏河国萨埵峠被足利尊氏的军队击败。1355年他在越后再度举兵，此后转战信浓，最终于1366年先于父亲去世。

en: Uesugi Shigeaki (dates unknown) was a Kamakura-period warrior, the legitimate son of Uesugi Yorishige. His younger brothers were Yorinari and Norifusa, and his sister Kiyoko, a consort of Ashikaga Sadauji, was the mother of Ashikaga Takauji, so the first Muromachi shōgun was his nephew. Known as Sakon-shōgen and Shuri-daibu, he served a lady in the court of Emperor Fushimi, who reigned from 1287 to 1298. One of his waka poems entered the Gyokuyō Wakashū, and he is counted the ancestor of the Ōgigayatsu Uesugi line.
zh: 上杉重显（生卒年不详）是日本镰仓时代的武将，上杉赖重的嫡男。其弟有赖成、宪房，妹妹清子是足利贞氏的侧室、足利尊氏的生母，因此室町幕府初代将军尊氏是他的外甥。他通称左近将监、修理大夫，曾侍奉伏见天皇（1287—1298年在位）宫中的女官；他的一首和歌被收入《玉叶和歌集》，并被视为扇谷上杉氏的远祖。

en: Uesugi Shigefusa was a mid-Kamakura court noble turned warrior and the founder of the Uesugi clan. The second son of the minor Kyoto official Fujiwara no Kiyofusa, he went down to Kamakura in 1252 in the retinue of the new shōgun Prince Munetaka and was granted the Uesugi manor in Ikaruga District, Tanba Province, from which he took his family name. When the prince was sent back to Kyoto in 1266, Shigefusa stayed, took up arms in shogunal service, and later served Ashikaga Yasuuji; his daughter, or possibly his sister, married Ashikaga Yoriuji and bore the clan head Ietoki.
zh: 上杉重房是镰仓时代中期由公家转为武家的人物，为上杉氏之祖。他是京都下级官员藤原清房的次子，1252年随新任将军宗尊亲王一行东下镰仓，受领丹波国何鹿郡上杉庄，此后以上杉为姓。1266年宗尊亲王被送回京都，重房留在镰仓，转为武士出仕幕府，后侍奉足利泰氏；其女或其妹嫁与足利赖氏，生下足利氏当主家时。

en: A daughter of Uesugi Shigefusa, founder of the Uesugi clan, she married the Kozuke warrior Yamana Masauji and was the mother of Yamana Tokiuji, who made the Yamana the leading warrior house of the San'in region.
zh: 她是上杉氏始祖上杉重房之女，嫁给上野国武将山名政氏，生子山名时氏；时氏后来使山名氏成为山阴地区首屈一指的武家。

en: Uesugi Shigeyoshi (died 28 January 1350) was a late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era warrior, a cousin of Ashikaga Takauji.
