Adopted into the Uesugi from a court-noble family, he joined the Kantō guard at Kamakura in 1334. The Taiheiki says he forged an imperial order to push a hesitant Takauji into battle at Takenoshita in 1335, and he followed him to Kyushu. As shugo of Izu and an aide to Ashikaga Tadayoshi he opposed Kō no Moronao; after their 1349 showdown he was exiled to Echizen and killed there early in 1350. His descendants became the Takuma Uesugi.
zh: 上杉重能（？—1350年1月28日）是日本镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将、官人，足利尊氏的表弟。他出身公卿之家，被母族上杉氏收养，1334年作为关东廂番的一员下向镰仓。《太平记》记载，1335年竹之下之战时，他伪造纶旨，促使犹豫不决的尊氏出阵，随后又随尊氏西走九州。室町幕府成立后他出任伊豆国守护，作为足利直义的亲信与高师直对立；1349年政争失败后被流放越前，1350年初在当地遇害。其后人称宅间上杉氏。

en: Uesugi Shigeyuki (1322–1338) was a Nanboku-chō warrior and third son of Uesugi Shigeaki. On the fifteenth day of the third month of 1338 he fell fighting beside Uesugi Norifuji at the Wataribe River in Shinano, aged seventeen.
zh: 上杉重行（1322—1338）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉重显的第三子。1338年3月15日，他在信浓国渡部川与上杉宪藤并肩作战时战死，年仅17岁。

en: Uesugi Tomofusa (1335–c. 1391) was the second head of the Inukake Uesugi line and a Kantō kanrei. His father Uesugi Norifuji fell in 1338, so he and his brother Tomomune were raised by a retainer; Uesugi Tomosada also acted as their guardian and may have adopted them. Appointed shugo of Tajima in 1349, Kazusa in 1364 and Shinano in 1366, he helped crush the Musashi Heikki rising in 1368 and was made Kantō kanrei jointly with Uesugi Yoshinori to support young Ashikaga Ujimitsu. He campaigned in Shinano in 1369 against Prince Muneyoshi and against the Nitta in 1370, and later withdrew to Kyoto, dying around 1391.
zh: 上杉朝房（1335—约1391）是日本南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，犬悬上杉氏第二代当主，曾任室町幕府关东管领及上总、信浓等国守护。父亲上杉宪藤1338年战死后，他与弟弟朝宗由家臣抚育；上杉朝定也曾监护他们，并可能收养了他们。他1349年任但马守护，1364年任上总守护，1366年任信浓守护，1368年协助平定武藏平一揆，随后与上杉能宪同任关东管领，辅佐年幼的镰仓公方足利氏满。1369年他出兵信浓攻击宗良亲王，1370年与新田氏交战，之后退住京都，约1391年在那里去世。

en: Uesugi Tomomune (c. 1337–1414) was head of the Inukake Uesugi and Kantō kanrei to the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Ujimitsu and Mitsukane. After his father Norifuji fell in 1338, he and his brother Tomofusa were raised by the retainer Ishikawa Kakudō. He held Kazusa from 1370 and led the Kamakura forces through all three campaigns of the 1380–1382 Oyama Yoshimasa revolt, taking Nantaiyama Castle in 1388. In 1395 he succeeded Uesugi Norikata as Kantō kanrei and Musashi shugo, resigning in 1405. After Mitsukane died in 1409 he retired to the Taizō-ji in Kazusa, and died there in 1414 aged seventy-six.
zh: 上杉朝宗（约1337—1414）是日本南北朝至室町时代前期的武将、守护大名，犬悬上杉氏当主，先后侍奉镰仓公方足利氏满、足利满兼两代。父亲上杉宪藤1338年战死后，他与兄长朝房由家臣石川觉道抚育。他1370年起领有上总，1380至1382年小山义政之乱中三度出任讨伐军大将，1388年攻落男体山城。1395年他继上杉宪方之后就任关东管领兼武藏守护，1405年辞任。1409年满兼死后，他退住上总国胎藏寺，1414年在寺中去世，终年76岁。

en: Uesugi Tomosada (1321–1352) headed the Futabashi branch of the Uesugi clan and served as shugo of Tango Province. After his father Shigeaki died young, he was protected by his aunt Uesugi Kiyoko, mother of Ashikaga Takauji and Tadayoshi, and served the brothers. In 1337, aged seventeen, he became Tango shugo and hikitsuke tōnin, and in 1344 the first head of the Naidan board. In the Kannō Disturbance he took Tadayoshi's side and acted as his envoy to Takauji in 1351. He died in Shinano in 1352; his adopted heir Akisada founded the Ogigayatsu Uesugi line.
zh: 上杉朝定（1321—1352）是上杉氏二桥家的当主，曾任丹后国守护。父亲上杉重显早逝后，他由姑母上杉清子（足利尊氏、足利直义兄弟之母）庇护，出仕足利兄弟。1337年，17岁的他被任命为丹后守护与引付头人，1344年又成为内谈方首任头人。观应之乱中他站在直义一方，1351年作为直义的使者与尊氏交涉。1352年他死于信浓，养子上杉显定后来定居镰仓扇谷，开创扇谷上杉家。

en: Uesugi Yorinari (died 1346) was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Northern and Southern Courts era, a grandson of Uesugi Shigefusa, the clan's founder. Appointed miumaya-bugyō, he later served as shugodai of Sagami and Tango provinces. He fought across the country in the following of his nephew Ashikaga Takauji, and in January 1338 helped drive Kitabatake Akiie's Southern Court army back from Nara. Through his many sons his bloodline passed into the Ōgigayatsu Uesugi, the Sanuki Nagao and the Hagiwara houses.
zh: 上杉赖成（？—1346）是日本镰仓末期至南北朝时代的武将，上杉氏始祖上杉重房之孙。他先被任命为御厩奉行，后历任相模国、丹后国守护代。他跟随外甥足利尊氏转战各地，1338年1月在奈良击退了北畠显家率领的南朝军队。他子嗣众多，血脉传入扇谷上杉氏、佐贯长尾氏和萩原氏。

en: Uesugi Yorishige was a warrior of the mid-Kamakura period and the second head of the Uesugi clan, born the heir of Uesugi Shigefusa. He deepened his house's ties with the Ashikaga, receiving the character 'yori' in his name from Ashikaga Yoriuji and marrying his daughter Kiyoko to Ashikaga Sadauji; she became the mother of Takauji and Tadayoshi. After the Ashikaga overthrew the Kamakura shogunate in 1333, Yorishige served as their house steward and stood at the centre of government. His son Shigeaki founded the Ōgigayatsu Uesugi line.
zh: 上杉赖重是镰仓时代中期的武士，上杉氏第二代当主，上杉重房的嫡子。他着力加深本族与足利氏的关系：名字中的“赖”字得自足利赖氏，又把女儿清子嫁给足利贞氏，清子后来生下尊氏与直义兄弟。1333年足利氏攻灭镰仓幕府后，赖重出任足利家家宰，居于政务中枢。其子重显成为扇谷上杉氏之祖。

en: Uesugi Yoshinori (1333–1378) was a Nanboku-chō warrior, son of Uesugi Noriaki and adopted heir of Uesugi Shigeyoshi. In the Kannō Disturbance he served Ashikaga Tadayoshi, raising troops in Hitachi in 1350. Defeated at the Sattatōge Pass late the following year, he lost the Izu shugo post but returned to favour after 1362. In 1368 he succeeded his father as head of the Yamanouchi Uesugi and shugo of Kōzuke, and with Uesugi Tomofusa served as Kantō kanrei, guiding the young kubo Ashikaga Ujimitsu. He died in 1378.
zh: 上杉能宪（1333—1378）是日本南北朝时代的武将，上杉宪显之子、上杉重能的养子。观应之乱中他出仕足利直义，1350年在常陆国举兵。次年年末他随直义一方在萨埵峠战败，被没收伊豆守护职，1362年后随父亲复权。1368年父亲死后，他继任山内上杉氏家督与上野守护，并与上杉朝房同任关东管领，辅佐年幼的镰仓公方足利氏满，1378年去世。

en: Unno Hiromichi was a warrior of the Unno clan of Chiisagata District in Shinano Province, named in its genealogies, with his father Shigemichi, as the clan's founder. He was the father of Unno Yukimichi and Yukichika.
zh: 海野广道是信浓国小县郡海野氏的武将，系图把他与父亲重道并列为海野氏之祖。他是海野幸通、幸亲之父。

en: Unno Nagauji (died 1243) was a Kamakura-period head of the Unno clan in Shinano Province, a son of Unno Yukiuji, and is named in genealogies among the ancestors of the Sanada clan. He is said to have served the third shogunal regent, Hōjō Yasutoki. The Shigeno genealogy in the Gunsho Ruijū calls his son Yukiharu 'Sanada Shichirō', the first appearance of the Sanada name in that record, and scholars identify him with the Unno Saemon Tarō named in the Azuma Kagami in 1241.
zh: 海野长氏（？—1243）是镰仓时代信浓国海野氏的当主、海野幸氏之子，系图把他列为真田氏的祖先之一，相传出仕第三代执权北条泰时。《群书类从》所收《信州滋野氏三家系图》把他的儿子幸春记作“真田七郎”，这是“真田”之名在该系图中的首次出现；学者还把《吾妻镜》1241年九月条中的“海野左卫门太郎”比定为长氏。

en: Unno Noriyuki was a son of Unno Yoriyuki, recorded in the Edo-period Shigeno genealogy in the Gunsho Ruijū. Given his dates, scholars sometimes identify him rather than his father as the tonsured Unno leader Shinano-gon-no-kami Nyudō attested in 1329.
zh: 海野则幸是海野赖幸之子，见于江户时代《群书类从》所收的滋野氏系图。按年代推算，也有学者认为1329年文书中出现的出家当主“海野信浓权守入道”其实是则幸，而非其父赖幸。

en: Genealogies name Shigemichi, heir of Shigeno no Norihiro, or his son Hiromichi as the founder of the Unno clan, named after its manor in Chiisagata, Shinano; they also make his second son Michinao the founder of the Nezu clan.
zh: 家谱称滋野则广的嫡子重道或其子广道为海野氏之祖，该氏得名于信浓国小县郡的海野庄；家谱又称重道的次子道直另立祢津氏。

en: Unno Shigeuji was a head of the Unno clan, known only from the Edo-period Shigeno genealogy in the Gunsho Ruijū as a son of Unno Nagauji and father of Yukinao.
zh: 海野茂氏是海野氏当主，仅见于江户时代《群书类从》所收的滋野氏系图，载他是海野长氏之子、海野幸直之父。

en: Unno Yoriyuki was a warrior of the Unno clan, the main line of the Shigeno family in Chiisagata District of Shinano Province. The Edo-period genealogy preserved in the Gunsho Ruijū gives him the court title Shinano no Kami and calls him a great-great-grandson of Unno Yukiuji, with a son named Noriyuki. Modern scholars identify Yoriyuki, or perhaps Noriyuki, with the Unno leader titled Shinano-gon-no-kami Nyudō, who held lands around Aida in 1329. Shigeno warriors fought for Hōjō Tokiyuki in the Nakasendai War of 1335, though Unno participation is conjectural. The same genealogy makes him an ancestor of the Sanada clan.
zh: 海野赖幸是信浓国小县郡滋野氏嫡流海野氏的武将。江户时代《群书类从》所收系图给他记载了“信浓守”的官途，称他是海野幸氏的玄孙，有一子名则幸。现代学者把赖幸（一说则幸）比定为海野氏首领“海野信浓权守入道”：此人1329年领有会田御厨等地。1335年中先代之乱中，滋野一族的武将追随北条时行作战，海野氏参战则只是推测。该系图还把他传为真田氏的祖先。

en: Unno Yukichika (1142–1184) was a Shinano warrior of the Unno clan, the main line of the Shigeno family, and succeeded his elder brother Yukimichi as its head. In the Hōgen War of 1156 he led three hundred cavalry under Minamoto no Yoshitomo. He joined Kiso Yoshinaka's rising in 1181 and fought at Yokotagawara, followed Yoshinaka to Kyoto, and took part in the battles of Mizushima and Hōjūji in 1183; his heir Yukihiro was killed at Mizushima. In early 1184 he fell at the Battle of Awazu with Yoshinaka, and their heads were exposed at Shichijōgawara.
zh: 海野幸亲（1142—1184）是信浓国武将、滋野氏嫡流海野氏的当主，继兄长幸通之后统领一族。1156年保元之乱时，他率三百骑兵投奔源义朝麾下。1181年他响应木曾义仲举兵，参加横田河原之战，随后随义仲上洛，1183年又参加水岛之战和法住寺之战，嫡子幸广在水岛阵亡。1184年初，他与义仲一同战死于粟津之战，首级被悬于七条河原示众。

en: Unno Yukimichi was the eldest son of Unno Hiromichi and an early head of the Unno clan of Chiisagata District in Shinano Province. His younger brother Yukichika succeeded him.
zh: 海野幸通是海野广道的长子、信浓国小县郡海野氏的早期当主，由弟弟幸亲继承家督。

en: Unno Yukinaga was a warrior of the Unno clan and the second son of Unno Yukichika; he was identified with Kakumei and Saibutsu, though a strong view holds that Yukinaga and Kakumei were different people.
zh: 海野幸长是海野氏武将、海野幸亲的次子；有说法将他与觉明、西佛视为同一人，但幸长与觉明为不同人的说法较为有力。

en: Unno Yukinao was a head of the Unno clan, known only from the Edo-period Shigeno genealogy in the Gunsho Ruijū as a son of Unno Shigeuji and father of Unno Yoriyuki.
zh: 海野幸直是海野氏当主，仅见于江户时代《群书类从》所收的滋野氏系图，载他是海野茂氏之子、海野赖幸之父。

en: Unno Yukiuji (born c. 1173), third son of Yukichika, was a Kamakura-period head of the Unno clan. In 1183 he accompanied Kiso Yoshinaka's heir Yoshitaka to Kamakura as a hostage, and when Yoshitaka fled execution the next year he served as his decoy; Yoritomo made him a retainer for his loyalty. Ranked among the Four Kings of Bow and Horse, he took part in the first archery ceremony at Tsurugaoka Hachimangū in 1190, fought in the Wada War of 1213 and the Jōkyū War of 1221, and in 1241 won a land suit against the Takeda in Kōzuke.
zh: 海野幸氏（约1173年生）是镰仓时代海野氏当主、海野幸亲的第三子。1183年，他作为人质随木曾义仲的嫡子义高前往镰仓；次年义高逃亡时，幸氏充当替身助其脱身，源赖朝赞赏他的忠勤，将其收为御家人。他与武田信光等人并称弓马四天王，1190年参加鹤冈八幡宫的弓始仪式，又参加1213年和田合战、1221年承久之乱，1241年在关于上野国领地的边界诉讼中胜诉武田氏。

en: Uno Norikage was an early Kamakura-period Murakami Genji warrior in Harima Province. Genealogies such as the Sonpi Bunmyaku relate that his ancestor Minamoto no Suefusa was exiled to Sayo Manor, where the family settled. During the Kenkyū era of the 1190s Norikage married a daughter of Hōjō Yoshitoki and was appointed jitō of Akamatsu village in Sayo. His heir Ienori took the village's name as his family name and became the first to call himself Akamatsu.
zh: 宇野则景是镰仓时代早期播磨国的村上源氏武士。《尊卑分脉》等家谱记载，其先祖源季房被流放至佐用庄，一族遂在当地定居。建久年间（1190年代），则景娶北条义时之女，被补任为佐用庄赤松村的地头。其嗣子家範以村名为姓氏，首称赤松氏，赤松氏由此发源。

en: Utsunomiya Fuyutsuna, first named Takafusa, was a son of Utsunomiya Sadatsuna of Shimotsuke, reportedly adopted by Utsunomiya Yorifusa of the Buzen Utsunomiya line, and became the seventh head of the Kii clan in Kyushu. He fought for Ashikaga Takauji's Northern Court and was made shugo of Chikugo and Buzen in 1352. He briefly submitted to the Southern Court in 1355, taking the name Fuyutsuna, possibly from a character of Ashikaga Tadafuyu's name, then returned to the north. In 1359 he fought Kikuchi Takemitsu by the Chikugo River and was defeated, after which the Kii clan rapidly declined.
zh: 宇都宫冬纲初名高房，是下野宇都宫贞纲之子，相传被丰前宇都宫氏的宇都宫赖房收为养子，后来成为九州城井氏第七代当主。他初随足利尊氏为北朝效力，1352年受任筑后、丰前守护。1355年他一度归顺南朝，改名冬纲，可能取自足利直冬名字中的一字，不久复归北朝。1359年，他在筑后川畔与菊池武光激战兵败，城井氏由此迅速衰落。

en: Utsunomiya Kagetsuna (1235–1298), seventh head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a gokenin in the mid-Kamakura shogunate. From 1252 he served Shogun Prince Munetaka, and he later rose through the shogunal administration to become governor of Shimotsuke and a member of both the Hikitsuke and Hyōjō councils. In 1283 he issued the Utsunomiya house code, modeled on the Goseibai Shikimoku. As a sworn brother of Adachi Yasumori, he was purged after the 1285 Shimotsuki incident, but returned to office when Taira no Yoritsuna fell in 1293. He died in 1298 aged sixty-four.
zh: 宇都宫景纲（1235—1298）是镰仓时代中期的幕府御家人、宇都宫氏第七代当主。1252年起侍奉将军宗尊亲王，受到重用，后历任下野守、引付众与评定众，在幕政中地位显赫。1283年，他依据《御成败式目》制定了《宇都宫家弘安式条》。他与安达泰盛是义兄弟，因此在1285年的霜月骚动中失势；1293年平赖纲在平禅门之乱中败死后，他才重返幕政。1298年去世，享年64岁。

en: Utsunomiya Kintsuna (1302–1356) was the ninth head of the Utsunomiya clan of Shimotsuke Province. In January 1333, during the Genkō War, he led the Ki and Sei warrior leagues against Kusunoki Masashige at Shitennō-ji in Settsu Province; wary of Kintsuna's military skill, Masashige chose a prolonged contest, while Kintsuna too avoided direct confrontation. After the Kamakura shogunate fell he served Emperor Go-Daigo's Kenmu government, then fought Ashikaga Takauji at Takenoshita in 1335 and later campaigned for the Southern Court under Kitabatake Akiie. He died in 1356, leaving waka poems in the Shinsenzai Wakashū.
zh: 宇都宫公纲（1302—1356）是下野国宇都宫氏第九代当主。1333年1月元弘之乱中，他率纪清两党在摄津国四天王寺对阵楠木正成，正成忌惮其武略而采取持久战，公纲也避免直接交锋。镰仓幕府灭亡后他出仕后醍醐天皇的建武政权，1335年又在竹之下与足利尊氏交战，此后转投南朝，随北畠显家转战各地。他于1356年去世，和歌作品被收入《新续古今和歌集》。

en: Hatta Munetsuna (1086–1162) was a warrior of the late Heian period, counted as the second head of the Utsunomiya clan. Born after the death of his natural father Fujiwara no Kanenaka, he became heir of his mother's husband, the clan founder Fujiwara no Sōen. Calling himself Hatta Gon no Kami, he held Hatta in Hitachi Province, married a daughter of the provincial Taira house, and drew the Haga clan of Moka under his sway, preparing its advance toward Utsunomiya. He died in 1162 aged seventy-seven. A daughter nursed Minamoto no Yoritomo; his heir Tomotsuna made Utsunomiya the clan seat.
zh: 八田宗纲（1086—1162）是平安时代后期的武将，被视为宇都宫氏第二代当主。他是藤原兼仲的遗腹子，后成为宇都宫氏始祖藤原宗圆的养子并继承家业。宗纲自称八田权守，领有常陆国八田，娶常陆大掾平氏之女，并把真冈的芳贺氏收归麾下，为家族向宇都宫发展奠定基础。他于1162年去世，享年77岁。其女曾哺育源赖朝，继承人朝纲则将宇都宫作为家族据点。

en: Utsunomiya Naritsuna (1156–1192) was the fourth head of the Utsunomiya clan in the early Kamakura period. In 1189 he joined the main army of Minamoto no Yoritomo's Ōshū campaign together with his father Tomotsuna; by then his own son Yoritsuna had been given as a foster son to Oyama Tomomitsu. Another son, Tomonari, was adopted into the Shioya house and became the ancestor of that branch. Skilled in waka like his sons, Naritsuna died young in 1192, predeceasing his father.
zh: 宇都宫业纲（1156—1192）是镰仓时代初期的宇都宫氏第四代当主。1189年，他随父朝纲加入源赖朝奥州合战的主力军；此时他的儿子赖纲已被送给小山政光当犹子。另一子朝业入嗣盐谷氏，成为盐谷家的始祖。业纲和后来以和歌闻名的儿子们一样长于歌道，于1192年早于其父去世。

en: Utsunomiya Sadatsuna (1266–1316), eighth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a general of the later Kamakura shogunate. He took his name from Hōjō Sadatoki. During the second Mongol invasion of 1281, the Kōan campaign, the regent Hōjō Tokimune named him commander of some sixty thousand gokenin from the Sanyō and San'in circuits, and he led them to Kyūshū; after the war he joined the Hikitsuke court. In 1305 he helped destroy Hōjō Munekata in the Kagen disturbance, and in 1312 he dedicated a great iron stupa at his late mother's memorial. He died in 1316 aged fifty-one.
zh: 宇都宫贞纲（1266—1316）是镰仓时代中后期的武将、宇都宫氏第八代当主，名字中的“贞”字拜领自北条贞时。1281年元寇弘安之役时，他奉执权北条时宗之命，作为总大将率领山阳、山阴两道约六万御家人出征九州；战后出任引付众。1305年嘉元之乱中，他奉贞时之命协助诛灭北条宗方。1312年，他在亡母十三回忌时供奉了罕见的巨型铁制塔婆。1316年去世，享年51岁。

en: Fujiwara no Sōen (1033–1111) was a late Heian nobleman regarded as the founder of the Utsunomiya clan of Shimotsuke Province. Genealogies make him the second son of Fujiwara no Kanefusa and a great-grandson of the regent Michikane. He served Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and Yoshiie in the Earlier Nine Years' War, earning merit through prayers for victory, and in 1063 was appointed protector of Shimotsuke and bettō of the province's ichinomiya, Futaarayama Shrine. Tradition credits him with building Utsunomiya Castle. He died in the tenth month of 1111, and the genealogies name Hatta Munetsuna as his successor.
zh: 藤原宗圆（1033—1111）是平安时代后期的贵族，被奉为下野国宇都宫氏的初代当主。据《尊卑分脉》等系图，他是藤原兼房的次子、关白藤原道兼的曾孙。前九年之役中，他追随源赖义、义家父子，以调伏凶徒的祈祷之功得到承认，于1063年就任下野国守护职和该国一宫二荒山神社的别当，即宇都宫座主。相传他还修筑了宇都宫城。他于1111年十月去世，系图载八田宗纲继为第二代当主。

en: Utsunomiya Tokitsuna, also called Tokikage, was the eldest son of Utsunomiya Yasumune and a warrior of the late Kamakura period. He inherited the Mumo manor in Hitachi Province and held the titles of Saemon-no-jō and Mikawa-no-kami. His son was Utsunomiya Yasufuji.
zh: 宇都宫时纲又称时景，是宇都宫泰宗的长子、镰仓时代后期武将，继承常陆国武茂庄，曾任左卫门尉、三河守，其子为宇都宫泰藤。

en: Utsunomiya Tomotsuna (1122–1204) was the third head of the Utsunomiya clan and a warrior at the court of the retired emperors in Kyoto. After Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180, Taira no Kiyomori detained him in the capital; only in 1184 was he allowed to join Yoritomo, who confirmed his lands. In the 1189 Ōshū campaign Tomotsuna fought with his son Naritsuna and the clan, and Yoritomo praised him as the finest bowman in Bandō. In 1194 the court ordered him placed in the custody of the provincial government of Bungo for seizing public land; he was pardoned in 1196 and died in 1204 aged eighty-three.
zh: 宇都宫朝纲（1122—1204）是宇都宫氏第三代当主，曾在京都的院厅担任武士。1180年源赖朝举兵后，他被平清盛扣留在京城，直到1184年才获准归附赖朝，本领得到安堵。1189年奥州合战时，朝纲携子业纲率一族从军，被赖朝赞为“坂东第一弓取”。1194年，他因侵占公田被朝廷裁定交丰后国国府收管，1196年获赦，1204年去世，享年83岁。

en: Utsunomiya Ujitsuna (1326–1370) was the tenth head of the Utsunomiya clan and the son of Kintsuna. Unlike his Southern Court father, he took service with Ashikaga Takauji: in the Kannō disturbance of 1351 he defeated the enemy at Naba in Kōzuke and at Ashigara in Sagami, helping decide the victory at the Sattayama Pass. In 1352 he was made shugo of Kōzuke and Echigo, but after falling out with the Kamakura kubō Ashikaga Motouji he lost both posts in 1362. He rebelled again during the Musashi uprising of 1368, surrendered, and died of illness on campaign in Kii in 1370.
zh: 宇都宫氏纲（1326—1370）是宇都宫氏第十代当主，公纲之子。与投身南朝的父亲不同，他出仕足利尊氏，1351年观应之乱中先后在上野那波庄和相模足柄山击败足利直义一方，奠定萨埵峠之战的胜局。1352年他受任上野、越后两国守护，后与镰仓公方足利基氏反目，1362年被剥夺两职。1368年他乘武藏平一揆之机再举反旗，兵败投降，1370年在纪州出阵时病死。

en: Utsunomiya Yasufuji (1302–1352) was a warrior of Shimotsuke Province, son of Mumo Tokitsuna, and a senior retainer of Nitta Yoshisada. In 1335 he fought Ashikaga Takauji at Yamazaki near Kyoto, and in 1336 he fled with Yoshisada to Echizen Province. When Yoshisada was killed at Fujishima in 1338, Yasufuji wandered the country carrying his lord's severed head, then buried it and became a Lotus sect monk named Renjō, settling in Mikawa Province. He died there in 1352. The later Ōkubo clan claimed him as their ancestor.
zh: 宇都宫泰藤（1302—1352）是下野国武将、武茂时纲之子，新田义贞的重臣。1335年，他在京都附近的山崎与足利尊氏交战，1336年随义贞逃往越前国。1338年义贞在藤岛战死后，泰藤携其首级辗转各地，随后将首级安葬并出家，皈依法华宗，法号莲常，定居三河国，于1352年病故。后世的大久保氏奉他为远祖。

en: Utsunomiya Yasumune was a general of the later Kamakura period, a younger son of Utsunomiya Kagetsuna and brother of the clan head Sadatsuna. He first bore the name Morimune, the character given him by Adachi Yasumori, and is thought to have renamed himself after Yasumori's destruction in the Shimotsuki incident of 1285. When Sadatsuna led the shogunal army against the second Mongol invasion in 1281, Yasumune followed him to Kyūshū and held Ōki Castle in Setaka, Chikugo Province, where he also managed a Tokudaiji family manor. His son Tokitsuna inherited Mumo manor in Hitachi Province, while Sadayasu became a land steward in Iyo Province and laid the foundations of the Iyo and later Chikugo Utsunomiya houses.
zh: 宇都宫泰宗是镰仓时代中后期的武将，宇都宫景纲之子、当主贞纲之弟。他初名盛宗，名字拜领自安达泰盛的一字，一般认为在1285年霜月骚动泰盛被诛后改名。1281年第二次元寇弘安之役时，他随贞纲出征九州，以筑后国山门郡濑高的大木城为据点，并以庄官身份管理当地的德大寺家庄园。诸子中，时纲领有常陆国武茂庄，贞泰前往伊予国担任地头，奠定了伊予宇都宫氏及后来筑后宇都宫氏的基础。

en: Utsunomiya Yasutsuna (1202–1260), sixth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a senior councillor of the Kamakura shogunate and a waka poet. The son of Yoritsuna by a daughter of Hōjō Tokimasa, he took his name from his cousin Hōjō Yasutoki. In 1238 he accompanied Shogun Kujō Yoritsune to Kyoto and became governor of Shimotsuke, and in 1243 he joined the Hyōjōshū council, on which he served until his death; he later held the shugo post of Mino. Fujiwara no Teika praised his verse, many of his poems entering the Gyokuyō Wakashū. He died in Kyoto in 1260, aged fifty-nine.
zh: 宇都宫泰纲（1202—1260）是宇都宫氏第六代当主、镰仓幕府重臣，也是和歌歌人。他是赖纲与北条时政之女所生，元服时拜领母方表兄北条泰时的偏讳“泰”字，得名泰纲。1238年随将军九条赖经上洛，任下野守；1243年进入评定众，直到去世都参与幕政，后又兼任美浓国守护。藤原定家称赞他的和歌“得骨”，《玉叶和歌集》收录其多首作品。1260年在京都去世，享年59岁。

en: Utsunomiya Yoritsuna (c. 1178–1259), fifth head of the Utsunomiya clan, was a Kamakura gokenin and noted waka poet. Fostered to Oyama Tomomitsu, he fought in the Ōshū campaign of 1189 and around 1204 became shugo of Iyo Province. In 1205, suspected in the Makishi plot against Shogun Sanetomo, he took vows as Rensei and retired to Ogura in Kyoto, studying Pure Land teachings under Shōkū. A close friend of Fujiwara no Teika, he married a daughter to Teika's son Tameie and made the Utsunomiya circle a third center of court poetry. He died in Kyoto in 1259 aged eighty-two.
zh: 宇都宫赖纲（约1178—1259）是宇都宫氏第五代当主、镰仓御家人，也是著名歌人。他成为小山政光的犹子，1189年参加奥州合战，约1204年出任伊予国守护。1205年，他因涉嫌卷入牧氏谋害将军源实朝的阴谋而出家，法名莲生，隐居京都小仓，随证空修习净土宗教义。他与藤原定家交谊深厚，把女儿嫁给定家之子为家，使宇都宫歌坛成为与京都、镰仓并列的和歌中心。1259年在京都去世，享年82岁。

en: Wachi no Morozane was a head of the Wachi clan, local warriors of Mitaki District in Bingo Province whose houses, together with the Eda and other kindred families, were known as the Hirosawa-shū. During the Nanboku-chō wars the Wachi first served Ashikaga Tadafuyu when he based himself in Bingo. In 1365 the shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiakira ordered Yamauchi Michitsugu and Yano Kōzuke no Suke to suppress Morozane at Hiramatsu Castle. By 1367 Yoshiakira had ordered Michitsugu to join Morozane against Yano and Ōta Bizen.
zh: 和智师实是备后国三谿郡国人领主和智氏的当主；和智氏与江田氏等同族诸家并称“广泽众”。南北朝动乱中，和智氏起初投身以备后为据点的足利直冬麾下。1365年，将军足利义诠命山内通继与矢野上野介镇压据守平松城的师实。到1367年，义诠已命通继与师实联手讨伐矢野及太田备前。

en: Wachi no Sanenari was a Kamakura-period warrior of Bingo province, son of Hirosawa Sanemura, whose family had held twelve villages of Mitaki District since 1192 for service at the Battle of Fujito. He divided his father's lands equally with his elder brother Sanetsuna, took Wachi Manor as his share and adopted the name Wachi, while Sanetsuna's line became the Eda. In Kangen 1 (1302) the former court lady Go-Fukakusain no Nijō, returning at the end of the year from a pilgrimage to Itsukushima, lodged first at Sanenari's house and then at his brother's, nearly driving the brothers to fight until their cousin Hirosawa Yukizane mediated.
zh: 和智实成是镰仓时代备后国的武士，广泽实村之子；其家因藤户之战的军功于1192年获赐备后国三谿郡十二乡。他与兄长实纲平分父亲遗领，自取和智庄，遂以和智（和知）为苗字，实纲一脉则称江田氏。乾元元年（1302年），已出宫的后深草院二条参拜安艺国严岛神社后，于年末归途中寄寓实成的居馆，随后又转往其兄实纲处，几乎引发兄弟交战，经二人的堂兄、广泽氏惣领行实仲裁方告平息。

en: Wachi no Sukesane was a head of the Wachi clan, local warriors of Mitaki District in Bingo Province. The clan descended from Kanto gokenin of the Hirosawa family, installed as jitō of Wachi Manor after the founding of the Kamakura shogunate, and took its name from the manor. During the Nanboku-chō period, Sukesane moved his seat to Kisa, after which the clan made Nantenzan Castle on Mount Nanten above the town its seat.
zh: 和智资实是备后国三谿郡国人领主和智氏的当主。和智氏原为关东御家人广泽氏，镰仓幕府成立后作为地头迁入备后国三谿郡和智庄，遂以庄名为苗字。南北朝时代，资实将据点迁往吉舍，此后和智氏以吉舍街市上方南天山上的南天山城为居城。

en: Wada Kenkai (died 1348), called Wada Shinbōchi in contemporary records, was a Southern Court warrior of the Wada family, a Kusunoki cadet house of Kawachi Province. Kusunoki genealogies make him a son of Kusunoki Masasue, younger brother of Kusunoki Masashige. He may be the same man as Wada Masaoki, who answered Kitabatake Akiie's rising and attacked Tange and Matsubara castles in Ise in 1338. He later followed the Kusunoki leader Masatsura and fell at the Battle of Shijōnawate on 4 February 1348, dying beside his lord.
zh: 和田贤快（？—1348）在当时的记载中多称“和田新発意”，是南朝武将，出身于河内国和田氏，即楠木氏的同族分家。楠木氏系图相传他是楠木正成之弟正季之子。一说他就是1338年响应北畠显家起兵、攻打伊势国丹下城和松原城的和田正兴。此后他追随楠木氏当主楠木正行，1348年2月4日在四条畷之战中与主君一同战死。

en: Waga Ieyuki, a son of Oniyanagi Mitsuyoshi of the Waga clan, lost his inheritance in a shogunal ruling for his brother Noriyoshi after their father was murdered in 1297.
zh: 和贺家行是和贺氏庶流鬼柳光义之子，1297年父亲遇害后，幕府在遗产争讼中裁定其兄宪义胜诉，否定了他的继承权。

en: Waga Mitsukage, heir of Oniyanagi Mitsuyoshi of the Waga clan, lost his inheritance when the shogunate ruled for his brother Noriyoshi in a dispute following their father's murder in 1297.
zh: 和贺光景是和贺氏庶流鬼柳光义的嫡子，1297年父亲遇害后，他与弟弟宪义争夺遗产，幕府裁定宪义胜诉，否定了他的继承权。

en: Waga Mitsuyoshi was, by the Oniyanagi genealogy, an illegitimate son of Yasuyoshi, third head of the Waga clan of Waga district in Mutsu; granted Oniyanagi in modern Kitakami, he founded the Oniyanagi branch.
zh: 据鬼柳氏系图，和贺光义是陆奥国和贺郡和贺氏宗家第三代当主泰义的庶子，受封鬼柳（在今岩手县北上市），为鬼柳氏之祖。

en: Waga Moriyoshi appears in the Oniyanagi genealogy as the son of Yasuyoshi and father of Nagayoshi; a genealogy of the Hondō clan of Dewa, which claimed descent from the Waga and the Seiwa Genji, instead names him as son of Yukiyoshi and father of Yoshiharu.
zh: 鬼柳文书系图列和贺盛义为泰义之子、长义之父；自称出自和贺氏庶流、系承清和源氏的出羽本堂氏系图则将他列为行义之子、义治之父。

en: Waga Motoyoshi was a warrior of the Waga clan, the local lords of Waga district in Mutsu province; a later regional chronicle, the Ōnan rakuhōshū, styles him Satsuma no kami. It records that in Kannō 3 (1352) the Northern Court shogun Ashikaga Takauji granted him three villages in the Yamamoto district of Dewa province, Yasumoto, Ajōji and Unjigarinosato. The Hondō clan of Semboku later traced its settlement in Dewa to this grant.
zh: 和贺基义是盘踞陆奥国和贺郡的和贺一族武士，后世地志《奥南落穗集》称他曾任萨摩守。该书记载，观应三年（1352年），北朝将军足利尊氏将出羽国山本郡的安本、阿条字、云志贺里三乡赐予他。后来仙北地方的本堂氏，便把家族定居出羽追溯到这次赐地。

en: Waga Nagayoshi was a member of the Waga clan of Mutsu province; a genealogy in the Oniyanagi documents names him as the son of Moriyoshi and styles him provisional governor of Satsuma.
zh: 和贺长义是陆奥国和贺一族成员，《鬼柳文书》所收系谱称他是盛义之子，官为萨摩权守。

en: Waga Noriyoshi, a son of Oniyanagi Mitsuyoshi of the Waga clan, won a shogunal ruling granting him his father's lands after Mitsuyoshi was murdered in 1297 and his brothers' claims were challenged.
zh: 和贺宪义是和贺氏庶流鬼柳光义之子，1297年光义遇害后，他质疑兄弟的继承主张，幕府裁定将父亲的遗产全部交给他。

en: Waga Tokikazu was a member of the Waga clan of Mutsu province; a clan genealogy names him as a son of Mitsuyoshi and the father of Yoshikazu.
zh: 和贺时顺是陆奥国和贺一族成员，家族系图称他是光义之子、义顺之父。

en: Waga Yasuyoshi was the third head of the Waga clan main line, jitō lords of Waga district in Mutsu, seated at Iwasaki in Kuroiwa; his illegitimate son Mitsuyoshi was enfeoffed at Oniyanagi in modern Kitakami.
zh: 和贺泰义是陆奥国和贺郡地头和贺氏宗家的第三代当主，据点在黑岩的岩崎；他的庶子光义领有鬼柳（在今岩手县北上市）。

en: Waga Yoshiyuki, first called Katta Saburō Saemonnojō, founded the Waga clan of Mutsu province. Genealogies kept by his descendants the Oniyanagi house make him the son of Karita Yoshisue, a Kamakura gokenin of the Chūjō line enfeoffed in Katta district, and the Azuma Kagami names him on the first day of Jōei 3 (1232). During the Jōkyū era of 1219 to 1222 he entered Waga district as jitō of half its lands, took the name Waga and seated his main line at Iwasaki in Kuroiwa, now Kitakami; his third son Kageyuki fathered the Susumago branch.
zh: 和贺义行初称刈田三郎左卫门尉，是陆奥国和贺氏的始祖。其庶流鬼柳家所传系图称，他是受封刈田郡的镰仓御家人、中条流苅田义季之子；《吾妻镜》贞永三年（1232年）正月一日条载有其名。承久年间（1219—1222年），他以半郡地头身份进入和贺郡，改称和贺氏，把宗家据点设在黑岩的岩崎，即今岩手县北上市；其三男景行为庶家须孙氏之祖。

en: Washizu Chikamori was the legitimate son and heir of Washizu Moriyasu, founder of the Washizu branch of the Ōuchi in Suo Province. He died without a male successor, and his daughter Zen'eni continued the line by adopting an heir from the main Ōuchi house.
zh: 鹫头亲盛是周防国鹫头氏始祖鹫头盛保的嫡男与继承人。他死后没有男性继承人，其女禅惠尼从大内氏宗家迎立养子，使鹫头氏的家名得以延续。

en: Washizu Moriyasu, also called Saburō, was the third son of Ōuchi Morifusa of Suo Province. He took the Washizu Manor in Tsuno District as his holding and adopted its name to found the Washizu, a cadet branch of the Ōuchi house.
zh: 鹫头盛保又名三郎，是周防国武士大内盛房的第三子。他以周防国都浓郡鹫头庄为领地，并以地名为姓，创立了大内氏的庶流鹫头氏。

en: Nagahiro Washizu was a Japanese warlord and shugo lord of the late Kamakura and Southern and Northern Courts period, born to Ōuchi Hiroie. The Washizu house, a branch of the Ōuchi based at Washizu Manor in Tsuno District, Suō Province, had no heir, so the nun Zen'ni adopted him as its successor. In 1333 Emperor Go-Daigo appointed him shugo of Suō after the Kamakura shogunate fell, replacing Ōuchi Hiroyuki, who had supported the shogunate. In February 1336 he fought for Ashikaga Takauji against the imperial army at Hyōgo in Settsu, and ruled the Ōuchi as Buzen no Kami. After his death, his second son Hironao inherited the Suō shugo post.
zh: 鹫头长弘是日本镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将、守护大名，本为大内弘家之子。鹫头氏是大内氏的分支，因领有周防国都浓郡鹫头庄而得名；宗家后继无人，一族的禅惠尼便收他为养子作为继承人。1333年镰仓幕府灭亡后，后醍醐天皇任命他为周防守护，取代依附幕府的大内弘幸。1336年2月，他在摄津国兵库为足利尊氏与官军作战，此后以丰前守的身份作为大内氏总领统辖全族。他死后由次子弘直继任周防守护。

en: Zen'eni, a Buddhist nun and daughter of Washizu Chikamori, adopted Ōuchi Hiroie's son Nagahiro from the main Ōuchi house as heir to the Washizu after her father died without a successor.
zh: 禅惠尼是鹫头亲盛之女，也是一位尼僧；父亲去世后没有继承人，她从大内氏宗家迎立大内弘家之子长弘为养子，继承鹫头家门。

en: Nagoya no Sazuke was a son of the Heian warrior Watanabe no Tsuna, born at Nagoya in Hizen Province around 990–995. Matsuura family genealogies make him the father of Takiguchi Yasushi and grandfather of Matsuura no Hisashi, founder of the Hizen Matsuura clan.
zh: 奈古屋授是平安时代武将渡边纲之子，约生于990—995年。据松浦氏家谱，他生于肥前国奈古屋，子为泷口泰，孙松浦久被奉为肥前松浦氏之祖。

en: Watanabe no Tsuna (953–1025) was a warrior of mid-Heian Japan, descended from Emperor Saga through the Saga Genji. Born after his father Minamoto no Atsuru's death in Musashi Province, he was adopted by Minamoto no Atsushi and settled at Watanabe in Settsu, taking that place as his surname and becoming ancestor of the Watanabe clan. He served Minamoto no Yorimitsu (Raikō) as foremost of his Four Heavenly Kings, and in 1020 received senior fifth rank and the governorship of Tango. Tales credit him with helping slay Shuten-dōji and severing Ibaraki-dōji's arm at Kyoto's Modoribashi bridge with the blade Higekiri.
zh: 渡边纲（953—1025）是日本平安时代中期武将，出自嵯峨源氏，为嵯峨天皇后裔。他生于武藏国，是源宛的遗腹子，后被源敦收为养子，移居摄津国渡边，遂以渡边为姓，成为渡边氏之祖。他出仕源赖光，位列赖光四天王之首，1020年叙正五位下、任丹后守。相传他曾随源赖光剿灭大江山的酒吞童子，并在京都一条戻桥以名刀髭切斩下茨木童子的一臂。

en: Watanabe no Yasushi, also called Takiguchi Yasushi, was a member of the Saga Genji, son of Watanabe no Sazuke and father of Matsuura no Hisashi, who in 1069 became steward of the Uno estate in Hizen and founded the Matsuura clan.
zh: 渡边泰，一称泷口泰，是嵯峨源氏的一员，渡边授之子、松浦久之父；松浦久于1069年出任肥前国宇野御厨庄官，成为松浦氏之祖。

en: Yabe Tomotsuna was a local lord of the Yabe clan in Inaba Province, recorded in 1340 when he seized the Chiji estate; he is also known to have held land at Tomiki in Hōmi district.
zh: 矢部纶纲是因幡国矢部氏的国人领主，史料记载他于1340年（历应三年）押领因幡国千土师乡，并在法美郡富木乡拥有领地。

en: Yabe Zenni (1187–1256) was a daughter of Miura clan leader Yoshimura. Around 1200 she married Hōjō Yasutoki, future third regent of the Kamakura shogunate, and bore his heir Tokiuji before the couple divorced. She then married Sahara Moritsura, bearing three sons, Mitsumori, Moritoki and Tokitsura; after his death she returned to her Yabe estate, took vows and the religious name Zen'a, and became known as Yabe Zenni. Her grandson Hōjō Tokiyori became the fifth regent. In the Hōji Conflict of 1247 her sons sided with the Hōjō, and Moritoki later revived the Miura name. When she died in 1256, Tokiyori mourned fifty days.
zh: 矢部禅尼（1187—1256）是三浦氏当主三浦义村之女。约1200年她嫁给后来成为镰仓幕府第三代执权的北条泰时，生下继承人北条时氏，后与泰时离异，改嫁佐原盛连，生有光盛、盛时、时连三子。盛连死后她回到矢部乡出家，法名禅阿，称矢部禅尼。她的孙子北条时赖成为第五代执权；1247年宝治合战时诸子站在北条一方，盛时后来恢复三浦之姓，再兴三浦家。1256年她去世，时赖为祖母服丧五十日。

en: Yamana Masauji was a warrior of the late Kamakura and Nanboku-cho periods, son of Yamana Yoshitoshi and head of a Yamana branch of the Nitta clan in Kozuke. When Nitta Yoshisada marched against Ashikaga Takauji in 1335, Masauji refused to follow the Nitta main line and sided instead with the Ashikaga, kinsmen of his wife, a daughter of Uesugi Shigefusa. After the Muromachi bakufu was founded in 1336 he went on serving Takauji. The family headship later passed to his son Yamana Tokiuji.
zh: 山名政氏是镰仓时代末期至南北朝时代的武将，山名义俊之子，身为上野国新田氏一族山名氏的当主。1335年新田义贞举兵讨伐足利尊氏时，政氏没有追随新田宗家，而是投奔妻子的亲族足利氏——其妻是上杉重房之女。1336年室町幕府成立后，他继续侍奉尊氏。家督之位后来由儿子山名时氏继承。

en: Yamana Moroyoshi (1328–1376) was the eldest son of Yamana Tokiuji and shugo of Tango, Hoki and Tajima. He served in the 1341 campaign against Enya Takasada and fought Kusunoki Masatsura in 1347. When Tokiuji defected to the Southern Court during the Kanno disturbance, Moroyoshi stayed with the Northern Court, fighting beside Ashikaga Yoshiakira at Yawata in 1352; he later rejoined his father, submitting with him in 1363 and inheriting Tango and Hoki. He became clan head in 1371 and built Utsubuki-yama Castle in Hoki. He died in 1376 aged 49; his eldest son was sickly and his other sons were young, so his brother Tokiyoshi succeeded him, contributing to a Yamana family feud.
zh: 山名师义（1328—1376）是山名时氏的嫡男，丹后、伯耆、但马三国守护。他参加了1341年讨伐盐冶高贞之役和1347年与楠木正行的战斗。观应之扰乱中，父亲时氏转投南朝，师义却留在北朝，1352年在八幡之战中随足利义诠作战；后来他与父亲合流，1363年一同归顺幕府，领有丹后与伯耆。1371年他继任家督，在伯耆修筑打吹山城。1376年他以49岁去世，因嫡男病弱、其他儿子年幼而由弟弟时义继位，成为山名一族内讧的原因之一。

en: Yamana Shigekuni was an early Kamakura-period warrior and gokenin of the Yamana clan of Yamana township in Kōzuke Province, born the son of Yamana Yoshisada. In October 1185 he rode among the mounted retainers who attended Minamoto no Yoritomo at the dedication of Shōchōju-in, the temple Yoritomo had founded to mourn his father Minamoto no Yoshitomo, taking sixth place in the seven ranks of attendants. His son Yamana Shigemura succeeded him as head of the family.
zh: 山名重国是镰仓时代初期的武士、御家人，属上野国山名乡的山名氏，为山名义节之子。1185年10月，源赖朝为追荐父亲源义朝而建的胜长寿院举行落成供养，重国以随兵身份出席，位列七列随兵中的第六列。家督后来由其子山名重村继承。

en: Yamana Shigemura was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yamana clan in Kōzuke Province and a son of Yamana Shigekuni, whose family headship he inherited. Genealogies make his line the clan's main branch and count him as the great-great-grandfather of the later shugo daimyō Yamana Tokiuji.
zh: 山名重村是上野国山名氏的镰仓时代武士，山名重国之子，继承了父亲的家督。谱系以他这一支为山名氏嫡流，后来的守护大名山名时氏是他的玄孙。

en: Yamana Tokiuji (c. 1303–1371) was a Nanboku-cho shugo lord of the Yamana clan. He joined Ashikaga Takauji's break with Emperor Go-Daigo and fought at the Minatogawa in 1336, becoming shugo of Hoki in 1337 and winning Tango, Izumo and Oki after the 1341 campaign against Enya Takasada. During the Kanno disturbance he changed sides repeatedly, briefly occupying Kyoto with Southern Court armies in 1353 and 1354. He submitted to the Muromachi bakufu in 1363 with his sons, receiving Hoki and Tamba and a seat on the hikitsuke court. By his death in 1371 the Yamana held five provinces.
zh: 山名时氏（约1303—1371）是南北朝时代山名氏的守护大名。他追随足利尊氏与后醍醐天皇决裂，参加1336年的凑川之战，1337年就任伯耆守护，1341年讨伐盐冶高贞后又得到丹后、出云、隐岐三国。观应之扰乱中他数度倒戈，曾在1353年和1354年随南朝军两度攻占京都。1363年他率诸子归顺室町幕府，领有伯耆、丹波两国并出任引付头人。到1371年去世时，山名氏已坐拥五国守护之职。

en: Yamana Yoshinaga was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yamana clan of Kōzuke Province. In the Yamana genealogy he is listed among the clan heads, as a son of Yamana Shigemura and the father of Yamana Yoshitoshi.
zh: 山名义长是上野国山名氏的镰仓时代武士。在山名氏当主谱系中，他是山名重村之子、山名义俊之父，列于重村之后、义俊之前。

en: Yamana Yoshinori (died 1219) was a Kamakura-period samurai lord and founder of the Yamana clan. A son born to a concubine of Nitta Yoshishige of the Seiwa Genji, he held Yamana township in Usui District, Kōzuke Province, from which he took his name, and around 1175 founded the Yamana Hachiman shrine. When Minamoto no Yoritomo rose in 1180 Yoshinori joined him at once, unlike his hesitant father. He fought in the Genpei War, served under Minamoto no Yoshitsune in 1184, was made governor of Izu Province in 1185, and joined the Ōshū campaign of 1189. In 1195 he accompanied Yoritomo to Kyoto.
zh: 山名义范（？—1219）是镰仓时代的武将，山名氏之祖。他是清和源氏新田义重的庶子，领有上野国碓冰郡山名乡，遂以山名为姓，约1175年创建山名八幡宫。1180年源赖朝举兵，与迟疑观望的父亲不同，义范立即驰赴其麾下。他参与源平合战，1184年随源义经西征追讨平氏，1185年就任伊豆守，1189年从军奥州之战。1195年随赖朝上洛。

en: Yamana Yoshisada was an early Kamakura-period warrior of the Yamana clan of Yamana township in Kōzuke Province. He was a son of the clan founder Yamana Yoshinori, and his own son Yamana Shigekuni succeeded as head of the family.
zh: 山名义节是镰仓时代初期的山名氏武士，世居上野国山名乡。他是山名氏始祖山名义范之子，其子山名重国后来继承家督。

en: Yamana Yoshitada (1337–c. 1408), second son of Yamana Tokiuji, was shugo of Mimasaka and Kii. He took the Mimasaka post from his brother Tokiyoshi in 1366 and in 1378 helped crush Hashimoto Shotoku's rising in Kii, adding Kii. In 1391 his brother Ujikiyo and nephew Mitsuyuki rebelled against Ashikaga Yoshimitsu in the Meitoku War; Yoshitada gave only hesitant assent and never left Kii, yet after the defeat the shogun confiscated both his provinces. In 1392 Ouchi Yoshihiro drove him to Yura harbour, where he took vows with seventeen kinsmen. Pardoned around 1406, he briefly served as shugo of Iwami.
zh: 山名义理（1337—约1408）是山名时氏的次子，美作、纪伊两国守护。1366年他接替弟弟时义任美作守护，1378年出兵镇压纪伊的桥本正督叛乱，又兼任纪伊守护。1391年明德之乱中，弟弟氏清与侄子满幸举兵反抗足利义满，义理虽被说服却始终没有从纪伊出兵；乱后两国仍被没收。1392年大内义弘攻入纪伊，他逃到由良凑，与十七名族人一同出家。约1406年他获赦免，一度出任石见守护。

en: Yamana Yoshitoshi was a late Kamakura-period warrior of the Yamana clan of Kōzuke Province. He is recorded as a son of Yamana Yoshinaga and the father of Yamana Masauji, whose own son Yamana Tokiuji rose to be a shugo daimyō.
zh: 山名义俊是上野国山名氏镰仓时代后期的武士，山名义长之子、山名政氏之父。政氏之子山名时氏后来成为守护大名。

en: Yamashiro Hiroshi, a Kamakura-period head of the Hizen Yamashiro and a son of its founder Yamashiro Kakoi, was the adopted heir of Gen'en; his own son Yamashiro Kai fell fighting the Mongol invasion in 1274.
zh: 山代广是镰仓时代肥前山代氏的首领，山代氏始祖山代围之子，源圆的养子；其子山代阶在1274年的元日战争中战死。

en: Yamashiro Hiroshi was a leader of the Yamashiro house, a branch of the Matsuura warrior bands of Hizen Province in northern Kyūshū. In 1337 Ashikaga Tadayoshi confirmed his stewardship of Yamashiro and other lands in the Uno estate. In 1350 Hiroshi transferred lands including Yamashiro to his eldest son Tsutomu. During the wars of the Northern and Southern Courts he took the Northern Court side with his kinsmen of the Matsuura party, and in 1359 he fought at the Battle of the Chikugo River, also called the Battle of Ōbaru, in the army of Shōni Yorihisa.
zh: 山代弘是山代氏的首领。山代氏是九州北部肥前国松浦党武士团的一支。1337年，足利直义安堵了他在宇野御厨的山代等地的地头职。1350年，弘将包括山代在内的领地让给嫡子勤。南北朝动乱时，山代弘与松浦党的同族一同站在北朝一方，1359年在北朝武将少贰赖尚的麾下参加了筑后川之战，又称大保原之战。

en: Yamashiro Kai was a Kamakura warrior of the Yamashiro house, a Matsuura band of Hizen Province in northern Kyūshū, and son of the house head Yamashiro Hiroshi. During the Mongol invasions of Japan, he served in the Matsuura contingent alongside Sashi Fusa, the sōryō of the Matsuura bands, and fell in battle against the invaders.
zh: 山代阶是镰仓时代武将，出身九州北部肥前国松浦党的支族山代氏，山代氏首领山代广之子。蒙古入侵日本时，他作为松浦党一员，与松浦党惣领佐志房并肩作战，在与元军的交战中战死。

en: Yamashiro Kakoi was a warrior of the late Heian period and the founder of the Yamashiro house, a branch of the Matsuura bands of Hizen Province. The sixth son of Matsuura Nao, a Junior Fifth Rank officer of the palace guards who held the Mikuriya manor, he established his family at Yamashiro in Matsuura District with his base in Kanzaki District, backing the Saga Genji warrior Minamoto no Mitsusue when he came down as steward of the Kanzaki manor. His son Gen'en inherited the Kamachi lands in Chikugo after 1221, while another son, Hiroshi, carried on the Yamashiro line.
zh: 山代围是平安时代末期的武将，肥前国松浦党支族山代氏的始祖。他是从五位兵卫尉、领有御厨庄的松浦直之第六子，在松浦郡山代地方起家，以神埼郡为据点；嵯峨源氏武将源满末作为庄官下向鸟羽院领神埼庄时，即以山代氏的武力为后盾。其子源圆于1221年承久之乱后继承筑后国蒲池氏的遗领，另一子山代广则延续山代氏一脉。

en: Yamashiro Katashi, also recorded as Minamoto no Tsubura or Gen'en, was an early Kamakura warrior and the third son of Yamashiro Kakoi, founder of the Hizen Yamashiro. After the Jōkyū War of 1221 he married a daughter of the Kamachi family of Chikugo Province and received its hereditary lands, becoming the ancestor of the Matsuura-party Kamachi clan. He had no son of his own, so the Yamashiro house passed to his nephew and adopted heir Hiroshi, while the Kamachi line was continued by Kamachi Hisauji.
zh: 山代固又记作源圆，是镰仓时代前期武将，肥前山代氏始祖山代围的第三子。1221年承久之乱后，他入赘筑后国蒲池氏，娶其家之女并继承遗领，成为松浦党蒲池氏的始祖。他没有亲生儿子，山代氏由其侄兼养子山代广继承；蒲池家则由蒲池久氏接续。

en: Yamashiro Sakai was a Hizen Province gokenin of the Yamashiro house, one of the Matsuura warrior bands of northern Kyūshū. In the Kōan campaign of the Mongol invasions, on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month of 1281, he fought in the Japanese assault on the Mongol Eastern Route Army on Iki Island, in a host of tens of thousands led by the Matsuura, Sonogi and Takagi bands and the Ryūzōji. For his distinguished service there he received a letter of commendation from Hōjō Tokisada, shugo of Hizen.
zh: 山代荣是肥前国御家人，出自九州北部松浦党的支族山代氏。1281年蒙古来袭（弘安之役）六月二十九日，日军以松浦党、彼杵、高木、龙造寺氏等数万之众，向占据壹岐岛的元军东路军发起总攻；山代荣在壹岐岛之战中奋战立功，并因此得到肥前守护北条时定颁下的嘉奖状。

en: Yamashiro Tsutomu was the eldest son of Yamashiro Hiroshi, from whom he received lands including Yamashiro in Hizen Province in 1350.
zh: 山代勤是山代弘的嫡子，1350年从父亲手中承受了肥前国山代等地的领地。

en: Taira no Kiyomoto, known as Yoshida no Kiyomoto, was the second son of Taira no Shigemoto, head of the Hitachi Taira; genealogies style him Yoshida Jirō, provisional governor of Settsu. He settled at Yoshida in Naka District, Hitachi Province, taking the place name as his surname to found the Hitachi Yoshida house. He married his daughter to Minamoto no Yoshinari, eldest son of Yoshimitsu, and she bore Satake Masayoshi, first head of the Satake. His children and grandchildren founded the Namekata, Kashima, Ishikawa and Aso clans.
zh: 平清干，即吉田清干，是常陆平氏当家平重干的次子，系图称吉田次郎、摄津权守。他在常陆国那珂郡吉田乡定居，以地名为苗字，成为常陆吉田氏之祖。他把女儿嫁给源义光的长子源义业，生下佐竹氏初代当主佐竹昌义。他的子孙分出了行方、鹿岛、石川、麻生等家族。

en: Taira no Morimoto, recorded as Yoshida Tarō in the genealogies, was a warrior of the Hitachi Taira's Yoshida line, a son of Yoshida no Kiyomoto and father of Ishikawa no Iemoto.
zh: 平盛干，系图中记作吉田太郎，是常陆平氏吉田氏一族，为吉田清干之子、石川家干之父。

en: Yoshimi Tameyori was a warrior of the early Kamakura period and the founder of the Yoshimi clan of Musashi Province. His grandfather Minamoto no Noriyori, a half-brother of Shōgun Minamoto no Yoritomo, was exiled after the Soga brothers' vendetta of 1193 and disappeared. Tameyori's father Han'en was spared through the intercession of Hiki no Ama, took the tonsure, and was granted Yoshimi manor in Yokomi District; Tameyori became a Kamakura gokenin, inherited the manor, and was the first of his line to call himself Yoshimi.
zh: 吉见为赖是镰仓时代初期的武将，武藏国吉见氏的始祖。其祖父源范赖是初代将军源赖朝的异母弟，在1193年的曾我兄弟复仇事件后被流放，下落不明。为赖之父范圆因比企尼等人求情而活命，出家后获赐横见郡吉见庄；为赖出仕镰仓幕府成为御家人，继承吉见庄，并首次以吉见为苗字，子孙遂称吉见氏。

en: Yoshimi Ujiyori was a Nanboku-cho warrior and shugo of Noto. Around 1348 he succeeded his father Yoshimi Yoritaka in the post, and after a brief interruption he was restored in 1352, holding Noto until 1379. During the Kanno disturbance he followed Ashikaga Takauji. As a Northern Court commander in Hokuriku he repeatedly fought the Southern Court general Momoi Naotsune and his son Naonobu in Noto and Etchu. In 1370 he replaced Imagawa Sadayo as head of the Muromachi bakufu's hikitsuke court.
zh: 吉见氏赖是南北朝时代武将、能登守护。约1348年他继承父亲吉见赖隆的职位，一度去任后于1352年复职，一直担任能登守护到1379年。观应之扰乱中他从属足利尊氏。作为北朝在北陆的武将，他与南朝将领桃井直常、直信父子在能登、越中屡度交战。1370年，他接替今川贞世出任室町幕府引付头人。

en: Yoshimi Yorimune, younger son of founder Yoshimi Tameyori, settled in Noto Province in Kamakura times; his sons founded the Musashi and Noto Yoshimi houses, and Yoritaka's line inherited the headship after the main line was extinguished.
zh: 吉见赖宗是镰仓时代武将，吉见氏始祖吉见为赖的少子，后定居能登国；其子分别开创武藏吉见氏与能登吉见氏，嫡流断绝后，由其子赖隆一系继承家督与武藏领地。

en: Yoshimi Yoritaka was a Nanboku-cho warrior of the Noto Yoshimi, a branch of the Minamoto, and son of Yoshimi Yorimune. He is listed as shugo of Etchu from before December 1336 and after April 1337, and in 1337 he became shugo of Noto, holding the post until 1346. In 1344 Inoue Toshikiyo, deposed shugo of Etchu allied with Southern Court forces in Echigo, fought Yoritaka fiercely in Noto until he surrendered in the intercalary ninth month of 1346. His son Ujiyori succeeded him around 1348.
zh: 吉见赖隆是南北朝时代武将，出身源氏旁支能登吉见氏，吉见赖宗之子。1336年12月以前他已担任越中守护，在任至1337年4月以后；1337年他又出任能登守护，一直任职到1346年。1344年，被罢免的越中守护井上俊清联合越后的南朝势力，在能登与赖隆激战，最终于1346年闰九月投降。约1348年，其子吉见氏赖继承了他的职位。

en: Yōmei (c. 540–587), the 31st emperor of Japan, was a son of Emperor Kinmei by Soga no Kitashihime, a daughter of the minister Soga no Iname, and thus stood close to the Soga clan. The chronicles give his personal name as Tachibana no Toyohi. He succeeded his half-brother Bidatsu in 585 amid the deepening feud between the pro-Buddhist Soga and the anti-Buddhist Mononobe, but reigned less than two years, dying in 587. By his consort Princess Anahobe no Hashihito he fathered Prince Shōtoku, who would become the great regent under Empress Suiko and a patron of Buddhism.
zh: 用明天皇（约540—587）是日本第31代天皇，钦明天皇与大臣苏我稻目之女苏我坚盐媛所生之子，与苏我氏关系密切；《日本书纪》称他为橘丰日天皇，《古事记》称橘丰日命。585年异母兄敏达天皇去世后，他在苏我氏崇佛与物部氏排佛之争愈演愈烈之际即位，在位不足两年，587年病死。他与皇女穴穗部间人所生之子即圣德太子，后者后来在推古天皇朝担任摄政，大力弘扬佛教。

en: Emperor Yōzei (869–949), personal name Sadaakira, was the 57th emperor of Japan, reigning from 876 to 884. The eldest son of Emperor Seiwa, he was named crown prince in infancy and ascended at nine, with his maternal uncle Fujiwara no Mototsune as regent. In 883 a courtier was beaten to death in the palace amid rumours of the emperor's involvement, and in 884 Mototsune deposed him, presenting the abdication as voluntary on grounds of illness. Yōzei then lived sixty-five years as a retired emperor, the longest such retirement on record, and was later known as a waka poet.
zh: 阳成天皇（869—949），名贞明，是日本第57代天皇，876年至884年在位。他是清和天皇的长子，未满周岁即被立为太子，九岁即位，由舅父藤原基经担任摄政。883年，一名近臣在宫中被殴打致死，坊间传言此事与天皇有关；884年基经将他废黜，对外称他因病自愿退位。此后阳成以上皇身份生活了六十五年，是有记载以来在任最久的太上皇，晚年以和歌诗人闻名。

en: Yuasa Munechika, known as Kusumoto Saemon-no-jō, was a gokenin warrior of the late Kamakura period and jitō, or estate steward, of Ategawa manor in Kii Province. On the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month, 1275, the peasants of the manor's Kamimura village submitted a petition accusing Munechika of threatening to cut off their ears and slice off their noses. Preserved in the Koyasan archives, the complaint is one of the best-known peasant suits of medieval Japan. He was the second son of Yuasa Muneuji and the father of Yuasa Munekuni.
zh: 汤浅宗亲，通称楠本左卫门尉，是镰仓时代后期的御家人、纪伊国阿弖河庄地头。1275年（建治元年）十月二十八日，庄内上村百姓递交诉状，控告宗亲以割耳削鼻相威胁；该诉状收入《高野山文书》，是日本中世最著名的百姓诉状之一。他是汤浅宗氏的次子，汤浅宗国之父。

en: Yuasa Munefuji was a leader of the Yuasa warrior band of Kii Province, based at Ategawa, and an ally of Kusunoki Masashige. In October 1331, on the Kamakura shogunate's orders, he stormed Masashige's castle of Shimo-Akasaka and was made its jitō steward, but in April 1332 Masashige retook the castle and Munefuji surrendered with his whole band. He then fought for the imperial side in Settsu and Kawachi, crossed to Shikoku with Wakiya Yoshisuke in 1340, and in 1352 escorted Emperor Go-Murakami to the Sumiyoshi Shrine. Later tradition numbers him among Masashige's eight chief retainers.
zh: 汤浅宗藤是纪伊国汤浅党的有力武士，本据在阿氐河庄，是楠木正成的盟友。1331年10月，他奉镰仓幕府之命攻打楠木正成据守的下赤坂城，获任命为地头；1332年4月，正成反攻夺回赤坂城，他率汤浅党投降，此后在摄津、河内为朝廷一方作战。1340年他随胁屋义助渡海前往四国，1352年又随侍后村上天皇行幸住吉社。后世将他列为楠公八臣之一。

en: Yuasa Munekuni was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yuasa clan in Kii Province. He was the son of Yuasa Munechika, jitō of Ategawa manor, and the father of Yuasa Munefuji, a leading warrior of the Yuasa band during the Nanboku-chō wars.
zh: 汤浅宗国是镰仓时代纪伊国汤浅氏的武士。他是阿弖河庄地头汤浅宗亲之子，其子汤浅宗藤是南北朝时期汤浅党的有力武士。

en: Yuasa Munemitsu was a Kamakura warrior of Kii Province, seventh son of Yuasa Muneshige. In 1197 Mongaku transferred to him the office of local administrator of Atekawa manor; in 1210 the shogunate confirmed his hereditary office as its land steward. In 1219 suit by Kumano shrine men brought exile to Tsushima, but he was recalled in 1221 and confirmed land steward of Atekawa, Hota and Tado manors, after which he took the name Hota. Though an illegitimate son, he made his line the leading branch of the Yuasa clan. Around 1224 he fought a boundary case against a Kōya-san monk in Kyoto, and later took orders as Jōshin.
zh: 汤浅宗光是镰仓时代纪伊国武士，汤浅宗重的第七子。1197年，文觉将纪伊阿氐河庄的下司职让给他；1210年，幕府安堵其家族相传的阿氐河庄地头职。1219年，他被熊野神人控诉，流放对马，1221年被召还，其阿氐河庄、保田庄、田殿庄的地头职得到安堵，此后改称保田氏。他虽是庶子，却奠定了自己这一支在汤浅一族中的主导地位。约1224年，他在京都就庄园边界争端与高野山僧人对质，后来出家，法号净心。

en: Yuasa Muneshige was a warrior of the late Heian and early Kamakura periods, said to have been a son of Fujiwara Munenaga, and lord of Yuasa Castle in Kii Province. In 1143 he built the castle on his Yuasa manor in Arita District. In 1159, the Gukanshō records, he brought Taira no Kiyomori, then on pilgrimage at Kumano, news of the Heiji Disturbance and went up to Kyoto with him, becoming a leading captain. After Kiyomori's death he held Yuasa Castle for the Taira before surrendering to Minamoto no Yoritomo, who confirmed his lands in 1186; his following became the Yuasa war band.
zh: 汤浅宗重是平安时代末期至镰仓时代初期的武将，相传为藤原北家藤原宗永之子，纪伊国汤浅城之主。1143年，他在自己的在田郡汤浅庄修筑汤浅城。《愚管抄》记载，1159年平清盛在熊野参拜时，他向清盛报告平治之乱爆发的消息，并随清盛上洛，成为其麾下有力武将。清盛死后，他据汤浅城支持平氏，后向源赖朝投降，1186年所领得到安堵；其势力后来被称为汤浅党。

en: Yuasa Muneuji, also called Ategawa Muneuji, was a Kamakura-period warrior of the Yuasa clan in Kii Province. The third son of Yuasa Munemitsu and grandson of Muneshige, he became jitō, or estate steward, of Ategawa manor and founded the Yuasa Ategawa house. After the death of the monk Myōe, Muneuji saw that Kanki-ji, the temple at Myōe's birthplace, had fallen into decline. He invited Myōe's disciple Kikai to restore it. His son Munechika inherited the office of jitō in 1273.
zh: 汤浅宗氏，又称阿弖川宗氏，是镰仓时代纪伊国汤浅氏的武士。他是汤浅宗光的三子、宗重之孙，担任阿弖河庄地头，开创了汤浅阿弖川家。僧人明惠去世后，宗氏见其出生地的欢喜寺衰落，便迎请明惠的弟子喜海复兴该寺。其子宗亲于1273年继承了地头之职。

en: Yūki Akitomo was the third head of the Shirakawa Yūki clan of Mutsu Province. The eldest son of Yūki Chikatomo, who had founded a separate Komine house, he succeeded his grandfather Munehiro as head of the Shirakawa line. He fought for the Northern Court: in 1346 against the Date and Tamura clans, and at Iwakiri Castle in 1351 with Kira Sadaie during the Kannō disturbance. In 1353 Ashikaga Takauji named him magistrate over eight Ōshū districts including Shirakawa, and in 1367 he defeated the rebel Kira Haruie. In 1369 he passed the headship to his adopted heir Mitsutomo.
zh: 结城显朝是陆奥国白河结城氏的第三代当主。其父结城亲朝另立小峰氏，因此他在祖父宗广死后继承白河本家。他为北朝作战：1346年随奥州管领攻打南朝方的伊达氏、田村氏；1351年观应扰乱时，与吉良贞家一同在岩切城作战。1353年，足利尊氏任命他为白河等奥州八郡的检断职；1367年，他奉第二代将军足利义诠之命讨伐反叛的吉良治家并取得胜利。1369年，他把家督让给养子满朝。

en: Yūki Chikatomo was the eldest son of Yūki Munehiro and a warrior of the Shirakawa Yūki clan in Mutsu Province. He fought with his father to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate in 1333 and held office in the Mutsu government under the Kenmu Restoration. In 1340 he built Komine Castle at Shirakawa and founded his own Komine branch house. Though he first served the Southern Court and fought around Shirakawa for Kitabatake Chikafusa, in 1343 he defected to the Northern Court in exchange for guarantees of his lands. He died in 1347.
zh: 结城亲朝是结城宗广的嫡子，陆奥国白河结城氏的武将。1333年，他与父亲一同参加攻灭镰仓幕府的战事；建武新政时在陆奥将军府任职。1340年他修筑白河小峰城，另立小峰氏分家。他起初从属南朝，为北畠亲房在白河一带作战，1343年却以安堵自己的所领为条件倒向北朝。1347年他去世。

en: Yūki Hirotsuna (1221–1278) was a mid-Kamakura warrior and the third head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Tomohiro in the eleventh month of 1255. In 1257 he was appointed a Kebiishi officer in Kyoto, and in 1260 he became assistant governor of Kōzuke Province, holding junior fifth rank, lower grade. Temple tradition calls him founder of the Chōraku-ji, where he devoted himself to the nenbutsu. He died in the sixth month of 1278 and was buried at the Shōmyō-ji in Yūki beside his father and grandfather; his son Tokihiro succeeded him.
zh: 结城广纲（1221—1278）是镰仓时代中期武士、御家人，下总结城氏第三代当主。1255年十一月，父亲朝广把家督让给他。1257年他被任为检非违使，1260年任上野介，叙从五位下。据新福寺寺传，他在文永年间开创长乐寺，皈依念佛宗。1278年六月去世，葬于结城称名寺，与父亲、祖父同寺；家督由儿子时广继承。

en: Yūki Munehiro (1266–1339) was the second head of the Shirakawa Yūki clan of Mutsu Province. A Kamakura retainer, he answered Emperor Go-Daigo's call in 1333 and stormed Kamakura with Nitta Yoshisada, overthrowing the Hōjō shogunate. He then governed the Ōshū lands with Kitabatake Akiie, and in 1336 helped retake Kyoto from Ashikaga Takauji, receiving the treasured sword Onimaru from Go-Daigo. After Akiie fell in 1338, he sailed from Ise toward Ōshū escorting Prince Noriyoshi, but his ship was wrecked and he died in Ise in 1339.
zh: 结城宗广（1266—1339）是陆奥国白河结城氏的第二代当主。他本为镰仓幕府御家人，1333年响应后醍醐天皇的讨幕纶旨，与新田义贞一同攻入镰仓，灭亡了北条氏掌权的镰仓幕府。建武新政时，他随北畠显家治理奥州，1336年又协助朝廷从足利尊氏手中夺回京都，受后醍醐天皇赐予宝刀鬼丸。1338年北畠显家战死后，他护送义良亲王从伊势渡海前往奥州，途中遭遇海难，1339年在伊势病逝。

en: Yūki Naomitsu (1330–1395) was the eighth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan. He succeeded his brother Naotomo in 1343 at fourteen and served Ashikaga Takauji in the Kannō disturbance. In 1352 he fought Nitta Yoshioki and Yoshimune's rising in Kōzuke, and in 1368 he joined Uesugi Noriaki against Nitta Yoshimune in Musashi. Trusted by three successive shōguns, he expanded the clan into Hitachi and held Awa Province as shugo. He took Buddhist vows in 1358 and died in 1395, leaving the headship to his son Motomitsu; he is credited with writing the Gen'ishū.
zh: 结城直光（1330—1395）是下总结城氏的第八代当主，曾任安房国守护。1343年兄直朝战死后，他十四岁继承家督，观应扰乱时站在足利尊氏一方。1352年新田义兴、义宗在上野国举兵，他加入尊氏方作战；1368年又随上杉宪显讨伐在武藏举兵的新田义宗。他深受足利尊氏、义诠、义满三代将军信任，将势力扩入常陆，一度担任安房国守护。他于1358年出家，1395年去世，家督由其子基光继承；相传他还是军记《源威集》的作者。

en: Yūki Naotomo (1325–1343) was the seventh head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan. When his father Tomosuke fell at the Battle of Tatarahama in 1336, he inherited the clan at the age of twelve. He served the Northern Court against the Southern Court Shirakawa Yūki and Seki houses. In 1343 he joined Kō no Morofuyu's siege of Seki Castle in Hitachi, held by Kitabatake Chikafusa, and on 3 April was mortally wounded in a sortie led by Kasuga Arikuni. He died aged nineteen, leaving no heir, and his younger brother Naomitsu succeeded him.
zh: 结城直朝（1325—1343）是下总结城氏的第七代当主。1336年父亲朝祐在多多良滨之战中战死，他以十二岁之龄继承家督，继续依附北朝，与南朝方的白河结城氏、关氏等对立。1343年，他随高师冬攻打北畠亲房据守的常陆国关城；4月3日，关城守军出击，他在与春日显国的交战中重伤而死，年仅十九岁。他没有子嗣，由弟弟直光继承家督。

en: Yūki Sadahiro (1289–1309) was a late Kamakura warrior and the fifth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, whose childhood name was Inujirōmaru. His father Tokihiro died in 1290 when Sadahiro was not yet one year old, so he inherited the headship as an infant and his mother, a daughter of Oyama Tokimura, administered the clan's affairs until he came of age. During Sadahiro's headship the Yūki abandoned Jōdo Shinshū Buddhism and turned to Zen. He died on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month, 1309, aged twenty-one; his one-year-old son Tomosuke, childhood name Inutsurumaru, succeeded him.
zh: 结城贞广（1289—1309）是镰仓时代后期武士、御家人，下总结城氏第五代当主，幼名犬次郎丸。1290年父亲时广去世，他出生不满一岁便继任当主，成年前由母亲小山时村之女实际打理家族事务。贞广当家时，结城氏放弃了原本信奉的净土真宗，改归禅宗。1309年十一月十三日，贞广去世，年仅二十一岁；年仅一岁的儿子犬鹤丸（朝祐）继任家督。

en: Yūki Sukehiro was a Kamakura-period warrior and founder of the Shirakawa branch of the Yūki clan. A younger son of Tomohiro, second head of the Shimōsa Yūki, he inherited the family's Shirakawa estates in Mutsu Province, granted to his grandfather Tomomitsu after the 1189 Ōshū campaign. In 1289 he went down to Ōshū and built Shirakawa Castle, establishing his branch there; even so, he held only part of the old Shirakawa lands, while the main Shimōsa house governed the rest through deputies. His son Munehiro succeeded him as the branch's second head.
zh: 结城祐广是镰仓时代武将、御家人，白河结城氏初代当主，下总结城氏二代当主朝广之子。他继承了祖父朝光因1189年奥州合战之功获封的陆奥国白河领地，1289年下向奥州，修筑白川城，在当地建立分家；不过他只继承了白河领地的一部分，其余仍由下总本家派代官管理。儿子宗广继任为白河结城氏二代当主。

en: Yūki Tokihiro (1267–1290) was a late Kamakura warrior and the fourth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, son of Hirotsuna. His given name bears a character granted him by Hōjō Tokimune, the eighth Kamakura regent. He succeeded his father around 1278 and held junior fifth rank and the office of left guards lieutenant. He married a daughter of Oyama Tokimura of the senior Oyama line, and his heir Sadahiro was born in 1289. Tokihiro died the next year, 1290, aged twenty-four, and was buried at the Shōmyō-ji in Yūki with the earlier heads of his house.
zh: 结城时广（1267—1290）是镰仓时代后期武士、御家人，下总结城氏第四代当主，广纲之子。他名字中的“时”字得自镰仓幕府第八代执权北条时宗的偏讳。约1278年继承家督，叙从五位下，任左卫门尉。他娶本家小山时村之女为妻，嫡子贞广生于1289年。次年即1290年，时广去世，年仅二十四岁，葬于结城称名寺，与历代当主同寺。

en: Yūki Tomohiro (1190–c. 1274), a Kamakura-period warrior, was the second head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Tomomitsu. In the 1221 Jōkyū War he commanded on the Hokuriku road and won distinction against the court's forces in Etchū Province, afterward becoming a guards captain. He later served as a Kebiishi officer policing Kyoto, and in 1242 was raised to senior fifth rank and appointed assistant minister of the treasury. His long headship saw the heyday of the Yūki clan; his son Hirotsuna succeeded him.
zh: 结城朝广（1190—约1274）是镰仓时代武将，下总结城氏第二代当主，继父朝光为家督。1221年承久之乱时，他任北陆道大将，在越中国与朝廷军作战立功，后任兵卫尉、左卫门尉。他又担任检非违使，负责京都治安，1242年叙正五位，任大藏权少辅。在他长期当家期间结城氏步入全盛；儿子广纲继任家督。

en: Yūki Tomomitsu (1168–1254), third son of Shimotsuke chieftain Oyama Masamitsu, founded the Shimōsa Yūki clan. In 1180 his mother Samukawa no Ama presented him to Minamoto no Yoritomo, who presided over his coming-of-age. He fought at Uji in 1184 and Dannoura in 1185, and in the 1189 Ōshū campaign slew enemy general Kongō Bettō Hidetsuna at Atsukashiyama, winning the three districts of Shirakawa. In 1199 he led sixty-six gokenin in the petition that overthrew Kajiwara no Kagetoki, commanded an army in the 1221 Jōkyū War, and joined the shogunate Council of State in 1235. He later took Buddhist vows.
zh: 结城朝光（1168—1254）是下野国豪族小山政光的第三子，下总结城氏的初代当主。1180年由母亲寒河尼引见投奔源赖朝，赖朝亲自主持他的元服。他参加了1184年的宇治川之战与1185年的坛之浦之战，1189年奥州合战时在阿津贺志山讨杀敌将金刚别当秀纲，因功获封奥州白河三郡。1199年，他领六十六名御家人联名上书，促成梶原景时倒台；1221年承久之乱中统率一军，1235年出任幕府评定众，后出家。

en: Yūki Tomosuke (1308–1336) was the sixth head of the Shimōsa Yūki clan, succeeding his father Sadahiro in 1309 while still called Inutsurumaru. As a Kamakura gokenin he first used the name Tomotaka, the character taka granted by Regent Hōjō Takatoki, and served in the 1331 siege of Kasagi Castle under Ashikaga Takauji before turning against the Hōjō. He then renamed himself Tomosuke, but the Kenmu government favored his Shirakawa kinsmen, so he joined Takauji's Northern Court side. He fought at Hakone and Takenoshita in 1336, followed Takauji to Kyushu, and fell at the Battle of Tatarahama the same year.
zh: 结城朝祐（1308—1336）是下总结城氏第六代当主，1309年父亲贞广去世时他仍叫犬鹤丸，幼年继任。作为镰仓御家人，他初名朝高，“高”字得自执权北条高时，1331年在足利高氏麾下参加笠置城之战，随后倒向反幕一方。他后来改名朝祐，但建武政权重用其白河分家，于是投奔足利尊氏的北朝阵营，1336年参加箱根·竹之下之战，随尊氏西下九州，同年战死于多多良滨之战。

en: Beatrice of Brandenburg (c. 1270–before 1316) was a German princess of the Brandenburg Ascanians, the second daughter of Margrave Otto V the Tall and Judith of Henneberg. Her betrothal to Bolko I the Strict, Duke of Świdnica, was celebrated at Spandau in 1279 and their church wedding followed in Berlin in 1284. She bore Bolko ten children. After his death in 1301, either she acted as regent for their minor sons with the support of her brother Margrave Herman, or Herman acted as regent on their behalf. By 1308 she had remarried Władysław, Duke of Koźle-Bytom-Siewierz, by whom she had two more children.
zh: 勃兰登堡的贝娅特丽克丝（约1270年生，1316年前卒）是出身阿斯坎尼家族勃兰登堡支系的德意志公主，为藩侯奥托五世（“高个子”）与亨讷贝格的尤迪思的次女。1279年，她与希维德尼察公爵博尔科一世（“严厉者”）在施潘道订婚，1284年在柏林正式成婚。她为博尔科生下十个子女。1301年丈夫去世后，可能是她在兄长藩侯赫尔曼支持下为年幼的儿子们摄政，也可能是赫尔曼代她和儿子们摄政。1308年前，她改嫁科兹莱-比托姆-谢维日公爵瓦迪斯瓦夫，又生有两个子女。

en: Bolesław II the Horned (c. 1220–1278) was a Silesian Piast, son of Henry II the Pious. He succeeded when his father fell fighting the Mongols at Legnica in 1241, but soon lost Kraków and his Greater Polish lands. In 1248 he divided Lower Silesia with his brothers, taking Legnica and ceding Głogów to Konrad in 1251. He was excommunicated for jailing the Bishop of Wrocław and did penance in 1261. In 1277, allied with Rudolf of Germany, he captured Henry IV of Wrocław and won at Stolec. He died in December 1278, leaving Henry V, Bolko I and Bernhard.
zh: 长角的波列斯瓦夫二世（约1220—1278）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族王公，虔敬者亨里克二世之子。1241年父亲在莱格尼察抗击蒙古人战死，他随即继位，但很快失去克拉科夫与大波兰领地。1248年他与诸弟分割下西里西亚，取得莱格尼察，1251年又把格沃古夫封给弟弟康拉德。他曾因囚禁弗罗茨瓦夫主教被开除教籍，1261年作出忏悔。1277年他与德意志国王鲁道夫结盟，俘获弗罗茨瓦夫的亨里克四世，并在斯托莱茨之战中取胜。1278年12月去世，留下亨里克五世、布尔科一世和伯恩哈德三子。

en: Bolko I the Strict (1252/1256–1301) was a Silesian Piast, second son of Bolesław II the Horned of Legnica. After his father died in 1278 he inherited Jawor and Lwówek with his brother Bernard, ruling Jawor alone from 1281 and gaining Świdnica in 1291. He married Beatrice of Brandenburg in 1284. Excommunicated in 1294, he stoutly defended his fortified towns against King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1295 and made his duchy a papal fief in 1299. He promoted German settlement and founded the Cistercian Krzeszów Abbey, where he was buried after he died on 9 November 1301.
zh: 严厉的布尔科一世（1252/1256—1301）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族王公，莱格尼察的长角波列斯瓦夫二世次子。1278年父亲去世后，他与弟弟伯恩哈德共治亚沃尔和勒武韦克，1281年起独治亚沃尔，1291年取得希维德尼察。1284年娶勃兰登堡的贝阿特丽切。1294年他被开除教籍；1295年凭坚固城防顽强抵御波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫二世，1299年将公国置于教皇治下，成为教皇封臣。他鼓励德意志移民，创立西多会克热舒夫修道院，1301年11月9日去世后葬于该院。

en: Henry I of Jawor (c. 1294–1346) was a Silesian Piast duke, the third son of Bolko I the Strict and Beatrice of Brandenburg. After his father's death in 1301 he ruled jointly with his brothers until the 1312 partition gave him Jawor and Lwówek. In 1319, when the Brandenburg Ascanians died out, he occupied eastern Lusatia around Zgorzelec and married Agnes, daughter of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. In 1337 he exchanged his Lusatian lands for the Duchy of Głogów and did homage to John of Bohemia. He died in 1346 and was buried at Krzeszów Abbey.
zh: 亚沃尔的亨里克一世（约1294—1346）是西里西亚皮亚斯特家族公爵，亚沃尔公爵“严厉的”布尔科一世与勃兰登堡的贝阿特丽切之第三子。1301年父亲去世后他与兄弟共治，1312年分封时获得亚沃尔和勒武韦克。1319年勃兰登堡阿斯坎尼家族绝嗣，他乘机占领兹戈热莱茨一带的东卢萨蒂亚，并于同年娶波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫二世之女阿格尼丝。1337年，他以卢萨蒂亚领地换得格沃古夫公国，并向波希米亚国王约翰行臣服礼。他于1346年去世，葬于克热舒夫修道院。

en: Jean-Baptiste de Machault, comte d'Arnouville (1701–1794), was a French statesman born in Paris. After serving in the Parlement of Paris and as intendant of Hainaut, he was appointed Controller-General of Finances in December 1745, when France was deep in debt from the War of the Austrian Succession. In 1749 he proposed the vingtième, a tax of one twentieth to be paid by all landowners including the clergy and nobility, but privileged opposition forced the plan's failure. He moved to the Naval Ministry in 1754, was dismissed in 1757, and in 1794 died in a Paris revolutionary prison aged ninety-two.
zh: 让-巴蒂斯特·德·马肖·达努维尔伯爵（1701—1794）是生于巴黎的法国政治家。他曾任职于巴黎高等法院、出任埃诺总督，后于1745年12月被任命为财政总监，当时法国正因奥地利王位继承战争负债累累。1749年，他提议开征二十分之一税，要求包括教士与贵族在内的所有土地所有者一律缴纳，却因特权阶层反对而失败。1754年他转任海军大臣，1757年被解职；1794年，他在巴黎的革命监狱中去世，终年九十二岁。

en: Jean Bureau (c. 1390–1463), born in Champagne, trained as a lawyer in Paris before he and his brother Gaspard offered their services as gunners to Charles VII in 1434. By 1439 Jean was master gunner of French artillery; the brothers benefited from improvements in gunpowder and cannon casting, and their batteries shaped the Normandy campaign of 1449–1450, from the fall of Rouen to the victory at Formigny. At Formigny two of their guns were captured by the English. In 1453 Bureau deployed 300 guns in fortified positions at Castillon, where cannon fire destroyed John Talbot's army and effectively ended the Hundred Years' War, after which he forced Bordeaux to surrender. He was knighted in 1461.
zh: 让·比罗（约1390—1463）生于香槟，早年在巴黎学习法律。1434年，他与兄弟加斯帕尔以炮兵技艺投奔查理七世；到1439年，让已成为法军炮兵总监。兄弟二人受益于火药和铸炮工艺的改进，他们的炮队左右了1449—1450年的诺曼底战局，从鲁昂陷落一直到福尔米尼告捷。在福尔米尼，他们的两门炮被英军夺走。1453年，比罗在卡斯蒂永的筑垒阵地布置300门火炮，炮火摧毁约翰·塔尔博特的军队，实际终结了百年战争，随后迫使波尔多投降。他于1461年受封骑士。

en: Jean-Baptiste Colbert (1619–1683) was a French statesman born in Reims to a merchant family. In 1652 he managed the affairs of the exiled Mazarin, to whom he reported that less than half the taxes paid reached the king. Recommended to Louis XIV by Mazarin, he became intendant of finances in May 1661, helped destroy Nicolas Fouquet, and was Controller-General of Finances from 1665 and Navy Secretary from 1669. His mercantilist program, later called Colbertism, reformed taxation, raised tariffs, set up royal manufactures such as the Gobelins works and the mirror factory of 1665, chartered the East India Company in 1664, and expanded France's navy and colonies. He founded the Academy of Sciences in 1666 and died on 6 September 1683.
zh: 让-巴蒂斯特·柯尔贝尔（1619—1683）是法国政治家，生于兰斯的一个商人家庭。1652年，他为流亡的马萨林管理事务，并向他报告缴纳的税款中不到一半进入国王的国库。他由马萨林举荐给路易十四，1661年5月被任命为财政督办，参与扳倒尼古拉·富凯，1665年出任财政总督，1669年又任海军国务大臣。他推行的重商主义政策后世称为柯尔贝尔主义：改革税制、提高关税，兴办戈布兰织毯厂和1665年的王家镜子厂等皇家手工工场，1664年特许成立东印度公司，并大力扩张法国海军与殖民地。他还在1666年创立科学院，1683年9月6日去世。

en: Juan de Beaumont (1419–1487) was prior of the Order of St John in Navarre and royal chancellor from 1434. From 1432 he was tutor and chief counsellor to Charles, Prince of Viana. The pope granted him the priory in 1435, though he did not meet its requirements, and he later had to dispute it with Sancho de Echauz. As leader of the Beaumont faction he backed Charles against the prince's father John II of Aragon in the Navarrese Civil War and was imprisoned after the defeat. Charles made him viscount of Abarca and Arberoa in 1455. He later joined the Catalan civil war, briefly ruling Catalonia as viceroy for Henry IV of Castile before defecting to the royalists in 1464. He died in 1487.
zh: 胡安·德·博蒙特（1419—1487）是医院骑士团在纳瓦拉的修院长，1434年起任王国首相。1432年起，他担任维亚纳亲王卡洛斯的师傅和首席谋臣。1435年教皇授予他修院长职位，尽管他不符合任职条件；后来他还与桑乔·德·埃绍兹争夺这一职位。作为博蒙特派的首领，他在纳瓦拉内战中支持卡洛斯对抗亲王的父亲阿拉贡国王胡安二世，亲王战败后他被囚禁。1455年，卡洛斯封他为阿瓦尔卡和阿韦罗亚子爵。后来他投身加泰罗尼亚内战，曾代表卡斯蒂利亚国王恩里克四世任加泰罗尼亚总督，1464年倒向王室派。他于1487年去世。

en: Jean de Fontaney (1643–1710) was a French Jesuit mathematician who taught astronomy at the Collège de Clermont in Paris. At Louis XIV's request, following an appeal from the Beijing missionary Ferdinand Verbiest, he set out with five scientifically trained Jesuits, among them Joachim Bouvet and Jean-François Gerbillon. One remained in Siam, while the other four accompanied him to China. They reached Beijing in February 1688 and were received by the Kangxi Emperor, who kept Bouvet and Gerbillon at court. He returned to France in 1703 and died at La Flèche in 1710.
zh: 让·德·丰特内（1643—1710），汉名洪若翰，是法国耶稣会数学家，在巴黎克莱蒙学院教授天文学。应路易十四派遣（此行源于在北京的传教士南怀仁的请求），他与白晋、张诚等五名精通科学的耶稣会士启程，其中一人留在暹罗，其余四人随他前往中国。他们于1688年2月抵达北京，觐见康熙帝，白晋与张诚被留在宫中效力。1703年他返回法国，1710年在拉弗莱什去世。

en: Jean d'Orléans (1402–1468), called the Bastard of Orléans and later Jean de Dunois, was the illegitimate son of Louis I, Duke of Orléans. While his half-brother the duke was held captive in England after Agincourt, he led the House of Orléans in the Dauphin's service. In 1427 he helped raise the siege of Montargis. He defended Orléans and relieved the city with Joan of Arc in 1429, then attended Charles VII's coronation. He helped retake Paris in 1436, was made Count of Dunois in 1439 and led the reconquest of Normandy and Guienne in its final phase. He died in 1468, after joining the League of the Public Weal against Louis XI in 1465.
zh: 让·德·奥尔良（1402—1468），人称“奥尔良的私生子”，后称让·德·迪努瓦，是奥尔良公爵路易一世的私生子。同父异母的兄长在阿金库尔战役后被英军长期囚禁，他遂以王太子麾下奥尔良家族之首的身份参战。1427年他协助解除蒙塔尔日之围。他守卫奥尔良城，1429年与贞德合力为该城解围，随后参加查理七世的加冕礼。1436年他协助收复巴黎，1439年受封迪努瓦伯爵，并在百年战争最后阶段率军收复诺曼底与吉耶讷。1465年他加入反对路易十一的“公益同盟”，1468年去世。

en: Martanda Cinkaiariyan (r. 1325–1348) was an early Aryacakravarti king of Jaffna, taking the throne name Pararasasekaram III. He put down revolts by the Vanniyar chieftains who controlled parts of the kingdom's interior and promoted agriculture and learning. His trading ships kept Jaffna in prosperous commerce with Yemen. Around 1344 the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited his court and recorded that the king accompanied him up the sacred peak of Sivanoli Padam Malai. Martanda left several inscriptions and was succeeded by his son Gunabhushana Cinkaiariyan.
zh: 马坦达·辛凯阿里扬（1325—1348年在位）是贾夫纳阿梨耶遮迦罗跋帝王朝早期国王，王号帕拉拉塞卡兰三世。他平定了据有王国内地大片土地的万尼耶酋长叛乱，并推动农业与学术。他的商船维持着贾夫纳与也门之间繁荣的贸易。约1344年，摩洛哥旅行家伊本·白图泰到访其宫廷，并记载国王陪同他登上西沃诺利帕达马莱圣山。马坦达留下数方铭文，死后由其子古纳布沙那·辛凯阿里扬继位。

en: Viravarman II was a Chandela king who ruled the Jejakabhukti region around 1315. He succeeded Hammiravarman after 1311 and is known only from the Larwari inscription, whose modest titles show the reduced status of the later Chandela rulers.
zh: 毗罗·跋摩二世是旃提罗王朝国王，约1315年统治杰贾卡布克提地区。他在1311年后继哈密拉跋摩为王，仅见于拉德瓦里铭文；铭文中的称号谦卑，反映出旃提罗末代君主地位的衰落。

en: Arghun Shah was chief of the Ja'un-i Qurban tribe of Khurasan and the most powerful amir of the Ilkhanid claimant Togha Temür. In 1337 he abandoned Togha Temür's western campaign, then captured and executed the governor Shaykh Ali Qushji, sending his head to the Jalayirid Hasan Buzurg, before reconciling with the khan and helping clear Khurasan of Jalayirid forces. In 1339 or 1340 he arrested the Shi'i preacher Hasan Juri. When the Sarbadars invaded in 1340 he was driven from Nishapur to Tus. He died in 1345 or 1346, after which his tribe abandoned Togha Temür's cause.
zh: 阿鲁浑·沙是呼罗珊札兀尼·库尔干部落的首领，也是伊利汗位争夺者脱合帖木儿麾下最有权势的异密。1337年，他退出脱合帖木儿的西征，继而擒杀呼罗珊长官谢赫·阿里·库什吉，将其首级送往札剌亦儿首领哈桑·布祖尔格处；但他随即与汗和解，协助把札剌亦儿势力逐出呼罗珊。1339或1340年，他拘捕什叶派传道者哈桑·朱里。1340年萨尔巴达尔人来攻，他从内沙布尔退守图斯。他死于1345或1346年，此后札兀尼·库尔班便抛弃了脱合帖木儿的事业。

en: Muhammad Beg succeeded Arghun Shah as chief of the Ja'un-i Qurban tribe of Khurasan. Soon after taking power around 1345, he abandoned the tribe's long alliance with the Ilkhanid claimant Togha Temür and allied instead with the Sarbadars.
zh: 穆罕默德·贝格继阿鲁浑·沙之后担任呼罗珊札兀尼·库尔干部落首领。约1345年掌权后不久，他便结束了该部与伊利汗位争夺者脱合帖木儿的长期同盟，转而与萨尔巴达尔人结盟。

en: Kanhadadeva (r. c. 1292–1311) was a Chahamana king who ruled Javalipura, modern Jalore in Rajasthan. From 1296 he shared power with his father Samantasimha, becoming sole ruler around 1305. In 1299 he refused Alauddin Khalji's army passage through his lands on its Gujarat campaign, and later bardic chronicles credit him with recovering the Somnath idol from the Delhi forces. After Alauddin's conquests isolated Jalore, a strong Delhi army under Malik Kamaluddin Gurg stormed the fort in 1311 and killed Kanhadadeva. His son Viramadeva survived him only days. Padmanabha's 1455 epic Kanhadade Prabandha hails him as a hero.
zh: 坎哈达德瓦（约1292—1311年在位）是乔汉（查哈马纳）王朝国王，统治阇瓦利普拉，即今拉贾斯坦邦的贾洛尔。自1296年起他与父亲萨曼塔辛哈共同执政，约1305年成为唯一统治者。1299年，他拒绝阿拉丁·卡尔吉出征古吉拉特的大军借道领地；后世吟游史书还称他从德里军中夺回了索姆纳特神像。阿拉丁的连年征服使贾洛尔陷入孤立，1311年马利克·卡马鲁丁·古尔格率德里大军攻陷城堡，斩杀坎哈达德瓦；其子毗罗摩提婆继位仅数日便死去。1455年帕德马纳布所作史诗《坎哈德·普拉班达》将他传颂为英雄。

en: Adityawarman (c. 1294–c. 1375) was the last powerful ruler of the Mauli dynasty in central Sumatra. The Javanese chronicle Pararaton places his birth at Trowulan, capital of Majapahit; his father was the nobleman Adwayawarman and his mother Dara Jingga, a Malay princess of Dharmasraya. As a senior minister of Majapahit, he helped direct its conquest of Sumatra's east coast, then in 1347 set up his own court at Malayapura near Pagaruyung and controlled the Minangkabau gold trade. A patron of Tantric Buddhism, he last appears in an inscription of 1375 and was succeeded by his son Ananggawarman.
zh: 阿蒂亚瓦曼（约1294—约1375）是苏门答腊中部茂利王朝最后一位强有力的统治者。据爪哇古籍《君王记》记载，他出生于满者伯夷首都多乌兰，父亲是贵族阿陀耶跋摩，母亲是达尔马斯拉耶的马来公主达拉·金加。他曾任满者伯夷重臣，参与征服苏门答腊东海岸，1347年在帕加鲁永附近的马来普拉建立朝廷，掌控米南加保的黄金贸易。他崇奉密宗佛教，1375年最后一次见于铭文记载，之后由其子阿南加跋摩继位。

en: Adwayawarman was a Javanese nobleman of the late Singhasari and early Majapahit period, named in West Sumatran inscriptions as the father of King Adityawarman of Malayapura: the Kuburajo I inscription records his name, while the Bukit Gombak inscription calls him Adwayadwaja. The historian Slamet Muljana identified him with Adwayabrahma, the Rakryan Mahamantri who in 1286 escorted the Amoghapasha statue to Dharmasraya on the Pamalayu expedition. The Javanese chronicle Pararaton names Dewa as the husband of the Malay princess Dara Jingga, brought to Java from Sumatra; his identification with Adwayawarman remains conjectural.
zh: 阿德瓦亚瓦尔曼是信诃沙里晚期至满者伯夷早期的爪哇贵族，西苏门答腊的铭文记载他是末罗瑜普拉国王阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼之父。库布拉约一号铭文提到他的名字，武吉甘柏铭文则称他为阿德瓦亚德瓦贾。史学家斯拉梅特·穆尔贾纳认为，他就是1286年巴马拉尤远征中护送阿摩伽帕夏像前往达摩室利耶的信诃沙里高官罗克兰·摩诃曼特里阿德瓦亚婆罗门。爪哇编年史《列王传》记载，被从苏门答腊带往爪哇的末罗瑜公主达拉·金佳嫁给了德瓦；德瓦与阿德瓦亚瓦尔曼为同一人仍只是推测。

en: Akarendrawarman was a king of the Malay kingdom in Sumatra who succeeded Tribhuwanaraja Mauli Warmadewa in 1316 and ruled until 1347, when his nephew Adityawarman followed him. He is named in the Pagaruyung VII inscription with the title Paduka Sri Maharajadhiraja Srimat Sri Akarendrawarman and governed with the aid of a minister called Tuhan Parpatih; the inscription places his realm at Parhyangan on Mount Marapi. The Suruaso inscription credits him with beginning an irrigation canal for the rice lands at Surawasa, a work completed by Adityawarman.
zh: 阿卡伦德拉跋摩是苏门答腊末罗瑜王国的国王，1316年继特里布瓦纳拉贾·茂利·瓦尔马提婆即位，统治至1347年，由外甥阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼继位。帕加鲁永七号铭文以“巴杜卡·室利·摩诃罗阇迪罗阇·室利马特·室利·阿卡伦德拉跋摩”的全号称呼他，记载他在大臣图罕·帕尔帕提辅佐下治国，其国位于马拉皮山的帕尔亨岸。苏鲁阿索铭文记载，他在苏拉瓦萨主持开凿灌溉渠、浇灌稻田，后由阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼续成。

en: Dara Jingga was a princess of the Malay kingdom of Dharmasraya in Sumatra, the daughter of King Tribhuwanaraja and elder sister of Dara Petak, who married Kertarajasa Jayawardhana, founder of Majapahit. After Singhasari's Pamalayu expedition of 1275–1293, she and her sister were taken to Java to be offered in marriage to King Kertanegara. On Kertanegara's death her sister married his heir Raden Wijaya, while Dara Jingga married a nobleman called Dewa. He has been conjecturally identified with Adwayawarman, who has in turn been identified with the Adwayabrahma named in the Padang Roco inscription. She was the mother of Adityawarman, later ruler of Malay Sumatra. Her name means scarlet dove in old Malay.
zh: 达拉·金佳是苏门答腊末罗瑜达摩室利耶王国的公主，国王特里布瓦纳拉贾之女，也是嫁给满者伯夷开国君主格尔达拉查沙·查耶瓦尔达纳的达拉·巴达克的姐姐。1275—1293年信诃沙里发动巴马拉尤远征后，她与妹妹被带往爪哇，原本要进献给国王格尔达纳卡拉为妃。格尔达纳卡拉死后，妹妹嫁给继位的拉登·韦查耶，达拉·金佳则嫁给名叫德瓦的贵族。有人推测德瓦是阿德瓦亚瓦尔曼，而后者也被认为可能是巴东罗科铭文所载的阿德瓦亚婆罗门。她是后来统治苏门答腊末罗瑜的阿迪蒂亚瓦尔曼之母；其名在古马来语中意为“猩红色的鸽子”。

en: Sri Maharaja Tribhuwanaraja Mauliwarmadewa was king of Dharmasraya in Bhumi Malayu, the Malay kingdom in Sumatra, and is named on the Padang Roco inscription of 1286. That year, after Singhasari's Pamalayu expedition reached Sumatra, he gratefully accepted a stone Amoghapasa statue sent by King Kertanegara of Java, a gift that may have affirmed vassalage or friendly relations between the kingdoms. Javanese chronicles make him the father of princesses Dara Jingga and Dara Petak; after Singhasari fell, Dara Petak married the Majapahit founder Raden Wijaya and bore King Jayanagara. Scholars consider him related to the earlier Srivijayan ruler Trailokyaraja.
zh: 圣大君特里布瓦纳拉贾·茂利瓦尔马提婆是苏门答腊末罗瑜故地达摩室利耶的国王，其名见于1286年的巴东罗科铭文。当年信诃沙里的巴马拉尤远征抵达苏门答腊后，他欣然接受爪哇国王格尔达纳卡拉赠送的不空羂索观音石像，这份赠礼可能确认了两国间的臣属或友好关系。爪哇史籍称他是达拉·金佳与达拉·巴达克两位公主之父；信诃沙里灭亡后，达拉·巴达克嫁给满者伯夷开国君主拉登·韦查耶，生下国王贾亚纳加拉。学者认为他与此前的室利佛逝君主德莱罗阇有亲缘关系。

en: Khengara (r. 1331–1351) was a Chudasama king of Saurashtra whose capital was Junagadh; he succeeded his father Mahipala I. He expelled the Muslim governors from Somnath and Prabhas Patan and restored the decayed Somnath temple. After sheltering Taghan, a rebel against Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq, he saw Junagadh besieged and captured in 1350; he was taken prisoner but soon released, while Taghan fled to Sindh. Inscriptions credit him with conquering eighteen coastal islands and patronizing music. He died in 1351 and was followed by his son Jayasimha I.
zh: 肯伽罗（1331—1351年在位）是索拉什特拉的珠多娑摩国王，定都朱纳格特，继父亲摩希波罗一世即位。他将穆斯林长官逐出索姆纳特和帕巴斯帕坦，修复了破败的索姆纳特神庙。他收容反叛德里苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克的塔甘后，朱纳格特于1350年遭到围攻并被攻陷；他本人被俘但很快获释，塔甘则逃往信德。铭文称他征服了沿海十八岛，并热心赞助音乐。他于1351年去世，其子阇耶辛哈一世继位。

en: Joan of Arc (c. 1412–1431) was a peasant girl from Domrémy who claimed that visions of Saints Michael, Margaret and Catherine bade her free France from the English. Sent to Orléans in 1429, she entered with a relief army carrying her banner, and inspired the relief of the siege within nine days. She encouraged the French pursuit of the English along the Loire, fought at Patay, and stood beside Charles VII at his coronation in Reims. She then took part in the unsuccessful siege of Paris. Captured by Burgundians at Compiègne in May 1430, she was sold to the English, convicted of heresy at Rouen, and burned at the stake on 30 May 1431. Her verdict was annulled in 1456, and she was canonized in 1920.
zh: 圣女贞德（约1412—1431）是栋雷米村的农家少女，自称奉大天使米迦勒、圣玛格丽特和圣凯瑟琳的启示，要把英格兰人逐出法兰西。1429年她被派往奥尔良，持旗随援军进入城中；在她的鼓舞下，围城在九天内解除。她鼓励法军沿卢瓦尔河追击英军，转战帕泰，并随侍查理七世在兰斯加冕。此后她参加了未能成功的巴黎围城战。1430年5月，她在贡比涅被勃艮第人俘虏，转卖给英格兰人，在鲁昂以异端罪名判处火刑，1431年5月30日就义。1456年原判被推翻，1920年她被追封为圣徒。

en: Jochi (c. 1182–c. 1225) was the eldest son of Genghis Khan and Börte. Börte had been a Merkit captive when he was conceived, and the paternity dispute, led by Chagatai, barred both from the succession. In 1206 Genghis gave him nine thousand warriors and the appanage furthest west, along the Irtysh. In 1207–1208 he subdued the forest peoples, including the Oirats and Yenisei Kyrgyz; over the following decade he campaigned intermittently against the Merkits and Qangli. In the Khwarazm war of 1219–1221, the siege of Gurganj deepened his breach with his father. He died estranged around 1225, and his son Batu inherited the ulus that became the Golden Horde.
zh: 术赤（约1182—约1225）是成吉思汗与孛儿帖的长子。他出生前孛儿帖曾被蔑儿乞人掳走，血统因而受到质疑，二弟察合台闹得最凶，这场争执最终使兄弟二人都被排除在汗位继承之外。1206年，成吉思汗封给他九千户战士和最西边、沿额尔齐斯河的封地。1207至1208年，他征服包括斡亦剌和叶尼塞吉尔吉斯在内的森林诸部；此后十年间，他不时征讨蔑儿乞和康里诸部。1219至1221年他参加攻灭花剌子模的战争，玉龙杰赤之围使他与父亲的裂痕加深。约1225年他在与家人失和中病死，其子拔都继承了他的兀鲁思，后来发展为金帐汗国。

en: Johan Offesson was a Scanian magnate from southwestern Skåne when the province had recently come under Swedish rule. In 1338 he led an uprising against King Magnus Eriksson of Sweden, who had bought Skåne from its Holstein pledge-holders in 1332. Defeated in 1339, he kept his life, but his stronghold Lindholmen at Svedala was razed to the ground and his family lost its estates in the Skytts and Oxie hundreds.
zh: 约翰·奥费松是斯科讷西南部的豪强，当时该省刚刚处于瑞典统治之下。1338年，他起兵反抗瑞典国王马格努斯·埃里克松，后者于1332年从荷尔斯泰因的受质者手中买下斯科讷。1339年他兵败，但获准活命，他在斯韦达拉的林霍尔门据点被夷为平地，家族在许茨、乌克瑟两地的领地也被没收。

en: Johann Sebastian Pfauser (c. 1520–1569), probably born at Constance, was a Lutheran theologian who became court preacher to Emperor Maximilian II in Vienna. Under his influence Maximilian read Protestant literature, turned away from purely Catholic practices and refused communion under the Catholic rite, though he never formally converted. Pfauser was in contact with Heinrich Bullinger in Zurich and faced Petrus Canisius in public disputations. Later superintendent at Lauingen in Swabia, he died there on 6 June 1569.
zh: 约翰·塞巴斯蒂安·普福泽（约1520—1569）可能生于康斯坦茨，是路德宗神学家，在维也纳任皇帝马克西米利安二世的宫廷牧师。在他影响下，马克西米利安开始阅读新教书籍，逐渐疏离纯正的天主教仪轨，并拒绝按天主教礼领受圣餐，但始终没有正式改宗。普福泽与苏黎世的海因里希·布林格保持联系，并在公开辩论中与彼得·卡尼修斯交锋。他后来任施瓦本劳因根的总监，1569年6月6日卒于当地。

en: Johann Tetzel (c. 1465–1519) was a German Dominican friar, born at Pirna in Saxony, who became grand commissioner for indulgences in Germany. He studied theology and philosophy at Leipzig before entering the order in 1489. He preached the Jubilee indulgence from 1502 and was made inquisitor of Poland in 1509. From January 1517 he sold indulgences for Archbishop Albrecht of Brandenburg in the dioceses of Magdeburg and Halberstadt, claiming the money would help rebuild St Peter's in Rome. His preaching moved Martin Luther to publish the Ninety-five Theses later that year. Tetzel took a doctorate at Frankfurt an der Oder defending indulgences in 1518, and died at Leipzig in August 1519.
zh: 若望·特次勒（约1465—1519）是德意志多明我会修士，生于萨克森的皮尔纳，后来成为天主教会在德意志的赎罪券总专员。他在莱比锡学习神学与哲学，1489年加入修会，1502年起宣讲禧年赎罪券，1509年受命为波兰的异端裁判官。1517年1月起，他为勃兰登堡的阿尔布雷希特大主教在马格德堡和哈尔伯施塔特教区推销赎罪券，声称所得钱财将用于重建罗马的圣彼得大教堂。他的宣讲促使马丁·路德在同年发表《九十五条论纲》。1518年，特次勒在奥得河畔法兰克福以捍卫赎罪券教义获得神学博士学位，1519年8月在莱比锡去世。

en: Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly (1559–1632), led Catholic forces in the Thirty Years' War. Born at Tilly in the Spanish Netherlands and Jesuit-educated at Cologne, he served under Alexander Farnese against the Dutch, including the 1585 Siege of Antwerp, and later fought the Turks in Hungary. In 1610 Maximilian of Bavaria made him commander of the Catholic League's army. He won at White Mountain in 1620, fought in the conquest of the Palatinate, and crushed the Danes at Lutter in 1626. His sack of Magdeburg in 1631 caused the deaths of some twenty thousand inhabitants. Routed by Gustavus Adolphus at Breitenfeld, he defeated the Swedes at Bamberg in 1632. Mortally wounded at Rain, he died at Ingolstadt on 30 April 1632.
