en: Andrea Dandolo was a Venetian nobleman, son of the jurist Vitale Dandolo and brother of Doge Enrico Dandolo. In 1151 he married Primera Polani, sealing reconciliation between the Dandolo and Polani families. He traded with Constantinople.
zh: 安德烈亚·丹多洛是威尼斯贵族，法学家维塔莱·丹多洛之子、总督恩里科·丹多洛之弟。1151年他与普里梅拉·波拉尼成婚，促成丹多洛与波拉尼两族和解；他经营对君士坦丁堡的贸易。

en: Angelo Morosini was a 13th-century Venetian nobleman who lived in the parish of Santa Maria Formosa. His son Marino Morosini was appointed count of Ossero on the island of Cherso in 1280 and was still count in 1301.
zh: 安杰洛·莫罗西尼是13世纪威尼斯贵族，家住圣福莫萨教区。其子马里诺·莫罗西尼于1280年受任凯尔索岛上的奥塞罗伯爵，1301年仍担任此职。

en: Antonia Contarini was a daughter of Andrea Contarini, the 60th doge of Venice, and his wife Costanza.
zh: 安东尼娅·孔塔里尼是第60任威尼斯总督安德烈亚·孔塔里尼与妻子科斯坦扎之女。

en: Antonio Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and one of at least eight sons of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. In 1348 he held office as Venetian count of Arbe, an island in Dalmatia, the coast over which King Louis I of Hungary was then quarrelling with Venice. His father had sought offices and favours for his sons, a nepotism so flagrant that the doge's death in December 1342 was soon followed by a Major Council act denying office to a living doge's kin and banning the ducal family from private trade.
zh: 安东尼奥·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈至少八个儿子之一。1348年，他担任威尼斯治下的阿尔贝伯爵，阿尔贝是达尔马提亚的一座岛屿，匈牙利国王拉约什一世当时正为这片海岸与威尼斯相争。他的父亲曾为诸子谋求官职和好处；其裙带之风过于张狂，因此1342年12月总督一死，大议会便立法剥夺在任总督亲属的任职资格，并禁止总督家族从事私人贸易。

en: Antonio Venier (c. 1330–1400), son of Nicolò Venier, came from a recently ennobled family with no famous ancestors and no weighty political alliances. He made his name in the wars against Genoa, serving around 1380 as provveditore of the Tenedos fortress and in 1381, on the eve of his election, as captain in Crete. In October 1382 he became the 62nd Doge of Venice and held the office until his death. He had a name as a rigid judge, and his reign bore it out: he was famed for incorruptibility and strict discipline. In his eighteen years the economy recovered and flourished, alliances extended Venetian rule into the Veneto hinterland, and in his last years Venice first clashed with the Ottoman Empire, already conquering in Europe and soon to contest Venetian power in the East. He died on 23 November 1400 and was buried at Santi Giovanni e Paolo.
zh: 安东尼奥·韦涅尔（约1330—1400）是尼科洛·韦涅尔之子，出身新晋贵族之家，没有显赫的祖先，也缺乏有分量的政治盟友。他在对热那亚的战争中崭露头角，约1380年镇守特内多斯要塞，1381年当选总督前夕被派往克里特担任指挥官。1382年10月，他成为第六十二任威尼斯总督，直至去世。他以断案严苛闻名，任期也印证了这一点：他以清廉和纪律严明著称。十八年间，威尼斯经济复苏并趋于繁荣，结盟政策使统治扩展到威尼托内陆；任期最后几年，威尼斯与已开始征服欧洲领土、日后将挑战威尼斯东方势力的奥斯曼帝国首次发生冲突。他于1400年11月23日去世，葬于圣乔凡尼保罗大教堂。

en: Antonio Zeno (c. 1330 – c. 1403) was a Venetian nobleman, brother of the navigator Nicolò Zeno and of Admiral Carlo Zeno. His fame rests on the Zeno narrative: in 1558 their descendant Nicolò Zeno the Younger published a map and letters claiming that in the 1390s Antonio and Nicolò sailed the North Atlantic at the bidding of a prince named Zichmni. The map was adopted by Gerardus Mercator, but modern scholarship generally regards the documents as a sixteenth-century forgery.
zh: 安东尼奥·泽诺（约1330—约1403）是威尼斯贵族，航海家尼科洛·泽诺与海军将领卡洛·泽诺的兄弟。他的名声来自“泽诺兄弟航行记”：1558年，他们的后裔小尼科洛·泽诺公布了一幅地图和若干信件，声称1390年代安东尼奥与尼科洛奉一位名为齐赫姆尼的亲王之命航行北大西洋。该地图曾被格拉杜斯·墨卡托采用，但现代学界普遍认为这些文献是16世纪的伪作。

en: Bartolomeo Gradenigo (1263–1342) was the 53rd Doge of Venice, elected on 7 November 1339 and in office until his death. Born into an ancient noble family, he grew rich in Eastern trade, served as podestà of Ragusa and Capodistria and as procurator in Venice, and was known for his love of luxury. Old and wealthy, he most likely spent part of his fortune on winning goodwill before the election. His three years were quiet: a gradual rapprochement with Genoa, a revolt in Crete, Turkish raids. He was nicknamed ‘the wheeler-dealer doge’ for using his influence to enrich himself and his family, and shortly before his death the ducal councillors forbade doges to abuse the office that way. Legend ties his reign to the storm of 15 February 1340, calmed by Saints Mark, George and Nicholas, whom a poor fisherman ferried across the lagoon; they left him a ring for the doge. He died on 28 December 1342.
zh: 巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈（1263—1342）是威尼斯第五十三任总督，1339年11月7日当选，在任直至去世。他出身古老的贵族家庭，靠东方贸易发家，曾出任拉古萨和卡波迪斯特里亚的波德斯塔以及威尼斯的检察官，以酷爱奢华著称。年迈而富有的他，很可能在选举前拿出了一部分家财来笼络人心。他在位三年相当平静：与热那亚逐步修好，只有克里特叛乱和土耳其人的袭扰。他因利用影响力为自己和家族敛财，得了“爱钻营的总督”的绰号，去世前不久，总督顾问便禁止总督如此滥用职权。传说1340年2月15日的大风暴与他的任期相连：圣马可、圣乔治和圣尼古拉由一名贫苦渔夫载过潟湖，平息了风浪，并留给渔夫一枚戒指转交总督。他于1342年12月28日去世。

en: Benedetto Dolfin was a Venetian patrician, the son of Enrico Dolfin, born into one of the wealthiest houses of the Venetian nobility. He was active in politics after the closing of the Great Council in 1297 and became procurator of St Mark's de supra in 1300. He foiled a conspiracy led by Marin Bocconio. His son Giovanni Dolfin, probably born around 1303, was elected doge of Venice in 1356.
zh: 贝内迪克特·多尔芬是威尼斯贵族，为恩里科·多尔芬之子，出身威尼斯最富有的世家之一。1297年大议会封闭后，他活跃于政坛，1300年出任圣马可行政长官。他粉碎了马林·博科尼奥领导的密谋。他的儿子乔瓦尼·多尔芬约生于1303年，于1356年当选威尼斯总督。

en: Bernardo de' Rossi is recorded as a knight, the only son among the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano.
zh: 贝尔纳多·德·罗西被记为骑士，是帕尔马佣兵将领彼得罗·德·罗西与卡莱斯塔诺的吉内拉·菲耶斯基六个孩子中唯一的儿子。

en: Bertuccio Contarini was a son of Andrea Contarini, the 60th doge of Venice, and his wife Costanza.
zh: 贝尔图乔·孔塔里尼是第60任威尼斯总督安德烈亚·孔塔里尼与妻子科斯坦扎之子。

en: Bertucci Gradenigo was the eldest son of Bartolomeo Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1339 to 1342. In 1328 he served as rector of Chioggia, and he died before his father, who died in December 1342.
zh: 贝尔图乔·格拉代尼戈是1339至1342年出任威尼斯总督的巴尔托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈的长子。1328年他担任基奥贾行政长官，并且先于父亲去世，其父于1342年12月离世。

en: Carlo Zeno (1333–1418) was a Venetian admiral, hero of the war against Genoa. Destined for the church, he left Padua and became a mercenary before entering Venetian service. As bailo of Negroponte he brought eighteen galleys back to Venice on 1 January 1380, in time to win the decisive Battle of Chioggia that June. He defeated the Genoese at Modon in 1403 and overthrew the Carraresi of Padua in 1405. Convicted of treason by the Council of Ten, he lost his offices and spent a year in prison. He died in Venice in 1418, honoured with a public funeral.
zh: 卡洛·泽诺（1333—1418）是威尼斯海军将领，也是对热那亚战争中的英雄。他原本被安排走教会道路，离开帕多瓦后投身为雇佣军，后来进入威尼斯服役。他任内格罗蓬特行政官时率十八艘桨帆船于1380年1月1日赶回威尼斯，及时参加了当年6月决定性的基奥贾战役。1403年他在莫东击败热那亚人，1405年推翻帕多瓦的卡拉拉家族。后来他被十人议会判叛国，剥夺职务并监禁一年。他于1418年在威尼斯去世，获赐公开葬礼。

en: Constance was the wife of the Venetian nobleman Andrea Contarini, with whom she had four children; Andrea was elected doge in 1368.
zh: 康斯坦丝是威尼斯贵族安德烈亚·孔塔里尼之妻，与他育有四个子女；安德烈亚于1368年当选总督。

en: Daniele Dolfin was a Venetian nobleman of the Dolfin family, the son of Benedetto Dolfin, Procurator of Saint Mark, and a brother of Doge Giovanni Dolfin. Unlike his brother, he never held any public office in Venice.
zh: 达尼埃莱·多尔芬是威尼斯多尔芬家族贵族，圣马可行政长官贝内代托·多尔芬之子、总督乔瓦尼·多尔芬的兄弟。与兄长不同，他未曾在威尼斯担任任何公职。

en: Domenico I Contarini (c. 1008–1071), the first doge from the great Contarini family, ruled Venice from 1041 until his death. In 1044 his support helped the patriarchate of Grado win papal recognition of its independence from Aquileia, restoring the autonomy of the church jurisdiction that included Venice. He strengthened ties with Constantinople, receiving the Byzantine title of imperial patrician by 1046 and becoming the first doge to receive the title of magister by 1064. In 1052 Emperor Henry III reaffirmed Venetian commercial privileges. Venice also reconquered Zadar and parts of Dalmatia from the Croatian kingdom. In 1063 he began rebuilding St Mark's Basilica and founded San Nicolò al Lido, where he was buried after his death in 1071.
zh: 多梅尼科一世·孔塔里尼（约1008—1071）是显赫的孔塔里尼家族出的第一位总督，1041年起统治威尼斯直至去世。1044年，在他支持下，格拉多宗主教区获得教皇承认，脱离阿奎莱亚独立，涵盖威尼斯的教会辖区也因此恢复自主。他加强与君士坦丁堡的关系，至1046年已获拜占庭帝国帕特里基奥斯的荣衔，至1064年成为首位获得“马吉斯特罗斯”头衔的总督。1052年，皇帝亨利三世重申了威尼斯的商业特权。威尼斯还从克罗地亚王国手中夺回扎达尔和达尔马提亚部分地区。1063年他动工重建圣马可大教堂，并修建了利多岛的圣尼各老堂；1071年他去世后即葬于该堂。

en: Domenico Dandolo (fl. 1085–1130s) was a Venetian merchant and head of the patrician Dandolo family. In 1085 he led an embassy to Constantinople, where Emperor Alexios I Komnenos issued a chrysobull granting the doge the title of protosebastos and the heritable rank of duke of Venice, Dalmatia and Croatia. After Pietro Polani became doge in 1130, Dandolo served at the ducal court as judge and gastald. His son Vitale was a Venetian ambassador and fathered Doge Enrico Dandolo.
zh: 多梅尼科·丹多洛（活跃于1085年至1130年代）是威尼斯商人、贵族丹多洛家族的族长。1085年，他率领使团前往君士坦丁堡，皇帝阿历克塞一世·科穆宁颁赐金玺诏书，授予总督“首席可敬者”头衔以及可世袭的威尼斯、达尔马提亚和克罗地亚公爵爵位。1130年彼得罗·波拉尼当选总督后，丹多洛以法官兼宫廷总管身份在总督宫廷供职。他的儿子维塔莱曾任威尼斯使节，是总督恩里科·丹多洛之父。

en: Domenico Contarini was a Venetian nobleman of the Contarini of Santa Maria Mater Domini and the father of Jacopo Contarini, elected the 47th doge of Venice in 1275. He may be the ducal councilor of that name recorded in 1198.
zh: 多梅尼科·孔塔里尼是威尼斯贵族，属孔塔里尼家族圣玛利亚天主之母支，是1275年当选第四十七任总督的雅科波·孔塔里尼之父，可能就是1198年文献所载的同名公爵顾问。

en: Domenico Morosini (died 1156) was doge of the Republic of Venice from 1148 until his death. He first won distinction fighting under Doge Domenico Michiel at the siege of Tyre in 1124. In 1147, as ambassador of Doge Pietro Polani to Constantinople, he negotiated with Emperor Manuel I Komnenos an alliance against the Normans, who had seized Corfu, securing renewed and expanded trading privileges for Venice, including duty-free commerce in Crete and Cyprus. Succeeding Polani, he reconciled the patrician factions that had long divided the city. His reign was marked by peace and renewed prosperity. He died in February 1156.
zh: 多梅尼科·莫罗西尼（？—1156）自1148年起担任威尼斯共和国总督，直至去世。他最早于1124年在总督多梅尼科·米基耶尔麾下参加围攻提尔之战，崭露头角。1147年，他作为总督彼得罗·波拉尼的使节前往君士坦丁堡，与曼努埃尔一世·科穆宁皇帝议定共同对抗占领科孚岛的诺曼人，为威尼斯争取到续签并扩大的贸易特权，包括在克里特与塞浦路斯免税通商。继任总督后，他弥合了长期分裂城邦的贵族派系之争，执政期间局势和平、商业重兴。他于1156年2月去世。

en: Donata Steno was a Venetian noblewoman and one of the sisters of Michele Steno, doge of Venice from 1400 to 1413, alongside Franceschina and Cristina, a Benedictine nun.
zh: 多娜塔·斯泰诺是威尼斯贵族女子，1400—1413年任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·斯泰诺的姐妹之一；他的姐妹另有弗兰切斯基娜和成为本笃会修女的克里斯蒂娜。

en: Enrico Dandolo (c. 1107–1205), a blind Venetian nobleman, was elected doge in 1192. After Byzantium imprisoned thousands of Venetians in 1171, he joined a Venetian expedition that collapsed amid plague in 1172. He later joined embassies to Constantinople, acting as a ducal legate in 1183 and helping negotiate the restoration of the Venetian quarter in 1184. In old age he led Venice into the Fourth Crusade: in 1202 the fleet he led sacked rebellious Zara, and on 12 April 1204 it stormed Constantinople, winning Venice a vast colonial empire. He accepted the Byzantine title of despot and died in Constantinople in 1205, buried in Hagia Sophia.
zh: 恩里科·丹多洛（约1107—1205）是双目失明的威尼斯贵族，1192年当选总督。拜占庭于1171年囚禁数千名威尼斯人后，他参加了威尼斯的远征，这次行动于1172年因瘟疫而瓦解。此后他参加出使君士坦丁堡的使团，1183年担任总督使节，1184年参与交涉，促成拜占庭恢复威尼斯侨民区。晚年他率领威尼斯投身第四次十字军东征：1202年，他率领的舰队洗劫了反叛的扎拉，1204年4月12日又攻陷君士坦丁堡，为威尼斯夺得了幅员辽阔的殖民帝国。他接受拜占庭式的“专制君主”头衔，1205年死于君士坦丁堡，葬于圣索菲亚大教堂。

en: Fantino Dandolo was a Venetian patrician whom Dandolo family genealogies name as the father of Andrea Dandolo, the learned doge of Venice elected in 1343, and of Simone and Agnese Dandolo.
zh: 凡蒂诺·丹多洛是威尼斯贵族，丹多洛家族家谱将他记载为1343年当选的威尼斯学者总督安德烈亚·丹多洛以及西蒙娜、阿涅塞·丹多洛的父亲。

en: Fantino Dandolo was the eldest son of Doge Andrea Dandolo and Francesca Morosini; he married Beriola Falier, a niece of a doge, and died around 1356.
zh: 凡蒂诺·丹多洛是总督安德烈·丹多洛与弗朗切斯卡·莫罗西尼的长子，娶总督的侄女贝里奥拉·法列罗为妻，约1356年去世。

en: Fantino Steno was a Venetian nobleman and a brother of Michele Steno, doge of Venice from 1400 to 1413. In 1358 he made a will naming Michele his universal heir should his wife have no children.
zh: 凡蒂诺·斯泰诺是威尼斯贵族，1400—1413年任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·斯泰诺的兄弟。1358年他立下遗嘱，规定若自己的妻子没有子嗣，便由米凯莱担任概括继承人。

en: Federico Cornaro (died 1382) was a Venetian patrician, merchant and diplomat. Trade with Cyprus made his fortune: King Peter I granted him the fief of Episkopi, which he made a major sugar plantation, and in 1365 he lent the king sixty thousand ducats. By 1379 he was the richest man in Venice. In 1368 he helped elect Doge Andrea Contarini, and in the War of Chioggia he secured Bernabò Visconti's alliance. In 1377 he married his son Pietro to Maria of Enghien, heiress of Argos and Nauplia, and ruled the lordship in the couple's name until his death. He was buried beside his brother Marco in the Frari church, where his son Giovanni later built him a funeral chapel.
zh: 费德里科·科尔纳罗（1382年卒）是威尼斯贵族、商人兼外交官。对塞浦路斯的贸易成就了他的家产：塞浦路斯国王彼得一世将埃皮斯科皮采邑封给他，他把这里建成大型甘蔗种植园，1365年又向国王放贷6万杜卡特。到1379年，他已是威尼斯首富。1368年他参与选举总督安德烈亚·孔塔里尼，基奥贾战争期间争取到贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂的同盟。1377年，他安排儿子彼得罗迎娶阿尔戈斯与纳夫普利翁的女继承人昂吉安的玛丽亚，并以这对夫妇的名义统治该领地，直至去世。他葬在弗拉里圣母堂兄弟马可的墓旁，儿子乔瓦尼后来在堂内为他建造了一座墓堂。

en: Felipa, whose family name is unrecorded, was the wife and possibly the second wife of Giovanni Gradenigo. She became dogaressa of Venice when he was elected doge in April 1355. Gradenigo died in office in August 1356.
zh: 菲莉帕是乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈之妻，可能是他的第二任妻子，家族姓氏已不可考。1355年4月丈夫当选威尼斯总督，她成为总督夫人。格拉代尼戈于1356年8月在任内去世。

en: Fiordelise (or Fiordilise) was the wife of Nicolò Gradenigo, a son of Doge Pietro Gradenigo, and her birth family is unknown. Her daughter Alucia, born by 1309, became dogaressa of Venice in 1354 as the wife of Marino Falier; she also left a daughter Engoldise.
zh: 菲奥代莉塞是威尼斯总督皮耶特罗·格拉代尼戈之子尼科洛·格拉代尼戈之妻，出身不详。其女阿卢奇亚1309年前已出生，嫁马里诺·法列罗，1354年成为总督夫人；另有女儿恩戈尔迪塞。

en: Franceschina Steno was a Venetian noblewoman and one of the sisters of Michele Steno, doge of Venice from 1400 to 1413, alongside Donata and Cristina, a Benedictine nun.
zh: 弗兰切斯基娜·斯泰诺是威尼斯贵族女子，1400—1413年任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·斯泰诺的姐妹之一；他的姐妹另有多娜塔和成为本笃会修女的克里斯蒂娜。

en: Francesco Dandolo (c. 1258–1339), one of Venice's ablest diplomats, was ambassador at Avignon to Popes Clement V and John XXII. He won the nickname Cane, dog, when he appeared before the pope wearing a chain to plead for the lifting of Venice's excommunication. Elected the fifty-second doge on 4 January 1329, he fought Mastino II della Scala of Verona for control of the Veneto trade routes. Verona's control of river trade and attempt to establish a base at Chioggia prompted Venice to form an alliance with Florence and other cities. The peace of 1337 to 1339 brought Treviso and Mestre under Venetian rule and launched Venice's expansion on the Italian mainland. Dandolo died on 1 November 1339 and was buried in the Frari.
zh: 弗朗切斯科·丹多洛（约1258—1339）是威尼斯最干练的外交家之一，曾出使阿维农，先后出使教皇克雷芒五世和约翰二十二世。他颈缠锁链出现在教皇面前，恳求解除对威尼斯的绝罚，由此得到“狗”的绰号。1329年1月4日，他当选第五十二任总督，为控制威尼托商路同维罗纳领主马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉开战。维罗纳控制河运并试图在基奥贾设立商站，促使威尼斯与佛罗伦萨等城市结盟。1337至1339年达成的和约使特雷维索和梅斯特雷归入威尼斯，开启了威尼斯在意大利本土的扩张。他于1339年11月1日去世，葬于弗拉里荣耀圣母堂。

en: Fresca de' Rossi was one of the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano, who married in 1328.
zh: 弗雷斯卡·德·罗西是帕尔马佣兵将领彼得罗·德·罗西与卡莱斯塔诺的吉内拉·菲耶斯基的六个孩子之一，两人于1328年结婚。

en: Giacomo Dandolo was a Venetian patrician of the Dandolo family's San Moisè branch, named by genealogical tradition as the father of the admiral Giberto Dandolo and grandfather of Doge Giovanni Dandolo.
zh: 贾科莫·丹多洛是威尼斯丹多洛家族圣莫伊塞支系的贵族。据谱系传统记载，他是海军将领吉尔贝托·丹多洛之父，也是威尼斯总督乔瓦尼·丹多洛的祖父。

en: Giberto Dandolo (1220–1279) was a Venetian admiral of the San Moisè branch of the Dandolo family. In 1249 he was among the electors of Doge Marino Morosini. In the spring of 1263 he led thirty-two galleys to Negroponte, threatened by Byzantine emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos, and off Settepozzi defeated a Genoese squadron, capturing four ships and killing the admiral Pietro Avvocato. Many of his men were wounded, preventing him from pursuing the surviving Genoese. From 1264 he served two years as captain and bailo at Negroponte, and he later sat six times in the Greater Council. In 1278 he was ambassador to Pope Nicholas III. He died in 1279, leaving a son Giovanni, who became doge in 1280.
zh: 吉尔贝托·丹多洛（1220—1279）是威尼斯海军将领，出身丹多洛家族的圣莫伊塞支系。1249年，他参与选举总督马里诺·莫罗西尼。1263年春，因内格罗蓬特受到拜占庭皇帝米哈伊尔八世·帕里奥洛加斯的威胁，他率领三十二艘桨帆船驰援，并在塞特波齐击败一支热那亚舰队，俘获敌船四艘，击杀热那亚舰队将领彼得罗·阿沃卡托。他的部下伤员众多，因而无法追击余下的热那亚舰队。1264年起，他以内格罗蓬特统领兼巴约的身份驻守两年，后来又六度进入大议会。1278年，他出使教皇尼古拉三世。他于1279年去世，其子乔瓦尼于1280年当选总督。

en: Ginella Fieschi was a daughter of the Genoese noble Carlo Fieschi of the counts of Lavagna and his wife Teodora. In 1328 she married the condottiero Pietro de' Rossi, lord of Parma, and bore him six children, including the knight Bernardo de' Rossi.
zh: 吉内拉·菲耶斯基是热那亚贵族、拉瓦尼亚伯爵家族的卡洛·菲耶斯基与妻子特奥多拉之女。1328年，她嫁给雇佣兵队长、帕尔马领主彼得罗·德罗西，为他生下六个子女，其中包括骑士贝尔纳多·德罗西。

en: Giovanni Dandolo, known as Cane, was a Venetian patrician of the Dandolo family's San Luca branch and the father of Francesco Dandolo, born around 1258, who was elected doge of Venice in 1329.
zh: 乔瓦尼·丹多洛人称“卡内”，是威尼斯丹多洛家族圣卢卡支系的贵族，为约1258年出生、1329年当选威尼斯总督的弗朗切斯科·丹多洛之父。

en: Giovanni Corner, called dai Santi Apostoli, was a Venetian nobleman and diplomat. With his wife Agnese he fathered Marco Corner, born in 1286, who became doge of Venice in 1365, and five other sons, among them Andrea, who held important public offices.
zh: 乔瓦尼·科尔纳罗，人称“圣使徒派”，是威尼斯贵族与外交官。他与妻子阿涅塞生有1286年出生、1365年出任威尼斯总督的马尔科·科尔纳罗，另有五个儿子，其中安德烈亚曾担任要职。

en: Giovanni Cornaro was one of the three sons Andrea Cornaro, the Venetian baron of Scarpanto, had by his first wife; after Andrea's death, his sons inherited his holdings in Crete and the Aegean islands.
zh: 乔瓦尼·科尔纳罗是威尼斯籍斯卡尔潘托男爵安德烈亚·科尔纳罗第一次婚姻所生之子；父亲死后，他与兄弟们继领家族在克里特和爱琴海诸岛的产业。

en: Giovanni Cornaro (c. 1210 – after 1291) was a Venetian nobleman and diplomat of the Cornaro dalla Sbarra branch, son of Andrea Cornaro and Marietta Contarini. First recorded in 1238 as envoy to Pope Gregory IX over trade disputes with Genoa, he later served at Emperor Frederick II's court and helped elect Marino Morosini doge in 1249. In 1274 he attended the Second Council of Lyon, and in 1291, as Procurator of Saint Mark, led an embassy to his grandnephew King Andrew III of Hungary. His son Marco was grandfather of Doge Marco Cornaro.
zh: 乔瓦尼·科尔纳罗（约1210年生，1291年后在世）是威尼斯贵族与外交官，出身科尔纳罗家族斯巴拉支，为安德烈亚·科尔纳罗与玛丽埃塔·孔塔里尼之子。1238年首次见于记载，奉命出使教皇格列高利九世，交涉威尼斯与热那亚的贸易争端；其后他在皇帝腓特烈二世的宫廷任职，1249年参与推选马里诺·莫罗西尼为总督。1274年他出席第二次里昂公会议，1291年以圣马可行政长官身份率使团出使匈牙利国王、他的甥外孙安德烈三世。其子马尔科是总督马尔科·科尔纳罗的祖父。

en: Giovanni Dandolo (c. 1240–1289), son of the admiral Giberto Dandolo, was elected the forty-eighth doge of Venice on 31 March 1280 while campaigning against Istria and Trieste. Before his election he had served as podestà of Bologna and Padua and commanded Venetian naval forces. His reign saw wars against the Patriarchate of Aquileia, the papal states and Ancona, and a Cretan revolt led by Alexios Kallergis and backed by Emperor Michael VIII. When Venice refused to join a papal attack on Sicily, Pope Martin IV excommunicated the Republic; Honorius IV lifted the sentence in 1285. In 1284 Dandolo issued Venice's first gold ducat, a coin accepted throughout its trading network. He died on 2 November 1289 and was buried at San Zanipolo.
zh: 乔瓦尼·丹多洛（约1240—1289）是海军将领吉尔贝托·丹多洛之子，1280年3月31日在征讨伊斯特拉和的里雅斯特时当选第四十八任威尼斯总督。当选前，他曾任博洛尼亚和帕多瓦的长官，并指挥威尼斯海军。他在位期间战事不断，先后与阿奎莱亚牧首区、教皇国和安科纳交战，并应对由阿历克塞·卡莱尔吉斯领导、拜占庭皇帝米哈伊尔八世支持的克里特叛乱。威尼斯拒绝参加教皇进攻西西里的行动后，教皇马丁四世将共和国革出教门，洪诺留四世于1285年解除这一处罚。1284年，丹多洛发行了威尼斯第一枚金杜卡特，这种金币在威尼斯的贸易网络中通行。他于1289年11月2日去世，葬于圣乔凡尼保罗大堂。

en: Giovanni Dandolo was a Venetian nobleman, son of the jurist Vitale Dandolo and brother of Doge Enrico Dandolo. He accompanied Enrico to Constantinople in 1170 and 1183, and in 1184 brought home large sums from the estates there of his uncle, the patriarch of Grado.
zh: 乔瓦尼·丹多洛是威尼斯贵族，法学家维塔莱·丹多洛之子、总督恩里科·丹多洛之弟。他于1170年和1183年随恩里科出使君士坦丁堡，1184年处理叔父、格拉多宗主教在当地的产业并带回大笔财富。

en: Giovanni Dolfin (c. 1303–1361) was the 57th Doge of Venice, elected on 13 August 1356 while leading the defence of Treviso against a besieging Hungarian army. Refused safe conduct, he broke through the encirclement to reach Venice for his enthronement. As doge he fought on against Louis I of Hungary, but defeat at Nervesa in February 1358 forced the Treaty of Zadar, by which Venice lost Dalmatia, Zara and Split while keeping naval predominance in the Adriatic. In 1358–1359 Padua threatened Venetian trade on the Brenta and forced Venice to stop trading with Egypt, contributing to an economic crisis. Dolfin had lost the sight of one eye to a battle wound. He died on 12 July 1361 and was buried in San Giovanni e Paolo.
zh: 乔瓦尼·多尔芬（约1303—1361）是威尼斯第五十七任总督。1356年8月13日当选时，他正指挥守卫被匈牙利军队围困的特雷维索；敌人拒绝给予安全通行，他便突围返回威尼斯就任。任内他继续与匈牙利国王路易一世作战，但1358年2月在内尔韦萨战败，被迫签订《扎达尔条约》，威尼斯丧失达尔马提亚、扎拉和斯普利特，仅保住亚得里亚海的海军优势。1358—1359年，帕多瓦威胁威尼斯在布伦塔河上的贸易，迫使威尼斯停止与埃及通商，加剧了经济危机。多尔芬曾因战伤失去一只眼睛的视力。他于1361年7月12日去世，葬于圣乔凡尼保罗大教堂。

en: Giovanni Gradenigo (c. 1279–1356), nicknamed Nason for his large nose, became the 56th Doge of Venice on 21 April 1355, in the wake of Marino Falier's execution for treason. He was a son of Marino Gradenigo, who died in Crete as duke of Candia, and Maria Dandolo. Gruff and austere, a man many avoided, he was nonetheless known as fiercely loyal to the Republic, which counted for most after a career as podestà of Capodistria, Padua and Treviso. In June, with the city frightened by conspiracies at home, he made peace with Genoa and ended a long, losing war; conspirators against Venice were executed, and measures were taken against the Republic's money troubles. Early in 1356 war broke out again on the mainland and in Dalmatia, a conflict that his successor Giovanni Dolfin would end at Zadar on bad terms. Gradenigo died on 8 August 1356, with little mark left on the state.
zh: 乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈（约1279—1356）因鼻子硕大得到绰号“大鼻子”，是威尼斯第五十六任总督。他是马里诺·格拉代尼戈与玛丽亚·丹多洛之子，父亲死于克里特，生前任康迪亚公爵。他性情严厉粗粝，许多人对他避之不及，却以对共和国忠心耿耿著称；在曾任卡波迪斯特里亚、帕多瓦和特雷维索的波德斯塔之后，这份忠诚成了他当选的最大筹码。1355年4月21日，在前任马里诺·法列罗因叛国被处斩之后，他当选总督。6月，国内阴谋频发，人心惶惶，他与热那亚媾和，结束了长期而不利的战争；密谋反对威尼斯的人被处决，共和国也着手应对财政困难。1356年初，战火在大陆和达尔马提亚重燃，这场战争要到继任者乔瓦尼·多尔芬手里才以不利的条件在扎拉收场。格拉代尼戈于1356年8月8日去世，没有在国政上留下多少印记。

en: Giovanni Gradenigo was a son of Bartolomeo Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1339 to 1342, and is recorded as having pursued a successful career in political, military and diplomatic offices.
zh: 乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈是1339至1342年任威尼斯总督的巴尔托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子，据载在政治、军事和外交职务上仕途顺利。

en: Giovanni Morosini was a 13th-century Venetian nobleman. His daughter Tommasina Morosini married Pietro Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1289, and was a niece of Tomasina Morosini, the Venetian-born queen of Hungary and mother of King Andrew III.
zh: 乔瓦尼·莫罗西尼是13世纪威尼斯贵族。其女托马西娜·莫罗西尼嫁给1289年就任的威尼斯总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈，她也是出生于威尼斯的匈牙利王后、安德烈三世之母托马西娜的侄女。

en: Giovanni Soranzo (c. 1245–1328), a former admiral, diplomat and Procurator of Saint Mark, was elected the 51st Doge of Venice on 13 July 1312. In 1296, during the war with Genoa, he led a fleet to the Bosphorus, captured an enemy galley and raided Caffa in Crimea. He withdrew to Negroponte in autumn and returned to honours in Venice. As podestà of Ferrara in 1308–1309 he faced Pope Clement V, who placed Venice under interdict before taking the city. Soranzo then failed to recover the lower Po with a fleet. In 1310, after the failed Tiepolo conspiracy, he negotiated Baiamonte Tiepolo's surrender. His dogate repaired relations with the papacy, and he received Dante in Venice in 1321.
zh: 乔瓦尼·索兰佐（约1245—1328）曾任舰队司令、外交官与圣马可行政长官，1312年7月13日当选第五十一任威尼斯总督。1296年对热那亚作战期间，他率舰队驶向博斯普鲁斯海峡，俘获一艘敌舰，并劫掠了克里米亚的卡法。秋天他撤至内格罗蓬特，返回威尼斯后受到隆重欢迎。1308至1309年他出任费拉拉长官，与教皇克雷芒五世对峙；教皇先对威尼斯施以禁罚，随后夺取该城。索兰佐接着率舰队收复波河下游，却遭失败。1310年蒂耶波洛阴谋失败后，他与巴亚蒙特·蒂耶波洛谈判，促成其投降。他任内修复了威尼斯与教廷的关系，并于1321年在威尼斯接待了但丁。

en: Giovanni Steno was a Venetian nobleman of the parish of Santa Maria del Giglio who married Lucia Lando and fathered Michele Steno, doge of Venice from 1400 to 1413. He held several senior public posts and died in 1352 fighting the Genoese at the Bosporus.
zh: 乔瓦尼·斯泰诺是居住在圣玛利亚·德尔·吉廖堂区的威尼斯贵族，娶露琪亚·兰多，是1400—1413年任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·斯泰诺之父。他曾担任多项重要公职，1352年在博斯普鲁斯与热那亚人作战时身亡。

en: Iacopo Falier was a Venetian patrician of the Faliero family's Santi Apostoli branch. With his wife Beriola Loredan he fathered Marino Faliero, elected doge of Venice in 1354 and executed after his failed coup, and the sons Ordelaffo and Marco.
zh: 雅各布·法列罗是威尼斯法列罗家族圣宗徒堂支系的贵族。他与妻子贝里奥拉·洛雷丹生有马里诺·法列罗——后者于1354年当选威尼斯总督，政变失败后被处决——以及奥尔代拉福、马可两个儿子。

en: Isabella de' Rossi was one of the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano, who married in 1328.
zh: 伊莎贝拉·德·罗西是帕尔马佣兵将领彼得罗·德·罗西与卡莱斯塔诺的吉内拉·菲耶斯基的六个孩子之一，两人于1328年结婚。

en: Jacopo Contarini (c. 1193–1280), the 47th doge of Venice, was born into the Contarini of Santa Maria Mater Domini. In 1265 he negotiated at Constantinople with Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos a truce Venice never ratified. Elected doge on 6 September 1275 as a compromise candidate, he was already in his eighties and let the councils rule through famine, plague and the wars with Ancona and Capodistria; a truce with Byzantium followed in 1278. He abdicated on 6 March 1280, retired to a monastery and died on 6 April. By his wife Jacobina he left sons Giovanni, Pietro and Marino.
zh: 雅科波·孔塔里尼（约1193—1280）是威尼斯第四十七任总督，出身孔塔里尼家族圣玛利亚天主之母支。1265年，他在君士坦丁堡与皇帝米哈伊尔八世·帕里奥洛加斯议定一项停战，威尼斯却始终未予批准。1275年9月6日，已年逾八旬的他作为妥协人选当选总督，任内把政务交给诸委员会，威尼斯连遭饥荒、瘟疫，又与安科纳和卡波迪斯特里亚交战，1278年与拜占庭达成停战。他于1280年3月6日退位，退隐修道院，4月6日去世。妻子雅各比娜生有乔瓦尼、彼得罗和马里诺。

en: Jacopo Tiepolo (c. 1170–1249) served as Doge of Venice from 1229 until his abdication in May 1249. A merchant trading with Constantinople in 1190, he became the first Venetian Duke of Crete (1209–1214). He called on Marco Sanudo to help suppress the Greek revolt of 1211, then persuaded him to abandon his own claims on the island. He was twice Podestà of Constantinople, signing treaties with Nicaea and the Sultanate of Rum. As doge he codified civil law and established the Venetian Senate. From 1237 he fought Emperor Frederick II: his son Pietro was captured at Cortenuova and executed in 1240, when Venice also seized Ferrara. Tiepolo reconquered Pula in 1242, abdicated in May 1249 and died two months later.
zh: 雅科波·提埃坡罗（约1170—1249）1229年出任威尼斯总督，直至1249年5月退位。1190年他曾与君士坦丁堡经商，后来成为首任由威尼斯人担任的克里特公爵（1209—1214）。他请马尔科·萨努多协助镇压1211年的希腊人起义，随后说服萨努多放弃对该岛的主张。他还两度出任君士坦丁堡长官，与尼西亚和鲁姆苏丹国签订条约。任总督期间，他主持编纂民法、设立威尼斯元老院。1237年起他与皇帝腓特烈二世交战：其子彼得罗在科尔泰诺瓦被俘，1240年被处死，同年威尼斯攻占费拉拉。提埃坡罗于1242年收复普拉，1249年5月退位，两个月后去世。

en: Leonardo Dandolo (1326–1406) was a Venetian nobleman, the younger son of Doge Andrea Dandolo and Francesca Morosini. He held a series of senior offices in the republic and served as a Venetian ambassador, dying on 16 January 1406.
zh: 莱奥纳尔多·丹多洛（1326—1406）是威尼斯贵族，总督安德烈亚·丹多洛与弗兰切斯卡·莫罗西尼的幼子。他曾在共和国担任一系列要职，并出任过威尼斯使节，于1406年1月16日去世。

en: Lorenzo Celsi (1310–1365) was a naval commander and diplomat from a family that had stayed out of public life, so his election as the 58th doge of Venice on 16 July 1361 came as a surprise. As captain of the sea in 1353 he took Genoese ships while escorting grain convoys. From 1359 he was ambassador to Emperor Charles IV, seeking recognition of Venetian rule over Treviso and Conegliano. Deadlocked electors settled on him for his victories over the Genoese. His reign saw a feud between hardliners and moderates over the ruling oligarchy, and the Cretan revolt of 1363, whose suppression he celebrated with lavish festivities. His style was sovereign: a servant walked before him with a rod like a sceptre. The Council of Ten put him on trial, perhaps just before or after his death on 18 July 1365; the next day the doge's oath was tightened. He left only daughters and was buried at Santa Maria della Celestia.
zh: 洛伦佐·切尔西（1310—1365）是海军将领与外交官，出身的家族一向置身公共事务之外，所以1361年7月16日他当选威尼斯第五十八任总督，实属意外。1353年他任海上统帅，在为运粮船队护航时俘获多艘热那亚船只。1359年起，他出使神圣罗马帝国皇帝查理四世，寻求皇帝承认威尼斯对特雷维索和科内利亚诺的统治。僵持不下的选举人最后看中他对热那亚人的战绩。他任内，强硬派与温和派围绕统治寡头集团争斗不休，1363年又爆发克里特岛起义，镇压成功后他举行了铺张的庆典。他的排场如同君主：仆人手持权杖般的短杖走在他前面。十人议会对他提起审判，时间可能在他1365年7月18日去世前后；次日，总督的就职誓约被收紧。他只留下女儿，葬于切莱斯蒂亚圣母堂。

en: Lorenzo Tiepolo (died 16 August 1275), son of Doge Jacopo Tiepolo, was Doge of Venice from 23 July 1268 until his death. A commander in the War of Saint Sabas against Genoa, he broke the siege of the Venetian quarter at Acre and in 1258 drove the Genoese from the city. In 1262 he took part in peace negotiations with William of Villehardouin, Prince of Achaea, whose vassal he was for Skopelos and Skyros. He was elected doge with 25 of 41 votes. As doge he made peace with Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and, at Cremona in 1270, with Genoa. A trade war with Bologna and its allies from 1270 ended in 1273 with Venice confirmed in control of the Po, after an initial Venetian setback in 1271.
zh: 洛伦佐·提埃坡罗（1275年8月16日卒）是总督雅科波·提埃坡罗之子，1268年7月23日当选威尼斯总督，在任直至去世。对热那亚的圣萨巴战争中，他率军解除了热那亚人对阿卡威尼斯街区的围困，并于1258年将热那亚人逐出该城。1262年他参加了与亚该亚亲王纪尧姆·德·维勒阿杜安的和谈，他因持有斯科派洛斯和斯基罗斯两岛而成为亲王的封臣。他以41票中的25票当选总督。任总督后，他与皇帝米海尔八世·巴列奥略媾和，又于1270年在克雷莫纳与热那亚议和。1270年起与博洛尼亚及其盟邦的贸易战于1273年结束，威尼斯对波河的控制权得到确认，此前威尼斯人曾于1271年受挫。

en: Luca Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman, the son of Marino Gradenigo, who died serving as Duke of Crete, and Maria Dandolo, and one of the brothers of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo.
zh: 卢卡·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，父亲马里诺·格拉代尼戈曾任干地亚公爵、卒于克里特，母亲是玛丽亚·丹多洛；他是总督乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈的兄弟之一。

en: Luca Gradenigo was a son of Giovanni Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1355 to 1356. The doge's five sons all took part in Venetian politics, but Luca and his brothers never obtained prominent positions in the Republic.
zh: 卢卡·格拉代尼戈是1355至1356年的威尼斯总督乔万尼·格拉代尼戈之子。总督的五个儿子都参与过威尼斯政治，但卢卡与兄弟们始终没有得到共和国的显要职位。

en: Luca Gradenigo was one of the sons of Bartolomeo Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1339 to 1342.
zh: 卢卡·格拉代尼戈是1339至1342年任威尼斯总督的巴尔托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈的儿子之一。

en: Luchina de' Rossi was a daughter of the Parmesan condottiero Pietro de' Rossi, lord of Parma, who was killed at the siege of Monselice in 1337. She and her five siblings, among them her sister Teodora, are recorded in their father's genealogy.
zh: 卢奇娜·德·罗西是帕尔马雇佣军首领、帕尔马领主彼得罗·德·罗西之女，其父于1337年围攻蒙塞利切时战死。她与特奥多拉等五名兄弟姐妹载于父亲的家谱中。

en: Lucia Lando was a Venetian noblewoman, the wife of Giovanni Steno and mother of Michele Steno, doge of Venice from 1400 to 1413. Her husband died fighting the Genoese at the Bosporus in 1352; her other children were Fantino, Franceschina and Donata.
zh: 露西娅·兰多是威尼斯贵族女性，嫁与乔瓦尼·斯特诺，1400至1413年担任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·斯特诺即其所生。丈夫1352年在博斯普鲁斯与热那亚人作战时身亡，她的其他子女有凡蒂诺、弗兰切斯奇娜与多纳塔。

en: Luigia de' Rossi was one of the six children of the Parmese condottiero Pietro de' Rossi and Ginella Fieschi of Calestano, who married in 1328.
zh: 路易贾·德·罗西是帕尔马佣兵将领彼得罗·德·罗西与卡莱斯塔诺的吉内拉·菲耶斯基的六个孩子之一，两人于1328年结婚。

en: Marco Cornaro (c. 1286–1368) came from one of Venice's oldest and richest families and made his own fortune in the Egypt trade. In 1337, in the war against the Scaligeri, he became podestà of Padua after Marsilio da Carrara negotiated its handover. As count of Zara he took refuge in the citadel when the city rose against Venice on 4 May 1345, and was rescued by Pietro Canal with five galleys; he later served as duke of Candia. In April 1355 the patricians met in his house to answer Faliero's coup, and Cornaro, put in charge of the defence, headed the Republic between Faliero's execution on 17 April and Giovanni Gradenigo's election four days later. His second wife Caterina's low birth made his own election difficult. Elected doge on 21 July 1365, he presided over economic growth overshadowed by territorial losses to Genoa and the Ottomans, and died on 13 January 1368.
zh: 马可·科尔纳罗（约1286—1368）出身威尼斯最古老、最富有的家族之一，自己的财富则来自对埃及的贸易。1337年，在对斯卡拉家族的战争中，马尔西利奥·达·卡拉拉谈妥交出帕多瓦，他随后出任该城行政长官。身为扎达尔伯爵，1345年5月4日城中反叛威尼斯时，他退守城堡，由皮埃特罗·卡纳尔率五艘桨帆船救出；后来他还出任干地亚公爵。1355年4月，贵族们聚在他家商议如何应对法列罗的政变，他受命主持城防，在4月17日法列罗被处决到四天后乔万尼·格拉代尼戈当选之间，执掌共和国。他的第二任妻子卡泰丽娜出身低微，使他的总督选举遇到阻力。1365年7月21日他当选总督，任内经济有所增长，但领土被热那亚和奥斯曼人蚕食；他于1368年1月13日去世。

en: Marco Cornaro was a son of Andrea Cornaro, the Venetian baron of Scarpanto, by his first wife; after Andrea's death, his sons inherited his holdings in Crete and the Aegean islands.
zh: 马可·科尔纳罗是威尼斯籍斯卡尔潘托男爵安德烈亚·科尔纳罗第一次婚姻所生之子；父亲死后，他与兄弟们继领家族在克里特和爱琴海诸岛的产业。

en: Marco Cornaro was the only recorded son of the Venetian diplomat Giovanni Cornaro; his son Giovanni Corner dai Santi Apostoli was the father of Marco Cornaro, doge of Venice from 1365 to 1368.
zh: 马尔科·科尔纳罗是威尼斯外交官乔瓦尼·科尔纳罗唯一见于记载的儿子；他的儿子乔瓦尼·科尔纳罗（圣使徒派）是1365至1368年任威尼斯总督的马尔科·科尔纳罗之父。

en: Marco Dandolo was a son of the Venetian Fantino Dandolo of the San Luca branch and a brother of Andrea Dandolo, doge of Venice.
zh: 马可·丹多洛是威尼斯圣卢卡支系的凡蒂诺·丹多洛之子，威尼斯总督安德烈亚·丹多洛的兄弟。

en: Marco Falier was a Venetian nobleman of the ancient Falier family, the son of Jacopo Falier and Beriola Loredan, and one of the brothers of Doge Marino Faliero, executed after his failed coup in 1355.
zh: 马尔科·法列罗是威尼斯古老法列罗家族的贵族，雅各布·法列罗与贝里奥拉·洛雷丹之子，为1355年政变失败后被处决的总督马里诺·法列罗的兄弟之一。

en: Marco Gradenigo (c. 1224–c. 1274) was a 13th-century Venetian noble and naval commander. In 1255 he led galleys to Negroponte and forced its surrender after a thirteen-month siege; as bailo from 1256 he built a league of Latin Greek lords against William of Villehardouin of Achaea, defeated at Karydi in 1258. As Podestà of Constantinople, his fleet was away attacking Daphnousia in July 1261 when Nicaean troops retook the city, and he evacuated the fleeing Latin emperor Baldwin II to Negroponte. He later led ten galleys under Jacopo Dondulo in the victory over Genoa at Trapani in 1266. He served as ducal councillor and commanded Venetian forces in the war with Bologna in 1270.
zh: 马可·格拉代尼戈（约1224—约1274）是13世纪威尼斯贵族与海军将领。1255年他率桨帆船驰援内格罗蓬特，围城十三个月后迫使该城投降；1256年起出任巴伊洛，联合希腊拉丁诸领主对抗亚该亚亲王纪尧姆·德·维勒阿杜安，却于1258年在卡里迪之战中被击败。担任君士坦丁堡波德斯塔期间，1261年7月他率舰队出击达夫努西亚，尼西亚军队趁机收复君士坦丁堡，他只得将出逃的拉丁皇帝鲍德温二世撤至内格罗蓬特。此后他在雅科波·东多洛麾下率十艘桨帆船参加1266年大胜热那亚的特拉帕尼海战。他曾任公爵顾问，并于1270年在对博洛尼亚的战争中指挥威尼斯军队。

en: Marco Gradenigo was one of the sons of Bartolomeo Gradenigo, doge of Venice from 1339 to 1342.
zh: 马尔科·格拉代尼戈是1339至1342年任威尼斯总督的巴尔托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈的儿子之一。

en: Marco Morosini, father of the Venetian chronicler Antonio Morosini, may have been a son of Marino Morosini and a brother of Doge Michele Morosini.
zh: 马尔科·莫罗西尼是威尼斯编年史家安东尼奥·莫罗西尼的父亲，可能是马里诺·莫罗西尼之子、总督米凯莱·莫罗西尼的兄弟。

en: Margaret (born c. 1310) was the wife of Marsilio de' Rossi, the Parmese condottiero and imperial vicar of Parma who fought for Venice against the Scaligers and died in Venice in August 1337. She was the mother of his daughter Teresa.
zh: 玛格丽特（约1310年生）是帕尔马雇佣兵首领、帕尔马帝国代理官马尔西利奥·德·罗西之妻。马尔西利奥曾为威尼斯效力、对抗斯卡拉家族，1337年8月死于威尼斯。她为丈夫生下女儿特蕾莎。

en: Maria, whose family name is unknown, was the wife of Lorenzo Celsi and dogaressa of Venice from his election in 1361. She was the mother of his only surviving daughters, Anna and Orsa, and was widowed by his death in July 1365.
zh: 玛丽亚的家族姓氏不详，她是洛伦佐·切尔西之妻，1361年丈夫当选后成为威尼斯总督夫人。她所生的女儿中只有安娜与奥尔莎存活，1365年7月切尔西去世后她成为寡妇。

en: Later genealogical tradition names Maria Dandolo as a daughter of Giovanni Dandolo, doge of Venice from 1280 to 1289, and the wife of the Venetian patrician Marino Gradenigo.
zh: 根据后世谱系传统，玛丽亚·丹多洛是1280至1289年任威尼斯总督的乔瓦尼·丹多洛之女，嫁给威尼斯贵族马里诺·格拉代尼戈。

en: Marino Contarini was a son of Andrea Contarini, the 60th doge of Venice, and his wife Costanza.
zh: 马里诺·孔塔里尼是第60任威尼斯总督安德烈亚·孔塔里尼与妻子科斯坦扎之子。

en: Marino Dandolo (died before 1243) was a Venetian nobleman who became the first Latin ruler of the island of Andros. In 1207 he joined Marco Sanudo's conquest of the Aegean islands and received Andros as a fief of the new Duchy of Naxos, and he helped build the castle in the island's capital. Around 1239 Geremia Ghisi, lord of the northern Aegean islands of Sciathos, Scopelos and Sciros, expelled him from Andros. Marino died in exile before August 1243. His wife Felicia kept half the island and later married Jacopo Querini.
zh: 马里诺·丹多洛（1243年前卒）是威尼斯贵族，成为爱琴海岛屿安德罗斯的第一位拉丁统治者。1207年，他随马尔科·萨努多征服爱琴海诸岛，受封安德罗斯，作为新建立的纳克索斯公国的附庸领地，并参与修建岛上首府的城堡。约1239年，据有斯基亚索斯、斯科派洛斯和斯基罗斯等爱琴海北部岛屿的杰雷米亚·吉西将他逐出安德罗斯。马里诺在流亡中于1243年8月前去世。他的妻子费利恰仍保有半个岛屿，后来改嫁雅各布·奎里尼。

en: Marino Falier (c. 1274–1355) was the 55th Doge of Venice, born into one of its oldest patrician houses. He had headed the Council of Ten from 1315, served as bailo of Negroponte from 1323. Elected doge on 11 September 1354 at about eighty, while ambassador to Pope Innocent VI at Avignon, he came home on 5 October to a Republic at war with Genoa, and on 4 November the Genoese destroyed the Venetian fleet at Sapienza. By April 1355 he was plotting with commoners to cut down the patricians and rule as prince. Tradition traces his grievance to a slight at the Carnival feast, though the best-known details are legend. The plot was betrayed on 14 April, and he was beheaded in the Ducal Palace courtyard on 17 April. In 1366 the Council of Ten had his portrait in the Great Council hall effaced and an inscription recording his treason put in its place.
zh: 马里诺·法列罗（约1274—1355）是威尼斯第五十五任总督，出身威尼斯最古老的贵族世家之一。他自1315年起出任十人团首领，1323年起任内格罗蓬特巴伊洛。1354年9月11日他当选总督时已年约八旬，正以使节身份在阿维尼翁觐见教皇英诺森六世；他10月5日回到威尼斯，共和国正与热那亚交战，11月4日热那亚人在萨皮恩扎歼灭了威尼斯舰队。至1355年4月，他已在与平民密谋铲除贵族、自立为君。传统上认为，他的怨恨起于狂欢节宴会上受到的冒犯，但最著名的细节出自传说。阴谋于4月14日败露，他于4月17日在总督宫庭院被斩首。1366年，十人团下令抹去他在大议事厅的肖像，并在原处写上记录其叛国之罪的铭文。

en: Marino Gradenigo (c. 1250–c. 1283) was a Venetian noble, the elder son of the admiral Marco Gradenigo and brother of Doge Pietro Gradenigo. He pursued a political and diplomatic career and governed Crete as Duke of Candia. He died on the island while still in office; his son Giovanni Gradenigo was elected doge in 1355.
zh: 马里诺·格拉代尼戈（约1250—约1283）是威尼斯贵族，海军将领马可·格拉代尼戈的长子、总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈之兄。他曾从事政治和外交活动，出任干地亚公爵，管辖克里特岛。他在任内卒于克里特，其子乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈后来于1355年当选总督。

en: Marino Gradenigo was a son of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo. He and his brothers took part in Venetian public life but never reached high office.
zh: 马里诺·格拉代尼戈是总督乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈之子。他与兄弟们参与过威尼斯的公共事务，但从未担任高官。

en: Marino Contarini was a Venetian nobleman, one of at least three sons of Jacopo Contarini, doge of Venice from 1275 to 1280, and his wife Jacobina; his brothers were Giovanni and Pietro Contarini.
zh: 马里诺·孔塔里尼是威尼斯贵族，为1275至1280年出任威尼斯总督的雅各布·孔塔里尼与其妻雅各比娜至少三个儿子之一，兄弟有乔瓦尼·孔塔里尼和彼得罗·孔塔里尼。

en: Marino Morosini (1181–1253) was doge of Venice from June 1249 until his death. Of the Morosini dalla Tressa branch, he served as ambassador, Duke of Candia and Procurator of Saint Mark's, and his election was the first by forty-one electors. His short reign brought prudent commercial policy and new trade treaties. When Louis IX of France crusaded against Egypt, Venice stayed neutral to safeguard its trade with the sultan. He admitted an inquisition court but reserved appointment of its judges, and created the Signori di Notte magistracy. He died on 1 January 1253 and was buried in Saint Mark's.
zh: 马里诺·莫罗西尼（1181—1253）自1249年6月起担任威尼斯总督，直至去世。他出身莫罗西尼家族“德拉特雷萨”支，当选前历任使节、干地亚公爵与圣马可行政长官；他也是首次由四十一名大选举人选出的总督。他短暂而太平的在任时期以审慎的商业政策和多项新商约著称。法王路易九世发动远征埃及时，威尼斯为维持与埃及苏丹的通商协定而保持中立。他准许宗教裁判所在威尼斯设立法庭，但坚持法官由共和国任命，还设立了“夜巡官”警务机构。他于1253年1月1日去世，葬于圣马可教堂。

en: Marino Morosini was a Venetian patrician and a son of the admiral and statesman Albertino Morosini, who made his will in 1305.
zh: 马里诺·莫罗西尼是威尼斯贵族，为海军将领兼政治家阿尔贝蒂诺·莫罗西尼之子，阿尔贝蒂诺于1305年立下遗嘱。

en: Marino Morosini was a Venetian nobleman, a son of Doge Domenico Morosini. In 1152 he commanded a Venetian fleet against Ancona, whose ships raided Venetian commerce, and quickly induced the city to conclude a treaty of friendship.
zh: 马里诺·莫罗西尼是威尼斯贵族，为总督多梅尼科·莫罗西尼之子。1152年，他奉命率领威尼斯舰队进攻安科纳——该城船只曾袭扰威尼斯商船——很快促使安科纳订立友好条约。

en: Marino Zorzi (c. 1238–1312) was the 50th doge of Venice, elected on 23 August 1311 after the death of Pietro Gradenigo. A seasoned diplomat, he had been ambassador to Pope Benedict XI in 1303 and was nicknamed ‘il Santo’ for his piety. Elected after the Tiepolo conspiracy of 1310 and the papal interdict over Ferrara, he failed to repair relations with Rome. A campaign against rebellious Zara ended in defeat, while a 1312 treaty with Padua settled Brenta navigation disputes. His reign lasted less than eleven months; he died on 3 July 1312.
zh: 马里诺·佐尔齐（约1238—1312）是第50任威尼斯总督，1311年8月23日在彼得罗·格拉代尼戈去世后当选。他是老练的外交家，1303年曾出使觐见教皇本笃十一世，因虔诚被称为‘圣人’。他在1310年蒂耶波洛阴谋和费拉拉战争引发的教皇禁令之后上台，却未能修复与罗马的关系。威尼斯征讨叛乱的扎拉失利，而1312年与帕多瓦签订的条约解决了布伦塔河航运争端。他在位不足11个月，于1312年7月3日去世。

en: Marsilio de' Rossi (1287–1337) was the soldier of the brothers who ran Parma, an Emilian condottiero and son of Guglielmo de' Rossi. In 1307 he served as captain of the people at Bologna, and in Carrara service was captured by Cangrande della Scala at Vicenza in 1314. Back in Parma from 1323, he joined his brother Rolando in driving out the Sanvitale. When Emperor Louis IV came down into Italy he sided with the Empire, and became imperial vicar of Parma and then of Lombardy; he took power in Parma himself when Rolando was arrested at Bologna in 1329. He was knighted after the battle of San Felice in 1332. When the Rossi fell in 1335 he fled to Venice and led one of its three armies against the Scaligers. He died on 16 August 1337, a week after his brother Pietro, who had held the supreme command. The historian Ireneo Affò judged that he joined courage with good sense.
zh: 马西利奥·德·罗西（1287—1337）是执掌帕尔马的罗西兄弟中的武将，艾米利亚佣兵将领，帕尔马的古列尔莫·德·罗西之子。1307年他出任博洛尼亚的人民队长，后为卡拉拉家族效力，1314年在维琴察被坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉俘获。1323年回到帕尔马后，他与兄长罗兰多一道逐走圣维塔莱家族。皇帝路易四世南下意大利后，他倒向帝国一方，受任帕尔马、继而伦巴第的帝国代理人；1329年罗兰多在博洛尼亚被捕，他接掌了帕尔马的大权。1332年圣费利切战役后获封骑士。1335年罗西家族失势，他逃往威尼斯，统领威尼斯三支大军之一对斯卡拉家族作战。1337年8月16日，他在曾任威尼斯军队最高统帅的弟弟彼得罗去世一周后病逝。历史学家伊雷内奥·阿弗奥评价他勇武而兼有智谋。

en: Matteo Zorzi was a member of the rising Venetian noble house of Zorzi and the father of Marino Zorzi, elected doge of Venice in 1311. His wife was named Maria, though her family name is unrecorded; nothing else of his life is known.
zh: 马泰奥·佐尔齐是崛起中的威尼斯贵族佐尔齐家族成员，其子马里诺·佐尔齐于1311年当选威尼斯总督。他的妻子名叫玛丽亚，姓氏失载，此外事迹不可考。

en: Michele Morosini was a Venetian nobleman, one of the four legitimate children of the statesman Albertino Morosini and his wife Marchesina, alongside Marino, Cubitosa and Caterina.
zh: 米凯莱·莫罗西尼是威尼斯贵族，为政治家阿尔贝蒂诺·莫罗西尼与妻子马尔凯西娜的四个婚生子女之一，同马里诺、库比托萨和卡泰丽娜为兄弟姐妹。

en: Michele Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman, the son of Marino Gradenigo, Duke of Crete, and Maria Dandolo, and a brother of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo.
zh: 米凯莱·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，父亲是曾任干地亚公爵的马里诺·格拉代尼戈，母亲为玛丽亚·丹多洛，他是总督乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈的兄弟之一。

en: Michele Morosini (1308–1382) was doge of Venice for only four months, from 10 June to 16 October 1382. Born into one of the city's most important families, he was extremely wealthy and made his name in trade. During the gruelling War of Chioggia against Genoa (1378–1381) he bought houses cheaply while the city struggled, and by the war's end he was counted among the richest men in Venice. Opinion of him divided: Marin Sanudo saw a noble merchant who gave generously to the state and served it faithfully, while others saw a speculator ready to do anything to be noticed. Elected after Andrea Contarini's death, he died of the plague and was buried at San Zanipolo, the traditional resting place of the doges. His wife was Cristina Condulmer.
zh: 米凯莱·莫罗西尼（1308—1382）担任威尼斯总督仅四个月，自1382年6月10日至10月16日。他出身威尼斯最显赫的家族之一，家财万贯，以经商闻名。1378至1381年威尼斯与热那亚进行惨烈的基奥贾战争，城中艰难，他趁机低价买下大量房产，战争结束时已被视为威尼斯最富有的人之一。世人对他评价不一：马林·萨努多视他为慷慨捐输、忠心事国的贵族商人，也有人视他为不择手段、只求出头的投机客。他在安德烈亚·孔塔里尼去世后当选总督，不久死于瘟疫，葬于历代总督传统的安葬地圣若望及保禄堂。妻子是克里斯蒂娜·孔杜尔梅。

en: Michele Morosini was a 13th-century Venetian noble of the Morosini dalla Sbarra branch, said to have served as podestà of Faenza. By Agnese Corner he fathered Albertino and Tomasina, who married Prince Stephen the Posthumous of Hungary and mothered Andrew III.
zh: 米凯莱·莫罗西尼是13世纪威尼斯贵族，属莫罗西尼家族“斜杠”支，有学者称他曾任法恩扎长官。他与阿涅塞·科尔纳生有阿尔贝蒂诺和托马西娜；后者嫁给匈牙利亲王“遗腹子”斯蒂芬，是安德烈三世的母亲。

en: Michele Steno (c. 1331–1413) was the doge under whom Venice began to expand onto the Italian mainland. In 1354 he was jailed for a month for writing insults against Doge Marino Faliero and his nephew in the doge's fireplace hall; legend later made the jibe the spark of Faliero's conspiracy. Blamed in part for the defeat at Pula in the War of Chioggia (1379), he recovered and in 1386 became Procurator of Saint Mark. In 1398–1400 he negotiated peace with Gian Galeazzo Visconti for the whole anti-Visconti alliance, and on 1 December 1400, a week after the old doge died, he was elected. After Visconti's death in 1402, Vicenza, Verona and other Veneto towns began to submit to Venice, and the war of 1404–1405 ended Carrara rule in Padua. Dalmatia returned in 1409, bought from Ladislaus of Naples. The last of the Steno line, he died on 26 December 1413 and was buried at Santa Marina.
zh: 米凯莱·斯泰诺（约1331—1413）是威尼斯总督，威尼斯向意大利大陆扩张就始于他任内。1354年，他因在总督壁炉厅里写下侮辱总督马里诺·法列罗及其侄子的言辞，被判入狱一个月；后世传说把这句嘲讽说成法列罗密谋的导火索。1379年基奥贾战争中，他因普拉战败负有部分责任，但仕途随后恢复，1386年出任圣马可行政长官。1398至1400年，他代表整个反维斯孔蒂同盟与詹加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂议和；1400年12月1日，在前任总督去世一周后当选。维斯孔蒂于1402年去世，维琴察、维罗纳等威尼托城镇自1404年起陆续归附威尼斯，1404至1405年的战争又终结了帕多瓦卡拉雷西家族的统治。1409年，达尔马提亚从那不勒斯国王拉迪斯劳手中买回。作为斯泰诺家族的最后一人，他于1413年12月26日去世，葬于圣玛丽娜教堂。

en: Nicolò Contarini was a wealthy Venetian nobleman of the Contarini dal Bovolo branch, whose son Andrea, born around 1300, became doge of Venice in 1368 and led the republic through the War of Chioggia against Genoa.
zh: 尼科洛·孔塔里尼是威尼斯贵族、孔塔里尼家族博沃洛支的富有成员；其子安德烈亚于1300年前后出生，1368年出任威尼斯总督，领导共和国经历了对热那亚的基奥贾战争。

en: Nicolò Gradenigo, known by the diminutive Nicoletto (c. 1267–c. 1317), was a Venetian noble, a son of Doge Pietro Gradenigo by Tommasina Morosini; he survived his father and was named in the doge's will in 1311.
zh: 尼科洛·格拉代尼戈，昵称尼科莱托（约1267—约1317），是威尼斯贵族、总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈与托马西娜·莫罗西尼之子；父亲1311年去世时他仍在世，名字见于其父的遗嘱。

en: Nicolò Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. He was one of at least eight sons whose careers Bartolomeo advanced through persistent, widely resented favouritism, until the Major Council, soon after the doge died in 1342, barred public office to the sons, brothers and nephews of a living doge and forbade the ducal family to trade. In 1348 Nicolò was sent as ambassador to King Louis I of Hungary, who was disputing Dalmatia with Venice, and he later served several times among the Savi, the Republic's senior advisory magistrates.
zh: 尼科洛·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子。巴托洛梅奥至少有八个儿子，凭恃广受非议的偏私为诸子谋求前程，他便是其中之一；1342年总督死后不久，大议会立法禁止在任总督的儿子、兄弟和侄子担任公职，并禁止总督家族经商。1348年，尼科洛受命出使正与威尼斯争夺达尔马提亚的匈牙利国王拉约什一世，后来又多次出任共和国的高级咨议官职“贤人”。

en: Nicolò Soranzo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Giovanni Soranzo, by either Francesca Molin or an unknown earlier wife; he predeceased his father, who died in office in 1328.
zh: 尼科洛·索兰佐是威尼斯贵族，为总督乔瓦尼·索兰佐之子，其母可能是弗朗切斯卡·莫林，也可能是一位不详的前妻；他先于1328年在任内去世的父亲离世。

en: Nicolò Venier was a Venetian nobleman and the father of Antonio Venier, who served as doge of Venice from 1382 until his death in 1400.
zh: 尼科洛·韦涅尔是威尼斯贵族，是1382年至1400年去世前担任威尼斯总督的安东尼奥·韦涅尔之父。

en: Nicolò Zeno (c. 1326–c. 1402) was a Venetian nobleman, the son of Pietro Zeno and brother of Carlo and Antonio Zeno.
zh: 尼科洛·泽诺（约1326—约1402）是威尼斯贵族，皮耶特罗·泽诺之子、卡洛和安东尼奥·泽诺的兄弟。

en: Ordelaffo Falier was a Venetian nobleman of the ancient Falier family, the son of Jacopo Falier and Beriola Loredan, and a brother of Doge Marino Faliero, sharing his name with an earlier doge of the early twelfth century. In 1344, while Marino was on an embassy to Avignon, Ordelaffo served in his place as podestà of Chioggia until his return. Ordelaffo died during the Black Death in 1348.
zh: 奥尔代拉福·法列罗是威尼斯古老法列罗家族的贵族，雅各布·法列罗与贝里奥拉·洛雷丹之子，总督马里诺·法列罗的兄弟；他的名字与12世纪初的一位同名总督相同。1344年，马里诺出使阿维尼翁期间，奥尔代拉福代他出任基奥贾行政长官，直至他归来。奥尔代拉福于1348年死于黑死病。

en: Orso Gradenigo was one of the five sons of Giovanni Gradenigo, who ruled Venice as doge from 1355 to 1356. Orso and his brothers took part in Venetian politics, though none rose to a prominent position.
zh: 奥尔索·格拉代尼戈是1355至1356年任威尼斯总督的乔万尼·格拉代尼戈的五子之一。奥尔索与兄弟们都参与威尼斯政治，但诸子无人出任显要职位。

en: Paolo Contarini was a son of Andrea Contarini, the 60th doge of Venice, and his wife Costanza.
zh: 保罗·孔塔里尼是第60任威尼斯总督安德烈亚·孔塔里尼与妻子科斯坦扎之子。

en: Paolo Morosini may have been a son of Marino Morosini and a brother of Michele Morosini, who became doge of Venice in 1382.
zh: 保罗·莫罗西尼可能是马里诺·莫罗西尼之子，也是1382年出任威尼斯总督的米凯莱·莫罗西尼的兄弟。

en: Pietro Dandolo was a Venetian nobleman of the early twelfth century, a son of the ambassador and ducal judge Domenico Dandolo, and an ancestor of Andrea Dandolo, who became doge of Venice in 1343.
zh: 彼得罗·丹多洛是12世纪初的威尼斯贵族，为大使兼公爵法官多梅尼科·丹多洛之子，也是1343年出任威尼斯总督的安德烈亚·丹多洛的先祖。

en: Pietro Dandolo was a Venetian patrician recorded in Dandolo family genealogies as the father of Fantino Dandolo and grandfather of Andrea Dandolo, who became doge of Venice in 1343.
zh: 彼得罗·丹多洛是威尼斯贵族，丹多洛家族家谱将他记载为凡蒂诺·丹多洛之父、1343年出任威尼斯总督的安德烈亚·丹多洛的祖父。

en: Pietro Dandolo was a son of Doge Andrea Dandolo; an edict issued upon Andrea's election barred Pietro and his brothers from holding public office during their father's rule when they came of age.
zh: 彼得罗·丹多洛是总督安德烈·丹多洛之子；安德烈当选时颁布的一项法令禁止彼得罗与他的兄弟成年后在父亲任内担任公职。

en: Pietro Gradenigo (1251–1311), 49th Doge of Venice from 1289 until his death, was elected while podestà of Capodistria. In 1279 he had been sent to Istria to reassert Venetian authority and suppress revolts. In February 1297 he carried through the Serrata del Maggior Consiglio, a measure restricting access to the Great Council that contributed to the gradual formation of a hereditary oligarchy. His reign saw defeat by Genoa at Curzola in 1298 and, from 1308, war over Ferrara that brought excommunication from Clement V. After Bajamonte Tiepolo's failed coup of June 1310, the Council of Ten was created. Gradenigo died on 13 August 1311 and, Venice being under interdict, was buried in an unmarked grave on Murano.
zh: 彼得罗·格拉代尼戈（1251—1311）是威尼斯第四十九任总督，1289年起任职直至去世，当选时正在卡波迪斯特里亚担任波德斯塔。1279年他曾被派往伊斯特拉，重申威尼斯的权威并镇压反抗。1297年2月，他推动通过大议会封闭令，限制进入大议会的资格，促成世袭寡头政体逐渐形成。任内威尼斯1298年在库尔佐拉海战中败于热那亚，1308年起因费拉拉与教皇国交战，被教皇克雷芒五世处以绝罚。1310年6月巴亚蒙特·蒂耶波洛政变失败后，十人团应运而生。1311年8月13日格拉代尼戈去世，由于威尼斯正受绝罚禁令，他被葬于穆拉诺岛的无名墓地。

en: Pietro Gradenigo was a son of Giovanni Gradenigo, doge of Venice in 1355–1356. He and his brothers took part in Venetian politics, but none reached a prominent position, perhaps because of their father's influence or the Great Council's measures against nepotism.
zh: 彼得罗·格拉代尼戈是1355至1356年任威尼斯总督的乔万尼·格拉代尼戈之子。他与兄弟们参与威尼斯政治，却无人做到显要职位，可能是受父亲影响或大议会抑制裙带关系的措施所限。

en: Pietro Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman and a son of Doge Bartolomeo Gradenigo. He and his brothers owed their advancement to their father's determined lobbying while he was doge, which so angered Venetian opinion that after Bartolomeo's death in 1342 the Major Council banned grants of office to a living doge's relatives. In 1355 Pietro served the Republic as count of Traù, on the Dalmatian coast that King Louis I of Hungary was contesting with Venice. In 1361, after Doge Giovanni Dolfin's death, he stood as a candidate for the dogeship himself, but the election went to Lorenzo Celsi.
zh: 彼得罗·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督巴托洛梅奥·格拉代尼戈之子。他和兄弟们的晋升都靠父亲任总督期间大力安插；这些做法激起公愤，巴托洛梅奥于1342年去世后，大议会遂立法禁止向在任总督的亲属授予公职。1355年，彼得罗代表威尼斯共和国出任特拉乌伯爵，所在的达尔马提亚海岸，正是匈牙利国王拉约什一世与威尼斯相争之地。1361年总督乔瓦尼·多尔芬去世后，他亲自参选总督，但最终由洛伦佐·切尔西当选。

en: Pietro de' Rossi (1303–1337) was the Emilian condottiero Venice set against the Scaligers. A son of Guglielmo de' Rossi of Parma, he had fought for the future Emperor Charles IV against the Castelbaldo league and held Lucca in vicariate until the Scaligers drove him out in 1334. In 1336 Doge Francesco Dandolo hired him and his brothers Rolando and Marsilio, naming Pietro commander of the anti-Scaliger league's troops. He razed the Saline castle at Chioggia that November, and on 3 August 1337 Padua surrendered to him through his uncle Marsilio da Carrara, the city's lord; Alberto II della Scala was captured in the siege and sent to prison in Venice. Five days later, in the first assault on Monselice, a Monselice peasant killed Pietro with a lance. The fortress was held by Pietro Dal Verme, and Pietro de' Rossi was buried in the Basilica of Saint Anthony at Padua.
zh: 彼得罗·德·罗西（1303—1337）是艾米利亚的佣兵将领，威尼斯用他来对付斯卡拉家族。他是帕尔马的古列尔莫·德·罗西之子，曾追随后来成为皇帝的查理四世攻打卡斯泰尔巴尔多联盟，并以代理人身份领有卢卡，直到1334年被斯卡拉家族赶走。1336年，总督弗朗切斯科·丹多洛雇用了他和兄弟罗兰多、马西利奥，任命彼得罗为反斯卡拉联盟军队的统帅。当年11月他摧毁了基奥贾的萨利内城堡；1337年8月3日，帕多瓦通过他的舅父、该城领主马西利奥·达·卡拉拉向他投降，阿尔贝托二世·德拉·斯卡拉在围城中被俘，押往威尼斯入狱。五天后，在对蒙塞利切的首次强攻中，一名当地农民用长矛刺死了彼得罗。守卫那座要塞的是彼得罗·达尔·韦尔梅，而彼得罗·德·罗西葬于帕多瓦圣安多尼圣殿。

en: Pietro Venier, son of Marco Venier, Lord of Cerigo, married Bonafemena Quirini and died before 1360.
zh: 彼得罗·韦涅尔是切里戈领主马尔科·韦涅尔之子，娶博纳费梅娜·奎里尼为妻，1360年前去世。

en: Pietro Zeno (died 1345) was a Venetian commander. As captain and bailiff of Negroponte in 1331–1333, he bought off a 380-ship Aydinid fleet under Umur Bey that raided the island in 1332. That July Doge Francesco Dandolo charged him and Pietro da Canale with arranging an anti-Turkish alliance, formally established as the Naval League by year's end. Zeno led its twenty galleys to victory over the emir of Karasi off Adramyttion on 14 September 1334. In 1343 the Grand Council sent him with five galleys to join the Smyrniote crusade; after Smyrna fell, he and other leaders, including Henry of Asti, were killed in an ambush by Umur Bey's forces while attempting to celebrate mass between the lines on 17 January 1345.
zh: 彼得罗·泽诺（1345年卒）是威尼斯将领。1331至1333年他任内格罗蓬特指挥官兼行政长官，1332年乌穆尔贝伊率艾登王朝380艘战船袭掠该岛时，他献贡金将其劝退。同年7月，总督弗朗切斯科·丹多洛命他与彼得罗·达·卡纳莱筹组反土耳其同盟，年底海上同盟正式成立。1334年9月14日，他率同盟二十艘桨帆船在阿德拉米蒂翁湾外击败卡拉西埃米尔的舰队。1343年，大议会派他率五艘桨帆船参加士麦那十字军；攻克士麦那后，1345年1月17日他与阿斯蒂的亨利等领袖试图在战线之间举行弥撒时，遭乌穆尔贝伊部下伏击身亡。

en: Bartolomeo Platina (1421–1481), born Bartolomeo Sacchi at Piadena near Cremona, was an Italian humanist writer. After soldiering and tutoring the Gonzaga sons in Mantua, he studied Greek in Florence and entered papal service in Rome. Under the anti-humanist Paul II, he was imprisoned in Castel Sant'Angelo in 1464 after protesting the loss of his papal office. In 1468 he was imprisoned again over accusations against Pomponio Leto's Roman Academy and interrogated under torture. Sixtus IV made him the first Vatican librarian in 1475. His De honesta voluptate et valetudine became the first printed cookbook, and his Lives of the Popes appeared in 1479, depicting Paul II harshly.
zh: 巴托洛米奥·普拉蒂纳（1421—1481），本名巴托洛梅奥·萨基，生于克雷莫纳附近的皮亚德纳，是意大利人文主义作家。他早年从军，后在曼托瓦担任贡扎加家族子弟的教师，又赴佛罗伦萨学习希腊语，随后到罗马为教廷效力。敌视人文主义的教皇保罗二世在位时，他因抗议失去教廷职位，于1464年被囚于圣天使城堡。1468年，蓬波尼奥·莱托的罗马学院遭到指控，他再次被囚并受酷刑审讯。1475年，西斯都四世任命他为首任梵蒂冈图书馆馆长。他的《论正当的享乐与健康》是第一部付印的烹饪书，1479年问世的《教皇传》则尖锐地描写了保罗二世。

en: Raniero Dandolo (died 1209) was a Venetian admiral and statesman, the only confirmed son of Doge Enrico Dandolo. From 1202 to 1205 he governed Venice as vice-doge during his father's absence on the Fourth Crusade, corresponding with Pope Innocent III over the installation of Tommaso Morosini as Latin patriarch of Constantinople. He also legislated as vice-doge, in a period when Venetian justice and government were becoming more dependent on written records. After his father's death he led the Venetian conquest of Crete against the Genoese, and after subduing most of the island he was killed there by an arrow in 1209. His daughter Anna married King Stefan Nemanjić of Serbia.
zh: 拉伊纳罗·丹多洛（1209年卒）是威尼斯海军将领与政治家，也是总督恩里科·丹多洛唯一可考的儿子。1202至1205年，父亲参加第四次十字军远征在外，他以副总督身份主持威尼斯政务，并就托马索·莫罗西尼出任君士坦丁堡拉丁牧首一事与教皇英诺森三世通信。他还以副总督身份立法，当时威尼斯的司法和国家治理正日益依赖书面记录。父亲死后，他率军同热那亚人争夺并征服克里特，在基本平定全岛后于1209年中箭身亡。他的女儿安娜嫁给了塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·尼曼伊奇。

en: Reniero Zeno (c. 1200–1268), son of Pietro Zeno, was the 45th Doge of Venice from January 1253 until his death. He served as podestà of Pola, Verona and other Italian cities, retook rebellious Zara in 1242 after a two-month siege and became captain-general of the Sea in 1244. In 1245 he and fellow Venetian envoys distanced themselves from the doge's anti-imperial policy before Emperor Frederick II. Elected doge while podestà of Fermo, he backed Pope Alexander IV against Ezzelino da Romano in 1256–1259 and fought the War of Saint Sabas against Genoa, winning at Settepozzi in 1263. His reign enacted Venice's 129-article maritime code and made a five-year truce with Byzantium in 1268. He died on 7 July 1268.
zh: 雷涅罗·泽诺（约1200—1268）是彼得罗·泽诺之子，1253年1月起出任第四十五任威尼斯总督，在任直至去世。他曾出任普拉、维罗纳等意大利城市的长官，1242年围攻两个月后收复反叛的扎拉，1244年受任为海军统帅。1245年，他与其他威尼斯使节在皇帝腓特烈二世面前表示不认同总督的反皇帝政策。他在担任费尔莫长官期间当选总督，1256至1259年支持教皇亚历山大四世讨伐埃泽利诺·达·罗马诺，又在圣萨巴战争中与热那亚作战，1263年于塞特波齐获胜。任内颁布了共129条的威尼斯海商法典，并于1268年与拜占庭缔结五年休战协定。他于1268年7月7日去世。

en: Rolando de' Rossi (c. 1285–1345) tried to make Parma his family's lordship while the papal legate at Bologna, the Scaligers of Verona and the Visconti of Milan all pressed on Emilia. In 1322 he imprisoned his rival Gianquirico Sanvitale and exiled his allies, and in 1325 the legate made him captain of the Church. In 1328 he expelled the papal government, allied with Cangrande della Scala and was given supreme power by the general council, becoming Parma's effective signore. The legate arrested him at Bologna in 1329, where he had gone to make peace. Freed in 1331, he submitted Parma to John of Bohemia and was made a count. With Scaliger raiders at the gates and Avignon and the Visconti refusing help, Parma surrendered to the Scaligers in June 1335, ending its self-rule. In exile he commanded Venice's army against them until the 1339 peace, which restored his estates but not his city. He died at Padua in May 1345.
zh: 罗兰多·德·罗西（约1285—1345）试图把帕尔马变成自家的领地，而当时博洛尼亚的教皇使节、维罗纳的斯卡拉家族和米兰的维斯孔蒂家族都在向艾米利亚伸手。1322年，他囚禁政敌詹基里科·桑维塔莱并放逐其盟友；1325年，使节任命他为教会队长。1328年，他驱逐教廷政府，与坎格兰德·德拉·斯卡拉结盟，总议会授予他最高权力，他成为帕尔马事实上的领主。1329年他前往博洛尼亚议和，却被使节逮捕。1331年获释后，他将帕尔马献给波希米亚国王约翰，受封伯爵。斯卡拉家族的劫掠压境，阿维尼翁和维斯孔蒂又都不肯援手，1335年6月帕尔马向斯卡拉家族投降，自治就此终结。流亡中，他统率威尼斯军队对抗斯卡拉家族，直到1339年和约；和约归还了他的产业，却没有归还帕尔马。1345年5月，他在帕多瓦去世。

en: Jacopo Sansovino (1486–1570), born Jacopo Tatti in Florence, took the name of his master Andrea Sansovino and became the defining architect of Venetian Renaissance classicism. A sculptor in Florence and Rome, where Raphael judged his wax copy of the Laocoön the best, he received commissions for a marble St James and a Bacchus in Florence. He fled to Venice after the Sack of Rome in 1527. From 1529, as chief architect to the Procurators of St Mark, he reshaped the area around St Mark's Square, building the Biblioteca Marciana, his masterpiece, the Zecca mint and the Loggetta of the Campanile. In the library he combined classical architecture with Venetian decorative tastes. He died in Venice in 1570.
zh: 雅各布·桑索维诺（1486—1570），本名雅各布·塔蒂，生于佛罗伦萨，后随恩师安德烈亚·桑索维诺改姓，是威尼斯文艺复兴古典主义建筑的奠基者。他早年在佛罗伦萨和罗马从事雕塑，他复制的《拉奥孔》蜡模曾被拉斐尔评为第一；他还在佛罗伦萨受托制作大理石圣雅各像和巴克斯像。1527年罗马之劫后他避居威尼斯。1529年起，他担任圣马可行政长官的首席建筑师，重塑了圣马可广场一带的面貌，代表作有圣马可图书馆、造币厂和钟楼旁的小敞廊。他在图书馆的设计中将古典建筑与威尼斯的装饰趣味结合。1570年他在威尼斯去世。

en: Simone Dandolo was a Venetian nobleman of the San Luca branch, the son of Fantino Dandolo and brother of Doge Andrea Dandolo. In 1345 he served as provveditore, supply commissioner, with the Venetian army that fought around the rebellious city of Zara in Dalmatia, a revolt that threatened Venice's hold on the coast. He afterwards became podestà of Treviso, and he later sat as one of the judges of Doge Marino Falier.
zh: 西莫内·丹多洛是威尼斯圣卢卡支系的贵族，凡蒂诺·丹多洛之子、总督安德烈亚·丹多洛的兄弟。1345年，他在达尔马提亚叛城扎拉一带作战的威尼斯军队中担任补给督办，这场叛乱动摇了威尼斯对达尔马提亚的统治。此后他出任特雷维索长官，后来又成为总督马里诺·法列罗手下的法官之一。

en: Stephen the Posthumous (1236–1271) was the posthumous son of King Andrew II of Hungary and Beatrice d'Este, born at Wehrda in Thuringia in 1236 after his mother fled King Béla IV. Béla, his half-brother, disputed his paternity and denied him the revenues due to a king's son. Raised from 1243 at the Ferrara court of Marquis Azzo VII d'Este, he married first Isabella Traversari and then Tomasina Morosini of Venice. His mother sought Venetian support for his claims, but Venice promised Béla in its 1244 peace treaty not to support them. He styled himself Duke of Slavonia and pressed his Hungarian claims without success. He died in Venice shortly after making his will on 10 April 1271. His son by Tomasina became King Andrew III, the last Árpád ruler.
zh: 遗腹子伊什特万（1236—1271）是匈牙利国王安德烈二世与埃斯特的贝亚特里切的遗腹子。母亲逃离国王贝拉四世后，于1236年在图林根的韦尔达生下他。同父异母的兄长贝拉质疑他的血统，拒绝给予他王子应得的收入。自1243年起，他在费拉拉侯爵阿佐七世·德埃斯特的宫廷长大，先娶伊莎贝拉·特拉韦尔萨里，后娶威尼斯的托马西娜·莫罗西尼。母亲曾寻求威尼斯支持他的权利主张，但威尼斯在1244年的和约中向贝拉承诺不予支持。他自称斯拉沃尼亚公爵，一再争取匈牙利的权益却始终无果。1271年4月10日立遗嘱后不久，他在威尼斯去世。他与托马西娜所生之子后来成为匈牙利国王安德烈三世，即阿帕德王朝末代君主。

en: Teodora de' Rossi was a daughter of the Parmesan condottiero Pietro de' Rossi, lord of Parma, who was killed at the siege of Monselice in 1337. She and her five siblings, among them her sister Luchina, are recorded in their father's genealogy.
zh: 特奥多拉·德·罗西是帕尔马雇佣军首领、帕尔马领主彼得罗·德·罗西之女，其父于1337年围攻蒙塞利切时战死。她与卢奇娜等五名兄弟姐妹载于父亲的家谱中。

en: Teresa de' Rossi (born 1330) was the daughter of the Parmesan condottiero Marsilio de' Rossi, lord of Parma, and his wife Margherita, of whom nothing but her name survives. Family genealogies record her marriage to the marquess Uberto Pallavicino.
zh: 特蕾莎·德·罗西（1330年生）是帕尔马雇佣军首领、帕尔马领主马西利奥·德·罗西与妻子玛格丽塔之女，其母仅留下名字。家谱记载她嫁给了侯爵乌贝托·帕拉维奇诺。

en: Jacopo Robusti, known as Tintoretto (1518–1594), was a Venetian Renaissance painter whose furious speed and bold brushwork earned him the nickname il Furioso. The son of a dyer, whence his name, he was briefly apprenticed to Titian and then trained alone, writing over his studio the motto Michelangelo's drawing and Titian's colour. His muscular figures, dramatic gestures and daring perspective made him the most distinctive painter of the later Venetian school. His Miracle of the Slave won acclaim in 1548, bringing him further commissions. Between 1565 and 1588 he painted many scenes for the Scuola Grande di San Rocco. After Paolo Veronese's death in 1588 he completed the giant Paradise for the Doge's Palace. He died in 1594 and was buried at the Madonna dell'Orto.
zh: 雅各布·罗布斯蒂，即丁托列托（1518—1594），是威尼斯文艺复兴画家，作画速度迅疾、笔触大胆，因而得名“狂热者”。他是染匠之子，绰号意即“小染匠”；他短暂入提香作坊学艺，此后独自苦练，在工作室上方写下“米开朗基罗的素描和提香的色彩”作为座右铭。他笔下人物雄健、手势夸张、透视大胆，是威尼斯画派后期最具个性的画家。1548年，他的《奴隶的奇迹》广获赞誉，为他带来更多委托。1565年至1588年间，他为圣洛克大会堂绘制了许多画作。1588年保罗·委罗内塞去世后，他为总督宫完成巨幅《天堂》，1594年去世，葬于果园圣母堂。

en: Tommasina Morosini (born in the 1260s) was a Venetian noblewoman who married Pietro Gradenigo, later doge of Venice. When he took office in December 1289 she became dogaressa, holding the position for some twenty years until her death in Venice before 1309. She was a niece of Tomasina Morosini, queen of Hungary and mother of Andrew III. She bore Gradenigo at least ten children, including Nicolò, who after her death served as a Venetian envoy to Treviso in 1314, and Isabetta, also called Anna, who married the Paduan lord Giacomo I da Carrara.
zh: 托马西娜·莫罗西尼（1260年代生）是威尼斯贵族女子，嫁给后来的威尼斯总督彼得罗·格拉代尼戈。1289年12月丈夫就任，她成为总督夫人，前后约二十年，直至1309年以前在威尼斯去世。她是匈牙利王后、安德烈三世之母托马西娜的侄女。她为格拉代尼戈生育至少十个子女，其中包括在她去世后于1314年出使特雷维索的尼科洛，以及又名安娜的伊莎贝塔，后者嫁给帕多瓦领主雅各布一世·达·卡拉拉。

en: Tommaso Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman, the son of Marino Gradenigo, Duke of Crete, and Maria Dandolo, and a brother of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo.
zh: 托马索·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，父亲是曾任干地亚公爵的马里诺·格拉代尼戈，母亲为玛丽亚·丹多洛，他是总督乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈的兄弟之一。

en: Tommaso Gradenigo was a Venetian nobleman, a son of Doge Giovanni Gradenigo and his second wife Felipa. In January 1353 his father named him an executor of the will made before leaving for Capodistria; no public office of his is recorded.
zh: 托马索·格拉代尼戈是威尼斯贵族，总督乔瓦尼·格拉代尼戈与第二任妻子费利帕之子。1353年1月，其父赴卡波迪斯特里亚任长官前立下遗嘱，指定他为执行人之一；史书未载他担任过公职。

en: Ugolino de' Rossi (c. 1300–1377) was bishop of Parma for fifty-four years, longer than anyone before or after him. In 1322 he was charged with lifting the church censures laid on the Parmesans for supplying troops to Galeazzo Visconti. The Rossi, now the city's masters, had the legate name him bishop; Pope John XXII ratified it in June 1323, when Ugolino held only minor orders. He was caught between his brothers' politics and the papacy: he fled to Corniglio when Louis IV showed interest in Parma in 1329, and to Avignon when the Scaligers took it in 1334. Back in 1341, he found his castles ruined and borrowed more than ten thousand gold florins from his brother Rolando. Unable to repay, he ceded chapter lands to his nephews. The Visconti, now lords of Parma, later called him to Milan, where he died on 28 April 1377, a friend and admirer of Petrarch.
zh: 乌戈利诺·德·罗西（约1300—1377）担任帕尔马主教长达54年，前后无人在任更久。1322年，帕尔马人因向加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂提供军队而受到教会惩罚，他受命为他们解除处分。罗西家族由此成为城中主宰，并让使节指定他出任主教；1323年6月教皇约翰二十二世批准任命，当时乌戈利诺只领有低级神品。他夹在兄弟们的政治与教廷之间：1329年路易四世对帕尔马表现出兴趣时，他逃往科尔尼廖；1334年斯卡拉家族夺取帕尔马后，他又逃往阿维尼翁。1341年返回时，他发现城堡尽毁，向兄长罗兰多借了一万多金弗罗林。因无力偿还，他把教区议事会的土地让给侄子们。后来他被已成为帕尔马新主人的维斯孔蒂家族召往米兰，1377年4月28日在当地去世，生前是彼特拉克的朋友与仰慕者。

en: Vitale Dandolo was a Venetian jurist and senior member of the ducal court, who served as ambassador to Ferrara and as bailo in Constantinople. He lived into his nineties, dying around 1174; his son Doge Enrico Dandolo remained under his authority until then.
zh: 维塔莱·丹多洛是威尼斯法学家、总督府核心成员，曾出使费拉拉，并任驻君士坦丁堡的巴约。他活到九十多岁，约1174年去世；在那之前，他的儿子、后来的总督恩里科·丹多洛一直处在他的父权之下。

en: Zanetta Dandolo was a daughter of Doge Andrea Dandolo and Francesca Morosini, and married a member of the Loredan family.
zh: 扎内塔·丹多洛是总督安德烈·丹多洛与弗朗切斯卡·莫罗西尼之女，嫁给洛雷丹家族的一名成员。

en: Zanino Dandolo was the natural son of Francesco Dandolo, the 52nd doge of Venice, born to a mistress outside the doge's marriage with Elisabetta Contarini. Francesco's only legitimate son, Gratone, had died before him. In his will, drawn up five days before his death on 31 October 1339, the doge left Zanino nearly all his estate, including the family palace at San Polo in Venice and extensive properties in the Ferrarese.
zh: 扎尼诺·丹多洛是第52任威尼斯总督弗朗切斯科·丹多洛的私生子，母亲是总督的情妇，而非总督之妻伊丽莎白·孔塔里尼。总督唯一的婚子格拉托内先他而死。在1339年10月31日去世前五天所立的遗嘱中，弗朗切斯科把几乎全部产业留给扎尼诺，包括家族在威尼斯圣波罗区的宫殿和在费拉拉地区的大批地产。

en: Alberto II della Scala (1306–1352) was the elder son of Alboino I della Scala and Beatrice da Correggio. After Cangrande I died in 1329, he became lord of Verona and ruled jointly with his younger brother Mastino II, though Mastino held the real power. In 1335 he took possession of Parma and occupied Reggio, which he handed over to the Gonzaga. The Scaligeri lost Padua in 1338 and Belluno and Feltre in 1339, and his 1341 attempt to overthrow Gonzaga rule in Reggio failed. He died in Verona on 13 September 1352, and Mastino's sons succeeded him.
zh: 阿尔贝托二世·德拉·斯卡拉（1306—1352）是阿尔博伊诺一世·德拉·斯卡拉与贝阿特丽切·达·科雷焦的长子。1329年坎格兰德一世去世后，他成为维罗纳领主，与弟弟马斯蒂诺二世共同执政，但实权掌握在马斯蒂诺手中。1335年，他取得帕尔马并攻占雷焦，随后把雷焦交给贡扎加家族。1338年和1339年，斯卡拉家族先后失去帕多瓦、贝卢诺和费尔特雷；1341年他试图推翻雷焦的贡扎加统治，也告失败。1352年9月13日他在维罗纳去世，领主之位由马斯蒂诺的儿子们继承。

en: Alberto I della Scala (c. 1245–1301) was the son of Jacopino della Scala and a trusted lieutenant of his elder brother Mastino I, inheriting his commercial office in 1269 and holding the podestà post in Mantua in 1272 and 1275. After Mastino's murder, the Veronese assembly elected him lifelong Captain and Rector on 27 October 1277. He made Verona a true signoria, requiring oaths of allegiance, building a bureaucracy and personal guard, and repelling a Guelph assault in 1278–1279. Marriage alliances and treaties with Mantua and Venice helped consolidate his position. His daughter Costanza married Obizzo II d'Este, Marquis of Ferrara. He died on 3 September 1301 and was succeeded by his son Bartolomeo; Alboino and Cangrande ruled after him.
zh: 阿尔贝托一世·德拉·斯卡拉（约1245—1301）是雅各皮诺·德拉·斯卡拉之子，也是兄长马斯蒂诺一世信任的副手：1269年他继承兄长掌管商业的官职，并于1272年和1275年出任曼托瓦最高行政长官。马斯蒂诺遇刺后，维罗纳议会于1277年10月27日推举他为终身领袖与执政。他把维罗纳建成真正的世袭领邦，要求官员宣誓效忠，设立官僚机构和私人卫队，并于1278至1279年击退圭尔夫派的进攻。联姻以及与曼托瓦和威尼斯订立的条约帮助他巩固地位。他的女儿科斯坦扎嫁给费拉拉侯爵奥比佐二世·德斯特。他于1301年9月3日去世，其子巴尔托洛梅奥继位，此后阿尔博伊诺和坎格兰德也相继统治维罗纳。

en: Alboino I della Scala (1284–1311), second son of Alberto I and Verde di Salizzole, became Lord of Verona after his brother Bartolomeo died in March 1304. In 1298 he married Caterina Visconti, daughter of Matteo I Visconti of Milan, and in 1306 Beatrice, daughter of Gilberto III da Correggio. From 1308 he ruled alongside his younger brother Cangrande. When the Emperor Henry VII entered Italy in 1311, he named the two brothers imperial vicars of Verona and its territory. Alboino died on 29 November 1311, leaving Cangrande to rule alone.
zh: 阿尔博伊诺一世·德拉·斯卡拉（1284—1311）是阿尔贝托一世与维尔德·迪·萨利佐莱的次子，1304年3月其兄巴尔托洛梅奥死后成为维罗纳领主。1298年他娶米兰的马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂之女卡泰丽娜·维斯孔蒂，1306年又娶吉尔贝托三世·达·科雷焦之女贝阿特丽切。1308年起，他与幼弟坎格兰德共同执政。1311年神圣罗马帝国皇帝亨利七世南下意大利，任命兄弟二人为维罗纳及其领地的帝国代理官。1311年11月29日阿尔博伊诺去世，坎格兰德独自执政。

en: Altino Castracani degli Antelminelli was the natural son of Castruccio Castracani, Ghibelline lord of Lucca, by an unnamed mistress; he is listed among the duke's children at his death in 1328.
zh: 阿尔蒂诺·卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利是卢卡吉伯林派领主卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼与一名情妇所生的私生子，1328年公爵去世时被列为其子嗣之一。

en: Antonio de' Rossi was a son of Rolando de' Rossi, Guelph lord of Parma and Lucca, and of Agnese Ruggeri. He was brother of Giacomo, first count of San Secondo, and of Bertrando. He died in 1388.
zh: 安东尼奥·德·罗西是帕尔马与卢卡的圭尔夫派领主罗兰多·德·罗西与阿涅塞·鲁杰里之子，圣塞孔多初代伯爵贾科莫及贝尔特兰多的兄弟，1388年去世。

en: Arrigo Castracani degli Antelminelli, called the Duchino (c. 1304–1357), was the eldest son and designated heir of the Lucchese condottiero Castruccio Castracani, the Ghibelline strongman who beat the Florentines at Altopascio in 1325 and was named duke of Lucca by Emperor Louis IV. In 1324 Arrigo built the Rocchetta Arrighina at Pietrasanta, and in 1325 became Lucca's captain general and rector for life. Castruccio died of fever in 1328 while preparing to fight Florence again, and Louis IV then took Pisa and Lucca from his son. Arrigo repeatedly tried to recover his family's rule: in 1331 he briefly seized Lucca, only to be driven out by King John of Bohemia. He married Costanza de' Rossi in 1334 and later fought alongside Pisa, but was again denied control of Lucca. Accused of conspiracy against Giovanni da Oleggio, he was executed at Bologna in 1357.
zh: 阿里戈·卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利，绰号“小公爵”（约1304—1357），是卢卡佣兵将领卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼的长子和指定继承人。卡斯特鲁乔是吉伯林派强人，1325年在阿尔托帕肖击败佛罗伦萨人，并被皇帝路易四世封为卢卡公爵。1324年，阿里戈在彼得拉桑塔修建阿里吉纳小堡垒，1325年获任卢卡终身总队长兼行政长官。1328年卡斯特鲁乔在筹备再战佛罗伦萨时病逝，路易四世随即夺走了儿子手中的比萨和卢卡。阿里戈屡次试图恢复家族统治：1331年他一度夺取卢卡，旋即被波希米亚国王约翰赶走。1334年他迎娶科斯坦察·德·罗西，后来与比萨并肩作战，却再度未能掌控卢卡。他因被指控密谋反对乔瓦尼·达·奥莱焦，于1357年在博洛尼亚被处决。

en: Bailardino Nogarola (c. 1270–1340) was a Veronese nobleman, diplomat and condottiero who spent his life in the service of the della Scala lords of Verona. He joined them in his youth and was knighted in 1295 together with Bartolomeo and Cangrande, sons of Alberto I della Scala, lord of Verona. For the family he served as podestà of Mantua, Vicenza, Treviso and Padua, and in 1311 went to Milan as Scaliger ambassador to meet Emperor Henry VII. In 1328 he stood at Cangrande's side on the day Cangrande took possession of Padua. When Cangrande died on 22 July 1329, Bailardino managed the passing of power to Cangrande's nephews Mastino II and Alberto II della Scala. He died at Nogarole Rocca on 24 October 1340 and was given a solemn funeral.
zh: 巴伊拉尔多·诺加罗拉（约1270—1340）是维罗纳贵族、外交官与雇佣兵首领，一生效力于统治维罗纳的德拉·斯卡拉家族。他年轻时便投身该家族，1295年与维罗纳领主阿尔贝托一世·德拉·斯卡拉之子巴尔托洛梅奥和坎格兰德一同受封骑士。他为家族出任曼托瓦、维琴察、特雷维索、帕多瓦的最高行政官，1311年作为斯卡拉家族的使节赴米兰觐见皇帝亨利七世。1328年坎格兰德占领帕多瓦那天，他侍立在侧。1329年7月22日坎格兰德去世，他主持权力交接，由坎格兰德的侄子马斯蒂诺二世和阿尔贝托二世接掌。1340年10月24日，他卒于诺加罗莱罗卡，获隆重葬礼。

en: Bailardino della Scala was a natural son of Bartolomeo I della Scala, lord of Verona, born around 1302.
zh: 巴伊拉尔迪诺·德拉·斯卡拉（约1302年生）是维罗纳领主巴尔托洛梅奥一世的私生子。

en: Bartolomeo I della Scala (1270–1304), eldest son of Alberto I and Verde di Salizzole, ruled Verona as lord from 1301. His father may have associated him in power as early as 1293. He succeeded at once as Captain and Rector, then stripped the guilds' council of its remaining authority. In 1291 he married Costanza di Antiochia, daughter of Corrado d'Antiochia. He sheltered the exiled Dante at his court, and Dante later praised him as il gran Lombardo in Paradise XVII. Bartolomeo died on 7 March 1304 and was succeeded by his brother Alboino.
zh: 巴尔托洛梅奥一世·德拉·斯卡拉（1270—1304）是阿尔贝托一世与维尔德·迪·萨利佐莱的长子，1301年起任维罗纳领主。其父可能早在1293年便让他共同执政。他随即继任领袖与执政之职，随后剥夺了行会会议仅存的权力。1291年，他娶科拉多·迪·安蒂奥基亚之女科斯坦扎·迪·安蒂奥基亚为妻。他曾在宫廷中收留流亡的但丁，但丁后来在《神曲·天堂篇》第十七篇中称他为“伟大的伦巴第人”。1304年3月7日他去世，其弟阿尔博伊诺继位。

en: Beatrice da Camino (died 1388) was the daughter of Rizzardo VI Novello da Camino, lord of Serravalle, and Verde della Scala, daughter of Alboino della Scala of Verona. Her father died in 1335 leaving no son, and she and her two sisters were pushed aside in the succession struggle over the Caminese fiefs. In 1351 she married Aldobrandino III d'Este, marquis of Ferrara. Years later she joined the conspiracy raised by her son Obizzo IV against Alberto V d'Este; when it failed, she was beheaded with him at Ferrara in 1388.
zh: 贝亚特里切·达·卡米诺（？—1388）是塞拉瓦莱领主里扎尔多六世（小里扎尔多）·达·卡米诺与维尔德的女儿，维尔德是维罗纳的阿尔博伊诺·德拉·斯卡拉之女。1335年父亲去世，没有留下男嗣，她和两个姊妹在卡米诺家族封地的继承纷争中遭排挤。1351年，她嫁给费拉拉侯爵阿尔多布兰迪诺三世·德斯特。后来她卷入儿子奥比佐四世反对阿尔贝托五世·德斯特的阴谋；叛乱被镇压后，她于1388年在费拉拉与儿子一同被斩首。

en: Beatrice Regina della Scala (1333–1384) was the youngest daughter of Mastino II della Scala, lord of Verona, and Taddea da Carrara. On 27 September 1350 she married Bernabò Visconti in Verona, a match arranged to seal peace between the Scaligeri and expansionist Milan. When Bernabò took power as lord of Milan in 1354, she became lady of the city and served as his political adviser. She was the mother of numerous children, among them Taddea, Viridis and Valentina, whose marriages linked Milan to ruling houses across Europe. She died on 18 June 1384.
zh: 贝亚特里切·雷吉娜·德拉·斯卡拉（1333—1384）是维罗纳领主马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉与塔代娅·达·卡拉拉的幼女。1350年9月27日，她在维罗纳嫁给贝尔纳博·维斯孔蒂，这桩婚事旨在让斯卡拉家族与扩张中的米兰缔和。1354年贝尔纳博成为米兰领主后，她成为米兰夫人，并充当丈夫的政治顾问。她子女众多，包括塔代娅、维里迪丝和瓦伦蒂娜，她们的婚姻把米兰与欧洲各地统治家族联系起来。她于1384年6月18日去世。

en: Bernardino da Fogliano was a son of Giberto da Fogliano, lord of Reggio Emilia, and died a violent death.
zh: 贝尔纳迪诺·达·福利亚诺是雷焦艾米利亚领主吉贝尔托·达·福利亚诺之子，死于暴力。

en: Bertolino da Fogliano was a son of Giberto da Fogliano, lord of Reggio Emilia, and a man-at-arms. He died in 1354.
zh: 贝尔托利诺·达·福利亚诺是雷焦艾米利亚领主吉贝尔托·达·福利亚诺之子，是一名军人，1354年去世。

en: Cagnolo Nogarola was a Veronese nobleman of the French-descended Nogarola family, the son of Bailardino Nogarola, condottiero and ambassador for the della Scala lords, by Contessa da Fogliano. He is remembered as a resident of the medieval brick house near the Scaliger tombs in Verona that later tradition identified as Romeo's home. Cagnolo died in 1359 without children, and under his father's will his entire patrimony passed to the della Scala.
zh: 卡尼奥洛·诺加罗拉是维罗纳贵族，出身有法国渊源的诺加罗拉家族，父亲是为德拉·斯卡拉家族效力的雇佣军首领兼外交官拜拉尔迪诺·诺加罗拉，母亲是孔泰萨·达·福利亚诺。他曾住在维罗纳斯卡拉家族陵墓附近的一座中世纪砖宅，这座宅邸后来被附会为罗密欧的故居。卡尼奥洛于1359年去世，没有子嗣；依照父亲遗嘱，他的全部家产都归入德拉·斯卡拉家族。

en: Cangrande II della Scala (7 June 1332 – 14 December 1359) was the eldest son of Mastino II della Scala and Taddea da Carrara. In 1350 he married Elizabeth, daughter of Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, and in 1351 he inherited the lordship of Verona and Vicenza, ruling his first year under the regency of his uncle Alberto II. Nicknamed Can Rabbioso, the Raging Dog, he governed Verona harshly with Brandenburg mercenaries and built Castelvecchio and its fortified bridge as a refuge. On 14 December 1359 his brother Cansignorio, aided by the Carraresi of Padua, assassinated him and seized power.
zh: 坎格兰德二世·德拉·斯卡拉（1332年6月7日—1359年12月14日）是马斯蒂诺二世·德拉·斯卡拉与塔代娅·达·卡拉拉的长子。1350年他迎娶皇帝路易四世之女巴伐利亚的伊丽莎白，1351年继承维罗纳与维琴察领主之位，头一年由叔父阿尔贝托二世摄政。他绰号“怒犬”，统治严苛，倚仗勃兰登堡雇佣兵，并修建老城堡及其设防桥梁作为避难之所。1359年12月14日，弟弟坎西尼奥里奥在帕多瓦卡拉拉家族帮助下将他刺杀，夺取了政权。

en: Cangrande I della Scala (9 March 1291 – 22 July 1329), third son of Alberto I and Verde di Salizzole, nicknamed Cangrande, the great dog, was knighted by his father in 1301 while still a child. He ruled Verona jointly with his brother Alboino from 1308 and alone from 1311, when Henry VII named him imperial vicar. As leader of the northern Italian Ghibellines he took Vicenza from Padua, seized Padua in 1328 and, after a siege, entered Treviso in July 1329. He was the chief patron of the exiled Dante. Cangrande died at Treviso on 22 July 1329; contemporary accounts attributed his illness to polluted spring water. His nephews Mastino II and Alberto II succeeded him.
zh: 坎格兰德一世·德拉·斯卡拉（1291年3月9日—1329年7月22日）是阿尔贝托一世与维尔德·迪·萨利佐莱的第三子，绰号“坎格兰德”，意为“大狗”。1301年，他年纪尚幼时便被父亲封为骑士。1308年起他与兄长阿尔博伊诺共同统治维罗纳，1311年亨利七世任命他为帝国代理官后独掌大权。作为北意大利吉伯林派的领袖，他从帕多瓦手中夺得维琴察，1328年攻占帕多瓦，1329年7月围攻并入主特雷维索。他也是流亡诗人但丁最主要的庇护人。1329年7月22日，他在特雷维索去世；同时代记载称他的病是饮用受污染的泉水所致。侄辈马斯蒂诺二世与阿尔贝托二世继位。

en: Catherine da Camino was the daughter of the Trevisan noble Rizzardo VII da Camino and Stilichia d'Onigo. In 1331 her father sealed his peace with the della Scala of Verona by betrothing her, still a child, to a natural son of Alberto II della Scala. The match did not take place, and in 1339 she became the second wife of Bertoldo I d'Este, marquis of Este and lord of Ariano in the Ferrarese. She was widowed when Bertoldo died on 21 July 1343.
zh: 卡泰丽娜·达·卡米诺是特雷维索贵族里扎尔多七世·达·卡米诺与斯蒂利基亚·迪·奥尼戈之女。1331年，她的父亲与维罗纳的德拉·斯卡拉家族议和，把尚在幼年的她许配给阿尔贝托二世·德拉·斯卡拉的一名私生子。这门婚事并未成行；1339年，她成为埃斯特侯爵、费拉拉地区阿里亚诺领主贝尔托尔多一世·德斯特的第二任妻子。1343年7月21日贝尔托尔多去世，她自此守寡。

en: Caterina della Scala (13th century – c. 1305) was a Veronese noblewoman, the daughter of Alberto I della Scala, lord of Verona, and Verde di Salizzole; she died in Verona around 1305.
zh: 卡特琳娜·德拉·斯卡拉（13世纪—约1305）是维罗纳贵族女子，维罗纳领主阿尔贝托一世·德拉·斯卡拉与维尔德·迪·萨利佐莱之女，约1305年在维罗纳去世。

en: Caterina Visconti (1282–1311) was a Milanese noblewoman, the daughter of Matteo I Visconti, lord of Milan, and Bonacossa Borri. In 1298 she married Alboino della Scala, who became lord of Verona in 1304, linking the rising Visconti and Scaliger houses. The marriage produced daughters, among them Alboina, who became abbess of the monastery of San Michele in Campagna near Verona. Caterina died in Verona in 1311, the year Alboino and his brother Cangrande were named imperial vicars by Emperor Henry VII.
zh: 卡特琳娜·维斯孔蒂（1282—1311）是米兰贵族女子，米兰领主马泰奥一世·维斯孔蒂与博纳科萨·博里之女。1298年，她嫁给1304年成为维罗纳领主的阿尔博伊诺·德拉·斯卡拉，联姻将崛起中的维斯孔蒂家族与斯卡拉家族联结起来。两人育有女儿，其中阿尔博伊娜后来成为维罗纳附近坎帕尼亚圣米凯莱修道院的院长。1311年，即阿尔博伊诺与其弟坎格兰德被皇帝亨利七世任命为帝国代理人的同年，卡特琳娜在维罗纳去世。

en: Contessa da Fogliano was a daughter of Niccolò da Fogliano, lord of Reggio Emilia, and Caterina della Scala of Verona. In 1306 she married the Veronese condottiero and diplomat Bailardino Nogarola, a servant of the Scaligeri.
zh: 孔泰莎·达·福利亚诺是雷焦艾米利亚领主尼科洛·达·福利亚诺与维罗纳的卡泰丽娜·德拉·斯卡拉之女。1306年，她嫁给效力斯卡拉家族的维罗纳将领、外交官拜拉迪诺·诺加罗拉。

en: Caterina de' Rossi was a daughter of Rolando de' Rossi, Guelph lord of Parma and Lucca, and of Agnese Ruggeri. She married Arrigo Castracani degli Antelminelli, son of Castruccio Castracani, lord of Lucca.
zh: 卡泰丽娜·德·罗西是帕尔马与卢卡的圭尔夫派领主罗兰多·德·罗西与阿涅塞·鲁杰里之女，嫁给卢卡领主卡斯特鲁乔·卡斯特拉卡尼之子阿里戈·卡斯特拉卡尼·德利·安泰尔米内利。

en: Francesco da Fogliano was a son of Giberto da Fogliano, lord of Reggio Emilia, and a man-at-arms. He was hanged in 1373.
zh: 弗朗切斯科·达·福利亚诺是雷焦艾米利亚领主吉贝尔托·达·福利亚诺之子，是一名军人，1373年被处以绞刑。

en: Fregnano della Scala (c. 1331–1354) was a natural son of Mastino II, the lord who in 1339 had been cut back to Verona and Vicenza; his half-brother Cangrande II now held Verona. Fregnano began as a soldier in 1350, sent to help Astorgio di Durafort, the papal rector of Romagna, against the Manfredi lords of Faenza. In 1354, while Cangrande was away at Bolzano, he joined a revolt backed by the Gonzaga of Mantua, named Paolo Pico podestà and proclaimed himself lord. Cangrande rushed back and on 25 February fought him at the Ponte Navi, where Fregnano fell into the Adige. His body was fished out and hung for days in the Piazza delle Erbe with other rebels.
zh: 弗雷尼亚诺·德拉·斯卡拉（约1331—1354）是马斯蒂诺二世的私生子；1339年马斯蒂诺二世被压缩到只剩维罗纳和维琴察，如今维罗纳由弗雷尼亚诺同父异母的兄弟坎格兰德二世执掌。弗雷尼亚诺1350年从军，被派去援助教皇国罗马涅省代牧阿斯托尔焦·迪·杜拉福尔，对付法恩扎的领主曼弗雷迪家族。1354年，趁坎格兰德二世前往博尔扎诺，他在曼托瓦贡扎加家族支持下参与叛乱，任命保罗·皮科为最高行政长官，并自立为领主。坎格兰德火速赶回，2月25日在纳维桥与他交战，弗雷尼亚诺坠入阿迪杰河。他的尸体被捞起，与其他叛乱者一起吊在百草广场示众多日。

en: Gherardo V da Camino (1290s–1349) was a nobleman of the March of Treviso, the son of Guecellone VIII da Camino and Beatrice da Prata, of the family's lower branch. From the 1320s he and his brother Rizzardo VII led the Caminesi against the della Scala of Verona, allying with Venice. After Rizzardo VI of the senior branch died without male heirs in 1335, they seized Serravalle in 1337, but Venice eventually took the fortress for its Terraferma. In 1340 the brothers divided their fiefs, Gherardo keeping Camino, Portobuffolé and Cordignano. He died around 1349, leaving a young son, Guecellone IX.
zh: 盖拉多五世·达·卡米诺（1290年代—1349）是特雷维索边区的贵族，属达·卡米诺家族的“下支”，为圭切洛内八世·达·卡米诺与贝亚特里切·达·普拉塔之子。从1320年代起，他与兄弟里扎尔多七世共同统领卡米诺家族，对抗维罗纳德拉·斯卡拉家族的扩张，并与威尼斯结盟。1335年长支的里扎尔多六世去世，没有男性继承人；1337年二人夺取塞拉瓦莱，但威尼斯最终把这座要塞并入其大陆领地。1340年兄弟瓜分封地，盖拉多分得卡米诺、波尔托布福莱和科尔迪尼亚诺。他约于1349年去世，留下幼子圭切洛内九世。

en: Giacomo de' Rossi (died c. 1370) was the son of Rolando de' Rossi and Agnese Ruggeri. After his father's bid to rule Parma had failed, the Rossi settled for a much smaller lordship, and Giacomo became its first count.
